<summary>Perf benchmarking script </summary>
```
import os                                                                                                                                                                                                        
import time                                                                                                                                                                                                      
from statistics import mean                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
import vllm                                                                                                                                                                                                      
import vllm._custom_ops                                                                                                                                                                                          
import torch                                                                                                                                                                                                     
import torch.nn.functional as F                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
print(hasattr(torch.ops, "_C"))                                                                                                                                                                                  
print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, "gelu_tanh_and_mul"))                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
def bench_once(fn, x, out=None, iters=200, warmup=50):                                                                                                                                                           
    for _ in range(warmup):                                                                                                                                                                                      
        if out is None:                                                                                                                                                                                          
            fn(x)                                                                                                                                                                                                
        else:                                                                                                                                                                                                    
            fn(out, x)                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    times = []                                                                                                                                                                                                   
    for _ in range(iters):                                                                                                                                                                                       
        t0 = time.perf_counter()                                                                                                                                                                                 
        if out is None:                                                                                                                                                                                          
            y = fn(x)                                                                                                                                                                                            
        else:                                                                                                                                                                                                    
            fn(out, x)                                                                                                                                                                                           
            y = out                                                                                                                                                                                              
        t1 = time.perf_counter()                                                                                                                                                                                 
        times.append(t1 - t0)                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    return y, times                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
def fmt_result(name, x, times):                                                                                                                                                                                  
    avg_s = mean(times)                                                                                                                                                                                          
    elems_per_s = x.numel() / avg_s                                                                                                                                                                              
    gib_per_s = (x.numel() * x.element_size()) / avg_s / (1024 ** 3)                                                                                                                                             
    print(                                                                                                                                                                                                       
        f"{name:20s}  avg={avg_s * 1e3:8.3f} ms  "                                                                                                                                                               
        f"throughput={elems_per_s / 1e6:10.3f} Melem/s  "                                                                                                                                          
        f"input_bw={gib_per_s:8.3f} GiB/s"
    )

def main():
    torch.set_grad_enabled(False)
    torch.set_num_threads(int(os.environ.get("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")))
    device = "cpu"

    # Try a few representative sizes.
    cases = [
        (4096, 4096),
        (8192, 4096),
        (16384, 4096),
    ]
    dtypes = [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]

    for dtype in dtypes:
        print(f"===== dtype={dtype} =====")
        for rows, cols in cases:
            x = torch.randn(rows, cols, dtype=dtype, device=device).contiguous()
            out = torch.empty_like(x)

            ref, t_ref = bench_once(
                lambda t: F.gelu(t, approximate="tanh"),
                x,
            )
            ker, t_ker = bench_once(
                torch.ops._C.gelu_tanh,
                x,
                out=out,
            )

            torch.testing.assert_close(
                ker.float(),
                ref.float(),
                rtol=1e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-4,
                atol=1e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-5,
            )

            print(f"shape=({rows}, {cols})")
            fmt_result("F.gelu(tanh)", x, t_ref)
            fmt_result("torch.ops._C.gelu_tanh", x, t_ker)
            print(f"speedup: {mean(t_ref) / mean(t_ker):8.3f}x")
            print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    with torch.inference_mode():
        main()

```

title: [NVFP4][Emulation] Fuse NVFP4 weight dequantization with compute in triton kernel for w13/w2 MOE MLP linears
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
## Purpose

On platforms without native NVFP4 hardware support (e.g. AMD MI350), NVFP4 MoE weights are currently dequantized for MOE emulation in BF16.

The previous implementation from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35737 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40033 dequantized the full weight tensors `w13` and `w2`, including ALL experts, before calling the standard Triton MoE GEMM kernel through `TritonExperts.apply`, materializing large intermediate BF16 tensors and adding memory bandwidth pressure.

## Implementation

This PR introduces a fused Triton kernel (`fused_moe_nvfp4_emulation_kernel`) that performs NVFP4 weight dequantization inline with the GEMM compute for both `w13` and `w2` MoE MLP linears. Each packed uint8 byte (two FP4 values) is loaded once, dequantized and immediately consumed by `tl.dot`, thus:

1. eliminating the need to materialize full dequantized weight tensors in HBM,
2. dequantizing only the experts hit through `expert_ids`, similar to [`fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/1c23c4203007d16d96b1f07847f5bf1b663ad0d7/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L59) currently used for w4a16 models on Instinct MI3xx (e.g. `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`)

title: [PERF] [Qwen3.5] Split mixed prefill+decode batches: route decodes to the recurrent kernel
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
# Description

This PR has 3 changes:

1. **Main: split mixed prefill+decode batches** (see below).
2. **Add MTP eval** config for Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4.
3. **Rename** `fast_kernel` → `aiter_kernel` (`fast_kernel` was too general).

## Problem

GDN attention ran **all** non-spec tokens through `chunk_gated_delta_rule`. Each decode becomes its own chunk padded to `FLA_CHUNK_SIZE=64`, so `D` decodes cost `D` near-empty 64-token chunks of wasted work. The ratio looks like this:

| Case | Kernel | Median (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| A. prefill 8192 | CuteDSL chunk | 464.1 |
| B. decode 953 | fused_sigmoid | 1843.7 |
| Sum | | 2370.8 |
| C. mixed unified (953+7239 → chunk) | CuteDSL chunk | 4361.6 |

With this PR:

| Case | Kernel | Median (µs) |
|---|---|---|
| split (pre+dec, this change) | CuteDSL + fused_sigmoid | 2256.5 |

PS: MTP already goes through this path.

## Solution

When a non-spec batch mixes prefills and decodes, peel the decode front-slice off to the recurrent update kernel `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` and run only the prefill tail through the chunk kernel. The metadata builder rebases chunk metadata to the prefill-only tail; outputs are stitched back in decode-first order.

## Tests

- `test_gdn_forward_core_split.py::test_forward_core_split_matches_unified`: split path matches the unified chunk-only path on `core_attn_out` and SSM-state. **8/8 passed** on B200 (bf16/fp32 × mixed-batch shapes).
- GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot, B200):

| Model | Threshold | Measured | Pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | 0.84 ± 0.03 | 0.8499 | ✅ |
| Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | 0.79 ± 0.03 | 0.7953 | ✅ |
| nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.8863 | ✅ |

## Performance

Kernel microbench (B200, cold-L2 CUPTI, 397B-A17B-NVFP4, mixed 953 decodes + 7239 prefill): unified chunk 4361 µs → split 2256 µs, **1.93× speedup** (1.88–2.17× across configs).

End-to-end (8×B200, DP=8+EP, ISL=8192/OSL=256, conc=2048, steady-state):

Server:

```bash
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800 VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=5.0 \
  vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
    --port 8000 -tp 1 -pp 1 -dp 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --language-model-only --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching --stream-interval=100
```

Client:

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend vllm --model nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
  --port 8000 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 256 \
  --max-concurrency 2048 --num-prompt 2048 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0.0
```

| Metric | Baseline (unified) | With split | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 131,976 | **164,156** | **+24.4%** |

title: [Bugfix] Prevent cuMemcpyBatchAsync segfault with MTP and KV offloading
author: JOSH1024
body:
**Bug:** 
Currently, vLLM crashes with a `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` segfault when using native KV offloading (`--kv-offloading-backend native`) alongside MTP speculative decoding on long contexts.

**Root cause:** 
I found that the `OffloadingConnectorScheduler` was accidentally including EAGLE/MTP draft-attention groups in both the load and store scheduling paths. Since these draft groups don't have stable block hashes and use tiny `gpu_block_size` values, it caused a massive miscalculation (`num_gpu_blocks = cdiv(420K, small_size) = 105022`). This resulted in an out-of-bounds GPU block index that triggered a silent, hard-to-debug CUDA segfault in `swap_blocks_batch`.

**Fix:** 
- Added an `is_eagle_group` flag to `GroupOffloadConfig` so we can easily spot these groups.
- Updated the scheduler to skip eagle groups entirely in all load/store scheduling loops. 
- As a defense-in-depth measure, I also added a pre-DMA bounds check in `gpu_worker.py`. This ensures that if any out-of-bounds block ID ever slips through in the future, it safely throws a clear Python `RuntimeError` instead of a silent CUDA segfault.

**Accountability:**
I used some AI assistance to help me track down the root cause and write the patches, but I have manually reviewed every changed line to ensure it's correct. I am relying on the GitHub CI to run the full Linux suite since I am developing on Windows.

**Testing:**
Verified the fix locally via a custom standalone regression test suite (8 passing tests ):
- Confirmed `is_eagle_group` correctly populates and defaults to `False` (preserving backward compatibility).
- Verified the load path (`update_state_after_alloc`) and store path (`_build_store_jobs`) appropriately skip MTP groups and correctly return `group_sizes=0` and `block_indices=0`.
- Verified the defense-in-depth bounds check safely catches out-of-bounds IDs before triggering the CUDA call.

Closes #44780

title: [Frontend][Core] Add release_kv_cache_memory() API
author: andakai
body:
## Motivation

Sleep level 2 releases KV cache memory, but it also discards model weights. This
is unnecessarily expensive when a framework only needs temporary GPU headroom
while keeping the same model instance resident.

One concrete use case is model weight update in RL training. The workaround in
[verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) uses
`sleep(level=2)` followed by `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` before updating the
standalone model. Releasing only the KV cache reduces peak GPU memory and can
avoid OOM during the update, without discarding and remapping weights.

## Summary

This PR adds `release_kv_cache_memory()` as a dedicated KV-only partial-sleep
operation. It discards KV cache allocations, keeps model weights resident, and
pauses scheduling until the released memory is restored with the existing
`wake_up()` API.

## Implementation

### Call flow

The offline and server entry points converge on the same engine path:

```text
LLM.release_kv_cache_memory() -> LLMEngine ---------\
                                                       -> EngineCore
POST /release_kv_cache_memory -> EngineClient ------/       |
                                                             v
                                      Executor.discard(("kv_cache",))
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                               Worker -> SleepModeBackend
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                           CuMem/XPU allocator.discard(tags)
```

`EngineCore` first pauses the scheduler and clears the prefix cache. Depending
on the selected pause mode, it either handles existing requests immediately or
waits for in-flight requests to finish before asking all workers to discard KV
cache allocations. The scheduler remains paused after release; a discard
failure also fails closed instead of resuming scheduling with potentially
partially unmapped memory.

At allocator level, only mapped allocations tagged `kv_cache` are unmapped and
released, without a CPU backup. Per-allocation mapping state prevents duplicate
unmap or map operations when release, sleep, and wake-up calls are mixed.

### Interaction with sleep levels

`release_kv_cache_memory()` is treated as a KV-only partial sleep. A later
`sleep(1)` or `sleep(2)` can upgrade that state to a full sleep:

| Current state | Operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully awake | `release_kv_cache_memory()` | KV cache discarded, weights resident, scheduler paused |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(1)` | Weights offloaded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(2)` | Weights discarded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | KV cache remapped and scheduling resumed |
| Full sleep | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | Only KV cache remapped; weights remain sleeping and scheduling stays paused |
| Full sleep | `wake_up()` | All allocations restored and scheduling resumed |

The executor tracks the exact internal state with `sleeping_tags`. Scheduling
is resumed only after no sleeping tags remain.

### Logging and observability

This PR reuses the existing sleep-state logger instead of adding a dedicated
`kv_cache_released` Prometheus state. After KV release, the existing metrics
report `awake=0`, `weights_offloaded=0`, and `discard_all=0`: the engine is not
available for scheduling, but it is not in sleep level 1 or 2. The precise
resource state remains available internally through `sleeping_tags`.

There is currently no requirement to monitor KV-only release separately. If
that becomes useful, a dedicated Prometheus state and its transition logic can
be added in a follow-up change.

## Scope

The public API intentionally supports only KV cache release. Existing sleep
levels already cover the other current cases:

- `sleep(1)` offloads weights and discards KV cache memory.
- `sleep(2)` discards all managed GPU memory.

A generic public tag API would also need to define whether each tag is discarded
or offloaded, increasing the API surface and overlapping with existing sleep
semantics. More fine-grained public memory management can be discussed when a
concrete additional use case appears; the internal `discard(tags)` path remains
extensible.

## Related work

- [vLLM#42658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42658) explores generic
  tag-level sleep management. This PR instead provides a smaller, explicit
  end-to-end API for the known KV-only use case.
- [vLLM#46438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46438) contains related
  allocator-level selective-discard work.
- [verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) demonstrates the
  downstream model-update use case and its current sleep/wake workaround.

This PR does not duplicate the generic public API proposed in #42658; its scope
and semantics are intentionally narrower.

## Tests

Local validation used an Enroot container on one NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3
and Torch 2.13.0+cu130. The PR Python source was tested with the image's
precompiled native libraries (vLLM distribution 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  -k "kv_cache_release_rejects_unsafe_state or pause_synchronizes_device" \
  -v -o addopts=""
```

Result: **5 passed**. Rejection coverage checks an unpaused scheduler, pending
requests, and pending batches independently, with no cache reset or discard on
failure. Removing each guard in memory caused its corresponding test to fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py \
  -k release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation \
  -x -v -o addopts="" --timeout=600
```

Result: **2 passed**. Real Qwen3-0.6B generation covers rejection without a pause,
KV-only release/wake-up, and release followed by full level-1 sleep/wake-up.
Checks use process-local mapped memory and compare greedy token IDs before and
after restoration.

```bash
pre-commit run --files tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

The test revision changes no production behavior; no additional model
benchmark was run beyond the generation-equivalence checks above.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to review the implementation, revise and validate the tests,
and draft this description.
The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and test scope.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output][Spec Decode] Advance grammar across reasoning boundary
author: yuyue0225sc
body:
### Purpose

Fixes #43388. Fixes #48228. Fixes #34650.

Under async scheduling + speculative decoding + a Qwen-style reasoning parser, `should_advance` in `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py` silently fails for JSON/regex/choice constraints. Two distinct bugs interact:

**Bug 1: the delta window misses the marker.** The delta window computed from `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` skips `</think>` whenever some drafts are rejected, because the placeholder count stays greater than zero. As a result `reasoning_ended` never flips, the grammar is never enforced, and the output contains Markdown fences or arbitrary prose.

**Bug 2: post-marker tokens never reach the FSM.** Even after `reasoning_ended` flips, the post-marker content tokens produced in the marker step never enter the grammar FSM. On the next step the bitmask is prepared with the grammar at its initial state, the model emits the opening token again, and `response_format=json_object` returns `{{...}` content — HTTP 200, but the body fails to parse on the client (the exact symptom reported in #48228).

This PR closes the inter-step state leak in `should_advance`. The sibling intra-step bitmask leak in `grammar_bitmask` was fixed by #44297 (merged); the patch sites are independent, and together they cover the full reasoning → content boundary under async + speculative decoding.

### Design

One unified boundary path for **all** constraint types (final shape reached through review with @yzong-rh):

1. `should_advance` accepts an optional `new_token_ids` argument from the scheduler call site and uses it as the exact delta window (fixes Bug 1). The two draft-validation call sites keep the placeholder fallback; their behavior is unchanged.
2. At the boundary, `should_advance` records `reasoning_end_token_index` and returns `True` for every constraint type. The scheduler then uses `trim_reasoning_for_advance()` + `accept_tokens()` to advance only the verified post-marker suffix (fixes Bug 2). `should_advance` no longer mutates the grammar — it only updates reasoning-boundary state and decides whether the scheduler should advance.

Earlier revisions used a conservative inline drain for JSON/regex/choice (advance inside `should_advance`, return `False`) while `STRUCTURAL_TAG` under spec decode used the scheduler's trim-and-advance path — two paths for the same boundary. The final revision removes that split: post-marker positions inside a speculative window are already constrained by `grammar_bitmask`, and rejection sampling prevents grammar-invalid drafts from being committed, so the committed suffix reaching `accept_tokens` is grammar-valid. Net effect on vLLM-side complexity: no per-constraint-type branching, no grammar side effects outside the scheduler, and a single boundary mechanism that any future backend-side delegation would migrate as one unit.

One intentional semantics change: an `accept_tokens` rejection at the boundary (not expected in the normal flow, per the invariant above) now terminates the request through the scheduler's standard error path instead of warn-and-continue, matching the existing non-reasoning path.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- #36138 (merged) fixed the spec-decode × structured-output bypass for single-token markers, but its placeholder math underflows past the marker under async scheduling + draft rejection (Bug 1) — #43388 still reproduced on Qwen3.5 + MTP.
- #43526 (closed) took the same first step but was closed by its author because post-marker tokens in the same batch were left unobserved by the FSM; this PR closes that gap.
- #43424 (open) targets multi-token markers (gpt-oss Harmony) via a different code path (`precommit_filter_tokens`); the scopes are complementary and can land in either order.

### Test Plan

Regression cases in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py`:

- `test_should_advance_uses_new_token_ids_when_provided` — Bug 1: the reasoner sees the exact multi-token delta rather than the placeholder-derived window.
- `test_should_advance_without_new_token_ids_falls_back` — backward compat for the no-arg call sites.
- `test_should_advance_trims_reasoning_prefix_for_json` — Bug 2: the boundary step records `reasoning_end_token_index`, returns `True`, and `trim_reasoning_for_advance` yields only the post-marker suffix.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/structured_output/ -v
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py -v
```

### Test Result

Re-verified on the current branch (merged with latest main), 8× H20, `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, `--reasoning-parser qwen3`:

- `json_object`, MTP k=4 (the #43388 scenario): **50/50** requests returned clean JSON. Baseline on main without this fix: 7/50 ok (86% failure — Markdown fences + leading garbage).
- Strict tool calling / `STRUCTURAL_TAG`, MTP k=1 (the #44006 scenario): **50/50** valid `tool_calls`, 0 HTTP 500 — confirms the unified path does not regress #44297.
- Unit: `tests/v1/structured_output/test_reasoning_structured_output.py` — 11 passed.

Independent verification on other hardware:

- @estrella159 applied https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44297 + this PR on vLLM 0.24.0 (Blackwell sm120), 8 launches per arm, 24 distinct prompts per launch:
Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (dense): strict-JSON validity 14.12/24 to 23.38/24 (paired p=0.0078). The patched MTP-on arm is statistically indistinguishable from MTP-off (23.25/24, p=1.0), i.e. the fix restores MTP-on to the MTP-off baseline.
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (MoE): 12.75/24 to 20.25/24 (paired p=0.0078). A residual gap to the MTP-off baseline remains (23.75/24, p=0.0078), attributable to a grammar-level whitespace-liveness hazard that spec-decode amplifies on this architecture.
- @stefanwichmann cherry-picked this PR on GB10 (DGX Spark), `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8`, across 5 fresh engine starts: 10/10 valid JSON with MTP re-enabled, doubled-brace output gone ([#48228 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48228)).
- @Mazyod  reproduced on google/gemma-4-E2B-it + MTP (num_speculative_tokens=2, L4, strict json_schema): JSON corruption at concurrency 8/16/24/32 went from 75%/100%/96%/91% baseline to 0% at every level with this PR, confirming both the should_advance and scheduler changes are required — first verification on a non-Qwen model family.
- @cresslank  independently validated `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark` with DSpark spec
  decode (Blackwell, async scheduling) — first run through DeepSeek's DSpark path
  rather than the MTP configs above, confirming the shared accept-side fix holds
  regardless of speculation method. Stock **7/20** → this PR **20/20** (matching
  speculation-off), plus **120/120** on a prompt-diverse liveness run, 0 boundary
  corruption; failures were malformed exactly at the reasoning→grammar transition.

<details>
<summary>E2E reproducer (server command + 50-trial classification client)</summary>

Server:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":4}' \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --enable-log-requests \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
  --trust-remote-code --enforce-eager \
  --port 8000
```

Client sends 50 requests asking for a JSON object describing Seoul, with `response_format={"type":"json_object"}` and `enable_thinking=true`, without forbidding Markdown (so the model falls back to its training-time formatting habit). Each response is classified as `ok` (raw JSON, parses, has required keys), `markdown_fence`, `leading_garbage`, `bad_json`, etc.

````python
import json, os, re, time
from collections import Counter
from openai import APIStatusError, OpenAI

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("VLLM_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1")
MODEL = os.environ.get("VLLM_MODEL", "qwen3.5-35b-a3b")
TRIALS = int(os.environ.get("TRIALS", "50"))

MESSAGES = [{"role": "user", "content": "Give me a JSON object describing Seoul, with keys city, country, and population."}]
REQUIRED_KEYS = ("city", "country", "population")

def classify(content):
    if not content or not content.strip():
        return "empty", ""
    raw = content
    s = content.strip()
    if s.startswith("```"):
        return "markdown_fence", s[:120]
    if raw[0] != "{":
        return "leading_garbage", repr(raw[:40])
    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", s, re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return "no_json", repr(s[:80])
    if m.group(0) != s:
        return "prose_wrapped", s[:120]
    try:
        obj = json.loads(s)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        return "bad_json", str(e)
    for k in REQUIRED_KEYS:
        if k not in obj:
            return "bad_json", "missing " + repr(k)
    return "ok", json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False)[:120]

def main():
    client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key="EMPTY", max_retries=0, timeout=120.0)
    counts = Counter()
    t0 = time.time()
    print("target:", BASE_URL, "model:", MODEL, "trials:", TRIALS)
    for i in range(1, TRIALS + 1):
        try:
            r = client.chat.completions.create(
                model=MODEL, messages=MESSAGES,
                response_format={"type": "json_object"},
                extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
                temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=4096,
            )
            kind, detail = classify(r.choices[0].message.content or "")
        except APIStatusError as e:
            kind, detail = "http_error", "HTTP " + str(e.status_code)
        except Exception as e:
            kind, detail = "client_error", type(e).__name__
        counts[kind] += 1
        print("[%3d/%d] %-20s %s" % (i, TRIALS, kind, detail), flush=True)
    print("\nsummary (%.1fs):" % (time.time() - t0))
    for k, n in counts.most_common():
        print("  %-20s %d" % (k, n))
    bug = counts["markdown_fence"] + counts["prose_wrapped"] + counts["no_json"] + counts["bad_json"] + counts["leading_garbage"]
    print("\nFAIL %d/%d" % (bug, TRIALS) if bug else "\nPASS %d/%d" % (counts["ok"], TRIALS))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
````

</details>

title: [Bugfix][Model] Voxtral realtime: fix boot OOM and engine crash at max_model_len
author: damienlaine
body:
Fixes for Voxtral realtime, all in the model and the realtime entrypoint. The unbounded-duration part is #45833 (stacked).

### Update 2026-10-05

Reworked after @andylolu2's review: no core changes anymore. Scheduler, runner and output_processor changes dropped (#58942 covers ERROR/ABORT, #42502 the generic scheduler guard).

### Fixes

- **Boot OOM (#38233)**: profiling runs one audio item of `max_model_len` tokens. With the default `max_model_len` (131072) that OOMs at boot on 16 GB. New `VoxtralRealtimeProcessingInfo`: the profiling audio is the largest streaming chunk (the prefix, 39 tokens), `{"audio": 1}` per update. The item size stays `max_model_len` because it also sizes the encoder cache: a paused session keeps its last chunk cached until it resumes, and a cache sized to one chunk deadlocks concurrent sessions (0/12 at `--max-num-batched-tokens 256`).
- **Engine crash at `max_model_len`**: a streaming session reaching the limit kills the EngineCore (`illegal memory access`) and every other session with it. `VoxtralRealtimeBuffer` now counts submitted tokens and ends the stream before `max_model_len`, so the session finishes normally.
- **WebSocket disconnect**: cancelling the generation task doesn't abort the engine request, the slot stays held. Cleanup now aborts it.

### Tests

RTX 4090 Laptop 16 GB, `--hf-overrides` sliding window 256, PIECEWISE:

- `--max-model-len 131072`: main OOMs during profiling, this PR boots.
- concurrent realtime streams: same transcripts, throughput and memory as with the previous runner change, no OOM. 12 sessions at `--max-num-batched-tokens 256`: 12/12, same as main.
- `--max-model-len 512`, 70 s streams over websocket: streams stop at the cap, client gets `transcription.done`, next session OK.

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py -k max_model_len   # 2 passed
```

`test_voxtral_realtime_generator_max_model_len` fails with `EngineDeadError` without the buffer cap.

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AITER MLA: size MTP verification decode metadata for real qlen/dtype
author: chaeminlim-mb
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm AITER MLA, MTP verification decode (qlen = `num_speculative_tokens + 1`, so 4 for MTP3) was sized as ordinary qlen=1 decode: `get_mla_metadata_info_v1` received `qo_len=1` and the kernel recomputed metadata internally for qlen>1. The verification logits come out wrong, the accept/reject step drifts from the target distribution, and accuracy drops. Passing q/kv dtypes (#46997) does not fix this on its own.

Fix: size the decode metadata from the real MTP qlen and the actual Q/KV dtypes (FP8 Q when the KV cache is FP8). qlen ≤ 4 keeps a native dense layout with persistent per-request causal boundaries; qlen > 4 falls back to qlen=1 split rows; CUDA-graph pad rows get synthesized `seq_lens`/`qo_indptr`.

Scoped to `rocm_aiter_mla.py` (ROCm AITER-only) plus its unit test. The draft-side MTP pieces (local-argmax `get_top_tokens`, `spec_step_idx` threading, attention head-count grouping) are a separate concern and are not in this PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
ruff check vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py -q   # ROCm-gated, CPU policy/arithmetic
```

GSM8K on TP8 DeepSeek-R1 FP8, MTP3, greedy, served from this branch against upstream `main`.

## Test Result

- Unit test: 11 passed (CPU, kernels mocked). Covers the qlen policy, native vs split routing, FP8 metadata sizing, CUDA-graph pad synthesis, and the split-path page-index expansion values — `_expand_mtp_decode_page_indices_kernel`'s output is now checked against hand-derived per-row causal indices, not just its launch grid.
- GSM8K (openai/gsm8k test, exact-match, n=200): 0.835 without the fix, 0.970 with it, on current upstream `main` — same build, only the Python differs. Re-run on this branch (MI300X, TP8, MTP3): 0.98 strict-match.
- Without the fix the 3rd MTP position collapses to ~0 acceptance and output degenerates; with it, per-position acceptance stays healthy (≈0.80 / 0.50 / 0.30) and completions are coherent.

Multi-GPU serving accuracy was run manually, not in CI.

title: [Bugfix] Fix MoE model load OOM in FlashInfer_TRTLLM  backend with sleep mode
author: andakai
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the load-time OOM reported in [#43951](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43951) for large BF16 MoE models using `--enable-sleep-mode` with the FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE backend.

Instead of bypassing the `max_split_size_mb=20` allocator policy introduced by [#41268](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41268), **this PR reduces the transient GPU memory created by FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE weight conversion itself.** The conversion now preallocates the final block-layout output tensors and writes each expert directly into the target storage, avoiding the previous per-expert clone/list/stack pattern.

## Issue

[#43951](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43951) reports that loading `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507` with sleep mode OOMs during weight loading, before CUDA graph profiling starts. The traceback points to `convert_moe_weights_to_flashinfer_trtllm_block_layout`, and the failing allocation can be as small as 20 MiB.

I reproduced the load path on H20-141GB by forcing the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend to pass the SM100 capability gate. The problem happens in model load stage, so this H20-forcing-to-run method is enough to reproduce this issue.

Repro command:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve \
  Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-sleep-mode \
  --load-format dummy \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.93 \
  --max-num-seqs 1024 \
  --skip-tokenizer-init
```

The issue is reproduced. Only Flashinfer_trtllm backend has the error, Trtion, flashinfer_cutlass backend can succeed because they have simple postprocess.

## Root Cause

For `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507`:

- `num_hidden_layers = 94`
- `num_experts = 128`
- `hidden_size = 4096`
- `moe_intermediate_size = 1536`
- `TP = 4`
- `dtype = BF16`

With TP=4:

- `intermediate_per_partition = 1536 / 4 = 384`
- `w13 = [128, 768, 4096]`
- `w2  = [128, 4096, 384]`

The sensitive path is FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE conversion. The original implementation creates per-expert temporary tensors such as cloned weights, permute indices, reordered tensors, contiguous copies, block-layout outputs, and finally stacked outputs.

Per expert:

- `w13[i]: [768, 4096] BF16 = 6 MiB`
- `w2[i] : [4096, 384] BF16 = 3 MiB`

**The permute index tensors are larger:**

- `w13` uint8 view size = `768 * 4096 * 2 = 6,291,456` elements, so int64 permute indices are about `48 MiB`
- `w2` uint8 view size = `4096 * 384 * 2 = 3,145,728` elements, so int64 permute indices are about `24 MiB`

**That `24 MiB` size is important because it is larger than the `20 MiB` split threshold from #41268.**

Observed allocator behavior for this model:

- `max_split_size_mb=20` -> OOM
- `max_split_size_mb=25` -> succeeds
- `max_split_size_mb=32` -> succeeds
- `max_split_size_mb=64` -> succeeds
- `max_split_size_mb=128` -> succeeds

This shows a conflict between #41268 and this workload. **#41268 uses `max_split_size_mb=20` to protect large cached blocks and avoid fragmentation during model loading. That behavior is useful for the original fragmentation problem.** However, FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE conversion repeatedly creates medium-sized temporary tensors, especially in the 20-50 MiB range, across 128 experts and 94 layers. **With sleep mode enabled, these allocations go through vLLM's CuMem weights pool, and the pool does not fully reclaim transient backing segments mid-load.**

FlashInfer CUTLASS and Triton did not reproduce this issue in my tests because their MoE post-processing does not create the same repeated transient allocation pattern.

## Why not bypass `max_split_size_mb=20`

**I considered bypassing `max_split_size_mb=20` for the FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE conversion.** That does fix this issue locally, but it also weakens the protection added by #41268.

I also tested the behavior without #41268's allocator policy and observed OOM later during warmup. This suggests #41268 is still necessary: during model loading, vLLM still needs to protect large tensors from fragmentation.

**Changing the global `max_split_size_mb` value is also not robust.** The right threshold depends on model shape and tensor parallel size. Larger MoE models can produce larger transient tensors, so values like 32, 64, or 128 MiB are only case-specific workarounds. Raising the global threshold also moves away from #41268's original goal.

## Fix

The original FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE conversion did this for each expert:

```text
clone -> index reorder -> contiguous -> convert_to_block_layout -> append to list
torch.stack(all_experts)
```

This PR changes the conversion to:

1. Preallocate the final `w13` and `w2` block-layout output tensors.
2. View each expert as `uint8`.
3. Inline the equivalent of `convert_to_block_layout` by reshaping to blocks and permuting dimensions.
4. Use `torch.index_select(..., out=...)` to write the permuted expert directly into the preallocated output tensor.
5. Fold the `swap_w13_to_w31` operation into the W13 permute indices, avoiding a full materialized swapped W13 tensor.

The block-layout transformation is still performed. It is just fused with the row permutation and written directly into the destination tensor, which avoids the previous clone/list/stack intermediates.

## Validation

### Time

Qwen3-235B TP=4 dummy load, forced H20 FlashInfer TRTLLM backend:

- Old conversion + sleep mode: OOM
- New conversion + sleep mode:
  - load completed
  - memory: `109.61 GiB`
  - load time: `3.001113s`
  - later expected H20 failure: `No supported CUDA architectures found for major versions [10, 12]`

No sleep mode comparison:

- Old conversion + no sleep mode:
  - run 1: `10.723114s`
  - run 2: `10.214007s`
- New conversion + no sleep mode:
  - `2.385791s`

So in this dummy-load, conversion-heavy setup, **the new path is roughly 4x faster than the original conversion.**

### Correctness check

I compared the old conversion and the new conversion using random BF16 tensors and bitwise `uint16` comparison.

Covered cases:

- Qwen-like TP4 full shape:
  - `w13=[128,768,4096]`
  - `w2=[128,4096,384]`
- DeepSeek-like TP4 shape
- DeepSeek-like TP2 shape

Result:

```text
ALL_BITWISE_EQUAL
```

## Limitations

The load/conversion path was validated on H20 by forcing the FlashInfer TRTLLM backend to pass the capability gate. Since FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE kernels are SM100/B-series only, H20 cannot validate final runtime kernel correctness. This should still be tested on B-series hardware.

title: [AuxOutput] Add block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs
author: xhx1022
body:
# AuxOutput Connector: block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs

## Summary

This PR introduces the first **AuxOutput Connector** implementation for vLLM.
The first supported auxiliary output is routed-expert output (R3): the expert IDs selected for
every token executed by an MoE model.

R3 cannot remain a request-local GPU buffer when prefix caching and async
scheduling are enabled:

- a prefix-cache hit skips model execution, so cached tokens produce no new R3;
- physical GPU/KV slots are reused and are not stable object identities;
- speculative decoding can execute rows that are later rejected;
- one result may contain cached blocks, new blocks, and a partial tail.

The connector stores immutable R3 blocks using KV-compatible block hashes. KV
and R3 for the same prefix can therefore be reused together. This PR provides a
bounded local SHM backend; distributed storage and more auxiliary output types are
follow-ups.

## Why an AuxOutput Connector?

The model capture hook only obtains a tensor from the current forward pass. A
separate lifecycle layer must decide:

- which logical tokens are accepted;
- which blocks are reusable across requests;
- when temporary GPU/CPU buffers can be released;
- where immutable blocks are stored; and
- how cached and new blocks form one ordered result.

These responsibilities also apply to future DSA and logprobs auxiliary outputs. The
connector keeps them out of the model runner and gives storage backends one
common object lifecycle. It is not a second KV Connector or a generic Scheduler
sidecar.

## Architecture

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| API / OutputProcessor                                             |
| Current: return complete R3                                       |
| Follow-up: return ordered auxiliary output keys                           |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| EngineCore                                                        |
| Scheduler -> AuxOutputSchedulerConnector                           |
|              - logical request progress                           |
|              - KV-compatible hashes                              |
|              - terminal events                                   |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                | per-step metadata
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU Worker                                                        |
| Model Runner -> router capture -> async GPU-to-CPU copy            |
|              -> AuxOutputWorkerConnector                           |
|                 - accepted-row assembly                           |
|                 - block publication/materialization               |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                  +-------------+-------------+
                  |                           |
                  v                           v
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
     | Current                  |  | Follow-up                |
     | Bounded local SHM        |  | Mooncake distributed     |
     | background publication   |  | immutable objects        |
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
```

The Scheduler connector owns logical progress and hashes, not payloads. The
Worker connector owns accepted R3 rows and publication. `BlockObjectStore` owns opaque
immutable blocks and retention, but knows nothing about tokens or speculative
decoding.

## Auxiliary output types

An execution auxiliary output is an auxiliary model output that is aligned to a stable
logical coordinate and may need to outlive the worker step that produced it.

| Auxiliary output | Coordinate | Reuse | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routed experts (R3) | Executed token | Prefix block | This PR |
| DSA routing/index data | Executed token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Logprobs/prompt logprobs | Predicted token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Multimodal auxiliary data | Request/object | Request only | Exploratory |
| Sampling candidate IDs | Sampling step | Request only | Exploratory |

Prefix-block auxiliary outputs are content-addressed and reusable with a matching
prefix. Request-only auxiliary outputs use the same storage contract but do not
participate in prefix hits. Reward values, tool results, finish reasons, and
Scheduler status remain normal request/control-plane metadata.

## Current PR scope

This PR implements:

- Model Runner V2 R3 capture;
- block-keyed SHM publication and prefix materialization;
- async scheduling, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, and preemption;
- background publication, bounded capacity, and KV-aligned retention;
- terminal-only R3 delivery for streaming output;
- fail-closed checks for unsupported configurations.

It does not implement Mooncake, public auxiliary output keys, additional auxiliary output
fields, PD disaggregation, or new parallel topologies.

When disabled, no auxiliary output capture buffer, Store, per-step metadata, or R3 copy
is created on the normal serving path.

The existing `--enable-return-routed-experts` flag and `routed_experts` response
field are unchanged. The new optional configuration is exposed as
`--aux-output-config` (`AuxOutputConfig` in Python).

## Follow-ups

```text
This PR
  R3 lifecycle + local SHM
        |
        v
Unified object/profile contract + ordered keys
        |
        v
Direct Mooncake backend
        |
        v
Joint KV + mandatory-auxiliary output prefix readiness
        |
        v
DSA, logprobs, and additional topology support
```

The main planned work is:

1. define a backend-independent object/profile contract and ordered key output;
2. add a direct Mooncake backend for external trainer/JAX consumers;
3. admit remote prefix hits only when KV and mandatory auxiliary outputs are ready;
4. add DSA and logprobs through small field adapters, not new lifecycle code;
5. validate CPU KV offload, PD, PP/DCP/PCP, and multi-writer deployments before
   enabling them.

## Validation

Naming-update validation: **96 passed, 1 skipped** across configuration, store,
capture, Scheduler, output, and Ray tests. An AST comparison verified that all
24 renamed files preserve the original logic, allowing renamed identifiers,
messages, and sorted imports. Additional smoke checks passed for the existing
R3 flag, the new JSON/Python configuration, compilation hashes, serialization,
object keys, and R3 bytes. The latest naming-only update was also exercised on GB200; results and
limitations are below.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/executor/test_ray_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py \
  -k 'aux_output or routed_experts or pending_output or store or worker or detach_zero_copy'
pre-commit run
```

### GB200 rename A/B (2026-09-08)

Compared `85f100032e` (before rename) with `f99d53b521` (after rename) on the
same two GB200 nodes (8 GPUs), using the locally cached DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base
FP8 weights. Both arms enable R3, MRV2, MP, TP1/DP8/EP8, async scheduling and
prefix caching. They use identical native libraries/dependencies; Python source
injection was verified by per-file SHA checks.

Workload: 64 concurrent requests, each with 262,144 input tokens and one output
token; synthetic token IDs, with output constrained to token 42. GPU memory
utilization is 0.90, max batched tokens 16,384, block size 256, and batch-invariant
mode is off. This is a serving/R3 regression test, not a model-quality evaluation.

| Measurement | Before rename | After rename |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total throughput (input + output tokens/s) | 82,741.42 | 82,568.30 |
| Total duration | 202.768 s | 203.193 s |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |
| Prefix-hit tokens in the timed workload | 0 | 0 |

Throughput changed by **−0.21%** in this single A/B: no obvious regression, not a
statistical significance claim. Startup and warmup are excluded. Both arms still
reported the same first-long-request `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` JIT
warning, so this is not a strictly all-kernels-warm measurement.

Correctness checks:

- All 128 long responses passed token-count, R3 row-count, shape and dtype checks.
- Separate cold/hot tests cover eight 1K-prompt/16-decode requests and eight
  64K-prompt/1-decode requests per version. The latter exercises multi-step
  chunked prefill. All requests' reused-prefix R3 SHA hashes match exactly:
  768 rows/request for the short case and 65,280 rows/request for the long case.
- All eight short cold requests have identical full R3 hashes across versions.

**Limitation: long-context full-output bitwise equivalence did not pass.** None
of the 64 full 256K R3 hashes matched across the two server runs. In the saved
request-0 sample, differences begin at row index 2051 and affect 55.38% of
elements. The same candidate version also differs when comparing the identical
first 64K input prefix in 256K versus 64K cold requests (first difference at
2051; 46.44% of elements). Recomputed decode R3 can differ between cold/hot runs
as well, already before the rename. These observations do not establish the
underlying cause or prove long-output equivalence; they must not be presented
as a full R3 correctness pass.

This run validates the response structure, exact cached-block reuse and short
cross-version outputs. It does not add new forced-preemption, speculative
decoding or free-generation quality coverage. Slurm job `24176` completed with
exit code 0; test containers and node allocations were released.

Development validation covers focused unit tests, async scheduling, forced
preemption, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, cold/hot prefix reuse,
streaming aggregation, SHM capacity/LRU behavior, pre-commit, and GB200/H200
throughput experiments reported in the PR discussion.

The latest update also moves R3 GPU-to-CPU transfer onto the existing async
output copy stream, avoiding a synchronous copy on the model execution critical
path.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, performance experiments,
and review. The submitting human reviewed the accepted changes and validation.

title: [Kernel] Extend Marlin thread-tile padding to MoE (WNA16 + FP8/MXFP8)
author: mgoin
body:
Follow-up to #45295, which added thread-tile padding to the dense Marlin paths and NVFP4 MoE. This extends the same mechanism to the remaining Marlin MoE preps: generic WNA16 (GPTQ/AWQ/compressed-tensors) and FP8/MXFP8.

TP sharding can leave the rank-local intermediate size off a Marlin thread tile. Today WNA16 MoE rejects Marlin and falls back to slower kernels, and FP8/MXFP8 MoE crash at repack. We now zero-pad the intermediate to a valid tile at weight prep. The padded region never reaches the MoE output: for WNA16, w13's padded output channels are zeroed by the zero-padded scales, so the padded inputs to w2 are zero; for FP8/MXFP8 a quantized zero decodes to 0.0, so padded weights drop out directly. The apply path recovers padded N from the packed weight shape, so nothing is threaded through new kwargs. hidden_size (the MoE I/O extent) is never padded; act-order and groups straddling the boundary keep the strict checks. Block-FP8 (weight_block_size=[128,128]) already requires intermediate % 128, so padding is a no-op there.

Not a duplicate: #45295 scoped MoE to NVFP4 only and left the rest as a follow-up.

## Test

`pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py` — 95 passed, 13 skipped. Adds CPU policy/gate tests plus GPU round-trips through the real prepare + repack + fused_marlin_moe vs the dequantized reference, at tile-misaligned intermediates:
- WNA16 GPTQ int4 (channelwise + groupwise) — symmetric int4 zero decodes to -8, exercising the zero-padded-scales cancellation; match is exact.
- FP8 weight-only (channelwise + tensorwise) and MXFP8 — match within fp8 precision.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; all changes reviewed by the submitter.

title: [Perf] Restore zero-init of swizzled NVFP4 scale buffer to recover Blackwell decode throughput
author: qiching
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a severe NVFP4 decode regression on Blackwell (B300 / GB300) introduced by #42988 ("[Perf] zeros -> empty to remove additional fill", commit `b29cbf0652`).

`create_fp4_scale_tensor` (`vllm/_custom_ops.py`) allocates the **swizzled** scale-factor buffer with shape `(round_up(m, 128), round_up(n // 16, 4) // 4)`, i.e. padded in both the M (to 128) and packed-K (to 4) dimensions. The NVFP4 quant kernel (`cvt_fp16_to_fp4`) writes scale factors through a swizzled tiled layout and does **not** write every padded element that the downstream NVFP4 GEMM subsequently reads. #42988 switched this allocation from `torch.zeros` to `torch.empty`, leaving those padded scale factors uninitialized → corrupted dequantization.

This is a **partial** revert of #42988: it restores `torch.zeros` for **only** the swizzled `int32` scale allocation. Everything else #42988 changed is intentionally kept (`torch.empty` / removed fill), because those buffers are genuinely safe to leave uninitialized:

- within the same function, the non-swizzled `uint8` branch allocates an **exact-size** buffer `(m, n // 16)` (no padding) whose kernel (`cvt_fp16_to_fp4_sf_major`, row-major `sf_out_rowmajor_u8`) fully covers it;
- the packed-FP8 scale, TurboQuant `attn_out`, and GDN `z_out` buffers are all fully overwritten before use.

So only the one padded buffer that the kernel does not fully initialize is restored to zero-init.

## Symptoms (measured)

For `con1 isl1000 osl1000`, TP4, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`:

- throughput collapse: ~87–93% drop in output-token throughput;
- output degeneration: output sequence length collapses far below the requested 1000 tokens;
- inter-token latency rises ~8–15×.

## Root cause

The fix relies on a narrow, directly-proven claim: the quant kernel leaves some consumer-visible elements of the padded swizzled buffer unwritten. This is proven by the fact that zero-initializing the buffer fully restores correct behavior, only possible if those elements were being read uninitialized. With `torch.zeros` they read a defined `0` (the long-standing pre-#42988 behavior).

## Validation

Single line toggled (`empty` ↔ `zeros`) on the swizzled `int32` allocation; `vllm serve` + `aiperf`, TP4, ISL/OSL=1000/1000. `OSL` below is the average output sequence length (requested 1000), derived from throughput; the derivation is approximate and can land slightly above the 1000 cap, so the meaningful signal is regressed (~65–127) vs. healthy (~870–1040), not the exact value.

**Per-hunk isolation, B300, Llama-3.3-70B, con=1** (proves this one line is necessary and sufficient):

| Configuration                                | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | OSL    |
| -------------------------------------------- | -----------: | -------: | -----: |
| Baseline (#42988 as-is, all `empty`)         |        19.56 |    50.62 |  127.0 |
| Revert **swizzled `int32`** line only        |       135.40 |     7.35 |  873.2 |
| Revert non-swizzled `uint8` line only        |        19.49 |    50.77 |  127.0 |
| Revert fp8-util line only                    |        19.56 |    50.59 |  127.0 |
| Revert all `empty`→`zeros`                   |       162.29 |     6.11 | 1041.4 |

**Before/after, GB300NVL, con=1:**

| Model                | Allocation        | Output tok/s | ITL (ms) | OSL   |
| -------------------- | ----------------- | -----------: | -------: | ----: |
| Llama-3.3-70B (dense)| `empty` (regressed) |        18.39 |    53.99 | 127.0 |
| Llama-3.3-70B (dense)| `zeros` (fixed)     |       143.25 |     6.88 | 997.8 |
| Kimi-K2.5 (1T MoE)   | `empty` (regressed) |        10.16 |    97.61 |  65.8 |
| Kimi-K2.5 (1T MoE)   | `zeros` (fixed)     |       148.28 |     6.58 | 999.6 |

**Concurrency sweep with the fix, GB300NVL**:

| Concurrency | Llama tok/s | Llama OSL | Kimi tok/s | Kimi OSL |
| ----------: | ----------: | --------: | ---------: | -------: |
| 1           |      137.93 |     995.0 |     147.57 |   1000.2 |
| 16          |     2020.14 |    1000.0 |    1047.85 |    999.9 |
| 64          |     7305.73 |     999.7 |    2770.39 |   1000.0 |
| 128         |    11478.84 |     999.8 |    4913.39 |   1000.0 |

Throughput scales monotonically and OSL stays at the full requested length at every concurrency for both models — no degeneration at scale.

##Related issue: 
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/45741

title: [Rust Frontend][Perf] Use dedicated runtime for HTTP/request-processing/ZMQ
author: BugenZhao
body:
Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com><!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

This PR improves Rust frontend responsiveness under high-concurrency workloads with CPU-heavy request preprocessing and busy engine transport paths.

The Rust frontend now separates the main async work into dedicated runtimes:

- HTTP runtime: accepts connections, routes lightweight endpoints, and writes responses.
- Request runtime: runs heavyweight inference/tokenization endpoints through Axum middleware, covering request extraction, validation, chat-template rendering, tokenization, request lowering, and engine submission.
- ZMQ runtime: drives engine-core transport send/receive, output dispatch, abort handling, and coordinator tasks.

This keeps long prompt preprocessing and ZMQ transport work from monopolizing HTTP worker threads, which improves `/health` tail latency and request-side throughput in stress tests.

## Implementation

- Add a request runtime owned by `AppState`, configurable with `VLLM_RS_REQUEST_WORKER_THREADS`.
- Add middleware that offloads heavyweight routes to the request runtime:
  - `/v1/chat/completions`
  - `/v1/completions`
  - `/tokenize`
  - `/inference/v1/generate`
- Add a dedicated ZMQ runtime in `engine-core-client`, configurable with `VLLM_RS_ZMQ_WORKER_THREADS`.
- Run engine sends and background ZMQ loops on the ZMQ runtime.

## Benchmark

- Rust frontend + Rust mock engine

title: [KV Offload] Support packed HMA KV cache layout
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Summary
- add an opt-in `VLLM_USE_PACKED_HMA_KV_CACHE` path for multi-group HMA KV cache packing
- keep the existing DeepSeek V4 packed path unchanged
- register packed HMA offload as one canonical backing tensor with one full-row ref per KV group, preserving the packed topology for CPU offload

## Duplicate-work check
- Checked open PRs for `packed HMA KV cache`, `gpt-oss gemma packed kv cache`, `VLLM_USE_PACKED_HMA_KV_CACHE`, `packed KV cache offloading`, and `hybrid KV cache offload`.

- #44577 is merged and this PR builds on that packed layout support rather than duplicating the DSV4 change.

## Benchmarks
- `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, B300, 128K, `OffloadingConnector`, 2 CPU-hit iterations: packed HMA full-row refs used 1 CPU tensor and averaged ~124.95 ms vs per-slice registration with 12 CPU tensors at ~144.37 ms (~13.5% faster).
- `google/gemma-3-1b-it`, 4K: packed HMA used 1 CPU tensor vs 4 and CPU-hit latency was effectively flat, ~12.23 ms vs ~12.32 ms.

title: [Kernel] TD operand loads for batched MoE GEMM (moe_mmk) on XPU
author: oonyshch
body:
### Purpose
Add a Tensor-Descriptor (TD) operand-load path to `moe_mmk` / `expert_triton_kernel` (the batched MoE expert GEMM) and enable it on XPU. On XPU, masked `tl.load` feeding `tl.dot` bypasses the Xe XMX 2D-block-read path; loading both operands via `tl.make_tensor_descriptor` restores it. Output is bit-identical to the non-TD path.

The batched kernel is the one used by **low-latency Expert-Parallel** dispatch (the batched activation format `[E_local, max_tokens, K]`), so its e2e effect must be measured **in that EP context**, not against the single-GPU fused MoE (a different path, rightly faster when a model fits on one GPU). This addresses the earlier review feedback: the correct comparison is **TD-on vs TD-off on the batched EP path**, which is what this PR touches. (Earlier single-GPU GraniteMoE numbers were misleading and are superseded below.)

Gated by `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD` (auto-on for XPU, opt-in on CUDA sm90+). Stacks under the portable low-latency all-to-all EP backend (#46871).

### Test Plan
- Kernel unit tests: `tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py` (TD vs plain bit-exact, zero-expert
  handling, device enablement, backend selection).
- E2E via `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve` on **2× Intel Arc B70**, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, batched
  Triton EP path (`--all2all-backend naive_low_latency`), bf16, `--enforce-eager`, seed 42.
  Isolates TD by toggling only `VLLM_TRITON_USE_TD`. (`VLLM_MLA_DISABLE=1` — DeepSeek MLA on XPU
  has a separate pre-existing numerics bug unrelated to this kernel.)
- Accuracy: gsm8k on GraniteMoE (standard attention → clean XPU read) confirms TD is neutral.

### Test Result

### Per-kernel microbench
- Arc B70 (E=8, K=N=2048, bf16): TD −89…−91% latency across tokens/expert.
- RTX 5060 / H200: TD −68…−70% (CUDA), gains scale with expert GEMM size; bit-exact.

### E2E on the batched low-latency EP path — 2× Arc B70, DeepSeek-V2-Lite (TD off vs on)

**Saturation (ShareGPT, 500 prompts):**

| metric | TD0 | TD1 | Δ TD1 vs TD0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| output tok/s | 134.2 | 290.6 | **+116%** |
| median TTFT | 27.1 s | 12.0 s | **−56%** |
| median TPOT | 797 ms | 334 ms | **−58%** |

**Single-stream (`--max-concurrency 1`, realistic low-latency regime):**

| metric | TD0 | TD1 | Δ | no-EP default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| median TTFT | 1033 ms | 600 ms | −42% | 427 ms |
| median TPOT | 353 ms | 270 ms | −24% | 124 ms |

### CUDA cross-check (DeepEP low-latency, Qwen3-30B-A3B, 4× H200)
+72% req/s, −53% TPOT with TD on; per-kernel 1.3–6.1× (scales with K/N); bit-identical.
(Logs: `cuda_td_deepep_ll_logs.zip`, attached below in a comment)

### Accuracy (TD is a bit-exact operand-load change)
GraniteMoE gsm8k (8-shot, 200): default 0.500 / TD0 0.480 / TD1 0.470 — flat within noise, matching the model's published ~0.49.

Takeaway: TD is a large, consistent win on the batched EP path it actually touches (+116% throughput, −58% TPOT on 2× Arc B70; +72% req/s on H200), bit-exact, accuracy-neutral, never a regression. 

Full XPU logs:
[pr46340_bench_logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30139331/pr46340_bench_logs.zip)

title: [GDN] Improve kkt kernel of CuteDSL prefill backend
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Purpose This a a follow-up of #43273. In this PR, I only focused on optimizing the matrix inverse pipeline inside the KKT kernel. A quick recap on the KKT kernel timeline This is a bit more detailed than the timeline shown previously in #43273, because the extra steps shown above (`Prepare gate/beta` and `Store Ab/Abg to tmem`) turn out to be the bottleneck! I asked Codex to add some instrumenting code so we can get an actual kernel timeline tcgen05 is so fast that `W MMA + U MMA + next KKT MMA` < `INV warps load and prepare beta/gate`! Furthermore, Ab/Abg preparation looks surprisingly slow, taking around 20-25% the time of inverse logic, which was supposed to be the most expensive. As it turns out again, doing multiplication can be a bottleneck on Blackwell. So how do we overcome it? ### Slow beta/gate preparation Move beta/gate preparations to extra warps! These prep warps can overlap with existing INV warps, and go 1 stage ahead of the INV warps -> when INV warps need beta/gate, those values are already ready in smem buffer -> no waiting ### Slow Ab/Abg prepration after `inverse(I+A)` Currently, we have a clear boundary between doing `inv(I+A)`, and then compute `Ab = inv(I+A) * beta` / `Abg = inv(I+A) * beta * gate`. ``` # current 1. compute inverse for diagonal 16x16 tiles (Newton-Schulz) 2. compute inverse for off-diagonal tiles (block forward-substitution) 3. compute Ab/Abg, and store to tmem ``` This cleanly separates the logic, but not optimal: there is an extra smem roundtrip, and we also unnecessarily store the zeros upper-triangular tiles. Instead, we can fuse Ab/Abg prep with the inverse steps. ``` # new 1. compute inverse for diagonal 16x16 tiles (Newton-Schulz) 1b. while the result is still in registers, compute Ab/Abg and store to tmem 2. compute inverse for off-diagonal tiles (block forward-substitution) 2b. while the result is still in registers, compute Ab/Abg and store to tmem ``` We save the unnecessary Ab/Abg computation for the upper triangular tiles. Before, we have 4x4 16x16 tiles. Now, we only need to compute and store (1+2+3+4) 16x16 Ab/Abg tiles. The new kernel timeline tcgen05 is still mostly idle. We can do pingpong schedule like FlashAttention in the future. ### Other cleanup I also take this opportunity to make small tweaks in the kernels that don't really bring significant changes - Move `elect_sync()` inside the tcgen05 helper functions. From my experience, this gives better codegen, as CuteDSL may generate weird predicated address calculations - Remove swizzled layout for `sA` and `sAi` - Use `TmaInfo` object returnted by `make_tiled_tma_atom` directly, no need to `(atom, tma_tensor, s_layout)` tuples. - Apply `f32x2` math as appropriate using `cutlass.range(vectorize=True)` - Remove adhoc BF16 bit manipulation in favour of built-in PTX like `neg.bf16x2` and `sub.bf16x2` ## Microbenchmarks GB200. FlashInfer as baseline | model_case | input_case | FlashInfer | Old CuteDSL | New CuteDSL | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | Qwen3.6-27B TP1 | 1x8192 | 0.422 ms (1.00x) | 0.369 ms (1.14x) | 0.352 ms (1.20x) | | Qwen3.6-27B TP1 | 1x16384 | 0.714 ms (1.00x) | 0.712 ms (1.00x) | 0.662 ms (1.08x) | | Qwen3.6-27B TP1 | 8x1024 | 0.281 ms (1.00x) | 0.297 ms (0.95x) | 0.271 ms (1.04x) | | Qwen3.6-27B TP1 | 8x2048 | 0.393 ms (1.00x) | 0.561 ms (0.70x) | 0.508 ms (0.77x) | | Qwen3.6-27B TP1 | 8@8192 (mixed) | 0.410 ms (1.00x) | 0.363 ms (1.13x) | 0.336 ms (1.22x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP1 | 1x8192 | 0.426 ms (1.00x) | 0.464 ms (0.92x) | 0.425 ms (1.00x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP1 | 1x16384 | 0.721 ms (1.00x) | 0.912 ms (0.79x) | 0.828 ms (0.87x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP1 | 8x1024 | 0.337 ms (1.00x) | 0.413 ms (0.82x) | 0.371 ms (0.91x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP1 | 8x2048 | 0.483 ms (1.00x) | 0.787 ms (0.61x) | 0.705 ms (0.69x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP1 | 8@8192 (mixed) | 0.463 ms (1.00x) | 0.470 ms (0.98x) | 0.425 ms (1.09x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 | 1x8192 | 0.424 ms (1.00x) | 0.242 ms (1.75x) | 0.243 ms (1.75x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 | 1x16384 | 0.713 ms (1.00x) | 0.437 ms (1.63x) | 0.430 ms (1.66x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 | 8x1024 | 0.175 ms (1.00x) | 0.132 ms (1.33x) | 0.123 ms (1.43x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 | 8x2048 | 0.207 ms (1.00x) | 0.190 ms (1.09x) | 0.183 ms (1.13x) | | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B TP4 | 8@8192 (mixed) | 0.379 ms (1.00x) | 0.220 ms (1.72x) | 0.228 ms (1.67x) | Around 10% improvements for TP1, which is huge considering this is just the KKT kernel (there are also the H and O kernels). For TP4, perf is mostly unchanged. ## E2E testing Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B AIME25 (exact match): 0.9167 8k-1 prefill only, GB200, concurrency 64 Branch | TPGS | TTFT ---|---|--- main | 25938 tok/s | 20.00s this PR | 25964 tok/s | 19.98s Pretty much noise, which is expected I suppose ---
