title: [Frontend] Add reusable TP1 initialized-engine snapshots
author: matteso1
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 MD018 MD041 -->

## Current status (September 21)

H200 acceptance passed on `8971c89708ea7dd0c7c14e34a3ec68d0a832773f`, using the exact image from [CI 89681](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89681) and the unchanged `.buildkite/scripts/initialized-snapshot-e2e.sh`. On the allocated full H200, the test created and inspected a snapshot, restored it, stopped and restarted the same container, then restored it again. Both public completions returned token `12095`, text ` Paris`, and log probability `-0.4242669641971588`, exactly matching the captured oracle.

Independent cleanup confirmed that the recorded processes, test container and both listening ports were gone, the GPU was idle, and the link-remap inventory was unchanged. Temporary files were removed after collecting the receipts; the host's original model cache and pre-existing images were preserved. The run used Qwen3-0.6B FP16, model runner V2 and the agreed privileged Docker setup with `kernel.io_uring_disabled=2`.

The first two attempts stopped before snapshot creation: registry access needed authentication, then the pinned model cache needed three missing repository text files. Both were resolved without changing the PR image or driver. The successful run used a complete, read-only private copy of the cache.

Full [CI 89681](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89681) passed on the H200-tested `8971c89708ea` head. This refresh merges main `382970ee6ca4`; snapshot feature files are unchanged and 82 snapshot tests plus repository checks pass. It also adds an eight-line fixture that fixes a locally reproduced quantization-test fork hang (20 passed in the exact bytecode CI image). [CI 90301](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90301) is validating `f26175fef21b`; the separate MI355 sampling failure also reproduces on main. The H200 acceptance above remains a result for its recorded image.

## Purpose and prior art

RFC #34303 and #37921/#37925 put CUDA checkpoint primitives below CRIU disk persistence. #35934 and #46089 explore related lifecycle and provider shapes, while #52132 keeps the frontend alive during EngineCore L3 sleep. This PR targets a different event: no serving process remains, and a trusted same-host operator restores one prepared Linux x86-64 TP1 engine before HTTP bind.

@simon-mo asked me to split the generic CLI work out of #51360. This PR is standalone: it registers the snapshot command and leaves the other commands on the existing dispatch path. The generated-help work in #54841 is separate and is not a dependency of this PR.

```bash
vllm snapshot create MODEL --snapshot-dir PATH --revision MODEL_SHA [serve args]
vllm snapshot inspect PATH
vllm snapshot restore PATH --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

## The fix

`vllm snapshot create` initializes the engine and records a deterministic one-token oracle. It uses the existing sleep level 2 lifecycle to release model weights and KV cache before CRIU dump. Restore reloads that state before binding HTTP, then reproduces the captured token ID, text, and sampled log probability before returning. A mismatch fails closed.

The public controller orchestrates the snapshot transaction. The private host runtime owns CRIU, PID and session identity, TCP inspection, `io_uring`, GPU inventory, pidfd pinning, link remaps, and rollback. Restore pins the restored tree before reading its PID file. Once process identity verification succeeds, failures terminate and wait for that tree. If verification itself fails, rollback writes an abort marker but does not signal unverified PIDs; surviving children can require operator cleanup if the snapshot server has already exited. The server path reuses the existing API-server construction and sleep level 2 wake sequence.

The manifest is a strict frozen Pydantic model, the child's ready and release markers validate through strict Pydantic wire models beside it, and an identity mismatch names every differing field. Selected environment values are stored as deterministic name-bound fingerprints, not plaintext. API keys and snapshot timeout controls are excluded, and literal API keys and Hugging Face tokens are redacted from recorded engine arguments. The protected CRIU artifact can still contain process secrets and must remain private.

Generated-cache files are not copied, but files the engine holds open from named cache roots are fingerprinted in the manifest, so a cache that rotates between capture and restore fails early and names the changed file instead of producing a permanently broken restore. Thanks to @fuhefei for surfacing the cache-expiry case on H20. The trusted-host port probe is best-effort only; it is not a reservation or listener authentication.

Create requires a quiet process tree. Current Hugging Face hub clients hold pooled connections for the process lifetime, so the documented flow downloads the model in its own step and runs create with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. A refused capture names the offending pid, process, and peer, matching the io_uring diagnostics.

## Measured

The earlier matched large-model campaign used source `5dd888926f`, Qwen3-32B BF16 TP1, and one H100 PCIe 80 GB. Model and generated-cache files were resident; compact artifact files were evicted before each restore.

| Path | Median activation | Samples |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary warm process | 54.7029 s | 3 |
| Snapshot restore | 20.3795 s | 3 |
| Reduction | 34.3234 s, 62.7% | 3 per arm |

The artifact used 5,879,914,496 allocated bytes. The 65,540,298,478-byte model tree remained external. Creation took 78.5275 seconds, n=1, so the measured saving broke even on the third activation. Every accepted trial returned token ID `12095` and text ` Paris`.

## Verified on hardware

Earlier tested head `b375063b51` ran the documented docker quickstart verbatim from scratch on an RTX 4090 Laptop GPU rig: image build with precompiled wheels, `hf download` in 16 seconds, offline create in 60 seconds, restore in 8 seconds, and the restored server returned the exact captured greedy completion, n=1. Running the documented flow end to end during hardening surfaced four issues in it; each was fixed by that tested head. The snapshot runtime installs in an isolated Docker stage that logs `[TIMING] snapshot runtime install` in the build output; the CI build of this head reports the uncached duration.

Older source `e464e2f6ae` built a Linux amd64 image from main `6df7adc17f` on the same rig. Qwen3-0.6B creation took 58.961 seconds, n=1, and produced a 3,565,976,397-byte manifest-reported artifact. The same artifact restored twice in one container across `docker stop` and `docker start`, in 3.233 and 2.931 seconds, n=1 each.

Both public requests returned token ID `12095`, text ` Paris`, and sampled log probability `-0.42565488815307617`, matching the manifest control. Shifting the expected log probability by 10 failed closed in 3.514 seconds, n=1, without publishing a ready server. Final checks found no remaining container, process, listener, GPU process, link remap, or changed `io_uring` state.

These performance measurements retain their tested SHAs. The September 17 H200 run above establishes lifecycle acceptance on its recorded `8971c89708ea` image; its whole-driver duration is not a restore-latency measurement.

## Earlier local verification

At exact head `b375063b51`, on a Linux x86-64 host:

```text
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_launch_cli.py \
  tests/cuda/test_cuda_compatibility_path.py
# 87 passed

uvx pre-commit run --files <all 14 changed files>
# all applicable hooks passed, including Python 3.10 mypy, ShellCheck,
# Docker version validation, and the root lazy-import check
```

The optional H200 job exercises exact image labels, create, inspect, two restores, the public oracle, and final container, PID, GPU-process, listener, and link-remap cleanup.

## Product envelope

- Linux x86-64 with one NVIDIA GPU, TP1, PP1, DP1, and prefill-context parallel size 1. Arm64 images intentionally omit the snapshot runtime.
- Same trusted host and GPU, with matching driver, kernel, Python, PyTorch, installed vLLM, model revision, engine arguments, selected environment, and checkpoint tools.
- Root or passwordless `sudo`, plus a private local artifact that can contain process memory and secrets.
- No external established TCP peer at capture, active `io_uring`, concurrent restore, cross-host migration, GPU relocation, or ordinary-start fallback.
- An immutable remote model revision and stable model, container, and generated-cache paths for the artifact lifetime.
- No power-loss durability guarantee. Publication fsyncs the manifest but does not explicitly flush all captured payload files and directories; recreate the artifact after an unclean host shutdown.

AI assistance was used. I take responsibility for the implementation, compatibility boundary, and measurements.

title: [Kernel] Use Murmur3 RNG for Gumbel sampling
author: freyfwt
body:
## Purpose

Replace the Gumbel sampler's Philox-based uniform generation with a manual Murmur3 x86_32 mixing path keyed by request seed, token position, and vocabulary offset. The goal is to preserve the target sampling distribution while improving RNG resolution and avoiding backend-specific math paths.

Related RFC: #54143.

This is not a duplicate of #47524. That PR keeps Philox and combines more of its output bits to improve uniform resolution; this PR evaluates a different RNG and a backend-independent logarithm path. The existing Philox helpers remain available for rejection sampling.

## Implementation

- Generate fp32 uniforms from the full 32-bit Murmur3 result through two exact 16-bit integer-to-float conversions, avoiding backend-dependent uint32-to-float behavior.
- Generate centered fp64 uniforms from 53 random bits and explicitly keep both endpoints open after fp64 rounding.
- Use a stable degree-8 approximation for `log1p(-u)` in the fp32 winning tail instead of a backend-specific libdevice call.
- Keep draft and target sampling on separate noise streams by salting the token position.
- Add Murmur3 known-answer and fp64 endpoint tests, retain the existing distribution tests, and make output-sensitive API tests deterministic where the RNG stream is not the behavior under test.
- Remove the API-level assumption that parallel completions must randomly finish at different lengths. Staggered child completion is already covered deterministically by the `ParentRequest` unit tests.

The current diff touches the sampler, its GPU tests, and three RNG-sensitive entrypoint tests.

## Compatibility Impact

Seeded non-greedy requests produce a different deterministic token sequence because the random-number stream changes. The intended categorical distribution, public API, logits-cache behavior, greedy path, and kernel launch structure are unchanged.

## Test Plan

- Validate Murmur3 outputs against fixed known answers and verify fp64 uniforms exclude both endpoints.
- Run the existing Gumbel distribution, drafting-stream, and edge-case tests on CUDA and ROCm.
- Run structured-output, reasoning, and parallel-completion entrypoint suites after removing assumptions about a particular seeded random sequence.
- Run repository formatting, lint, type, import, DCO, and policy checks.
- Compare Philox and Murmur3 kernel latency on NVIDIA and Ascend hardware.

## Test Result

- Local commit hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, typos, mypy, SPDX, import, and policy checks.
- Targeted Python 3.12 mypy, `compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed for the final fixes.
- [Buildkite CI #86309](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/86309) reported zero failed selected jobs. The NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI300 basic-correctness lanes passed, as did the selected NVIDIA/AMD entrypoint integration lanes. The aggregate Buildkite status remained open on optional manual gates when this result was recorded.
- Split-16 fp32 reconstruction matched correctly rounded fp32 values for 2,000,000 random uint32 inputs with 0 mismatches.
- Joint RNG checks over `(seed, position, offset)` found no detectable abnormal correlation: token-token Pearson z-scores had mean -0.009, standard deviation 0.998, and maximum absolute z-score 3.90; byte, bit, and serial checks were also within expected statistical noise.
- Sampler-level Monte Carlo tests found no detectable categorical bias after using the full 32-bit source. For vocabulary size 129,280 and 100,000 draws, tail-mass z-scores were -1.18 at logit gap 18 and -1.09 at logit gap 20. The earlier 24-bit path produced -5.89 and -5.16 respectively.
### Model-level serving validation (RTX 5090)

A model-level A/B was run with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (vocab 151,936), Model Runner V2, and seeded non-greedy sampling (`temperature=0.8`, `top_p=0.95`). The exact `gumbel.py` files from base `570735520942` and head `2803c10512dd` were tested in the same fixed runtime (vLLM `0.17.2rc1.dev3682+g426e59f62`, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0).

- Functional smoke: two independent no-prefix-cache runs per revision; every run completed 34/34 HTTP requests. In both head runs, all 16/16 sequential prompt/seed pairs and the seeded `n=4` request reproduced exactly. No empty output, engine error, OOM, or NaN was observed.
- Baseline also reproduced 16/16 sequential prompt/seed pairs, but its seeded `n=4` request was not fully identical in either run.
- Base/head output sequences changed as expected with the RNG stream replacement: only 1/16 first-pass completions matched exactly.
- Serving A/B: 5 runs per revision, 128 requests/run, 256 input + 128 output tokens, concurrency 32, fixed request seed, and `ignore_eos`; 640/640 requests succeeded for each revision.

| Metric (median of 5 run-level values) | Baseline | Murmur3 head | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Request throughput (req/s) | 49.22 | 51.26 | +4.15% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 6,299.86 | 6,561.30 | +4.15% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 71.40 | 75.99 | +6.43% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 4.524 | 4.291 | -5.15% |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 4.527 | 4.311 | -4.79% |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 91.21 | 103.83 | +13.84% |
| P99 TPOT (ms) | 6.817 | 5.720 | -16.09% |
| P99 ITL (ms) | 8.880 | 8.626 | -2.86% |

The host was shared with an unrelated 8-GPU workload (per-run output-throughput CV: 11.5% baseline, 7.4% head), so these results are used as a **no-material-regression check**, not as a clean speedup claim.

Method note: the available runtime image predates the `is_drafting` call-site update. Both variants therefore used the same one-line `is_drafting=False` harness adapter. This model-level run validates the normal non-drafting path; drafting/speculative behavior is outside its scope.

## Performance

The following kernel microbenchmarks were collected during development on 2026-08-08. They predate the final fp32-uniform, logarithm, and fp64-endpoint changes in the current head, so they demonstrate cross-backend feasibility but are not presented as final-head performance numbers. They measure kernel latency rather than end-to-end serving performance, and absolute latency should not be compared across devices.

### NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090

The recorded run used 10 warmups and 100 measured rounds.

| Shape | Philox (ms) | Murmur3 (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x 20 | 0.0082 | 0.0080 | 1.02x |
| 1 x 151,936 | 0.0100 | 0.0100 | 1.00x |
| 8 x 151,936 | 0.0142 | 0.0125 | 1.13x |
| 64 x 151,936 | 0.0408 | 0.0301 | 1.35x |
| 128 x 163,840 | 0.0755 | 0.0508 | 1.49x |
| 128 x 262,144 | 0.1213 | 0.0946 | 1.28x |

### Ascend A3

The benchmark recorded both full-candidate and 20-candidate modes where applicable.

| Shape | Candidates | Philox (ms) | Murmur3 (ms) | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x 20 | all | 0.3334 | 0.0395 | 8.44x |
| 1 x 151,936 | all | 1.2781 | 0.0479 | 26.68x |
| 1 x 151,936 | 20 | 1.2874 | 0.0567 | 22.71x |
| 8 x 151,936 | all | 9.4195 | 0.1324 | 71.14x |
| 8 x 151,936 | 20 | 9.4190 | 0.1324 | 71.14x |
| 64 x 151,936 | all | 74.8993 | 0.8550 | 87.60x |
| 64 x 151,936 | 20 | 74.9010 | 0.8549 | 87.61x |
| 128 x 163,840 | all | 160.4593 | 1.7986 | 89.21x |
| 128 x 163,840 | 20 | 160.4597 | 1.7982 | 89.23x |

A current-head rerun with the exact benchmark command, dtype, synchronization method, and software versions is still needed before treating these as reproducible final performance claims.

## Documentation

No documentation change is needed because this is an internal kernel implementation change with no API or configuration changes.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation and PR description and is attributed in the commits. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line and validating the change end to end.

title: [Quantization] Support online quantization with partially pre-quantized checkpoints
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

Allow online quantization on the unquantized `linear` or `moe` (or fine-grained `targets`) portions of a partially pre-quantized checkpoint **from ANY `quant_method` (Quark, ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, etc.)**. 

The original `quant_method` remains responsible for its pre-quantized layers, the composed config applies the requested online method only when the checkpoint returns an unquantized method.

Example use cases:
- Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49313 that attempts to do the same for `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` that quantizes only the MOE layers.
- Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48983 that attempts to do the same with modelopt checkpoint
- Take e.g. [`nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4) (modelopt checkpoint) or [`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4) (quark checkpoint) that apply non-shared MOE expert only quantization, and quantize additional layers as needed (for evaluation or optimization purposes
- Relax the need to release several models with different preset pre-quantized layers / different ignore lists).
- Eventually, support `shared_experts` online quantization +fusion (not in this PR, see draft https://github.com/fxmarty-amd/vllm/pull/6)

This PR will work nicely with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51285 once it is merged.

Implementation details:

- Online quantization is stored as `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config`. `QuantizationConfig.get_effective_quant_method` **resolves the global quant method, including both the base checkpoint quant method and the online quant method**. The original `QuantizationConfig` subclass instantiation is preserved (e.g. `Fp8Config`), so **model developers do not need to be aware of this online quantization composition** (see examples below).
- Selected layers for `online` that are already pre-quantized fail clearly instead of being silently replaced.
- Activation-only overrides remain owned by the original checkpoint quantizer
- `quantization_config.ignore` excludes applies only to `online`, as done currently on `main`.

Preserving the original checkpoint config type is required for existing model-specific behavior:

- Quark Qwen3Next shared-expert fusion reads Quark exclusion metadata and controls fusion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L81-L98 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_next.py#L154-L162
- Kimi K2.5 checks for `CompressedTensorsConfig` before quantizing its multimodal projector: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/kimi_k25.py#L393-L396
- GLM4.1V selects a compressed-tensors-specific QKV prefix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/glm4_1v.py#L303-L308
- Qianfan OCR applies `Fp8Config` visual-layer safety exclusions: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4f76c8ad9d8ec06e91ac9c84895e07a1913d7726/vllm/model_executor/models/qianfan_ocr.py#L69-L92

Behavior change from `main`: `--quantization-config` can now be used with a checkpoint `quant_method` for online weight composition. A request that selects an already pre-quantized layer now fails clearly instead of replacing the checkpoint method.

Left to do:

- [ ] Real model testing.
- [ ] Is `--quantization-config` usage for different `quant_method` (base + online) ok?
- [ ] Is `QuantizationConfig.online_quant_config` ok?

## Test Plan

Added tests in

- `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_compatibility -vvvvv -s`
- `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k test_online_prequantized_checkpoint_selected_layer_fails -vvvvv -s`
- `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k tinysmokeqwen3moe -vvvvv -s`

The tests cover Quark, ModelOpt, and compressed-tensors dispatch; activation-only overrides; online ignore retaining checkpoint quantization; and real tiny compressed-tensors checkpoint conflicts for selected linear and MoE layers.

## Test Result

Passes on MI355.

## Alternative implementation

An alternative could be to have `ComposedQuantizationConfig` holding both the base config and online config. It does not work well due the reasons above, and due to the requirement to hack `__getattr__`, etc. in this case.

title: [Perf] Narrow DeepSeek V3.2 eager CUDA graph region
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Purpose

The portable DeepSeek-V3.2 attention path currently decorates the entire fused attention method with `eager_break_during_capture`. Only the sparse indexer and backend `forward_mqa` call require that eager boundary, so query preparation, fused norm/RoPE, and other graph-safe work are replayed as direct launches on every layer.

This change:

- inlines the graph-safe part of `_fused_attention` into `forward`;
- narrows the eager region to `_sparse_indexer_and_attn`;
- keeps the UV projection in the eager region so it can consume the backend-owned attention output without an extra copy;
- preserves the existing broad eager path for the ROCm subclass.

A one-request kernel trace showed 333 fewer direct launches while retaining 79 CUDA graph launches. The launches moved into graphs were 78 fused norm/RoPE kernels, 78 W_UK BMMs, 99 query/indexer GEMMs, and 78 fused-Q kernels.

### Non-duplication

I searched open PRs for DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM CUDA graph, sparse-indexer, and `eager_break_during_capture` changes. Related PRs such as #50005 (NVIDIA DCP correctness), #47355 (indexer side-stream overlap), and #47335 (ROCm fused indexer-Q) address different paths or concerns. None narrows the eager-break boundary in the portable DeepSeek-V3.2 attention implementation.

## Test Plan

- Run the focused breakable-CUDA-graph tests.
- Run all applicable pre-commit hooks on both changed files.
- Serve GLM-5.2-NVFP4 with dummy weights through the portable model override and Rust frontend using TP4/EP4, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching disabled, and the default CUDA graph mode.
- Measure TTFT with 256 sequential requests after 8 warmups, each with an 8-token prompt and one output token.
- Profile the kernel launch trace.
- Compare the no-copy implementation against an alternative that copies the backend attention output into a static buffer and captures the UV BMM.

## Test Result

```text
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py -q
14 passed, 18 warnings in 5.90s

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v32/attention.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/rocm.py
All applicable hooks passed.
```

GLM-5.2 TTFT, Rust frontend, dummy weights, TP4/EP4, concurrency 1, prefix caching disabled:

| Variant | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | p99 TTFT | Throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Current main | 57.42 ms | 56.99 ms | 60.89 ms | 17.39 req/s |
| This change | 28.72 ms | 28.65 ms | 30.76 ms | 34.74 req/s |

All 256 requests completed successfully in both runs.

An explicit PIECEWISE-only comparison found that copying the attention output and capturing the UV BMM was another 7.43% faster than the no-copy form (26.51 ms versus 28.64 ms mean TTFT). However, that variant failed with OOM during the FULL capture phase of the default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` initialization. This PR retains the no-copy form, which successfully initializes in the default mode and does not require backend output-buffer support.

The refactor does not change the attention equations or checkpoint loading, so no model-quality evaluation was required.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, kernel-trace analysis, benchmarking, validation orchestration, and drafting this description. The human submitter must review every changed line and be able to explain and defend the eager-boundary and backend-output trade-offs before marking this PR ready for review.

---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR is described.
- [x] The test plan is provided.
- [x] The test results and before/after comparison are provided.
- [x] No documentation update is needed for this internal execution-path refactor.
</details>

title: [ROCm][DSV4] Preserve native MXFP4 TP8 shard allocation
author: Fangzhou-Ai
body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4 has a 3072-wide routed-expert intermediate, so effective MoE TP8
owns a native 384-wide MXFP4 shard. The generic ROCm allocation path rounded
that shard to 512 before parameter allocation and checkpoint loading. This was
physical padding rather than failed checkpoint sharding, and it inflated the
routed-expert allocation by 33%.

The rounding rule now lives in the generic MXFP4 oracle beside the existing
Kimi-K3 special case:

- the generic `Mxfp4MoEMethod` passes activation to the rounding oracle;
- AITER BF16/SiLU uses its 128-aligned layout regardless of model or routing
  method, keeping native shards such as I384 at TP8;
- every other activation and backend retains its existing alignment;
- no AMD-specific `RoutedExperts` subclass, quantization method, file, or model
  wiring is needed;
- a focused regression test covers the native I384 allocation.

EP checkpoint loading and expert mapping are unchanged.

## Memory validation

The 64-file checkpoint contains 805.33 GiB of safetensors: 778.148 GiB of
routed-expert tensors and 27.171 GiB of tensors replicated under DPA. The
header-derived per-rank payload for an eight-way routed-expert shard is:

```text
778.148 / 8 + 27.171 = 124.439 GiB/rank
```

Measured with the same no-prefix TP1 x DP8, EP-off configuration on 8x gfx950:

| Revision | Routed layout/rank | Model/rank | KV/rank | KV tokens/rank |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Parent `821717118f` | 384 experts x physical I512 | 156.45 GiB | 39.31 GiB | 2,859,796 |
| This change | 384 experts x native I384 | 125.20 GiB | 71.85 GiB | 5,226,632 |

The change saves 31.25 GiB of model memory per rank, increases available KV by
32.54 GiB, and increases KV-token capacity by 82.76%. The I384 model allocation
is within 0.61% of the checkpoint-header prediction.

EP8 is intentionally unchanged. A separate EP8 validation loaded 48 of 384
full-width I3072 experts per rank and measured 124.61 GiB model memory, 69.79
GiB KV, and 5,076,613 KV tokens per rank.

vLLM still reserves total memory according to `gpu_memory_utilization`; the
recovered model memory becomes KV capacity rather than reducing the final
`rocm-smi` allocation. The W2 E8M0 scale columns retain their separate 12-to-16
safety padding.

## 8K/1K performance

Paired fresh-server C64 runs used `dsv4_rocm_bench/run_inferencex_8k1k.sh`
with prefix caching disabled, ISL 8192, OSL 1024, random range ratio 0.8, 128
warmups, and 384 measured requests. Both runs completed 384/384 with identical
input/output length arrays and exact totals of 2,826,122 input and 356,155
output tokens. Neither run had a failed request or server error.

| Metric | Parent I512 | Native I384 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Duration | 619.83 s | 603.90 s | -2.57% |
| Output throughput | 574.60 tok/s | 589.75 tok/s | +2.64% |
| Total throughput | 5,134.13 tok/s | 5,269.50 tok/s | +2.64% |
| Median TTFT | 1,395.61 ms | 1,391.15 ms | -0.32% |
| P90 TTFT | 8,439.19 ms | 8,535.07 ms | +1.14% |
| Median TPOT | 113.08 ms | 110.00 ms | -2.72% |
| P90 TPOT | 126.59 ms | 122.33 ms | -3.37% |
| Median E2E | 105.59 s | 103.70 s | -1.79% |
| P90 E2E | 125.97 s | 122.76 s | -2.55% |

This passes the predeclared non-regression gates of at least 95% throughput and
no more than 10% median/P90 TPOT or E2E regression.

### Additional TP8 concurrency sweep

A further InferenceX-aligned TP8/DP1 sweep used the same 8K/1K random workload,
with prefix caching disabled, random range ratio 0.8, 2x-concurrency warmups,
and 10x-concurrency measured requests. Every paired run completed all requests
with identical input/output length arrays and token totals.

#### Reproduction commands

The equivalent expanded server command used for both arms was:

```bash
cd /tmp
unset PYTHONPATH VIRTUAL_ENV
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1
export FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR=vllm/.venv/cache/flydsl
mkdir -p "$FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR"

vllm/.venv/bin/vllm serve \
  /shared_nfs/huggingface_models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --port 8888 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --async-scheduling \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --moe-backend aiter \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'
```

No explicit `--max-model-len`, `--max-num-seqs`, or
`--max-num-batched-tokens` override was used. The concurrency sweep used:

```bash
cd /tmp
unset PYTHONPATH VIRTUAL_ENV
OUTDIR=/tmp/dsv4_8k1k_results
mkdir -p "$OUTDIR"

for CONC in 1 4 16 64; do
  vllm/.venv/bin/python \
    InferenceX/utils/bench_serving/benchmark_serving.py \
    --model /shared_nfs/huggingface_models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \

| Concurrency | Requests/arm | Parent I512 total tok/s | Native I384 total tok/s | Throughput | Mean TPOT change | Mean E2E change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

The sweep shows a marginal, consistent gain at concurrency 1-16 and a clearer
gain at concurrency 64. TTFT was mixed at lower concurrency, while mean TTFT at
concurrency 64 improved from 1,945.50 ms to 1,689.19 ms (-13.17%).

## Agentic C64 prefix-cache performance

Paired fresh-server, one-hour C64 agentic runs used TP1 x DP8 with EP off,
prefix caching enabled, consistent-hash session affinity, a 600-second cache
pressure warmup, `VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=32768`, and maximum
context 1,048,576. Both temporary test worktrees also carried the already
merged packed-KV zeroing fix #50276. It was applied identically to both arms,
is already present on upstream `main`, and is not part of this PR.

| Metric | Parent I512 | Native I384 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 1,370 | 2,020 | +47.45% |
| Request throughput | 0.3764 req/s | 0.5549 req/s | +47.45% |
| Input throughput | 47,525.70 tok/s | 63,733.23 tok/s | +34.10% |
| Output throughput | 282.88 tok/s | 429.77 tok/s | +51.92% |
| Total throughput | 47,808.59 tok/s | 64,163.00 tok/s | +34.21% |
| Mean TTFT | 4,430.35 ms | 2,679.73 ms | -39.51% |
| Mean TPOT / ITL | 242.82 ms | 180.69 ms | -25.59% |
| Median TPOT / ITL | 171.67 ms | 167.23 ms | -2.59% |
| P90 TPOT / ITL | 340.25 ms | 239.54 ms | -29.60% |
| P99 TPOT / ITL | 2,041.13 ms | 539.81 ms | -73.55% |
| Mean E2E latency | 183.43 s | 137.24 s | -25.18% |
| P90 E2E latency | 434.07 s | 310.45 s | -28.48% |
| Actual prefix-cache hit | 93.82% | 95.79% | +1.97 pp |
| Limiting-rank KV avg / peak | 60.62% / 80.74% | 27.51% / 43.68% | lower |

AIPerf exports TPOT under `inter_token_latency`; it uses the standard
per-request formula `(E2E - TTFT) / (output tokens - 1)`.

The native-I384 arm completed 2,020 profiling requests with zero errors. The
57 requests still in flight at the fixed duration boundary were normal teardown
cancellations and were excluded from the profile. The theoretical trace hit
rate was 97.24% on the parent and 96.69% on I384 because the completed-request
mix differs in a duration-based run; the measured server hit rate nevertheless
improved by 1.97 percentage points.

AIPerf emitted generic counter-reset warnings while exporting warmup metrics.
The warned deltas match the warmup series, not profiling. Server and router logs
show exactly eight one-time starts and no restart, VM fault, OOM, worker death,
engine death, or HTTP 5xx response.

This paired test demonstrates a large end-to-end improvement from the change.
It does not isolate the contribution of additional KV capacity from the reduced
physical MoE width because both are direct effects of removing I512 padding.

## Checkpoint compatibility

Normal Hugging Face/Quark checkpoint loading is unchanged. Existing vLLM
`sharded_state` snapshots whose AITER BF16/SiLU tensors used the generic ROCm
256-alignment must be regenerated when the physical shape changes. For DSV4
TP8, this means regenerating snapshots that stored I512 for the new I384
allocation.

## Duplicate-work check

The required open-PR searches were rerun immediately before submission and
found no functional duplicate:

- #46201 changes gpt-oss runtime pad deltas, not resident DSV4 MXFP4 tensor
  allocation.
- #48728 is unmerged FHMoE work and is outside this PR's scope; this change
  only adjusts the currently merged AITER BF16/SiLU allocation policy.
- #50928 changes Kimi-K3 model-level shard sizing, not DSV4 backend alignment.
- #50597 adds the adjacent AITER/SiTU Kimi-K3 128-alignment rule. This
  change extends the same backend alignment policy to SiLU without a model or
  routing-method special case.
- #51217 generalizes masked activation for padded DeepEP/Humming layouts; it
  does not change MXFP4 parameter shapes or DSV4 checkpoint allocation.

## Tests

# all hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, Python 3.10 mypy, SPDX,

```

## Model evaluation

Full 1,319-sample, 5-shot GSM8K on the fresh AMD-local effective-TP8 build,
with concurrency 64, temperature 0, `reasoning_effort=none`, maximum context
9472, maximum output 2048, and no sample limit:

- strict exact match: **0.962092 +/- 0.005260**;
- flexible extract: **0.961334 +/- 0.005311**;

- no server traceback, OOM, engine death, HTTP 4xx, or HTTP 5xx marker.

title: [Core] Reject new requests while generation is paused
author: aoshen02
body:
Addresses the second problem in #51476. Redesigned per @hao-aaron's review: the engine, not each frontend, is the source of truth for pause admission.

Builds on #59559, now merged.

## Purpose

`pause_generation(mode="abort"|"wait")` and `sleep()` treat the pause as a generation boundary, but requests arriving afterwards were silently queued in the paused engine and then served after resume, under the new weights.

## Contract

- Once `pause_generation(abort|wait)` returns, and until `resume_generation()` returns, new requests from **every** API server sharing the engine fail with `EnginePausedError` (HTTP 503, retryable). `keep` still accepts and queues them.
- A request racing the pause call itself may be rejected or treated as in-flight. It never hangs and never leaves residue.
- A paused engine (`abort`/`wait`) accepts no input except KV-transfer cleanup markers. A streaming-input session's next input is rejected the same way, which ends the session in the engine and on the client.

## Change

- **Engine admission.** `_reject_add_while_paused` runs next to `_reject_add_in_shutdown`, before `add_request`, so a rejected add never reaches the scheduler or DP wave state. It rejects only in `PAUSED_NEW` (abort/wait), and lets `abort_immediately` markers through so P/D KV cleanup still runs. The rejection also ends any open streaming session under the rejected id, since the client treats a rejected id as finished. The busy loop handles ADDs and pause/resume serially, so no lock is needed.
- **Surfacing.** New `FinishReason.PAUSED`. `OutputProcessor` finishes the rejected child like any finished request and raises `EnginePausedError` (a `GracefulHTTPError`, 503) to its caller. `generate` then aborts the request, reclaiming `n>1` siblings; it only does so after the fan-out is fully sent, so no child can slip in untracked after a resume. The Rust frontend maps it to a 503 (`engine_paused`) in `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and `/inference/v1/generate`, and to `UNAVAILABLE` over gRPC.
- **Rejected streaming and pooling requests.** A rejected streaming-input session stops taking input (its input task is cancelled), whoever reads its collector, and any chunk its input task sent after the rejection is aborted in the engine. Under DP load balancing that abort follows main's `streaming_reqs` routing (#58942), so an open session's abort reaches every engine even after the rejection retired its route. A rejected pooling request no longer hits a generation-only assert: `AsyncLLM.encode` raises `EnginePausedError`, and the sync `LLMEngine` over multiprocessing gets an empty result.
- **DP.** With rejection alone, the frontend's `FIRST_REQ` for a rejected request would leave it believing a wave was running, and the first request after resume hung in the DP collective (Python and standalone Rust frontends alike). #59559 removed the frontend wake altogether: engines alone start waves, so this PR needs no DP-specific change.
The previous revision's client-side admission flag, control-plane lock and reopen logic are removed.

The scheduler is not touched, and `ABORT` handling and sleep/resume behave as on main.

## Known limitations

- `wait` behaves as on main for requests admitted before the pause: running ones finish, but ones still queued (or preempted during the drain) stay queued and run after resume. Draining them too needs a scheduler change, left to a follow-up PR on top of this one.
- `stream=true` HTTP requests receive the 503 as an SSE error chunk, because the rejection arrives after the response has started.
- The sync `LLMEngine` over multiprocessing returns `finish_reason="paused"` rather than raising. The in-process engine (`VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`) has no API server in front of it and still queues requests while paused, as on main.
- Closing a streaming-input session's input while paused: an idle session closes normally (the client completes it and the engine ends it). A session closed while its chunk is still running under `wait` fails with a 503 rather than finishing that chunk.
- As on main, `wait` with `clear_cache=True` fails the cache reset while an idle streaming session holds KV.

## Test Plan

- `test_engine_core.py`: engine-side rejection per pause state ends any open session under the rejected id, and KV cleanup markers pass.
- `test_output_processor.py`: a paused rejection finishes cleanly for generate and pooling, sync and async, and stops a streaming session's input.
- `test_async_llm.py`: admission per mode through a direct collector (`n=2`, no residue, `keep` proven to reach the paused engine); a pause mid `n>1` fan-out reclaims a sibling the pause left queued.
- `test_async_llm_dp.py`: the late-request drain tests also assert rejection and no residue, and that the next request after resume completes.
- `test_pause_multi_frontend.py` (new): with `--api-server-count 2`, all 32 requests after `/pause` get 503 and all succeed after `/resume`.
- Rust `routes/tests.rs`: a paused rejection is an `engine_paused` error on every route that maps it: a 503 from `/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` and non-streaming `/inference/v1/generate`, and an SSE error from streaming `/inference/v1/generate`.

## Test Result

All runs inside `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (af7f9488c) with the PR files bind-mounted, `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` / `ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b`, on H200. GPUs were shared with another job; a test that failed at engine start-up on memory was rerun alone.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| New unit tests (engine core, output processor, DP LB client, plus #59559's wave announce; run before the DP LB abort test was dropped for main's #58942 routing) | 14 passed |
| Pause tests in `test_async_llm.py` | 10 passed |
| HTTP: multi-frontend + RLHF pause lifecycle (MRV1/MRV2 × abort/wait/keep) | 7 passed |
| `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_output_processor.py`, `admission_control`, `streaming_input/` | 306 passed (plus the 4 above); 9 fail identically without this PR or need >1 GPU |
| Full `test_async_llm.py`, streaming-input e2e, RLHF suite | 55 passed; 7 are the vision model failing engine init under the shared-GPU memory cap |
| Full `test_async_llm_dp.py`, mp + ray (incl. #59559's repro) | 28 passed, 4 skipped |
| DP=2 MoE, `--api-server-count 2`: six pause/resume cycles (abort/wait/keep) under load, then sleep/wake | rejected while paused, all served after resume |
| Rust `vllm-engine-core-client` and `vllm-server` | 132 and 469 passed |
| `vllm-rs serve` (standalone and bootstrapped) + DP (MoE, 2 ranks): request rejected while paused, then resume | next request completes |

Mutation checks: reverting only the same-id session end at the gate, the client-side streaming end, or the `generate` sibling abort makes its test fail; breaking the `Paused` mapping in any one of the four Rust route cases fails the Rust route test.

## Essential Elements

- Not a duplicate: supersedes this PR's earlier client-side design. #51487 is the conservative counterpart.
- Control-plane and scheduling only, no effect on model output; no eval run.
- AI assistance was used (Claude, with Codex, Kimi K3 and Claude Fable as independent adversarial reviewers). The submitter reviewed every changed line and the runs above.

title: [Perf] Launch the top-k/top-p Triton sampler kernel with 8 warps
author: BabyDrangoner
body:
## Purpose

`_topk_topp_kernel` (the Qrita sampler kernel from #42191) runs one program per logits row, and each program serially sweeps the whole vocab row in `BLOCK_SIZE=8192` tiles. Triton's default `num_warps=4` leaves an 8192-wide fp32 tile at 16 elements per lane, so per-tile latency — which directly bounds kernel latency — is warp-starved. This kernel is on the hot path for seeded / per-request-generator sampling on CUDA (FlashInfer rejects per-request generators): on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 batch-16 decode it was the single largest non-GEMM kernel per step.

This PR launches the kernel with `num_warps=8` on CUDA (ROCm keeps the default: 64-wide wavefronts, no hardware to measure; CPU/XPU untouched).

## Results

Swept vocab {32000, 50257, 151936} × batch {8…256} × {k-only, p-only, k+p} on two architectures, fp32 logits, k=20/p=0.95, median of 30 iters:

| | RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) | H20 (SM90) |
|---|---|---|
| combinations faster | 36/36 | 54/54 |
| speedup range | 1.2–1.5x | 1.02–1.85x (mean 1.37x) |
| regressions | none | none |
| e2e | `_topk_topp_kernel` 305.8 → 165.9 µs/step (1.84x) on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 batch-16 seeded decode | `TopKTopPSampler` op 1.16–1.24x; sampled token ids identical in 128/128 seeded draws |

Sample rows (SM120 / SM90, k+p):

| vocab | batch | 4 warps | 8 warps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 151936 | 64 | 218.8 / 236.0 µs | 154.2 / 145.0 µs |
| 151936 | 256 | 698.4 / 963.3 µs | 526.1 / 582.3 µs |
| 32000 | 256 | 146.3 / 237.4 µs | 110.8 / 174.7 µs |

`BLOCK_SIZE` sweeps (4k/8k/16k) on both arches confirmed 8192 stays the right tile size; only the warp count was off. Why 8 and not 16: on SM120, 16 warps ties on 151k vocab and loses on 32k; on H20, 16 wins 9 of 12 points by up to 11%. 8 is the safe uniform pick on both — happy to make it arch-conditional if preferred.

## Correctness

- top-k and top-k+top-p masks: bitwise identical between 4 and 8 warps on both arches (36/36 and 162/162 cases).
- pure top-p: rare pivot-boundary flips (2/36 single-token on SM120; up to 28 tokens in the worst H20 case). Against a float64 nucleus reference, 8 warps is no less accurate than 4 — both sit at the same ~1e-5 kept-mass distance that predates this PR.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
```

## Test Result

Green on both boxes, identical baseline vs patched: 129 passed / 2 skipped (SM120), 135 passed / 2 skipped (H20).

(Correction: this description previously reported 7 `TestFlashInferDistributionMatch` failures as pre-existing FlashInfer issues — they were just missing `scipy` on the test box. All 7 pass with scipy installed.)

title: [Bugfix] Make DSV4 sparse MLA work end-to-end for plain decode, MTP, and DSpark
author: lucifer1004
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 could not run reliably through the SM120 sparse MLA backend. This fixes the seven defects that blocked it across all three decode modes -- plain decode, MTP, and DSpark -- verified end-to-end on 8xRTX PRO 6000 Blackwell across in-flight batching and prefill/decode disaggregation.

Commits 1-5 unblock DSpark. Commits 6-7 fix a hang that is **not** DSpark-specific: it strands any MTP (`next_n > 1`) server on this backend once the batch drains, and is a pre-existing defect on `main` rather than a regression from this PR. It is filed as #51593, with the full root-cause analysis in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51593#issuecomment-5237934676).

## Why this is not a duplicate

This consolidates #51042 after coordination with the maintainers (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51042#issuecomment-5230492529). @ilmarkov is `Co-authored-by` on the SWA-width commit, whose `amd/rocm.py` hunk and `decode_swa_width` field are his work. Two deliberate design differences are described in that comment.

Duplicate checks run for `dspark`, `sparse MLA SWA width`, `mxfp4 gemm1_alpha`, and `deepseek v4 expert placement`; no other open PR covers the remaining four commits.

For commits 6-7, checks run for `persistent_topk`, `indexer seq_lens spec decode`, and `51593 in:body`. Two open PRs are adjacent but do not overlap:

- **#43970** (MLA indexer / MTP) touches the same two files. Its "drop padded MTP decode slots" applies to the variable-length flatten branch, which computes `seq_len - decode_len` = `0 - 0` = `0` and is already safe. The uniform and native spec-decode paths that produce the negative length are untouched by it. The two changes are complementary and do not conflict.
- **#49139** fixes a different bug in `persistent_topk.cuh` (radix histogram reuse after short rows). Worth flagging the interaction: its precondition is a CTA group processing rows that cross `RADIX_THRESHOLD`, and the out-of-range lengths fixed here cause exactly that spuriously. That PR is still needed for genuinely long rows.

## What is fixed

1. **SWA widths** — non-causal draft batches allocate `decode_swa_indices` wider than `window_size`, but the FlashInfer DSV4 path reshaped with `window_size` and crashed the draft. The dense width is now carried on the metadata. The non-causal width pads to a multiple of 64 (192 for the K=5 shape: 128 sliding-window + 5 draft entries) rather than 128 (256), matching the kernel's 64-entry tile; both dispatch after flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4380, and 192 measures 13-16% faster at >=8 tokens.

2. **Workspace lanes** — the DSpark target and draft CUDA graphs retain workspace views concurrently, so one buffer per ubatch let a resize for one orphan the other's live tensor. The second lane is allocated only for V2 DSpark.

3. **Graph replay and draft KV** — `sample_idx_mapping` was zero-filled, so capture executed padding rows that scattered into request slot 0; captured backbone outputs could be freed before replay read their storage; draft KV could be written into physical block 0, the null block. Draft sampling also moves to a disjoint Philox counter range, since the rejection sampler keys both its acceptance uniform and its recovery Gumbel noise by token position.

4. **MXFP4 SwiGLU parameters** — `FlashInferExperts` injected the GPT-OSS activation constants (`gemm1_alpha=1.702`, `gemm1_beta=1.0`, `gemm1_clamp_limit=7.0`) for every mxfp4 weight dtype. DeepSeek V4 uses this path under `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, so its SwiGLU was evaluated with GPT-OSS constants and generation collapsed. GPT-OSS is unaffected: `GptOssMxfp4MoEMethod` supplies the same constants through its quant config, which the added test pins.

5. **SM120 gate** — a FlashInfer build can expose the sparse MLA decode API without carrying the DSV4 specialization a configuration needs. That now fails at model init with the required `(num_q_heads, top_k)` shape instead of an opaque kernel launch failure at the first decode.

6. **Negative indexer context lengths under MTP** — padded decode slots carry `seq_len == 0`, and with `next_n > 1` both spec-decode paths computed a negative per-token context length for the first token of each padded request (`0 - 2 + 0 + 1 = -1`). The sparse-MLA top-k kernels consume `lengths` as `uint32`, so `-1` is read as ~4.29e9. Clamped at 0 in both paths, matching the variable-length path which already yields `0`. With `next_n == 1` the expression collapses to `seq_len`, which is why plain decode never hit this.

7. **Top-k kernels hardened against out-of-range lengths** — `persistent_topk_kernel` cast `lengths` to `uint32` *before* testing `RADIX_THRESHOLD`, so the bogus ~4.29e9 forced the row onto the multi-CTA radix path. Because the `cta_in_group != 0` early exit is decided from the host-side `max_seq_len` while the per-row branch reads device memory, the two disagreed and stranded the group leader on the inter-CTA barrier forever — the kernel never retired, the async output-copy event never fired, and the engine hung waiting for a response that was never sent. The row length is now clamped to `min(stride, max_seq_len)` before any decision, which also removes an out-of-bounds read into the next row. `cooperative_topk` compares signed (so it cannot hang) but then casts to `uint32`, emitting indices `0..TopK-1` instead of `-1` padding; clamped as well.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, gsm8k `n=1319`:

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract | acceptance | FlashInfer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| target-only, TP4 | 0.9454 | 0.9454 | — | main @ 7f614b86 |
| DSpark, TP4 | 0.9477 | 0.9477 | 65.5% | main @ 7f614b86 |
| DSpark, TP4+EP4 | 0.9462 | 0.9462 | 67.1% | dc963cc0 |
| DSpark + P/D (mooncake) | 0.9492 | 0.9500 | — | dc963cc0 |

Standard rejection sampling is distribution-preserving, and DSpark lands 0.0023 from target-only against a difference-stderr of ~0.009 (0.26 sigma), on the same checkpoint and the same tree.

MTP on the base checkpoint (`num_nextn_predict_layers = 1`), the configuration that #51593 hangs on, gsm8k `n=1319`:

| configuration | strict-match |
| --- | --- |
| MTP, TP4 (commits 6-7 applied) | 0.9477 |

That sits inside the 0.9454-0.9492 band spanned by the target-only and DSpark rows above, on the same checkpoint and tree, so the clamp does not move accuracy. No unfixed baseline is quoted for this row: without commits 6-7 the same server wedges under the drain reproducer within 30-180 s (see Test plan), and I did not obtain a clean unfixed eval run to compare against.

Isolating fix 4 — identical configuration with only that commit removed:

| configuration | strict-match | flexible-extract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target-only, TP4 | 0.0000 | 0.0220 |
| DSpark, TP4 | 0.0000 | 0.0174 |

The TP4 pair was measured on both FlashInfer revisions with no significant change (DSpark 0.9454 -> 0.9477, target-only 0.9462 -> 0.9454), so the two rows measured on the earlier revision are directly comparable.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
       tests/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/test_utils.py \
       tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
       tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py \
       tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py
```

Result: **71 passed, 141 skipped**.

For commits 6-7, a drain-shaped reproducer (waves of concurrent completions that retire unevenly, wedging the unfixed build in 30-180 s) against `deepseek-v4-flash` with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`, TP4:

| build | runs | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unfixed | — | hangs within 30-180 s; all 4 GPUs pinned at 100% util / 0% memory util |
| commit 6 only | 13 | all clean |
| commit 7 only (commit 6 reverted, so negative lengths still reach the kernel) | 3 | all clean |

The commit-7-only run is the one that shows the kernel guard is load-bearing rather than dead code: with commit 6 in place nothing negative ever reaches the kernel, so it would pass either way.

Root cause was confirmed on a live hang with cuda-gdb: exactly one of 16 CTAs resident, spinning in `wait_ge`, with `arrival_counter == 1` against `target_val == 2` — a group leader waiting on a peer that had already taken the `max_seq_len` early exit.

## AI assistance

This work was produced with AI assistance. Every changed line has been reviewed by the submitter, and the tests and evaluations above were executed on the hardware described, with results reported as measured.

title: Add Muse Glimmer model support
author: xianbaoqian
body:
Dense 29.6B vision-language model with a ViT-G/14 perception encoder and 128K context. Adds the model, its config and processor, channel-scoped reasoning and ATEM tool-call parsers, and DFlash speculative decoding support for its draft head.

The model does not emit JSON tool calls and does not wrap reasoning in <think> tags. Every turn is a sequence of channel-scoped messages, and both parsers key off that framing, so --tool-call-parser muse_glimmer and --reasoning-parser muse_glimmer are used together. The reasoning parser forces skip_special_tokens=False; without it the markers are stripped before parsing and both channels collapse into content.

tool_choice="required" and named tool_choice set
supports_required_and_named=False so vLLM does not apply JSON guided decoding to them -- that path assumes JSON tool calls, and forcing it here either trapped the call in the reasoning channel or leaked the raw framing into content.

The DFlash draft head (MuseGlimmerAssistantModel) reuses the existing qwen3_dflash implementation: same architecture, same tensors. It reads the target's residual stream at layers [1, 13, 25, 37, 49] and predicts a 16-slot block per forward.

Squashed from the onyx-support integration branch (30 commits).

title: [Kernel][Perf] Add fused CUDA post-conv MTP decode kernel for Qwen3.5 GDN
author: Jie-Fang
body:
## Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
Speed up Qwen3.5 (GDN linear attention) MTP speculative decode on Blackwell. During                                                                                                                                                                                                     
MTP decode, the Triton path launches a chain of small kernels per step (gating,                                                                                                                                                                                                         
delta-rule recurrence, state rewind/update, gated RMSNorm), which leaves the GPU                                                                                                                                                                                                        
latency-bound at decode batch sizes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
This PR adds a single fused CUDA kernel, `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp`, that                                                                                                                                                                                                         
consumes the post-convolution `mixed_qkv` and performs the entire GDN MTP decode                                                                                                                                                                                                        
step in one launch:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
- SiLU activation on q/k/v and gating (`softplus`/`sigmoid` on `a`, `b`, `A_log`,                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  `dt_bias`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
- the gated delta-rule recurrence over up to 8 speculative tokens per request,                                                                                                                                                                                                          
  with rewind to the last accepted token via `num_accepted_tokens`                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
- recurrent state update in place (BF16 or FP32 state)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
- gated RMSNorm epilogue, with output precision matched to the Triton path 

## Test Plan

New/extended tests (all require SM100):                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
```bash                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py -v                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -v                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -v                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
pytest tests/test_envs.py -k "gdn"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
pytest tests/compile/test_config.py                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
```                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
`test_gdn_fused_mtp.py` covers the model-path dispatch for pure spec-decode,                                                                                                                                                                                                            
mixed, prefill, and regular-decode batches against the Triton reference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                
`test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py::test_fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_ratio8` covers                                                                                                                                                                                                        
the kernel directly for BF16/FP32 state, ragged acceptance patterns, and TP head                                                                                                                                                                                                        
counts (tp4/tp16).

## Test Result

On 1x B200 (SM100), CUDA 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
- `tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_fused_mtp.py`: **6 passed**                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
- `tests/kernels/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py`: **70 passed**                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
- `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **10 passed**                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
- `tests/test_envs.py -k gdn`: **1 passed**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
- `tests/compile/test_config.py`: **44 passed** 

## Microbenchmark

1x B200, CUDA 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130. Both variants measured over the
**same kernel boundary**: post-conv `mixed_qkv` in, gated+normed
`core_attn_out` out, recurrent state updated in place.

- Triton path = `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` + gated RMSNorm
  (`rmsnorm_fn`), exactly as dispatched by `_forward_core_fused_norm` today.
- Fused path = single `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` launch.
- Timed by capturing 20 iterations in a CUDA graph and replaying 50x with CUDA
  events (production MTP decode runs under full CUDA graphs, so graph-replay
  GPU time is the relevant metric; CPU launch overhead excluded for both).
- **cold** rotates input/state buffer sets so the working set exceeds 4x L2
  (126 MB), i.e. state comes from HBM as in real serving where other layers
  evict L2 between calls; **warm** reuses one buffer set (L2-hot upper bound).
- K=V=128, 4 MTP tokens/request, `num_accepted_tokens=2`. Context length does
  not affect either variant (fixed-size recurrent state), so results apply to
  any seqlen (e.g. 8192).

Cold-cache speedup is **1.17x-2.20x**, largest in the latency-sensitive
BS=4-32 decode regime.

**TP=4 (H=4, HV=32), bfloat16 recurrent state**

## Model Evaluation

An lm_eval score comparison was not run: the fused path requires the
`num_v_heads == 8 * num_k_heads` GDN head layout, and no public Qwen3.5
checkpoint ships that config (0.8B is 16/16, 35B-A3B is 16/32, 397B-A17B is
16/64) — on those models the dispatch check never selects the fused kernel, so
default behavior is unchanged. Correctness of the fused kernel against the
Triton path is covered by the numerical-equivalence tests above:
`test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py::test_fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_ratio8`
checks kernel outputs and updated recurrent state against
`fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` + `rmsnorm_fn` across BF16/FP32 state,
ragged acceptance patterns, and TP head counts, and `test_gdn_fused_mtp.py`
checks the model-path dispatch (pure / mixed / prefill / decode batches)
end-to-end at the layer level.

title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Support causal multi-token verification
author: YukioZzz
body:
## Summary

Enable ROCm AITER MLA decode context parallelism for causal multi-token target verification. Each verification token gets its correct per-rank causal KV window, and rank-local partial outputs are merged through the existing DCP attention merge.

This PR is scoped to the ROCm AITER target backend. Hybrid prefix-cache geometry and external connector integration remain separate changes.

## Implementation

- Compute each verification row's global causal boundary and map it to the rank-local KV length.
- Expand physical KV blocks into the bounded subpages consumed by segmented AITER MLA.
- Run segmented MLA with unreduced partial output, then merge its base-2 statistics into BF16 output plus natural-log LSE for the cross-rank merge.
- Make the metadata builder the single owner of decode routing. Presence of an `AiterDCPVerifyView` selects segmented DCP verification; the implementation consumes that decision without recomputing it.
- Allocate stable row metadata and use a maximum DCP-local KV bound during FULL graph capture. Replay still masks inactive segments using actual row lengths.
- Keep single-token decode on the existing Gluon/ASM selection and keep DCP multi-token verification out of those paths.
- Allow ROCm DCP configurations to retain FULL CUDA graphs; PCP remains on the existing PIECEWISE fallback.

## Validation

### Focused ROCm tests

Revision: `e1843114b7c233a9c71ad44b28bf63426ad64836`

```text
540 passed, 14 warnings in 31.56s
```

The suite includes an actual FP8 segmented-kernel correctness test with `DCP=2`, `qlen=3`, and 96 gathered query heads. It builds each rank's causal row view through `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder`, computes both rank-local partials through `AiterMLAImpl.forward_mqa()`, merges them using their returned LSE, and compares the result against global causal attention.

It also covers:

- per-row causal DCP lengths and cross-rank coverage;
- block-to-subpage expansion and bounds;
- empty-row and natural-log LSE reduction;
- static FULL-graph metadata bounds;
- FP8 single-token decode routing;
- DCP multi-token routing to segmented MLA rather than Gluon/ASM.

Negative control: the causal-reference test was rerun after changing only the row-boundary calculation back to the previous committed-prefix-only form. The fixed implementation passed. The old calculation failed deterministically with 2,671/147,456 output elements outside tolerance and a maximum absolute difference of 0.1311. This test-only mutation was not committed.

### Full-model regression

Configuration:

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`
- PR revision: `e1843114b7c233a9c71ad44b28bf63426ad64836`
- Base: `2c7d7dd64a2eaba0feedf42cab2f527486d7479c`
- Real Kimi-K3 target weights
- TP8 / DCP8, A2A DCP, KV interleave 1
- FP8 KV cache
- maximum model length 1,048,576
- FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs, capture sizes 1 through 32
- maximum batch size 32
- prefix caching enabled

Full lm-eval GSM8K, 5-shot, 1,319 samples, concurrency 64, default generation length (`max_length=2047`):

```text
strict-match exact_match:     0.9613343442 +/- 0.0053105832
flexible-extract exact_match: 0.9613343442 +/- 0.0053105832
evaluation time:              335 seconds
server errors:                0
server tracebacks:            0
HSA memory-access faults:     0
```

The server selected `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, completed both PIECEWISE and FULL graph capture, exposed 27,012,229 KV-cache tokens, and remained healthy after the evaluation. The staged runtime files were checked against a SHA256 manifest in the container, and the server log recorded the exact PR revision above.

This target-only run validates the DCP8/FP8-KV full-model accuracy baseline. The causal multi-token target path is covered directly by the focused causal-reference test.

### Stacked target-verification run

PR 54546 at `8474084088b12b7bc3ca35cf6d74f87cb7161f92` was cleanly stacked on this PR head to enable Triton MLA for the non-causal draft group. The target retained the same TP8/DCP8, FP8-KV, 1M, FULL graph, and maximum-batch-32 configuration. The speculative configuration used two draft tokens, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling, and Triton MLA for the draft.

```text

GSM8K samples:                1319/1319 at concurrency 64
strict-match exact_match:     0.9628506444 +/- 0.0052095163

mean acceptance length:       2.67-2.74 in the final 10 windows

HSA memory-access faults:     0
```

This run exercises the ROCm AITER segmented causal target-verification path from this PR together with PR 54546's non-causal draft capability. The server completed FULL graph capture and remained healthy after evaluation.

title: [6/N][KV-Cache Layout Refactor] Standardize KV cache layout
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Purpose

The core of the KV-cache layout standardization series (RFC #42082). 

Standardizes every KV cache allocation on the logical `[L, B, H, N, C]` vocabulary:

- `KVCacheLayout` enumerates the physical stride permutations (`LBHNC`, `LBNHC`, `LHBNC`, `BLHNC`, `BLNHC`, `BHLNC`)
- Layout resolution has a single writer: attention-backend selection publishes the layout into `CacheConfig` (test override > backend-required > `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` > connector preference > `LBNHC`); every consumer reads it from there.
- `indexes_kv_by_block_stride` and per-backend cache-shape/stride-order hooks are removed — the standardized views make them constant.

Replaces #44458 (same content, restacked).

FULL CI Run; No PR related failures

submitter.
