title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Prefetch ll_bf16 router weights for M=1
author: mingg26
body:
## Purpose

Reduce the Kimi-K3 single-token AttnRes-to-router latency by loading the first
`ll_bf16` router-weight tiles before the incoming PDL wait.

The optimized kernel is selected from the runtime `M` shape:

- `M == 1`: use the weight-prefetch PDL specialization;
- every other `M`: use the original `ll_bf16` kernel unchanged.

The earlier AttnRes and latent-MoE-tail changes have been removed. AttnRes is
now provided by #54261, which is included in the rebased `main` base.

## Duplicate-work check

Open-PR searches for `ll_bf16 PDL` and `router weight prefetch` found no PR
implementing this optimization. This PR is intentionally limited to the
`ll_bf16` shape dispatch and does not duplicate #54261.

## Implementation

- Add an optional dot-product path that preloads the first eight static
  weight tiles before `griddepcontrol_wait()`.
- Keep separate compiled-kernel caches for the original and prefetch variants.
- Dispatch the prefetch variant only for `hidden_states.shape[0] == 1`.
- Add a unit test covering the `M=1` versus `M>1` dispatch boundary.

## Validation

Hardware: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, CUDA graph, cold L2, SM clock locked at 1980 MHz
for performance measurements.

Tests:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py -v`
  - `136 passed`
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`
  - passed
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`
  - passed
- Incremental `_C_stable_libtorch` build and install against rebased `main`
  - passed

The full kernel suite covers dot-product and split-K shapes, single-token
production shapes, numerical edge cases, deterministic output, CUDA graphs,
and dispatch/cache behavior.

## Performance

Timed region: merged native AttnRes followed by `ll_bf16`, including the PDL
handoff. L2 is flushed before the graph replay; AttnRes then produces the
activation consumed by `ll_bf16`.

For `M=1`, `N in {256, 384, 896}`, and AttnRes block counts `{1, 4, 8}`, all
nine tested production combinations were neutral or faster:

- median speedup range: `+0.26%` to `+20.13%`;
- mean speedup range: `+2.20%` to `+19.05%`;
- `M=1, N=896, blocks=8`: `16.288 us -> 14.240 us` median (`+14.38%`).

A forced prefetch run at `M=4, N=896, blocks=8` regressed from
`16.288 us -> 16.320 us` median (`-0.20%`) and `-1.30%` by mean. Therefore the
production dispatch deliberately keeps the specialization at `M == 1`.

No model-output evaluation was needed because this changes kernel scheduling,
not the mathematical operation; the full numerical suite passed. The previous
TP8 serving result from the broader pre-cleanup diff is not claimed here.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for diff cleanup, rebase support, test execution, and
benchmark analysis. The human submitter must review every changed line and be
able to defend the change end-to-end.

title: [Core][Feat] Pluggable KVCacheConfigBuilder for platform/model-specific KV cache planning
author: wangxiyuan
body: RFC: #62100 ## Purpose Follow-up to #42309. vLLM picks the KV cache grouping of every model with one heuristic in core (`get_kv_cache_groups()`). New hybrid models, drafters, cache precisions and platforms keep needing plans that this heuristic does not give, so each new model changes core, and vllm-ascend monkey-patches core planning to use its own DSV4 plan. This PR adds an **experimental** pluggable `KVCacheConfigBuilder`. Core keeps one planning flow and checks every plan. A platform selects a builder that decides grouping and placement, and a model can return its own groups. The interfaces can change, in particular when #61452 changes the KV cache group data structure. ## Changes - **`KVCacheConfigBuilder`** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_config_builder.py`) with two decisions: `get_kv_cache_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_spec)` and `get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)`. A platform selects the class with `Platform.get_kv_cache_config_builder_cls`; the default is `DefaultKVCacheConfigBuilder`. - **Core owns the planning flow.** `get_kv_cache_configs` is a core function, not a builder method: merge specs, group, check, project onto PP stages, apply the block-count override, auto-fit and admission, place, and converge ranks. Platforms make only the two decisions above. - **Bytes per block come from the builder's placement.** Core places one block and reads its single device backing, so a platform with its own placement does not compute memory separately. A placement with several device allocations overrides the private, transitional `_get_pool_bytes_per_block` (until worker-driven allocation, #42449). - **Model-owned grouping.** A model class can implement `SupportsKVCacheGrouping.get_kv_cache_groups` (a classmethod). Priority: a platform builder that overrides grouping (it reaches the model hook only through `super()`), then the model hook, then the default heuristic. - **Every grouping is checked**, from any source, on the planning path and both profiling paths: each layer is in exactly one group. - **Profiling** passes `num_blocks` directly instead of temporarily setting `num_gpu_blocks_override`. Bug fixes: - PP projection now keeps `host_resident`, `role` and `enable_kv_transfer` on partially projected groups. - `num_gpu_blocks_override` no longer inflates the one-block probe (it gave `500 * C` instead of `C` bytes per block). - HiSparse keeps the direct bytes computation, because probing its placement would size the host pool before auto-fit. A model hook combined with HiSparse raises a clear error. ## Users - vllm-ascend#18359 moves the Ascend plans into an `AscendKVCacheConfigBuilder` and removes most of its planning patches. - wangxiyuan/vllm#2 (stacked on this PR): model hooks for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Kimi-K3 (Kimi-K3 + DSpark: 5 groups instead of 20), and golden grouping plans per model. Not a duplicate: #58638 (#58207, #58380) improves the default heuristic for drafters. That work is complementary; this PR adds the extension point and does not change the default grouping. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_config_builder.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py ``` ## Test Result 83 passed (head `6283b0aca3`, GB200 node). AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR. The authors reviewed every changed line. Co-Authored-By: Yifan Qiao Co-Authored-By: Mengqing Cao Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5

title: [Perf][Kernel] Initialize NVFP4 padding in quant kernel
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #49775 and #45739.

#45739 used a separate `torch.zeros` allocation to initialize padded NVFP4 scales. This PR moves the required initialization into the CUDA quantization kernel, allowing the wrapper to safely use `torch.empty` and avoid the extra zero-fill launch.

It also:

- Preserves a specialized fast path for unpadded output.
- Retains programmatic dependent launch support.
- Adds sentinel-based regression coverage for padded rows and columns.

This does not duplicate #47587, which covers FlashInfer’s TRT-LLM 8x4 layout. This PR targets vLLM’s built-in 128x4 swizzled kernel.

## Test Result

Validated on NVIDIA B300 with CUDA 13.4 (`sm_103a`):

- Full vLLM build passed.
- NVFP4 quantization suite: `62 passed`.
- Compute Sanitizer: `2 passed`, `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`.
- Ruff, mypy, clang-format, typos, SPDX, forbidden-import and CUDA-call hooks passed.

The benchmark results that motivated this change are documented in [the original discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49775#issuecomment-5375613975). For Llama 3.3 70B (`N=8192`, `K=28672`), the built-in 128x4 swizzled kernel shows the following before/after results:

| M | vLLM `main`, before (us) | This PR (us) | Speedup | FlashInfer CuTe-DSL (us) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.133 | 1.912 | 1.639x | 2.418 |
| 16 | 3.132 | 2.008 | 1.560x | 2.636 |
| 32 | 3.197 | 2.089 | 1.531x | 2.790 |
| 64 | 3.411 | 2.200 | 1.550x | 2.900 |
| 128 | 3.305 | 2.497 | 1.324x | 3.253 |
| 256 | 4.576 | 3.718 | 1.231x | 4.031 |
| 512 | 6.828 | 5.834 | 1.170x | 5.600 |
| 1024 | 10.791 | 9.822 | 1.099x | 9.750 |
| 2048 | 24.675 | 24.857 | 0.993x | 28.773 |
| 4096 | 46.590 | 47.080 | 0.990x | 47.462 |
| 8192 | 90.676 | 91.298 | 0.993x | 93.118 |

The change improves the launch-bound small- and medium-`M` cases by up to 1.64x and is effectively neutral at large `M`, where quantization work dominates the removed initialization overhead.

AI assistance was used to port the existing fix onto current `main`.

title: [Kimi K3] Support internal prefix checkpoints with partial prefix caching and spec-decoding
author: ZeldaHuang
body:
## Purpose

Extend the Kimi-K3 prefill checkpoint optimization from #52789 to support:

- speculative decoding / Eagle block rewind;
- partial prefix caching (`prefix_match_unit < Mamba block size`); and
- checkpoint blocks restored through KV connectors such as MooncakeStore.

The cache manager and FlashKDA worker share the same checkpoint-validity rules, so a checkpoint block is allocated and hashed only when the worker can write it. For an aligned partial checkpoint, the already reserved request-owned checkpoint block is re-keyed from its provisional boundary to the state position actually exported by FlashKDA.

This PR keeps the block allocation, eviction, and free lifecycle introduced in #52789.

## Test Plan

- Run pre-commit and the KDA metadata, Mamba aligned-chunk, partial-prefix-cache, and prefix-caching unit tests.
- Deploy Kimi-K3 with TP8/EP8 on two 4-GPU nodes using FlashKDA (`DS` conv-state layout), prefix caching, and public `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` speculative decoding.
- Compare non-partial prefix caching with `prefix_match_unit=128` by sending exact token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`: 8 streams grow from 120K to 164K by 2K per round, with a barrier between rounds and three measured repeats per variant.
- With D-Spark-7 and Partial128 enabled, run the complete 1,000-sample OCR-Bench three times sequentially and audit all saved responses.
- Retain the MooncakeStore + NIXL PD E2E coverage previously run for this PR.

Nightly image used for the latest regression:

```text
inferactinc/dev:vllm-k3-arm64-cu13-7b1bb3a
```

The PR source was overlaid on this image and `_C_stable_libtorch.so` was rebuilt
from the same `main` commit because the binary bundled in the image predates the
current Kimi-K3 custom-op ABI.

Important server options for the latest run:

```bash
export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS
export VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TOKENSPEED_MLA
export VLLM_KIMI_K3_GEMM_RS=1
export TOKENSPEED_MLA_PREFILL_BACKEND=cutedsl

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --nnodes 2 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --prefix-match-unit 128 \
  --max-model-len 180000 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \
  --kda-prefill-backend flashkda \
  --speculative-config \
    '{"method":"dspark","model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --enforce-eager
```

The non-partial variant uses the same deployment without `--prefix-match-unit 128`.

## Test Result

### Static and unit tests

- Pre-commit: all hooks passed on every changed file.
- Focused unit suite: **113 passed**.
- The aligned re-key regression covers `B=H=32`, prompt length 104, and Eagle rewind: the provisional `hash@96` checkpoint block is re-keyed to the exported `state@64` boundary, and the stale hash is removed.

### Latest-nightly TP8 performance

The PR-description workload was run unchanged: exact token-ID prompts sent to
`/v1/completions`, 8 streams, 120K to 164K, +2K per round, and a barrier after
each group of 8 requests. Each variant used one complete unmeasured workload
warmup followed by three measured repeats. All 528 incremental requests per
variant completed without failures.

| Variant | Incremental P50 TTFT | Effective req/s | Mean cached tokens | Mean recomputed tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| D-Spark-7, non-partial | 1,526.59 ms | 4.639 | 138,196.36 | 4,803.64 |
| D-Spark-7, Partial128 | **1,136.22 ms** | **5.941** | **140,590.55** | **2,409.45** |

Partial128 cached 2,394.18 more tokens per incremental request and reduced
recomputation by **49.84%**. Incremental P50 TTFT improved by **25.57%** and
effective throughput improved by **28.08%**. Mean cold TTFT was effectively
unchanged (4,696.35 vs. 4,675.71 ms, -0.44%).

Per-repeat P50 TTFT:

| Variant | Repeat 1 | Repeat 2 | Repeat 3 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Non-partial | 1,535.89 ms | 1,520.75 ms | 1,523.12 ms |
| Partial128 | 1,110.32 ms | 1,088.71 ms | 1,209.62 ms |

### OCR-Bench: D-Spark-7 + Partial128

All three runs used one unchanged deployment and processed the full benchmark sequentially.

| Run | Accuracy | Standard error | Scored samples | Request errors | Suspect outputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0.881 | 0.0102 | 1,000 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.889 | 0.0099 | 1,000 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 0.886 | 0.0101 | 1,000 | 0 | 0 |

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable the AITER GDN decode fast path for flat qkvz layouts
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose `_forward_core_rocm` currently gates the AITER GDN decode fast path on `self.gqa_interleaved_layout`, so only Qwen3-Next takes it and flat-layout models (e.g. Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8) fall through to the generic path. #42880 added that guard because the fused reshape+conv kernel only understood Qwen3-Next's packing and read the wrong columns from a flat tensor. ROCm/aiter#3251 added a `qkvz_layout` parameter handling both. It selects the source index mapping only — outputs stay in canonical order, so the downstream `fused_rearrange_sigmoid_gated_delta_rule` is unchanged — and `"interleaved"` stays the default, so Qwen3-Next is bit-identical. This PR passes the layout through and drops the layout guard. Older AITER builds would raise `TypeError`, so `gdn_fused_conv_supports_qkvz_layout()` probes the signature once (mirroring `fused_moe_supports_gate_mode()`) and flat layouts keep the guard there. The fast path returns before the entire generic block, so four kernel launches per GDN layer per step become two: `core_attn_out.zero_()` and `z_out[:] = z` are pure removals, since the AITER kernel writes both buffers including the padding rows above `num_actual_tokens`. Also adds `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn` to the Kernels Mamba `source_file_dependencies`, which did not list it. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_rocm_layout_dispatch.py -q ``` New host-side tests (CPU, no GPU or AITER needed) covering flat dispatch with and without kernel support, Qwen3-Next non-regression on both, batch shapes that must stay generic, and the capability probe. Accuracy uses the `lm_eval` invocation from #42880; performance uses decode traces of `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` on 8x MI355X. ## Test Result ```bash 14 passed. ``` **Performance:** Serving benchmark on `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, 8x MI355X, TP8, fixed input/output lengths (`--random-range-ratio 0`), one run per point, measured against a stock build of the same commit. | ISL | OSL | Conc | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | | ---- | ---- | ---- | ------------------------- | --------------------- | | 1024 | 1024 | 4 | 250.6 → 258.6 (+3.2%) | 15.66 → 15.16 (-3.2%) | | 1024 | 1024 | 16 | 674.0 → 688.3 (+2.1%) | 22.95 → 22.45 (-2.1%) | | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 1,560.7 → 1,594.7 (+2.2%) | 38.82 → 37.94 (-2.3%) | **Accuracy:** GSM8K, 5-shot, seed 4321, `batch_size=128`: | Run | flexible-extract | strict-match | | ------------------- | ---------------- | --------------- | | Stock (main) | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | | This PR | 0.9348 ± 0.0068 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | No accuracy regression. **(Decode) trace:** | Kernel | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | `core_attn_out.zero_()` | 3933 / 16.3 ms | absent | | `direct_copy_kernel` (`z_out[:] = z`) | 3920 / 17.0 ms | absent | | `_causal_conv1d_update_kernel` | 3933 / 16.7 ms | absent | | `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel` | 3933 / 23.7 ms | absent | | `_reshape_causal_conv1d_update_single_token_kernel` | absent | 3933 / 17.3 ms | | `fused_rearrange_sigmoid_gated_delta_rule_update_kernel` | absent | 3933 / 20.7 ms | | **GDN decode window** | **73.7 ms** | **38.0 ms** | Current main: This PR: ---

title: [Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Skip DP sync before EAGLE/MTP draft prefill
author: TheEpicDolphin
body:
# Summary Currently, the V2 model runner speculator for EAGLE/MTP performs a CPU all-reduce (in `sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding`) to synchronize the `num_tokens`, `uniform_token_count`, `cg_mode`, etc, across DP ranks before each of the draft prefill (drafts first token), and the draft multi-step decode (drafts N-1 tokens). Similarly, the multi-module MTP speculator does the DP-sync before the mutl-step drafting loop (drafts all N tokens). The CPU all-reduce adds significant CPU overhead during serving. # This PR Passes the DP-synced values (number of tokens, uniform token count, eager) from the model runner's call to `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` before the target forward, and reuses it for draft prefill during EAGLE/MTP and before the draft loop during multi-module MTP. This allows skipping a CPU all-reduce, and directly fetching the correct batch descriptor using the DP-synced values. # Evals/Benchmarks **Setup.** GSM8K (1319 questions), `dp=2, tp=2, --enable-expert-parallel` on 4×GB200. Perf via `vllm bench serve --dataset-name custom --dataset-path gsm8k.jsonl --backend openai-chat --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 64 --num-warmups 64 --num-prompts 1319 --custom-output-len 2048 --temperature 0 --top-p 1.0`. title: [3/N] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA decode hot-buffering
author: MatthewBonanni
body: ## Summary HiSparse adds a host-resident tier beneath vLLM's normal GPU KV cache for sparse-MLA decode. Unlike the original always-host-resident design in #46326, this implementation keeps as much KV as possible in the normal device cache and spills pages to pinned host memory only when GPU capacity must be reclaimed. Supersedes #46326. ## Design overview ```text resident GPU pages | | spill under pressure v pinned host pool ---- selected top-k misses ----> per-request GPU hot buffer ^ | | v +---------------- prefix reuse ---------------- sparse attention ``` The active indexer cache remains device-resident and produces the logical top-k positions needed by sparse attention. A fused CUDA resolver maps each selected position through three possible locations: 1. a normal resident GPU page; 2. an existing row in the request's GPU hot buffer; 3. the pinned host pool. Resident hits return before the hot-cache lookup. Hot hits update a GPU-side LRU, while misses replace LRU entries by gathering only the selected host rows. Resolution, replacement, and LRU updates remain on the GPU and are compatible with CUDA graph replay. HiSparse does not maintain a private host-side copy of indexer KV. The indexer remains a normal prefix-cacheable GPU cache group. When OffloadingConnector is configured alongside HiSparse, generic KV offloading preserves and restores the indexer while HiSparse continues to own only sparse-MLA residency. If the sparse host prefix extends beyond the available indexer prefix, the scheduler restores only the missing indexer suffix, capped at the sparse host boundary. Without generic offloading, the request falls back to the shorter shared prefix and recomputes the remainder. ## Residency and ownership The normal KV cache manager continues to own GPU block allocation. `HiSparseCoordinator` owns logical host blocks, host-prefix identity, and residency transitions. When GPU pressure requires reclaiming a resident page, the coordinator reserves its host destination and sends a transfer command to the worker. The resident GPU block becomes reusable after every worker has acknowledged that the copy is enqueued in stream order. The host page is not published for prefix reuse until every copy has completed. The main components are: - `HiSparseCoordinator`: scheduler-side host allocation, prefix state, and spill policy. - `HiSparseConnector`: carries residency commands and transfer acknowledgements between scheduler and workers. - `HiSparseConnectorWorker`: manages the pinned host-pool lifecycle and executes copies. - `HiSparseRuntime`: owns each cache's host/hot views, GPU LRU state, and fused attention-time resolution. Host blocks use the same token hashes as their resident counterparts, but their hashes are published only after the contents are durable. Spilling therefore preserves prefix-cache value without allowing an incomplete host write to be reused. ## P/D and NIXL integration NIXL remains the P/D transport; HiSparse determines the decoder-side landing policy. The decoder chooses one policy per request during admission: - If the imported prefix fits in the normal GPU pools, NIXL writes it into resident device pages. - Otherwise, the bulk sparse-MLA KV lands in the registered HiSparse host pool. Device-only regions such as the indexer are still imported to GPU, the request receives its fixed hot-buffer allocation, and pages needed immediately are mirrored into resident GPU pages. The two generic connector prerequisites below are intentionally separate from HiSparse: - #53779 lets connectors select externally transferable cache groups while retaining their scheduler group IDs. - #53780 carries stride, capacity, block size, group mapping, and identity per NIXL region, allowing P/D peers with different layouts and memory placement. #53263 is a separate, optional optimization for same-node P/D. It stages device-to-host NIXL reads through decoder GPU memory to avoid UCX's slow TCP loopback path. It is not required by the intended multi-node P/D design. ## Scope This PR implements the NVIDIA sparse-MLA path and includes the staging required for correct local or mixed prefill on a decode worker. Metrics are split into #53782, and DeepSeek V4's compressed cache geometry is split into #53592. ## Preliminary results Preliminary B300 results: AI assistance was used in the preparation of this PR.

title: [Feature][PCP] Support decode-only FULL CUDA graphs
author: pisceskkk
body:
## Purpose

Enable prefill context parallelism (PCP) to use decode-only FULL CUDA graphs through `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.

This change:

- keeps PCP graph capture and replay on persistent rank-local input buffers;
- selects PCP persistent capture inputs from the graph mode and typed `PCPManager` in one linear branch;
- keeps standard block-table, slot-mapping, and DCP preparation together in the common capture path;
- passes the batch execution descriptor through the PCP adapter and derives mode-specific token and request padding in one place;
- preserves graph-padded request and token capacities after PCP batch partitioning;
- prepares PCP-local block tables, slot mappings, and attention metadata for FULL capture and dummy runs;
- keeps pure `FULL` mode restricted because PCP prefill uses a separately dispatched execution path;
- adds focused unit and GSM8K E2E coverage for configuration validation, prefill rejection, request padding, persistent PCP buffers, and combined CUDA graph mode.

## Test Plan

Full GPU accuracy validation:

- NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 x2, GPU 4/5
- GLM-4.7-Flash, BF16
- TP=1, PCP=2, EP=2
- max model length 8192; max sequences 32; max batched tokens 32768
- GSM8K, all 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 32, temperature 0, seed 42, max output tokens 4096
- eager, `PIECEWISE`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`

## Test Result

All four services completed the full 1319-question dataset with zero invalid completions and zero request errors.

The graph-mode deltas remain within 0.61 percentage points of eager on this evaluation. Service logs were also checked for graph replay, CUDA, NCCL, and EngineCore failures.

Current branch validation at `f832b6a7a75745bbf80dbb9763cea1d4ed587356`:

title: [Kernel] Fuse DeepEP-v2 decode globalize+align into one launch
author: elvircrn
body:
Fuses the DeepEP-v2 INDEXED cudagraph-decode metadata chain (`_globalize_recv_topk_idx` + `moe_align_block_size` + `count_and_sort_expert_tokens`) into a single CUDA launch for the Humming path.

`recv_topk_idx` holds **local** expert ids; the kernel bins by local id (align/sort) while writing back the global id, and reads `num_recv` on-device from `psum[-1]` so it is CUDA-graph safe. Sizing by local (not global) experts shrinks the sentinel/`expert_ids` region by ~`ep_size` under EP. The fused kernel also produces the optional scatter index used by Humming for larger EP batches.

The fused path is selected for CUDA Humming INDEXED experts when DeepEP-v2 defers globalization during CUDA-graph decode. Other paths keep the standalone globalization and alignment behavior.

## Numbers

H200, EP32, INDEXED decode — fused vs the 3-kernel chain, measured before the October 6 rebase:

| tokens | speedup |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1.23x |
| 8 | 1.14x |
| 32 | 1.16x |
| 64 | 1.36x |
| 128 | 1.67x |
| 256 (n=8192) | 2.01x |

## Testing

After the October 12 rebase onto upstream commit `c599b5971`: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the six changed Python files; Apple `clang-format` 21 `--dry-run --Werror` passed on the changed CUDA/C++ files; `git diff --check` passed. `git range-diff` confirmed that the functional patch is unchanged apart from adapting paths to upstream's new `csrc/moe` layout. CI then found a stale `libtorch_stable/torch_utils.h` include in the moved CUDA source; commit `52d7e1c15` changes it to `torch_utils.h`, matching the other MoE CUDA files. The corrected include and formatting were checked locally, but the CUDA build needs to rerun in CI. The pinned `clang-format` and mypy hooks passed on the prior October 7 base but were not rerun here. `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_globalize_align_block_size.py -v` could not run on the macOS rebase host. The test includes correctness cases for the optional scatter index.

Pending on CUDA hardware: `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuild, the pytest run, and a model evaluation (for example gsm8k) with the fused path active. The kernel originated from a validated standalone prototype; the measurements above have not been repeated on the rebased code.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate — no open PR fused this chain when the PR was created (`gh pr list --search "globalize align"`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) was used. Human review of the rebase resolution and GPU validation are pending.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Enable a4w4 flydsl kernels for KimiK3
author: ppalanga
body:
## Summary

- When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1` (the existing Kimi-K3 recipe toggle), route SiTU MXFP4 routed experts through AITER's **a4w4** flydsl kernels (`afp4_wfp4_fp4`, `fp4q`) instead of the previous **a8w4** path (`afp8_wfp4_fp8`, `fp8q`, `_gui_` interleave).
- vLLM sets `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=1` at init and clears any legacy `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` override (AITER checks A8W4 first, so leaving it set would still pick afp8).
- SiTUv2 gate/up weights use the **separated** layout to match ATOM kernel selection.

No new env flags; the existing recipe variable keeps its name for compatibility.

## AITER requirement

This path needs [ROCm/aiter#4463](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4463) (first tagged in **AITER v0.1.20**): `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` dispatch plus `kimik3_a4w4_{un,}tuned_fmoe.csv`. vLLM `main` already pins `AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.21.post1`, which includes that PR.

On AITER **v0.1.19** (this PR's original docker pin), a4w4 still launches `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` but logs **heuristic FlyDSL fallback** because the tuned CSV rows are missing. That is not the tuned a4w4 config from #4463.

## Motivation

Trace comparison on Kimi-K3 / MI355X shows vLLM dispatching `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp8_wfp4_fp8_*_gui_xcd4_*` while ATOM uses `mfma_moe1_silu_mul_afp4_wfp4_fp4_*_situv2_*`. AITER supports a4w4 via `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` in #4463; vLLM previously wired the recipe toggle to a8w4. Open PR #50813 adds explicit opt-in a8w4 for Quark checkpoints — this change makes a4w4 the default for the existing SiTUv2 recipe path.

## Results

GSM8K (Kimi-K3 MXFP4, MI355X, TP=8, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`, greedy 5-shot, full test split `n=1319`):

| Filter | Metric | This PR (a4w4) | Prior a8w4 recipe |
|---|---|---|---|
| strict-match | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |
| flexible-extract | exact_match | **0.9659 ± 0.005** | 0.9666 |

No accuracy regression (within stderr). Decode dispatch used `flydsl_moe1_afp4_wfp4_bf16_*` (fp4 activations); no `afp8` / `_gui_` kernels.

`niah_single_2` at 32k (`n=20`): **1.0** on both a4w4 and a8w4.

8k ISL / 1k OSL serving on AITER **without** #4463 tuned CSVs (heuristic a4w4 vs tuned a8w4) is a wash (~0.5% at conc 4/8). Isolated kernel timings in AITER #4463 show a4w4 ahead of a8w4 once the tuned rows are present.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k situv2` on gfx950
- [x] Serve Kimi-K3 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`; confirm a4w4 FlyDSL (`afp4_wfp4_bf16`, not `afp8` / `fp8q` / `_gui_`)
- [ ] Confirm **tuned** a4w4 configs (`using 2stage`, no `heuristic FlyDSL fallback`) on AITER >= v0.1.20
- [ ] Do **not** set `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` in launch scripts (overrides a4w4)
- [x] GSM8K vs prior a8w4 baseline (see Results)
- [x] `niah_single_2` vs prior a8w4
- [ ] 8k/1k serving A/B on AITER with #4463 tuned CSVs
- [ ] Verify cudagraph correctness under full decode (SiTUv2 a4w4 flydsl path, distinct from generic `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4` cudagraph issue in #44988)

title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] Add FLy: entropy-gated deferred verification for draft-model speculative decoding
author: eecspan
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds [FLy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.22972), an opt-in, lossy speculative verification policy, with support for both ModelRunner V1 and ModelRunner V2.

Standard verification stops at the first rejected draft token. FLy can accept an isolated rejection when the target entropy is high and the next `W` draft tokens all pass native verification. It needs no additional checkpoint or target forward pass. FLy does not preserve the target distribution and may reduce output quality; standard verification remains the default.

## Results at a glance

- **MRV2:** four recent models using DSpark/MTP, evaluated on AMD MI355X and NVIDIA B300. Across batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64, FLy improves decode throughput over Standard SD at all 48 model/platform/batch points: **1.055x–1.310x on AMD** and **1.041x–1.273x on NVIDIA**.
- **MRV2 quality:** Target / Standard SD / FLy comparisons on GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, and GPQA-Diamond. Minimum measured accuracy retention relative to Target is **96.43% on AMD** and **96.30% on NVIDIA**, both one-question differences on AIME25. These are single-pass measurements, not a quality guarantee.
- **V1:** the existing four target/draft pairs across ten benchmarks show **1.067x–1.938x** throughput versus Standard SD on AMD MI355X. Additional NVIDIA and non-zero-temperature results are retained below.

## Implementation

FLy changes verification decisions, using the native acceptance rule for each sampling mode: token equality for greedy target sampling, target-only acceptance for greedy drafting with random target sampling, or probability-ratio acceptance for probabilistic drafting.

A rejected position is eligible only when its draft token is not masked by target constraints, its top-k target entropy meets the threshold, and a full window of `W` subsequent draft tokens passes native verification. Another rejection within that window rejects the original position; a short trailing window is not deferred.

- **MRV1:** a pre-pass overrides the target argmax or uniform sample consumed by the existing acceptance kernels. The random path checks positive target and draft probability before forcing acceptance. Softmax is computed once and reused.
- **MRV2:** the rejection kernel tracks a pending rejection and commits the window only after all `W` native acceptances. Failed windows recover at the original rejected position, preserving that position's argmax or probability-normalization statistics.

Entropy is computed from processed target scores as `-sum(p * log(p))` over the largest `fly_entropy_top_k` probabilities, without renormalizing that subset. The default top-k is 3. This is the implementation's top-k gate, rather than the paper's full-vocabulary normalized entropy.

Configuration validates the window and logs a one-time lossy-method warning. Probabilistic drafting retains draft probabilities for FLy. The V1 pre-pass uses int64 vocabulary-offset arithmetic to avoid overflow on large batches.

This PR also rejects `use_heterogeneous_vocab=True` together with `use_local_argmax_reduction=True`: the local-argmax path otherwise bypasses vocabulary intersection and token-ID mapping. This validation applies to all verification methods. FLy-specific entropy and acceptance work runs only when explicitly enabled.

## Usage

```python
from vllm import LLM

llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
    speculative_config={
        "method": "draft_model",
        "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 8,
        "rejection_sample_method": "fly",
        "fly_window_size": 6,
        "fly_entropy_threshold": 0.3,
        "fly_entropy_top_k": 3,
    },
)
```

`fly_window_size` defaults to `min(6, num_speculative_tokens - 1)`. FLy requires at least two speculative tokens and a window smaller than that count. `fly_entropy_top_k` must be positive and is capped at the vocabulary size.

FLy supports heterogeneous vocabularies through the existing token mapping with greedy drafting. The proposer allowlist has been removed; `extract_hidden_states` is explicitly rejected because it does not perform speculative verification.

Standalone `draft_model` proposing uses MRV1. MRV2 supports FLy with its supported proposers, including MTP and DSpark as evaluated below. FLy does not force a fallback to MRV1. The MRV2 measurements use `fly_window_size=2`, as specified in their setup.

## ModelRunner V2 evaluation

All runs use ModelRunner V2 and the models' native speculative heads. Draft sampling is greedy. FLy uses `window=2`, a default entropy threshold of `0.3`, and entropy top-k `3`.

Target-only (`T`) is the primary quality reference, while Standard SD (`SD`) is included as a sanity baseline. `FLy−T` is the absolute accuracy difference, and retention is `FLy correct / Target correct`.

| Model | Speculative method | K | AMD MI355X TP | NVIDIA B300 TP | Reasoning effort |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | DSpark | 7 | 4 | 2 | `high` |
| Qwen3.8-27B | MTP | 3 | 2 | 1 | `xhigh` |
| GLM-5.2-FP8 | MTP | 5 | 4 | 4 | `max` |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | MTP | 8 | 2 | 1 | thinking enabled |

## ModelRunner V1 evaluation

<details>
<summary>Full V1 results, including sampling-policy and NVIDIA coverage</summary>

### Setup

The V1 primary results run on **AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950)** with torch.compile and HIP graph enabled, at temperature 0 with greedy drafting and target-only verification. The evaluation covers `draft_model` drafting; these V1 tables do not measure hidden-state drafting methods.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 15 | 1 | 32 |
| DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B / 8B | 15 | 1 | 32 |
| Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8-KV / Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 25 | 2 | 32 |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 / Qwen3-8B | 15 | 2 | 16 |

Standard SD and FLy differ by exactly one setting, `rejection_sample_method` (`"standard"` vs `"fly"`). The draft checkpoint, `num_speculative_tokens`, torch.compile and graph-capture settings, sampling parameters and the V1 draft-model proposer path are identical, so both configurations have identical prerequisites.

`T` / `SD` / `FLy` denote target-only decoding, standard speculative decoding and FLy. Throughput is generated output tokens per second, draft acceptance excludes bonus tokens, and `tau = 1 + accepted draft tokens / verification rounds`. Quality is compared directly against Target-only. `FLy−T` is the absolute accuracy difference in percentage points, calculated from the displayed accuracies or correct counts; percentage-based deltas therefore inherit the rounding of the source tables. Every row states its own concurrency (`BS`). Spec-Bench quality is measured on its 80-question math subset while throughput uses the full 480-prompt workload.

title: [feat] FlashInfer CuteDSL MegaMoE integration
author: jdebache
body:
## Purpose

This changeset attempts to use the recently added CuteDSL MegaMoE kernels from FlashInfer to accelerate large batch size (prefill mostly) inference. We will evaluate on several models to exercise as many paths as possible.

It is effectively a generalization of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49636 beyond DeepSeekV4.

## Test Plan

To test this feature, we evaluate accuracy against baseline with the GSM8K eval and we measured performance using `vllm bench serve` in simulated prefill scenarios (setting OSL to 1), where these kernels should excel. We chose a variety of models to attempt to cover as many code paths as possible.

All runs were performed on 4xGB200 whenever possible. For DeepSeekV4 Pro, we instead ran on 8xB200.

The servers were started with variations of the following, adjusted per model:

**Baseline server**

```bash
vllm serve \
  $MODEL_PATH \
  --served-model-name evaluation-model \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --language-model-only --enforce-eager \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --seed 42 --port 8000
```

**Candidate server**

```bash
vllm serve \
  $MODEL_PATH \
```

body:
## Purpose
This is a PR for the proposal defined in this [RFC #53916](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53916) for implementing text watermarking in vLLM. Refer to that RFC for all design decisions, justifications and empirical results.

We implement:
- a new watermarking sampler using the Gumbel-max algorithm
- a new detection primitive for this sampler
- a stable PRF to be used for keyed generation
- a per-request `watermarking=false` opt-out while keeping the algorithm and key engine-level
- an example endpoint for detection

title: [MoE][DeepEPV2] Add PaddedStandard activation format
author: bnellnm
body:
## Motivation

`DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize` hands the experts an activation tensor whose **row count is an upper bound rather than the exact token count**, so some rows are inactive padding. The shape is still 2D `(num_tokens, hidden_dim)` — the padding is in the token dimension; nothing is padded along `E`. It arises because the number of tokens a rank receives after dispatch is data-dependent and not knowable on the host without a device sync, from two sources:

- **decode / cudagraph mode** — the recv buffer is sized to the worst case (`R * num_max_tokens_per_rank`); only the `[0, num_recv_tokens)` prefix is written and the tail is left **uninitialized**.
- **prefill mode** — tokens are grouped per-expert and each expert's block is padded up to `expert_alignment`; those gaps are zeroed.

Inactive rows are signalled by setting all of their `topk_ids` slots to `-1`, and `ExpertTokensMetadata.psum_recv_per_rank` carries the real/padding boundary on device (reading it host-side would break CUDA-graph capture).

Previously this was hidden behind the generic `Standard` activation format, so experts had no way to know their input might contain such rows. Kernels that *can* skip padding couldn't opt in, and kernels that *can't* handle it had no way to reject the layout. That is a correctness issue, not just a missed optimization: the decode-mode tail is uninitialized, so an expert that builds routing by scanning every row can read garbage that aliases a valid expert id and corrupt real tokens.

This PR introduces a distinct `PaddedStandard` activation format so that the padding contract is communicated explicitly from the prepare/finalize stage to the experts, and only experts that actually support padded input are selected.

## Design

`PaddedStandard` is modeled as a **superset** of `Standard`: a padding-aware kernel treats unpadded input as the zero-padding case, so it accepts both formats, while a `Standard`-only kernel accepts only `Standard`.
`BatchedExperts` remains a disjoint format.

Declaring `PaddedStandard` is a contract: the kernel must either skip inactive rows or produce results for them that are safe to discard, and must honor the `-1` markers rather than trusting row contents.

Rather than have each experts kernel enumerate a list of accepted formats, every kernel declares a single `activation_format()` and the superset relation is expressed by one directional helper on the enum:

```python                                                                                                                              
class FusedMoEActivationFormat(Enum):                                                                                                  
    Standard = ("standard",)                                                                                                           
    BatchedExperts = ("batched_experts",)                                                                                              
    PaddedStandard = ("padded_standard",)                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                       
    def is_superset(self, pf_format: "FusedMoEActivationFormat") -> bool:                                                              
        """Whether this (experts) format is a superset of `pf_format`, i.e. an                                                         
        experts kernel declaring `self` can consume activations produced by a                                                          
        prepare/finalize step in `pf_format`."""                                                                                       
        if self == pf_format:                                                                                                          
            return True                                                                                                                
        return (                                                                                                                       
            self == FusedMoEActivationFormat.PaddedStandard                                                                            
            and pf_format == FusedMoEActivationFormat.Standard                                                                         
        )                                                                                                                              
```                                                                                                                                    

The relation is directional and used as `expert_format.is_superset(pf_format)` everywhere: the experts format (`self`) must be a superset of the prepare/finalize format (the argument).

## What changed

### New activation format
- Added `FusedMoEActivationFormat.PaddedStandard` and the `is_superset()` relation (`modular_kernel.py`).
- `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize.activation_format` now reports `PaddedStandard` instead of `Standard` (`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py`).

### Experts declare a single activation format
- `FusedMoEExperts.activation_format() -> FusedMoEActivationFormat` (kept single-valued; no list). Experts that support padded input declare `PaddedStandard`:
  - `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (Blackwell only)
  - `HummingIndexedExperts`
  - `TrtLlmMxfp4Mxfp8ExpertsModular` (mxfp4+mxfp8)
  - `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` and `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` — the TRTLLM-Gen
    kernels skip padding rows at tile granularity (only the modular variants;
    the monolithic classes stay `Standard`).
- All other experts declare their single existing format (`Standard` or `BatchedExperts`).

### TRTLLM mxfp4 expert split
- `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModular` was split into `TrtLlmMxfp4ExpertsModularBase` + two subclasses, because only the mxfp4+mxfp8 variant supports `PaddedStandard`. `_supports_quant_scheme` was moved down into the subclasses/monolithic class accordingly.

### Format-compatibility checks go through `is_superset`
- `FusedMoEExperts.is_supported_config`: `cls.activation_format().is_superset(activation_format)`.
- `FusedMoEKernel._post_init_setup`: asserts `fused_experts.activation_format().is_superset(prepare_finalize.activation_format)`.
- Test tooling `modular_kernel_tools/common.py` validity check uses the same relation instead of format equality.

### Batched detection uses an `is_batched` property
- `BatchedExperts` is disjoint, so instead of raw `== BatchedExperts` comparisons
  there is a `FusedMoEActivationFormat.is_batched` property that encapsulates the
  single legitimate identity check. All batched-detection sites (`__init__`
  validation, `HummingExpertsBase.is_batched`, cutlass `use_batched_format`,
  `FusedMoEConfig.use_batched_activation_format`, the oracle backend-remap
  branches, and `mk_objects.py`) use `<format>.is_batched`.

### Centralized format selection
- Added `FusedMoEConfig.activation_format` property that resolves the all2all format once: `BatchedExperts` for DeepEP-LL / NIXL-EP / `batched_triton`, `PaddedStandard` for DeepEP V2, else `Standard`.
- Moved `use_batched_activation_format` from `FusedMoEParallelConfig` to `FusedMoEConfig` (now defined in terms of `activation_format`).
- All per-dtype oracle selectors (`fp8`, `int8`, `int_wna16`, `mxfp4`, `mxfp8`, `nvfp4`, `unquantized`, `w4a8`, `w4a8_int8`, `humming_utils`) now use `config.activation_format` instead of each re-deriving the batched/standard branch.
- Fixed a latent bug in `oracle/fp8.py`: the explicit-DeepGEMM branch tested `== Standard` (which would misroute a `PaddedStandard` config to `BATCHED_DEEPGEMM`); it now tests `== BatchedExperts`.

### `CompressedTensorsW4A4Mxfp4MoEMethod` can reach `DeepGemmFP4Experts`
The method picked its `FusedMoEExperts` class from a hardcoded if-chain
(`CutlassExpertsMxfp4._supports_current_device()` → `is_xpu()` → Marlin) that never
consulted `activation_format`, so on SM100 it always chose `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`
(`Standard`) and `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize` tripped the assert in
`modular_kernel.py`. `--moe-backend=deep_gemm` now joins `b12x` in deferring to
`select_mxfp4_moe_backend`, which is format-aware:

```python                                                                                                                              
if moe.moe_backend == "b12x" or moe.moe_backend == "deep_gemm":                                                                        
    self.mxfp4_backend, experts_cls = select_mxfp4_moe_backend(moe)                                                                    
```                                                                                                                                    

`process_weights_after_loading` gains the matching `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` branch.
`DeepGemmFP4Experts` has no `process_weights_after_loading` of its own, so without it
the DeepGEMM scale packing never ran and the weights fell through the `else`
catch-all into `prepare_moe_fp4_layer_for_marlin`.

Selection is unchanged for every other `--moe-backend` value, including `auto`: the
CUTLASS / XPU / Marlin chain is untouched. This is deliberately the narrow fix —
routing the remaining mxfp4 call sites (`inc_mxfp4_moe.py`, `quark_moe.py`) through
the oracle, and teaching the oracle about `CutlassExpertsMxfp4`, is a follow-up PR.

## Testing

### New tests

- Padding test for deep_gemm in `test_deepgemm.py`
- `test_trtllm_bf16_moe_padding_robust` — padding-robustness: poison the padding
  (NaN in the workspace arena / in the inactive rows of a hand-built `PaddedStandard`
  buffer whose `topk_ids` are `-1`) and assert the valid outputs stay finite and are
  bit-identical to a clean-padding run.
  These prove padding is excluded from results, **not** physical compute-skipping:
  MoE rows are independent in the token dimension and TRTLLM activation quant is
  per-row, so skipping and compute-then-discard give identical valid outputs. The
  compute-savings of tile/block-granularity skipping is a benchmark concern, not a
  pytest assertion.
- Updated `test_deepep_v2_moe.py` to only use experts that support the new format.

### Results

Run on 8× B200 (SM100), FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13.0:

```                                                                                                                                    
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py                         20 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_bf16_moe.py                   5 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py (full matrix)      18 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_unquantized_backend_selection.py    25 passed                                                                   
tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_kernel_oracle.py                 1 passed                                                                   
tests/quantization/test_auto_round.py         97 passed, 5 failed                                                                      
```                                                                                                                                    

The 5 `test_auto_round.py` failures are all `test_auto_round_model` end-to-end engine
starts and fail identically on an unmodified tree: this checkout's compiled `_C`
extension is stale relative to the Python wrappers (`_C::gptq_marlin_repack()`
signature mismatch; `Failed to initialize MXFP4 GEMM: status=7` /
`Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 700` from `cutlass_mxfp4_group_mm`). Not
related to this change.

Tolerances in `test_deepep_v2_moe.py` are now scaled to the magnitude of the
reference output (`_scaled_tolerances`) rather than fixed. The output std grows
with the accumulation length, so a fixed `atol` was both too tight at the largest
shape — `(222, 1024, 2048)` fp8 failed with 25/454656 elements just over `6e-2`,
the tail of a smooth error distribution rather than any real defect — and far too
loose at the smallest. Measured `max_err/std` is stable per dtype across every
MNK (bf16 ≤ 0.06, fp8 ≤ 0.33), so the fraction is set per dtype with ~2x headroom.
This tightens the small shapes substantially (bf16 `(1, 256, 256)`: `atol` 1e-1 →
~2e-3) while removing the large-shape false failure.

`test_deepep_v2_moe.py` now pairs DeepEP V2 only with padding-aware TRTLLM experts
(`flashinfer_trtllm` for bf16, `trtllm_fp8` for fp8); the `flashinfer_cutlass`
(`Standard`) path was dropped since it cannot consume the padded layout under the
`is_superset` gate.

Local-run caveat: on a single-node NVLink box DeepEP v2 needs `EP_DISABLE_GIN=1`,
because it otherwise requires NCCL GIN/RDMA for `num_ranks > 1` and
`ncclDevCommCreate` fails. Multi-node genuinely needs GIN — do not set this
globally in CI.

### Model evals

gsm8k, 1319 questions, 5-shot, DP=4 + `--enable-expert-parallel                                                                        
--all2all-backend deepep_v2`, no `--enforce-eager` (eager mode never populates
`psum_recv_per_rank`, so the padded decode layout under test would not appear).
`tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/moe-refactor-dp-ep/config-b200-deepep-v2.txt`:

| model | experts | measured | threshold |                                                                                             
| --- | --- | --- | --- |                                                                                                              
| `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` | `TrtLlmBf16ExpertsModular` | 0.8893 | 0.88 |                                                                  
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct-FP8` | `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` | 0.8954 | 0.88 |                                                
| `nm-testing/Qwen3-30B-A3B-MXFP4A16` | `DeepGemmFP4Experts` (psum) | 0.8196 | 0.79 |                                                  

The mxfp4 row sits below the 0.88 W4A16 baseline because `--moe-backend=deep_gemm`
forces `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` activations, not because of padding: the same backend
without EP or DeepEP scores 0.8059, i.e. slightly *lower* than the padded EP run.

Backend selection was confirmed on the mxfp4 run rather than assumed — the server log
shows `Using 'DEEPGEMM_MXFP4' Mxfp4 MoE backend` / `Using DeepGemmFP4Experts` paired
with `DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize`. Before the `deep_gemm` routing fix this exact
configuration hit the activation-format assert in `modular_kernel.py`.

Not covered: `tests/evals/gpt_oss/configs/gpt-oss-20b-sm100-fi-mxfp4-mxfp8-trtllm-deepep-v2.yaml`.
gpt-oss's hidden size 2880 is rounded up to 3072 by
`DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize.maybe_roundup_layer_hidden_size` (2880 × bf16 = 5760 B →
6144 B transfer atom), but `modular_kernel.py:1526` allocates the finalize output as
`torch.empty_like(hidden_states)` at the unpadded 2880, so `output.copy_(combined_x)`
gets a 2880↔3072 shape conflict. That allocation does not honor the padded-output
contract the model side already assumes (`gpt_oss.py:415` slices
`self.experts(...)[:, : self.hidden_size]`). Separately,
`tests/evals/gpt_oss/test_gpqa_correctness.py:128` hardcodes `--enforce-eager`, which
leaves `psum_recv_per_rank` unpopulated, so this config could not exercise decode
padding even if it started.

## Notes
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change (tests + comments).
- Not a duplicate: introduces a new activation-format category rather than modifying existing dispatch behavior; no open PR adds a padded standard MoE format.

title: [Bugfix] Remove race in fused groupwise RMSNorm quantization
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Fix three flaky fused quantized RMSNorm failures observed in the H200 kernel CI job:
https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/85850#01a04456-3602-4e62-b405-0c986c85cdc3

The two group-64 scale failures were caused by a real shared-memory race in `warpReduceMaxSpecialized`. Each reduction stage read values written by other lanes in the preceding stage without synchronization. CUDA racecheck reported thousands of hazards for the failing specialization.

Replace that reduction with a register-based warp shuffle and write only the final lane-0 result back to shared memory. This supports both CUDA warp-32 and ROCm wave-32/wave-64 paths and also handles groups with more or fewer contributors than the warp width.

The remaining CUDA BF16 per-token FP8 case had bit-identical scales and one isolated output differing by exactly one E4M3 ULP out of 2,103,296 values. Keep scale comparison strict, but permit a bounded number of isolated one-ULP output differences for this specific CUDA/BF16/per-token/FP8 configuration.

## Why this is not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `fused quant layernorm`, `rms_norm_per_block_quant`, and `warpReduceMaxSpecialized`. No open PR addresses this reduction race or the per-token assertion.

The nearest open work is materially different:

- #45770 adds mixed input/weight dtype support.
- #49639 restores the scalar RMSNorm intermediate rounding boundary.
- #37196 refactors older static quantization kernels.

None changes `quantization/fused_kernels/layernorm_utils.cuh` or removes this shared-memory hazard.

## Performance

Direct H200 measurements timed the full fused op with preallocated outputs. Cold-L2 results used explicit L2 flushing; hot results used ten kernels per CUDA graph replay. Builds were alternated new/old/new or old/new/old to control for drift.

| BF16 + residual case | Cold L2, old -> new | Hot CUDA graph, old -> new |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2048x1024, group-64 INT8 | 22.82 -> 19.39 us (**15.0% faster**) | 17.81 -> 14.36 us (**19.3% faster**) |
| 2048x1024, group-64 FP8 | 24.48 -> 20.96 us (**14.4% faster**) | 19.68 -> 16.16 us (**17.9% faster**) |
| 2048x1024, group-128 FP8 | 22.50 -> 20.03 us (**11.0% faster**) | 17.67 -> 15.16 us (**14.2% faster**) |
| 1x1024, group-64 FP8 | 7.84 -> 7.84 us (no change) | 4.13 -> 4.01 us (**2.9% faster**) |
| 1x5120, group-64 FP8 | 12.45 -> 12.03 us (**3.3% faster**) | 7.77 -> 7.28 us (**6.3% faster**) |
| 1x5120, group-128 FP8 | 11.74 -> 11.52 us (**1.9% faster**) | 7.05 -> 6.77 us (**4.0% faster**) |

CUPTI Python was unavailable locally, so the FlashInfer benchmark helper used its CUDA-event/CUDA-graph fallback.

## Model evaluation

A seeded two-layer `Qwen2ForCausalLM` model-output equivalence check replaced all five RMSNorm outputs with FP8 group quantize/dequantize results and compared the unfused reference against this fused kernel over an 8x32 token batch:

| Group size | Token logits | Top-1 agreement | Max / mean abs logit diff | Mean cosine | Repeat deterministic |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 256 | 100% | 0 / 0 | 1.0 | yes, bitwise |
| 128 | 256 | 100% | 0 / 0 | 1.0 | yes, bitwise |

## Test plan and results

CUDA incremental build:

```bash
cmake --build --preset release --target install
```

Passed.

Original three failing cases:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[False-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1024-int8-group-64-tma-0-scale-ub-False]' \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[False-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1024-float8_e4m3fn-group-64-tma-0-scale-ub-False]' \
  'tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py::test_rms_norm[True-cuda:0-0-dtype0-True-2048x1027-float8_e4m3fn-per-token-tma-0-scale-ub-False]'
```

Result: `3 passed, 14 warnings`.

Additional correctness coverage:

- FP8 group-64 at 1x5120: passed.
- INT8 group-128 at 1x5120: passed.
- 100 repeated 2048x1024 group-64 scale comparisons across INT8 and FP8: all bitwise deterministic.

CUDA racecheck covered both the original group-64 specialization and wider group-64/group-128 configurations:

```text
RACECHECK SUMMARY: 0 hazards displayed (0 errors, 0 warnings)
```

Before this change, the original specialization reported four warning classes and thousands of hazards.

Applicable repository hooks:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fused_kernels/layernorm_utils.cuh \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_quant_layernorm.py
```

All passed.

## AI assistance

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block (mamba align context recompute)
author: Ledgero
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fixes #53477. DFlash and DSpark preserve the target KV cache and do not require the EAGLE-style trailing prefix-cache block drop. Scoping that drop correctly restores reusable Mamba checkpoints in `--mamba-cache-mode align` and prevents full-context recomputation on subsequent replies.

## Claims

- DFlash/DSpark no longer drop the last prefix-cache block solely because `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` also matches those methods.
- Existing EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP behavior is unchanged, including the `disable_eagle_block_drop` opt-out and its warning.
- `use_eagle()` remains unchanged for encoder shift, lookahead budgeting, and other existing specification-decoding behavior.

## Validation

Local reproduction (2x L40S, vLLM 0.26.0 layout, Qwen3.5-4B hybrid target + Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft, three-turn conversation with a shared 30x system prefix):

| Configuration | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash + mamba align | `cached=[0, 0, 0]` (full recompute every turn) | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| DFlash + mamba all | `[0, 0, 0]` | `[0, 560, 560]` |
| no spec + align/all | `[0, 1056, 1136]` | unchanged |
| MTP + align | no regression observed | no regression observed |

Acceptance comparison against upstream main, using the same models, seed, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=128`, warmed prefix cache, and the V2 runner:

| Method | Prompts | Baseline rate / length | This PR rate / length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DFlash | 32 | 0.14804 / 3.36859 | 0.15199 / 3.43189 |
| DSpark | 128 | 0.34399 / 3.40794 | 0.34512 / 3.41582 |

Targeted tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py::test_eagle_block_drop_can_be_disabled_without_disabling_eagle -q
# 8 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q
# 46 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k mamba_align
# 2 passed, 229 deselected

.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
git diff --check
```

Independent validations since opening:

- dtandersen: Intel Arc B70, Qwen3.8-27B-INT4 + DFlash2 - token corruption with prefix caching resolved.
- vedcsolution: 4x DGX Spark GB10 (TP4), GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2 - identical-request prefix hits `0/12,552` to `4,608`, TTFT `3.9s` to `1.55s`; an extra KDA over-truncation was also fixed (69-scenario tool-call suite `89` to `91`).
- positive666 closed #54041 as superseded by this PR after validating both approaches.

## Details

### Root cause

`SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle()` is a broad predicate for speculative decoding that reads target hidden states, and it intentionally matches `eagle`, `eagle3`, `mtp`, `dflash`, and `dspark`. #53388 derived `use_eagle_block_drop()` from that broad predicate.

EAGLE-style drafters construct a position's draft KV from the target hidden state **and the next token**. DFlash/DSpark construct it from the target hidden state alone. Therefore only EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP need the trailing EAGLE block drop; both DFlash and DSpark preserve the target KV cache.

For a prompt shorter than two Mamba blocks, the spurious back-off produced this sequence:

1. `last_cache_position == 0`, so the prompt was a single chunk ending off the Mamba block grid.
2. Mamba align mode only materializes a reusable recurrent state at a block-aligned chunk end.
3. `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()` converged the next turn's hit to zero, causing full-context recomputation.

### Implementation

- `vllm/config/speculative.py`: add `needs_eagle_block_drop()` for the precise EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP capability, and compose `use_eagle_block_drop()` from it plus `disable_eagle_block_drop`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: reuse `needs_eagle_block_drop()` in the warning condition. The existing split back-off, `KVCacheManager(use_eagle=...)`, offloading, and Mooncake paths now receive `False` for DFlash/DSpark without changing `use_eagle()`.
- `tests/test_config.py`: parameterize the existing config test over EAGLE3/MTP (drop) and DFlash/DSpark (no drop), both with the opt-out enabled and disabled.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: set the now-separate `use_eagle_block_drop` scheduler value in the Mamba-align EAGLE fixture.

The change is limited to the prefix-cache trailing-block policy. EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP retain the previous default behavior, and the existing explicit opt-out remains available.

### Related work and duplication

No open PR addresses #53477. Related work includes #53388 (merged opt-out for EAGLE trailing-block dropping), #30877 (Mamba align prefix caching), #42971, and #44082. None previously corrected the DFlash/DSpark classification.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Make native CUDA AttnRes the SM100 default
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Make the native CUDA Kimi-K3 AttnRes implementation the default for dense
`hidden_size=7168` inputs on SM100.

This PR:

- extends the existing register/TMEM kernel to cover block counts 0 through 8,
  optional prefix addition, optional output normalization, and block-bank
  writes;
- uses the existing source-chunk schedule for all supported block counts,
  while preserving a compile-time-folded common path;
- makes output normalization a compile-time specialization so the disabled
  path elides its shared-memory buffer, barrier, and arithmetic;
- delays the PDL wait until the first producer-dependent prefix or delta TMA
  for every native shape and triggers dependents after the producer TMAs;
- retains Triton as the fallback for unsupported devices and non-dense row
  layouts; and
- adds a reproducible CUDA-versus-Triton kernel benchmark.

Duplicate-work check: the author of #53524 coordinated moving its AttnRes PDL
handoff into this integrated change; that PR's remaining distinct scope is its
C=1 MoE/router work. #50760 changes warmup profiles only. Neither otherwise
extends the native kernel to all Kimi-K3 AttnRes call variants.

## Performance

Measured on GPU 7, an NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, with PyTorch 2.13.0 and CUDA 13.0.
Times are median microseconds; lower is better.

| Tokens | Blocks | Triton | CUDA | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 0 | 8.19 | 8.19 | 1.00x |
| 1 | 1 | 10.24 | 8.19 | 1.25x |
| 1 | 4 | 12.29 | 8.22 | 1.49x |
| 1 | 8 | 14.34 | 10.24 | 1.40x |
| 4096 | 8 | 204.77 | 122.88 | 1.67x |
| 8192 | 8 | 395.30 | 229.44 | 1.72x |

For the measured `M <= 16` cases with one or more block rows, CUDA was 1.20x
to 1.49x faster than Triton. The zero-block path tied Triton at 8.19 us.

In a captured single-token CUDA graph, profiler device rows for the CUDA
kernel were 3.67, 4.44, and 5.48 us for 1, 4, and 8 block rows. Full graph
replay medians were 8.03, 10.05, and 10.05 us, respectively.

The no-output-normalization specialization was neutral for the measured
`M <= 16` cases and up to 4.6% faster for larger measured shapes. For example,
the 8-block, M=1024 case improved from 40.86 to 38.98 us.

## Test Plan

```bash
cmake --build cmake-build-release --target _C_stable_libtorch
cmake --install cmake-build-release --component _C_stable_libtorch

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_attn_res.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_aux_attn_res_stream.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py -q

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_attn_res.py \
  --num-tokens 1 16 1024 4096 8192 \
  --num-blocks 0 1 4 8 --warmup-ms 50 --repeat-ms 200

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_attn_res.py \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/attn_res_kernel.cu \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/torch_bindings.cpp \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_attn_res.py \
  vllm/_custom_ops.py \
  vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/attn_res.py
```

## Test Result

- Incremental CUDA build: passed.
- Focused Kimi-K3 suite: 34 passed, 9 platform skips.
- Benchmark reference checks for 0, 1, 4, and 8 blocks: passed.
- All pre-commit hooks on changed files: passed.
- Model evaluation: run on the full Kimi-K3 checkpoint across five serving
  configurations; see Model Evaluation below. Kernel outputs and in-place
  mutations are additionally checked against the PyTorch reference across all
  block counts and fused variants.

## Model Evaluation

Full `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (MXFP4) on GB300 (SM100), vLLM
`0.17.2rc1.dev5039+g73b83949f`, across five serving configurations. GSM8K is
5-shot via `/v1/completions` (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95); OCRBench is
multimodal chat with thinking effort high (temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0).
Reported scores are GSM8K strict-match exact match and OCRBench Final Score
Norm.

| Config | Topology | GSM8K | OCRBench | Request errors |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| TP8 | TP8 | 95.53% (n=1319) | 89.3 (893/1000) | 0 |
| TEP8 | TP8 + EP | 97.27% (n=1319) | 89.3 (893/1000) | 0 |
| DEP16 | TP1 x DP16 x EP16 | 95.98% (n=1319) | 89.2 (892/1000) | 0 |
| TP8, `--max-num-seqs 16` | TP8, eval concurrency 8 | 96.36% (n=1319) | n/a | 0 |
| TP8, serial | TP8, eval concurrency 1 | 99.60% (n=250) | n/a | 0 |

No accuracy regression. GSM8K spans 95.5% to 97.3% across topologies, which is
within run-to-run variance for temperature-0.6 sampling (roughly +/-0.5 point
standard error at n=1319). OCRBench agrees to within 0.1 point across the three
multimodal configurations.

The two low-concurrency rows are the most direct check on this change: they
hold decode batches at 1 to 16 tokens, the small-batch regime this PR moves
from Triton onto the native kernel. The serial row's 99.60% reflects its
250-sample subset rather than a topology difference -- scoring the TP8 run's
own outputs on those identical 250 items gives 98.80%, a two-item difference.

AI assistance disclosure: AI assistance was used for implementation,
benchmarking, testing, and PR preparation. This PR is left as a draft until the
human submitter reviews every changed line and confirms they can defend the
change end-to-end.
