title: [Feature] Add fixed-token prefill scoring
author: aoshen02
body:
## Summary

This PR adds request-wise fixed-token prefill logprob scoring for OPD / top-k distillation:

- `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids`: candidate token IDs to score.
- `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_start`: absolute first causal prompt row to score.

The result is returned through the existing engine-core and `RequestOutput` paths for the V2 GPU runner.

This is M1 of RFC #56860. Per-position candidate lists (M2) are tracked there.

## Design

For a prompt of length `C` followed by student-generated output tokens, the hidden state at row `i` predicts token `i + 1`. Therefore the first output token is predicted by row `C - 1`. An OPD request sets:

```python
prompt_logprob_token_ids=teacher_topk_union
prompt_logprob_start=C - 1
```

This returns exactly the student probabilities needed for the output suffix. It does not score the earlier context rows. The dedicated result is source-row aligned and contains only requested rows; unlike `prompt_logprobs`, it does not add a leading `None` sentinel.

The candidate IDs are request-wise and fixed across positions, matching M1 of #56860. For each scheduled prefill chunk, the runner converts the absolute start into the chunk-relative row range, runs the lm-head only on that range, and gathers the requested IDs. The worker keeps one `[num_scored_rows, num_ids]` buffer per request, allocated on the first prefill chunk and written in place chunk by chunk, and emits it on the last chunk. Nothing is concatenated, and a request whose start is past the last scorable row emits an empty buffer rather than nothing.

This bounds intermediate memory by the requested suffix and candidate width rather than the full prompt. With `prompt_logprob_start=C-1`, the retained result is proportional to the generated output length. The implementation intentionally keeps the existing chunking and output plumbing instead of adding a new sparse protocol.

### Scoring reuses the sampler's kernel

Scoring calls the existing `compute_token_logprobs()` rather than computing `gather - logsumexp` in the logits' own dtype. That kernel already does exactly this gather: it accumulates max and logsumexp in fp32 and emits only the requested columns, so it materializes no `[tokens, vocab]` tensor either.

The kernel indexed `token_ids` as contiguous rows. It now takes a row stride for `token_ids`, as it already did for `logits`, so the request-wise IDs are passed as a broadcast `[rows, num_ids]` view (stride 0) and are never copied out per row. Existing callers pass contiguous tensors and are unaffected.

This matters numerically. Reducing over a 151936-entry bfloat16 vocabulary loses about 1e-1 of accuracy; against vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs` on the same forward pass, an in-dtype reduction disagreed by up to 7.78e-02. Through the shared kernel the values are bit-identical to `prompt_logprobs` (see Verification).

## Naming

The request-side parameters follow the existing `logprobs` / `prompt_logprobs` prefix convention: `SamplingParams.logprob_token_ids` already exists on main (#43463) and scores caller-supplied token IDs at sampled positions, so `prompt_logprob_token_ids` is its prefill counterpart.

The result is named after that parameter: `RequestOutput.prompt_token_id_logprobs`, a plain `[num_scored_rows, len(prompt_logprob_token_ids)]` float32 array whose columns follow the order the IDs were requested in. The IDs are not echoed back: the caller supplied them, so a container pairing them with the scores would carry nothing the caller does not already have, and nothing between the worker and the output needs them either.

Returning `list[dict[int, float]]` instead would cost ~22 MB of Python objects for a 1000-row, 242-ID request against ~1 MB for the array, and callers doing top-k distillation want the array rather than dicts they have to re-flatten.

## Token-in/token-out HTTP and the Rust frontend

`/inference/v1/generate` takes raw `SamplingParams`, so it accepts both parameters; the non-streaming response returns the scores as `prompt_token_id_logprobs`, a base64 `.npy` float32 array (`np.load(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(s)))`), the encoding `routed_experts` already uses on this endpoint. Streaming follows `prompt_logprobs`: the Python frontend omits the field, the Rust frontend rejects the request.

`EngineCoreOutput` is `array_like` on the Python side and decoded positionally by the Rust engine-core client (`Deserialize_tuple`), so the field is appended last there too, kept as the wire ndarray with its aux frame resolved in place; the server writes its float32 bytes straight into the `.npy`. The Rust frontend forwards `prompt_logprob_token_ids` / `prompt_logprob_start` and, since it bypasses `InputProcessor`, checks the candidate count against `max_logprobs` and the ids against the vocabulary, as it does for `logprob_token_ids`. Its `.npy` encoder is byte-identical to `numpy2base64`. OpenAI routes are unchanged.

## Limits

The candidate count is bounded by the existing `max_logprobs` (`--max-logprobs`, default 20), not by a new constant. One logprob per requested ID is returned per scored row, which is exactly the quantity that setting already bounds for `logprobs` and `prompt_logprobs`, and `-1` opens it to the whole vocabulary here too. A distillation workload wanting a few hundred candidates therefore needs the operator to raise `--max-logprobs`, the same opt-in the existing full-vocabulary path requires.

Because the default rejects any realistic candidate set, this is the first error most callers of the parameter will meet, so it names the value to set rather than just the setting:

```
Requested prompt_logprob_token_ids of length 242, which is greater than
max allowed: 20. Set max_logprobs (--max-logprobs) to at least 242.
```

Both spellings appear because `--max-logprobs` is not what a caller using `LLM(...)` sets. The sibling errors in `_validate_logprobs` carry no such hint; the asymmetry is deliberate, and easy to drop if reviewers would rather keep them uniform.

The parameter is implemented for the V2 GPU runner only, so the input processor rejects it with a `VLLMValidationError` naming `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` when that runner is not in use, rather than letting the V1 runner return `None`. `prompt_logprob_start` without `prompt_logprob_token_ids` is likewise rejected instead of being silently ignored.

`logprob_token_ids` keeps its own `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS = 128` because that number is physical: it is the row width `LogprobTokenIdsState` preallocates. Prompt scoring allocates per request, so it has no such structural bound and does not need a constant of its own.

On the output path the result is owned by `LogprobsProcessor` alongside sample and prompt logprobs, and reached through the same single `update_from_output` call. That also gives it the same `RequestOutputKind.DELTA` handling: like prompt logprobs it is popped, so a streaming request carries it on exactly one output at the end of prefill instead of re-attaching the array to every later delta.

It is kept out of `prompt_logprobs_dict` deliberately: `LogprobsTensors` carries an implicit target-token column and a rank column, neither of which is meaningful for a caller-fixed ID set, and `prompt_logprobs` prepends a `None` sentinel for position 0 that this result must not have. Reusing that container would mean populating two columns with placeholder values and then documenting that they are meaningless.

## Relationship to SGLang

SGLang main uses the same two concepts: request-wise `token_ids_logprob` and an absolute `logprob_start_len`. Its scheduler converts the absolute position to a per-chunk pruned range, and its logits processor applies the lm-head only to suffix hidden states. This V2 implementation follows that lifecycle and offset model while reusing vLLM's existing chunk helper and logprob kernel.

SGLang main does not currently expose a per-position candidate-ID API; this PR therefore does not add one. Per-position candidates are proposed as M2 in #56860.

## Scope / non-goals

This is M1 of #56860. It does not add per-position candidate lists (M2 in #56860), streaming updates, a scoring-only lifecycle, speculative/beam support, multimodal scoring, prefix-cache reads, or an OpenAI protocol field. Those can be evaluated separately if a concrete caller requires them.

This is complementary to open PR #39351 (generative scoring with `max_tokens=0`, which targets next-token scoring) and #49171 (skipping logits for unfinished chunk prefills). This PR scores arbitrary fixed IDs at selected prefill positions. No other open PR adds fixed-ID prefill scoring.

## Verification

All runs used the vLLM nightly container (`0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c`) on 4x GB200, with this branch's Python layer overlaid on the image's compiled package. Performance runs used a dedicated node with the checkpoint staged in `/dev/shm`.

### Correctness

`Qwen3-0.6B`, 193-token prompt (`193 % 64 == 1`, so the final prefill chunk holds a single token), 10 checks, all passing:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chunked prefill (64 tokens/chunk) row count vs unchunked | identical |
| Chunked values vs unchunked | max abs diff `0.00e+00` |
| Values vs vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs=-1`, same request | max abs diff `0.00e+00` |
| Full-vocab `prompt_logprobs=-1` row normalizes | logsumexp over 151936 entries = `+1.24e-07` |
| Row alignment (scan row offsets -2..+2 against HF) | offset 0 median `0.051`; ±1 median `2.43` / `2.43` |
| Result shape / dtype | `(92, 7)` float32 |
| vs HuggingFace `log_softmax` reference | median `5.12e-02` |

The last row needs a control, since vLLM and HuggingFace disagree on this model regardless of this feature. Running vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs` against the same HF reference on the same prompt gives median `4.95e-02`. The residual is the pre-existing vLLM-vs-HF gap (TRTLLM attention, bfloat16), not this path: the two agree to within 3%.

Row alignment is worth calling out separately: a ±1 row shift would still look plausible on a single-number comparison, but scanning offsets shows offset 0 fitting 47x better than its neighbours.

### Preemption

Preemption in the middle of a chunked prefill needs no special handling: the V2 scheduler reports a resumed request as a new one, and the runner drops the worker's state on preemption (`finish_requests` runs before `add_requests`), so the partial buffer is discarded and the re-prefill rebuilds it from the first chunk and emits it once. A resumed request whose prefill had already completed is the case that does need a guard:

A request resumed after preemption re-prefills its prompt plus the tokens it already generated. Those rows are not prompt positions, and its scores were emitted before the preemption, so the accumulator has to skip the resumed prefill — the same condition `compute_prompt_logprobs` already guards with `prompt_lens < prefill_len`. An earlier revision of this PR did not, which is not a silent numerical error: the resumed request emits a result on a step that must produce none, and the engine dies on the scheduler's own invariant.

```
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 2131, in update_from_output
    assert not prompt_token_id_logprobs
AssertionError
```

`test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption` is added to `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py`, next to the existing prompt-logprobs preemption test and reusing its setup for forcing chunking and preemption. Verified as a regression test in both directions: it fails with the above assertion against the pre-fix code and passes with the guard in place.

### Performance

`Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507`, TP4, 8192-token context, median of 5 reps, `prompt_logprob_start` set to score the last N rows:

| Scored rows x candidate IDs | median | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline (no scoring) | 75.2 ms | — |
| 1000 x 64 | 77.1 ms | +2.0 ms |
| 1000 x 242 | 77.7 ms | +2.6 ms |
| 1000 x 1024 | 80.6 ms | +5.5 ms |
| 4000 x 64 | 80.7 ms | +5.6 ms |
| 4000 x 242 | 81.7 ms | +6.6 ms |
| 4000 x 1024 | 88.9 ms | +13.7 ms |
| `prompt_logprobs=0`, all 8192 rows | 146.2 ms | +71.0 ms |

Row count dominates: at a fixed 64 IDs, going 1000 -> 4000 rows costs +3.6 ms, while at 1000 rows a 16x increase in candidates (64 -> 1024) costs +3.5 ms. In the intended distillation range the feature is roughly 10x cheaper than the existing full-row path while returning far more per row.

Cost grows with `rows x ids`, and at a wide candidate set it crosses over (separate run, baseline 76.6 ms):

| Scored rows x candidate IDs | median | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4000 x 1024 | 89.6 ms | +13.0 ms |
| 4000 x 4096 | 108.4 ms | +31.7 ms |
| 4000 x 16384 | 176.0 ms | +99.4 ms |
| `prompt_logprobs=0`, all 8192 rows | 146.1 ms | +69.5 ms |

So 16384 candidates over 4000 rows costs more than scoring every row with `prompt_logprobs=0` — though it returns 16384 candidates per row rather than one target token. The crossover is around 40M `row x id` pairs; beyond that, callers should compare against the full-row path. This is another reason the ceiling is `max_logprobs` rather than a constant of our own: the operator who opens that gate is the one accepting the cost.

### Commands

```bash
# correctness (11 checks) and the two sweeps above
MODEL=/models/Qwen3-0.6B ./_bench/run.sh test_correctness.py
MODEL=/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 TP=4 CONTEXT=8192 ./_bench/run.sh test_perf.py

# upstream tests covering the changed kernel and the preemption path
pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption \
          tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprobs_with_chunking_and_preemption
# -> 2 passed in 79.69s   (1 failed against the pre-fix code, as above)

pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py
# -> 3 passed in 1.12s    (adds the DELTA pop test)

pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k "logprob_token_ids"
# -> 6 passed in 5.22s    (adds the max_logprobs ceiling test, which also
#    pins that the message names the value to raise the setting to)

cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
# -> 102 passed, including python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding, which
#    round-trips fixtures generated from the current Python definitions
cargo fmt --check   # clean

pre-commit run   # ruff, ruff-format, mypy-3.10, SPDX, forbidden-imports: all pass
```

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and reran the tests above.

## Update 2026-09-17: re-verification after merging main, Rust e2e, audit fixes

Re-run on the merge commit with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` container of 2026-09-15 (`0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9`), this branch's Python overlaid, GB200.

- `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids`: 3 passed. The chunked-prefill/preemption test now also compares its scores against an unchunked, unpreempted run of the same requests (`rtol=0.1`: batch composition moves bf16 tail logprobs by ~2%, a misaligned row differs by nats). `tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py`: passes.
- Correctness script: 10/10 (chunked vs unchunked `0.00e+00`, vs `prompt_logprobs=-1` `0.00e+00`, row-offset scan picks 0).
- Perf (same setup as above, baseline 77.2 ms): 1000×64 +0.9, 1000×242 +1.6, 1000×1024 +3.9, 4000×64 +4.4, 4000×242 +5.6, 4000×1024 +11.3 ms; `prompt_logprobs=0` all rows +73 ms.
- **Cost with the feature off**: every per-step touchpoint mirrors the existing `prompt_logprobs_dict` one beside it (an unconditional worker call that returns on an empty dict, one dict comprehension over an empty dict, one `dict.get` per request in the scheduler, a trailing `None` field that `omit_defaults` drops from the wire). Measured A/B on one GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, 256 requests × 256 greedy decode steps, no scoring params, merge base vs this branch, two alternating rounds: 4.059 / 4.121 ms per step (base) vs 4.138 / 4.094 ms per step (branch); the round-to-round drift (1.5%) is larger than the A/B difference in either direction.
- **Rust frontend e2e** (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `vllm-rs` built from this branch, Qwen3-0.6B, chunked prefill at 64 tokens): the same `vllm serve` config brought up with the Python and the Rust frontend agrees on greedy completions, `echo` logprobs (the lm_eval/CI path) and `prompt_logprobs`, and a 32-request concurrent burst matches sequential greedy; 17/17. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client`: 113 passed. The binary has to come from this branch: the Rust client decodes `EngineCoreOutput` positionally with a fixed length, so a `vllm-rs` built before this PR rejects the appended field (`array had incorrect length, expected 17`).

**Audit fixes** (Codex, read-only, on the diff). Two configurations let a prefill skip prompt rows that must be scored, which would have emitted uninitialized rows; one is rejected here, the other is fixed for `prompt_logprobs` too. An explicit `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` is left to the caller, as it is for `prompt_logprobs`:

1. A KV connector prefix hit: `skip_reading_prefix_cache` gated only the local prefix cache, so a remote hit (NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake, MoRIIO) skipped rows for `prompt_logprobs` as much as for this feature. Split out as #57269, which makes the scheduler discard the hit for such requests; this PR depends on it and no longer carries that change itself.
2. `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` (Gemma3n) leaves non-sampled rows without the cross-decoder; rejected, as `prompt_logprobs` already is in `AsyncLLM`, but in `InputProcessor` so both engines agree.

Not changed: with `n > 1` every child scores the prompt and, in DELTA mode, each child's first output carries the matrix, exactly as `prompt_logprobs` behaves today.

## Update 2026-09-20: partially scored prefills

A second review found that a prefill can begin past `prompt_logprob_start`, leaving the leading rows of the score buffer unwritten while the buffer is still emitted at its full shape. Two ways in: a caller passing `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` explicitly (the force-set in `__post_init__` only applies when the flag is left `None`), and a streaming-input session, which extends its prompt in place and keeps its computed tokens, so the next prefill starts mid-prompt with `prefill_len == prompt_len`.

`prompt_logprobs` degrades on the same paths by returning fewer entries. This path was worse: the shape stayed correct and the leading rows carried uninitialized device memory. With the guard removed, the new regression test shows what a caller would have received:

```
array([[ 1.84094184e-40,  0.00000000e+00,  1.85467457e-40],
       [ 0.00000000e+00,  1.87048122e-40,  0.00000000e+00], ...
       [-2.19386425e+01, -2.27218456e+01, -2.54796581e+01]], dtype=float32)
```

The leading rows are denormals rather than log probabilities, and `exp` maps them to ~1.0 — the worst direction for a distillation target.

The worker now drops a request whose first scoring chunk starts past its first scored row (`chunk_start > req.start`), so the caller gets no scores rather than fabricated ones. This covers both entry points without an admission gate, and the condition is exact: a chunk starting before the first scored row still writes every scored row and is emitted as before.

Also in this update: `trace_decode_token_ids` rejects `prompt_logprob_token_ids` as it already rejects `prompt_logprobs`, and the row convention (row i predicts prompt token i+1, last prompt row excluded, result shape) is stated on the parameter and the result instead of only in the tests.

Verification: `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids` 4 passed, correctness 10/10 on the same GB200 setup. The new test is a real regression test: with the guard removed it fails with the array above.

## Update 2026-09-21: `/inference/v1/generate`, Python and Rust

Before this update the endpoint accepted the parameters, scored the prompt, and dropped the result: `GenerateResponse` had no field for it, and the Rust frontend silently discarded the parameters. Both frontends now return it (see "Token-in/token-out HTTP and the Rust frontend" above).

Verification (GB200, nightly container with this branch overlaid, Qwen3-0.6B, `vllm-rs` built from this branch):

- New `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_prompt_token_id_logprobs`: posts to `/inference/v1/generate` with `prompt_logprob_token_ids`, `prompt_logprob_start=1` and `prompt_logprobs=0`, decodes the `.npy`, checks the shape and that each target token's score matches `prompt_logprobs` from the same response. Passes with the Python frontend and with the Rust frontend; fails with a `vllm-rs` built from the previous head of this branch (same container, same engine), so the Rust change is what makes it pass.
- Whole file, Python frontend: 12 passed, 1 error (`test_generate_with_lora_adapter`: the offline container cannot download the adapter). Rust frontend: the new test passes; `test_generate_logprobs[1]`, `test_generate_logprobs[5]` and `test_stop_string_workflow` fail identically with the previous-head binary, so they predate this change.
- `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-text -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server`: all pass (new: lowering validation, streaming rejection, `.npy` bytes equal to `numpy2base64`). `cargo clippy` clean; `pre-commit` passes.

title: [Bugfix] Don't let a structured-output request sample from an unmasked row
author: ArcheyChen
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn. ## Purpose Part of #54437. `StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` constrains a row only while `apply_bitmask` holds, and a `-1` placeholder in the scheduled draft window sets `seen_padding`, so every row after it is filled with `_full_mask` — every token in the vocabulary allowed: ```python # vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens): apply_bitmask = not failed and not seen_padding and i >= constraint_start self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),)) if token == -1: seen_padding = True ``` That is sound when the `-1` means "`validate_tokens` rejected this draft": the first `-1` then sits at exactly the draft the grammar rejected, that draft's own row is still masked, so it is rejected and acceptance never reaches the permissive rows. It is not sound when the `-1` means "the drafts never reached the scheduler", which happens because the draft hand-off carries no identity — `DraftTokensHandler` keeps one slot that every `execute_model` overwrites (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`), and it also clears the payload entirely for a batch with no structured-output requests. The worker meanwhile verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens`, so acceptance can walk straight into rows that constrain nothing and the request emits tokens the grammar never allowed. #54437 has the full chain, a model-free reproduction on `main`, and field measurements. This PR is the fail-closed half: it makes the permissive rows unreachable regardless of why the drafts went missing. The identity fix for the hand-off is a separate change. **Not a duplicate of #56802.** That PR implements the other half of #54437 — identity for the hand-off, so the drafts are not lost in the first place. It is complementary: its lookup miss path falls back to exactly the invalidation this PR adds, so on a miss without this PR the bitmask still fails open. ## Change Carry, per structured-output request, how many leading drafts the bitmask actually constrained, and invalidate the drafts from that index on, so `is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0` pins the accepted length before sampling can reach a permissive row. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: `get_grammar_bitmask` fills `num_acceptable_drafts` with `len(strip_speculative_padding(window))`, reusing the helper #48200 introduced. - `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: `GrammarOutput.num_acceptable_drafts`, a defaulted field, so existing constructors keep working. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/structured_outputs.py`: `grammar_invalid_drafts` turns that into a mask over logit rows, built on device: a draft is invalid when its local position exceeds its request's `num_acceptable_drafts`. The local position is `expanded_local_pos`, which `expand_idx_mapping` derives from the device `cu_num_logits` — the same (request, position) keying `apply_grammar_bitmask` uses, so it stays correct when adaptive verification trims drafts on device and `cu_num_logits_np` is only an upper bound. When every request's scheduled drafts are within its limit (fully back-filled, the normal case) it returns `None` on the CPU and launches nothing. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: `sample()` calls it after applying the bitmask and hands the mask to the rejection sampler. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`: verification runs against `draft_sampled.masked_fill(mask, -1)`. `apply_sampling_params` and the watermarking context still receive the real draft ids, so penalties and bad-words are unaffected. - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`: shard the new per-request list the same way as the bitmask. No kernel change: `rejection_sampler_utils` already resamples a `-1` position straight from the target distribution rather than from the residual. That matters — `max(p - q, 0)` is the residual of a *genuine* rejection, and forcing one where `p ≈ q` collapses it across the vocabulary. When the drafts are fully back-filled nothing is invalidated and behaviour is unchanged. Absent the field — an older scheduler, or warmup — the whole window is invalidated, which is the conservative choice. Production diff is 85 added / 3 removed lines across those six files. ## Test Plan ```bash # Unit coverage for the new helper, plus the suites this PR's call paths touch. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \ tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q ``` `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py` — 5 cases covering `grammar_invalid_drafts`: whole window, partial window, nothing to do, per-request offset, and **adaptive verification with an uneven reallocation** (the device layout differs from `cu_num_logits_np`). **End-to-end reproduction.** Not committed, per review. Save the file below as `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py` and run it on `main` and on this branch: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py -q ``` It drives the real `GPUModelRunner.sample()` → `apply_grammar_bitmask` → `RejectionSampler` path with a bitmask whose leading rows carry a real mask and whose later rows are `_full_mask`, and with the drafts the worker holds on the GPU disagreeing with the scheduler's padded copy, which is what a lost hand-off produces. Temperature 0, one request, four logit rows, so it is deterministic.
tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 # SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project """Acceptance must stop at the last bitmask row that carries a real mask. `grammar_bitmask` stops constraining rows once it meets a -1 placeholder in the scheduled draft window, and the worker verifies the drafts it holds on the GPU rather than the scheduler's padded copy. When the two disagree -- the hand-off lost a step's drafts, see #54437 -- acceptance can walk into a row where every token is allowed. The grammar here admits only LEGAL. The scheduled window is back-filled one draft deep, so rows 0 and 1 carry a real mask and rows 2.. are `_full_mask`, while the drafts on the GPU would carry acceptance into row 2 and emit ILLEGAL. """ from types import SimpleNamespace import numpy as np import pytest import torch from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import GrammarOutput from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.states import NO_LOGPROBS from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.rejection_sampler import RejectionSampler from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.structured_outputs import StructuredOutputsWorker VOCAB = 128 K = 3 # drafts per step NUM_LOGITS = K + 1 # + the bonus row LEGAL = 7 ILLEGAL = 99 # Index of the first -1 in the scheduled window: rows 0..1 are masked. NUM_ACCEPTABLE = 1 def _bitmask() -> np.ndarray: """Rows 0..NUM_ACCEPTABLE constrained to LEGAL, the rest fully permissive.""" mask = np.zeros((NUM_LOGITS, cdiv(VOCAB, 32)), dtype=np.int32) for row in range(NUM_LOGITS): if row <= NUM_ACCEPTABLE: mask[row, LEGAL // 32] = 1 << (LEGAL % 32) else: mask[row, :] = -1 # every token allowed return mask def _input_batch(device: torch.device) -> SimpleNamespace: cu_np = np.array([0, NUM_LOGITS], dtype=np.int32) # draft_sampled = input_ids[logits_indices]; entry i + 1 is draft i, so the # drafts the GPU holds are [LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL]. input_ids = torch.tensor( [LEGAL, LEGAL, LEGAL, ILLEGAL], dtype=torch.int32, device=device ) return SimpleNamespace( num_reqs=1, req_ids=["g"], num_draft_tokens=K, num_draft_tokens_per_req=np.array([K], dtype=np.int32), input_ids=input_ids, logits_indices=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), positions=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int64, device=device), cu_num_logits_np=cu_np, cu_num_logits=torch.from_numpy(cu_np).to(device), idx_mapping_np=np.array([0], dtype=np.int32), idx_mapping=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_idx_mapping=torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), expanded_local_pos=torch.arange(NUM_LOGITS, dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32, device=device), seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound=torch.tensor([64], dtype=torch.int32), ) def _logits(device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor: """Every row prefers its own draft, so nothing but the mask can reject one.""" logits = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, VOCAB, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) logits[0, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[1, LEGAL] = 10.0 logits[2, ILLEGAL] = 10.0 # row 2 is permissive, so this wins there logits[3, LEGAL] = 10.0 return logits def _rejection_sampler(device: torch.device) -> RejectionSampler: sampler = object.__new__(RejectionSampler) sampler.num_speculative_steps = K sampler.enable_adaptive_verification = False sampler.use_block_verification = False sampler.synthetic_conditional_rates = None sampler.watermark_key = None zeros_f = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) # greedy sampler.sampler = SimpleNamespace( compute_nans=False, logprobs_mode="raw_logprobs", use_fp64_gumbel=False, apply_sampling_params=lambda logits, *args, **kwargs: logits, sampling_states=SimpleNamespace( temperature=SimpleNamespace(gpu=zeros_f), seeds=SimpleNamespace(gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)), max_num_logprobs=lambda _: NO_LOGPROBS, ), req_states=SimpleNamespace( prefill_len=SimpleNamespace( gpu=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) ) ), ) return sampler @pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="Requires CUDA") def test_acceptance_stops_at_the_last_masked_row(): device = torch.device("cuda") input_batch = _input_batch(device) logits = _logits(device) runner = object.__new__(GPUModelRunner) runner.device = device runner.vocab_size = VOCAB runner.batch_sharder = None runner.sampler = None runner.model = SimpleNamespace(compute_logits=lambda hidden: logits) runner.rejection_sampler = _rejection_sampler(device) runner.speculator = SimpleNamespace(draft_logits=None) runner.structured_outputs_worker = StructuredOutputsWorker( max_num_logits=NUM_LOGITS, vocab_size=VOCAB, device=device, mask_stride=NUM_LOGITS, num_bonus_tokens=1, ) grammar_output = GrammarOutput(["g"], _bitmask()) # The scheduler reports how many leading drafts the bitmask constrained. # Absent on an older scheduler, where the whole window is invalidated. grammar_output.num_acceptable_drafts = [NUM_ACCEPTABLE] hidden = torch.zeros(NUM_LOGITS, 8, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) sampler_output, num_sampled, _ = runner.sample(hidden, input_batch, grammar_output) accepted = int(num_sampled[0].item()) emitted = sampler_output.sampled_token_ids[0, :accepted].tolist() assert ILLEGAL not in emitted, ( f"emitted {emitted}: a draft verified against a permissive row was " f"accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint" ) # Draft 0 may be accepted; draft 1 must not be, because accepting it moves # sampling into row 2, which constrains nothing. assert accepted == NUM_ACCEPTABLE + 1 assert emitted == [LEGAL] * accepted ```
## Test Result End-to-end reproduction on `main` @ `2798f668`: ``` E AssertionError: emitted [7, 7, 99, 7]: a draft verified against a permissive row was accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint E assert 99 not in [7, 7, 99, 7] 1 failed, 14 warnings in 1.00s ``` Token 7 is the only token the grammar admits; token 99 is one it never admits. On this branch, same base: ``` 1 passed, 14 warnings in 1.26s ``` and the Test Plan selection is `71 passed, 1 xfailed`. ### Model evaluation One RTX 4090, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, Qwen3-8B + `Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` (K=4), `--async-scheduling`, xgrammar. `lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 200`: | | exact_match, strict-match | exact_match, flexible-extract | |---|---|---| | `main` @ `0bfc7a15` | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | | this PR @ `ec112592`, same base | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | gsm8k carries no structured-output requests, so that is the "speculative decoding is untouched" half. For the structured-output half, a mixed grammar + plain load with every grammar response validated against its JSON schema (4 concurrency mixes, 49 grammar requests) gives 0 schema violations, 0 `grammar rejected tokens` and 0 `Failed to advance FSM` on both `main` and this PR — which is the expected result at `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, where the hand-off does not get clobbered. Both were measured at `ec112592`. The review round since changed only how the invalid drafts are located, and that code runs only for a batch that holds a structured-output request whose drafts were not fully back-filled — which neither gsm8k (no grammar requests) nor the `pp=1` load (always fully back-filled) produces. I have not re-run them for that reason; happy to if you want the numbers on the current head. Beyond that: both this change and the identity fix have been running in production on a 2-node x 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`, `tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding, K=7, xgrammar). Before them, `tool_choice=required` and `json_schema` failed 100% of the time whenever a second structured-output request was resident; after, 72/72 concurrent grammar requests complete with zero `grammar rejected` lines and zero engine errors. Independently, @xinli-sw [reports](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54442#issuecomment-5822629259) that this PR fixes a `pipeline_parallel_size=2` x `tensor_parallel_size=8` deployment with DSpark (K=3) on 16x B200. ## AI assistance This PR contains AI-generated code. The root-cause analysis, the instrumentation behind the numbers in #54437, and the patch were produced with Claude, with the consumption-time-snapshot idea and the fail-closed requirement contributed by GPT-5.6. The adaptive-verification issue in review was caught by an AI reviewer and fixed with Claude. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and the evaluation above, and validated the behaviour end-to-end on the deployment described. Commits carry: ``` Co-authored-by: GPT-5.6 Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) ```

title: [Kernel][Qwen] Add Hopper LL-GEMM tuning table for Qwen4Exp
author: zigzagcai
body:
## Purpose

Add an independently tuned Hopper (`SM90`) LL-GEMM table for Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decode, using the existing shared CuTe DSL skinny-GEMM implementation.

Following review feedback, the earlier Hopper-only HyperConnection fusion has been removed. The final diff only:

- adds explicit H200 plans for the model's TP=4 local projection shapes;
- covers selected decode batch sizes from `M={1,2,4,8,16}` instead of reusing the SM103 table or restricting Hopper to `M=1`;
- falls back to the standard linear implementation whenever a shape/M point did not show a repeatable H200 win; and
- adds table-integrity and H200 correctness coverage for every selected plan.

Dispatch remains narrowly guarded to SM90, BF16, unquantized layers, packed row-major inputs, and exact table entries. SM103 behavior is unchanged, and unsupported shapes, M values, dtypes, layouts, quantization methods, and platforms retain the existing path.

### H200 tuning methodology

Hardware: NVIDIA H200 SXM, BF16. Shapes are the actual local `(N, K)` weights in a TP=4 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next deployment.

I swept all ten projection candidates at every `M` in `{1,2,4,8,16}` (50 shape/M points). Depending on shape, each point searched 80-666 legal combinations of:

- block size: `32,64,96,128,160,192,224,256`;
- outputs per CTA: `1,2,3,4,6,8`;
- vector width: `1,2,4,8`;
- K unroll: `1,2,4,8`, plus the full tile count where legal; and
- dynamic versus static K.

Finalists were measured with 21 paired hot CUDA-graph replays and 101 paired L2-flush replays. A plan was retained only when its median improvement over `torch.nn.functional.linear` was at least approximately 3% in both regimes. The retained plan was then remeasured independently. This produced 31 plans across nine shapes; the other 19 points use the standard linear fallback.

The table below reports the independent hot-replay speedup for retained plans. `fallback` means the point was swept but failed the dual hot/L2-flush qualification. In particular, HC-up `(10240, 320)` remains on the standard implementation for every tested M.

| Local `(N, K)` | M=1 | M=2 | M=4 | M=8 | M=16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(4096, 2560)` | 1.382x | 1.199x | fallback | fallback | fallback |
| `(2560, 1536)` | 1.495x | 1.288x | 1.096x | fallback | fallback |
| `(24, 2560)` | 2.117x | 2.257x | 2.274x | 2.397x | 1.809x |
| `(3584, 2560)` | 1.376x | 1.226x | fallback | fallback | fallback |
| `(640, 2560)` | 2.686x | 2.219x | 1.971x | 1.465x | fallback |
| `(320, 2560)` | 2.285x | 2.178x | 2.062x | 1.650x | 1.254x |
| `(62080, 2560)` | 1.165x | 1.116x | fallback | fallback | fallback |
| `(336, 10240)` | 2.071x | 1.850x | 1.580x | 1.172x | fallback |
| `(10240, 320)` | fallback | fallback | fallback | fallback | fallback |
| `(320, 10240)` | 2.111x | 1.865x | 1.466x | 1.164x | fallback |

All 31 independently validated points beat the standard linear path, with speedups from 1.096x to 2.686x and maximum absolute error no larger than `0.015625`.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Correctness, fallback, routing, and table-integrity tests on H200.
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py

# Repository checks for the final two-file diff.
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py \
  tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py
```

The serving A/B used the parent of this PR, `e0d27040ddcc5ac31cf01c5b04a7d764ccba656d`, as the baseline. Baseline and optimized servers used the same four H200 GPUs and arguments, with separate cold vLLM caches:

```text
vllm serve <Qwen3.8-Flash-Next> \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-Flash-Next \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --moe-backend triton \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --language-model-only \
  --load-format fastsafetensors
```

Matched sequential decode workload: 2 warmups plus 24 measured requests, exactly 2048 input tokens and 512 output tokens per request, concurrency 1, temperature 0, `ignore_eos`, seed 401.

## Test Result

### End-to-end serving A/B

Both variants completed 24/24 requests.

| Metric | Baseline | SM90 tuned table | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 136.20 tok/s | 155.47 tok/s | **+14.15%** |
| Request throughput | 0.2660 req/s | 0.3037 req/s | **+14.15%** |
| Median TPOT | 6.279 ms | 5.478 ms | **-12.75%** |
| Mean TPOT | 6.342 ms | 5.521 ms | **-12.95%** |
| P99 TPOT | 7.388 ms | 6.421 ms | **-13.09%** |
| Median TTFT | 447.87 ms | 406.89 ms | -9.15% |

The primary claim is decode TPOT/throughput. TTFT was noisy in this sequential workload and is included for completeness rather than claimed as a robust improvement. On a per-request basis, 23 of 24 requests had lower TPOT with the tuned table; their mean speedup was 1.151x.

### Correctness and repository checks

all hooks passed
