title: [ROCm] Give turboquant boundary layers a layout-compatible backend
author: stefankoncarevic
body:
## Purpose

The `(MI300) LM Eval TurboQuant KV Cache` group, added by [#50519](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50519), fails all four of its tests in [AMD CI build 12548](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12548/list?sid=01a0609c-72b4-4312-b09a-ec5852db1fc7&tab=output). Each server exits during startup with:

```
ValueError: No KV cache layout satisfies every supported set: [['LHBNC', 'LBHNC'], ['LBNHC']].
```

A `turboquant_*` KV cache never covers the whole model. `TurboQuantConfig.get_boundary_skip_layers` keeps the first and last two attention layers of a dense model at the native dtype, so those layers select an attention backend of their own while every other layer selects `TURBOQUANT`. On ROCm they land on `ROCM_ATTN`, first in the platform's priority list, which reads `LHBNC` or `LBHNC` and keeps the K and V groups in separate planes. `TURBOQUANT` reads only `LBNHC`, because it packs K and V into one slot per token and head. One layout has to serve the whole worker, so the intersection is empty and `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` raises.

This treats an empty intersection as a reason the backend is invalid for the layer. The boundary layers then get `TRITON_ATTN`, which is stride-aware and declares no layout preference, and the run resolves to `LBNHC`. The same filter applies to an explicit `--attention-backend`, a path that already tolerates a mismatch on a `turboquant_*` run because no single backend can serve every layer. Runs whose KV cache dtype is not `turboquant_*` are unaffected.

## Test Plan

On one MI300X (gfx942), the failing group itself:

```bash
pytest -s -v evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py \
    --config-list-file=configs/models-turboquant.txt
```

and the ROCm selector unit tests:

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_attention_backends_selection.py
```

## Test Result

The group is green, 4 passed in 10m35s over all 1319 questions per config.



---

<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][ROCm] Fix MoRI-IO KV block-offset for speculative decoding (MTP)
author: MohitAMD
body:
## Summary
Under **speculative decoding (e.g. MTP)** over MoRI-IO PD-disaggregation, the prefill
(producer) KV-cache manager reserves `num_speculative_tokens` lookahead blocks that the
decode (consumer) side never allocates. The producer's local block list therefore ends up
**longer** than the consumer's remote list, and the first prefill→decode KV write crashed
with `ValueError: local_block_ids longer than remote_block_ids` (e.g. 8003 vs 8000 at n=3),
making MTP unusable on MoRI-IO.

## Fix
The surplus is trailing lookahead scratch, not prompt KV, so it must be dropped **before**
the producer saves — not masked at transfer time.

- **Clamp on the WRITE producer save path** (`MoRIIOConnectorScheduler`): a new
  `_clamp_to_prompt_blocks` trims each **full-attention** KV group to its prompt length
  (`ceil(num_prompt_tokens / block_size)`), block-size-agnostic and per-group so it works
  under the hybrid multi-KV-group manager. Sliding-window groups are left untouched.
- **Chunked-prefill final-chunk detection by token progress** (`_is_final_prefill_chunk`):
  the save fires when `num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled >= num_prompt_tokens`, which is
  immune to speculative-lookahead block inflation (a block-count check is not). This also
  correctly handles a final chunk that allocates **no new blocks** (`new_block_ids is None`),
  which previously dropped the save and hung the decode leg.
- **Keep the loud invariant**: `compute_block_transfer_offsets` still raises on a genuinely
  longer-local list — a real bug in READ mode — rather than silently clamping. The relaxation
  lives only in the WRITE save path where the surplus is legitimate.
- **Fail closed on unsupported combos**: MoRI-IO WRITE mode + sliding-window attention (with
  or without spec decode) raises `NotImplementedError`, because the positional prompt-prefix
  save would ship out-of-window null blocks. READ + SWA (+ spec) is unaffected: block ids are
  pre-clipped to computed tokens before the connector sees them.

## Tests
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_connector.py`: WRITE-mode clamp (single- and
  multi-group), chunked-prefill accumulation, the lookahead final-chunk regression (final
  chunk with `new_block_ids=None`), and the WRITE spec+SWA guard (reachable only under a
  uniform SWA model with `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_kv_layout.py`: retains the loud longer-local

This is the only open PR addressing MoRI-IO KV block-offset handling under speculative
decoding. It builds on (does not duplicate) the upstream hybrid/multi-KV-group MoRI-IO
refactor: it keeps that connector's structure and guards, and only adds the spec-decode
clamp + lookahead-safe final-chunk detection on top.

title: [Kernel][HY V4] Add Triton iHC pre/post fallback
author: linitra24
body:
Add in-tree Triton implementations for the HY V4 iHC pre and post operations.

The runtime dispatch order is:

1. Use HPC-Ops when enabled and supported.
2. Otherwise use the Triton implementation on NVIDIA CUDA with FP16/BF16 inputs.
3. Fall back to the existing eager PyTorch implementation for unsupported configurations.

The Triton implementation is adapted from [sglang#36805](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36805).

## Purpose

Provide an in-tree, portable iHC implementation for NVIDIA GPUs where HPC-Ops is unavailable or unsupported, while retaining the existing eager implementation as the final fallback.

## Test Plan

- Kernel benchmark: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_hy_v4_ihc.py` on one NVIDIA H20 (SM90), using CUPTI timing with cold L2, FP16/BF16, hidden sizes 4096/6144, and 1-8192 tokens.
- Accuracy and end-to-end runtime: serve `Hy4-preview-FP8` on four H20 GPUs with TP=8. Run the full GSM8K test set through the completion API with lm-eval (`local-completions`, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 1319 samples, concurrency 8, `max_gen_toks=256`, `max_length=8192`).
- End-to-end performance: serve Hy4-preview-FP8 on eight H20 GPUs with TP=8, MTP and prefix caching disabled. Send 100 requests with 2048 input and 256 output tokens at 10 requests/s.

## Test Result

Kernel results (Triton vs. eager):

- iHC pre: **2.88x-9.97x** faster.
- iHC post: **3.91x-12.83x** faster.

---

Full GSM8K results:

| Backend | Strict exact match | Flexible exact match |
|---|---:|---:|
| Eager | 86.58% | 85.60% | 
| Triton | 86.20% | 85.97% | 

Accuracy is comparable: both metric differences are 0.38 percentage points and are smaller than their approximately 0.94-0.97 percentage-point standard errors, so no measurable accuracy regression was observed.

---

Eight-H20 end-to-end serving results:

Metric | Eager | Triton | Change
-- | -- | -- | --
Output throughput | 214.51 tok/s | 267.57 tok/s | +24.74%
Total token throughput | 1930.55 tok/s | 2408.13 tok/s | +24.74%
Mean TTFT | 42634.72 ms | 32370.70 ms | -24.07%
Mean TPOT | 275.70 ms | 223.66 ms | -18.87%

The HPC-Ops implementation was not benchmarked because the current implementation only supports SM100/SM103, while H20 is SM90.

title: [Performance][DSv4] Size dequant gather launch grid by rows
author: aoshen02
body:
## Summary

`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache_cutedsl` launched `grid = (num_reqs, 1024)`. The SWA call gathers 128 rows per request and the compressed call ~1k rows, so most of the 32k CTAs did no work; measured effective bandwidth was 0.35–2.4 TB/s on GB200 (8 TB/s HBM). `grid.y` is now picked per call from the launch shape.

## Where this kernel is hot: batch-invariant (deterministic) serving

The kernel came in with vllm-project/vllm#42236, which profiled **prefill** — one request, thousands to 262k rows per launch. At that shape a fixed `grid.y = 1024` is close to optimal, and this PR changes nothing there (table below). The shape that is badly served by a fixed grid is **many requests × few rows each**, and that is exactly what batch-invariant DSv4 decode produces on every step. Four things in `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention` combine to put this kernel on the BI decode critical path:

1. **BI decode has to use the sparse kernel, and only the sparse path gathers.** `_forward_decode` dispatches on `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL`. The `paged` path calls `flash_mla_with_kvcache` straight on the paged cache and never touches this kernel; its KV split comes from the in-kernel planner (`tile_scheduler_metadata` / `num_splits`), which plans over the whole batch, so the reduction order moves with batch composition. The `sparse` path instead materializes compressed KV and SWA KV into a dense workspace with two `dequantize_and_gather_k_cache` calls per layer and feeds `flash_mla_sparse_fwd`. So with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` + `VLLM_DS4_DECODE_KERNEL=sparse` this kernel runs **84 times per decode step**, where the non-BI (`paged`) configuration runs it zero times per decode step. The cost measured below is a cost that only the BI arm pays.

2. **BI decode is one token per request.** The BI branch requires `query_len == 1` for every request and pins `max_gather` to `window_size` (128). A decode step is therefore 32 requests × 128 rows — 4096 rows spread over 32×1024 = 32768 CTAs with the old grid. Measured 18.9 µs for work that takes 3.0 µs.

3. **BI replaces the batch maximum with model capacity, so the caller's row bound stops being informative.** Outside BI, `max_compressed` is the batch max of `seq_len / compress_ratio`. Under BI it must be `ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, otherwise the flattened KV stride and every request's base index depend on its neighbours' lengths and a request would not land at the same addresses alone and in a packed batch. For the compressed gather that makes `out.shape[1] - offset` = 262272 while the real work is ~1k rows per request. This is why `ceil(max_rows / 4)` alone cannot pick the grid in this configuration and the total-CTA cap is the term that actually binds.

4. **BI prefill runs one request per chunk.** The grouped prefill chunk plan picks workspace dimensions and offsets from all requests in a chunk, so BI mode puts each request in its own chunk to keep N, M, gathers, indices and launch geometry dependent on that request alone. Prefill launches therefore arrive as many `num_reqs = 1` calls rather than a few batched ones.

Net effect on the configuration we run (DSv4-Flash-Base, GB200 DP8/EP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, sparse decode): **1.66 ms → 0.51 ms of gather per decode step**. This is one of three kernel-side changes (#18, this, #20) that together take BI=1 from −10.8 % to +1.3 % output throughput against the best BI=0 run at 256 concurrency.

`grid.y` is now a runtime `Int32` kernel argument, computed per call in the wrapper:

```
grid.y = max(1, min(ceil(max_rows / 4), ceil(8192 / num_reqs)))
```

Two terms, both measured rather than assumed:

| term | what it does | dropping it costs |
|---|---|---|
| `ceil(max_rows / 4)` | one row per warp is all the parallelism a request can use; a CTA has 4 warps | 32-request SWA decode 3.1 → 18.7 µs (**6.1×**), because grid.y would stay 1024 |
| `ceil(8192 / num_reqs)` | hold the whole grid near 8192 CTAs, where measured throughput plateaus at every request count | 1-request 262144-row gather 67.7 → 276.1 µs (**4.1×**) if the first term is capped low enough to serve decode; 32-request decode 10.8 → 21.9 µs (**2.0×**) if it is not |

`max_rows` is the caller's upper bound on rows per request (`out.shape[1] - offset`). The public signature is unchanged — the grid is no longer a compile-time property of the kernel, so one compiled variant serves every launch shape.

The 8192-CTA plateau was found by sweeping grid.y per shape with the same interleaved harness as the tables below: single-request gathers keep improving up to 8192 CTAs (262144 rows: 71.0 µs at 1024, 69.9 at 4096, 67.9 at 8192), 4-request prefill peaks at 2048 per request (11.4 → 9.7 µs), and 32-request decode peaks at 256 per request — all three are the same total.

This supersedes the first version of this PR (compile-time `grid.y = clamp(ceil(max_rows/4), 1, 128)`), which made single-request gathers of 16k–262k rows — the prefill / full-context shapes exercised by vllm-project/vllm#42236 — up to 3.9× slower than the original grid (262144 rows: 275 vs 70 µs).

## Numerics

Each CTA does exactly the same per-row work as before; only the row→CTA assignment changes. Every case in the shape sweep is `torch.equal` to the old kernel and to the Triton reference for every `grid.y`.

E2E gate (DSv4-Flash-Base, GB200 DP8/EP8, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, cudagraph `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, together with #18): **512/512 bitwise vs the previous kernel** (g0 vs baseline), run-to-run r1/r2/r3 pairwise 512/512, batch-invariance and prefill/decode rescore gates bitwise.

## Perf

GB200, same shape set as vllm-project/vllm#42236 in the same table format, plus the batch-invariant decode shapes this PR targets. Every number in a row comes from **one process where the three arms are captured as separate CUDA graphs and replayed round-robin**, 61 replays each, median reported — so clock drift and cache state hit all columns equally and small deltas are meaningful. Block tables rotate over 8 disjoint regions of a 2.4 GB cache so nothing is served out of L2; absolute values therefore differ from #42236's harness. Raw data: `agent_run/results/kernel-opt-20260902/dequant-gather/v4/ab3_r1.json`.

title: [Perf] Accumulate Conformer attention scores with baddbmm
author: Levius-Fubuki
body:
## Purpose

Conformer relative attention currently materializes the content scores, adds
the shifted positional scores, and then launches a separate in-place scale.
This PR uses standard `torch.baddbmm` to accumulate the scaled content scores
directly into the scaled positional scores:

```text
before: {bmm: 2, add: 1, mul_: 1}
after:  {bmm: 1, baddbmm: 1}
```

This removes one score-sized intermediate and the separate add/scale kernels.
It keeps one portable PyTorch path with no custom kernel, architecture gate,
device branch, or device-specific tuning.

## Test Plan

### Regression test

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/test_conformer_encoder.py
```

The test instantiates the real module and compares final output and post-softmax
attention against the pre-change implementation for sequence lengths 2 and 8.
It covers masking and production-style batch-1 positional broadcasting.

### Lint and pre-commit

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  tests/models/multimodal/test_conformer_encoder.py \
  vllm/model_executor/models/conformer_encoder.py
```

### RTX 4090 CUDA Graph microbenchmark

```bash
python tools/bench_vllm_conformer_baddbmm.py \
  --mode benchmark \
  --batches 1 4 16 --heads 4 8 \
  --sequences 64 128 256 512 1024 \
  --head-dims 32 64 --dtypes float16 bfloat16 \
  --warmups 25 --iterations 200 --repeats 5 \
  --output portability-benchmark.csv
```

Hardware/software: NVIDIA RTX 4090, driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.0,
PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. No configuration changes.

| B | H | T | D | dtype | Old p10/p50/p90 (us) | New p10/p50/p90 (us) | p50 speedup | Old/New extra peak allocation (MiB) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---|:---|:---|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 64 | 64 | FP16 | 9.18 / 9.18 / 9.20 | 8.28 / 8.28 / 8.29 | 1.11x | 0.16 / 0.12 |
| 1 | 8 | 128 | 32 | BF16 | 9.62 / 9.80 / 10.54 | 8.71 / 9.55 / 9.56 | 1.03x | 1.25 / 1.00 |

| 16 | 4 | 256 | 64 | BF16 | 100.56 / 100.62 / 100.73 | 93.93 / 94.03 / 94.05 | 1.07x | 40.03 / 32.03 |

| 16 | 8 | 1024 | 64 | BF16 | 4084.58 / 4085.03 / 4085.41 | 3514.84 / 3515.28 / 3515.57 | 1.16x | 1280.25 / 1024.25 |

Across all 120 CUDA Graph rows, the geometric-mean speedup was approximately
1.11x; the median was 1.09x and the observed minimum was 1.03x. All 240
eager/CUDA Graph rows passed numerical validation with zero OOM rows and zero
harness-reported allocation regressions.

The non-contiguous Q/K operands require the same two reshape copies in both the
old `matmul` path and the new path. The measured allocation reduction comes
from removing the additional score-sized add result. FP16/BF16 changed-input
CUDA Graph replay and a focused `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` smoke check also
passed.

The standalone harness, raw CSV, and gate output are available in the
[benchmark artifact Gist](https://gist.github.com/Levius-Fubuki/c125b9c6696331d65acef27d3d7fe5f1).

These are isolated score-chain results from one RTX 4090 run, not end-to-end

title: [Perf][Distributed] Add low-SM multimem reduce-scatter for SM100/SM103
author: zyongye
body:
## Purpose

Add a low-SM MNNVL reduce-scatter backend for TP2, TP4, and TP8 MNNVL groups on SM100 or SM103. The kernel uses `multimem.ld_reduce` to reduce across the NVLS multicast mapping and ordinary local stores for each rank-owned output shard. It launches at most 8 CTAs per GPU with 1024 threads and an 8-way vector unroll.

The dispatcher uses total input message bytes and keeps a single explicit backend policy:

- `<= 16 MiB`: existing MNNVL Lamport reduce-scatter.
- `> 16 MiB` and `<= 64 MiB`: multimem reduce-scatter when its gate passes.
- `> 64 MiB`: return `None` to the existing NCCL reduce-scatter fallback.

The multimem gate requires TP2, TP4, or TP8, exact SM100 or SM103, BF16/FP16/FP32, valid 16-byte shard alignment, a group-spanning NVLS multicast mapping, and non-batch-invariant execution. Unsupported topology, architecture, dtype, alignment, mapping initialization, and message size all fail closed to the existing fallback.

The 64 MiB symmetric staging buffer is allocated lazily on the first eligible reduce-scatter. All ranks reduce their local allocation result before entering symmetric-memory rendezvous, so a failure on one rank makes the whole group fall back without stranding peers.

The 64 MiB upper cutoff is deliberately below the measured hot-cache crossover near 76 MiB and bounds the added symmetric staging allocation. Production-path timings include the staging copy and required barriers and report the median maximum-rank CUDA event time on 8x B300:

| Input size | Multimem, 8 CTA | NCCL | Multimem vs. NCCL |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 MiB, hot | 137.38 us | 148.83 us | 7.7% faster |
| 64 MiB, cold L2 | 141.18 us | 150.27 us | 6.0% faster |
| 76 MiB, hot | 161.79 us | 162.21 us | 0.3% faster |
| 96 MiB, hot | 198.53 us | 180.67 us | 9.9% slower |

A reusable multi-rank benchmark is included under `benchmarks/kernels/` and checks every eager and captured workspace against an FP32 distributed reference before timing.

This does not duplicate an existing contribution. Open PR and issue searches for SM100/SM103, multimem, custom all-reduce, and reduce-scatter found no implementation of this path. #50182 only adjusts symmetric-memory multicast selection, #44080 adjusts sequence-parallel fusion limits, and #53852 adds a FlashInfer all-reduce cutoff override.

## Test Plan

```bash
cmake --build --preset release --target install

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py \
  -k 'mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_platform_gate or mnnvl_reduce_scatter_backend_gate or cross_node_mnnvl_gate' -q

env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py \
  -k mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter -v -s

env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  .venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_multimem_reduce_scatter.py \
  --dtype bf16 --blocks 8

env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  .venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_multimem_reduce_scatter.py \
  --message-bytes 64M --dtype f16 --blocks 8 \
  --num-workspaces 2 --warmup-replays 4 --samples 11

env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
  .venv/bin/python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_multimem_reduce_scatter.py \
  --message-bytes 64M --dtype f32 --blocks 8 \
  --num-workspaces 2 --warmup-replays 4 --samples 11

pre-commit run --files \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_multimem_reduce_scatter.py \
  csrc/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.cuh \
  csrc/custom_all_reduce.cuh \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.cu \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter_ops.cpp \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/ops.h \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py \
  vllm/_custom_ops.py \
  vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py
```

## Test Result

- Incremental CUDA build: passed.
- Focused gate, cutoff, allocation-failure, and rendezvous-failure tests: 39 passed, 10 deselected.
- TP2/TP4/TP8 integration tests: 3 passed. They verify lazy staging allocation, then exercise Lamport at 1 MiB, multimem at 20 MiB, and automatic NCCL fallback immediately above 64 MiB.
- BF16 cutoff sweep: passed distributed correctness checks for Lamport, multimem, and NCCL.
- FP16 and FP32 at 64 MiB: passed distributed correctness checks; the multimem path measured 137.25 us for each dtype.
- CUDA graph capture/replay: every candidate workspace was replayed and validated at TP2, TP4, and TP8 before timing.
- SM100 code-generation and resource audit for all three kernel instantiations: 62 registers/thread, 128-byte stack, zero shared/local memory.
- Applicable pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Model evaluation: not applicable; this changes only collective transport selection and no model computation. Numerical outputs are covered against an FP32 distributed reference for BF16, FP16, and FP32.

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, benchmarking, testing, and PR preparation. The human submitter requested submission and is responsible for reviewing and defending every changed line.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Pad fp16/bf16 GEMM weight row stride for L2 cache
author: mgehre-amd
body:
On gfx11 (RDNA3/3.5) a dense GEMM whose weight row stride is a multiple of 2048 bytes collide on the L2/MALL hashes, costing a large share of achievable bandwidth. Offsetting the row stride by one 128 B cache line dodges the collision.
This PR improves TTFT by up to 13% and TPOT by up to 3%.

We pad the row stride once in `UnquantizedLinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading`.
It has a minimal impact on memory consumption on affected layers only (1.29 % of weight memory for Qwen3-8B: 171 MiB on 12.94 GiB).

The predicate is `(K * element_size) % 2048 == 0`, so for bf16/fp16 it fires on any layer
with `K % 1024 == 0`. That covers most of the Llama/Qwen dense family: for Qwen3-8B all
four linears qualify (`qkv`/`o`/`gate_up` `K=4096` → 8192 B, `down` `K=12288` → 24576 B).

Gated on gfx11. This might also apply to gfx12, but we will need to measure and can enable as a follow up.

## Benchmark

On AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151),
`--num-prompts 5`, 2 interleaved reps per cell. Before/after this PR.

| Model (in/out len) | Qualifying | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | Weight memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-8B` 1920/128 | 100 % | 918.02 → 852.39 ms (**−7.15 %**) | 72.15 → 69.83 ms (**−3.21 %**) | 15.27 → 15.47 GiB |
| `Qwen3-8B` 128/128 | 100 % | 119.35 → 103.59 ms (**−13.20 %**) | 70.50 → 68.11 ms (**−3.39 %**) | 15.27 → 15.47 GiB |
| `Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct` 1920/128 | 70.7 % | 969.01 → 932.10 ms (**−3.81 %**) | 30.37 → 29.36 ms (**−3.33 %**) | 7.16 → 7.27 GiB |
| `Qwen3-4B` 1920/128 | 10.4 % | 512.12 → 510.49 ms (not resolvable) | 38.85 → 38.03 ms (**−2.11 %**) | 7.56 → 7.57 GiB |
| `Qwen2-1.5B-Instruct` 1920/128 | 0 % | 198.34 → 201.03 ms (no effect) | 14.64 → 14.74 ms (no effect) | 2.89 → 2.89 GiB |

## Accuracy

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, full 1319-question test set, 5-shot, greedy
(temperature 0.0, seed 42), `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` on gfx1151:

| | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid |

| padding off | 88.931 % | 1173 / 1319 | 0.0 |
