title: [Perf][Model] Qwen4Exp QSA: sm_90 tuning table for _select_config
author: ShuoleiWang
body:
## Purpose

Retune one kernel's launch parameters for sm_90 (H100/H200/H20): `_qsa_sparse_paged_gqa_splitk_kernel`, the Triton split-K kernel that runs the sparse attention of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's QSA layers over the 2048 selected tokens per query. Its tile width, split count and warps per CTA come from `_select_config()` in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa.py`, a table tuned on GB300 (#55557 added an sm_120 table beside it). Measured on H20, the GB300 entries are the wrong geometry in most decode regions, so this PR adds `_select_sm90_config()` in the same shape as the sm_120 helper. Besides that nothing else changes. Regions where the default entry is already fastest return `None` and keep it.

Each row below is one region of `_select_config`'s key, `base_programs = query rows × kv_heads per rank` (at TP8 with MTP3 that is 4 × concurrency, so the second column shows which serving points land in the region). "GB300 entry" is what runs today, "sm_90 entry" what this PR selects on H100/H200/H20; a tuple is (BLOCK_N, target_splits, num_warps). "Latency" is the change in this kernel's time per call when switching from the GB300 entry to the sm_90 entry, measured on one H20 (attention + split-K merge + fused output gate, CUDA-graph replay, median of 3 interleaved orders × 9 replays, hot and L2-evicted), at the three head geometries group 3 / 6 / 12 = query heads per kv head at TP8 / TP4 / TP1-2. Negative is faster.

bf16 K/V cache:

| `base_programs` | TP8 + MTP3 | GB300 entry | sm_90 entry | latency, group 3 / 6 / 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | C1 – C6 | (32, 64, 4) | (64, 64, 2) | −11 % / −12 % / −14 % at 4 rows, −12 % / −19 % / −21 % at 16 rows |
| 25 … 32 | C7 – C8 | (32, 16, 1) | (64, 64, 2) | −7 % / −7 % / ±0 |
| 33 … 64 | C9 – C16 | (32, 8, 1) | (32, 16, 1) | −8 % / −6 % / −4 % |
| 65 … 128 | C17 – C32 | (32, 4, 1) | (32, 8, 1) | −14 % / −13 % / −9 % |
| 129 … 256 | C33 – C64 | (32, 8, 1) | unchanged | best candidate within 3 % of the default |
| 257 … 512 | C65 – C128 | (64, 4, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −13 % / −12 % / −4 % |
| 513 … 2048 | C129 – C512 | (64, 1, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −18 % / not measured / −1 % |
| > 2048 | prefill | (32, 1, 1) prefill, (64, 1, 2) decode | unchanged | prefill entry re-confirmed (8 neighbours slower); decode entry not measured |

fp8 K/V cache (the path added by #55557):

| `base_programs` | TP8 + MTP3 | GB300 entry | sm_90 entry | latency, group 3 / 6 / 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | C1 – C6 | (32, 64, 4) | (64, 64, 2) | −8 % / −8 % / −20 % at 4 rows, −15 % / −18 % / −22 % at 16 rows |
| 25 … 32 | C7 – C8 | (32, 16, 1) | unchanged | default is fastest (best candidate +8 … +18 %) |
| 33 … 256 | C9 – C64 | (32, 8, 1) / (32, 4, 1) / (32, 8, 1) | unchanged | default is fastest at group 3 (candidates −1 … +3 %); groups 6 / 12 not measured |
| 257 … 512 | C65 – C128 | (64, 4, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −43 % / −43 % / −31 % |
| 513 … 2048 | C129 – C512 | (64, 1, 2) | (32, 4, 1) | −53 % / −45 % / −43 % |
| > 2048 | prefill | same as bf16 | unchanged | not measured |

Why: at small `base_programs` the kernel hands tiles to split programs stride-wise, so (32, 64, 4) leaves one program with a two-tile tail (65 tiles over 64 splits) that the launch waits for, whereas a 64-wide tile gives 33 tiles over 33 splits, one per program. From a few hundred programs up the kernel is gather-bound and wants resident CTAs: BLOCK_N 64 needs 68–76 KB of shared memory per CTA (3 CTAs/SM) against 35–41 KB for BLOCK_N 32 with one warp (6 CTAs/SM). With fp8 the in-kernel dequant adds per-tile work, which is why the 64-wide entries lose almost half the time there.

No region regresses beyond run-to-run noise on any geometry; every candidate passed the FP32 reference at `rtol=atol=2e-2`. This kernel is 3–9 % of a decode step on this model, so end-to-end throughput moves by well under 1 % with bf16 caches; with fp8 caches the change is about 6 % of a C128 decode step. All measurements are H20; H100/H200 were not available. `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py` (added here) re-measures one shape in about 10 s, so a maintainer can check the direction there:

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 [--kv-dtype fp8]
```

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "<q>"` for `qsa select_config`, `qsa sm90`, `qsa hopper`, `qsa H20`, `qwen4_exp sparse attention tuning`: no open PR touches the sm_90 entries of this table. The open QSA PRs are #55430 (tile-union prefill kernel on SM121) and #55122 (deterministic persistent top-k), both orthogonal; #55557 (merged) added the sm_120 table this PR sits next to.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py -k "select_config_regions or sm90_"
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --candidates 64,4,2 32,8,1 32,6,1
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 1 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --candidates 32,64,4 64,64,2
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 128 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --kv-dtype fp8 --candidates 64,4,2 32,6,1
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_qsa_select_config.py --requests 4 --query-len 4 --group 3 --kv-heads 1 --kv-dtype fp8 --candidates 32,64,4 64,64,4
```

In addition, on 8× H20 (TP8/EP8, MTP3, bf16 K/V, `--cudagraph-capture-sizes 1 4 16 64 256 512`), stock vs this PR: server start and graph capture, `vllm bench serve` random 8k-in/1k-out at C1 (8 prompts) and C128 (256 prompts), greedy generations with `logprobs` on 16 prompts, and GSM8K through lm-evaluation-harness (0-shot chat template, greedy, first 300 problems, identical prompts on both servers).

## Test Result

Unit tests (H20, main `fc8132a5` tree):

| command | result |

| whole file | 83 passed, 0 failed |

Sweep script (H20; `current` is the entry this PR selects):

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 rows, group 3 | bf16 | (32, 4, 1) 343 µs | (64, 4, 2) 387 µs | +13 % |
| 4 rows, group 3 | bf16 | (64, 64, 2) 12.6 µs | (32, 64, 4) 14.9 µs | +18 % hot / +10 % L2-evicted |

Both servers captured every PIECEWISE and FULL graph size. The patched server's Triton cache holds only the (1 warp, N32) and (2 warps, N64) attention specializations; the stock one also has (4 warps, N32), i.e. the sm_90 table is the one running.

Model evaluation. The split count changes the split-K reduction order, so greedy outputs diverge from stock at near-ties: at every divergence the top-1/top-2 margin is 0–0.75 logprob (0–6 bf16 ULPs) and the other arm's token is inside the top-5; 12 of 16 chat prompts have bit-identical first-token top-5 logprobs.

title: [torch.compile] Canonicalize functionalized split slices for fusion pa…
author: laithsakka
body:
### Purpose
PyTorch 2.15 changed functionalization replay for multi-output views in [pytorch/pytorch#194037](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/194037). Individual split_with_sizes outputs are now regenerated as contiguous slice nodes.

This graph change prevented vLLM passes that expect a canonical split_with_sizes plus getitem representation from matching. It caused:

1. QKNormRoPEFusionPass to report norm_rope_fusion=0 instead of 6.
2. ScatterSplitReplacementPass to leave two slice_scatter operations in the graph.

### This PR 
Extend SplitCoalescingPass to convert complete, contiguous, unit-step slice partitions into one split_with_sizes node with indexed getitem users.

The rewrite is deliberately conservative. It requires concrete bounds, positive widths, full dimension coverage, compatible tensor metadata, and no gaps or overlaps. 

## Fix existing 
This PR also fixes an existing SplitCoalescingPass correctness bug. Previously, two split_with_sizes nodes were considered duplicates when they had the same input and split sizes, even if they split different dimensions:
```
split_with_sizes(x, [4, 4], dim=0)
split_with_sizes(x, [4, 4], dim=1)
```
The pass could incorrectly replace one with the other. The updated coalescing identity includes the normalized split dimension, so only semantically equivalent splits are merged. The new regression test verifies that splits on different dimensions remain separate.

### Test Plan
python -m ruff format --check \
  vllm/compilation/passes/utility/split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py

python -m ruff check \
  vllm/compilation/passes/utility/split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/passes/test_split_coalescing.py \
  tests/compile/passes/test_scatter_split_replace.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/passes/test_qk_norm_rope_fusion.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python -m pytest -q \
  'tests/compile/fusions_e2e/test_tp1_quant.py::test_tp1_fp8_fusions[inductor_partition-+quant_fp8,-rms_norm-6-TRITON_ATTN-Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-<lambda>-model_kwargs1-<lambda>-False]'
### Test Result
Before:
```
norm_rope_fusion expected: [6], found: [0]
```
```
test_scatter_split_replace[float16]:
assert op_count(aten.slice_scatter.default) == 0
found: 2
```
```
test_scatter_split_replace[bfloat16]:
assert op_count(aten.slice_scatter.default) == 0
found: 2
After:
```
all pass after

title: [Model] Use upstream GLM-5.3 and Qwen4-Exp configs and processor
author: hmellor
body:
## Purpose

Transformers ships `glm5_next` as of **v5.16.1** and `qwen4_exp` as of **v5.16.0**, so the vendored copies can go. Raises the `transformers` floor in `requirements/common.txt` from `>= 5.10.4` to `>= 5.16.1` — CI already pins `transformers==5.16.1` exactly in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in`, so this only makes the declared minimum match what is already tested.

Removed:

- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/glm5_next.py` (420 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/glm5next.py` (953 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen4_exp.py`
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/config.py`

Net **-1961 lines**.

### Not a straight deletion

The upstream classes are not drop-in replacements, so the model code moves to their spellings:

| vLLM read | upstream ships |
|---|---|
| `mla_nope` | `mla_use_nope` |
| `num_experts_per_token` | `num_experts_per_tok` |
| `moe_renormalize` | `norm_topk_prob` |
| `mhc_num_residual_streams` | `hc_mult` |
| `mhc_sinkhorn_iterations` | `hc_sinkhorn_iters` |

`is_moe` / `is_kda_layer` / `is_linear_attn` now derive from `layer_types`, and text-level reads go through `hf_text_config` now that the top-level config no longer mirrors its `text_config` via `__getattribute__`.

I verified the rename table by loading the real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` `config.json` through upstream's `Glm5NextConfig` and diffing the resolved attribute surface against every attribute the model tree reads.

### Behaviour deliberately preserved

Three things in the vendored code were intentional divergences, not schema, and are kept with their explanations:

1. **Vision `rms_norm_eps` stays 1e-6.** The checkpoint ships 1e-5 and upstream honours it; the vendored config force-overrode it because 1e-5 "produces repetitive/degraded image descriptions". Now a named constant at its single call site.
2. **The frame sampler moves to `Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices`**, its only consumer, rather than being replaced by upstream's `sample_frames`. See the open question below — this one is worth a second look.
3. **The `NotImplementedError` guards** for config options this implementation lacks move into `_validate_supported_config`, called from `Glm5NextModel.__init__`.

Three GLM-5.3 values have no source in either the checkpoint or the upstream config, so they become named constants rather than silently-missing attributes: `mhc_tau` (0.05), `mhc_post_mult_value` (2.0), `logit_scale` (1.0).

### Hybrid layer accounting

Both vendored configs supplied a `layers_block_type` property that mapped their sparse-attention layer type onto `"attention"`. Without it, `ModelConfig.get_num_layers_by_block_type` falls through to its `layer_types` branch, which only recognised `"full_attention"` — so both models would have counted **zero** attention layers. It now counts `deepseek_sparse_attention` and `qwen_sparse_attention` too, which is what both properties did.

`_get_full_attention_layer_indices` in the turboquant config has the same blind spot, but it already checks `layer_types` first and so is unchanged by this PR. Flagging it as a separate pre-existing issue rather than widening scope here.

### Open question: the frame sampler

This PR keeps vLLM's own frame sampler, but I am not confident that is the right call and would like a view on it.

The sampler's docstring justifies diverging from the reference implementation by noting that the linspace variant "cost 4 points on video grounding evals". That comment describes only the **short-clip** branch (`total_frames < extract_t`), which requires `fps < 2`; I could not construct a case where that branch differs from upstream at all.

The branch that does differ is the common one, for an unrelated reason: vLLM walks at `1/(temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` (0.25s), collecting ~2x the candidates, then re-spreads them with `linspace`. Upstream walks at `1/target_fps` (0.5s) and keeps its picks. Over a sweep of realistic sources, **38/53 cases differ** — same frame counts, different indices:

| case | vLLM | upstream |
|---|---|---|
| 30s @30fps | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 76, 91, 106` | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105` |
| 3 frames @2fps | `0, 1, 2, 2` | `0, 1` |

vLLM's spacing drifts off the target fps and short sources pick up a duplicated tail frame from the odd-parity pad. There is also no consistency argument for keeping our own: `create_hf_metadata` sets `do_sample_frames = len(valid_frame_indices) == source.total_frames_num`, so whenever the backend sub-samples the processor is told not to re-sample, and the backend's choice is authoritative either way.

So switching to upstream's `sample_frames` would delete the last vendored piece and looks more correct on the merits — but it changes frame selection for nearly every video, so it needs a video eval that I could not run. Keeping ours (what this PR does) preserves exactly what ships today at no eval cost. Happy to switch if a reviewer with a GPU wants to take the eval.

### Dropped code left over from Qwen3-Next — please sanity-check

`Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` selected between a MoE block and a dense `Qwen3NextMLP`:

```python
mlp_only_layers = getattr(config, "mlp_only_layers", [])
num_experts = getattr(config, "num_experts", 0) or 0
absolute_layer_id = self.layer_idx + 1
is_moe_layer = self.layer_idx not in mlp_only_layers and (
    num_experts > 0 and absolute_layer_id % config.decoder_sparse_step == 0
)
```

This is a verbatim lift of `qwen3_next.py:479-485`, which arrived with the original support PR (#53896) — Qwen4Exp derives from Qwen3-Next and still subclasses `Qwen3NextAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`. `decoder_sparse_step` and `mlp_only_layers` are Qwen3-Next concepts; upstream's `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` declares neither, and neither appears anywhere in `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` or `...-FP8`. They only resolved because the vendored config subclassed `Qwen3NextConfig` and inherited them, which is why nothing ever flagged the branch as dead.

Evaluating the original expression against both checkpoints with the old vendored config gives `is_moe_layer` **True for 48/48 layers**, no dense layers: with `mlp_only_layers=[]`, `num_experts=512` and `decoder_sparse_step=1` it reduces to `True` for any layer index. So this PR builds the MoE block unconditionally and drops the branch, its guards and the `Qwen3NextMLP` import (`-38/+6`).

Worth a second opinion, since it is a deletion rather than a rename: a hypothetical future checkpoint setting `mlp_only_layers` or `decoder_sparse_step` would previously have been honoured and now would not. Upstream's `qwen4_exp` has no dense path at all (neither key appears in the model, and `validate_architecture` requires `num_experts > 0`), so such a checkpoint would not load in transformers either — which is why I think dropping it is right. Happy to restore it as `getattr(config, "decoder_sparse_step", 1)` with only the dead `else` removed if a reviewer would rather keep the guard.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_config.py \
       tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
       tests/transformers_utils/test_config.py \
       tests/multimodal/test_video.py \
       tests/test_config.py
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Also ran a differential check of the vendored vs upstream `smart_resize` across an 8232-point grid of sizes, frame counts and token budgets, since upstream denominates its bounds in vision tokens where the vendored one took raw pixels.

## Test Result

Every suite was run on this branch **and** on the base commit in a second worktree, because this machine has pre-existing video-codec failures.

| suite | base | branch |
|---|---|---|
| the four files above | 24 failed, 433 passed, 18 skipped | 24 failed, **430** passed, 18 skipped |
| `tests/multimodal/test_video.py` | 14 failed, 70 passed, 6 skipped | 14 failed, 70 passed, 6 skipped |

**Identical failure sets.** The −3 passed is exactly accounted for: 7 removed cases that tested the vendored config's own behaviour, 4 added for the relocated layer-type accounting. The 24 pre-existing failures are macOS video-codec and unrelated `test_vllm_config_defaults` / `test_ir_op_priority_ctx` cases, all failing identically at the base commit.

`smart_resize` differential: **8232/8232 agree, 0 mismatches.**

`pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, including `mypy`.

Both public checkpoints were loaded through the upstream config classes to check the ported attribute surface directly, rather than inferring it:

- `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next`: **37/39** attributes the model tree reads resolve; the two that do not are `decoder_sparse_step` and `intermediate_size`, both discussed above.
- `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`: every renamed field resolves to the expected value, and the three with no source anywhere are the named constants above.

Layer accounting on the real `layer_types`, which both vendored `layers_block_type` properties used to supply:

| checkpoint | layer_types | attention | linear_attention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 36 `linear_attention`, 12 `qwen_sparse_attention` | 12 | 36 |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 34 `linear_attention`, 11 `deepseek_sparse_attention` | 11 | 34 |

Both sum to the full layer count. Without the `get_num_layers_by_block_type` change, both would report **0** attention layers.

### Not covered

- **No GPU here, so no model eval was run.** The change is intended to be behaviour-preserving and the value-level equivalences above were verified statically against the real checkpoint config, but a multimodal smoke test on GLM-5.3-Flash would be worth having before merge — the vision `rms_norm_eps` path in particular fails silently rather than loudly if it regresses.

## Notes

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable layer-aware CSA2 multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has three attention layer shapes: full CSA2 layers (2/8/14/20) run SWA + compressor + indexer and build a new global KV cache with their own Top-K indices; reindex CSA2 layers (24/28/32/36) run SWA + indexer only, re-scoring Top-K over an earlier layer's global KV cache; all other layers are dense or pure SWA. The shared v4.1 pipeline overlaps the full CSA2 layers with **three** fork/join pairs per step (input projections; Q/SWA-insert vs compressor; indexer vs cache-insert) and the reindex layers with one. On ROCm each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream, so the multi-stream launch cost outweighs the overlap benefit there. --- This PR gives the ROCm attention layer a layer-type-aware scheme with exactly one fork/join per step: **Full CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_full`)**: one 3-stream fork right after the input norm. - default stream: fused wqa+wkv → q/kv split+norm → wq_b → fused qnorm/RoPE/SWA-insert; - aux stream 0: the compressor chain (kv_score GEMM → save/compress/norm → RoPE-quant cache insert); - aux stream 1: indexer `weights_proj`. After the single join, the indexer K write (`_produce_k`, whose `wk` consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (`forward_q`, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA. **Reindex CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_reindex`)**: the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path. **Dense layers**: fully serial (`aux_stream_list` disabled). --- A new shared helper `execute_in_parallel_default_first` (in `vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py`) mirrors `execute_in_parallel` but enqueues the default chain before the aux chains — the default chain is the longest, so starting it first shortens the step tail while the aux streams still only wait on the pre-fork default-stream work. The fork is gated exactly like the shipped v4.0 multi-stream gate (#51794/#56853): it only runs where the fork/join becomes static graph edges (inside capture, or with non-dict metadata such as the profile run); everywhere else — including MRV1, which keeps its wide eager region (#51430) — the layer falls back to the fully sequential base pipeline. The CUDA/NVIDIA path is untouched except for a behavior-neutral base refactor: the v4.1 indexer's query path is extracted into `DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q`, still driven unchanged by the base `forward` (`_produce_k` keeps its private name). This is not a duplicate of #51794/#56853, which cover v4.0: v4.1-flash has a different topology (the indexer derives K from the kv-source compressor's latent, with no indexer-local compressor), so the overlap must differ per layer type. ## Trace Comparison (Take conc=4 as an example) **With regard to CSA2 layers with compressor and indexer (layer_id=2/8/14/20):** Before: > The default NV path launches multi-stream 3 times per layer, which is inefficient on ROCm path (multi-stream cost > overlap benefit). After (**20.76%** faster than the old pattern): --- **With regard to CSA2 layers only with indexer (layer_id=24/28/32/36):** Before: > No need to overlap indexer weight projection, since the benefit (4 μs) < the multi-stream cost (5 μs + 6 μs = 11 μs). Instead, we prefer to overlap SWA process and indexer process. After (**11.90%** faster than the old pattern): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with server launch commands below: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 GPU_COUNT=4 export HF_HOME=/shared/models vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --no-swa-bounded-replay \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ 2>&1 | tee "${OUTDIR}/server.log" ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000,tokenized_requests=False \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` > [!NOTE] > All tests based on latest `nightly-rocm100` image. ## Test Result ### Benchmark By the way, note that the e2e benefit could be small, since there are onlt **8** layers that we can optimize (overlap), while other layers always execute serially. | Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | | ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | :-----: | -------------: | :------: | -------------: | :-----: | | 1 | main | 114.47 | — | 392.61 | — | 8.32 | — | | 1 | this PR | 117.28 | 2.45% ↑ | 266.06 | 32.23% ↓ | 8.25 | 0.84% ↓ | | 4 | main | 381.72 | — | 348.33 | — | 9.86 | — | | 4 | this PR | 386.47 | 1.24% ↑ | 331.76 | 4.76% ↓ | 9.76 | 1.01% ↓ | | 16 | main | 1018.13 | — | 496.96 | — | 14.73 | — | | 16 | this PR | 1018.69 | 0.06% ↑ | 495.02 | 0.39% ↓ | 14.73 | 0.00% | | 64 | main | 1912.44 | — | 1165.33 | — | 31.71 | — | | 64 | this PR | 1920.10 | 0.40% ↑ | 1160.00 | 0.46% ↓ | 31.59 | 0.38% ↓ | In summary, the performance data indicates that this PR provides consistent throughput gains and latency reductions without introducing a regression in the tested metrics. The most noticeable benefit is at low concurrency, while at higher concurrency (conc=16 and 64) the changes are comparatively small, suggesting that the optimization has limited additional impact once the system becomes heavily loaded. ### Accuracy Test Main: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| This PR: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9371|± |0.0067| ---

title: [Kernel][MiniMax-M3] Add Triton query-tiled sparse prefill tuned on Hopper
author: NVShreyas
body:
## Purpose

MiniMax-M3 sparse prefill currently launches one Triton program per query token. Adjacent queries often select overlapping sparse KV blocks, so this PR adds an opt-in query-tiled kernel that:

- groups adjacent queries into one program,
- enumerates the distinct union of their selected blocks,
- loads each union K/V block once, and
- gates each block by per-query membership and causality.

Hopper selects the tiled prefill kernel automatically; other CUDA architectures continue to use the generic scalar kernel. The decode kernel now validates persistent top-k block IDs before dereferencing the block table, which makes mixed chunked-prefill/prefix-reuse batches safe.

This is not a duplicate of the open MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention work:

- #52963 targets ROCm/gfx950.
- #55372 targets query-tiled verify-decode attention, while this PR targets prefill.

AI assistance was used to implement, test, benchmark, and prepare this change. The human submitter reviewed the complete diff and approved submission.

## Test Plan

Correctness (H100 Buildkite):

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py
```

This existing H100 kernel shard tracks changes under `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/` and runs the CUDA parity test directly. It covers partial query tiles, mixed request lengths and prefixes, selected-block membership, non-identity paging, and both NHD and HND KV layouts.

```bash

  vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/ops/sparse_prefill.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py
```

The one-off microbenchmark harness is not included in the tree. The H200 matrix covers the original scalar, standalone tiled, and PR implementations; tile sizes 1/2/4/8/16/32; six prefill geometries; BF16 and FP8 KV; and 16/8/0 shared selections out of top-k 16.

## Test Result

### Correctness

- CUDA parity coverage is in `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py` and runs in the H100 Buildkite kernel shard.
- Coverage includes partial query tiles, mixed request lengths and prefixes, selected-block membership, non-identity paging, and NHD/HND KV layouts.
- H200 maximum absolute error across the benchmark matrix: `0.0009765625`.
- Pre-commit passed.

### H200 kernel microbenchmarks

Median speedup over the original single tile kernel across six shapes:

| KV dtype / shared top-k | Best representative tile | Median speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| BF16 / 16 of 16 | 8 | 4.49x |
| FP8 / 16 of 16 | 16 | 5.37x |
| BF16 / 8 of 16 | 8 | 1.16x |
| FP8 / 8 of 16 | 2 | 1.20x |

Representative high-overlap results:

- batch 32, q256, BF16: `1.0259 ms -> 0.2252 ms` with tile 8, or 4.56x.
- long-context FP8: approximately 5.37-5.39x with tile 16.

### E2E Prefill-focused SPEED-Bench

A matched scalar/tiled A/B used the full `speed_bench_throughput_8k_low_entropy` split on TP8 H200. Each independent trial ran 512 conversations with fixed OSL 256, temperature 0, seed 42, `min_tokens=256`, and `ignore_eos=true`. Scalar and tiled runs processed identical totals of 2,870,600 input tokens and 131,072 output tokens with zero request errors. Median ISL was 8,223 tokens (mean 5,606.6).

One scalar sweep and one tile-16 sweep were run with MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8 on one 8xH200 node per sweep. The AIPerf workload used fixed synthetic ISL 8102 (8278 server-counted tokens after chat templating), fixed OSL 1024, no shared prefix, temperature 0, seed 42, `min_tokens=1024`, and `ignore_eos=true`. Every request produced exactly 1024 tokens, and scalar/tiled total output-token counts matched at every concurrency.

title: [Core][Kernel] Share persistent workspaces for Marlin and Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Purpose

Co-authored by: ErinYin <liang.yin@daocloud.io>

Humming grouped MoE currently retains permutation scratch in every layer, so its persistent memory grows with the number of layers. Marlin lock buffers are also owned by individual layers or kernels, tying their lifetime to weight preparation and reload.

This PR gives both resources a shared owner in `WorkspaceManager`:

- Add `get_persistent_resource(key, factory)` for objects with stable storage and `get_persistent(...)` for fixed-shape tensors. Resources are cached separately for each `(ubatch, lane)` and must exist before workspace locking.
- Share compatible Humming `MoEPermuteScratch` objects across sequential layers. Compatibility includes capacity, routing dimensions, device, hidden size, and dtype.
- Acquire Marlin locks at execution time, with separate buffers for concurrent CUDA streams as well as ubatches and lanes. Zero-initialize once; successful Marlin calls restore their counters to zero.
- Resolve dense Marlin workspace lookup inside a runtime custom op so `torch.compile` does not trace execution-context selection.
- Preserve standalone allocation when no workspace manager exists and support explicit Marlin workspaces.

### Relationship to existing work

This combines the direction of #50626 and #56764 with a general resource API. #50626 is the earlier tensor-only Marlin implementation; #56764 adds a Humming-specific cache and accessor to `WorkspaceManager`. Here, the manager handles resource lifetime and execution-slot isolation, while each backend defines its own resource and compatibility key. The intent is to consolidate both changes around that shared API.

Addresses the memory issue in #56759 and relates to the runtime-storage ownership discussion in #48312. Searches for those issues and for `marlin workspace`, `workspace persistent`, and `humming scratch` found the related PRs above; the distinction is the combined, backend-independent resource API.

#55105 remains complementary: its dispatch-capacity and runtime-dtype fixes can feed into the shared scratch accessor, while its activation-buffer fixes stay in Humming. Those fixes are not included here.

## Test Plan

Tests cover resource reuse and locking, standalone fallback, isolation across execution slots and CUDA streams, weight-preparation behavior, and compiled Marlin execution. Permutation tests compare outputs with and without persistent scratch; CUDA graph tests change inputs, routing, and graph sizes to detect stale metadata or aliasing.

Latest targeted runs on NVIDIA B300:

```bash
# 488 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  -k 'permute or humming or workspace or persistent' --timeout=180 -q

# 20 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_isolated_across_execution_slots \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py \
  tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed; run with FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via PYTHONPATH
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py::test_moe_permute_scratch_reused_across_graph_sizes \
  --timeout=180 -q

# 112 passed, 13 skipped
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_tile_padding.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  -k 'marlin or workspace' --timeout=180 -q

# 1 passed
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py -k persistent_locks -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run
git diff --check
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and repository checks.

Before publication, the commit was rebased onto `f3aa88d230`. The only conflict was an obsolete Marlin workspace docstring; the implementation was preserved. Hooks passed again, followed by **60 passed** in this focused run (FlashInfer 0.6.17 pinned via `PYTHONPATH`):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_marlin_gemm.py \
  -k 'persistent or humming or scratch or marlin_prepare_layer or marlin_post_load or marlin_workspace' \
  --timeout=180 -q
```

## Test Result

### Humming memory

Before the rebase, compared clean base `35dc273072ff133743bc5fcfa306bf030fa8730b` with this change using the same compiled extensions and dependency versions. Model: `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`, revision `a1ff8c8967426709e5528307c14c52c17616b008` (40 MoE layers, hidden size 2048, 256 experts, top-k 8).

Configuration: one B300, TP=1/DP=1, BF16, Humming for linear and MoE, **`VLLM_HUMMING_MOE_GEMM_TYPE=grouped`**. Worker probes confirmed all 40 layers used `HummingGroupedExperts`. Fixed 8 GiB KV cache, max model length 8192, max sequences 32, async scheduling disabled, seed 0, V2 runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled with capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]`. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17.

Live PyTorch GPU allocation immediately after initialization, in GiB (2^30 bytes):

| Max batched tokens | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2048 | 33.412 | 30.953 | **2.459** |
| 8192 | 41.352 | 31.516 | **9.836** |

The number of scratch objects falls from 40 to 1. At 8192 tokens, their storage falls from 10330.684 MiB to 258.267 MiB: **97.5% less scratch memory**. Each distinct configuration or concurrently active execution slot still needs separate storage. Fixing the KV-cache budget keeps vLLM from consuming the saving as a larger KV cache.

The 8192-token pair ran sequentially on the same reserved GPU, with fresh processes. The 2048-token baseline and repeated full baseline used another B300 of the same model. These measurements do not establish a latency improvement.

### Model evaluation

Full GSM8K with the grouped Humming configuration above, 1319 questions, five shots, greedy sampling, and a 256-output-token limit, using the repository's GSM8K prompt/scoring helpers:

| Run | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before | 1208/1319 | 91.58% | 1 |
| After | 1203/1319 | 91.21% | 1 |
| Before, repeated control | 1201/1319 | 91.05% | 1 |

The candidate falls within the observed baseline accuracy range. This does **not** establish bitwise equivalence or rule out a causal accuracy effect: 690/1319 token sequences match between before/after, while only 669/1319 match between the two unmodified baseline runs. Repeated greedy requests also vary on both versions, including after prefix-cache resets; the cause remains unresolved.

Marlin additionally passed the repository GSM8K serving evaluation on 128 questions with five shots: **119/128 (92.97%), zero invalid answers**, using the same model with both backends set to Marlin, max sequences 16, max batched tokens 2048, and graph sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`.

### Remaining validation

No H200 or end-to-end distributed DeepEP v2/HT/LL, DBO, or DSpark serving run was performed. Expert-map and execution-slot tests cover local behavior and do not substitute for those runs. The model evaluation uses BF16/SILU and does not cover the FP8/SITU cases discussed in #55105.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, testing, and drafting this PR.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Offload streaming derender detokenization
author: KEYS-A15
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57350.

The plain streaming chat and completion derender paths currently `call _detokenize_delta()` synchronously from the FastAPI event-loop thread. Under concurrent streaming workloads, this can serialize derender processing and delay unrelated asynchronous work.

This PR:

- Creates an asynchronous wrapper around `_detokenize_delta()` using the renderer's existing shared executor.
- Awaits that wrapper from both `derender_chat_stream()` and derender_completion_stream().
- `Keeps _detokenize_delta()` synchronous for code already executing within the renderer executor.
- Adds regression coverage verifying that both streaming paths execute detokenization on the configured renderer executor rather than the event-loop thread.
- Streaming derender suite after rebasing onto current `upstream/main`: `60 passed, 1 xfailed` (an upstream test marked as an expected failure)

I searched open PRs by issue number and behavior keywords. #50550 modifies the streaming reasoning/tool-parser path, while this PR targets the plain incremental-detokenization path. The distinction and proposed executor boundary were confirmed in #57350 before implementation.

This changes execution placement only. It does not change tokenization semantics, stream-state handling, output ordering, model execution, or the public API.

**AI disclosure:** This PR includes code developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex during implementation, test design, and review. I reviewed and understood every changed line and ran all tests listed below.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
  -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/renderers/online_derenderer.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

The focused regression test was also run before and after the production change. It exercises both public streaming methods and compares the detokenization thread with the event-loop thread and the configured executor worker.

The performance workload used 20 concurrent streams with 2,048 one-token chunks per stream, for 40,960 derender requests per run. Tokenization probes using a 1,537-token prompt were issued every 250 ms while derender was under load. Each configuration was run three times, and the table reports the median of the per-run measurements.

The benchmark compared `upstream/main` at `6dc34b6334` with this PR at `a1de8533fe`, using `--renderer-num-workers` values of 1 and 4.

## Test Result

- Streaming derender suite: `61 passed, 1 xfailed`
- The expected failure is an existing parser-path case tracked by #55195.
- Ruff formatting and linting: passed.
- Mypy and all other applicable pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Focused regression before the fix: both chat and completion cases failed because detokenization ran on the event-loop thread.
- Focused regression after the fix: both cases passed and ran on the configured renderer executor.

### Concurrent streaming benchmark

| Workers | Version         | Throughput (tok/s) | Derender p50 | Derender p99 | Cadence p50 | Cadence p99 | In-load tokenize p50 | In-load tokenize p99 |
| ------: | --------------- | -----------------: | -----------: | -----------: | ----------: | ----------: | -------------------: | -------------------: |
|       1 | `upstream/main` |            1120.04 |     7.318 ms |    93.818 ms |    7.316 ms |   93.826 ms |            26.974 ms |           104.076 ms |
|       1 | This PR         |            1118.19 |     7.131 ms |    96.195 ms |    7.131 ms |   96.202 ms |            23.564 ms |           102.095 ms |
|       4 | `upstream/main` |            1098.88 |     7.179 ms |   101.206 ms |    7.178 ms |  101.215 ms |            25.042 ms |           107.417 ms |
|       4 | This PR         |            1112.55 |     7.061 ms |   101.228 ms |    7.061 ms |  101.226 ms |            27.383 ms |           131.855 ms |

With one renderer worker, throughput was effectively unchanged (`-0.2%`), median derender latency improved slightly, and in-load tokenization did not regress. With four workers, throughput improved by `1.2%`, median derender latency improved by `1.6%`, and derender and cadence p99 remained effectively unchanged.

The four-worker in-load tokenization p99 median was higher for this PR, although the individual-run ranges overlapped substantially (`93.87–129.97 ms` upstream and `105.89–134.84 ms` for this PR). This may indicate renderer-pool contention or normal tail-latency variance; the benchmark does not distinguish between them. The results show no material derender throughput or cadence regression from the additional executor hop.

No model evaluation was run because this change does not affect model execution, sampling, token selection, or generated output.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Add AITER FlyDSL GDN prefill backend
author: mjkvaak-amd
body:
## Purpose

Add `aiter_flydsl` as an opt-in GDN prefill backend on ROCm. Supported BF16 GDN layers with 128-dimensional key and value heads route through AITER's optimized VK implementation with both the fused FlyDSL prepare stage and FlyDSL K5 enabled; unsupported platforms, shapes, dtypes, and older AITER builds retain the Triton/FLA path.

This requires the AITER APIs from ROCm/aiter#4532, ROCm/aiter#4598, ROCm/aiter#4694, ROCm/aiter#4732, and the prepare-kernel fix in ROCm/aiter#4952; all merged.

## Test Plan

**Hardware:** 8x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3
**Model:** `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8, BF16 GDN, FP8 KV cache

* **Kernel case:** Added `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference`: packed sequences `[70, 130]`, BF16 Q/K/V, FP32 state, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device and compared against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off. Using that as the reference means the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend exists to select. Verified passing on MI355X (gfx950).
* **Reference:** AITER `chunk_gated_delta_rule_opt_vk` with Triton prepare and Triton VK K5
* **Unit tests:** `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_aiter_flydsl.py`, pruned to the cases that guard correctness:
  * `test_aiter_flydsl_prefill_matches_triton_reference[fp32_state|bf16_state]` — the numerical check. Packed sequences `[70, 130]` (both span several 64-token chunks and end in a partial one), BF16 Q/K/V, 128-dim heads, GQA ratio 2, run on device against the *same* AITER entry point with `use_chunk_flydsl`/`use_prepare_flydsl` off, so the two calls differ only in the kernels this backend selects. Parametrized over the SSM state dtype because `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` can make it FP32 or BF16 and the backend forwards `initial_state.dtype` to AITER; it also asserts the final state comes back in that dtype, since it is written back into the cache.
  * `test_resolve_aiter_flydsl_gdn_prefill_backend` — the shape/dtype gate. FlyDSL is only taken for BF16 with 128/128 key/value heads; any other combination must stay on Triton rather than reach kernels that don't support it.
  * `test_kda_style_model_cannot_select_flydsl` — Kimi K3 KDA shares this layer but builds its own chunk metadata, which the FlyDSL path skips. This pins that the resolver turns it down before that mismatch can happen.
  * `test_explicit_aiter_flydsl_fails_closed[kernels_missing|not_rocm]` — an explicit `aiter_flydsl` request on a build without the kernels, or off ROCm, raises instead of silently running Triton and reporting the run as FlyDSL.

## Test Result

### Unit tests
```sh
9 passed              # MI355X (gfx950), VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, incl. fp32_state and bf16_state
ruff format --check: passed
```

title: [DFlash] Capture the context K/V precompute in the draft CUDA graph
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still runs the context K/V precompute (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`) eagerly outside the graph, because the number of context tokens varies from step to step.

This PR captures the context K/V precompute ahead of the query forward in the draft's FULL decode graph. Each graph stores one full verify of context rows per request; rows past the batch are padded with `PAD_SLOT_ID` so they write no K/V, and any prefill context beyond the graph's rows is stored eagerly before replay. The precompute has no host syncs, so every DFlash drafter captures it. The draft attention metadata build stays eager, as before.


## Validation

Capturing the context K/V precompute must not change the speculator's proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy between this branch's parent commit (`c723a831a8`) and `d8de1d3a2f`, and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed.

### Setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and full decode CUDA graphs.
- **Topologies:**
  - **DEP4:** MegaMoE backend with adaptive verification.
  - **TP4:** auto MoE backend with fixed verification.

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each pair runs the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction.

Acceptance length is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the whole run for DEP4. For TP4, it is aggregated from the engine's periodic SpecDecoding log windows over the steady state; the same method is used on both sides of each pair.

| Configuration | Acceptance length, incl. bonus (parent → PR) | GSM8K (parent → PR) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DEP4 | 3.411 → **3.434** | 1234 → 1228 / 1319 (93.56% → 93.10%) |
| TP4 | 3.471 → **3.463** | 1227 → 1219 / 1319 (93.03% → 92.42%) |

- The acceptance deltas are within ±1% and have opposite signs across the two topologies, and the per-position acceptance curves coincide. The captured precompute therefore does not change what the drafter proposes.
- The GSM8K deltas are run-to-run noise: two repeats of the same DEP4 parent configuration scored 0.9219 and 0.9356 (an 18/1319 spread), which is wider than any delta in the table.
- These results establish parity with the parent; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K server configuration</summary>

Common flags:

```bash
--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128
```

DSpark is configured with 5 speculative tokens.

- **DEP4:** `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, with adaptive verification enabled.
- **TP4:** `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, with the auto MoE backend and adaptive verification disabled.

</details>

### Serving benchmark

TP4, DSpark (5 speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance length 5.5), random dataset with 128 input / 1,024 output tokens. **Base** is main and **PR** is `d8de1d3a2f`. CPU/step is the host time per engine step, measured with an injected per-step probe.

| Concurrency | CPU/step | TPOT | ITL |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.77 → 5.03 ms | 1.27 → 1.08 ms (−15.2%) | 6.95 → 5.88 ms (−15.3%) |
| 8 | 6.64 → 5.24 ms | 1.87 → 1.84 ms (−1.6%) | 9.96 → 9.90 ms (−0.6%) |
| 64 | 6.82 → 5.43 ms | 3.90 → 3.87 ms (−0.7%) | 19.97 → 20.01 ms (+0.2%) |

The PR cuts host time per step by 1.4–1.7 ms. At concurrency 1 the step is host-bound, so this carries through to a ~15% lower TPOT and ITL; at higher concurrency the GPU dominates and latency is roughly unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark configuration</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":5.5}'

vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|64>
```

</details>

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q
```

AI assistance was used for this change: the implementation, the evaluation runs, and this description were produced with Claude Code.

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3][Perf] Fuse MLA decode KV-cache write and Q-prep via AITER
author: rbrugaro-amd
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, Kimi-K3 MLA decode runs the per-layer query preparation and the KV-cache
write as separate launches:

1. `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` — the fp8 KV-cache write
2. `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` — the
   `[ql_nope | q_pe]` concat and that query's static fp8 quant

This collapses both into a single AITER `fused_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla`
launch: **288 → 144 kernel launches and 1351.8 → 682.8 µs (1.98×) per rank over
6 decode steps**, i.e. **9.39 → 4.74 µs per MLA layer per decode step** on
MI355X at TP=8.

Kimi-K3 MLA is NoPE (`mla_use_nope`), while that kernel always applies RoPE and
takes the cos/sin caches as required arguments. It is fed an **identity rotation**
(`cos = 1, sin = 0`) so the rotation degenerates to a no-op — the same approach
ROCm/ATOM uses to route K3 through this kernel.

The identity cache is a **single row**. AITER's per-head and `_opt` decode kernels
clamp `pos` into `[0, cos_cache.size(0))` before indexing, so real positions pass
straight through; a full-length constant cache would otherwise cost ~268 MB at
K3's `max_position_embeddings` of 1 048 576 to express a provable no-op. AITER's
*general* decode kernel does **not** clamp, so the layer refuses
the head counts that would select it (`kv_lora_rank * num_heads < 2048`, i.e.
≤3 heads/rank, reachable at TP=32).

## Scope, and why this is small

This is a **kernel-count / device-time optimization on the MLA decode path**. The
two replaced kernels are a sub-1% slice of a decode step, on 24 MLA layers in a
model that is roughly 1:3 MLA:KDA. End-to-end serving throughput improvement is below 1%

## Relationship to #47757 and #57452

**This supersedes #57452**, which I opened for the same optimization and will
close in favor of this one. That PR stacked on #47757: it carried #47757's six
commits so CI could run, and extended its hook in the shared
`MLAAttention.forward_impl`, also touching
`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py`. Two problems with that shape:

- it could not merge until #47757 did, and it is still under review
- it modified shared MLA code, so every MLA model and backend was in the blast
  radius of a Kimi-K3-only optimization

This PR drops both. It touches **no shared code at all** — only
`vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/` — mirroring the vendor-local q/kv RMSNorm fusion that
the same wrapper already owns (#52494, merged). Consequences:

- no dependency on #47757, so CI runs standalone and this can merge in any order
- zero blast radius: no other model, backend or platform can be affected
- it is a **single file** — the AITER call lives directly in the K3 wrapper

#47757 remains complementary: it fuses the **sparse** MLA path (deepseek_v32)
through the shared hook, while this fuses the **dense** Kimi-K3 path inside the
vendor wrapper. Different call sites, no conflict in either merge order.

**Updated after review** (thanks @Rohan138) — the fused call is no longer a
registered custom op, the `torch.compiler.is_compiling()` guard is gone, and the
branch now lives directly in `forward()` instead of a helper returning `None`.
That folded the separate ops module away, so this is now one file. All numbers
below were re-measured on the refactored code.

On `is_compiling()`: the baseline's `triton_poi_fused…` kernel comes from
`mla_decode_concat_quant_fp8` compiling its own `forward_native` (class docstring
at `mla_attention.py:1541`), not from the model being compiled — Kimi-K3 is not
`@support_torch_compile`. The guard was dead code.

### Why not a duplicate

- **#47757** — same kernel, sparse MLA on deepseek_v32; this is the dense K3 path
  and the NoPE handling is new.
- **#55230** — same kernel family, DeepSeek-R1, edits shared `layers/mla.py`.
- **#45798 / #38313 / #41099 / #41101** — the same fusion as a torch.compile
  graph-rewrite pass. Kimi-K3 is not `@support_torch_compile`, so those never fire.
- **#53166** — K3 ROCm MLA, but chunked-context *gather*, a different op.
- **#52494** (merged) — the sibling q/kv RMSNorm fusion in this same wrapper.

## Implementation

One file, `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/mla.py`, on the existing K3 wrapper:

- **`_fused_qk_prep_supported()`** resolves everything fixed at load time —
  platform, KV-cache dtype, shapes, DCP/PCP/HiSparse, head padding, and which
  `W_UK` variant is live. Evaluated once in `__init__`.
- **`_fused_decode()`** mirrors `MLAAttention.forward_impl`'s `W_UK` dispatch
  *including its precedence* (fp4 before fp8; both flags can be set at once) so
  `ql_nope` is bit-identical to what the unfused path feeds its concat+quant,
  then issues the fused call and continues through `impl.forward_mqa` and
  `_v_up_proj`.

With the static gating hoisted into `__init__`, the only per-batch condition left
in `forward()` is that the batch is **decode-only**. Everything else takes the
stock `MLAAttention` path, unchanged:

- any batch that is not purely decode (the fused call covers only the MQA slice,
  so a mixed batch's prefill rows would never reach the KV cache)
- **DCP** (the kernel skips `slot < 0` rows, which would then be garbage after the
  query all-gather), **PCP** and **HiSparse** (both rewrite the KV inputs/slots
  before the standalone write, which this path bypasses)
- the fp8-bmm and AMX `W_UK` variants, and any `q_pad_num_heads` head padding
- profile/dummy runs, an unallocated KV cache, or a missing slot mapping
- non-ROCm, non-fp8 KV cache, or head counts that would select AITER's
  non-clamping general decode kernel

## Test Plan

All numbers below are from the **stock upstream nightly**
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-0bfc7a15d095fe83ecc82b50561a93c177fece2d`
(2026-09-16), 8× MI355X, Kimi-K3 fp4, TP=8, with **no benchmark harness and no
vendor patches** — plain `vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`:

### Server (identical for both arms)

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve $MODEL \
  --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --language-model-only \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 32768 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010
```

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is the only environment variable set.

### Perf

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --tokenizer $MODEL --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8010 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 8192 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts $CONC --max-concurrency $CONC \
  --seed 42 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

### Kernel census

Add `--profiler-config` to the same serve command, then bracket a decode phase:

```bash
# appended to the serve command above
--profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"/out/traces",
                    "torch_profiler_use_gzip":true,"ignore_frontend":true,
                    "delay_iterations":0,"max_iterations":6}'

# with a bench in flight and past prefill:
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/start_profile
sleep 15
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8010/stop_profile
```

### Accuracy

```bash
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --tasks gsm8k --output_path out --log_samples \
  --model_args model=moonshotai/Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/chat/completions,\
api_key=EMPTY,eos_string='</s>',num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=32768 \
  --gen_kwargs max_tokens=4096,temperature=0,top_p=1
```

## Results

### 1. Decode kernel census — two kernels become one

Rank-0 torch profile, 6 engine steps, 24 MLA layers, `144 = 24 × 6`:

| kernel | baseline | fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| `vllm::concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 144 (668.0 µs) | **0** |
| `triton_poi_fused__to_copy_cat_clamp_mul_reciprocal_view_0` | 144 (683.8 µs) | **0** |
| `aiter::fuse_qk_rope_concat_and_cache_mla_kernel` | 0 | **144** (682.8 µs) |

**288 → 144 launches, 1351.8 → 682.8 µs = 1.98×.**
Per MLA layer per decode step: **9.39 → 4.74 µs**.

Dispatch lands on AITER's `_opt` decode kernel rather than `per_head` —
`per_head` requires `kv_cache.size(1) == 1` and vLLM derives 1536 here. The `_opt`
gate is `kv_lora_rank × num_heads ≥ 2048`; at TP=8 that is 512 × 12 = 6144.
`_opt` is also the position-clamping kernel the single-row identity cache needs.

### 2. GSM8K — no accuracy regression

Full 1319 questions, 5-shot, `temperature=0, top_p=1`, `max_tokens=4096`,
chat template applied:

| arm | strict-match | flexible-extract | stderr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fused | **0.9545** | 0.9553 | 0.0057 |

### 3. E2E serving — unchanged within noise

ISL 1024 / OSL 8192 C=1|8|32 one repeat showed TPOT p50 (ms), ITL p50 (ms), ITL p90 (ms), out tok/s for Conc 1 and 8 are flat to within 0.2%. Conc 32 moves ~0.7% in the baseline's favor, having moved ~1% the other way before the refactor — same essential code, opposite sign, so nothing is claimed in either direction.

This is the expected outcome. The fusion removes a sub-1% slice of a decode
step's device time; for scale, `cross_device_reduce_2stage` alone is ~46% of
rank-0 decode device time in the same trace.

title: [Bugfix][KVConnector] Fix MoRI-IO WRITE-mode requests stranded in WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
author: akshayv
body:
## Purpose

In MoRI-IO WRITE (push) mode, decode requests can get stuck in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` forever when decode is overloaded. The engine stays healthy and keeps serving new requests, so this shows up as a benchmark that never finishes rather than as an error. At 1024 in / 1024 out, 128 requests at concurrency 64, with decode limited to 20 running requests, runs on `main` stall before all requests finish.

This PR fixes two causes. A third cause, decode preemption, is fixed by #53250. This PR used to include the same change, but it has been removed in favour of that PR.

### 1. Prefill gives up on a deferred write without telling decode

In push mode the proxy sends each request to prefill and decode at the same time. Prefill computes the KV cache and then waits for decode to allocate blocks and send their IDs. If decode is busy, the request can wait in decode's queue for longer than `defer_timeout` (60 s). On `main`, prefill then frees its blocks and drops the write, but never tells decode. When decode later admits the request, it waits for KV that will never arrive.

Now, when a deferred write times out:

- Prefill marks the transfer as finished under the lock, so a late block allocation from decode is ignored and no write can start. If the allocation arrived just before the timeout, the write goes ahead as normal.
- Prefill sends `write_failed` to every decode DP rank. Prefill never received the allocation, so it cannot know which rank owns the request. Ranks that do not own it ignore the message, and decode keeps only a bounded number of unmatched failures.
- Prefill then releases its blocks, even if sending a notification failed. This is safe because no write was ever issued.
- Decode reports the request as a failed KV load. It is then failed or recomputed according to `kv_load_failure_policy`. Because no write was issued, decode can free its blocks straight away.

The prefill scheduler no longer has its own WRITE-mode timeout that freed blocks on its own. Only the worker releases them, after the transfer is marked finished.

### 2. A full local prefix-cache hit sent an empty block list

When decode already had the whole prompt in its prefix cache, it sent prefill an empty block list. Prefill rejects that with `MoRIIOError("block_notify_list cannot be empty")` and keeps its blocks. Decode now sends a release message instead, so prefill frees them.

### Related PRs

- #53250 stops a preempted decode request from waiting for a second push. Under the overload above, decode preemption also strands requests, so this PR relies on #53250 to fully fix the hang. With `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, #53250 is also what lets a failed request recompute locally.
- #58962 adds a receive timeout on decode for when prefill dies mid-transfer. In that case decode cannot know whether a write is still in flight, so it keeps the blocks. The two PRs cover different failures: this one handles a live prefill that never started the write, and #58962 handles a prefill that cannot send anything.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, which need neither ROCm nor the `mori` package:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_write_done_routing.py
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio*.py
```

End-to-end reproduction in WRITE mode with the `xgmi` backend. Start the proxy first so both engines can register:

```bash
python examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8402
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8400 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8400",
      "handshake_port": "8600",
      "notify_port": "8500"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --port 8401 \
  --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 20 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_consumer",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "backend": "xgmi",
      "read_mode": false,
      "proxy_ip": "127.0.0.1",
      "proxy_ping_port": "36367",
      "http_port": "8401",
      "handshake_port": "8601",
      "notify_port": "8501"
    }
  }'
```

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://localhost:8402 \
  --endpoint /v1/completions --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 64 --seed 8088 --ignore-eos
```

`--max-num-seqs 20` makes decode the bottleneck so that some requests wait longer than `defer_timeout`. Add `"kv_load_failure_policy": "recompute"` to the decode config to have timed-out requests recomputed instead of failed.

## Test Result

All 207 MoRI-IO unit tests pass on ROCm with `mori` installed (204 on `main`, plus 3 new). The new tests, in the CPU-only `test_moriio_write_done_routing.py`, cover:

- an expired deferred write: the transfer is marked finished, prefill blocks are released, `write_failed` reaches every decode DP rank across pods, and a late allocation is ignored
- the prefill scheduler waiting for the worker's ACK instead of freeing WRITE blocks on its own timeout
- decode reporting `write_failed` as a failed KV load on the rank that owns the request

End-to-end, using the commands above with #53250 applied (2× Radeon AI Pro R9700S, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), the benchmark finishes and KV cache usage returns to zero on both prefill and decode:

| decode `kv_load_failure_policy` | Successful | Failed | Deferred writes timed out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fail` (default) | 109 | 19 | 19 |
| `recompute` | 128 | 0 | 34 |

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable DPA+ETP prefill compute/comm dual-batch-overlap for DeepSeek-V4
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose This PR enables prefill dual-batch-overlap (DBO) for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm in data-parallel deployments: attention DP, experts TP via flattened TP, no EP (e.g. `--data-parallel-size 8`). Today `--enable-dbo` splits a step into two ubatches and runs them as a two-thread ping-pong on a compute stream and a comm stream. However, only the DeepEP-HT prepare/finalize moves its collectives to the comm stream. The naive DP/EP path (`allgather_reducescatter`, used by DP deployments without `--enable-expert-parallel`) runs its MoE all-gather (dispatch) and reduce-scatter (combine) synchronously on the compute stream. Both ubatches therefore serialize, and DBO gives no benefit in prefill. On ROCm this path was also blocked by the microbatching config check. This PR makes the naive DP/EP prepare/finalize hand each collective to the comm stream, using the same compute/comm handoff as DeepEP-HT. While one ubatch's all-gather/reduce-scatter is in flight, the peer ubatch runs attention/MoE compute. It also fixes several DBO correctness issues that DeepSeek-V4 hits on this path. ### Key Changes **MoE prepare/finalize (DBO comm overlap):** - **`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNaiveDPEPModular`** (`fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py`): `dispatch()` / `combine_into_output()` now run inside a new `_comm_region()` context. Under an active DBO context, it yields the CPU to the peer ubatch, switches to the comm stream for the collective, and syncs back to the compute stream on exit. Outside DBO, and during cudagraph capture, it does nothing: the collective stays on the calling stream, so non-DBO behavior is unchanged on every platform. The class reports `supports_dbo()` only on ROCm, the only platform where this path has been validated. - **`FusedMoEPrepareAndFinalize.supports_dbo()`** (`modular_kernel.py`): New capability, defaulting to `supports_async()`, so existing implementations behave exactly as before. The synchronous `_prepare` / `_finalize` paths now assert `not dbo_enabled() or supports_dbo()`. The naive DP/EP class keeps `supports_async()` as `False`. This avoids overloading `supports_async()`, which also drives MK-internal shared-expert overlap on every forward. - **`VllmConfig`** (`config/vllm.py`): Allows `allgather_reducescatter` with microbatching on ROCm. **Ubatching fixes:** - **`UBatchWrapper._run_ubatches`** (`v1/worker/gpu_ubatch_wrapper.py`): Eager ubatch threads now call `torch.accelerator.set_device_index(self.device)`, as `_capture_ubatches` already did. A new thread starts on device 0. Without this call, each thread's first `current_stream()` created a stream on GPU 0 and waited on it, so every DP rank put work on GPU 0. That slowed rank 0, and every rank then waited on rank 0 at each MoE collective. This was the main cause of the earlier ~30% regression with DBO. - **`maybe_create_ubatch_slices`** (`v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py`): The last split point (`cu_num_tokens[-1]`, a `np.int32`) is cast to `int` at the source. Previously the numpy scalar reached the DeepSeek-V4 C128A metadata builder and failed Triton specialization (`TypeError: failed to specialize argument of type: numpy.int32`). An explicit `list[int]` `split_point` is now handled as explicit split points instead of being list-multiplied. - **`_make_metadata_with_slice`** (`v1/worker/ubatch_utils.py`): Slices `CommonAttentionMetadata.positions` per ubatch. Without this, startup fails with `positions is required for C128A metadata build`. - **`UBatchContext.token_offset` / `dbo_current_ubatch_token_offset()`** (`v1/worker/ubatching.py`): Exposes each ubatch's row offset in the parent batch. It returns 0 outside DBO. **DeepSeek-V4 (AMD):** - **`DeepseekV4Model.forward`** (`models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`): Writes `_mtp_hidden_buffer` at the current ubatch's token offset. Previously both ubatch threads wrote from row 0, so the MTP drafter read misaligned hidden states for the step. **Tests:** - `tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py`: Covers `_comm_region` handoff, the no-op without DBO, skip during graph capture, compute-stream restore on error, `supports_dbo()` being ROCm-only while `supports_async()` stays `False`, and the default `supports_dbo()` contract. - `tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py`: Covers per-thread ubatch token offsets and Python-int ubatch slice bounds. > [!NOTE] > **`supports_dbo()` vs. `dbo_enabled()`** > > - `supports_dbo()` is a static **capability** of the prepare/finalize class: *can* it run correctly under DBO? It does not depend on the current step. For the naive DP/EP class it is `current_platform.is_rocm()`. It is used only as a guard in the modular kernel: `assert not dbo_enabled() or supports_dbo()`. > - `dbo_enabled()` is per-thread **runtime state**: is the calling thread *currently* inside a ubatch context? It is True only inside the ubatch threads of a step that was actually split. It is used in `_comm_region()` to decide, per call, whether to hand the collective to the comm stream. > > | Platform | Step | `supports_dbo()` | `dbo_enabled()` | Behavior | > |---|---|---|---|---| > | ROCm | not split (below threshold, a DP rank opted out, or DBO off) | True | False | Collective stays on the calling stream (unchanged) | > | ROCm | split prefill | True | True | Collective runs on the comm stream, overlapped with the peer ubatch | > | Others | any | False | False | Unchanged. Microbatching with `allgather_reducescatter` is still rejected at config time. | > > Neither replaces the other. With only `dbo_enabled()`, a synchronous prepare/finalize that never handled DBO could silently run under it. With only `supports_dbo()`, `_comm_region()` could not tell a split step from a normal one. Previously the PR overloaded `supports_async()` to return `dbo_enabled()`, which mixed the two concepts. It also changed MK-internal shared-expert scheduling per thread, because `can_overlap_shared_experts` reads `supports_async()`. ## Trace Comparison (Conc=64, Prefill) Main (DBO disabled): This PR (DBO enabled, **9.25%** faster per layer): ## Test Plan Unit tests: ```bash pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py -v ``` Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` (with `OSL=1`) and `agentic` workloads, using the server launch command below. Main runs use the same command without the three `--*dbo*` flags. ```bash export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S='10800' export VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL='32768' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER='1' export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION='INT4' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE='1' export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS='0' export OMP_NUM_THREADS='1' vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --port 8333 \ --served-model-name 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro' \ --trust-remote-code \ --async-scheduling \ --distributed-executor-backend 'mp' \ --kv-cache-dtype 'fp8' \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --data-parallel-size 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \ --moe-backend 'aiter' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "rejection_sample_method": "synthetic", "synthetic_acceptance_length": 2.49}' \ --tokenizer-mode 'deepseek_v4' \ --tool-call-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --reasoning-parser 'deepseek_v4' \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \ --prefill-schedule-interval 8 \ --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 64 \ --load-format fastsafetensors \ --enable-dbo \ --dbo-prefill-token-threshold 8192 \ --dbo-decode-token-threshold 8192 ``` > [!NOTE] > `--dbo-decode-token-threshold` defaults to 32. With MTP, a 64-request decode step has 256 tokens and would be microbatched, and microbatched decode is ~1.8x slower per token. Setting it to 8192 keeps decode on the regular FULL cudagraph path, so DBO only applies to prefill. Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=/shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` ## Test Result ### Unit Tests All tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py` and `tests/v1/worker/test_ubatch_offsets.py` pass. ### Benchmark **Fixed sequence length (prefill only):** > Uses the SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with `OSL=1` to measure prefill only. This way, the requests received across DP ranks meet the DBO gate in more steps (microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks). Concurrency | Version | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | P99 TTFT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | Main (DBO disabled) | 922.68 | — | 922.68 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ | 1000.28 | 8.41% ↑ 4 | Main (DBO disabled) | 1005.18 | — | 1220.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 1016.20 | 1.10% ↑ | 1289.38 | 5.65% ↑ 16 | Main (DBO disabled) | 2140.47 | — | 3912.48 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 2205.26 | 3.03% ↑ | 3767.09 | 3.72% ↓ 64 | Main (DBO disabled) | 5858.52 | — | 10182.92 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 5477.98 | 6.49% ↓ | 9482.81 | 6.87% ↓ 128 | Main (DBO disabled) | 10858.97 | — | 19695.63 | —   | This PR (DBO enabled) | 10042.61 | 7.52% ↓ | 18934.63 | 3.86% ↓ DBO helps most at high concurrency (`conc=64/128`), where it reduces both mean and tail TTFT by ~4–8%. At low concurrency it adds a small regression, largest at `conc=1` (+8.4%). There the batch is too small to hide the collective, and the split adds overhead. Users can raise `--dbo-prefill-token-threshold` to keep small batches unsplit. **Agentic replay (conc=64):** > DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4 on 8x MI350X, DP8, MTP (3 speculative tokens), prefix caching on. Requests average ~97K prompt tokens and ~620 output tokens. 729 (Main) and 766 (DBO) requests were profiled, with no errors. Version | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- Main (DBO disabled) | 703.40 | — | 2,173.93 | — | 44.69 | — This PR (DBO enabled) | 752.46 | 6.97% ↑ | 2,112.09 | 2.85% ↓ | 43.15 | 3.45% ↓ The earlier ~30% throughput regression with DBO is gone, mainly because of the device fix in `_run_ubatches`. DBO now matches or slightly beats Main on all three metrics. Flat TPOT confirms that decode is not microbatched. Read these results as parity or a modest gain rather than a definitive speedup. Because microbatching is all-or-none across DP ranks, only a small share of steps are split in this workload. ### Accuracy Test Task | Filter | n-shot | Metric | Main (DBO disabled) | This PR (DBO enabled) | Change -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- gsm8k | flexible-extract | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ gsm8k | strict-match | 5 | exact_match ↑ | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9538 ± 0.0058 | +0.0038 (+0.40%) ↑ ---
