title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

On SM100/SM103, the DSv4.1 O-projection runs four kernels per layer. At decode batch sizes the first three are latency-bound and together take 11-12 µs on GB200 (DSv4.1-Flash, TP=4):

```
before: attn_out ─▶ [Triton] inverse RoPE + per-32 FP8 quant ─▶ [DeepGEMM] fp8_einsum wo_a ─BF16─▶ [FlashInfer] MXFP8 quantize ─▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
after:  attn_out ─▶ [FusedWoAKernel] inverse RoPE + quant + wo_a + MXFP8 quant ──────────────────────────────────────────▶ [FlashInfer CuTe-DSL] wo_b
```

This PR adds `FusedWoAKernel`, a CuTe-DSL kernel that replaces the first three and hands `wo_b` a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`, so `wo_b` skips its own quantize. Each cluster owns 128 `wo_a` output rows and each of its CTAs one head of K (split-K by heads per group); at TP=4 that is 128 CTAs per token tile in clusters of 8:

1. **Weight prefetch under PDL:** before `griddepcontrol.wait`, each CTA TMA-loads its 64 KiB FP8 weight slice and TMA-loads its packed weight scales, overlapping the attention kernel. The MMA warp transposes the scales into the `tcgen05.cp` layout before use. TMEM is allocated after the wait, since a PDL predecessor may still hold it.
2. **Inverse RoPE + quant into SMEM:** the CTA reads its head of the BF16 attention output, applies inverse RoPE to the last 64 dims, quantizes per 32 elements with UE8M0 scales, and writes straight into the swizzled SMEM MMA operand, with no global round trip.
3. **Pipelined block-scaled MMA:** `tcgen05` MXFP8 MMA with the weight as the 128-row operand and tokens as N, accumulating in TMEM. Each 128-wide K stage has its own mbarrier, so the MMA starts on a stage once its weights land and its activations are quantized; the last stage triggers `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` for `wo_b`.
4. **Split-K reduce + output quant:** partials are reduced over DSMEM (each CTA reduces a subset of tokens), rounded to BF16 like the unfused `z`, and quantized to MXFP8 in FlashInfer's F8_128x4 scale layout, including the zero padding FlashInfer's quantizer writes.

The latest kernel update preloads the RoPE coefficients across tokens to overlap global loads, narrows two CTA barriers to the 128 TMEM readers, and uses `redux.sync.max.abs.f32` for output amax. Explicit `mul.rn.f32` / `fma.rn.f32` preserves the prior RoPE rounding order; split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding are unchanged.

`dsv41_o_proj(layer, attn_out, positions)`, which the FlashMLA and FlashInfer backends call directly, takes the fused path on SM100/SM103 when each group has at most 8 local heads (one portable cluster), `o_lora_rank` is a multiple of 128, `wo_a` is per-32 FP8 and `wo_b` is FlashInfer CuTe-DSL MXFP8. The pushed head supports 1–32 tokens. The local extension measured below supports 1–96 when `n_local_heads * (o_lora_rank // 128) <= 128` (DSv4.1-Flash TP4/TP8), retaining 1–32 for TP1/TP2. Other batches and unsupported layouts use `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`. Mega Attention retains its own output-projection path.

The extension keeps each compute tile at most 32 tokens and adds token tiles in the launch grid. For T65–96 it balances three tiles in multiples of four (24/28/32 tokens per tile). Scale stores use the global token row within the existing 128-row F8_128x4 layout; the extension preserves split-K accumulation and BF16 rounding.

The kernel follows the `VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel` warmup contract. The FlashMLA and FlashInfer SM100/SM103 backends register it at construction, and warmup compiles every token count accepted by dispatch: 32 on the pushed head, and 96 for eligible shapes in the local extension (all 96 TP4 keys compiled in 54.11 s in the earlier extension check): target graphs, DSpark draft graphs and eager batches land on different counts, so covering the whole range keeps runtime compile-free. `_wo_b_proj` keeps pre-quantized activations off GEMM-RS, which only runs from 128 tokens.

The kernel binds `amax`, `exponent` and `inv` before its output stage. vLLM imports `quack`, which rewrites `if const_expr(S) or D:` process-wide into a constexpr if; without the binding, token counts whose input stage takes the dynamic path (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, ...) fail warmup with `TYPE_UNSTABLE_JOIN` inside a server even though they compile in isolation.

Why not DeepGEMM: its 26/09 release lets `fp8_einsum` emit FP8 with packed UE8M0 scales from the GEMM epilogue, which covers only the third kernel and can only feed a DeepGEMM `wo_b`. It has no hook on the A-operand side, so the inverse RoPE + quant cannot be fused into it.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `wo_a`, `fused wo_a`, `DSv4.1 o_proj`, `inverse RoPE MXFP8`, `fused_inv_rope` and `o_proj cutedsl`. #57977 (draft) also targets the `wo_a` to `wo_b` handoff, but keeps `fp8_einsum`, has it emit MXFP8, and moves `wo_b` to DeepGEMM; this PR instead collapses the whole pre-`wo_b` chain into one kernel for small batches. Both touch the same call sites; if #57977 lands first, the fused kernel could emit DeepGEMM's packed scale layout for that `wo_b` instead. #58621 changes DSv4, not DSv4.1.

## Validation

The fused kernel should cut decode latency at small batch sizes without changing what the model produces. The kernel microbenchmark below was rerun on the local 96-token extension based on `4f59bdde4b`, against the unfused path unchanged from merge-base `e33de821c0`; rows 97–128 were added on the PR head `813bcd4042`. The serving benchmark, the DSpark GSM8K run 3 and the concurrency-16 GSM8K run 4 were run on the PR head `813bcd4042`; the other acceptance, GSM8K and GPQA results are retained from the earlier PR revision, before the latest kernel optimization and token-range extension.

### Serving / model evaluation setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1; both sides share one venv built from the merge-base's precompiled wheel and the same kernel caches.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).

The fused FP8 data and scales are bit-identical to the unfused path in most cases; otherwise split-K accumulation order flips rare values (relative L2 up to 6.7e-4 after `wo_b`).

Latest kernel optimization (`e63dfaec75` → `4f59bdde4b`):

- **704 additional CUDA graph cases** compare FP8 output and every scale byte against the previous fused kernel, including all token counts 1–32, multiple group/head layouts, padded and offset buffers, zero inputs and varied magnitudes. All are bit-identical; 192 cases run with quack's preprocessor active.
- Compute Sanitizer racecheck at T = 3, 8, 31, 32: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- The fresh WO-A chain benchmark checks all 32 token counts against the unfused path before timing, using the existing relative-L2 tolerance of 3e-3 and checking zero scale padding.

Current local 96-token extension (`ad641eda52dd` kernel SHA-256):

- All 96 token counts pass comparison to the unfused chain before timing: maximum relative L2 `0.00074270298` against the existing `< 3e-3` tolerance; scale padding is zero. Small differences from the unfused chain reflect the existing split-K accumulation order.
- Current source: 768 cases (all T1–96, eight input cases, two CUDA graph replays each) compare FP8 output and every scale byte to the prior 32-token fused kernel, concatenating chunks for larger batches. All are bit-identical, with quack active.
- TP1 shape additionally passed 32 cases at T1,3,8,32, bit-identical to the prior fused kernel.
- The 96-token implementation before the readability cleanup passed 90 existing pytest cases; Compute Sanitizer at T65,73,84,96 reported zero device memory errors and zero race hazards. Sanitizer runs used `--report-api-errors no` for known CUDA Python `cuGetProcAddress_v2` feature probes.

- The local FlashInfer sparse-attention API mismatch still blocks server initialization; the serving benchmark and GSM8K runs 3 (DSpark) and 4 above were run on `813bcd4042` in the earlier evaluation environment (FlashInfer 0.7.0).

title: [Perf][Attention] Remove D2H sync from FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA plan under async scheduling
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

With async scheduling, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` did a blocking D2H copy on every metadata build. FlashInfer bakes each row's `kv_len` into its schedule on the host, and `seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound` is optimistic under async spec decode, so the builder copied `positions` / `seq_lens` back to get exact lengths. With MTP that happens on every draft step too. On GLM-5.3-Flash this made async scheduling *slower* than `--no-async-scheduling` (11.1 vs 7.7 ms TPOT at c=1).

How it works:

1. **Plan on the CPU with the upper bound plus slack.** The host bound, padded by 32 tokens and capped at the max valid count, is available without touching the GPU, so there's no sync.
2. **Clamp on the GPU.** FlashInfer keeps the plan in its int workspace as a list of work items with `kv_start`/`kv_end`. A small Triton kernel (`_clamp_work_kv_end`) computes each row's exact valid count on device from `seq_lens` / `query_start_loc` / `req_id_per_token` (same formula as before) and clamps every work item's `kv_end` to it. The FA3 kernel never reads past `kv_end`, so the slack (and the `-1` tail of the index buffer) is never touched.
3. **Reuse the plan across steps.** Contexts grow by a few tokens per step and the slack absorbs that, so while the new bounds still fit, `wrapper.plan()` is skipped and only the clamp runs. This is also why no-async gets slightly faster.

```
before:  GPU seq_lens --(blocking D2H)--> CPU exact lens --> plan --> run
after:   CPU upper bound + 32 --> plan (usually reused)
         GPU: clamp kv_end to exact lens (Triton, no sync) --> run
```

Notes:
- This reads `wrapper._plan_info` and the planned int workspace (the `MLAPlanInfo` layout from `scheduler.cuh`). The plan-info length is asserted, and the per-work capacity is read from the layout rather than hardcoded.
- With adaptive verification the host query split may not match the device one, so the host bound falls back to the batch max for every row.
- The exact (syncing) path is only used when there's no host upper bound.
- Only affects `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (Hopper; the default sparse backend for NoPE models such as GLM-5.3-Flash).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs touching this backend. #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and indexer workspace sizing, and #58260 chunks plan/run for >16k-row steps. Neither addresses the sync. #58260 does touch `plan()` / `build()`, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` on H100. I updated the existing tests to the new `plan()` signature and added two GPU tests against real FlashInfer. One checks that an upper-bound plan plus the device clamp matches an exact plan (including MTP-style multi-query rows around `index_topk` and a batch spanning several clamp blocks). The other checks that the plan is reused across growing contexts without replanning.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV cache, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, `max-model-len 32768`. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos` at concurrency 1/8/32, at least 32 prompts, each point run twice, no profiler.
- Accuracy: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot).
- Syncs: a torch profiler trace on the patched server shows no blocking sync left in the draft-step metadata build (before: 13 per ~5 steps, ~79 ms total, at `_kv_lens_host`).

All E2E runs, baseline included, have the fp8 plan-dtype fix from #55222 applied locally, since fp8 KV on this backend fails without it.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 18 passed.

Mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, async | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| **this PR, async** | 128.1 / 126.9 / **6.86** | 188.0 / 152.7 / **17.36** | 283.7 / 251.5 / **37.04** |

title: [Perf] JIT monitor: hook TileLang JITImpl.compile instead of __call__
author: NickLucche
body:
## Purpose

The JIT monitor is switched on after warmup, and it wraps TileLang's `JITImpl.__call__`. As a result, every TileLang kernel launch pays for the wrapper, including building the cache-miss key, even though nearly all of those calls hit the kernel cache. TileLang's `__call__` only calls `self.compile()` on a cache miss, so this PR hooks `compile` instead. The monitor still catches every post-warmup JIT compile, and cache hits no longer go through it.

This matters for models with many TileLang launches outside CUDA graphs. For example, GLM-5.3-Flash runs ~72 mhc TileLang calls per eager step (prefill / mixed batches).

**Not a duplicate:** I searched open PRs for jit_monitor / TileLang and found nothing related.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/jit_monitor/` (the fake `JITImpl` now calls `compile()` on a cache miss, like the real one).
- Microbench: 2000 `mhc_post_tilelang` calls after warmup, with the monitor off and on, on H100.
- E2E: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`, TP8 on H100, fp8 KV, MTP with 5 speculative tokens, async scheduling. Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random 1024 in / 128 out, each point run twice.

## Test Result

Unit tests: 25 passed, 7 skipped.

Microbench (µs per call):

| | monitor off | monitor on |
|---|---|---|
| main (wrap `__call__`) | 15.7 | 25.9 |
| this PR (wrap `compile`) | 15.5 | 15.6 |

That's ~10 µs × ~72 calls ≈ 0.7 ms of CPU per eager step removed on GLM-5.3-Flash.

E2E, mean TTFT / median TTFT / mean TPOT (ms), average of 2 runs:

| | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 136.6 / 138.8 / 11.09 | 226.2 / 188.6 / 21.87 | 338.2 / 319.9 / 45.04 |
| this PR | 133.0 / 135.5 / 11.11 | 219.2 / 187.0 / 21.45 | 331.3 / 312.8 / 45.04 |

TTFT improves 2–3%. TPOT is within noise because decode runs under CUDA graphs. The change is small, but so is the diff, and the monitor stays functionally the same.

---

title: [Perf] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel, 7 kernels -> 1, 6x speedup on all shapes for this kernel
author: fululi12
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the isolated kernel, both versions in the same process. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing six of seven kernel launches on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency.

## Purpose

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s `"align"` branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request:

```python
start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
offsets = torch.arange(1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks, ...)
indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
```

The arithmetic is trivial, but as PyTorch ops it is **seven kernel launches** over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor — which holds a **single element** in a one-request decode. Almost all of the cost is launch overhead rather than work.

This is a **shared utility**: `gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call it, so the change is not specific to one model.

## Measured

On MI355X, both versions in the same process so it is like-for-like:

| num_reqs | spec blocks | kernels | us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **7** | **7 -> 1** | **10.81 -> 1.78** | **6.06x** |
| 1 | 3 | 7 -> 1 | 10.91 -> 1.79 | 6.11x |
| 8 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 10.73 -> 1.82 | 5.90x |
| 64 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 12.02 -> 1.95 | 6.16x |

The gain is **flat in batch size**, because the cost is per-launch rather than per-element.

For context on why this site was picked: in a Kimi-K3 concurrency-1 decode trace, attributing every GPU kernel back to its Python call site ranks this the **highest kernels-per-invocation** of any non-model-math site in that model — 7.0 kernels and 19.6 us per invocation. Every other call site in that model is already at or near one kernel per call.

To be explicit about scope: this is a **kernel-level claim**. Against a multi-millisecond decode step it is a fraction of a percent end-to-end, and I am not claiming a measurable throughput change.

## Correctness

**Update after review ([@ChuanLi1101](https://github.com/ChuanLi1101)):** the first version of this kernel indexed the block table as `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, which silently assumes a **column stride of 1**. The `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` it replaces honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. The kernel now takes `block_table.stride(0)`, `block_table.stride(1)` and `seq_lens.stride(0)` explicitly, matching the existing `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` helper.

Worth stating plainly: the original 48-shape sweep below **did not catch this**, because every block table it generated was contiguous. The test added in this PR closes that gap.

Verification now lives in-tree at `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, so CI runs it rather than it being an out-of-tree script. It pins the kernel to the pre-fusion expression over:

- **48 shape combinations** — `num_reqs` 1/2/8/64 x `block_size` 16/64/256 x `num_speculative_blocks` 0/1/3/7, bit-identical (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- **a non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — the regression test for the bug above
- **`seq_len == 0`**, the CUDA-graph padding row the previous `clamp_(min=0)` guarded, which must clamp to row 0
- **`num_reqs == 0`**, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the **`"all"` / `"none"`** passthrough modes, which still return the input tensor itself rather than a copy

55 tests pass against the fixed kernel. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than merely covering the line.

The kernel keeps the same in-range assumption the existing `torch.gather` already relies on: `start + num_speculative_blocks` must lie inside the block-table row.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — 55 tests, in-tree so CI runs them
- [x] 48 shape combinations bit-identical on device (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- [x] Non-contiguous block table (`stride(1) != 1`) — fails on the pre-fix kernel, passes now
- [x] Edge cases: `num_reqs == 0`, `seq_len == 0` clamp path, `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough
- [x] Timing on MI355X: 7 kernels -> 1, 10.81 us -> 1.78 us (6.06x) at the single-request shape. **Kernel-level only; no end-to-end throughput claim.**
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean

title: [ROCm][CI] Make ROCm 10.0 the default image; keep ROCm 7.2 as -rocm72
author: Rohan138
body:
## Purpose

Make ROCm 10.0 (TheRock) the default ROCm image and wheel, keeping ROCm 7.2 available for a transition period.

- Rename `Dockerfile.rocm{,_base}` → `Dockerfile.rocm_72{,_base}` and `Dockerfile.rock{,_base}` → `Dockerfile.rocm{,_base}`, so all CI now builds ROCm 10.0.
- Images: `:nightly` / `:latest` are ROCm 10.0 (also tagged `-rocm100`); ROCm 7.2 is published as `-rocm72`.
- Wheels: `wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/` now serves ROCm 10.0 (`rocm100`); ROCm 7.2 stays at `rocm/<ver>/rocm723`. Install:
  ```bash
  uv pip install "vllm[device-gfx942]" --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/
  ```
  The index hosts vLLM, triton, FA, aiter, amdsmi and a torch repacked to require our triton, and links the ROCm SDK and GPU kernels from AMD's whl-next index.

- Both stacks go through the same scripts and pipeline steps: each ROCm script takes the stack's base Dockerfile, and `.buildkite/scripts/rocm/stack.sh` derives the version, variant, cache keys and image tags from it.
- Internal ECR tags are renamed to the variant (e.g. `<commit>-rocm100`), so the first run rebuilds each base image once.

Known gaps: wheel installs miss the image's build-time ROCm patches, and the amdsmi wheel still needs a hardware check.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed and owned by me. No duplicate PR exists.

## Test Plan

YAML/shellcheck/ruff, `tests/tools/test_docker_build_metadata_args.py`, dry runs of the publish/upload scripts against a fake S3, and `uv pip compile "vllm[device-gfx942]"` against a locally generated index.

## Test Result

All pass; the one-liner resolves to our torch/triton plus AMD's SDK and gfx942 kernels. Full builds and the AMD test suite still need to run.

title: [Kernel] Bump FlashKDA to keep the recurrent state in fp32
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Purpose

Bumps the FlashKDA pin from `b59532f` to `17a037d`, the merge of vllm-project/FlashKDA#13 on its `dev` branch.

Before this change, FlashKDA's K2 kernel stored the KDA recurrent state in bf16 and rounded it after every 16-token tile. On long GLM-5.3-Flash prefills the error builds up across tiles and across chunked-prefill boundaries, and it shows up as corrupted long-context tool-call output. FlashKDA#13 keeps the state in fp32 between tiles, adds missing TMA store waits, and fixes a register-pressure regression on sm_10x.

The only change is the one-line `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/flashkda.cmake`. FlashKDA's op schema, `flash_kda.h`, source file list and cutlass submodule are the same at both commits.

Not a duplicate: no other change to the FlashKDA pin is on main since #12, and I found no open PR bumping it.

## Test Plan

All runs used RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, with FlashKDA built at the PR #13 content, on B200 (sm_100f, cu130) and H200.

- FlashKDA `tests/test_fwd_full.py`, which is a bitwise comparison against `torch_ref` covering fixed, varlen, batched and up to 1M-token cases.
- Relative error against an fp64 reference, using real GLM-5.3-Flash layer-0 activations.
- A long-context tool-call corruption probe (GLM-5.3-Flash, 34k and 42k-token prompts, salted cold prefills).
- `vllm bench serve` with the random dataset, 16 output tokens, 2k to 32k inputs and concurrency 1 to 64.

## Test Result

- `test_fwd_full`: 580/580 on B200.
- Final-state relative error, 4k to 128k tokens: 0.37-0.39%, previously 0.85-1.24%. Output relative error: 0.47%, previously 0.48%.
- Probe at 42k on B200, 256 samples per arm: 224/256 (87.5%) correct, previously 173/256 (67.6%). At 34k: 253/256 vs 256/256.
- H200 probe at 42k (emulated MoE, to isolate FlashKDA): 31/32, previously 21/32.
- Kernel time on B200: geomean 4.6% faster than the old pin.
- End-to-end serving on B200: throughput within ±1.3% of the old pin, which is within run-to-run noise.

**AI assistance:** Claude (Claude Code) helped with the FlashKDA kernel changes in FlashKDA#13, the benchmarks and quality runs above, and this pin bump and description. I reviewed the change and the results. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer.

title: [Perf][Model Loader] Fault in mmap'd weight pages before host-to-device copies on integrated GPUs
author: Willian-Zhang
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58726.

On integrated GPUs (DGX Spark / GB10), the shared weight loaders copy each checkpoint tensor to the GPU with `param.copy_(loaded_weight)` straight from the safetensors mmap view. For a contiguous, same-dtype source, PyTorch passes that pageable pointer directly to the driver copy, so the page faults happen inside the copy. On GB10 that is several times slower than faulting the same pages on the CPU first: 1.7–3.0 ms vs 0.08–0.64 ms per 800 KiB tensor in #58726. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` has at least 140k such tensors, and its main weight load takes 452 s from NFS and 475 s from local NVMe.

This adds `copy_weight_(dst, src)` to `vllm/model_executor/utils.py`. On an integrated GPU it touches one byte per page of `src`, then runs `dst.copy_(src)`. It is used at the 26 copy sites of the shared loaders: `linear.py` (8), `parameter.py` (6), `routed_experts.py` (8), `vocab_parallel_embedding.py` (2) and `default_weight_loader` (2).

- **Gate:** `current_platform.is_integrated_gpu()` for a CUDA destination, cached per device. On a discrete Ada Lovelace GPU the same micro-benchmark shows the plain copy is fastest in every cache state, and the touch adds 0.022–0.028 ms per tensor, so it stays off there. When off, the extra checks cost ~0.46 µs per call (0.91 vs 0.45 µs for a 16-byte CPU copy), about 0.14 s per 300k tensors.
- **Only contiguous, same-dtype CPU sources are touched.** Non-contiguous or dtype-converting copies already go through a CPU temporary in PyTorch (`copy_requires_temporaries` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu`), which faults the pages on the CPU.
- **Why at the copy site rather than in `safetensors_weights_iterator`** (discussed with @gitbisector in #58726):
  - Under TP each rank touches only the slice it copies. A prefault in the iterator read whole tensors: ~287 GiB per rank on DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4, and a slower load at the default `read_ahead_kb=128`.
  - The touch runs right before the copy, so a consumer that buffers the weight stream can't have the pages evicted in between.
  - Tensors a model serves from the mapping (#58439) are never copied, so they are never touched, and no size cap is needed.
- **Not covered:** model-specific loaders that call `.copy_()` or `.to(device)` themselves keep today's behaviour until they call the helper. Its docstring says to. @stecasta routed one such out-of-tree expert loader through it: ~55 GiB of copies moved onto the touch path, and its weight loading took about 70% less time. @JimmyToluene found an in-tree one, the Qwen4Exp PLE shard copy in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ple.py`; routing it through the helper is a follow-up.
- **Measured only on GB10** (TP=1 below, TP=4 by @gitbisector). Other integrated devices, such as Jetson Orin / Thor, will take the touch path but are untested. I haven't checked what GH200 reports as `is_integrated`; if it reports 0, nothing changes there.

## Test Plan

- New tests in `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`:
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_copies_exact_bytes`: with the gate forced on, the helper accepts 0-d, empty, bf16, fp8 and dim-1-narrowed sources and copies them byte for byte. CI has no integrated GPU, so this is the only coverage of that path.
  - `test_copy_weight_prefault_maps_the_mmap_view`: after the call, every page of a safetensors view is mapped (`/proc/self/smaps` Rss of the file mapping). With the touch disabled it fails: 64 KiB mapped vs 4 MiB.
- Existing CPU-runnable loader tests, before and after the change.
- `pre-commit` on the changed files, including `mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`.
- Boot A/B on a DGX Spark.

```bash
# CPU only, repo on PYTHONPATH inside vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130), no GPU
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w:ro -e PYTHONPATH=/w -w /w --entrypoint bash vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0 -c \
  "uv pip install --system -q tblib pytest && python3 -m pytest -q \
   tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \
   tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
   tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py"

pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files <changed files>
```

## Test Result

- `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`: 18 passed (12 existing, 6 new).
- Loader tests: 216 passed, 5 skipped. 38 tests fail with and without the change, the same set on both, all because the container has no GPU:
  - 18 error at setup with `Failed to infer device type`.
  - 18 `test_reload` cases fail because `current_platform.device_count` is `None`.
  - 2 `test_fp8_tp_default_keeps_refined_layout[*-triton]` cases can't confirm the Triton kernel, so the layer pads its TP shard instead of refining the block shape.
- `pre-commit` and `mypy-3.12` passed.

### Boot A/B, DGX Spark (GB10), TP=1

Nine full server boots of `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, interleaved, with the client page cache for the checkpoint dropped before each one.

- **Build:** the image is vLLM v0.30.0 plus out-of-tree patches, not `main`. The helper is copied from this branch and applied to v0.30.0's copies of the same files (25 sites; v0.30.0's `_load_w2` has no chunk loop). It predates a cleanup that renamed the gate function and dropped a redundant `numel() > 0` check, which doesn't change behaviour here. A counting wrapper, not part of this PR, logged the gate and how many copies were touched.
- **Out-of-tree patches on in every arm:** the expert-name index (= #58720, merged), an MTP name prefilter, and the PLE table served from the mapping (never copied).
- **Storage:** NFS with the client's `read_ahead_kb` at 16384, or local NVMe at the default 128.

| loader | storage | main load (s) | MTP load (s) | start → `/health` (s) | swapped out, start → KV profile (GiB) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | NFS | 451.8 | 36.1 | 584 | 4.4 |
| this PR (3 boots) | NFS | 25.9 / 27.0 / 28.0 | 0.8 | 124–129 | 3.6–4.3 |
| stock | NVMe | 475.2 | 31.7 | 609 | 4.2 |
| this PR (2 boots) | NVMe | 46.4 / 54.5 | 2.6–2.9 | 149–153 | 3.2–4.0 |
| *out-of-tree, for reference: `pread` tensors ≤ 64 MiB in the iterator, clone / chunked copy above that* | NFS / NVMe | 21.0 / 88.5 | 1.2 / 1.3 | 113 / 179 | 0 / 0 |

- The gate logged `cuda:0 = True` in every boot with this PR. By the counter's last line (140,000 calls), 139,965 copies (63.4 GiB) had been touched. The other 35 were copies PyTorch stages through a CPU temporary anyway.
- Greedy outputs (5 prompts × 400 tokens, temperature 0) and first-token logprobs are identical in all nine boots, and decode speed is unchanged. No accuracy eval was run here: the touch only reads the source, so the loaded weights are byte-identical (unit test above). @stecasta's GSM8K run is below.
- Swap: loading from mmap views pushes 3.2–4.4 GiB of other memory to swap on this 128 GB machine, and stock loading does it as much as this PR. The pread variant doesn't map the files and doesn't swap. vLLM counts the swapped-out memory as free when it sizes the KV cache. I haven't looked into why the kernel swaps here.

### TP=1, warm cache (from @hclsys, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5919067348))

`Qwen3-1.7B` on one GB10, `load_format=safetensors`, `enforce_eager`, page cache warm, fresh process per run, this branch vs its merge-base `77871126f9`.

| | `Loading weights took` | `LLM()` init |
|---|---:|---:|
| merge-base (3 runs) | 20.2–23.7 s | 44.4–54.8 s |
| this PR (2 runs) | 0.50 / 0.69 s | 26.3 / 29.4 s |

The third base run came after the PR runs, so the difference isn't cache order. With the cache warm the time isn't disk reads but the faults taken through a fresh mapping during the copy. On a discrete RTX PRO 6000 the touch makes no difference, ~0.1 ms per tensor either way (@gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58726#issuecomment-5918595410)).

### TP=1, cold cache (from @stecasta, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#pullrequestreview-5496877797))

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` with a DFlash2 drafter on one GB10, v0.31.0 plus internal patches with this PR applied as a Python overlay. Checkpoint on local disk (`read_ahead_kb=128`), page cache dropped before every boot, two boots per arm.

| | `Loading weights took`, main model | `Model loading took` | start → `/health` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| stock | 96.5 / 96.7 s | 122 / 122 s | 595 / 591 s |
| this PR | 9.5 / 9.8 s | 16 / 16 s | 486 / 486 s |

GSM8K-256 with this PR: 244/256, in line with stock. Minimum `MemAvailable` (~38.5 GiB) and peak swap (0.5 GiB) during load were the same in both arms.

### TP=1 on a `main`-based nightly (from @jschmied, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5865989952))

RadixArk's ModelOpt NVFP4/FP8 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (120 GB, 206 files) on local NVMe at `read_ahead_kb` 128, nightly `1ea7c63f4` with this PR's diff (all 26 sites), 2 cold starts per arm, alternating. Main weight load 504.9 / 534.0 s stock, 65.9 / 64.9 s with this PR. With the expert-name index from #58720 (merged after `1ea7c63f4`) as well, 41.6 / 41.9 s ([data](https://github.com/jschmied/qwen38-flash-next-gb10/blob/1313d7b4b458f9e0462f0d79c02323663cbacdfd/notes/data/fastload/fastload.txt)). Greedy output identical in every start.

### TP=1, cold cache, current head (from @JimmyToluene, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-6349449742))

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 (103 GiB, 299,817 tensors) on one GB10, nightly `21d93d0d8c0e` with this PR at `f66f2108c`. Local NVMe at `read_ahead_kb=128`, page cache dropped before each boot, one boot per arm. In stock, py-spy put 97.7% of load samples on the two expert `copy_` lines in `routed_experts.py`, with no I/O wait.

| | stock | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| main `Loading weights took` | 660.7 s | 71.3 s |
|  routed experts, 70.6 GB | 435 s | 52 s |
|  dense, 10.3 GB | 63 s | 5 s |
|  PLE n-gram table, 28.8 GB | 160 s | 14 s\* |
| MTP drafter load | 82.8 s | 55.5 s |
| start → `/health` | 969 s | 345 s |

\* With one more call site, the PLE shard copy in `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/ple.py`, routed through `copy_weight_`. This PR doesn't change that file, so on its own the PLE table stays on the stock path.

Teacher-forced logprobs of 16 fixed generations (3,761 tokens) differ from stock by mean |Δlogprob| 0.034 (p99 0.37), the same as stock against itself.

### TP=4 (from @gitbisector, [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58868#issuecomment-5852543296))

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on four GB10s, this PR ported to a v0.28.1-based build (25 of the 26 sites), load-only boots, page cache dropped before each, arms interleaved. Times are `Model loading took` on the slowest rank.

| `read_ahead_kb` | boots | stock | this PR | read per rank vs stock |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 3 + 3 | 192–195 s | 156–161 s (−18%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 128 | 3 + 3 | 205–207 s | 149–151 s (−27%) | +0–8 GiB |
| 1024, consumer that sorts the stream | 1 + 1 | 248 s | 225 s | +2–10 GiB |

At 128 the iterator-level prefault made this load slower (202 → 241 s) because every rank read whole tensors (~287 GiB); at the copy site each rank reads about what stock reads. Most of the gain is the slowest rank catching up: in stock, the ranks holding slices 0 and 2 lag by 25–60 s on small same-dtype slices (expert scales, FP8 attention rows). The routed experts there are `I8` loaded into `uint8` params, a converting copy that PyTorch already stages on the CPU, so the helper touches 5.6 of 72.3 GiB per rank.

## Duplicate-work check

- No open PR references #58726; searches for "prefault", "integrated gpu weight loading" and "mmap page fault copy" found none that change these copy sites.
- #49991 (ROCm, clones in the iterator behind an env flag, for a KFD copy-on-write issue) and #50794 (Ascend, clones before the H2D copy to avoid a DMA hang) handle the same copies on other platforms, for different causes.
- #57973 (safetensors prefetch loader) and #55985 (fastsafetensors fit planner) are alternative load paths.
- #58857 / #58782 remove the `sorted()` buffering in the DeepSeek-V4 VL wrappers; complementary to this.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5.5): implementation, tests, the boot A/B scripts, and a draft of this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and boots above on my own machines.

title: [Perf][Spec Decode] Avoid target request padding in DP drafter
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Purpose

When a target FULL CUDA graph pads its request count, `DPSyncState.num_reqs` describes graph capacity rather than the number of scheduled requests. Reusing that capacity for uniform drafter steps makes active DP ranks select larger draft graphs than needed.

This PR keeps the DP-wide maximum real request count alongside graph capacity and uses it for uniform drafter dispatch. It also shrinks online dummy-rank DFlash batches coherently across input preparation, graph dispatch, attention metadata, EPLB preparation, and draft generation. Startup graph capture retains its required capacity.

## Test Plan & Result

The performance validation below uses the official nightly build at the PR base. This PR uses the same nightly plus only the four Python files changed by this PR; the runtime SHA-256 values were verified after the overlay was applied.

### GPU environment

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
- Hardware: two non-production nodes, one arm per node, with 8x NVIDIA H20 96GB per arm.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989`
- Baseline: the official nightly without a source change.

### vLLM Startup Command

```bash
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8010 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,64,128,256,512]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --disable-uvicorn-access-log
```

### Performance Test

```bash
# Concurrency 64 example.
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai \
  --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8010 \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tokenizer /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 3500 \
  --random-output-len 1500 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --num-prompts 640 \
  --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 64 \
  --seed 42 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --extra-body '{"seed":42}' \
  --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 64 \
  --save-result \
  --save-detailed
```

All 890 requests completed in each arm without failures or Pod restarts.

Each point uses `num-prompts = 10 * concurrency`, random input 3500, output 1500, and seed 42. Both arms receive byte-identical input and output token arrays at each point.

| Concurrency | Output TPS Baseline -> This PR | Mean TPOT Baseline -> This PR | Acceptance Baseline -> This PR | Mean TTFT Baseline -> This PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 84.42 -> 86.09 (+1.98%) | 11.32 -> 11.15 ms (-1.57%) | 94.22% -> 85.63% (-8.58pp) | 795.0 -> 716.5 ms (-9.88%) |
| 8 | 471.97 -> 539.51 (+14.31%) | 15.23 -> 13.72 ms (-9.94%) | 84.54% -> 88.38% (+3.84pp) | 1339.1 -> 1271.8 ms (-5.02%) |
| 16 | 775.13 -> 842.71 (+8.72%) | 18.71 -> 17.01 ms (-9.06%) | 80.29% -> 82.97% (+2.68pp) | 1179.1 -> 1089.1 ms (-7.63%) |
| 64 | 1341.96 -> 1356.23 (+1.06%) | 44.55 -> 43.89 ms (-1.47%) | 81.09% -> 76.13% (-4.97pp) | 2306.4 -> 2371.9 ms (+2.84%) |

Acceptance varies between the two arms, but This PR improves output throughput and mean TPOT at every measured concurrency. This consistent end-to-end benefit across C1/C8/C16/C64 supports the optimization in this PR.

### GSM8K Test

Both arms were evaluated simultaneously with EvalScope 1.9.1 using the full 1319-sample zero-shot GSM8K test split and identical generation parameters.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":0}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 8 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.95,"max_tokens":8192,"timeout":3600,"seed":0,"reasoning_effort":"high"}' \
  --work-dir ./gsm8k-results \
  --no-timestamp
```

- Baseline: 1270/1319 (96.29%).
- This PR: 1264/1319 (95.83%).
- Paired outcomes: 1257 both correct, 13 baseline-only correct, 7 This PR-only correct, and 42 both wrong.
- Exact two-sided McNemar test: `p=0.26318`; no statistically significant difference.
- API errors: zero in both arms. Baseline had three and This PR had five outputs reach the 8192-token limit.
- EvalScope performance: mean latency 7.58 -> 7.13 s (-5.90%); average output throughput 52.17 -> 56.16 tok/s (+7.65%).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to instrument the DP drafter path, identify the online dummy-rank graph mismatch, implement the follow-up optimization, run GPU validation, and summarize the results.

title: [Kernel] Register the cudnn backend for FlashInfer BF16 mm
author: schopde-nvidia
body:
## Purpose

Only the cute-dsl backend is wired up for unquantized BF16 linear layers, and it is restricted to sm_10x. That restriction is correct for cute-dsl (FlashInfer raises `BackendSupportedError` for it on sm_120), but `mm_bf16` also has a cudnn backend that runs there, so consumer Blackwell (sm_120/121) currently has no FlashInfer path for unquantized BF16 at all.

## Changes

Splits the shape/layout checks out of the cute-dsl predicate into a shared `_bf16_mm_shape_supported`, keeps the sm_10x gate on cute-dsl alone, and registers a new `flashinfer_cudnn` entry in `_FLASHINFER_BF16_BACKENDS`. The cudnn path is bounded by output width (`N <= 128`): swept on GB10 (sm_121, K=5120), FlashInfer wins 5-6x at `N<=128` and loses 2-4x at `N=512`, so diverting every unquantized GEMM would be a net loss on a model with a mix of widths.

```
        M=1    M=2    M=4    M=8   M=16   M=32
  N=96  1.09   6.14   6.15   1.26   1.28   1.20
 N=128  1.01   5.38   1.26   1.35   1.42   1.51
 N=192  0.85   4.31   1.17   1.26   1.38   1.31
 N=256  1.14   1.38   1.26   1.37   0.89   0.96
 N=512  0.27   0.37   0.41   0.53   0.63   0.75
```
(cuBLAS_us / flashinfer_us, >1 means FlashInfer wins)

Selection is unchanged by default; this only makes `--linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` usable for BF16, which was already an accepted `LinearBackend` value for NVFP4.

## Relationship to other open work

This generalizes the win a GDN-specific custom op (routing `in_proj_ba` to FlashInfer, #57318) was chasing for one projection. `in_proj_ba`'s output width (`2 * num_v_heads`) is `<= 96` for every shipped Qwen GDN model, so it qualifies for this path automatically via `--linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` (or `--unquantized-linear-backend flashinfer_cudnn` from #59021) — no GDN-specific routing code needed. Once this lands, #57318's bespoke custom op can likely be simplified or dropped in favor of this general path.

## Test plan

- `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py').read())"` — parses cleanly.
- Selection unchanged by default (`linear_backend` unset continues to resolve to `default_unquantized_gemm`); the new `flashinfer_cudnn` entry is only reachable when explicitly requested.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and this description.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Enable decoder SWA bounded replay
author: frida-andersson
body:
## Summary

#58132 added decoder-side SWA bounded replay for the CUDA model. This PR enables it on ROCm. During eager prefill, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, then layer 20 and layers 21–39 run on each request's last 128 tokens. The final `mhc_post` runs on that replay batch. Decode graphs stay on the full batch. #59532's replay graphs are already used: the AMD model uses `DeepseekV41ModelState`.

The AMD attention class does not override `forward_kv`. Replay calls `DeepseekV4Attention.forward_kv`, which writes the uint8 SWA cache through `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`.

## What changed

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py`: `write_kv` on the last KV source, then `DecoderReplayLayers` from that layer. Pass `write_kv`, the attention metadata prefixes, and that layer's SWA prefix. `mhc_post` runs inside the replay batch. The return is `(hidden_states, pre_mix, *aux)`. The aux state at the cut is captured on the trimmed rows.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`: no `forward_kv` override. The shared method calls `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and then the compressor insert and indexer K write.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/vl_model.py`: forward `decoder_replay_layers` from the language model.
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py`: when decoder replay layers exist and the prefix-cache window is 0, build `replay_start` and warm the gather kernel. The pad kernel stays on the prefix-cache path.
- Tests cover a 300-token forward (trim, both `mhc_post` calls, the cut-aux capture, the prefix set from the cut, and the SWA insert) and window 0 warming gather without the pad kernel.

## Gating

On when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is set and the v2 model runner is in use. Off with `--no-swa-bounded-replay`. The last KV source must have `compress_ratio <= 1`, and no Engram layer may sit at or after it. ROCm does not read `swa_cache_layer.bounded_replay`; that flag is the prefix-cache path, and attention forces it off. CUDA still requires it. Replay graphs follow `compilation_config.cudagraph_decoder_replay` (default on) and `decoder_replay_trim_threshold` (default 768).

## Depends on

#59894 is in this base. It replaced the row buffers with `write_kv` and `first_swa_prefix`, and replay starts at the last KV source. #56638 is in this base. It replaced #59136 and bounds the ROCm prefill SWA indices at the replay start. #59532 is in this base and supplies the replay graphs. None of the three are in this diff.

## Performance

4× MI325X (gfx942), TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, spec decode off, prefix cache off, HIP INT4 QuickReduce, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. `max_num_seqs` left at the default. Head `bf6a231a018d`, rebased onto main `c75cb63cd2bb`. The bench, GSM8K, and NIAH below were measured before that rebase and were not re-run. The extension is the installed ROCm nightly `0.31.1rc1.dev1+gbb87d227d`.

Serve log: `Decoder SWA bounded replay: in eager prefill steps, layer 20 writes its KV for every token, and the rest of it and layers 21-39 run on each request's last 128 tokens only.` Also `cudagraph_decoder_replay: True` and `Capturing decoder replay CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 4/4`.

4 prompts, 16384 in, 128 out, concurrency 1, seed 7. Both arms completed 4 requests.

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median TTFT | 1176.37 ms | 629.97 ms (−46.4%) |
| Mean TTFT | 1176.09 ms | 629.65 ms (−46.5%) |
| Median TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 10.59 ms | 10.58 ms |
| Output throughput | 50.75 tok/s | 64.87 tok/s (+27.8%) |

## Accuracy

RULER `niah_single_2` was not re-run after this drop. On the previous head, 500 samples at 16384 tokens scored 1.0 off and 1.0 on. 65536 was not run.

The 300-token forward wrote the same uint8 SWA cache as `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert`. That write covers full blocks and a 12-token tail, and the spare block stayed at the poison value.

GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, spec decode off, prefix cache off, `max_num_seqs` at the default:

| Metric | Replay off | Replay on |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict-match | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |
| flexible-extract | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 | 0.9257 ± 0.0072 |

## Test result

```
11 passed, 14 warnings in 8.17s
```

`test_deepseek_v41_amd_replay_forward.py` and `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py`, on GPU 4, after the rebase.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip padded work in SM100 FP4 DeepGEMM experts
author: tlrmchlsmth
body:
## Purpose

Avoid computing with padding in the Blackwell FP4 DeepGEMM MoEs layers. Currently we are doing so in both GEMMs and activations.  This mainly affects the decoder when running DeepEPv2+ DeepGEMM. This PR updates the grouped GEMMs to use DeepGEMM's prefix-sum scheduler, and changes the packed SiLU+mul+FP8-quantization kernel to use those endpoints to process only live rows.

Each endpoint is the aligned expert start plus its actual token count; the next expert starts at the preceding endpoint rounded up to the GEMM alignment. No count readback, additional launch, or DeepGEMM source change is required. Activation workspaces keep their allocated capacity. The per-row layout metadata shrinks from 112 KiB to 128 bytes for 32 local experts and 28,672 allocated rows.

The quantization metadata is optional. Calls without it retain the original dense launch configuration, and the metadata loads compile out. SM120 and FP8 expert callers retain their existing path. Padding outputs are left unwritten; the down GEMM uses the same bounds to identify live rows. `mk_alignment_scope` and `ensure_zero_padding=True` remain in place.

The new activation masking also differs from #51332/#51217 (shared masked activation/Humming paths) and #53911 (Humming indexed metadata preparation): `DeepGemmFP4Experts` directly calls the packed-UE8M0 fused activation kernel. Those changes do not pass this caller's expert endpoints into that kernel. Open-PR searches for DeepGEMM prefix sums and SiLU padding found no implementation of this change. No associated issue is being closed.

## Test Plan

Conflict-resolution update (2026-10-06): merged upstream main `5ab4e4445b` in `e704a97688`. Resolved the graph-replay test conflict by retaining upstream packed/float32/ceil-UE8M0 scale-format coverage and this PR's `is_cuda_alike()` CUDA/ROCm guard. Applicable pre-commit hooks (including mypy 3.10), mypy 3.12, syntax checks for the five affected Python files, and `git diff origin/main --check` passed. GPU tests and model evaluations were not rerun: the local machine has no CUDA GPU. The GPU results below describe the earlier validated revision.

Validation used 8×GB200, DeepSeek-V4-Flash revision `60d8d70770c6776ff598c94bb586a859a38244f1`, EP8/DP8/TP1, DeepEP V2 + DeepGEMM. Both nodes shared one ready NVLink ComputeDomain; all eight ranks passed peer-memory and NCCL checks.

- 69 activation tests passed on GB200, including the corrected benchmark rerun. New cases check bitwise live FP8 values and packed scales, poisoned alignment gaps and unused capacity, empty experts, all-empty counts, clamping, and changing counts on CUDA-graph replay.
- Interleaved CUDA-graph kernel benchmarks used five warmups and 25 samples, with 16 calls per graph. The old packed quantization functions were loaded as the control; ten cases cover padded and fully populated buffers.
- Full FFN comparison uses the same saved real inputs on both variants: layer 10, 512 tokens/GPU, five warmups and 25 unprofiled graph replays per rank. A device all-reduce precedes the timed interval. Three separate outer profiles per rank provide kernel timings. Untimed audits verify both GEMMs' scheduler selection and the activation's actual expert bounds.
- Paired full-model GSM8K: all 1,319 questions, five-shot, greedy, seed 42, maximum output 256 tokens, concurrency 64, FP8 KV, no MTP, eager prefill and full decode graphs.

Commands executed in the validation environment:

```bash
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /bundle/test_padding.py -q --disable-warnings
/tmp/check/.venv/bin/python /bundle/benchmark.py --baseline /bundle/baseline.py --output "$out/benchmark.json"
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python /bundle/worker.pyz \
  --spec /bundle/$backend.json --job-id "$backend" \
  --output-dir "$out" --node-count 2 --local-world-size 4 \
  --node-rank-env JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX \
  --rendezvous-host "$head" --rendezvous-port 29500
/tmp/validation/.venv/bin/python -u /bundle/serve_and_evaluate.py
```

`test_padding.py` is an unchanged copy of `tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_per_token_group_quant_fp8_colmajor.py`; `benchmark.py` is the standalone script included below (removed from the repository). The FFN and GSM8K orchestration uses an external experiment harness.

All relevant pre-commit hooks, including mypy, and `git diff --check` passed.

## Test Result

The latest paired run compares this PR's prefix-sum GEMMs with and without activation masking:

| Measurement | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full FFN, unprofiled | 425.5 µs | 385.7 µs |
| SiLU+mul+quant, separately profiled | 76.0 µs | 20.7 µs |
| Standalone quantization: 3,072 live / 28,672 allocated rows, hidden 2,048 | 63.984 µs | 10.510 µs |

Full FFN latency fell 9.36% (1.103× speedup); outputs match bit for bit on all eight ranks, including eager versus graph execution. Both projections used prefix sums in both variants; only the masked variant supplied expert bounds to activation. The median profiled activation saving is larger than the FFN saving because ranks carry different amounts of expert work and meet again at combine. Main activation workspaces are unchanged.

**Dense-path control:** calls without metadata preserve the original launch and differed by 0.20% faster to 0.39% slower across ten controls in the corrected rerun. At 28,672×2,048, the old and new dense paths measured 64.082 and 64.020 µs; at 28,672×7,168, 217.796 and 217.814 µs. No extra kernel or GPU-to-host count synchronization is introduced.

Supplying metadata for an already full buffer does have a small checking/scheduling cost in some shapes: 64.082→64.822 µs for the fully populated 28,672×2,048 case, and approximately 0.15–0.32 µs for the tested smaller group-128 cases. The ordinary dense path does not pay this cost. The 28,672×7,168 metadata-aware case improved from 217.796 to 212.236 µs. The benchmark includes these full-buffer cases rather than measuring padded buffers alone.

| Paired GSM8K | Prefix sums only | + activation masking |
|---|---:|---:|
| Correct / questions | 1,253 / 1,319 | 1,259 / 1,319 |
| Accuracy | 94.996% | 95.451% |
| Configured 95% threshold | Did not pass | Passed |
| HTTP errors | 0 | 0 |

All prompts and labels matched. There were three control-only correct answers and nine masked-only correct answers. This is an accuracy check, not evidence that masking improves model quality: repeating the unchanged control also produced 16 correctness flips while retaining the same total score. The previous and repeated controls used identical MoE sources.

The earlier scheduler-only validation, before this activation update, measured stock versus prefix sums at 717.4 versus 428.7 µs for the same FFN setup, also with bitwise-identical outputs. Those are from a separate paired run. Stock GSM8K was 1,255/1,319 (95.148%), versus prefix sums at 1,253/1,319 (94.996%).

The runtime image was pinned at `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:f29125bcc6d276ed38a67c9dfd4e51ccbaba09ad92847a0913c0df38d9c05c71` (vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9`). The experiment overlaid the two MoE Python files and only the two packed-quantization functions in `fp8_utils.py`; installed hashes were checked on both nodes. DeepGEMM headers were unmodified. These results are not from a rebuild of all of current main.

AI assistance: Codex helped implement the change, run validation, and prepare this description. This remains a draft pending human review and verification before marking ready.

## Standalone activation benchmark

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script, reproduction command, and recorded output</summary>

Save the following script as `benchmark.py`. It replays all three captured graphs and synchronizes before checking live FP8 values and packed scales. This fixes the pre-replay comparison of uninitialized captured scale tensors.

```python
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project

"""Compare dense and expert-aware packed quantization with CUDA graph timing."""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import json
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.fp8_utils import (
    silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", args.baseline)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    baseline = module.silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton
    warmups, iterations, graph_calls = 5, 25, 16
    results = []
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    cases = [
        (128, 1, 128, 256, 128),
        (512, 4, 128, 2048, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 1, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 0, 2048, 128),
        (28672, 32, 896, 7168, 128),
        (28672, 32, 96, 7168, 128),
        (4096, 32, 128, 2048, 32),
    ]
    for capacity, experts, live_per_expert, hidden, group in cases:
        x = torch.randn((capacity, hidden * 2), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        starts = torch.arange(experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
        starts *= ((live_per_expert + 127) // 128) * 128
        ends = starts + live_per_expert
        graphs = {}
        for name, fn, kwargs in [
            ("baseline", baseline, {}),
            ("dense", silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton, {}),
            (
                "expert",
                silu_mul_quant_fp8_packed_triton,
                {"expert_ends": ends, "expert_alignment": 128},
            ),
        ]:
            output = torch.empty(
                (capacity, hidden), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
            )

            def invoke(fn=fn, output=output, kwargs=kwargs, x=x, group=group):
                return fn(
                    x, group_size=group, output_q=output, clamp_limit=10.0, **kwargs
                )

            for _ in range(warmups):
                invoke()
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
                for _ in range(graph_calls):
                    q, s = invoke()
            graphs[name] = (graph, q, s)

        for graph, _, _ in graphs.values():
            graph.replay()
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

        live = torch.zeros(capacity, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bool)
        for start in starts.tolist():
            live[start : start + live_per_expert] = True
        for name in ("dense", "expert"):
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                graphs["baseline"][1].view(torch.uint8)[live],
                rtol=0,
                atol=0,
            )
            torch.testing.assert_close(
                graphs[name][2][live], graphs["baseline"][2][live], rtol=0, atol=0
            )
        samples = {name: [] for name in graphs}
        for iteration in range(iterations):
            order = list(graphs)
            if iteration % 2:
                order.reverse()
            for name in order:
                begin, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
                begin.record()
                graphs[name][0].replay()
                end.record()
                end.synchronize()
                samples[name].append(begin.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / graph_calls)
        result = dict(
            capacity=capacity,
            experts=experts,
            live_rows=experts * live_per_expert,
            hidden=hidden,
            group_size=group,
            samples_us=samples,
            median_us={k: statistics.median(v) for k, v in samples.items()},
        )
        results.append(result)
        print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
    args.output.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
                "warmups": warmups,
                "iterations": iterations,
                "graph_calls": graph_calls,
                "results": results,
            },
            indent=2,
        )
        + "\n"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```bash
git show 6117e97834:vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/fp8_utils.py > baseline.py
.venv/bin/python benchmark.py --baseline baseline.py --output benchmark.json
```

title: [ROCm][Kimi-K3] Fuse AttnRes output with per-token FP8 input quantization
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Summary

Eligible Kimi-K3 AMD AttnRes outputs currently materialize BF16 activations that the next linear immediately quantizes. Fuse that per-token FP8 conversion into AttnRes and pass native `QuantizedActivation` to supported consumers.

```diff
 AttnRes + output RMSNorm
-  store BF16 → per-token FP8 quant → input GEMM
+  store FP8 + scale → input GEMM
```

Enable the path only for `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and only when all consumers accept the same key. Mixed MoE/router consumers, unsupported linear kernels, and batch-invariant mode retain the original path. Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization and the prefix/block write contract.

This is independent of PD connector work and targets main. Duplicate checks covered #50682, #52968, and #53154: #52968's current diff covers convolution and sigmoid/multiply; #53154 covers MXFP4 output fusions. This PR supplies AttnRes per-token FP8 inputs. The current rowwise Torch FP8 KDA kernel does not expose the required input capability, so this PR does not claim all KDA inputs are fused.

## Evidence

### CI follow-up (2026-10-08)

[Buildkite #93497](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93497) exposed an implicit compiled reference in the FP8 output test when AITER is disabled. Commit `42f0ad593` sets `compile_native=False` for the `QuantFP8` reference, keeping its rounding independent of Inductor fusion. Production code and every numerical tolerance are unchanged. The AttnRes and MLA/KDA direct-return suites pass with AITER disabled (**23 passed**) and enabled (**23 passed**); changed-file pre-commit and Python 3.12 mypy pass. [Buildkite #93546](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/93546) retries the failed K3 step on that commit.


- **Before:** AttnRes and per-token quantization launch separately.
  **After:** A single producer emits activation and scale. Existing + new AttnRes cases passed on all eight MI355X GPUs (16 tests/rank in the final run, including the three capability cases), with exact prefix/block writes, scale rtol 1e-6, and rounding differences limited to an adjacent FP8 code in <1e-4 of values. Three direct-return tests also passed.
- In the paired rank-0 prefill trace, the corresponding standalone AITER per-token quant kernel count falls from 4009 to 3078 (931 calls removed), while AttnRes executes the same 3553 calls.
- `pre-commit run` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual`: passed.
- Eight-rank `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_amd_fp8_fusions.py` compares AttnRes + quant + one MLA input GEMM (N2112/K7168), using nine rotated CUDA-graph samples per rank. Median of per-rank medians, four residual blocks:

| Tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16 | 17.110 | 16.597 |
| 256 | 31.701 | 30.168 |
| 4096 | 183.573 | 173.933 |
| 16384 | 682.589 | 657.554 |

This is a producer/projection segment benchmark. One-token results are essentially unchanged; it does not establish a PD throughput gain.

Paired full-model integration validation used the same eight MI355X GPUs, TP8/DCP8, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, 80 sequences / 16384 batched tokens / 1048576 context. The candidate adds both this PR and the companion DCP prefill fusion #59070 to an exact saved diagnostic baseline; the following model results are combined, not isolated attribution to this PR.

- Three unprofiled repetitions of the same eight-case prefix chain: all 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match. Median TTFT: cold 32K 1701.03 → 1673.86 ms; exact 32K repeat 83.37 → 77.13 ms; the two other repeats 69.97 → 64.42 and 70.79 → 64.56 ms. The 1024-token append is essentially unchanged (290.44 → 291.09 ms).
- Natural-acceptance C16 decode diagnostic: TPOT 9.867 → 9.840 ms. This is a local single-instance test, not the formal synthetic-AL3 PD C16 benchmark.
- GSM8K, first 128 test examples, 5-shot, seed `0,1234,1234,1234`, concurrency 16, greedy generation, max 8192 output tokens: **127/128 (99.21875%) before and after**, for both extractors. The missed example changes (baseline doc 125; candidate doc 84). Aggregate accuracy is unchanged, but this does not establish per-example equivalence or a full-dataset accuracy result.
- Eight 33K+ context checks (cold and cached): every final arithmetic question is answered correctly. Full continuations match in 7/8 cases; the remaining continuation differs after the correct answer. Outputs/logprobs are not bit-exact.

Evaluation command:

```bash
python -m lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:2584/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=1,timeout=1800,max_length=1048576,max_gen_toks=8192' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --limit 128 \
  --gen_kwargs 'max_gen_toks=8192,temperature=0.0,do_sample=False' \
  --seed 0,1234,1234,1234 --log_samples --output_path results
```

Full-dataset accuracy and isolated per-PR model measurements remain review work before merging.


Kernel test/benchmark commands (GPU tests were assigned one pytest process per rank across all eight devices):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_attn_res.py -q
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node=8 \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_kimi_k3_amd_fp8_fusions.py --output results
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way

No checkpoint or cache format change. Reverting restores the original computation path.

**Blast Radius:** ROCm

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used for implementation, analysis, and validation.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Keep DCP prefill context in FP8 through AllGather
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

Keep ROCm MLA's cached DCP context in FP8 through AllGather, then use AITER's fused gather/projection kernel to expand it into K/V. This removes the BF16 communication payload and separate reorganization, dequantization, projection and packing operations for supported configurations.

```diff
 local cached context
-  gather/dequant → BF16 AllGather → reorg → kv_b_proj → K/V pack
+  gather bytes → FP8 AllGather → fused reorg/dequant/kv_b_proj/K/V pack
```

## Claims

- Halves AllGather bytes for the same padded row count, preserving the existing FP8 cache bytes, workspace capacity, chunking and merge plan.
- Falls back to the original path for unsupported cache formats, dimensions, dtypes or projection layouts. The optional upstream K/V concatenation callback is forwarded on that fallback.
- Historical full-model K3 measurements below show unchanged aggregate GSM8K accuracy and lower cached-prefix TTFT with **both this PR and #59069**. Those measurements do not isolate this PR's end-to-end contribution or validate the current rebased head.

## Validation

### Full-set K3 GSM8K (2026-10-12)

| Full GSM8K | Original context path | Fused context path |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Strict match | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| Flexible extract | **1264/1319 (95.8302%)** | **1263/1319 (95.7544%)** |
| HTTP success | 1319/1319 | 1319/1319 |
| Output-cap hits | 0 | 0 |
| Natural DSpark token acceptance | 96567/121728 (79.3301%) | 96818/122628 (78.9526%) |

### End-to-end K3 serving performance

Historical paired run on **8 × MI355X, TP8/DCP8**, complete Kimi-K3, FP8 KV, DSpark3 with natural/standard rejection, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 80 max sequences, 16,384 batched tokens and 1,048,576 context. Candidate includes **#59069 + #59070**. These are full-model, single-instance serving measurements, not PD throughput measurements.

Each row reports server TTFT in **milliseconds, median [min, max] over three unprofiled repetitions** of the same prefix chain. All 24 first-token outputs, cache-hit counts and computed-token counts match between baseline and candidate.

| Request | Baseline TTFT | Candidate TTFT | Median change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold 32K prompt | 1701.03 [1700.41, 1701.44] | 1673.86 [1670.82, 1673.95] | −1.60% |
| Exact 32K repeat | 83.37 [82.56, 83.38] | 77.13 [77.05, 77.41] | −7.49% |
| Append 1,024 tokens | 290.44 [288.19, 297.70] | 291.09 [288.70, 294.20] | +0.22% |
| Fork at token 12,032 | 1114.15 [1114.11, 1114.24] | 1091.69 [1090.71, 1091.89] | −2.02% |
| Repeat fork | 69.97 [69.47, 72.26] | 64.42 [64.28, 64.70] | −7.94% |
| Append 1,024 to fork | 284.95 [284.06, 286.92] | 282.61 [278.15, 290.25] | −0.82% |
| Sibling at token 12,032 | 1115.93 [1114.84, 1116.79] | 1093.48 [1092.50, 1093.77] | −2.01% |
| Repeat sibling | 70.79 [70.36, 71.16] | 64.56 [64.54, 64.80] | −8.79% |

The 1,024-token append is effectively unchanged. In a separate single C16 natural-acceptance decode diagnostic, TPOT is **9.867 → 9.840 ms** and request-group elapsed time is **2.312 → 2.288 s**; no statistical speedup claim is made from that single pair. Eight 33K+ context arithmetic checks all answer correctly; 7/8 full continuations match.

<details>
<summary>Segment benchmark, provenance and reproduction</summary>

Eight-GPU gather-through-K/V-expansion benchmark with real NCCL AllGather, two requests with uneven rank tails/nonzero starts and BF16 weights. Nine rotated samples per rank, five-call CUDA-graph replay; median of eight rank medians:

| Context tokens | Before (µs) | After (µs) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,446 | 74.80 | 60.94 |
| 12,198 | 289.05 | 151.89 |
| 49,062 | 778.18 | 386.80 |
| 98,214 | 1267.18 | 709.19 |
| 196,518 | 2397.64 | 1356.37 |

K/V relative L2 is approximately 0.00135/0.00251 (<0.004), and RoPE channels are exact. This segment excludes attention and the rest of the model. The full-model trace records 384 fused gather/projection calls replacing 384 separate gather/dequant calls. The first graph benchmark required termination during NCCL cleanup after measurements were saved; a follow-up eight-rank 1,024-local-token run with explicit cleanup exited successfully. The benchmark was later removed from the PR to reduce review scope; its source remains in the [original PR revision](https://github.com/whx-sjtu/vllm/blob/b7cf4d59ad25437799c91ff1e2de570e72bad7aa/benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py).

Historical K3 results were collected on 2026-09-28: saved diagnostic baseline `d7b093131` (snapshot based on `ccfd1cea75eff8956c5d08b15a7eaec8891642e9`) versus integration commit `3b1aa4f043ae37ba1b2099ae2ed5e04fdd31e5dd`. Archived `comparison.json`, `prefill-comparison.json`, raw per-request timings, model launch manifests and lm-eval result/sample files were checked when updating this description. Both arms use the same dependencies and serving configuration. The isolated DeepSeek smoke test loaded `f3bb722300272d27eee288657db9df8d75d79f6f`; subsequent `8c0884efd` has the identical production tree. Neither archived model experiment is a fresh run of the 2026-10-08 head.

K3 evaluation command (run against each serving configuration):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m lm_eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args 'model=Kimi-K3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:2584/v1/completions,tokenizer_backend=None,tokenized_requests=False,num_concurrent=16,max_retries=1,timeout=1800,max_length=1048576,max_gen_toks=8192' \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 --limit 128 \
  --gen_kwargs 'max_gen_toks=8192,temperature=0.0,do_sample=False' \
  --seed 0,1234,1234,1234 --log_samples --output_path results
```

Current regression commands (with AITER gather/projection dependencies available):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_op_registration.py -q
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_mla_dcp_context.py
```

The full-set K3 and independent prefix-path results above cover `e95f8244`. Whole-model validation of the later automatic main merge `c90a66e3` remains separate.

</details>

## Details

A compact row map is built once per metadata step; the shared eligibility check prevents unnecessary map construction for unsupported configurations. Expose the AITER operation through `_aiter_ops.py`, including mutation declarations, fake implementation and opcheck coverage. The required kernel was already present in main's pinned AITER `v0.1.23`; this PR requires no AITER bump or PD connector changes.

Duplicate checks covered #50682, #53166, #56881 and #52239. #53166 enables the AITER gather path only at DCP=1; #56881 packs already-projected K/V in the NVIDIA path; #52239 uses NVIDIA symmetric-memory multicast. This change supplies ROCm compressed AllGather plus fused expansion at DCP>1.

title: [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX
author: tianmu-li
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

# [CPU] Improve long-context MTP attention scheduling on AMX

## Purpose

Extend CPU attention's grouped-query (GQA) scheduling to eligible
causal multi-token requests, including MTP verification and short prefill. The
existing batch-level GQA fast path requires an all-q1 decode batch, so these
requests do not receive the same grouped scheduling. The scheduler evaluates
grouped query heads and split-KV work using each request's query length,
causality, and AMX geometry, then selects a plan through its cost model. This
applies with auto, FP8 E4M3, and FP8 E5M2 KV cache.

## Duplicate-work Check

PR [#46154](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46154) is related but not
a duplicate. It fixes generic mixed-batch GQA decode classification when
split-KV can divide a prefill request into one-token work items. This change
adds request-level eligibility based on causality, prefill state, and
verification query length, and uses it to enable AMX speculative multi-token
GQA scheduling with BF16 attention and FP8 KV.

Issue [#46131](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46131), its comments,
open PRs referencing the issue, and open PRs matching CPU attention/GQA/spec
decode terms were checked. #46154 was the relevant overlap found.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_group_head_counts.py
.venv/bin/python -P -m pytest -s -v \
  tests/evals/mrcr/test_mrcr_correctness.py \
  --config-list-file="$MRCR_CONFIG_LIST"
```

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 128K \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# In another terminal:
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 100000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --request-rate inf \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 1 --num-warmups 1 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 1000
```

Serving uses BF16 TP1, batch size 1, and no prefix caching. The original
comparison also used auto KV with and without MTP3. The MRCR configs use the
existing 40-sample inputs and thresholds with three speculative tokens. Set
`MRCR_CONFIG_LIST` to the auto-KV or FP8-KV config list for each evaluation.

## Test Result

Serving used 100k input/1k output tokens with zero failures. Main
`6b24bd8e75a3` values are medians of three timed requests. Auto-KV branch
`65e9381658fe` values are also three-request medians; FP8 branch
`59b2f5f7b4` is one timed request after one warmup, built from the same source
state just before that commit. The FP8 fix leaves auto-KV scheduler selection
unchanged.

| Configuration | Main output tok/s | Branch output tok/s | Main TPOT (ms) | Branch TPOT (ms) | Main TTFT (s) | Branch TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |

| MTP3, FP8 KV, post-fix | 8.62 | 9.36 | 37.25 | 27.57 | 80.73 | 81.20 |

The original FP8 branch run had **87.14 s TTFT**: its new AMX work
materializer also handled ordinary FP8 prefill. Routing FP8 batches without

reduced TTFT to **81.20 s**, within **0.58%** of main. FP8 MTP acceptance was
**98.7%** on the post-fix timed request (767/777 draft tokens). The generic
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8` option maps to E4M3 in CPU attention on both arms.

- Original CPU attention and metadata tests: **1,637 passed, 1,154 skipped**.
