title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Add SM121 TP=1 skinny-GEMM plans
author: stecasta
body:
## Overview

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decode ITL **-9.5% at concurrency 1 on a single DGX Spark (SM121, TP=1)** by adding SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=1 BF16 shapes, which today fall back to cuBLAS. The LM head `(248320, 2560)` gives most of it (-8.3% alone); the remaining rows add -1.3% on `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, where the router, HC projections and shared-expert gate are BF16 and the other dense projections are MXFP8. On `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` attention, GDN and shared experts are BF16 as well and use the same rows; that checkpoint does not fit a single Spark, so it is not measured end to end.

Complements #59632 (SM121 plans for TP=2 shapes, from #59605): this PR only adds TP=1 keys to the same mechanism. Happy to fold this into #59632 or rebase on it, whichever lands first.

## Claims

- In a c1 decode step (MTP k=3) the LM head runs 4 times: 3 draft steps at M=1 (cuBLAS gemv, 6.8 ms each) and the target verify at M=4 (5.3 ms), 25.7 ms or about 33% of the 77.6 ms step (torch profiler, `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`). Almost all of the end-to-end gain comes from the three M=1 calls (about 2.2 ms saved each).
- cuBLAS reaches about 175 GB/s at M=1 on this shape; the skinny GEMM reaches 253 GB/s: **1.45x at M=1**, 1.04x to 1.08x at M=2 to 16.
- End to end: ITL 25.30 to 22.91 ms (-9.5%), output tokens/s +9.9% at concurrency 1 (mean of two interleaved runs per arm; LM-head rows alone: 23.20 ms, -8.3%); parity at concurrency 8 (its M=32 verify step is outside the skinny GEMM range and stays on cuBLAS).
- GSM8K within run-to-run noise: base 249 / 247, LM-head rows only 245 / 247, full table 246 / 246 of 256 (two runs each; two identical base runs differ by 2).

## Validation

**Kernel**, GB10 (p4242-0063, about 2.5 GHz), FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 30; cosine 1.000000 vs `F.linear` for every config:

| M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 7262 | 5016 | 1.45x |
| 2 | 5217 | 5038 | 1.04x |
| 4 | 5257 | 4917 | 1.07x |
| 8 | 5291 | 4890 | 1.08x |
| 16 | 5336 | 4933 | 1.08x |
| 32 | 5608 | n/a (M <= 16) | |

Other TP=1 shapes, same sweep (selected config vs cuBLAS; cells under 1.03x stay on cuBLAS):

| Shape (N, K) | Layer | M=1 | M=4 | M=8 | M=16 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (1, 2560) | shared-expert gate | 5.58x | 1.91x | 1.47x | 1.07x |
| (96, 2560) | GDN B/A | 1.82x | 5.53x | 4.07x | 1.14x |
| (336, 10240) | HC down/injection | 1.41x | 1.36x | 1.31x | 1.13x |
| (512, 2560) | router | 1.71x | 2.09x | 1.88x | 1.38x |
| (640, 2560) | QSA indexer Q/K | 1.73x | 1.95x | 1.92x | 1.48x |
| (1280, 2560) | shared-expert gate/up | 1.86x | 1.52x | 1.55x | 1.46x |
| (2560, 640) | shared-expert down | 2.01x | 1.74x | 1.72x | 1.34x |
| (2560, 6144) | GDN/QSA output | 1.12x | 1.17x | 1.18x | 1.13x |
| (10240, 320) | HC up | 1.23x | 1.22x | 1.20x | cuBLAS |
| (13312, 2560) | QSA QKV/gate | 1.48x | 1.12x | 1.16x | 1.13x |
| (16384, 2560) | GDN QKVZ | 1.47x | 1.11x | 1.12x | 1.11x |

These are cold-L2 numbers. Weights of 7 MB or less stay in L2 in the server, where an in-server torch profile showed little gain for the HC, router and shared-gate rows; the end-to-end numbers below are the claim.

A bake-off on the LM-head shape (FlashInfer `mm_bf16` cudnn / cublaslt / tinygemm, b12x `bf16_vocab_projection` default config) found nothing faster than the skinny GEMM at M=2 to 16; at M=1 b12x was 4% faster than the skinny config but would need a new dependency.

**End to end**, same node (p4242-0074), `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, TP=1, MTP k=3 with forced acceptance length 3, FP8 KV, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, two interleaved runs per arm, mean:

| Concurrency | Requests | ITL p50 (ms) base / LM head / full | Output tok/s base / LM head / full | TTFT p50 (ms) base / LM head / full |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8 | 25.30 / 23.20 / 22.91 (-9.5%) | 38.3 / 41.55 / 42.1 (+9.9%) | 891 / 878 / 881 |
| 8 | 16 | 57.92 / 58.05 / 58.17 | 127.7 / 128.0 / 128.3 | 4429 / 4416 / 4430 |

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, first 256 test questions, greedy, thinking off, speculative decoding off, 8 concurrent requests, two runs each: base 249 and 247, LM-head rows only 245 and 247, full table 246 and 246 (of 256). Batch composition varies between runs, so identical configs differ by a few questions.

Disclaimers:
- End to end ran on vLLM `af7f9488c` (the image used for Flash-Next serving) with this PR's table overlaid on `low_latency_gemm.py`.
- Small request counts per cell (8 and 16); baseline repeats on one node agreed within 1.5%.
- `(13312, 2560)` is the unfused QSA QKV/gate shape; after #59533 lands, the fused `(13952, 2560)` key needs a row (sweep data available).
- SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) is not covered: on the 600 W Server Edition the LM head gains only 1.07x to 1.09x, since cuBLAS is already close to that card's bandwidth.

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k "qwen4_exp" -v
```

On GB10 (p4242-0070): the Qwen4Exp capability-routing test and the SM121 selected-shape test (cosine > 0.999 vs `F.linear` for every shape and M in the table), run against this branch's `low_latency_gemm.py`: 64 passed. The rest of the file needs GLM-5.2 modules that are not in the Spark serving image.

</details>

## Details

- Same table pattern as SM100/SM90 (#59214): exact capability `(12, 1)`, keyed by the local weight shape, configs selected by a CUDA graph sweep against cuBLAS.
- This PR does not change any other GPU or the selection logic.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the sweep scripts, measurements and this description; the change and the numbers were reviewed by the submitter. Duplicate check: #59632 is the only open SM121 plan PR for Qwen4Exp and covers TP=2 shapes only.

title: [ROCm] Octave KV (`ROCM_OCTAVE`): native 3-bit KV cache backend for AMD GPUs
author: JartX
body:
## Overview Adds `ROCM_OCTAVE`, an attention backend that keeps the KV cache of full-attention layers at 3-4 bits per value, with native HIP kernels for RDNA3 (gfx1100) and MI300X (gfx942). Select it with `--kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v3`, `octave_k3v4` or `octave_k3v3_compact` (216, 248 and 196 bytes per slot at head size 256, against 1024 for fp16). RFC: #59773. `docs/design/rocm_octave.md` describes the format and the per-architecture contract. ## Claims - **Capacity:** - On 4× RX 7900 XTX with Qwen3.8-27B, 4.6× the KV tokens of fp16. - On one MI300X, 1.95× the tokens of AITER's fp8 cache (7.0M vs 3.6M, i.e. 53 vs 27 concurrent 128k requests). - **Quality:** GSM8K and a 126k needle-in-a-haystack test match fp16 and fp8 on both architectures. Next-token NLL at 380k is +0.0009 to +0.0015 nats over fp16. - **Speed:** - On MI300X, decode for one request matches AITER fp8. Per layer it is faster from 32k on (65 vs 103 µs at 128k). - On RDNA3 at 380k, per layer, decode is 4.6× faster than TurboQuant and MTP verification 11× faster. - **Works with MTP and CUDA graphs.** No host syncs in the metadata builder. We have served it in production on RDNA3 since October 2, 2026. - **Guarded to the validated architectures**, gfx1100 and gfx942: - CMake builds the sources and registers the ops only for them. - `supports_compute_capability` rejects other devices. - The tests skip elsewhere. ## Validation **Models.** Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (compressed-tensors, int4, group 32). To reproduce, [`cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4`](https://huggingface.co/cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4) is a public checkpoint with the same scheme and architecture; KV token counts will differ slightly. **Tests** (`pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py`), on this branch at 28aa54ed9a (merged with `main` 3897f95cf1): | | gfx1100 | gfx942 | |---|---|---| | `test_rocm_octave.py` | 105 passed | 87 passed, 18 skipped (sparse decode is gfx1100-only) | | Octave kernels with scratch in the built `.so` | 0 of 108 | 0 of 108 | - The tests compare store, decode and prefill with the PyTorch reference for all three cache dtypes. That covers: - the native and the portable decode; - 1 and 4 query tokens (MTP); - padded queries and 1-256 KV splits; - fp16 and bf16; - prefill over a cached prefix with several requests; - the sparse (QSA) decode. - To check that the tests can fail, I broke the kernels on purpose several times: a wrong codebook, a least-squares scale, a wrong `log2(e)`, a missing query debias. Each time the relevant tests failed. - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on gfx942: served `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4` with `octave_k3v3` and MTP k=3 through 40 GSM8K questions with no sync error (97.5%). - pre-commit passes on the changed files, except `update-dockerfile-graph`, which needs `/bin/bash` and cannot run on my machine. mypy (CI stage) passes. - CI: the AMD `kernels/attention` step runs `test_rocm_octave.py` on its MI300 runners (gfx942). gfx1100 is not in CI; it was validated locally as above. **MI300X end to end.** Setup: - 1× MI300X, TP1, fp16, MTP k=3, `--max-model-len 131072`; only the cache dtype changes between rows. - GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, chat, thinking off, 200 questions, temperature 0.6. - NIAH: details below. - Speed: `vllm bench serve`. - The fp8 row is forced with `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA`. With only `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, vLLM picks `ROCM_ATTN`. | KV cache | KV tokens | GSM8K | NIAH | decode at 126k | TPOT 1 user, 8k / 32k / 100k | TTFT 100k | 16 users, 8k | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 7,014,973 | 98.0 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.2 s | 221 tok/s | | `octave_k3v4` | 6,391,547 | 97.5 | 28/28 | 52 tok/s | 15 / 15 / 19 ms | 20.2 s | 226 tok/s | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 7,446,005 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 16 / 18 / 16 ms | 20.1 s | 211 tok/s | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 3,597,048 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 50 tok/s | 15 / 17 / 16 ms | 18.6 s | 235 tok/s | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1,952,899 | 97.0 | 28/28 | 6 tok/s | 22 / 45 / 108 ms | 23.1 s | 120 tok/s | AITER is ahead with 16 users and in time to first token at 100k, which points at our prefill over a cached prefix; that is the next thing to work on.
MI300X: NIAH in detail The haystack is vLLM's own Python source, cut to 126k tokens. 16 keys are inserted every ~7.7k tokens, each a line such as `# PROJECT KEY Aldebaran: WK3DEGZD`, with star names as look-alike labels and random 8-character values. The same document is cut at 32k, 64k and 126k, which hold 4, 8 and 16 keys. For each key present the model is asked, thinking off, for only that key's value; an answer counts if it contains the exact value. Keys sit between 3% and 95% of the context. | KV cache | 32k (4 keys) | 64k (8 keys) | 126k (16 keys) | another key's value returned | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v4` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 4/4 | 8/8 | 16/16 | 0 | The model saturates this task at 128k. So it shows that the 3-bit cache loses no retrieval there; it does not rank the formats. The harder test is the 800k key curve in the RFC, where the keys start to blur only past 640k, because of the model and not the cache.
MI300X: vllm bench serve in detail Setup: - Random prompts (`--dataset-name random`), 512 output tokens with `--ignore-eos`, `--seed 0`, no prefix reuse. - One user at a time: 6 prompts at 8k, 4 at 32k and 3 at 100k. - 16 concurrent users: 64 prompts at 8k. No request failed. Each cell is median TTFT / median TPOT / output tok/s. Random tokens give MTP a low acceptance, the same for every row. | KV cache | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` | 1.55 s / 15.3 ms / 51.3 | 5.99 s / 18.1 ms / 33.4 | 20.2 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.34 s / 62.1 ms / 221 | | `octave_k3v4` | 1.55 s / 15.4 ms / 52.4 | 6.06 s / 15.3 ms / 35.8 | 20.2 s / 19.2 ms / 17.1 | 3.95 s / 57.0 ms / 226 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 1.57 s / 16.2 ms / 50.2 | 6.73 s / 17.6 ms / 32.4 | 20.1 s / 15.6 ms / 17.9 | 3.27 s / 57.2 ms / 211 | | fp8, `ROCM_AITER_FA` | 1.57 s / 15.2 ms / 49.3 | 5.53 s / 17.1 ms / 34.1 | 18.6 s / 16.2 ms / 19.0 | 3.29 s / 49.9 ms / 235 | | fp16, `ROCM_ATTN` | 1.64 s / 22.5 ms / 36.8 | 5.78 s / 44.6 ms / 16.9 | 23.1 s / 108.4 ms / 6.2 | 7.26 s / 112.4 ms / 120 | Without MTP, to compare with UltraQuant (#57057), which needs bf16 here: | KV cache | KV tokens | 8k, 1 user | 32k, 1 user | 100k, 1 user | 8k, 16 users | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `octave_k3v3` (fp16) | 9,437,184 | 1.57 s / 51.9 ms / 18.2 | 5.28 s / 52.2 ms / 16.0 | 19.1 s / 52.6 ms / 11.1 | 10.9 s / 82.0 ms / 157 | | `ultraquant_4bit` (bf16) | 7,730,626 | 1.84 s / 58.5 ms / 16.1 | 6.24 s / 66.0 ms / 12.8 | 20.3 s / 87.5 ms / 7.9 | 14.0 s / 94.5 ms / 135 | On gfx942 UltraQuant's FlyDSL decode is not used, because it targets gfx950 and does not cover 6 query heads per KV head, so this is its Triton fallback. With MTP k=3 its output was not usable on this setup (GSM8K 1%, NIAH 0/28); without MTP it is correct (GSM8K 98.0, NIAH 28/28). This says nothing about UltraQuant on gfx950.
MI300X: attention per layer `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`, 6 query heads, 1 KV head. | | `octave_k3v3` | fp8, AITER | |---|---|---| | decode, 1 token at 8k | 25 µs | 16 µs | | decode, 1 token at 32k | 32 µs | 33 µs | | decode, 1 token at 128k | 65 µs | 103 µs | | decode, 16 requests at 32k | 227 µs | 323 µs | | decode, 64 requests at 8k | 220 µs | 352 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens at 32k | 61 µs | — | Prefill, against `ROCM_AITER_FA` with an fp16 cache: - 8k with no prefix: 2.76 vs 2.50 ms. - Two 2k chunks over an 8k prefix: 3.28 vs 6.76 ms. - A 2k chunk over a 32k prefix: 5.44 vs 7.15 ms.
RDNA3 (4× RX 7900 XTX, TP4) evaluation Setup: - 8 GB of KV cache per GPU, same image and flags for every row. - GSM8K: chat, thinking off, 500 questions, temperature 0.6, no MTP so that TurboQuant is correct. - NLL: one 380k-token document. | KV cache | Bytes | GSM8K | NLL over fp16 | |---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 1024 | 91.8 | — | | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | 230 | 89.8 | +0.00155 | | `octave_k3v4` | 248 | 91.4 | +0.00086 | | `octave_k3v3` | 216 | 92.4 | +0.00125 | | `octave_k3v3_compact` | 196 | 91.8 | +0.00150 | Attention per layer at 380k (one TP4 shard): | | fp16 | `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | `octave_k3v3_compact` | `octave_k3v3` | |---|---|---|---|---| | decode, 1 token | 2370 µs | 2565 µs | 563 µs | 614 µs | | MTP verify, 4 tokens | 48.8 ms | 6.65 ms | 0.58 ms | 0.62 ms | | prefill, 2048-token chunk | 125.6 ms | 86.6 ms | 60.8 ms | 63.9 ms | Time to first token at 380k, end to end with MTP and a cold prefix: - `octave_k3v3_compact`: 297 s; - fp16: 371 s; - TurboQuant: 621 s. At 100k all three are within 8%, because the GEMMs and the all-reduce dominate. When I replaced the metadata builder the backend first inherited with its own, I checked that nothing moved (TP4, MTP, GSM8K 500 at concurrency 6): - GSM8K: 92.2 → 91.8; - MTP acceptance: 83.33% → 83.39%; - output: 216.1 → 216.8 tok/s.
Sparse attention (qwen4_exp QSA) evaluation Setup: - 4x RX 7900 XTX, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next W4A16 (asymmetric, g32), TP4, fp16, `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, no prefix caching. - NLL from `prompt_logprobs` over 12 documents of ~8k tokens, split at position 2048, and over 24 short documents. - Values in nats over fp16; mean NLL repeats to about ±0.003 nats. | KV cache | KV tokens | NLL pos >= 2048 | NLL pos < 2048 | NLL short | |---|---|---|---|---| | fp16 | 47,409 | 1.0856 | 1.6707 | 1.1788 | | `octave_k3v3`, no window | 155,930 | +0.0395 | +0.0851 | +0.0708 | | `octave_k3v3` | 155,930 | +0.0163 | -0.0221 | +0.0085 | That run used our fork for the fp16 port of QSA and two RDNA3 MoE fixes, which go in separate PRs. On this branch alone the QSA path is bf16, like upstream.
## Details What changes. Most of the PR is new files: - `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_octave.py`: the format and its PyTorch reference, which defines the byte layout. - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_octave_attn.py`: the backend and its metadata builder. - `csrc/attention/octave_*`, the kernels: - store, reduce, rotation and a portable decode, shared by both architectures; - WMMA decode and prefill for gfx1100; - MFMA decode and prefill for gfx942; - the op registration in `octave_torch_bindings.cpp`. - Tests, docs, and `--model` plus the new cache dtypes in `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`. Changes to existing files are small: - the three cache dtypes in `vllm/config/cache.py`, `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py` and `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`; - the backend in the registry and in the ROCm platform's selection; - the sources in `CMakeLists.txt`; - `customize_spec` now runs under the current vLLM config, because the backend needs the model's rotary dims to size the slot; - in `qwen4_exp` (QSA), Octave as the main cache through a sparse decode, with the new fused QSA prepare turned off for an Octave cache, since it writes raw BF16 K/V. Nothing changes for other backends or cache dtypes. Design choices a reviewer may want to know about: - **Native kernels only.** There is no Triton fallback; an architecture is added once it has its own kernels and passes the tests and an end-to-end run. The RFC lists what each one needs. - **The metadata builder is the backend's own.** It builds the per-query maps on the device without host syncs, supports `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs, and refreshes the maps between fused MTP draft steps. - **On gfx942**: - QK runs on `v_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`, with the query split into high and low int8 halves. - V is widened to fp16 by one `v_perm`: each codebook byte becomes an exact fp16 denormal, which the MI300 MFMA keeps. - The decode file is built with `-amdgpu-mfma-vgpr-form`, so the accumulators do not halve the occupancy. - **Supported models.** Head size 256 with 64 RoPE dims, i.e. Qwen3-Next and Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8. - The decode handles up to 8 query heads per KV head on each GPU. - The sparse decode and the exact sink/recent window are QSA-only and gfx1100-only for now. - Head size 128 is the next step. - **Size.** This is a large PR: about 1.4k lines of gfx942 kernels on top of the RDNA3 ones. Each architecture lives in its own file behind the same `octave_prefill` / `octave_decode` entry points, so it can be reviewed and later removed on its own. **Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs and issues for `octave`, `turboquant rocm`, `kv cache 3-bit`, `kv cache quantization hip` and `lloyd-max kv`. The closest are: - UltraQuant (#57057): FP4 with FlyDSL for gfx950, built on TurboQuant. - KVarN (#46613 / #46812): Triton, CUDA-first. - #43835: HIP int8/int4 for CDNA. - #40396: a Triton TurboQuant decode for MI300X. - #53231: TurboQuant for Gemma 4 on ROCm. - #59132: Triton attention for RDNA without KV quantization. None targets RDNA with native kernels, and none runs below 8 bits with MTP on ROCm. **AI assistance.** I used AI assistance to write this PR: Claude, and Qwen3.8-27B running locally on the boxes it was measured on. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and evaluations above, and can answer for the change. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Bugfix][Watermarking] Keep draft prompt lengths valid under CUDA graphs
author: simon-veitner-redhat
body:
## Overview

Fix stale prompt lengths in the draft watermark deduplication mask under CUDA graphs. The bug came in with #56807. I found it while reviewing #59554, which would expose DFlash to it too.

## Claims

- With `dual_key_gumbel` and the default `deduplicate_contexts="single_turn"`, draft sampling under FULL CUDA graphs (default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) read prompt lengths from a stale UVA buffer after new requests arrived. This affects EAGLE3, MTP and DSpark (reproduced; EAGLE shares the autoregressive path). Some drafts were sampled without key A where they should carry it, and some repeated contexts were not deduplicated. Graph and eager mode now agree.
- No host sync, and no end-to-end change I can separate from run-to-run noise (see Performance). The fix adds one async copy of `max_num_reqs` int32 values per propose. The captured dedup kernel then reads device memory instead of pinned host memory, which is faster in a microbenchmark.

## Validation

Engine harness: Qwen3-4B targets (Qwen3.5-0.8B for MTP) with dedup `single_turn`. It compares the dedup mask each draft row actually used against a CPU reference built from the true prompt lengths. Compared with the engine-level script under Reproduction, it also covers Poisson arrivals, MTP and DSpark. λ is arrivals per engine step.

| Workload | Before (FULL graph) | After (FULL graph) | Eager |
|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 K=3, crafted (one request at a time, prompt-copying) | 576/1905 mask rows wrong; 536 accepted drafts lacked key A | 0/1896 | 0/1896 |
| EAGLE3 K=3, online Poisson (λ=0.2, mean concurrency 12) | 43/23178 mask rows wrong (41 falsely skipped, 2 missed dedup) | 0/23178 | 0/23325 |
| MTP K=3, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 32.6% / 2.06% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |
| DSpark K=7, crafted / online λ=0.02 | 39.5% / 2.05% of accepted drafts falsely skipped; online also 74 rows with missed dedup | n/a / 0 | 0 / n/a |

The MTP and DSpark "after" numbers come from the harness's patched `prepare()`, not from a commit tree. The EAGLE3 online "after" rows used the first revision of this fix, which differed only in copying into a `[:num_reqs]` slice. The EAGLE3 crafted "after" and eager runs use this commit.

Host sync: `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, EAGLE3 under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, 12 staggered admissions and 98 `prepare()` calls: clean. A deliberate `.item()` in `prepare()` trips the check, so the check does cover this path.

Unit test:

```bash
pytest tests/watermarking/test_watermarking.py -k reads_current_prompt_lens   # fails on main, passes with the fix
pytest tests/watermarking/                                                    # 148 passed (B300)
```

The test is CUDA-only. CI runs `tests/watermarking` only in the CPU "V1 Others" step, where it is skipped. I ran it locally on a B300: it fails on main and passes with the fix, and the suite passes (148).

About 1-2% of accepted drafts are affected at low traffic (EAGLE3 0.98%, MTP 2.06%, DSpark 2.05%) and 0.54% when busy (EAGLE3). Per-category detection rates in paired runs are identical for EAGLE3 and within noise for MTP and DSpark: at most 2 of 19-20 requests differ. The bug still breaks the watermark's own contract, and graph and eager runs diverge.

### Performance

Setup: B300, Qwen3-4B with EAGLE3 (`AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3`, K=3, probabilistic), `dual_key_gumbel`, temperature 1.0, random 1024 in / 256 out with `--ignore-eos` (64 prompts at c=1 and c=8, 256 at c=64), default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Main and fix servers ran in parallel on two GPUs, swapped each round, for 10 rounds of 2 passes. Δ is the mean of the per-round paired change, ± the 95% CI. A/A is the same comparison of main against main (4 rounds).

| Concurrency | Output tok/s (main → fix) | Δ tok/s | Δ mean TPOT | Δ mean TTFT | Acceptance length | A/A Δ tok/s | A/A Δ TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 464.7 → 462.3 | −0.5% ± 0.6 | +0.5% ± 0.6 | +1.8% ± 2.0 | 1.632 → 1.632 | −0.4% ± 0.6 | +0.6% ± 3.4 |
| 8 | 3032 → 3012 | −0.6% ± 0.8 | +0.4% ± 0.9 | +2.3% ± 1.7 | 1.658 → 1.662 | −0.3% ± 3.3 | −1.2% ± 5.6 |
| 64 | 10543 → 10495 | −0.4% ± 0.8 | +0.3% ± 0.9 | +0.8% ± 1.5 | 1.533 → 1.533 | +0.3% ± 1.2 | −0.7% ± 4.1 |

Throughput and TPOT change by less than 1%, with CIs that include zero. The A/A differences are of similar size.

Mean TTFT is 0.35-0.65 ms (0.8-2.3%) higher. Only the c=8 CI excludes zero (+0.7% to +4.0%). Between two identical main servers, per-round TTFT differences range from −6% to +3%, and one A/A CI (c=64 acceptance length) also excludes zero. I read the TTFT difference as noise, but these runs cannot rule out a TTFT cost of a few percent at c=8.

`prepare()` alone, with a UVA-backed prompt-length source and the speculator's two gathers: host time goes from 48.4-48.9 µs to 51.4-52.1 µs (+3 µs for one more copy launch). The copy itself takes 4.2 µs on the GPU at `max_num_reqs=1024` and 0.9 µs at 256. The dedup kernel runs once per draft step, so three times per propose at K=3. Replayed in a CUDA graph, those three steps get faster because the kernel reads device memory instead of pinned host memory: 12.3 → 8.7 µs with 1 request and 30.2 → 17.0 µs with 1024 requests (`max_num_reqs=1024`).

### Reproduction

A standalone script shows the bug without a model. It captures the draft dedup mask in a CUDA graph, admits a request (which moves `prompt_len.gpu` to the next pool buffer), and compares the replayed graph with eager mode. Run it on a CUDA GPU with `python repro_stale_prompt_len.py`.

<details>
<summary>repro_stale_prompt_len.py</summary>

```python
# Draft watermark dedup mask under a CUDA graph reads a stale prompt length.
import torch

import vllm
from vllm.v1.watermarking.gumbel import GumbelWatermarker
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.buffer_utils import UvaBackedTensor

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
dev = torch.device("cuda")
wm = DraftWatermarker(GumbelWatermarker(key=42, context_width=2), max_num_reqs=1,
                      device=dev, num_speculative_steps=1,
                      deduplicate_contexts="single_turn",
                      deduplicate_contexts_max_history=None)
prompt_len = UvaBackedTensor(1, dtype=torch.int32)  # like req_states.prompt_len
# Request in slot 0: prompt [5, 6, 9], generated [5, 6], next draft context
# [5, 6]. The context repeats only inside the prompt, so with single_turn the
# draft must use key A. Read with prompt length 0, it looks like repeated
# generated text and the draft skips key A.
tokens = torch.tensor([[5, 6, 9, 5, 6]], device=dev)
total_len = torch.tensor([5], device=dev)
ctx = torch.tensor([[5, 6]], device=dev)
enabled = torch.tensor([True], device=dev)
logits = torch.zeros(1, 8, device=dev)
idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
temp, draft_step = torch.ones(1, device=dev), torch.tensor(0, device=dev)

def prepare():  # the speculator calls this on every propose()
    wm.prepare(ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_len.gpu, total_len)

def uses_key_a():  # per-row mask that draft sampling uses for key A
    return wm._sampling_state(logits, idx, temp, draft_step, ctx)[1]

prepare()  # capture time: slot 0 has prompt length 0
uses_key_a()  # warm up outside capture
graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
    graph_out = uses_key_a()
# A step that admits a request runs copy_to_uva(), which moves
# prompt_len.gpu to the next buffer of its round-robin pool.
prompt_len.np[0] = 3
prompt_len.copy_to_uva()
prepare()
eager = uses_key_a().item()
graph.replay()
replayed = graph_out.item()
print(f"eager: key A={eager}  graph: key A={replayed}  ->",
      "OK" if eager == replayed else "STALE prompt length in graph")
```

</details>

Main:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=False  -> STALE prompt length in graph
```

With the fix:

```
eager: key A=True  graph: key A=True  -> OK
```

An engine-level script runs EAGLE3 with `dual_key_gumbel` through `LLM`, admits 24 requests one at a time, and counts draft rows whose dedup mask differs from the mask built from the current prompt lengths. Run `python engine_repro.py` for the default CUDA graph mode and `python engine_repro.py eager` for eager mode (30-45 s each on a B300).

<details>
<summary>engine_repro.py</summary>

```python
# EAGLE3 + dual_key_gumbel: compare the dedup mask each draft row used with the
# mask recomputed, in the same CUDA graph, from the current prompt lengths.
import os
import sys

import torch

os.environ.update(VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER="1", VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING="0")
import vllm  # noqa: E402
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.watermarking.spec_decode import DraftWatermarker as DW  # noqa: E402
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark import draft_watermarking_mask  # noqa: E402

print("vllm from", vllm.__file__)
orig_init, orig_prepare, orig_state = DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state
instances = []

def __init__(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args):
    orig_init(self, wm, max_num_reqs, device, *args)
    self.true_pl = torch.zeros(max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    self.stats = torch.zeros(3, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)  # rows, wrong, skip
    instances.append(self)

def prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens):
    orig_prepare(self, ctx, enabled, tokens, prompt_lens, total_lens)
    self.true_pl.copy_(prompt_lens)  # current prompt lengths

def _sampling_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx):
    steps, mask = orig_state(self, logits, idx, temps, step, ctx)
    ref = draft_watermarking_mask(
        self.all_token_ids, idx, self.true_pl, self.total_lens, self.prior_contexts,
        ctx, steps, self.enabled[: len(ctx)] & (temps != 0),
        self.deduplicate_contexts_max_history, False)
    self.stats += torch.stack(
        [torch.ones_like(ref).sum(), (mask != ref).sum(), (ref & ~mask).sum()])
    return steps, mask

DW.__init__, DW.prepare, DW._sampling_state = __init__, prepare, _sampling_state
wm = {"algorithm": "dual_key_gumbel", "key": 42, "context_width": 4}
spec = {"method": "eagle3", "model": "AngelSlim/Qwen3-4B_eagle3",
        "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}
llm = LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-4B", speculative_config=spec, watermark_config=wm, seed=0,
          max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.5,
          enforce_eager=sys.argv[1:] == ["eager"])
(dw,) = instances
dw.stats.zero_()  # drop warmup and capture rows
text = ("The committee met on Tuesday to review the annual budget. The members agreed "
        "to fund the public libraries, repair the old bridge near the river, and hire "
        "two more nurses for the clinic. The mayor promised a full report next month.")
for i in range(24):  # one request at a time; each admission rotates the UVA pool
    ask = f"Repeat exactly, word for word:\n{text}" if i % 3 == 1 else "Say hi."
    llm.chat([{"role": "user", "content": f"[{i}] {ask}"}],
             SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, seed=i, max_tokens=96), use_tqdm=False,
             chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False})
rows, wrong, skipped = dw.stats.tolist()
print(f"draft rows={rows}  mask rows wrong={wrong}  wrongly skipped key A={skipped}")
```

</details>

| Run | Output |
|---|---|
| Main, CUDA graphs (2 runs, identical) | `draft rows=714  mask rows wrong=129  wrongly skipped key A=129` |
| Fix, CUDA graphs | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Main, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |
| Fix, eager | `draft rows=720  mask rows wrong=0  wrongly skipped key A=0` |


## Details

**Root cause:** `req_states.prompt_len` is a `UvaBackedTensor`. `copy_to_uva()` runs from `apply_staged_writes` on steps that add requests, and it moves `.gpu` round-robin across the buffer pool. `DraftWatermarker.prepare()` stored that reference, so a captured `draft_watermarking_mask` kept reading the capture-time buffer. Newly admitted requests then see the previous occupant's prompt length until the pool comes back around:
- If the stale length is shorter than the real one, prompt n-grams count as generated history and the draft skips key A.
- If it is longer, real repeats are missed.

**Fix:** `DraftWatermarker` owns an int32 `[max_num_reqs]` buffer, and `prepare()` copies into it. This follows the existing `contexts` and `enabled` copies in the same method. It is also the principle MRV2 states for fused draft decoding: replayed tensor state must live in persistent storage.

I found no other inputs to captured draft sampling that go stale:
- `all_token_ids` and `total_len` are `StagedWriteTensor`s whose `.gpu` never moves.
- `contexts` and `enabled` are already copied into owned buffers.
- Other UVA-backed inputs to the draft path (temperature, seeds) are already copied into speculator-owned buffers. The remaining readers run eagerly.

**Unchanged behavior:** eager mode and the watermark-off path are unaffected. By code inspection, dedup modes `none` and `all` do not depend on prompt lengths: `none` returns before the mask is built, and `all` searches from position 0. The copy still runs in those modes; its cost is negligible.

**Alternatives:**
- Making `RequestState.prompt_len` a stable `StagedWriteTensor` would fix this for every future graph reader. It touches the penalties, bad_words, trace_replay and model_runner readers, and the `LogitsProcessor` interface types `prompt_len` as `UvaBackedTensor`, so it is better done as a separate refactor.
- A persistent device mirror inside `UvaBackedTensor` would cost a copy for every user.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Overlap the mHC gate projection with attention and FFN
author: cpersson-amd
body:
## Overview

On ROCm, each DeepSeek V4.1 mHC seam ran the whole fused AITER kernel pair on the default stream before the next sublayer could start. That pair is the post block, the gate projection, Sinkhorn, and the collapse with RMSNorm. This PR moves the gate projection onto a side stream inside FULL HIP graphs, so it overlaps with the following attention or FFN. The default stream now only runs the post block plus the RMSNorm'd collapse, in one new Triton kernel. This is the ROCm counterpart of the CUDA overlap in [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603).

## Claims

- Output throughput is up 0.3% to 5.4% end to end on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, EP, FP8 KV, MI355X, at every concurrency from 1 to 128 at TP2, TP4 and TP8.
- The new residual and the gates (post, comb, next pre) are bit-identical to the fused AITER seam. The layer input is bit-identical up to 16 tokens and within one bf16 ulp above that.
- No change outside FULL-graph decode with at most 128 tokens. Prefill, piecewise graphs, eager mode, CUDA and DSpark draft layers keep the current path.



## Validation



### Kernel

MI355X, HIP-graph replay time per seam. "Fused" is `mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rms_norm_aiter` (main + reduce kernels). "Input kernel" is the new `mhc_post_collapse_rms_norm_triton`, the only part left on the default stream. "Gates" is the side-stream work.


| tokens | fused (µs) | input kernel (µs) | gates on side stream (µs) |
| ------ | ---------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1      | 9.91       | 4.15              | 8.48                      |
| 4      | 10.24      | 4.26              | 9.01                      |
| 16     | 10.41      | 4.37              | 9.17                      |


The default-stream seam goes from about 10 µs to about 4.3 µs. That is roughly 0.5 ms per decode step across the 86 seams that take the overlap (43 layers × 2).

### End-to-end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, TP4, EP, FP8 KV, 12 sweep points. Mean TPOT in ms and output throughput in tok/s:


| input / output | concurrency | TPOT main | TPOT this PR | Δ     | tok/s main | tok/s this PR | Δ     |
| -------------- | ----------- | --------- | ------------ | ----- | ---------- | ------------- | ----- |
| 8192 / 1024    | 4           | 8.08      | 7.70         | -4.8% | 466.71     | 488.68        | +4.7% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 8           | 9.80      | 9.46         | -3.5% | 773.17     | 799.60        | +3.4% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 16          | 11.84     | 11.50        | -2.9% | 1262.50    | 1300.66       | +3.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 32          | 16.12     | 15.69        | -2.7% | 1786.03    | 1833.31       | +2.6% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 64          | 23.14     | 22.90        | -1.1% | 2516.82    | 2539.97       | +0.9% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 128         | 35.31     | 34.51        | -2.3% | 3161.18    | 3225.27       | +2.0% |
| 8192 / 1024    | 256         | 58.27     | 57.96        | -0.5% | 3795.31    | 3815.37       | +0.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 4           | 13.80     | 13.47        | -2.4% | 227.83     | 233.61        | +2.5% |
| 60000 / 600    | 16          | 39.88     | 39.98        | +0.2% | 337.21     | 338.35        | +0.3% |
| 60000 / 600    | 64          | 138.79    | 136.17       | -1.9% | 388.60     | 394.46        | +1.5% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 4           | 16.85     | 16.53        | -1.9% | 185.12     | 187.66        | +1.4% |
| 128000 / 1024  | 16          | 54.22     | 53.73        | -0.9% | 247.55     | 250.08        | +1.0% |


The mean is -2.05% TPOT and +2.00% throughput. Throughput is higher at all 12 points and TPOT lower at 11; the exception is 60000 / 600 at concurrency 16, at +0.2%. Median TPOT gives -2.14%, also 11 of 12, so the whole distribution moves rather than a tail.

**TP2, TP4 and TP8 at concurrency 1 to 128.** Random 2048 in / 256 out, same build for both arms on one node, overlap on against `MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS=0`. The overlap arm ran with a limit of 512, which at these concurrencies covers the same decode steps as 128. TP2 and TP8 had a warm-up pass and TP4 did not. These sweeps predate the switch to the global aux stream and events. Change in output throughput:

| concurrency | TP2   | TP4   | TP8   |
| ----------- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1           | +5.4% | +5.2% | +5.4% |
| 2           | +5.0% | +5.4% | +4.9% |
| 4           | +4.5% | +4.7% | +4.0% |
| 8           | +3.4% | +3.7% | +3.6% |
| 16          | +3.0% | +3.2% | +4.2% |
| 24          | +2.3% | +3.9% | +3.7% |
| 32          | +1.9% | +2.9% | +2.6% |
| 48          | +2.2% | +2.8% | +3.7% |
| 64          | +1.3% | +2.9% | +2.4% |
| 96          | +0.8% | +2.0% | +0.3% |
| 128         | +1.4% | +1.7% | +1.4% |

Every point improves. The gain shrinks from about +5% at concurrency 1 to +0.3–2% at 96–128, where it is within about 1% run-to-run noise.

### Accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, `lm_eval` `local-completions`, full test split, `num_concurrent=32`:


| run     | flexible-extract | strict-match    |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| default | 0.9227 ± 0.0074  | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |
| this PR | 0.9234 ± 0.0073  | 0.9234 ± 0.0073 |


### Tests

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py -k rocm
```

All pass on MI355X. `test_deepseek_v41_rocm_mhc_overlap_matches_fused_seam` is new and runs at 1, 2, 7, 16, 64 and 128 tokens. After joining the side stream, it compares every output with `MHCPreDelayedOp.forward_hip` (the fused AITER seam):

- the residual and gates must match exactly;
- the layer input must match within one bf16 ulp, and it must already be usable before the join;
- the same checks are repeated across three HIP-graph replays with changing inputs.

CI runs it in `:amd: (MI355) mHC Kernels`.

## Details

**Why the split is exact.** In AITER's fused seam (`_mhc_fused_post_pre_delayed_rmsnorm_main_kernel`), the post-mix is rounded to bf16 once, and that rounded `R'` feeds the projection, the square sums and the collapse. This PR splits the seam in two:

- The new kernel recomputes `R'` with the same expression order, so it is bit-identical, then collapses it with the carried pre-mix and applies the RMSNorm.
- The side stream runs AITER's own fused kernel on `R'` without the post (`HAS_POST=False`). Its gates are therefore the same numbers.

Only the RMSNorm's row sum differs. The new kernel holds a token's row in registers and sums it in one pass, while AITER reduces it across split-K programs, so the order changes. That is exact at decode sizes, and within one ulp otherwise.

**Gating.** The overlap runs only inside FULL HIP-graph capture, not in piecewise graphs, with `0 < tokens <= MHC_OVERLAP_MAX_TOKENS` (128). Fork and join then become graph edges; `DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention` keeps its aux streams to captured graphs for the same reason. It also requires AITER's fused delayed seam (`HAS_AITER_MHC_FUSED_POST_PRE_DELAYED_RMS_NORM`), `hc_mult == 4`, and no ubatching. The 128-token limit is the largest tested point. The gain was still positive there but shrinking (above), and the overlap was not measured beyond it, although FULL graphs go up to 512 tokens.

**Seams.** The overlap applies to every FFN seam and to the attention seam of every layer after the first. Layer 0's broadcast seam and Engram seams already take a different path and keep it. The gate stream is joined after attention and at the end of each layer, which is where the gates are next read. The stream is separate from the attention aux streams, as on CUDA. `record_stream` keeps the side stream's inputs and the main stream's gate outputs alive across the fork. No host synchronization is added.

**Limitations.**

- **Tuning:** the token limit was tuned on MI355X TP2, TP4 and TP8.



### Existing PRs

I searched vllm-project/vllm PRs (open and closed) for mHC overlap, coefficient and side-stream work on ROCm. None moves the mHC seam off the default stream on ROCm.

- [#57603](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57603) (merged) is the CUDA version. It needs SM100 and DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`, and stops at 16 tokens. This PR follows its structure, gating and join points.
- [#56853](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56853) (merged) adds an attention-side aux stream for DeepSeek-V4 HCA layers. It keeps the mHC seam serial on the default stream, which is what this PR changes.
- [#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) (merged) introduced the fused AITER delayed seam that this PR splits.

title: [Quantization] Support compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE with FP8 activations via Mxfp4MoEMethod
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load compressed-tensors checkpoints with MXFP4 weights and dynamic FP8 activations (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, `RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash converted to CT) and run them with the FP8 activations the checkpoint declares. Alternative to #59376 (cc @kylesayrs).

**Depends on #61556.** Humming 0.1.16, which `main` pins today, rejects FP8 (GS128) activations with MXFP4 weights, so these checkpoints fail to load with `--moe-backend humming` until #61556 lands.

## Claims

- MoE experts: `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4MoEMethod(Mxfp4MoEMethod)` only handles the `*_weight_packed` checkpoint naming and the declared activation scheme. Backend selection, weight conversion, size round-up, monolithic kernels and EPLB are inherited from the native MXFP4 method.
- The checkpoint's FP8 activation key reaches the Humming MoE backend. Before, it was dropped and Humming ran BF16 activations (W4A16) unless `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` was set.
- Dense linears with MXFP4 weights and FP8 inputs (GLM-5.3's dense MLPs target `Linear`) use a new `CompressedTensorsW4A8Mxfp4` scheme that requests FP8 activations, instead of the W4A4 scheme requesting MXFP4 activations.
- `get_moe_method` looks up the expert scheme with the layer's `ckpt_*_proj_name`, and DeepSeek-V4 (NVIDIA) passes `ckpt_names=("w1", "w2", "w3")`, so name-based targets such as `re:.*experts\.\d+\.w\d+$` match.

## Validation

H200 (SM90), `--moe-backend humming`, checked by inspecting the loaded layers.

| Model | Config | Dense MXFP4 linear | MoE experts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MXFP4-DSFP8 (real weights) | TP1 | n/a (FP8 block) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (W4A16 before this PR's 2nd commit) |
| GLM-5.3-MXFP4xFP8_BLOCK (dummy weights, 5 layers) | TP1, TP2, TP2+EP | Humming, FP8 GS128 (FP8 per-token before) | Humming, FP8 GS128 (BF16 before) |

These runs used the v0.32.0 release branch with #61556, and `main` with #61556 applied. With `main` alone, the Humming 0.1.16 schema check rejects the combination. EP selects `HummingGroupedExperts` and TP selects `HummingIndexedExperts`. Greedy outputs match between TP2 and TP2+EP.

GSM8K, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --temperature 0 --max-tokens 1024`, 1319 questions, 5-shot):

| Checkpoint / activations | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B` BF16 | 0.956 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A16 (previous behavior) | 0.958 |
| MXFP4-DSFP8, MoE W4A8 (this PR) | 0.961 |

Tests:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k mxfp4 -v  # 4 passed (H200, main)
pre-commit run --files <changed files>  # incl. mypy
```

The original commit was also validated on B300 (SM103): a layer harness loading a real `RoutedExperts` with random MXFP4 weights was bitwise equal to native `Mxfp4Config` across the default, monolithic TRTLLM, unaligned-shape, `triton_unfused`, `marlin`, `deep_gemm`, `flashinfer_cutlass` and `flashinfer_trtllm` backends. Converted DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 generated the same token ids and logprobs as the original checkpoint on 8 prompts.

## Details

**Root cause of the BF16 fallback.** For `Mxfp4MoeBackend.HUMMING`, the MoE conversion built Humming's input schema only from `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` (`TODO: read input_quant_config from quant_config`), so an unset env meant BF16. With schema fallback enabled, Humming also demotes group-scaled FP8 to A16 (`prefer wna16 for groupwise weight or groupwise input`). Output still looked correct, so the slower path went unnoticed. `Mxfp4MoEMethod` now takes an optional `activation_key`. The HUMMING conversion uses it with fallback disabled, unless the env override is set. Other backends ignore the key.

**Performance.** At the GLM-5.x expert GEMM shapes (N/K 4096/6144 and 6144/2048, 32 experts, top-8; `benchmarks/bench_humming.py` at the #61556 Humming pin), W4A8 is 1.4-1.8x faster than W4A16 for M >= 256. End to end, the small Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 1x H200 is 3-8% slower with W4A8 than with W4A16 across prefill- and decode-heavy runs (hidden 2048, expert intermediate 512, so the per-layer activation quantization is not amortized). This PR follows the checkpoint's declared scheme. `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG` still overrides it.

**Limitations**
- ROCm, XPU and CPU have no MXFP4 linear kernel for FP8 activations, so MXFP4 x FP8 dense layers keep the previous MXFP4-activation path there, with a warning. MI300 CI hit this; the linear test is CUDA-only.
- Blackwell: dense linears now use Humming FP8, which is slower than FlashInfer W4A4 on SM100 but matches the checkpoint. The MoE still picks its Blackwell backend without the activation key, so it uses MXFP8 or BF16 activations instead of `DEEPGEMM_MXFP4` (FP8 GS128 x MXFP4). Hooking that up is left for a follow-up issue.
- The AMD, XPU, CPU and V4.1 DeepSeek model variants still need the same `ckpt_names` one-liner; untested here.
- The rename breaks the pre-processed weight cache, so `supports_pre_processed_weights` is off for this method.
- Converting DeepSeek-V4-Flash with vllm-project/compressed-tensors#902 also emits `shared_experts.w\d+` targets, while vLLM names that layer `shared_experts.down_proj`; that needs a fix in the converter or model.

**Not a duplicate:** #59376 targets the same scheme with a different design; only one should merge. #58714 adds a separate CT -> `HummingMoEMethod` route for the same checkpoints; this PR covers that path through the native MXFP4 method. #56523 and #56306 migrate the W4A4 method to the oracle and do not touch this scheme.

title: [Feature][PCP] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support
author: wangyicong52
body:
## Overview

Add text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) support on NVIDIA CUDA to Model Runner V2 with FlashMLA sparse attention.

This PR intentionally targets a colocated single-model instance only. P/D disaggregation and KV transfer are not supported in this initial scope. The implementation keeps compressed KV, indexer, SWA, Engram lookback, MoE routing inputs, and padding consistent across PCP ranks while closing ratio-2 pairs split across PCP chunks with gathered predecessor rows.

Related to #25749 and #49109. This PR targets the DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/2 cache path and does not add the V4 C4/C128 or MegaMoE work from #43809.

## Supported Scope

- NVIDIA CUDA only: text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Model Runner V2 with `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`.
- One colocated model instance with PP=DP=DCP=1.
- Prefill PCP with arbitrary PCP chunk boundaries, including ranks with no local decode requests.
- Tensor parallelism and PCP can be composed; the validation below covers TP8/PCP1, TP4/PCP2, and TP2/PCP4 on an 8-GPU node.
- Expert parallel execution with the `allgather_reducescatter` all-to-all backend.
- Eager execution with synchronous scheduling.

## Not Supported Yet

- P/D disaggregation or any KV connector.
- ROCm.
- Pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, decode context parallelism, or microbatching with PCP.
- Prefix caching or SWA bounded replay with PCP.
- Speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, or MegaMoE with PCP.
- Multimodal inputs, encoder-decoder models, or LoRA with PCP.
- Attention backends other than the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA sparse path.

These constraints are deliberate so the first upstream step establishes standalone PCP correctness without mixing in KV handoff or replay semantics. Follow-up work will expand one boundary at a time: first standalone cache/replay behavior, then additional single-instance parallel topologies and runtime features, and finally P/D disaggregation with a minimal direct connector before layering prefix caching, bounded replay, and speculative Decode support.

## Implementation

- Compress ratio-2 groups on each rank's local token rows. Gather only the last FP32 row of each local chunk to close cross-rank pairs and keep the open ring rows consistent.
- Keep PCP linkage in model-specific compressor metadata; `InputBatch` and `PCPManager` remain unchanged relative to `main`.
- Gather BF16 compressor latents in one cache-insert path shared with ratio 1, then use the aligned gathered positions and slots for main KV and Indexer K writes.
- Keep Engram lookback, MoE routing token IDs, padding, compressed KV, indexer keys, and SWA metadata aligned across PCP ranks.
- Keep PCP collectives ordered consistently across ranks, including empty local shards and requests with no local decode rows.

Engram embeddings remain TP-sharded, so increasing PCP can increase host memory requirements.

## Rank-local Compressor Revision

Following LucasWilkinson's review, this revision adopts [wangyicong52/vllm#1](https://github.com/wangyicong52/vllm/pull/1), authored by Lucas Wilkinson, at `b06bea7abc4eb5cf6965fe704d16257ac7c70697`. title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Release shared memory on NIXL setup failure
author: DGlan
body:
## Overview

Prevent leaked shared memory when ECCPU scheduler initialization fails with NIXL enabled. The constructor currently raises without releasing the region it has already allocated.

## Claims

- Failed NIXL setup releases the scheduler-owned mmap file, file descriptors, and mapping while preserving the original exception.

## Validation

Review validation with NIXL 1.4.1: the previous constructor test file reproduced the test-order failure (6 passed, 1 failed); importing `data.nixl` before monkeypatching fixes its cached bindings, and all 7 constructor tests pass together. The suites below were rerun after merging upstream main.

The missing-NIXL regression fails against the unchanged scheduler because the mmap file remains, and passes with this fix. A second CPU regression raises during control-transport creation after data transport setup, and checks deregistration, shared-region release, and preservation of the original exception.

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/scheduler \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py -q
# 76 passed (NIXL 1.4.1 installed)

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  -m cpu_test tests/v1/ec_connector/unit -q
# 62 passed, 350 deselected

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_ctor.py \
  vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/cpu/scheduler/__init__.py
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and test tethering.
```


Nearby transport/session/scheduler tests also passed (95 tests):

```bash
uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_data.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_session.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_control.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_consumer.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_scheduler_nixl_producer.py -q
```

A separate CPU check exercised `ECConnectorFactory` through `ECCPUConnector` using real `VllmConfig`/`ModelConfig` objects and a local tiny Llava configuration, without replacing the shared-memory factory. The unchanged scheduler left the file, two file descriptors, and a mapping after the missing-NIXL error; the fixed scheduler left none, with the same error. Descriptors and mappings were checked through `/proc/self/fd` and `/proc/self/maps`.

Environment: Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL, Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cpu, editable source with official v0.30.0 CPU precompiled binaries. Exact-commit CPU binaries were unavailable. NIXL 1.4.1 was installed for this review revision, and the constructor wiring test exercised real NIXL registration and ZMQ session startup. Full GPU serving and cross-process NIXL data transfer were not run; local validation covers scheduler construction and startup-failure cleanup. The new test is selected by the existing CPU EC connector job in `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml`.

## Details

The region is allocated before `_setup_nixl`; if setup raises, the caller never receives a scheduler to shut down. The constructor owns failure unwinding through `shutdown()`, releasing NIXL resources before the shared region. `_setup_nixl()` propagates errors without a second cleanup handler.

Related: #56507, #56508. The related test/doc PR covers import isolation and documentation, rather than constructor cleanup. Searches for EC scheduler cleanup, NIXL initialization, and shared-memory leaks found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex prepared the patch and this review revision, and ran the validation above. The submitting human reviewed the original patch, personally reran its 74-pass/1-skip suite, and authorized this revision to address the review. No inference-output or performance change is claimed.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Exchange packed FP8 Engram rows across DP and feed wkv MXFP8
author: Juntian777
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables are already MXFP8 (FP8 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values) and `wkv` is an MXFP8 GEMM, but the lookup dequantizes each row to BF16, DP replicas all-gather those 512-byte rows layer by layer, and `wkv` quantizes them right back. This PR keeps rows packed from the host table to `wkv`.

- **Packed rows, direct MXFP8.** The lookup copies each row's 256 FP8 bytes and 8 scale bytes as they are, and one unpack kernel writes them in FlashInfer's MXFP8 activation layout (F8_128x4 scales). `wkv` takes them as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both the dequant and the requant are gone, and the output is bit-identical.
- **One all-to-all per prefill step.** `EngramBatch` looks up every local Engram layer into one packed buffer and exchanges it with a single all-to-all, which sends each rank only its own tokens (264 instead of 512 bytes per head row, 1/DP of an all-gather), then unpacks all layers in one launch.
- **Peer exchange for decode.** Below 128 tokens per rank, `EngramPeerExchange` replaces the hash all-gather and the per-layer row all-gathers: ranks publish ids in symmetric memory, look up their head shard for every peer's tokens, and read their own tokens back from the peers after a barrier. All layers share one lookup and one unpack launch.

The batched path serves DP-sharded tables (`embedding_across_dp` without DP-shared memory) with TP = 1, `head_dim % 128 == 0`, no LoRA (it wraps `wkv` after construction), and a `wkv` kernel that takes F8_128x4 scales (reusing `can_fuse_query_quant`). The peer exchange also needs SM100, CPU offload, and 2/4/8 fully connected GPUs; without it every slot uses the all-to-all, which on DEP4 HBM tables at 1–127 tokens per rank is 19–58 us faster than the BF16 path. Everything else, including TP, DP-shared tables, single replicas and ROCm, keeps the existing BF16 path unchanged. Communication stays on the current stream and `wkv` still runs in `Engram.forward`.

Also changed along the way:

- `EngramBatch` is an `nn.Module`, so the peer exchange's pointer tables are model buffers that level-2 sleep restores.
- `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` and the Engram unpack kernel share the F8_128x4 scale offset and size helpers.

## Kernel microbenchmark

The benchmarks, E2E runs and the first accuracy table were measured on d593d7f5df. 3724967bb9 only drops paths that DEP + THP never takes and keeps its `wkv` outputs bitwise identical (see Test Result).

Engram only, two layers (lookup, exchange, and anything needed to reach the MXFP8 `wkv` input), 4 x GB300 in one node. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB per layer) as DP-shared `/dev/shm` tables or private THP shards, uniform random ids rotating 3 sets, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample, full CUDA graph replay, median of 40 samples of the slowest rank, best of 2 rounds. Since this PR's output is already the `wkv` input, the BF16 columns include their activation quantization (17 us for decode, 203 us at 32K tokens).

DEP4:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 80 | 36 | 2.22x |
| 8 | 34 | 81 | 38 | 2.13x |
| 32 | 38 | 93 | 40 | 2.33x |
| 64 | 44 | 106 | 43 | 2.47x |
| 127 | 136 | 136 | 50 | 2.72x |
| 128 | 140 | 136 | 72 | 1.89x |
| 1024 | 2442 | 315 | 179 | 1.76x |
| 4096 | 5326 | 1097 | 534 | 2.05x |
| 8192 | 8224 | 2087 | 1010 | 2.07x |
| 16384 | 11854 | 4047 | 1954 | 2.07x |
| 32768 | 16008 | 7860 | 3800 | 2.07x |

DEP2:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 73 | 38 | 1.92x |
| 8 | 34 | 74 | 40 | 1.85x |
| 32 | 35 | 81 | 43 | 1.88x |
| 64 | 41 | 90 | 44 | 2.05x |
| 127 | 66 | 107 | 49 | 2.18x |
| 128 | 62 | 107 | 71 | 1.51x |
| 1024 | 2015 | 228 | 168 | 1.36x |
| 4096 | 4629 | 754 | 507 | 1.49x |
| 8192 | 6873 | 1407 | 970 | 1.45x |
| 16384 | 9511 | 2709 | 1879 | 1.44x |
| 32768 | 12389 | 5268 | 3672 | 1.43x |

DP-shared tables need no exchange, so at 1–64 tokens they are at most 8 us faster than this PR; from 1024 tokens this PR is 3.4–13.6x faster than them. The 127 → 128 step is the switch from the peer exchange to the all-to-all.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the packed lookup output, and a 4-GPU check of the batched staging across peer and all-to-all slots, uneven and idle replicas, and full and breakable CUDA graph replays. The peer path needs SM100, so other GPUs only cover the all-to-all path.

## Test Result

On 3724967bb9, 202 passed on 4x GB200 (102 Engram kernel, 27 distributed, 73 `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py`). Ruff, format and mypy pass.

Also checked locally, without adding tests:

- The staged MXFP8 bytes equal the table rows byte for byte on DEP2 and DEP4 with 22 and 24 heads, 1–3 layers starting at a non-zero hash index, pinned, THP and HBM tables, 1–4096 tokens around the 127/128 boundary (sorted lookups included), and 24 unsynchronized steps that switch between peer exchange and all-to-all.
- Real layer 1 and 14 checkpoint rows and `wkv` weights: the `wkv` output is bitwise identical to the BF16 path at 129, 1024 and 4096 tokens, with CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS.
- DEP4 `Engram.forward` through the peer exchange and the all-to-all in eager mode and full and breakable graph replays: bitwise identical to the BF16 path.
- 3724967bb9 vs d593d7f5df on DEP4 (24 heads x 256, 2 layers, 10% dead ids, idle ranks; pinned tables at 1–512 and HBM tables at 128–512 tokens per rank): staged MXFP8 values and `wkv` outputs (CuTe-DSL and CUTLASS) are bitwise identical; only the scales of padding and unowned rows change from 127 to 0.
- After a simulated level-2 sleep the peer exchange's pointer tables are restored and its lookups stay exact.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV cache, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, prefix caching off. Offline `LLM` per DP rank, one prompt per rank (nominal length minus 7 tokens per rank), `max_tokens=1`; TTFT is `scheduled_ts` to `first_token_ts` on the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat. Measured on top of #59532 with `max_cudagraph_capture_size=8192` (default size list, so 1K–8K prefills run in PIECEWISE graphs) and `max_num_seqs=64`. Prompts are uniformly random token ids; a repeated sentence keeps the few distinct n-gram rows in cache and hides Engram entirely.

| tokens/rank | DP-shared TTFT (ms) | THP + all-gather TTFT (ms) | this PR TTFT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 60.2 | 61.7 | 60.5 | 0.99x | 1.02x |
| 4096 | 129.7 | 128.0 | 127.2 | 1.02x | 1.01x |
| 8192 | 220.2 | 214.2 | 213.9 | 1.03x | 1.00x |
| 16384 | 248.1 | 242.6 | 240.5 | 1.03x | 1.01x |
| 32768 | 466.0 | 447.4 | 446.5 | 1.04x | 1.00x |

Repeat spread is under 2.5 ms (5 ms for DP-shared at 32K). The gain over DP-shared tables matches the microbenchmark: at 8K the two Engram layers take 7.2 ms less, close to the 6.3 ms measured end to end. Against THP tables with all-gather it is about 1 ms per step, within noise end to end.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

Same setup on `main` (default capture sizes up to 512, `max_num_seqs=128`), short prompts, 64 output tokens with the decode token fixed to hold MoE routing constant. Mean request TPOT of the slowest rank, median of 3 repeats after a warmup repeat.

| batch/rank | DP-shared TPOT (ms) | THP + all-gather TPOT (ms) | this PR TPOT (ms) | vs DP-shared | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.072 | 6.128 | 6.082 | 1.00x | 1.01x |
| 8 | 6.457 | 6.501 | 6.453 | 1.00x | 1.01x |
| 32 | 8.199 | 8.292 | 7.928 | 1.03x | 1.05x |
| 64 | 10.833 | 11.157 | 10.832 | 1.00x | 1.03x |
| 127 | 14.043 | 14.403 | 14.046 | 1.00x | 1.03x |

Engram is under 1% of TPOT, and the fixed decode token keeps its rows cache-resident, so decode shows that private THP tables no longer cost anything over DP-shared ones rather than the full lookup saving.

## Accuracy (DEP4, this PR)

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32, two passes on one `vllm serve` DEP4 server per side (same engine setup as the E2E runs, `main` with DP-shared tables vs this PR with THP tables). No request errors.

| | strict match (pass 1 / 2) | flexible extract (pass 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| `main`, DP-shared tables | 92.87% / 92.95% | 92.80% / 92.87% |
| this PR, THP tables | 93.33% / 93.10% | 93.25% / 93.03% |

Both are within one standard error (±0.7 points); no accuracy gain is claimed.

GSM8K with DSpark on 3724967bb9 (DEP4, MegaMoE, `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, 5 speculative tokens with adaptive verification, THP tables; same lm-eval setup with a 1024-token cap), against the DEP4 base run in #59511 with DP-shared tables:

| #59511 base, DP-shared tables | 92.57% | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |
| this PR, THP tables | 92.57% | 3.398 | 0.795 / 0.644 / 0.446 / 0.319 / 0.194 |

  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=4096,temperature=0"

The baseline uses `"dp_shared_memory":true,"use_thp":false`. The DSpark run uses the DEP4 GSM8K serve flags from #59511 plus the `--engram-config` above, and `max_gen_toks=1024`.

Searched open PRs for `engram`, `engram fp8`, `engram all-to-all`, `engram peer` and `DeepSeek-V4.1 engram`. #56989 packs FP8 rows for the TP head exchange (opt-in, TP > 1 without SP) and dequantizes them before `wkv`; this PR leaves TP alone and covers Engram DP, feeding `wkv` directly. #57893 tunes small-lookup tiles. #58766 fed MXFP8 rows to `wkv` through the existing gathers and was closed by its author after merge conflicts, without review; this PR keeps that idea and also replaces the gathers.

title: [MRV2][Spec Decode] Quantized draft lm_head for drafters that share the target head
author: stecasta
body:
## Overview **Decode at c=1 on SPEED-Bench goes from 39.4 to 46.5 tok/s (+18%) with average AL unchanged (-0.4%)** with an NVFP4 draft head, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 + MTP (k=3), one DGX Spark, measured on three nodes with the SM121 skinny-GEMM plans from #59753. An MTP or EAGLE drafter that shares the target's lm_head reads the whole head once per draft token; on a 248k x 2560 BF16 head that is the largest kernel in a draft step. A new opt-in key gives the drafter a private quantized copy of the head. The target still verifies with its own BF16 head, so outputs are unchanged; only the acceptance length can move. ```bash vllm serve --speculative-config \ '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "nvfp4"}' ``` ## Claims - `"nvfp4"`: E2M1 weights with an E4M3 scale per 16 values, weight-only on the platform's W4A16 kernel, chosen by `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel` (Marlin on SM12x; activations stay BF16/FP16). `"fp8"`: per-row FP8 weights and per-token FP8 activations, reusing the existing online `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod` on the platform FP8 kernel (`CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` on GB10). CUDA graphs and TP work (each rank quantizes its own shard). - Decode on GB10: +17.5% to +18.4% at c=1 and +9% to +11% at c=4 (NVFP4, three nodes), +10.8% / +6.5% (FP8, one node). AL within run-to-run noise, including multilingual (every row of the head stays available). GSM8K unchanged (earlier run, below). - Probabilistic drafting stays exact: the quantized logits are both sampled and used as q. - Extra memory: about 0.35 GiB (NVFP4) or 0.6 GiB (FP8) for a 248k x 2560 head, created inside model loading, so profiled KV sizing accounts for it. With `--kv-cache-memory-bytes`, leave room for it. ## Validation SPEED-Bench qualitative (11 categories at c=1 and c=4, greedy, 256 output tokens), Flash-Next, MTP k=3, real AL from the spec-decode counters, full vocabulary. Each node ran stock and the quantized head back to back; vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with the skinny-GEMM plans of #59753 applied, plus this PR. ``` decode tok/s per user stock c=1 NVFP4 c=1 stock c=4 NVFP4 c=4 p4242-0121 39.42 46.63 (+18.3%) 26.61 29.46 (+10.7%) p4242-0547 39.45 46.69 (+18.4%) 26.54 29.44 (+10.9%) p4242-0122 39.36 46.24 (+17.5%) 26.55 28.95 (+9.0%) p4242-0122, FP8 head 43.61 (+10.8%) 28.28 (+6.5%) AL, mean of 3 nodes stock 2.670 NVFP4 2.658 (-0.4%) multilingual 2.799 / 2.845 ```
Earlier measurement, before #59753 (ABBA, larger gain) Without the skinny-GEMM plans the BF16 head GEMV is slower, so the same change measured +27%. Stock and NVFP4 ran in ABBA order (stock, nvfp4, nvfp4, stock) on one GB10 node (p4242-0073, median SM clock 2242 MHz); numbers are the mean of the two runs per arm. | vs. BF16 head | AL (avg) | AL (multilingual) | decode c=1 | decode c=1 (multilingual) | decode c=4 | step, forced AL 3, c=1 | GSM8K (256) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | BF16 head (stock) | 2.673 | 2.859 | 35.6 tok/s | 36.9 tok/s | 27.2 tok/s | 73.7 ms | 243 | | NVFP4 draft head | 2.664 (-0.3%) | 2.851 (-0.3%) | **45.2 tok/s (+27.1%)** | 46.7 tok/s (+26.7%) | 30.4 tok/s (+11.7%) | 58.2 ms | 243 | | FP8 draft head (separate node, own stock) | +0.2% | -0.6% | **+21.0%** | +19.1% | +9.7% | 61.6 ms | 247 vs 244 | The FP8 serving row comes from a second GB10 node (p4242-0067, 2496 MHz, 7G KV) against its own stock arm (36.1 tok/s c=1, AL 2.664); the forced-AL step times and GSM8K for stock and NVFP4 are from an earlier same-node run (p4242-0074, 2489 MHz). Forced AL 3, c=4 per-user step: 114.2 / 102.4 / 104.1 ms (stock / NVFP4 / FP8).
Kernel choice, draft head GEMV only (248320 x 2560, CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 3 x 100 replays): ``` GB200 (SM100) GB10 (SM121, M>=4) BF16 (cuBLAS) 191 to 196 us 5.50 to 5.58 ms FP8 W8A8 (selector) 111 to 113 us 2.80 to 2.84 ms <- used for "fp8" FP8 W8A16 Marlin 145 to 153 us 2.80 to 2.82 ms NVFP4 W4A16 Marlin 133 to 149 us 1.60 to 1.64 ms <- used for "nvfp4" ``` FP8 reuses the online PTPC method (platform W8A8 kernel, needs SM89+): 1.3x faster than Marlin on GB200, parity on GB10. NVFP4 picks its kernel with `init_nvfp4_linear_kernel(use_a16=True)`, so `--linear-backend`, `linear_backend_per_quant` and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` apply as for any NVFP4 linear layer. On SM100/103 the default is the CuTe DSL W4A16 kernel, which measured 1.42x slower than Marlin at M=16 on GB200; `linear_backend_per_quant={"nvfp4_w4a16": "marlin"}` selects Marlin there. Independent reproduction at TP2 on 2x DGX Spark (earlier revision, MTP k=4, [#56577 comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56577#issuecomment-5994233686)): +18.5% (fp8) and +19.5% (nvfp4) decode at c=1, greedy outputs byte-identical across arms. Disclaimers: - Greedy decoding on this model is not bit-reproducible run to run; per-category AL moves up to about 3% in either direction for stock as well. Across the three nodes above stock varies by 0.2% and NVFP4 by 1.0%. Absolute tok/s also varies across Spark nodes and recipes, so compare arms only within one node. - The gain shrinks with concurrency, where more tokens share each head read. ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py # all passed (GB10) pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py -k draft_lm_head # 2 passed (GB10) ```
Setup Setup: vLLM nightly `0cbac6cd1` with #59753 applied (not in the earlier ABBA run), this PR and two Flash-Next serving prerequisites (#59309, #56273); `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ada4da32, FP8 KV cache, `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 7G` (8G in the earlier ABBA run), `--max-model-len 49152`, `--max-num-seqs 8`, MTP drafter MoE on Marlin. Every arm used the same settings.
## Details - Design: the quantization lives with the other online quantization methods, in `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py`. `quantized_lm_head_copy()` builds a plain `ParallelLMHead` with that quant method and quantizes it straight from this rank's shard of the target head, so no bf16 copy is made and the target head is unchanged. FP8 reuses the existing `Fp8PtpcOnlineLinearMethod`; NVFP4 adds a small weight-only method (`_LMHeadNvfp4Method`) that quantizes the head and hands it to the selected W4A16 kernel. `ParallelLMHead` gains an optional `quant_method` argument, which `VocabParallelEmbedding` already has. vllm-ascend overrides `ParallelLMHead.__init__` without this argument, so the soft-fail Ascend NPU interface check flags it; on Ascend, `draft_lm_head_quantization` needs the override updated. `"nvfp4"` needs a CUDA W4A16 kernel, so on ROCm only `"fp8"` is available and the tests skip the nvfp4 cases there. - Hook: `load_eagle_model` gives the drafter that head instead of the shared target head, including the MTP per-layer `shared_head.head`. - Derived state: the copy is kept out of layerwise reload and re-derived in place from the target head whenever the target's weights are replaced (`reload_weights`, weight transfer), so sleep mode, weight reload and weight transfer keep working. During a draft-only weight update the drafter shares the target head again, as on main, and the copy is re-derived when the update finishes. - Scope: MRV2 drafters loaded through `load_eagle_model` (EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP) that share an unquantized fp16/bf16 lm_head running in the model dtype; other cases are rejected at config validation or load. Gemma-4 MTP is excluded because it scores a subset of its tied embedding rows directly and has no shared lm_head. DFlash and DSpark can call the same helper in a follow-up. - Not a duplicate: #56577 (Qwen4Exp only, env var, eager only) and #47584 (DSpark only, env var) add an FP8 draft head for one model or method; this is the generic version behind one config key, with CUDA graphs and NVFP4. #59740 (reduced draft vocabulary) composes with it; both add a draft-head key to `speculative_config` and hook the same place in `load_eagle_model`, so whichever lands second will reuse this quantizer for the list rows (as `draft_token_map_quantization` there) rather than add a second one. #41000, #42124 and #58343 concern heads quantized in the checkpoint, and the online quantization framework (#51285) covers linear and MoE layers but not `ParallelLMHead`. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and benchmark harness; I reviewed every changed line and ran the measurements above.

**Reproduction on upstream main (DGX Spark, GB10)** Upstream main 02b83919aa with the heads of #59958, #59973, #59740, #60068 and #54614 merged, no other runtime patches. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 6 with confidence stop 0.6, sparse draft head via `draft_token_map` (32k ids, 16384 dynamic rows at rank 256, `draft_token_map_quantization: nvfp4`), FP8 KV, `host_file_gather` PLE tables. SPEED-Bench throughput 2K in / 1K out, fixed OSL, c=1, n=20: | Build | tok/s/user | AL | GSM8K-256 | |---|---|---|---| | upstream main + these PRs | 49.94 | 2.68 | 249/256 | | our internal stack, same node | 49.73 | 2.65 | 245/256 | The PR route reproduces the internal stack result within noise.

title: [Perf] V2 runner decode optimizations for NVIDIA Confidential Computing
author: ybgao-nvidia
body:
## Purpose

This PR supersedes #52226 by porting the NVIDIA Confidential Computing (CC) decode optimizations to the V2 GPU model runner, and fixes the UVA incoherence bug that makes V2 produce garbage under CC. 

The incoherence issue with UVA was initially reported in #57224 and independently fixed by @juhiechandra in #57404 via a runtime coherence probe in `is_uva_available()`. This PR instead gates UVA on CC detection and adds a staged-copy fallback so that disabling UVA does not reintroduce host-synchronous copy stalls.

### Background

NVIDIA Confidential Computing protects workloads in confidential VMs by encrypting PCIe traffic through bounce buffers. This has two consequences for the V2 runner:

1. **Pinned host memory is not coherent from the device.** The V2 runner's `UvaBufferPool` writes inputs into pinned host memory and has the GPU read them directly through the UVA mapping. Under CC the GPU sees a stale snapshot of that memory, so the model runner produces garbage.
2. **`cudaMemcpyAsync` on pinned memory is host-synchronous.** The issuing thread blocks until the copy, and everything already queued on its stream, completes. This causes:
   - **H2D input copies** on the compute stream to block the scheduler thread behind the in-flight forward pass.
   - **Per-step D2H token readback** to delay the next CUDA graph launch.

### Changes

All changes are gated on CC detection; non-CC code paths are untouched.

- **CC detection**: `Platform.is_confidential_compute()`, auto-detected via NVML on CUDA with a `VLLM_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE=0/1` override.
- **UVA disabled under CC**: `is_uva_available()` returns `False` under CC, so the buffer pool falls back to explicit copies. A new `StagedH2DBuffer` mirrors each pinned host buffer into a device tensor on every `uva()` call, keeping the pool's invariant that a slot is only reused once no GPU reader is in flight.
- **Staged H2D input copies**: `staged_h2d()` in `vllm/v1/conf_compute_utils.py` issues the host-synchronous copy on an idle prep stream so the host only waits for the transfer itself, then orders the compute stream after it with `wait_stream` / `record_stream`. `async_tensor_h2d()` routes through this path under CC, so call sites in `encoder_decoder.py`, `encoder_only.py`, and `zero_block_ids()` need no CC-specific logic.
- **Deferred D2H output readback**: `AsyncOutput` and `AsyncPoolingOutput` record a source-ready event on the main stream at construction and issue the D2H copies from `get_output()` on the executor's output thread, instead of blocking the scheduler thread.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_conf_compute_copies.py` covering UVA availability under CC, `staged_h2d()` with pinned and pageable sources, `async_tensor_h2d()` routing, `StagedH2DBuffer` pool round-trips, and deferred D2H semantics.
- Decode benchmark on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, B300, CC enabled, comparing against the V2 runner with CC off and against the V2 runner on `main` with CC on.

## Test Result

Decode throughput (output tok/s per GPU). Slowdown is the increase in time per output token relative to CC off.

| Concurrency | CC off | main, CC on | This PR, CC on | Slowdown before | Slowdown after |
|------------:|-------:|------------:|---------------:|----------------:|---------------:|
| 4           | 129    | 85          | 118            | 51.8%           | 9.3%           |
| 8           | 212    | 147         | 198            | 44.2%           | 7.1%           |
| 16          | 352    | 250         | 322            | 40.8%           | 9.3%           |
| 32          | 534    | 397         | 490            | 34.5%           | 9.0%           |
| 64          | 796    | 617         | 741            | 29.0%           | 7.4%           |
| 128         | 1229   | 953         | 1120           | 29.0%           | 9.7%           |

The per-token CC slowdown drops from 29–52% to 7–10% across all concurrencies, bringing CC throughput to 91–93% of the non-CC baseline.
speedup_claims: 52% to 7–10% across all concurrencies, bringing CC throughput

speedup_evidence.claim: 52% to 7–10% across all concurrencies, bringing CC throughput
