title: [Perf][ROCm][Kernel] Add W4A8 int8-dot MXFP4 GEMV for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 d…
author: xiao-llm
body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in MXFP4 linear kernel for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 (gfx11) decode. For 1-8 tokens, activations are quantized to int8 per 32-element group, and each group is reduced with `v_dot4_i32_iu8` (`__builtin_amdgcn_sudot4`). E2M1 values times 2 are integers in [-12, 12], so weights map to int8 exactly through a 16-entry table; one fp32 multiply per group applies the E8M0 weight scale, the activation scale, and the 1/2. The approach follows ggml's MMVQ / q8_1 path (llama.cpp, MIT).

- Weights are read in the Quark OCP MX checkpoint layout (`[N, K/2]` uint8 E2M1, `[N, K/32]` uint8 E8M0). No repack, no extra weight memory.
- M > 8 (prefill) runs the same math as `EmulationMxfp4LinearKernel` (activation QDQ, dequant, `F.linear`).
- The M <= 8 / M > 8 split is inside a custom op, so torch.compile and CUDA graphs see one op.

Enable with:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1
```

Opt-in because int8 activation rounding differs from the MXFP4 activation QDQ the checkpoint declares. With the flag off, or on non-gfx11 GPUs, kernel selection is unchanged.

Related: #46676 adds a W4A16 (fp32 FMA) scalar + WMMA MXFP4 kernel for gfx1100. This PR is independent: a different algorithm for the small-M regime (2-5x fewer instructions per weight at M = 1-8). The two PRs only touch the same registration lists.

## Benchmarks

AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, RDNA 3.5), `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, single stream (`--max-num-seqs 1`), CUDA graphs and torch.compile on, `vllm bench serve` random 128 in / 256 out.

### Comparison with #46676 and emulation (MTP=3, MXFP4 lm_head)

Same model, same machine, all three with the lm_head quantized to MXFP4 (see note). GSM8K 5-shot, lm-eval `local-completions`, greedy.

| Config | Decode kernel (M <= 8) | Decode tok/s | GSM8K (questions) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| **This PR + MXFP4 lm_head** | W4A8 int8-dot GEMV | **28.89** | **96.51% (1319)** |
| #46676 + MXFP4 lm_head | W4A16 scalar FMA (WMMA for M > 8) | 26.19 | 96.51% (1319) |
| Emulation + MXFP4 lm_head | dequant + `F.linear` | 4.94 | 96.75% (1319) |

- 10% faster than #46676 at equal accuracy, 5.8x faster than the default emulation path.
- For reference, llama.cpp (ROCmFP4 4-bit GGUF, own quantization incl. lm_head) runs 29.1 tok/s at MTP=3 on the same machine.

**Note on activations:** this PR skips the checkpoint's MXFP4 activation QDQ when the flag is on. Decode quantizes activations to int8 per 32-element group (finer than MXFP4); prompts (M > 8) use bf16 activations. Applying the MXFP4 activation QDQ on prompts while decoding with int8 activations dropped GSM8K to ~80% in our runs, so the prompt path is weight-only, matching #46676.

**Note on the MXFP4 lm_head:** the checkpoint ships the lm_head ([248320, 5120]) in bf16, and this PR keeps it that way. For the comparison above, it was quantized to MXFP4 at load time (round-to-nearest, one E8M0 scale per 32 weights), the same for all three configs. It cuts the lm_head from 2.54 GB to 0.68 GB; with MTP=3 the lm_head is read 4 times per step (3 draft + 1 verify), so this is worth ~6 tok/s (22.45 â†’ 28.89). It is not part of this PR and will be proposed separately.

The model card reports 95.0% (bf16 base: 93.3%) with sampling and thinking-mode settings

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
```

All pass on gfx1151. The new tests cover:

- output vs a reference implementation for M = 1..8, four shapes, fp16 and bf16;
- closeness to the bf16 dequantized result;
- M = 0 and M = 9 rejected by the op;
- `torch.library.opcheck`;
- CUDA graph capture and replay;
- dispatch for M = 1, 8, 9, 64 (kernel vs fallback);
- selection: chosen only with the flag on gfx11; MXFP6 and non-ROCm rejected.

Serve command used:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1 vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'   # MTP rows only
```

## Details

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `csrc/rocm/mxfp4_w4a8_gemv.cu` | int8 activation quant + W4A8 GEMV, templated on M = 1..8 and fp16/bf16 |
| `csrc/rocm/ops.h`, `csrc/rocm/torch_bindings.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` | build and register `_rocm_C::mxfp4_w4a8_gemv` |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp4/rdna_w4a8.py` | `RdnaW4A8MxFp4LinearKernel`, M-based dispatch in a custom op |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py` | first in the ROCm MXFP4 kernel list (selected only when supported) |
| `vllm/envs.py` | `VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8` (default `False`) |
| `vllm/_custom_ops.py` | Python wrapper and fake impl |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py` | new tests |

- Device code is compiled only for `__GFX11__` (empty stubs elsewhere); the host entry point also checks for gfx11 at runtime.
- One wave per output column; lanes stride over the 32-weight groups along K, then a shuffle reduction. Accumulation is fp32 over the full K, one rounding to the output dtype.

Trade-offs and follow-ups:

- One extra activation-quant launch per linear (fusing it into the GEMV is a follow-up).
- M > 8 dequantizes per call, as the emulation kernel does; a faster prefill path is a separate PR.

title: [Perf][Nemotron-Parse] Do image rescale/normalize on the device
author: HangruiCao2000
body:
## Overview

Opts `NemotronParseForConditionalGeneration` into vLLM's existing `mm_device_do_normalize` path, so the fixed 2048x1664 canvas travels to the device as `uint8` and the rescale/normalize happens in `FusedMMInputNorm` instead of as single-threaded CPU work inside the engine process.

Please do aware this change depends on pending tied embedding fix for nemoparse2.0 embedding.

The checkpoint ships its image processor as remote code, and its `preprocess(self, images, return_tensors=None, **kwargs)` **ignores** the `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs that `MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs` injects when the feature is on: it always runs `ToTensor` and normalizes from `self.do_normalize`. Setting the model flag alone would therefore normalize twice. The `_call_hf_processor` override replays the processor's own pipeline up to (but not including) `ToTensor` to produce the raw canvas, and raises -- pointing at `--no-mm-device-do-normalize` -- if a checkpoint does not expose that pipeline, so "feature on => `uint8`" holds by construction.

## Claims

- `supports_mm_device_do_normalize = True`; `build_mm_input_norm()` builds the norm and `_process_image_input` applies it unconditionally, as in the other models that opt in. With the feature off that is `IdentityInputNorm`, i.e. a plain cast.
- With the feature off, behaviour is identical to today.
- Both published checkpoints are handled: v1.2 (albumentations `transform` branch) and 2.0 (`_pad_to_size` branch).
- Payload per request drops 40.89 MB fp32 -> 10.22 MB uint8.

## Validation

Run on the latest `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` = `0.31.1rc1.dev23+g43b4aaea3`, whose `nemotron_parse.py` is byte-identical to this patch's parent and whose `layers/fusion/mm_input_norm.py` is byte-identical to this branch -- so the Triton `forward_cuda`, `IdentityInputNorm` and `_load_norm_params` exercised here are the ones this change targets. One H100, `--dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.25 --max-num-seqs 16`.

Greedy request on a sample document page (`max_tokens 512, temperature 0, top_k 1, repetition_penalty 1.1, skip_special_tokens false`):

| engine | flag | dtype at model | `input_norm` | output sha256[:16] | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| patched | on | `uint8` | `FusedMMInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| patched | off | `bfloat16` | `IdentityInputNorm` | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | off | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |
| unpatched | on | `bfloat16` | - | `b37da04a78014080` | 180 |

Unpatched + on logs `Model does not support mm_device_do_normalize, forcing ... False`, confirming the flag is the only opt-in.

**Numerics** -- device path vs the host path it replaces:

| case | bf16 | fp16 | fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| real page, 10,223,616 elements | **equal, 0 mismatched** | equal, 0 | max abs 2.4e-07 |
| all 3x256 possible byte values | **equal, 0 mismatched** | 3 at 1 ULP | max abs 4.8e-07 |
| `forward_cuda` vs `forward_native` | equal, 0 | equal, 0 | max abs 1.2e-07 |



**Latency**, 3 interleaved reps per arm, fresh server each, identical flags:

| | encoder-only p50 (`max_tokens=1`) | c=1 p50 | c=8 aggregate |
|---|---|---|---|
| on | **132.5 ms** | **131.8 ms** | 937.9 tok/s |
| off | 263.1 ms | 261.5 ms | 772.7 tok/s |

**1.99x**, with the per-rep ranges non-overlapping across all six reps, and +21% aggregate throughput at c=8. 

The win is, An isolated single-threaded CPU microbenchmark attributes the win: the processor's float work goes 160.3 ms -> 5.9 ms.

The added `tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_nemotron_parse.py` passes (2 passed).

Re-verified after making `input_norm` unconditional, same nightly, one H100: both flag arms produce identical output (`b37da04a78014080`, 5 greedy reps each), TTFT p50 226.8 -> 118.6 ms. With the feature off the unconditional call is bit-identical to the `pixel_values.to(dtype)` it replaces -- 0 differing elements of 10,223,616, in bf16, fp16 and fp32 -- so the default path is unchanged. Deleting `_resize_with_aspect_ratio` or `_pad_to_size` from the processor raises a `RuntimeError` naming `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`.

## Details

`_build_uint8_canvas` depends on three attributes of the checkpoint's remote-code image processor: `_resize_with_aspect_ratio`, `_pad_to_size` and `transform`. Two are private by convention and none is a stable API. If they change, the lookup raises and the error names `--no-mm-device-do-normalize`, so the failure is loud instead of a silent loss of the speedup. The cleaner fix lives in the checkpoint: `preprocess` should honour its own `do_rescale` / `do_normalize` kwargs, after which this override can be deleted entirely. I am happy to drop the override and gate the feature on that instead if reviewers prefer.

Reproducing the `b37da04a78014080` output on `NVIDIA-Nemotron-Parse-2.0` additionally requires the tied-`lm_head` fix (#60272, a re-land of #53020); without it that checkpoint's output head is randomly initialized and the server emits garbage while reporting healthy. That fix is independent of this change and was applied only for the validation runs above.

Not covered: CUDA only (`forward_xpu` / `forward_oot` are untouched and untested); one image per request, which is this model's `get_supported_mm_limits`.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Single-launch fused scoring+top-k kernel for sparse-indexer prefill, without materializing logits
author: LopezCastroRoberto
body: (this PR description was manually written by me) ## Summary * Adds one persistent CUDA kernel that scores every visible key of a sparse-indexer prefill chunk and selects each row's top-k keys (k = 512, 1024 or 2048) **without materializing the `[rows, keys]` logits matrix**. * One launch covers a prefill chunk of up to 16,384 query rows and up to 1M keys, including multi-request chunks. The dense path needs up to 127 call pairs (`fp8_mqa_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`) for the same chunk. * The output matches the dense path up to ties at the top-k boundary: the gated path ranks 24-bit score codes, and rows the gate cannot serve are rescanned exactly in fp32. ## Acknowledgements We'd like to acknowledge the authors of LiteTopK ([arXiv:2607.11976](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976), #48726), who were the first to fuse sparse-attention indexer scoring with top-k selection without materializing the full logits matrix, using classic sample-based threshold filtering. I open a separate PR because: * **Scope:** LiteTopK fuses only single-request chunks of exactly 8192/8128 rows with 192K–1M keys. Other chunks keep dense chunking, and even a fused chunk needs a separate seed-logits launch and about 2.6 GiB of workspace. Here every eligible chunk (≤ 16384 rows, ≤ 1M keys, multi-request) is one launch with no logits buffer and a 296 MiB workspace. * **Correctness:** on B300 (commit `c7184685`) I found an undersized shared-memory allocation (4100 memcheck errors), racecheck hazards in the candidate ring and the seed/radix-select kernels, and no recovery from candidate-buffer overflow (the mapping kernel traps). LiteTopK's selection is also approximate (99.998% recall); this PR matches dense up to boundary ties. * **Performance:** the only B300 serving data in #48726 shows TTFT within ~1% of stock at ~200K tokens. This PR measures 1.10× at 256K and 2.05× at 1.04M (different setups, so not like-for-like). However, most of this kernel is largely an adaptation of DeepSeek's code. This PR replaces the logits write-out with a sampled gate, candidate emission and in-kernel top-k selection. ## Motivation: what materializing the scores costs The dense prefill path writes the fp32 scores of every (query row, visible key) pair to HBM, then reads them back to select the top-k. One 16,384-row prefill chunk needs `16,384 × keys × 4 B` of logits: | Keys | Logits for one 16K-row chunk | Dense calls under the 512 MiB budget | Logits HBM traffic (write + read) | |---|---|---|---| | 16K | 1 GiB | 2 | 2 GiB | | 128K | 8 GiB | 16 | 16 GiB | | 512K | 32 GiB | 64 | 64 GiB | | 1M | 64 GiB | 127 | 128 GiB | This produces the following pattern: It gets worse with context, e.g. at ISL 512K: Two consequences: 1. **The logits budget trades KV-cache capacity against indexer speed.** During memory profiling, `sparse_attn_indexer` allocates a dummy `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB` buffer, so the logits budget is part of the peak memory the KV cache is sized from. On GLM-5.x with an FP8 KV cache, one token costs 47.7 KB per GPU (78 MLA layers × 576 B + 21 indexer layers × 132 B; MLA KV is replicated across TP ranks). Measured at startup (TP4, B300, `--max-model-len 1048576`): | Configuration | Available KV memory | KV cache tokens | |---|---|---| | Dense, 512 MiB budget (default) | 115.66 GiB | 2,603,456 | | Dense, 8 GiB budget | 109.23 GiB | 2,458,816 (−5.6%) | | Fused (this PR) | 115.37 GiB | 2,596,928 (−0.25%) | At the default budget the logits buffer fits under the profiling run's other peak allocations, so it costs no KV cache. The cost is speed: rows per dense call shrink as keys grow (2²⁷ / keys), so a 128K-token prefill in 16K-token steps needs 76 dense call pairs and a 1M-token prefill needs 4,217. With the fused path (top-2048), the first four steps, whose rows see fewer than 64K keys, stay dense (21 call pairs) and every later step is one fused call: 4 at 128K, 60 at 1M. Buying fewer dense calls means raising the budget, and that memory comes straight out of the KV cache: an 8 GiB budget (one dense call per 16K-row chunk at 128K keys) costs 144,640 tokens of KV cache. One dense call per chunk at 1M keys would need 64 GiB, more than the KV cache of the entire 1M-token sequence (46.6 GiB). The fused kernel serves long-context chunks in one call each with a fixed 296 MiB workspace. 2. **The logits round trip is pure overhead.** Only k of the `keys` scores per row are needed. The fused kernel writes only a gated candidate set, about 1K–4.5K candidates per row depending on k (median on the captures below) at 6 B each, i.e. about 0.1–0.45 GB per 16K-row chunk, against 16–128 GiB of logits traffic at 128K–1M keys. ## What this PR does **Kernel** (`csrc/fused_mqa_topk/`). One CTA per SM; each CTA claims 8-row blocks from a global counter (heaviest first) and keeps one continuous Q/KV/TMEM pipeline across blocks: * **Scoring:** the FP8 MQA-logits pipeline adapted from DeepGEMM (TMA loads, UMMA into TMEM, warp-specialized producers). Since relu(s) = (s + |s|) / 2, the weighted sum of the linear halves is a single query (the heads folded with their weights) times the key; it runs on the tensor core as extra UMMA rows, so the math warps only accumulate the |s| terms. * **Sampled gate:** a strided sample of the block's keys gives each row a threshold that keeps a few thousand candidates. The sample histogram is binned relative to each row's maximum over the first sample tile, so rows whose scores share a large common offset still get a tight gate. * **Candidate emission:** keys above the gate are buffered per warp and drained to a per-row candidate slab by two drain warps while the scan continues. * **Selection:** one warp per row selects the top-k from its candidates in shared memory (a sampled bracket, then histogram levels in registers), right after the block's scan, before its slot is reused. * **Exact rescan:** a row whose candidate count leaves `[k, 16384]`, a row with weights unsafe to scale, or a block whose candidates exceed the selection scratch is rescanned exactly in fp32 (the dense scoring pipeline with a streaming top-k merge), so the output never depends on the gate being right. ### Memory * Fused workspace: a pool of 2 eight-row slots per SM, fixed size, independent of rows, keys and context. It is 296 MiB on a 148-SM B300, allocated once per device during the profiling run, so it is accounted against the KV cache: −6,528 tokens (−0.25%) versus dense at the default budget (table above). * The profiling run still reserves the dense logits budget: chunks below the dispatch threshold take the dense path. ### Limitations of this PR -- TODOs Anything outside these bounds takes the existing dense path, unchanged. * **Hardware:** SM100 family only (i.e., B200/GB200, B300/GB300). * **Models:** 32 index heads × 128 dims (e.g., GLM-5.2/5.3, GLM-5.3 kpool, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), top-k 512/1024/2048, FP8 indexer cache. * Not supported yet: DeepSeek-V3.2 (64 index heads), MXFP4 indexer cache, and the DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level candidate selection layers (below). * **Parallelism:** TP, DP (with or without EP) and PCP (with or without DCP) are supported. DCP without PCP is not: each rank holds only a shard of the KV cache, so it keeps the dense path. GLM-5.3-Flash's kpool indexer does not support PCP + DCP itself. Only TP4 is validated end to end. * **Sizes:** up to 1M keys and 16,384 rows per call. The row cap is not a kernel-limitation: larger chunks are not validated end to end yet, so are excluded. Only chunks whose longest row sees ≥ 32K keys (≥ 64K for top-2048) use the kernel. **DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level candidate selection.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 8 indexer layers (`index_source_layer_ids` 2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36). Only layers 2, 8 and 14 use the kernel at this point, which is why its e2e gain is smaller than GLM-5.x (every GLM-5.x indexer layer uses the kernel). See figure below. * **Layer 20 (candidate source)** also writes, per row, the top 2,048 blocks of 8 keys ranked by their max score. The kernel would need a second output and a second selection over block maxima, which rank far deeper than its 512-key gate. * **Layers 24–36 (consumers)** mask their scores to those blocks before the top-512. The kernel would need the block list as an input. * **`indexer_sparse_logits`** (opt-in) already speeds up the consumers by scoring only the candidate blocks, but it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62011 addresses this. ## Performance **Kernel.** B300, real GLM-5.x indexer inputs captured from serving (MRCR 2- and 8-needle and random prompts, layers 0, 9 and 19), one 16,384-row prefill chunk, top-2048, median of `do_bench_cudagraph(rep=200)` over captures. Dense is chunked by the 512 MiB budget exactly as in vLLM and captured in one CUDA graph. | Keys | Captures | Dense (ms) | Fused (ms) | Speedup, median (range) | Fused exact top-k | Dense exact top-k | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 32K | 9 | 2.62 | 2.43 | 1.05× (1.00–1.21) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 64K | 9 | 6.12 | 4.71 | 1.29× (1.22–1.36) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 128K | 9 | 13.0 | 8.76 | 1.49× (1.41–1.53) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 256K | 9 | 27.8 | 16.9 | 1.63× (1.58–1.66) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 448K | 9 | 62.8 | 29.0 | 2.20× (2.11–2.22) | 9/9 | 0/9 | | 512K | 6 | 78.4 | 32.8 | 2.40× (2.34–2.42) | 6/6 | 0/6 | | 944K | 3 | 246 | 58.9 | 4.18× (4.13–4.21) | 3/3 | 0/3 | | 1M | 3 | 280 | 62.0 | 4.52× (4.38–4.55) | 3/3 | 0/3 | "Exact top-k": the selected keys' scores equal the fp32 top-k scores. The current dense path rounds its logits to bf16, so it is not exact at the boundary. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61149#issuecomment-6412098207 **End to end.** TP4, B300, FP8 KV cache, prefix caching off. Dense is the upstream base of this PR. Up to 32K every chunk stays dense (below the dispatch threshold of 64K visible keys). At 64K only the last chunk of each prompt reaches it. At 1.04M, TTFT drops by 711 s (55%). The two Flash models gain less in the same concurrency sweep, for different reasons: * **GLM-5.3-Flash: every indexer layer uses the kernel, but each one gains less.** All 45 layers compute the indexer and all take the kernel. Its kpool indexer scores pools of 4 tokens and selects 512 of them, so a 1M-token prompt is 256K keys at top-512 per layer. There the kernel is 1.7× faster than dense, against 4.4× at 1M keys. The kernel's advantage grows with keys, because dense needs more logits windows and each one re-reads every key. The kernel also only starts at 128K tokens (the 32K-key top-512 threshold). * **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: only some indexer layers use the kernel at this point (see detailed explanation above in Limitations/TODOs).** 8 of its 40 layers compute the indexer (the rest reuse one). Only layers 2, 8 and 14 take the kernel, at half-length keys (ratio-2 compressed, 512K keys for 1M tokens) and top-512. **Extending this kernel to other layers is a TODO for follow-up PRs**. * **GLM-5.2/5.3,** by comparison: 21 of 78 layers compute the indexer, all 21 take the kernel, at 1M keys and top-2048. ## Accuracy MRCR shows no accuracy difference: fused and dense agree within noise in every context range. Measured before the latest refactors, which keep the output exact up to ties (real-capture validation below). Context | Samples | Fused | Dense | Difference -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 0–8K | 103 | 0.394 | 0.335 | +0.059 (+0.9σ) 8K–16K | 98 | 0.220 | 0.148 | +0.072 (+1.5σ) 16K–32K | 101 | 0.416 | 0.380 | +0.036 (+0.5σ) 32K–64K | 98 | 0.495 | 0.484 | +0.011 (+0.2σ) 64K–128K | 99 | 0.789 | 0.713 | +0.076 (+1.4σ) 128K–256K | 101 | 0.768 | 0.791 | −0.022 (−0.5σ) 256K–512K | 100 | 0.724 | 0.779 | −0.054 (−1.1σ) 512K–1M | 97 | 0.683 | 0.683 | 0.000 All | 797 | 0.561 ± 0.016 | 0.539 ± 0.016 | +0.022 (+1.0σ)

title: [Perf][Gemma4][Multimodal] Fuse Gemma4Unified 2D posemb and batch image/video embedder
author: lucianommartins
body:
## Overview This pull request optimizes the vision and multimodal input processing pipeline of `Gemma4Unified` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`, used by `google/gemma-4-12B-it`) via two key performance and architectural enhancements: 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Factorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: Replaces the sequential, un-fused PyTorch loop over coordinate axes and position indices with a single clean, vectorized PyTorch implementation using contiguous 1D `F.embedding` lookups on `self.pos_embedding.view(-1, embed_dim)`, in-place `.add_` accumulation, and masked fill, cleanly preserving `positions_xy != -1` coordinate masking with 100% bit-exact numerical parity without requiring Triton or custom C++/CUDA kernels. 2. **Memory-Bounded Chunking & Cross-Request Image & Multi-Frame Video Batching**: Vectorizes `_process_image_input` (both 3D `torch.Tensor` and `list[torch.Tensor]`) and `_process_video_input` across all prompt requests and video frames into unified 2D batch GEMM projections (`self.patch_dense` and `self.embed_vision`), eliminating per-request and per-frame Python iteration overhead. Memory usage is safely bounded via `_vision_chunk` which dynamically mirrors `_encoder_chunk` logic and bounds peak memory per chunk based on available accelerator memory (short-circuiting memory queries when batch size <= 1, and guarded with `gpu_sync_allowed()`). Duplicate-work check: verified via GitHub PR search that no open pull request vectorizes the Gemma 4 Unified 2D position embedding or batches its multimodal vision embedder projections. ## Claims 1. **Component Vision & Video Embedder Speedup (`Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`, `google/gemma-4-12B-it`)**: - **Vectorized Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: **1.25x – 1.38x speedup** (`0.310 ms -> 0.248 ms` at 280 tokens; `0.325 ms -> 0.236 ms` at 2240 tokens) with **100.0% bit-exact parity**. - **Batched Image Input Processing (`_process_image_input`)**: - `1 image` (`280` patches): **1.23x speedup** (`1.413 ms -> 1.148 ms`, **100.0% bit-exact**). - `2 images` (`560` patches): **2.03x speedup** (`2.648 ms -> 1.306 ms`, `-1.34 ms`). - `4 images` (`1120` patches): **2.71x speedup** (`4.714 ms -> 1.743 ms`, `-2.97 ms`). - `8 images` (`2240` patches): **3.30x speedup** (`9.030 ms -> 2.737 ms`, `-6.29 ms`). - `16 images` (`4480` patches): **4.28x speedup** (`18.125 ms -> 4.234 ms`, `-13.89 ms`). - Variable-length image batches (`list[torch.Tensor]`): up to **4.46x speedup** (`9.572 ms -> 2.147 ms` at 8 images). - **Batched Video Input Processing (`_process_video_input`)**: - `1 video (4 frames)`: **3.92x speedup** (`5.100 ms -> 1.302 ms`, `-3.80 ms`). - `1 video (8 frames)`: **5.47x speedup** (`9.600 ms -> 1.754 ms`, `-7.85 ms`). - `2 videos (16 frames)`: **6.32x speedup** (`18.215 ms -> 2.883 ms`, `-15.33 ms`). - `4 videos (32 frames)`: **6.82x speedup** (`37.385 ms -> 5.480 ms`, `-31.91 ms`). - `8 videos (64 frames, Suite 1)`: **6.94x speedup** (`73.23 ms -> 10.56 ms`, `-62.67 ms`). 2. **Realistic End-to-End Serving Impact (Amdahl's Law on Encoder-Free `Gemma4Unified`)**: - Because `Gemma4Unified` (`google/gemma-4-12B-it`) is an **encoder-free** architecture (its vision module is only 2 linear projections + 3 norms + 2D pos lookup, with no ViT tower), GPU vision embedding takes `1.22–35.79 ms` for `1–32` images vs `70–1030 ms` for CPU PIL image preprocessing + the 40-layer 12B language model inside `llm.generate()`. - Benchmarked on the V1 engine with `enforce_eager=False` (`torch.compile` + CUDA Graphs enabled), the deterministic GPU vision embedder savings (`-0.11 ms` at 1 image up to `-13.55 ms` at 16 images and `-62.67 ms` at 64 video frames) translates to a **1.01x – 1.04x end-to-end `llm.generate()` speedup** (`72.69 -> 70.43 ms` prefill at `bs=1`, `408.97 -> 393.92 ms` prefill at `bs=8`, `1076.41 -> 1031.63 ms` E2E at `bs=8`) with **100.0% greedy token parity**. 3. **Strict Architectural Isolation**: - All changes are strictly isolated to `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py` (`Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`, used exclusively by `google/gemma-4-12B-it`). Tower-based Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) use `gemma4_mm.py` and are 100% untouched. 4. **Lossless Numerical & Bit-Level Parity**: - **100.0% Bit-Exact** on factorized 2D position embeddings (`bit_exact_pct = 100.0%`, `within_1ulp_pct = 100.0%`, `max_abs_diff = 0.0`, `cosine_sim = 1.00000`). - Bit-exact on small image batches, and `>= 0.99999` cosine similarity across large multi-image and multi-frame video batches (standard BF16 GEMM batching associativity). ## Validation ### 1. Unit Tests & Linters All linters and unit tests pass cleanly with 0 errors: ```bash # Unit test suite pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: 20 passed, 19 skipped # Ruff linter ruff check vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: All checks passed! # Ruff formatter ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_gemma4_unified.py # Output: 2 files already formatted # Standalone microbenchmark verification python performance-speedup/pr_benchmarks/bench_pr4_unified_vision.py --mode standalone # Output: All 16 benchmark cases executed successfully with 0 parity errors ``` ### 2. Because `Gemma4Unified` is encoder-free (no ViT tower), we list both the total `llm.generate()` latency (which includes CPU PIL image preprocessing + the 40-layer 12B LLM) and the deterministic GPU savings from `_process_image_input` (Suite 1) for the corresponding total image count (`Batch Size * Num Images`).* | Model | Case | Batch Size | Imgs/Req (Total Imgs) | Max Tokens | Base E2E (ms) | Feat E2E (ms) | Isolated Vision Embedder Δ (ms) | E2E Speedup | Token Match | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs1 | 1 | 1 (1) | 1 | 72.69 | 70.43 | -0.11 ms (1.22 -> 1.11) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs2 | 2 | 1 (2) | 1 | 122.67 | 118.89 | -1.02 ms (2.27 -> 1.25) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs4 | 4 | 1 (4) | 1 | 216.97 | 210.18 | -2.91 ms (4.44 -> 1.53) | **1.03x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_1img_bs8 | 8 | 1 (8) | 1 | 408.97 | 393.92 | -6.34 ms (8.72 -> 2.38) | **1.04x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs1 | 1 | 4 (4) | 1 | 233.87 | 228.26 | -2.96 ms (4.45 -> 1.49) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs2 | 2 | 4 (8) | 1 | 440.64 | 434.88 | -6.59 ms (8.83 -> 2.24) | **1.01x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_prefill_4img_bs4 | 4 | 4 (16) | 1 | 859.29 | 838.22 | -13.87 ms (17.70 -> 3.83) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs1 | 1 | 2 (2) | 16 | 387.77 | 382.00 | -1.02 ms (2.27 -> 1.25) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs2 | 2 | 2 (4) | 16 | 475.80 | 468.50 | -2.91 ms (4.44 -> 1.53) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs4 | 4 | 2 (8) | 16 | 675.28 | 660.30 | -6.34 ms (8.72 -> 2.38) | **1.02x** | 100.0% | | gemma-4-12B-it | mm_serving_e2e_bs8 | 8 | 2 (16) | 16 | 1076.41 | 1031.63 | -13.55 ms (17.59 -> 4.04) | **1.04x** | 100.0% | ## Technical Details ### Root Cause Analysis In `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_unified.py`): 1. **Un-vectorized 2D Position Embedding Kernel**: `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb` previously computed factorized 2D sinusoidal position embeddings using separate PyTorch operations: slicing coordinate channels, executing multiple 3D tensor indexing lookups (`self.pos_embedding[clamped_pos[..., 0], 0, :]`), masking invalid patch positions where `positions_xy != -1`, and concatenating/normalizing. On modern GPUs, dispatching multiple small kernels over 280-2240 visual tokens caused excessive kernel launch latency (~0.31 ms), bounding vision preprocessing throughput. 2. **Sequential Un-batched Multimodal Inputs**: In `_process_image_input`, when multiple images were passed (either as a 3D tensor or a list of tensors across requests in continuous batching), each image was processed individually through `self.vision_embedder` and `self.embed_vision` via an inline `for pv, pp in zip(pixel_values, pixel_position_ids)` loop. Similarly, `_process_video_input` iterated over each video and each frame sequentially in Python. For an 8-frame video, this dispatched 8 independent vision embedder projections and 8 `ColumnParallelLinear` multimodal projections, incurring significant CPU launch overhead and leaving GPU SMs underutilized. ### Implementation Details 1. **Vectorized PyTorch 2D Position Embedding (`_factorized_posemb`)**: - Replaces multi-step 3D tensor slicing with a single contiguous 1D embedding lookup using `F.embedding`. - Flattens `self.pos_embedding` from `[max_size, 2, embed_dim]` to `[max_size * 2, embed_dim]` via `.view(-1, embed_dim)`. - Computes flat indices `x_flat = pos_x * 2` and `y_flat = pos_y * 2 + 1`, clamping `-1` padding values before lookup. - Computes `out = F.embedding(x_flat, flat_weights)` and performs an in-place accumulation `out.add_(F.embedding(y_flat, flat_weights))`. - Applies `.masked_fill_(~valid_mask.unsqueeze(-1), 0.0)` in-place where `positions_xy == -1`, producing exact zero padding and preserving 100% bit-exact parity without Triton or custom kernel dependencies. 2. **Memory-Bounded Dynamic Chunking (`_vision_chunk` and `_embed_vision_patches`)**: - Mirrors the proven `_encoder_chunk` mechanism to dynamically split large image/video batches based on available accelerator memory budget, avoiding OOMs on large multimodal prompts. - Short-circuits when `total_items <= 1` (a single image or video), directly passing inputs through without executing the `torch.accelerator.get_memory_info()` syscall. - Wraps accelerator memory queries with `with gpu_sync_allowed():` context guards to respect vLLM async execution and CUDA graph capture invariants. 3. **Unified Batched Multimodal Projections**: - `_process_image_input`: - When receiving a 3D `torch.Tensor` of shape `[N, S, D]` (batched images), it passes the tensor directly through `self._embed_vision_patches` in one pass, flattens all patches across images to `[N * S, D_in]`, executes a single batched GEMM projection through `self.embed_vision`, and unbinds into per-image feature chunks. - When receiving a `list[torch.Tensor]` of variable-length images, it flattens each image's patch tokens, tracks slice lengths, concatenates into a unified 2D batch `[total_patches, D]`, runs a single `self.embed_vision` projection, and splits back into per-image tensors using `torch.split`. - `_process_video_input`: - Embeds all frames of all videos in a single unified tensor pass through `self._embed_vision_patches` and `self.embed_vision`, splitting features by `video_frame_counts`. ### Tradeoffs & Encapsulation - **Zero Non-Gemma Regressions**: All modifications are strictly encapsulated within `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. Standard Gemma 4 models (`E2B`, `E4B`, `26B-A4B`, `31B`) and text-only generation paths are completely untouched. - **Pure PyTorch Simplicity & Portability**: Completely eliminates the need for Triton or hardware-specific kernels, ensuring immediate zero-overhead support across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD ROCm, TPUs, and CPUs. - **Bit-Exact Numerical Fidelity**: Position embedding outputs are 100.0% bit-exact to PyTorch reference implementations. Full image and video embeddings retain 100.0% bit-exact parity at low batch sizes and > 0.99999 cosine similarity across large batches. ### Model & Workload Applicability Matrix | Model / Workload | Direct / Transitive / N/A | Supported Architecture | Technical Justification | | :--- | :---: | :--- | :--- | | `google/gemma-4-12B-it` | Direct Optimization | Gemma4Unified (Encoder-free Vision) | Uses `Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder` and `Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration`. | | `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 MoE (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `google/gemma-4-31B-it` | Zero-Regression Guard | Gemma4 Dense (SigLIP Vision Tower) | Uses standard SigLIP tower; bypasses Gemma4Unified embedder. Verified 100% token match. | | `DiffusionGemma` | N/A | Diffusion Transformer (DiT) | Diffusion model architecture; does not use Gemma4Unified vision embedder. | ## Reproducibility & Benchmark Scripts
Microbenchmark Reproduction Script (bench_pr4_unified_vision.py) ```python # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 """Benchmark PR4: Unified Vision Embedder Vectorization and Batching. Compares `main` (0838cd6593) vs `lucianommartins/gemma4-pr4-unified-vision`. Supports branch comparison, worker mode, standalone benchmark, and file comparison. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import os import sys from pathlib import Path from types import SimpleNamespace from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union import torch import torch.nn as nn sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent)) from common_harness import compute_parity_metrics, measure_cuda_latency, run_branch_comparison CASES = [ ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=280)", "posemb", 280), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=560)", "posemb", 560), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=1120)", "posemb", 1120), ("Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder._factorized_posemb (tokens=2240)", "posemb", 2240), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (1 images, 280 patches)", "image", 1), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (2 images, 280 patches)", "image", 2), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (4 images, 280 patches)", "image", 4), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (8 images, 280 patches)", "image", 8), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (16 images, 280 patches)", "image", 16), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 2 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 2), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 4 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 4), ("Gemma4Unified._process_image_input (varlen 8 images, 140..280 patches)", "image_varlen", 8), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (1 videos, 4 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (1, 4)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (1 videos, 8 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (1, 8)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (2 videos, 16 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (2, 16)), ("Gemma4Unified._process_video_input (4 videos, 32 frames, 280 patches)", "video", (4, 32)), ] _VLLM_CTX = None def init_dist(): global _VLLM_CTX import tempfile from vllm.config.vllm import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config from vllm.distributed import init_distributed_environment, initialize_model_parallel if _VLLM_CTX is None: _VLLM_CTX = set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()) _VLLM_CTX.__enter__() if not torch.distributed.is_initialized(): fd, temp_file = tempfile.mkstemp() os.close(fd) init_distributed_environment( world_size=1, rank=0, distributed_init_method=f"file://{temp_file}", local_rank=0, backend="nccl", ) initialize_model_parallel(1, 1) def setup_embedder_and_model(): init_dist() from vllm.model_executor.models.gemma4_mm import Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder from vllm.model_executor.models.gemma4_unified import ( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder, ) device = torch.device("cuda:0") dtype = torch.bfloat16 # Real dimensions from google/gemma-4-12B-it Unified vision config model_patch_size = 48 patch_dim = model_patch_size * model_patch_size * 3 # 6912 mm_embed_dim = 3840 mm_posemb_size = 1120 v_config = SimpleNamespace( model_patch_size=model_patch_size, mm_embed_dim=mm_embed_dim, mm_posemb_size=mm_posemb_size, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, ) multimodal_config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_size=mm_embed_dim, output_proj_dims=mm_embed_dim, rms_norm_eps=1e-6, ) text_config = SimpleNamespace( hidden_size=mm_embed_dim, ) torch.manual_seed(42) torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(42) embedder = Gemma4UnifiedVisionEmbedder(v_config).to(device=device, dtype=dtype) for p in embedder.parameters(): p.data.normal_(0.0, 0.02) embedder.patch_ln1.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.patch_ln1.bias.data.zero_() embedder.patch_ln2.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.patch_ln2.bias.data.zero_() embedder.pos_norm.weight.data.fill_(1.0) embedder.pos_norm.bias.data.zero_() embed_vision = Gemma4MultimodalEmbedder(multimodal_config, text_config).to(device=device, dtype=dtype) for p in embed_vision.parameters(): p.data.normal_(0.0, 0.02) class UnifiedRunner(nn.Module): def __init__(self, ve, ev): super().__init__() self.vision_embedder = ve self.embed_vision = ev if hasattr(Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, "_vision_chunk"): _vision_chunk = staticmethod( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._vision_chunk ) if hasattr(Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration, "_embed_vision_patches"): _embed_vision_patches = ( Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._embed_vision_patches ) _process_image_input = Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._process_image_input _process_video_input = Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration._process_video_input model = UnifiedRunner(embedder, embed_vision) return embedder, model, patch_dim, mm_posemb_size def run_worker(out_path: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]: device = torch.device("cuda:0") dtype = torch.bfloat16 embedder, model, patch_dim, max_posemb_size = setup_embedder_and_model() results = {} for name, kind, param in CASES: print(f" Executing case: {name}") torch.manual_seed(42) torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(42) if kind == "posemb": num_tokens = param xy = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (num_tokens, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) # Inject ~10% padded -1 positions to verify bit-exactness on padded tokens pad_mask = torch.rand(num_tokens, device=device) < 0.10 xy[pad_mask] = -1 def run_fn(): return embedder._factorized_posemb(xy) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=10, reps=50) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "image": num_images = param num_patches = 280 pv_img = torch.randn(num_images, num_patches, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp_img = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (num_images, num_patches, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) # Add ~10% padded patches pad_mask = torch.rand(num_images, num_patches, device=device) < 0.10 pp_img[pad_mask] = -1 image_input = {"pixel_values": pv_img, "pixel_position_ids": pp_img} def run_fn(): res = model._process_image_input(image_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "image_varlen": num_images = param # Generate variable length list of images with 140..280 patches pv_list = [] pp_list = [] for i in range(num_images): p_count = 140 + (i % 2) * 140 # 140 or 280 pv = torch.randn(p_count, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (p_count, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) pad_mask = torch.rand(p_count, device=device) < 0.10 pp[pad_mask] = -1 pv_list.append(pv) pp_list.append(pp) image_input = {"pixel_values": pv_list, "pixel_position_ids": pp_list} def run_fn(): res = model._process_image_input(image_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } elif kind == "video": num_videos, total_frames = param num_patches = 280 pv_vid = torch.randn(total_frames, num_patches, patch_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype) pp_vid = torch.randint(0, max_posemb_size, (total_frames, num_patches, 2), device=device, dtype=torch.long) pad_mask = torch.rand(total_frames, num_patches, device=device) < 0.10 pp_vid[pad_mask] = -1 frames_per_vid = total_frames // num_videos frame_counts = [frames_per_vid] * num_videos # adjust if remainder frame_counts[-1] += total_frames - sum(frame_counts) video_input = { "pixel_values_videos": pv_vid, "pixel_position_ids_videos": pp_vid, "video_frame_counts": frame_counts, } def run_fn(): res = model._process_video_input(video_input) return torch.cat(res, dim=0) latency_ms = measure_cuda_latency(run_fn, warmup=5, reps=25) out_tensor = run_fn() results[name] = { "latency_ms": latency_ms, "tensor": out_tensor.detach().clone().cpu(), } if out_path: torch.save(results, out_path) print(f"Worker finished. Saved to {out_path}") return results def print_comparison_table(data_base: Dict[str, Any], data_feat: Dict[str, Any]): header = ( f"| Case | Base (ms) | Feat (ms) | Speedup | Gain (%) | " f"Bit-Exact (%) | Within 1-ULP (%) | Max Diff | Cos Sim | Extra |" ) separator = "| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |" print(header) print(separator) for case, cb in data_base.items(): if case not in data_feat: continue cf = data_feat[case] base_ms = cb["latency_ms"] feat_ms = cf["latency_ms"] speedup = base_ms / max(feat_ms, 1e-6) pct_gain = (speedup - 1.0) * 100.0 tb = cb.get("tensor") tf = cf.get("tensor") if tb is not None and tf is not None: parity = compute_parity_metrics(tb, tf) else: parity = {"bit_exact_pct": 100.0, "within_1ulp_pct": 100.0, "max_abs_diff": 0.0, "cosine_sim": 1.0} extra_b = cb.get("extra", "") extra_f = cf.get("extra", "") extra_str = f"{extra_b} -> {extra_f}" if (extra_b or extra_f) else "" diff_str = f"{parity['max_abs_diff']:.2e}" if parity['max_abs_diff'] > 0 else "0.0" print( f"| {case} | {base_ms:.3f} | {feat_ms:.3f} | {speedup:.2f}x | " f"{pct_gain:+.1f}% | {parity['bit_exact_pct']:.1f}% | " f"{parity['within_1ulp_pct']:.1f}% | {diff_str} | " f"{parity['cosine_sim']:.5f} | {extra_str} |" ) def run_standalone(save_path: Optional[str] = None): print("Running PR4 benchmark in standalone mode on active branch...") results = run_worker(out_path=save_path) print("\n| Test Case | Latency (ms) |") print("| :--- | :---: |") for name, r in res

title: [ROCm][RDNA][Perf] W4A16: packed fp16 prefill dequant and tiles for gfx1151
author: stoivonen-amd
body:
## Overview

Speeds up fp16 prefill in `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` on gfx1151 (Strix Halo). The Triton prefill GEMM dequantizes two 4-bit weights per instruction, and gets tiles tuned for that dequant. Supersedes draft #55711.

## Claims

- fp16 prefill latency on gfx1151: 5–18% faster on Qwen3-4B (symmetric) at every prompt length from 64 to 2048 tokens, and 17–19% faster on Qwen3-8B (asymmetric) from 512 tokens, unchanged below.
- No change for bf16, or on any GPU other than gfx1151.
- No accuracy change: the dequant arithmetic is exact, and kernel output is bit-identical to main in all 1248 configs swept.

## Validation

All measurements: gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2, Triton 3.8.0. main is c83935b300. Benchmarks ran on 23a1a2b640, which differs from this PR's head only in comments and in where `packed_dequant` is decided (same result for every dtype, zero-point and M). GSM8K and tests ran on the head.

**End-to-end prefill latency**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size 1 --output-len 1 --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 30 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0`. One process per run, main and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is main → this PR, median over reps in ms, with the delta; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B, fp16, sym | Qwen3-8B, fp16, asym | Qwen3-8B, bf16, asym (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 34.9 → 33.0 (−5.4%) | 71.1 → 71.6 (+0.7% ~) | 74.1 → 74.2 (+0.2% ~) |
| 128 | 51.5 → 46.7 (−9.4%) | 92.2 → 92.5 (+0.3% ~) | 96.3 → 96.2 (−0.2% ~) |
| 192 | 76.5 → 72.6 (−5.1%) | 140.9 → 140.3 (−0.4% ~) | 147.9 → 148.0 (+0.0% ~) |
| 256 | 91.1 → 76.5 (−16.0%) | 165.0 → 163.1 (−1.1%) | 174.8 → 172.8 (−1.1% ~) |
| 512 | 175.7 → 144.3 (−17.9%) | 325.7 → 264.5 (−18.8%) | 340.6 → 342.1 (+0.4% ~) |
| 2048 | 782.7 → 673.5 (−14.0%) | 1346.3 → 1118.8 (−16.9%) | 1366.0 → 1364.8 (−0.1% ~) |

**Large batches**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size {128,256} --output-len {1,128} --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --seed 0`. One process per run, main (11a8d571d2, this PR's parent) and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is the change in end-to-end latency from main, median over reps; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| batch | prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 1 | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 128 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 1 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 128 | −47.8% | −26.3% | −51.8% | −28.6% |

Qwen3-8B bf16 (control, prompt 512): batch 128 +2.9% ~ at output 1 and −0.1% ~ at output 128; batch 256 −0.5% ~ and +0.4% ~.

Models are `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` and `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16`.

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, 5-shot, 500 questions, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against a server started with `--dtype float16 --max-model-len 4096`. Differences are ±1 question.

| model | dtype | quant | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | asym | 0.884 | 0.882 |
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | sym | 0.848 | 0.850 |

**Tests**: 135 passed on gfx1151. CI has no gfx11 runners: the AMD kernel quantization shards run on MI300/MI355, where these tests skip.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py
```

<details>
<summary>Kernel sweep</summary>

Calls `_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply_impl` directly with the main and PR copies of `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`, timed with `triton.testing.do_bench` and a cache flush between reps, as in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`. Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B qkv/o/gate_up/down shapes, group size 32/64/128, M 6–2048, 1248 configs, 3 reps with rotating order. Geomean kernel time vs main; lower is better.

| dtype | quant | M | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 | sym | ≤ 128 | 0.972 | 0.979 |
| fp16 | sym | 129–256 | 0.845 | 0.968 |
| fp16 | sym | > 256 | 0.762 | 0.787 |
| fp16 | asym | ≤ 128 | 0.999 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | 129–256 | 0.996 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | > 256 | 0.766 | 0.795 |
| bf16 | sym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 0.999–1.000 |
| bf16 | asym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 1.000 |

Output bit-identical to main: 1248 of 1248 configs.

Geomeans hide some per-shape losses for symmetric fp16: 46 of its 312 configs are more than 2% slower than main (195 are more than 2% faster). The worst is Qwen3-1.7B `down_proj` (K = 6144, N = 2048) at M = 129–192, 13–22% slower. Every loss was already present in #55711.

</details>

## Details

**Packed dequant.** For a 4-bit value `n`, the bits `0x6400 | n` read as fp16 are exactly `1024 + n`. One `v_and_or_b32` (`(x & 0x000F000F) | 0x64006400`) does this for two values at once, instead of the `v_and_b16` + `v_or_b16` per value that Triton emits. The ExLlama shuffle layout already puts paired values 16 bits apart, so no extra shuffling is needed. The kernel subtracts `1024 + zp` instead of `zp`, which is exact because fp16 represents every integer below 2048.

**When it is used.** Only fp16 on gfx1151, the only GPU it was measured on, decided on the host and passed to the kernel as the `PACKED_DEQUANT` constexpr. Asymmetric layers use it only above M = 256: the extra zero-point load made it 1.2–2.4x slower per GEMM below that.

**Tiles.** The packed fp16 path and the scalar bf16 path want different tiles, most visibly `BLOCK_N` 256 vs 64 at deep M. `_select_skinny_gfx1151_config` picks new tiles and `num_stages=1` for fp16 above M = 128 (M = 256 for asymmetric). Everything else keeps the existing ladder and overrides unchanged. `num_stages=1` stays off bf16, where it cost 15.8% end-to-end on an asymmetric model.

**Numerics.** The dequant result is unchanged. The new tiles change `BLOCK_K`, and with it the fp32 accumulation order, so fp16 output is not guaranteed bit-identical. In the kernel sweep it was bit-identical in all 1248 configs.

**Not duplicating.** #57199 changes the HIP decode kernel, not the Triton prefill path. #52637 changes symmetric weight loading in `process_weights_after_loading`. #60710 adds an opt-in (default off) dense weight cache that skips the int4 dequant at M ≥ 256; it edits the same file but leaves the Triton dequant and tile selection alone. No other open PR touches the prefill dequant or the gfx1151 tile selection.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] MSA prefill attends with the E4M3 query; bump fmha_sm100 to 968061a
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview With CUTLASS MSA sparse decode on (an NVFP4 KV cache, or an FP8 E4M3 cache with the `CUTLASS_MSA` decode backend), the fused QK-norm/RoPE/insert kernel writes MiniMax-M3's query only in E4M3. `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl` then dequantized it back into the BF16 query buffer before every prefill. Both `fmha_sm100` prefill kernels take an E4M3 query natively, so prefill now passes it through as is. The PR also bumps `fmha_sm100` (vllm-project/MSA) from `be4a52a` to `968061a`. The new pin includes MSA's Blackwell prefill port, which now serves an E4M3 query over vLLM's packed K|V pages (vllm-project/MSA#32). ## Claims - MSA prefill attention is **26–37% faster with an FP8 KV cache** and **8–13% faster with an NVFP4 KV cache** than on main (per layer on GB300; table below). - Prefill no longer makes a BF16 copy of the query. Only the Triton decode fallback still reads the dequantized query. - BF16 caches and the default Triton decode backend for FP8 caches still pass a BF16 query, so their path is unchanged. ## Validation **Tests:** on GB300 (SM103, CUDA 13.4, `fmha_sm100` built from the new pin), `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py tests/kernels/test_minimax_m3_sparse_attn_fp8_scale.py tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py` gives **240 passed, 45 skipped**. All skips are ROCm-only tests. The MSA test file runs in CI on B200. - New `test_msa_prefill_reads_query_fp8_over_fp8_cache[tp1|tp4]` covers FP8-cache prefill, including chunks over cached context, with CUTLASS decode on. It checks that `sparse_atten_func` receives the E4M3 query and that the output matches Triton on the dequantized query. - `test_msa_prefill_nvfp4_matches_triton_on_dequantized_cache` now checks that `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` receives the E4M3 query. Its reference is now the cache as an E4M3-query kernel reads it (see Details). - Both prefill tests require all but 1e-4 of the elements within atol/rtol 0.05 and bound the rest at 0.25. The E4M3 probabilities are rounded per split, and splits follow the SM count, so a rare element lands just past 0.05: 1 of 4.1M on B200 CI. On GB300 over 16 seeds the worst case is 2.4e-7 of the elements and 0.07 max abs error. - On the old code, all four prefill cases fail with `[torch.bfloat16] == [torch.float8_e4m3fn]`. **Performance:** `MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl.forward` on prefill-only batches (`build_k2q_csr` + attention + combine, plus the dequant where the query is BF16). GB300, one request, top-k 16, page 128. Each value is the median of 3×50 iterations after warmup; spread ≤1%, except ±5% on the first FP8 row of the main run. | KV cache | Q heads / KV heads | Query tokens @ cached context | main (MSA `be4a52a`, BF16 q) | pin bump only (BF16 q) | this PR (E4M3 q) | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | FP8 | 16 / 1 (TP4) | 8k @ 0 | 411 µs | 368 µs | 303 µs (-26%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 462 µs | 439 µs | 314 µs (-32%) | | FP8 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 801 µs | 754 µs | 530 µs (-34%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 (TP1) | 8k @ 0 | 1423 µs | 1320 µs | 891 µs (-37%) | | FP8 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1498 µs | 1423 µs | 985 µs (-34%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 0 | 379 µs | 375 µs | 342 µs (-10%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 8k @ 32k | 457 µs | 458 µs | 420 µs (-8%) | | NVFP4 | 16 / 1 | 16k @ 112k | 798 µs | 795 µs | 695 µs (-13%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 0 | 1411 µs | 1395 µs | 1255 µs (-11%) | | NVFP4 | 64 / 4 | 8k @ 32k | 1491 µs | 1491 µs | 1317 µs (-12%) | Percentages are relative to main. With the new pin, a BF16 query over the FP8 cache also reaches the Blackwell port, but with BF16 MMAs. The E4M3 query gives the bulk of the FP8 gain at either pin: on main's pin alone it is 13–24% (411 → 356, 462 → 367, 801 → 623, 1423 → 1083, 1498 → 1162 µs).
Benchmark script (run from the repo root with PYTHONPATH=.) ```python """Per-layer MSA prefill attention (impl.forward) with an E4M3 query.""" import math from types import SimpleNamespace import torch import tests.kernels.attention.test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode as t from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.sparse_attention import ( MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata, MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata) BLK, TOPK = 128, 16 def case(q_len, seq_len, hkv, g): pos = torch.arange(seq_len - q_len, seq_len, device="cuda") visible = pos // BLK + 1 vmax = int(visible.max()) r = torch.rand(q_len, hkv, vmax, device="cuda", generator=g) ar = torch.arange(vmax, device="cuda") r = torch.where(ar < visible[:, None, None] - 1, r, -1.0) r = torch.where(ar == visible[:, None, None] - 1, 2.0, r) k = min(TOPK, vmax) val, idx = r.topk(k, dim=-1) topk = torch.where(val >= 0, idx, -1).int() if k < TOPK: topk = torch.cat([topk, topk.new_full((q_len, hkv, TOPK - k), -1)], -1) pages = math.ceil(seq_len / BLK) block_table = torch.randperm(pages, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")[None] seq = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_q = torch.tensor([0, q_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") cu_k = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") p = MiniMaxM3SparsePrefillMetadata( cu_seqlens_q=cu_q, cu_seqlens_k=cu_k, seq_lens=seq, context_lens=seq - q_len, block_table=block_table, max_query_len=q_len, max_seq_len=seq_len, total_kv_blocks=pages) md = MiniMaxM3SparseMetadata( seq_lens=seq, max_seq_len=seq_len, slot_mapping=torch.empty(q_len, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"), num_actual_tokens=q_len, num_decodes=0, num_decode_tokens=0, num_prefills=1, num_prefill_tokens=q_len, prefill=p) return md, topk, pages def bench(fn, iters=50): for _ in range(10): fn() torch.cuda.synchronize() s, e = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) s.record() for _ in range(iters): fn() e.record() torch.cuda.synchronize() return s.elapsed_time(e) / iters * 1e3 g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0) for kv_dtype in ("fp8", "nvfp4"): for hq, hkv, q_len, ctx in ((16, 1, 8192, 0), (16, 1, 8192, 32768), (16, 1, 16384, 114688), (64, 4, 8192, 0), (64, 4, 8192, 32768)): md, topk, pages = case(q_len, ctx + q_len, hkv, g) k_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") v_scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") if kv_dtype == "nvfp4": kv_cache, _ = t._make_nvfp4_kv_cache(pages, hkv, "nvfp4", k_scale, v_scale) else: kv_cache = (torch.randn(pages, hkv, BLK, 256, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) layer = SimpleNamespace(layer_name="l", topk_indices_buffer=topk, _q_scale_float=0.5, _k_scale=k_scale, _v_scale=v_scale) qf = torch.randn(q_len, hq * 128, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) query = torch.empty(q_len, hq * 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") out = torch.empty_like(query) impl = t.MiniMaxM3SparseMSAImpl( num_heads=hq, head_size=128, scale=t.SM_SCALE, num_kv_heads=hkv, kv_cache_dtype=kv_dtype, topk_blocks=TOPK, sparse_block_size=BLK, msa_decode_backend="cutlass") assert impl.use_cutlass_decode with override_forward_context(ForwardContext(no_compile_layers={}, attn_metadata={"l": md}, slot_mapping={})): bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf), iters=200) ts = [bench(lambda: impl.forward(layer, query, kv_cache, out, query_fp8=qf)) for _ in range(3)] print(f"{kv_dtype} H{hq}/{hkv} q{q_len} ctx{ctx}: " + " ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in ts) + " us") ```
**No end-to-end accuracy eval or serving benchmark** is included; validation is the kernel-level numerics and per-layer timings above. ## Details **Kernel capability (MSA `968061a`; same at `be4a52a` except the Blackwell port):** - `sparse_atten_func` accepts an FP8 E4M3 query over FP8 E4M3 K/V and runs FP8 QK/PV MMAs, on the Blackwell port when eligible. The BF16-Q × FP8-K/V mode stages K/V up to BF16 instead. - `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` accepts a BF16 or E4M3 query. With E4M3 it dequantizes each NVFP4 `code × block_scale` to E4M3 instead of BF16, and applies the K global scale to the scores and the V global scale in the combine. **Scales:** `q_scale` folds into `softmax_scale`. The FP8 cache is written with unit scales and the NVFP4 global scales are passed as before, so K/V scale handling is unchanged. **Numerics:** the E4M3-query kernels round the softmax probabilities to E4M3. The NVFP4 kernel also rounds K/V to E4M3. On the NVFP4 test (TP1): - Against the E4M3-staged cache: max abs error 0.06, and 0 of 4.1M elements outside atol/rtol 0.05. - Against the exact BF16 dequantization: max 0.14, with 122 of 4.1M elements outside that tolerance. This is why the test's reference changed. On the FP8 test the max abs error is ≈0.03. **Limitations:** validated on SM103. SM100 is covered by the CI kernel job. The E4M3-query NVFP4 kernel is untested on SM107 here. **MSA pin bump (`be4a52a` → `968061a`):** - The functions vLLM calls keep their signatures: `fmha_sm100`, `fmha_sm100_plan`, `_fmha_sm100(_plan)`, `sparse_topk_select`, `sparse_atten_func`, `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func` and `nvfp4_head_slot_views`. - vLLM's decode plans still pin `decode_backend="kv_mode3"`. The new `prefill_backend` plan option only routes sparse-prefill plans built through `fmha_sm100_plan`, which vLLM does not use. - The cmake install list adds the files the package now imports: `_jit_cache.py`, `msa_warmup.py`, `q8kv4_prefill_adapter.py` and `prefill_q8kv4/`. **Duplicate check:** no open PR touches the MSA prefill query or `fmha_sm100.cmake`. Open MiniMax-M3 MSA PRs (#55838, #56932, #59979) change decode or indexer metadata only. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement, test and benchmark this change. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Spec Decode] Skip metadata build for dflash/dspark when all model backends support it
author: TheEpicDolphin
body: # Context Continuing the effort from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58463 to remove unnecessary attention metadata rebuilds before FULL cudagraph replays for draft model-based speculators. I found an opportunity to use the same `supports_draft_decode_metadata_update` flag to gate updating the metadata within the captured decode step for DFlash/DSpark, reducing GPU kernel launch overhead. # This PR Adds support for skipping the full attention metadata rebuild before replaying the uniform decode cudagraph. Previously, only the `TargetDependentARSpeculator` was leveraging the `update_draft_decode_metadata` operations for its attention backends to update the attention metadata in a cudagraph-safe way. In this PR, I move that logic for deciding draft model eligibility (`supports_update_decode_metadata`) for this optimization to the base class `DraftModelSpeculator`, and then i have both `TargetDependentARSpeculator` and `DFlashSpeculator` check this eligibility. If True, capture the `_update_draft_decode_metadata` op in the graph before the draft model forward. Otherwise, rebuild the attention metadata eagerly via `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` before replaying the graph. This optimization has been enabled for DeepSeek V4.1 + DSpark, as verified below. ## Profile Captured while serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on 4xGB200: **Before** **After** ## Benchmarks / Evals **Setup (both subsections).** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark with `num_speculative_tokens=5`, 4x GB200 (TP4), `--max-model-len 102400 --max-num-seqs 128 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'`, adaptive verification off, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. Speed-Bench is 2K/2K (`throughput_16k`, `low_entropy`), with prompts scaled 8x concurrency (min 16), seed 0, and a fresh server per arm. In both subsections the PR server logged no "cannot update draft decode metadata" warning, so the in-graph metadata update was active. ### Greedy draft sampling Baseline is `main` at `b6d8e8afd9`; PR is `1abc890148`. **Speed-Bench, temperature 0.** Each value is the mean of repeated runs: 3 runs at concurrency 1, 2 runs at 16 and 64. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.96 | 6.94 | -0.3% | 1.91 | 1.90 | 521.2 | 520.7 | -0.1% | 3.760 | 3.747 | | 16 | 16.11 | 16.04 | -0.4% | 4.92 | 4.91 | 3144.3 | 3113.5 | -1.0% | 3.775 | 3.755 | | 64 | 30.37 | 30.36 | 0.0% | 9.88 | 9.94 | 6249.0 | 6250.2 | 0.0% | 3.795 | 3.795 | Step time is unchanged at every concurrency. As with MTP in #58463, the host work this removes is not on the critical path for this model at TP4. Acceptance length differs between arms by at most 0.02, while runs of the same arm vary by up to 0.16 at concurrency 1. **AIME25** (MQA, 2 epochs x 30 problems, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, max 98304 tokens, 64 concurrent): | Arm | Exact match | pass@2 | Samples | Request errors | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | base | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | | PR | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 60 | 0 | Accuracy is identical. Every sample includes reasoning, with median completion lengths of 5.3k tokens (base) and 4.9k (PR). ### Probabilistic draft sampling `--speculative-config` adds `"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"`. Baseline is `main` at `240785b82c`; PR is `6065f7c37c` (this branch rebased onto that baseline). **Speed-Bench, temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0.** Each value is the mean of 2 runs. Individual acceptance lengths are in brackets. | Concurrency | ITL p50 base (ms) | ITL p50 PR (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 base (ms) | TPOT p50 PR (ms) | Output tok/s base | Output tok/s PR | Δ | Accept. len base | Accept. len PR | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 6.89 | 6.86 | -0.4% | 1.95 | 1.86 | 505.1 | 514.8 | +1.9% | 3.60 [3.68, 3.52] | 3.66 [3.71, 3.61] | | 16 | 16.05 | 16.02 | -0.2% | 5.01 | 5.06 | 3051.8 | 3046.9 | -0.2% | 3.64 [3.65, 3.62] | 3.65 [3.65, 3.65] | | 64 | 30.51 | 30.50 | 0.0% | 10.28 | 10.43 | 6061.4 | 5972.4 | -1.5% | 3.66 [3.65, 3.67] | 3.67 [3.66, 3.68] | Median ITL matches within 0.03 ms. The -1.5% throughput at concurrency 64 comes from a single PR run (5930 vs 6015 tok/s for the other); output lengths vary between runs at temperature 1.0. Acceptance length is equal or higher for the PR at every concurrency, and the largest gap (+0.06 at concurrency 1) is smaller than the baseline's own run-to-run spread (0.16). **gsm8k** (1319 questions, 5-shot `/v1/completions`, temperature 1.0, max 512 tokens, 64 concurrent). Acceptance is computed from the server's spec-decode counters over the eval: | Arm | Accuracy | Invalid | Accept. len | Per-position acceptance (0-4) | |---|---:|---:|---:|---| | base | 0.838 | 1.1% | 3.296 | 0.779 / 0.605 / 0.423 / 0.298 / 0.190 | | PR | 0.835 | 1.1% | 3.299 | 0.782 / 0.603 / 0.421 / 0.298 / 0.195 | Accuracy is within 4 questions, and per-position acceptance shows no drop at later draft positions, which is where a stale non-causal window would show up first.

title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save the EAGLE attention proof with hybrid Mamba partial tails
author: Dao007forever
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This is the Mooncake connector part of #59826 by @wzhao18. It was split off at review so the core fixes could land first as #60533, which is now merged. The Mooncake store tail save now includes the full-attention KV that proves the Mamba checkpoint under EAGLE. It also pins those blocks until the asynchronous save completes.

## Claims

- After a GPU prefix-cache reset, a hybrid attention + Mamba prompt that uses EAGLE can hit its Mamba checkpoint again from the Mooncake store. Before this change the external hit was 0 tokens.
- The tail's attention blocks stay referenced until every rank finishes the save. They can no longer be reused while the save reads them.
- The scheduler computes each tail once and sends it to the worker, so the blocks it pins are exactly the blocks the worker puts. Later saves no longer re-send the tail.
- The Kimi K3 prefix-cache test starts a Mooncake master from a pytest fixture and runs a Mooncake resend case (`test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`).

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
```

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This branch | 480 passed |
| `main`, with this PR's test files copied in (measured at 22948c5, before the scheduler-side tail commit) | 29 failed, 233 passed (scheduler, worker and HMA end-to-end suites) |

On `main`, failing tests include `test_eagle_attention_proof_published_after_checkpoint_handoff`, `test_mooncake_lookup_reuses_resolved_hash_checkpoint`, `test_finished_partial_tail_is_pre_pinned_as_store_job` and `test_sub_block_partial_tail_offload_reads_cow_block`.

`ruff` is clean. `mypy` reports no new errors: the 10 in `worker.py` also appear on `main` in the same environment and come from pyzmq typing.

**Not run here:** the Kimi K3 end-to-end case (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py::test_mooncake_resend_reuses_prompt_checkpoint`). It needs GPUs, RDMA and `mooncake_master`; its fixture starts the master, and it skips where the binary is missing. #59826 reports an end-to-end gain with this change and the core fixes combined: Kimi K3, 1P1D DCP8 + DCP8, DSpark k4, prefix-match unit 128. At concurrency 128, the prefix hit rate went from 90.47% to 94.04% and throughput from 11,371 to 15,754 TPS/GPU. Those numbers include #60533 and have not been re-measured for this PR alone.

## Details

**Root cause.** Take P = 7,449 tokens, prefix-match unit U = 128 and EAGLE block drop on, so the Mamba checkpoint is H = 7,296.

1. The first request computes the prompt. On the GPU, the Mamba state is registered at 7,296 and the attention tail at 7,424, which is H + U.
2. Normal Mooncake saves store attention only up to the last scheduler-block boundary, 7,168. Mamba state is never stored by normal saves.
3. The partial-tail save stores the Mamba state at 7,296. But it clipped attention to the same position (key `hash@7296`), so the proof at `hash@7424` was never stored.
4. After a GPU reset, the Mooncake lookup works like this:
   - Attention matches 7,296, and the EAGLE drop brings it to 7,168.
   - Mamba has no state at or below 7,168.
   - The hit is 0.

**Fix.**
- **Boundary puts.** `ReqMeta.boundary_puts` lists every block the job stores under an explicit prefix hash, as `BoundaryPut(group_id, block_id, num_tokens)`. The scheduler resolves and pins all of them; the worker writes each block under `block_hashes[num_tokens // U - 1]` (`_boundary_puts`). Two kinds of entries:
  - **Mamba state.** Each core hand-off, whether a block-aligned snapshot or the sub-block tail at H, becomes one put of the handed-off block. Under DCP, Mamba blocks are smaller than the LCM, and only the boundary block is stored.
  - **Non-Mamba tail.** `_partial_tail_non_mamba_puts` (scheduler, once per store job) covers each non-Mamba group from the last scheduler-block boundary to H plus that group's `eagle_proof_margin`, once that much has been computed. Each block is keyed at its end, clipped to that point; null and missing blocks are skipped.
- **Publishing.** The tail is published on the save that first covers the whole prompt (`ReqMeta.publish_partial_tail`, which mirrors the tracker's `partial_tail_sent`), or when a Mamba hand-off arrives. The boundary is derived from the prompt length, so a job without a Mamba hand-off can still publish the attention proof. Later saves carry no tail.
- **Pinning.** A store job pins exactly its boundary puts' blocks (plus every non-Mamba block for a normal save). Before, a finish-time tail pinned only the Mamba block while the worker read attention blocks from the freed table.
- **Prompt length vs. prefill end.** `ReqMeta` separates `num_prompt_tokens` (used for the checkpoint) from `prefill_end_tokens` (includes output tokens replayed after preemption, used for store masks), and adds `completed_token_len`.
- **External lookup.** It scans past the hit limit for EAGLE groups, as the core lookup does since #60533. The shared helpers `eagle_proof_margin` and `partial_hash_hits_enabled` replace the local copies.
- **Partial hits follow core.** Mooncake used to decide `enable_partial_hash_hits` itself, from the Mamba specs of the groups it transfers. Core also requires every group's manager to support fine-grained lookups (a sliding-window group needs block-aligned ones) and counts groups the store does not transfer, so the two could disagree. Mooncake's scheduler and worker now read core's resolved `kv_cache_config.cache_hit_alignment_tokens`. One core line makes that possible: `engine/core.py` sets the field (and `hash_block_size`) on the scheduler's `KVCacheConfig` as well as the workers'; the scheduler's copy is deep-copied before they are resolved, and core itself does not read them there.

**Known limitations and follow-ups:**
- The prompt-completion tail is sent once. If that save is skipped under store pressure or its put fails, it is not retried; before, every later save rebuilt it (and `batch_is_exist` dropped it once stored). The Mamba state already worked this way, because its CoW block is pinned only for its own job.

**Duplicate check.** #59826 contains these changes. Splitting it into core (#60533) and Mooncake parts was requested at review, so this PR is that Mooncake part, not a duplicate.

**AI assistance.** Claude Code was used to port #59826's Mooncake changes onto current `main`, run the tests above and draft this description. The submitter has reviewed the changes.

---
