title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode on MI300X and MI325X (gfx942)
author: maeehart
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode kernels of #60397 to gfx942 (MI300X and MI325X). A standard decoder layer then runs as 2 kernels instead of 32. The path is opt-in with `--monokernel`, as on gfx950.

The PR was rebased onto `main` after #61082 as one commit. The commits after it merge `main` and answer the second review (see Details). gfx942 now runs the same layers whole as gfx950, with the switch of #61082 (see Details). The latest commits take the PR out of shared code, as RFC #60904 asks, and merge `main` with #62131 (see Details). The AgentX and GSM8K comparisons below are from 67206b7 and the commits before it, when the switch was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`. The checks of the latest commits are at the end of Validation.

## Claims

MI325X, TP4, DSpark with 5 drafts. Each AgentX run is 3,600 s and is scored with InferenceX's own result code.

- AgentX at concurrency 1, against `main`: interactivity P50 goes from **216.85 to 503.53 tokens/s/user** (2.32×), P90 from **182.25 to 411.26** (2.26×), and total throughput per GPU from 4,024 to 6,546 tokens/s (1.63×).
- AgentX at concurrency 2, 4 and 8, against InferenceX's published MI325X points: P90 goes from **153.22 to 368.64** (2.41×), from **142.75 to 316.28** (2.22×) and from **81.52 to 162.61** (1.99×).
- A standard decoder layer takes 115 µs instead of 320 µs. A decode period of one request takes 7.2 ms instead of 17.9 ms.
- GSM8K strict match at concurrency 7, 3 runs each: `main` 0.9247 and this PR 0.9270 on average (pooled p 0.49). The difference is not significant.
- On a2ce22d7e317 at concurrency 7, GPQA-Diamond is 85.0%, AIME25 99.0% and RULER NIAH 40 of 40 in every cell, against 85.3%, 99.4% and 40 of 40 for the reference arm of #60397 on MI355X.
- The gfx942 code runs only with `--monokernel`, on gfx942. Outside `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/` and the tests, the PR adds an 8-line hook to the DSpark speculator and two CI jobs.
- On gfx950 all 76 builds of the mono kernels, the 12 of the DSpark draft's runner included, have the same register and LDS use as on `main` and the same count of each instruction, apart from 1 or 2 more `s_waitcnt` in K2 and the FFN launch. The draft runner's scratch is now laid out for its MoE, see Details.
- On MI355X with `--monokernel` at TP2, two runs of each arm on 6caadd0, before #62131: GSM8K strict match 0.9257 and 0.9242 against 0.9249 and 0.9272 for `main` (see Validation).

## Limits on gfx942

- TP4 only. At TP2 the path logs one line and every layer runs vLLM's path.
- Decode steps of up to 42 rows, which is 7 requests with 5 DSpark drafts. A gfx942 workgroup has 64 KB of LDS, against 160 KB on gfx950, so a GEMV pass takes 6 tokens instead of 16. A larger step, prefill, a mixed step and a PIECEWISE graph run vLLM's path on every layer and every rank.
- gfx942 has no scaled FP4 or FP8 MFMA and uses FNUZ FP8, so the kernels read their own copies of the weights. At TP4 the weights take 170.11 GiB a rank instead of 98.88 GiB. On MI325X with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` the KV cache still holds 11.18 million tokens. MI300X (192 GiB) does not fit this well, so the numbers here are for MI325X.

## Validation

`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on MI325X, TP4. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`. The PR arm is the same image with the `vllm/` changes of #60397 and this PR copied over its `vllm` package. Both arms use the same command and environment, apart from the switch, which was `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1` on those commits.

**AgentX, concurrency 1, against `main`.** One 3,600 s run per arm, each on a fresh server.

| | `main` | PR | PR / `main` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Measured requests, no errors | 239 | 306 | |
| Interactivity P50 (tokens/s/user) | 216.85 | 503.53 | 2.32× |
| Interactivity P90 (tokens/s/user) | 182.25 | 411.26 | 2.26× |
| TTFT P50 (s) | 0.510 | 0.544 | |
| Total throughput per GPU (tokens/s) | 4,024 | 6,546 | 1.63× |

**AgentX, concurrency 2, 4 and 8.** There is no `main` run at these concurrencies, so the reference is InferenceX's published MI325X TP4 points ([Actions run 35637516947](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/35637516947)). They come from an older nightly. At concurrency 1 the published P90 is 189.90, close to our `main` run.

| Concurrency | P90, published | P90, PR | Throughput per GPU, published | Throughput per GPU, PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 153.22 | 368.64 (2.41×) | 4,255 | 6,729 (1.58×) |
| 4 | 142.75 | 316.28 (2.22×) | 6,315 | 8,882 (1.41×) |
| 8 | 81.52 | 162.61 (1.99×) | 10,998 | 14,839 (1.35×) |

At concurrency 8, steps of more than 42 rows ran vLLM's path during 0.14% of the decode time.

**Accuracy.** `lm_eval` `gsm8k`, 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, greedy, DSpark with block rejection. At concurrency 7 every decode step of this PR takes the mono path. Strict match of each run:

| | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrency 1 | 0.9340, 0.9318 | 0.9272 |
| Concurrency 7 | 0.9242, 0.9257, 0.9242 | 0.9295, 0.9242, 0.9265, 0.9303 |

Two runs of the same code differ by up to 0.6 points, so the runs are pooled with a Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with one stratum a question. At concurrency 7 this PR scores 0.23 points more than `main` (p 0.49). Over all runs the mono path scores 0.14 points less (p 0.54). The mono kernels quantize the activations to MXFP8, where vLLM's gfx942 path keeps bf16.

**GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and RULER NIAH.** A build of a2ce22d7e317 with `--monokernel` at TP4 and concurrency 7, with the sample counts of #60397: GPQA-Diamond with 2 option orders and 4 seeds at up to 32K tokens, AIME25 with 16 seeds at up to 64K tokens, and NIAH with `niah_single_1`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K, 40 samples a cell. The reference is the MI355X result of #60397. The runs are in the comments [for NIAH](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6178954285), [for AIME25](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6182853591) and [for GPQA-Diamond](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60731#issuecomment-6191592654).

| | This PR, MI325X TP4 | #60397 mono, MI355X TP2 | #60397 reference, MI355X TP2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GPQA-Diamond | 85.0% (1347 of 1584) | 85.1 ± 2.2% | 85.3 ± 2.2% |
| AIME25 | 99.0% (475 of 480) | 98.3 ± 0.8% | 99.4 ± 0.3% |
| RULER NIAH, 9 cells | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each | 40 of 40 in each |

A debugging patch, not part of this PR, ran vLLM's own layer after each mono layer on the same inputs, in steps of 6 to 42 rows. No output had a non-finite value, and the index layers' top-512 lists matched vLLM's in all 481,944 entries.

**gfx950.** `main` and this PR on the same MI355X node, two runs each, in the order PR, `main`, `main`, PR. All four runs use `--monokernel` at TP2, DSpark with 5 drafts, probabilistic drafts and block rejection, and the same server arguments (see Reproduce). `main` is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1`, and the PR runs use the same image with this PR's files at 6caadd0 copied in. At 6caadd0 the PR still held a change of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` that it no longer has (see Changes outside the model directory), and `main` did not have #62131 yet. The speed rows use random prompts of 1024 tokens and 1024 output tokens, 16 requests at concurrency 1 and 64 at concurrency 8.

| | `main`, run 1 | `main`, run 2 | This PR, run 1 | This PR, run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 8, strict match | 0.9249 | 0.9272 | 0.9257 | 0.9242 |
| Concurrency 1, output throughput (tokens/s) | 520.34 | 579.54 | 584.43 | 577.95 |
| Concurrency 1, median TPOT (ms) | 1.59 | 1.56 | 1.54 | 1.48 |
| Concurrency 1, median ITL (ms) | 7.60 | 7.59 | 7.36 | 7.38 |
| Concurrency 1, median TTFT (ms) | 66.30 | 66.55 | 67.09 | 67.02 |
| Concurrency 8, output throughput (tokens/s) | 2038.63 | 1986.51 | 2049.16 | 2099.40 |
| Concurrency 8, median TPOT (ms) | 3.37 | 3.35 | 3.47 | 3.17 |
| Concurrency 8, median ITL (ms) | 17.06 | 16.99 | 16.84 | 16.77 |
| Concurrency 8, median TTFT (ms) | 84.37 | 83.77 | 84.51 | 83.91 |

GSM8K is the same within the spread of the runs, and the median TTFT differs by less than 1 ms. With DSpark a decode step streams several tokens, so the median ITL is the time of one decode step. It was about 0.2 ms shorter with the PR, from that `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change. The TPOT also depends on how many drafts are accepted. In the first `main` run a few first tokens took more than a second, which lowered its throughput at concurrency 1.

**Tests.** The kernel tests are in `tests/kernels/models/amd/` and run in a new one-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`. A new four-GPU MI300 job in `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` runs the real-model and graph replay tests on gfx942 at TP4. On MI325X all of them pass on 6cb1400, and the two TP4 files take about 10 minutes. On MI355X the two TP4 files pass their CDNA4 cases on 0597d94 too, and their gfx942 cases skip there.

| File | Compared against |
|---|---|
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_topk.py` | vLLM's `top_k_per_row_decode` and its candidate mask, for contexts from 100 to 300,000 tokens |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_cand_logits.py` | AITER's dense logits at the candidate positions, bit for bit |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_sparse_indexer.py` | vLLM's ROCm indexer op on a decode step, for a layer without candidate blocks, for layer 20, which writes them, and for a layer that reads them. The gfx942 indexer layer runs its own copy of that op's decode path, and this test fails when the two stop agreeing |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` | the old SWA metadata ops and top-k packing, on 800 random batches |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` | vLLM's Markov sampling loop, and each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's logits, exactly |
| `test_dsv41_gfx942_draft_lm_head.py` | an fp32 GEMM. It also checks that `wvSplitK` gets no 5-row GEMM with `--monokernel` and keeps it without |
| `test_dsv41_mono_gfx942.py` | torch references for K2's key lists, the first layer's seam, the GEMV cores and the gfx942 FP4 and FP8 conversions |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` | vLLM's own decoder layers in a five-layer model with random weights, at TP4 with the FP8 indexer, at steps of 8 rows (two GEMV passes, the second one padded) and 42 rows (the limit), every layer at every decode step |
| `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` | the composed runner at TP4 on the copies made at load: the padded step against its rows run alone, and 300 replays of steps of 6, 8 and 42 rows in one CUDA graph against the first run, bit for bit |

On f0a549d a TP4 server with the mono path also answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9303, 0.9272 and 0.9257. On the rebased commit pre-commit passes, and the 60 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU. On a2ce22d7e317, which merges `main` into the rebased commit, the new MI300 job passes in CI, and a TP4 server with the mono path ran GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and NIAH (see Accuracy). The commits after it merge `main` again and follow four changes on `main`: #58689, which renamed the V4.1 ROCm attention classes, #55090, which split the skinny GEMM check, #58800, which moved the gfx1250 check out of `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl`, and #61161, which mixes the draft step into the seed of the draft sampler. The fused Markov launch now mixes in its draft step too, so its draft tokens stay the same as those of vLLM's loop.

The latest commits move the gfx942 top-k launches into an indexer layer in the model folder, add a test that compares that layer with vLLM's indexer op, drop the `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` change, and merge `main` with #62131. On 6cb1400 pre-commit passes, the 76 tests of `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` pass on CPU, and the kernel tests and the two TP4 files pass on MI325X with the ROCm 7.2 nightly and with the ROCm 10 nightly. The new indexer test fails on a copy of the layer whose logits take the head weights of the wrong rows. With the ROCm 7.2 nightly a TP4 server with the mono path answered the sanity prompts correctly, one at a time and 7 at once, and three GSM8K runs at concurrency 7 gave strict match 0.9310, 0.9303 and 0.9295. With the ROCm 10 nightly such a server also answered the sanity prompts correctly, and GSM8K gave 0.9295, 0.9272 and 0.9242. In one of three starts with the mono path on ROCm 10 the server hung before it was ready: three ranks stopped in AITER's custom all-reduce while it registered the buffers of the decoder replay CUDA graphs, which `main` also captures. On gfx950 the 76 builds compile, see Claims, and on MI355X a TP2 server with the mono path ran the DSpark draft layers whole with the fix of #62131's scratch and answered the sanity prompts correctly.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server, the same for both arms apart from `--monokernel`, which the `main` arm leaves out:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR
export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_ROCM_FLYDSL_QR_INT4=1
export VLLM_DSV41_FUSED_COMBINE_TOPK_SWA=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1
export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

GSM8K uses `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` instead of the two synthetic keys, with `lm_eval` 0.4.9.2 and `num_concurrent=1` for the concurrency 1 runs:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=7,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512,temperature=0.0,top_p=1.0
```

AgentX is the InferenceX AgentX client ([agentx-standalone.md](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/inferencex-e2e/docs/agentx-standalone.md)) with the arguments of the InferenceX AgentX sweep and `--concurrency 1`, 2, 4 or 8. InferenceX's `python -m infx.results.agentic.process_agentic_result` scored each run with `TP=4 GPU_COUNT=4`.

The gfx950 runs, with the same server for both arms:

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --monokernel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'
```

The speed rows are `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, with `--max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 16` and with `--max-concurrency 8 --num-prompts 64`. GSM8K is the `lm_eval` command above with `num_concurrent=8` and `--gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=2048`.

Kernel tests on one GPU, and the TP4 tests on four:

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/models/amd/
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py
```

</details>

## Details

- **Layers.** gfx942 runs every backbone layer whole, as gfx950 does since #61082. The index layers use vLLM's FP8 indexer, because the MXFP4 indexer cache needs CDNA4. vLLM's compressor and indexer run between K1 and K2, as on gfx950. On gfx942 `mono/keylist.py` then writes the layer's key lists, so K2 is the build without the key table. On gfx942 the 3 DSpark draft layers take the FFN launch after vLLM's attention, built for the draft's 128 experts and top 3, on the target's runner. On gfx950 they run whole on a runner of their own, as #62131 added.
- **gfx942 helper ops** in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`: the sparse indexer's decode top-512 (`topk512_gfx942.cu`) and its candidate logits, the SWA decode metadata and the top-k packing as one launch each, and DSpark's Markov sampling as one launch a draft step. With `--monokernel` on gfx942 the V4.1 ROCm attention takes the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. It runs vLLM's ROCm indexer op on every step except a step of only decode rows, which runs the decode path of that op with the top-k launches in front of vLLM's ops. The DSpark speculator asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, and the DSv4.1 draft model runs the fused Markov launches there. `draft_lm_head.py` pads the DSpark draft's 5-row logits GEMM to 6 rows, so that vLLM's dispatch takes the torch GEMM instead of `wvSplitK`. For the 32320 × 5120 lm_head shard that takes 96 µs instead of 295 µs on MI325X. Each helper leaves a call it cannot take to vLLM's own op. `topk512_gfx942.cu` is built with hipcc when the model is created. If the build fails, a warning is logged and the indexer runs vLLM's top-k ops.
- **Weight copies.** The routed experts are copied in the byte order of the gfx942 GEMVs, without vLLM's padding columns, and the dense linears as e4m3 bytes, because vLLM dequantizes those to bf16 on gfx942. The copies are made when vLLM processes the weights at load, so vLLM counts them as model memory when it sizes the KV cache. A reload writes the new copies into the first ones in place, because the kernels and the captured CUDA graphs hold their addresses.
- **Changes outside the model directory.** One hook in the DSpark speculator: `_sample_sequential` asks the draft model's `sample_sequential` first, if the model has one, and runs its own loop when the call returns False. Only the DSv4.1 draft model has one, and it takes a step only with `--monokernel` on gfx942. The rest are the two CI jobs. The earlier hooks in `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` are now the indexer layer of `sparse_indexer.py`. The change of the padding loops of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel` is dropped, because #58633 parallelises the same padding.
- **Merge of #62131.** #62131 runs the DSpark draft layers whole on gfx950, on a runner of their own whose MoE takes one FP4 group an ug task (`DRAFT_UG_GROUPS`). Its scratch was laid out for the default two groups, and with one group the ug flags take twice the room. So the flags of the upper half of the tasks were written over the start of the `normed` rows that the MoE reads as its input, at TP 2 and 4 and for every step width. Only the draft layers could be affected, not the target's output, and in a GSM8K check on MI355X `main` accepted as many drafts as this PR, so the overlap did not show there. `scratch_layout` and `scratch_bytes` now take the runner's groups. `run_ffn` checks that each MoE region of a build fits the layout, and that check found the overlap when the draft runner's K2 was built. The FFN launch reads the target's layout, because it runs on the target's runner, also for a gfx942 draft layer.
- **Since the first review.** The branch is rebased onto `main` as one commit. The gfx942 ops moved from `vllm/model_executor/layers/dsv41_gfx942/` into `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/`, as RFC #60904 asks for model kernels. `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_SHADOW` and its layer-by-layer check are removed. The rebase onto #61082 takes its switch and its layer plan on gfx942 too. That removes the gfx942 paths of their own for the first layer, the window layers and the index layers, apart from `mono/keylist.py`.
- **Since the second review.** The kernel tests moved to `tests/kernels/models/amd/`. The fused Markov test checks each draft token against vLLM's `_sample_logits` on the same step's cached logits. The change to vLLM's skinny GEMM dispatch is reverted, and only the DSpark draft's lm_head avoids `wvSplitK`, with `--monokernel` on gfx942. `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` and a gfx942 graph replay test in `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` run at TP4 in a new four-GPU MI300 job. On gfx942 the first layer's output bound in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` is 6% instead of 3%, because vLLM's gfx942 MoE keeps bf16 activations and the kernels quantize them to MXFP8, which alone moves the FFN output of the test's random weights by 4.65%. The residual stream then differs by up to 2.5% instead of 0.4 to 0.7%, so past the first layer a routing near-tie there is a gap of up to 0.02 instead of 0.01, and up to a third of the tokens may flip an expert instead of a quarter (22% seen).
- **Relation to other PRs.** Draft #61482 moves the FlyDSL stages to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`, and this PR edits the files it moves. Whichever of the two merges second needs a rebase. If this PR merges first, its gfx942 tests can check #61482's move on MI325X. #62131 is merged into this branch, see Merge of #62131. #58633 parallelises the padding of `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`, which this PR changed until the latest commits, and neither PR needs the other. #61311 moves `amd/mono/` to `amd/specialized_decode/mono/` and replaces `mono_decode.py`, as RFC #60904 describes. A trial merge of the two conflicts in 15 files, among them `mono_decode.py` and `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, which #61311 deletes and this PR changes. So whichever of the two merges second needs a port. #61869 adds a fused Markov sampler at the start of `_sample_sequential`, next to this PR's hook, and the two merge there without a conflict.
- **Follow-ups.** Steps of more than 42 rows on gfx942, so that 8 or more concurrent requests with 5 drafts also take the mono path. One copy of the routed experts instead of two. Other TP sizes on gfx942. The whole DSpark draft layers on gfx942, as on gfx950. `topk512_gfx942.cu` as a compiled op in `csrc/`.

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Declare 64-token kernel blocks for SM120 sparse backends
author: xzwgit
body:
### Summary
On SM120, the DSV41 sparse-MLA backends declare only `[128]`-token kernel blocks (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` returns `[64 if family(90) else 128]` / `[128]`), so serving with `--block-size 64` dies in block-size negotiation:

```
ValueError: No common block size for 64 (FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41: [128]; DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER: [128])
```

This declares `[64]` on SM12x for the two sites (indexer backend, sparse MLA backend, FlashInfer sparse backend), mirroring the existing SM90 branch. The SWA/backend selection is untouched.

The approach is @aagallo's (described in #59203); this PR adds the validated matrix below.

### Matrix validation (8x RTX PRO 6000, SM120, TP8)
Stack: vLLM `0.31.1rc1.dev158+gab905a885` + FlashInfer `0.7.1rc5`, `--block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, DeepGEMM switched between PR14 head (`40592bd`) and the current pin (`1e1842a`):

| vLLM tree | DeepGEMM | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock | `1e1842a` | fails negotiation (error above) |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| this PR (uniform `[64]`) | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant (`[64,128]` + `64*max(1,cr)` specs) | `40592bd` | serves, 17x19=323 |
| per-layer variant | `1e1842a` | serves, 17x19=323 |

All four patched cells boot in ~90-160 s and answer correctly; zero failures. An earlier `attention.hpp:484` observed with uniform-64 on an older stack (0.30.1rc1.dev738 + FlashInfer main @c11f8ba + DeepGEMM 6901431) does not reproduce on current main with either DeepGEMM build — details in #59203.

Pairs naturally with #57292 (fail-fast when FlashInfer lacks runtime page sizes).

Addresses the SM120 serving failure in #59203.

### Test Plan
- [x] 5-cell matrix above (serve + correctness per cell)
- [x] pre-commit / CI

---

## Requirements & validation (added after review)

**FlashInfer requirement: `flashinfer-python >= 0.7.1rc5` (runtime page sizes).** Measured end to end on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120):
- pinned `0.7.0.post1` + this PR: does **not** serve — fails in ~110 s with `page_block_size=32 is unsupported; decode kernels are instantiated only for page_block_size=64` (64-token kernel blocks give ratio-2 layers 32-token compressed pages; the pin has no runtime page sizes). Stock fails on the pin as well.
- `0.7.1rc5` + this PR: serves at default and `--block-size 64`; `--block-size 128` does not serve on this stack in either declaration form (see matrix below), so the PR buys default-64 — the only geometry that serves on the default BLHNC layout.

Landing order per review discussion: after the FlashInfer bump (#60948), or together with the #57292 guard.

**Matrix (stock / A=[64] / C=[64,128] x default / 64 / 128, GSM8K n=100):** stock fails both ways (assertions upthread); A and C serve at default and 64 (GSM8K 89-91%, no variant-dependent degradation); 128 fails under both declarations (A: BLHNC layout guard; C: FlashInfer `block_kv == 32 or block_kv == 64`). Decode throughput of the four servable configs is within <1% at c1/c4.

**No unit test, by review:** an earlier revision added `tests/v1/attention/test_dsv41_indexer_block_sizes.py`, but it pinned kernel-support values that will drift (and the block size is asserted in C++ at kernel launch, so a black-box version would need a real kernel anyway). Per review it was removed and each SM12x `[64]` now carries a short inline comment naming the failure it avoids (#59203).

**Revalidation on the final form** — 8x RTX PRO 6000 96 GB (SM120), vLLM 0.33.0 with these two declarations, fp8 KV, no explicit `--block-size`: negotiation reports `Setting kv cache block size to 64 for FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41/DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA/DEEPSEEK_V41_INDEXER/CompressorBackend`; READY in ~7.5 min (cold JIT); KV cache 2,397,337 tokens at 32,768 max-model-len; 4/4 short-answer probes correct and greedy output byte-identical across 3 runs.

Coordinated with #56509 (same failure, overlapping declarations).

title: [ROCm][Perf] Apply opt-in paged MXFP4 sparse indexer dense path for DeepSeek-V4
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Purpose

#58671 added a paged MXFP4 sparse indexer for DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm gfx950. The indexer K cache is stored as MXFP4 (68 B per token instead of 132 B for FP8) in the preshuffled page order that aiter's `pa_mqa_logits_mxfp4` reads. That kernel scores the cache in place, so prefill no longer gathers K first. The PR has two layers:

- the **dense** path, which scores the whole context. It is model-agnostic.
- the **candidate-pool** path, which only exists because of V4.1's two-level indexer.

This PR brings the dense path to DeepSeek-V4 (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro: 30 indexer layers at compress ratio 4, 64 heads × 128, top-k 1024). Today V4 on ROCm can only use the FP8 indexer cache, because:

- `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4()` rejects every model except `deepseek_v41` on ROCm;
- `SparseAttnIndexer.forward_hip` asserts that the cache is not FP4;
- V4's own MXFP4 Q/K Triton kernels pack FP4 with CUDA PTX (`cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2.f32`), so they cannot run on ROCm.

The feature is opt-in, as on V4.1:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro -tp 8 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

The default path (FP8 indexer cache) is unchanged.

## Changes

### K write: ROCm pooling kernel + aiter's cache op

In V4 the indexer K is produced by the indexer's own `DeepseekCompressor`. One fused Triton kernel does pool → RMSNorm → RoPE → MXFP4 → cache store, and nothing before the norm ever reaches memory. On ROCm we split it into two launches:

1. A new Triton kernel, `_compress_pool_kernel`, does the softmax-gated overlap pooling. It is copied from V4's fused kernel, up to the norm. It writes one bf16 row per boundary token into a scratch buffer that all indexer layers share (`[max_num_batched_tokens, 128]`).
2. aiter's public `k_norm_rope_mxfp4_cache(..., shuffle=layout)` then applies norm → RoPE → MXFP4 and stores into the preshuffled pages. This is the same op V4.1 uses, through the same `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store` wrapper.

This keeps the page layout and the quantization defined only in aiter, which is the principle #58671 follows (`rocm_paged_mxfp4_cache_layout` is the only place vLLM reads the layout).

The cost is one extra small launch per indexer layer, plus a bf16 round trip of the pooled row before the norm. That rounding error (~2⁻⁹) is two orders of magnitude below the MXFP4 quantization step. A fully fused ROCm kernel can follow if profiles show the extra launch matters.

### Q quant

The Q path uses aiter's `q_rope_mxfp4_quant`, through the existing `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant`. It produces fp32 weights with the softmax and head scales folded in, as the aiter MQA-logits kernel expects.

### Scoring and metadata

Both are reused unchanged:

- `RocmSparseAttnIndexer`, which calls `rocm_mxfp4_sparse_attn_indexer` with no candidate blocks;
- the model-agnostic `RocmMxfp4IndexerMetadataBuilder`.

A new `DeepseekV4RocmMxfp4IndexerBackend` subclasses `DeepseekV4IndexerBackend`, so V4's 256-token blocks and ROCm adaptive-verification support carry over. At compress ratio 4 that gives 64-entry pages, which is aiter's preferred page size.

### Keeping CUDA untouched

Shared V4 code only gains extract-method / ClassVar hooks. The code inside them is moved verbatim, and the ROCm subclasses override the hooks.

### Other changes

- `FusedKVCompressNormRopeInsertIndexerTritonKernel.get_warmup_keys()` returns no keys on ROCm with an MXFP4 indexer cache. The warmup is a process-wide singleton that every non-CUDA compressor registers, including V4's head-512 attention compressors, so without this guard the PTX MXFP4 variant was compiled at startup and failed (`error: unknown asm constraint 'f'`). ROCm never runs that kernel: it writes the cache with aiter's op.
- `dsa_indexer_uses_fp4()`: the ROCm branch now accepts `deepseek_v4` as well as `deepseek_v41`. The CDNA4 and aiter checks are unchanged, and the CUDA branch is untouched.
- `_aiter_indexer_cache_ops`, `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_k_store` and `rocm_mxfp4_indexer_q_quant` move from `models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py` to `v1/attention/ops/rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py`, so V4 and V4.1 share them. They are still importable from the old module.

## Test Plan

### Unit Test

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_dsv4_mxfp4_indexer.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_compressor_gemm_fusion.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_wo_a.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_dspark_rocm.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_rocm_adaptive.py \
    tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py \
    tests/kernels/test_deepseek_v4_cpu_kernels.py
```

### Benchmark

Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` and `agentic` workload with server launch commands below.

Fixed sequence length:

```bash
vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --port 8333 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --data-parallel-size 1 \
    --max-model-len 9472 \
    --max-num-seqs 512 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --async-scheduling \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --moe-backend aiter \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 2}' \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

Agentic replay:

```bash
vllm serve /shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8333 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --async-scheduling \
    --distributed-executor-backend mp \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
    --data-parallel-size 8 \
    --prefill-schedule-interval 8 \
    --long-prefill-token-threshold 16384 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \
    --moe-backend aiter \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}' \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --max-num-seqs 64 \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'
```

### Accuracy Test

Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`:

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=/shared/models/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000 \
  --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --num_fewshot 5 \
  --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log
```

## Test Result

### Unit Test

- New tests: 4 passed. The ROCm compressor's pages match aiter's writer fed by torch pooling byte for byte (0 mismatched bytes). As a sanity check, feeding a shifted window mismatches 21.8% of bytes, so the test does detect wrong pooling.
- V4.1 MXFP4 indexer tests: 37 passed.
- V4 ROCm / compressor tests: 99 passed, 137 skipped (platform-gated).

### Benchmark

Fixed sequence length:

| Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) |  Change | Mean TTFT (ms) |   Change | Mean TPOT (ms) |  Change |
| ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | ------: | -------------: | -------: | -------------: | ------: |
|    1 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                          145.99 |       — |         597.24 |        — |           6.24 |       — |
|    1 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                          156.34 | 7.09% ↑ |         413.91 | 30.70% ↓ |           5.96 | 4.49% ↓ |
|    4 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                          454.91 |       — |         504.07 |        — |           8.02 |       — |
|    4 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                          466.92 | 2.64% ↑ |         437.29 | 13.25% ↓ |           7.95 | 0.87% ↓ |
|   16 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                         1020.90 |       — |         744.88 |        — |          14.51 |       — |
|   16 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                         1030.30 | 0.92% ↑ |         681.89 |  8.46% ↓ |          14.46 | 0.34% ↓ |
|   64 | Main (FP8 Indexer)    |                         1629.53 |       — |        1637.36 |        — |          36.85 |       — |
|   64 | This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) |                         1656.28 | 1.64% ↑ |        1622.58 |  0.90% ↓ |          36.29 | 1.52% ↓ |

In summary, this PR delivers a clear overall improvement over Main: throughput increases across all concurrency levels, Mean TTFT decreases substantially—especially at low and medium concurrency—and Mean TPOT remains slightly better across the board. The results suggest that the optimization is beneficial for both latency-sensitive workloads and overall serving throughput, with the most pronounced gains appearing at lower concurrency.

Agentic replay:

| Indexer | Output Token Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | KV Cache Capacity (tokens) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Main (FP8 Indexer) | 697.25 | 2,442.24 | 46.01 | 4,589,684 |
| This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) | 675.83 (3.07% ↓) | 2,321.05 (4.96% ↓) | 43.42 (5.62% ↓) | 5,010,749 (9.17% ↑) |

- **Latency improves: mean TPOT -5.62%, mean TTFT -4.96%.** TPOT is the most consistent signal: both MXFP4 runs (44.60 / 42.24 ms) had lower TPOT than both FP8 runs (46.98 / 45.03 ms). TTFT varied by up to 13% between runs of the same configuration, so treat its gain as indicative.
- **Output token throughput is within noise (-3.07%).** On this workload, aggregate throughput is driven mainly by the trace replay and by output lengths.
- **KV cache capacity: +9.17%.** The MXFP4 indexer cache takes 68 B per compressed token instead of 132 B, and the freed memory goes to the KV pool. Peak KV usage stayed below 40% in all runs, so this workload does not yet turn the extra KV capacity into throughput. Higher-concurrency or longer-context workloads should benefit more.

### Accuracy Test

GSM8K:

| Task  | Filter           | n-shot | Metric        | Main (FP8) | This PR (MXFP4) |       Change |
| ----- | ---------------- | -----: | ------------- | ---------: | --------------: | -----------: |
| gsm8k | flexible-extract |      5 | exact_match ↑ |     0.9492 |          0.9477 | -0.16% ↓ |
| gsm8k | strict-match     |      5 | exact_match ↑ |     0.9500 |          0.9484 | -0.17% ↓ |

The MXFP4 indexer in this PR shows very small accuracy degradation compared with the FP8 indexer in main. On GSM8K, the flexible-extract exact-match score decreases from 94.92% to 94.77% (-0.16%), while the strict-match score decreases from 95.00% to 94.84% (-0.17%). Overall, the accuracy impact is negligible (<0.2% relative), indicating that the MXFP4 indexer largely preserves the model's original accuracy.

GPQA Diamond (newly added):

| Indexer | GPQA Diamond | Empty Responses (reasoning over budget) |
|---|---|---|
| Main (FP8 Indexer) | 0.7121 ± 0.0323 | 13 / 198 |
| This PR (MXFP4 Indexer) | 0.7121 ± 0.0323 | 11 / 198 |

- **Accuracy is unchanged:** both indexers score 0.7121. Per question, 124 are correct in both runs, and the disagreements are symmetric (17 vs 17, McNemar p = 1.0).
- **This exercises the indexer's long-context path:** with thinking, reasoning traces run to tens of thousands of tokens. Most decode steps are therefore far past 4096 tokens (top-k 1024 × compress ratio 4), where the indexer starts its sparse top-k selection.
- **KV cache capacity grows by 9.19%**, since the MXFP4 indexer cache stores 68 B per token instead of 132 B.
- The 11–13 empty responses are questions whose greedy reasoning did not finish within the 131072-token budget. They affect both runs alike.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] DeepGEMM FP8 MegaMoE with fused shared experts
author: gcanlin
body:
## Overview

Run GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE layers with DeepGEMM's FP8xFP8 MegaMoE (routed and shared experts in one kernel that also dispatches and combines across the EP group), using the official FP8 checkpoint. Enabled by `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'` with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size N --enable-expert-parallel`.

Related: #55275 (BF16 / MXFP4 MegaMoE for GLM, open), #54049 (FlashInfer NVFP4 mega kernel).

## Claims

- On the AgentX replay at concurrency 96, DEP4 with MegaMoE gives 1.6x the output throughput of DEP4 on the generic MoE path.
- Against TP4 it is about level on throughput (+6%, one run each) and has about a fifth of the TTFT.
- It prefills 1.8x faster than DEP4 generic and 2.5x faster than TP4.
- AIME 2026 Pass@1 matches the generic MoE path (0.934 vs 0.939 with a 131K output cap) and is 0.977 with the 1M context.
- A weight reload, in layerwise or direct mode, restores byte-identical weights at the same addresses.
- No change for any other `moe_backend`.

## Validation

4x B200, nightly `8cbd5d03` with this change applied, MTP 5 with acceptance fixed by `synthetic_acceptance_length` 3.61. The three arms ran on the same node and in the same container, one run each; they differ only in parallel layout and `moe_backend`.

AgentX replay (InferenceX-pinned aiperf, `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`), concurrency 96, 1 hour:

| metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| output tok/s | 3,152 | 2,063 | **3,332** |
| input tok/s | 380,126 | 234,727 | **399,297** |
| total tok/s | 383,278 | 236,790 | **402,628** |
| requests completed (errors) | 11,372 (4) | 8,143 (1) | 11,986 (5) |
| TTFT avg / p50 / p99 | 3.93 / 2.19 / 23.8 s | 2.36 / 1.47 / 17.3 s | **0.81 / 0.49 / 5.99 s** |
| ITL avg | 18.3 ms | 45.6 ms | 19.5 ms |
| output tok/s per user | 64.0 | 26.2 | 64.1 |
| prefix cache hit | 93.9% | 92.4% | 94.0% |
| of which GPU / host reload | 6.2% / 87.7% | 50.9% / 41.5% | 71.2% / 22.8% |
| preemptions | 35 | 53 | 2 |

`vllm bench serve`, random prompts, concurrency 128, on the same servers:

| workload (in/out) | metric | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 / 1 | total tok/s | 46,334 | 63,900 | **115,081** |
| | mean TTFT | 20.8 s | 15.2 s | 8.4 s |
| 1024 / 1024 | output tok/s | 7,895 | 8,478 | **11,691** |
| | mean TTFT | 4.31 s | 1.86 s | 0.85 s |

Accuracy:

| eval | TP4 | DEP4, generic MoE | DEP4, MegaMoE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K, lm-eval 5-shot, 1,319 questions | 0.9757 ± 0.0042 | – | 0.9735 ± 0.0044 |
| AIME 2026 Pass@1, 30 problems x 32 samples | – | 0.939 ± 0.006 | 0.934 ± 0.006 |

GSM8K ran on nightly `43b4aaea` (TP4) and the servers above (MegaMoE). AIME ran on nightly `df3bd094` with this branch, both arms in the same container (MTP 3, fp8 KV, 131K output cap) with DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompt and rule-based judge, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95; the generic arm runs `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` on the checkpoint's own scales. With the full 1M context MegaMoE reaches **0.977 ± 0.005**; the remaining loss is mostly problem 15 (0.72), where 12 of 32 samples never stop and loop until the context is full.

Weight reload, 4x B200, nightly `e0d00e4b8e` with this branch, DEP4, MTP 3. The experts are zeroed before each reload, which breaks every greedy output; all results are compared with the cold start:

| metric | layerwise | direct |
|---|---:|---:|
| target reload time | 41.6 s | 37.3 s |
| parameters and buffers differing (5,900 across ranks) | 0 | 0 |
| parameters and buffers moved | 0 | 0 |
| greedy outputs matching (4 short prompts) | 4/4 | 4/4 |

The same holds for a second reload, a reload of the MTP drafter, and an update that sends expert weights and block scales in separate `load_weights` calls. Long prompts (about 14K tokens) already vary between identical runs without a reload, on both MoE backends, so they are not compared. No real NCCL or IPC trainer was run.

Unit tests: `pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_mega_moe.py`, 5 passed.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONHASHSEED=42 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 96 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.61}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true,"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":300000000000,"enable_cross_layers_blocks":"true","lazy_offload":false}}'

vllm-router --port 8000 --worker-urls http://127.0.0.1:8001 --intra-node-data-parallel-size 4 --policy consistent_hash

aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --concurrency 96 --benchmark-duration 3600 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126
```

AIME 2026:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92
```

The client sends DeepInfer's `eval/aime` prompts (`build_records`) to `/v1/chat/completions` with `temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95`, 32 samples per problem, and scores `reasoning + "</think>" + content` with its `score_rollout`. Samples were drawn with a 131K output cap first; the 82 that hit it were continued from their own text to the 1M context, which samples the same distribution as the larger cap.

The baselines drop `moe_backend` (DEP4, generic) or use `--tensor-parallel-size 4` alone with `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1` on the router (TP4). The generic path picked `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` for the FP8 experts. The random-prompt rows were measured on the same servers before the replay with `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --max-concurrency 128`.
</details>

## Details

- The checkpoint's experts are block FP8 (E4M3, one float32 scale per 128x128 block). DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE feeds scales to the block-scaled MMA and needs UE8M0 scales per row and 32 columns, so the routed and shared expert weights are requantized once at load (`requant_block_fp8_to_ue8m0`).
- This requantization is lossy: about 2.4% relative L2 per weight tensor and about 3.9% on one MoE layer's output (layer 15, real weights, random inputs). The generic TRTLLM path uses the checkpoint's scales as they are. The GSM8K gap above is within one standard error.
- Routing stays outside the kernel: `fused_topk_bias` (sigmoid, score correction bias), with `routed_scaling_factor` folded into the top-k weights. DeepGEMM's Mega Gate only supports `sqrtsoftplus`.
- `Glm5NextMegaMoEExperts` subclasses `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts`, which is unchanged, with the `MEGA_MOE_MXFP8` format. E4M3 shards load straight into the kernel layout; their float32 block scales are staged in `*_weight_scale_inv`, and the model's `process_weights_after_loading` calls `requantize_block_fp8()`, which rounds every newly loaded shard to UE8M0 1x32 scales in place (main model, multimodal wrapper and MTP drafter).
- A weight update may send an expert weight and its block scale in separate `load_weights` calls; by the end of the load both must be in, or `requantize_block_fp8()` raises.
- Reload and weight transfer finish with that hook (#64357, and direct mode from #64336), so the kernel tensors keep their storage. The derived UE8M0 scales are marked `weight_loader_numel = 0`, so a layerwise reload replays a layer as soon as its checkpoint tensors are in.
- The block-FP8 shared expert is fused the same way: the experts own its weights and the model builds no shared MLP.
- `--prefix-match-unit` matters for this model independently of this PR: the KDA state page makes the KV block 8,960 tokens under DEP4, and without the flag prefix hits land on whole blocks.
- Limitations: `tensor_parallel_size=1` only; SM100 only; no sharded RDT or sparse NCCL updates. Under DEP4 each rank holds 8.8M KV tokens.

title: [Dependency] Upgrade FlashInfer to 0.7.1
author: wzhao18
body:
## Overview

Upgrade FlashInfer from `0.7.0.post1` to `0.7.1` for standard CUDA and Rubin builds. Explicitly select the CuTe DSL KDA prefill backend to avoid the inference-tensor crash observed in the B200 Kimi K3 CI job.

## Claims

- Update the shared `flashinfer-python` pin to `0.7.1`, retaining upstream's common `flashinfer download-kernels` installation flow for CUDA and Rubin.
- Keep KDA prefill on FlashInfer with inference mode enabled. No FlashInfer modifications, metadata copies, or test changes are required.

## Validation

On an allocated NVIDIA GB300 node with FlashInfer 0.7.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, and nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, using an isolated checkout and the existing environment:

- Reproduced all three original KDA failures before the fix; all three passed afterward (prefill correctness, near-collinear keys, and cross-stream breakable CUDA graph).
- `pytest -v tests/models/kimi_k3 --ignore=tests/models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py tests/kernels/attention/test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py` — **260 passed, 154 skipped**. This is the B200 Kimi K3 CI test selection, executed on GB300. Tests used the environment's `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files requirements/cuda.txt vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kda.py` — passed after rebasing.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

GPU tests were run before the final rebase; the rebase did not change Kimi implementation or test files. B200 execution, full model accuracy evaluations, and standard/Rubin container builds have not been performed for this revision. The earlier MI250 EAGLE3 acceptance failure remains unresolved and should be reassessed in CI; it is not established to be an existing main failure.

## Details

FlashInfer's automatic small-BH prefill path caches packed sequence metadata using `cu_seqlens._version`. Inference tensors have no version counter, so this raises before kernel launch. Explicit `backend="cute-dsl"` avoids that path without changing PyTorch inference mode.

This bypasses the small-BH optimization. GB300 CUPTI microbenchmarks (BF16, D128, bounded gate, cold L2, eager GPU timing; median of three blocks of 20 samples) measured:

| Heads / tokens | FlashKDA (us) | FlashInfer auto (us) | Explicit CuTe DSL (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 12 / 128 | 45.7 | 31.3 | 23.6 |
| 12 / 2,048 | 118.6 | 71.5 | 80.4 |
| 12 / 8,192 | 355.4 | 214.1 | 270.1 |
| 96 / 8,192 | 863.7 | 459.5 | 459.1 |

Auto was measured with ordinary metadata tensors to avoid the crash. Explicit CuTe DSL was faster than FlashKDA for these cases, but 12–26% slower than working auto selection for the two longer H12 cases. These are microbenchmarks, not end-to-end serving measurements. Output and final-state correctness were checked before timing.

Rebased onto upstream main `838526c7e5`. Upstream removed separate cubin/JIT-cache pins in favor of `flashinfer download-kernels`; this PR preserves that change. Rubin continues to use the shared FlashInfer pin.

The initial duplicate-work search found no other open PR implementing this version upgrade; this updates the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate. No associated issue. AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, investigation, and validation.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Serve and store OffloadingConnector partial tails with EAGLE/MTP groups
author: kimseunghyun-kr
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Problem.** With an EAGLE/MTP draft model and `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the native CPU `OffloadingConnector` never serves a partial tail. So every hit from the CPU tier stops at a scheduler-block boundary, and the tokens after it are computed again.

**Fix, in three parts:**
1. **Lookup:** look up the tail at the EAGLE proof position, as Mooncake does since #60695.
2. **Store:** fix the store gate. Before, it always skipped the one step that can store the tail.
3. **Store policy:** store an EAGLE tail only for a request that loaded from the CPU tier. Without this, parts 1 and 2 double the GPU → CPU traffic, and serving gets slower (P95 TTFT 13 % higher without it in a same-day control, see Validation).

**Result** (8 × A100, MLPerf agentic, 3 × 60 min per arm): no serving regression; SLO pass 92.42 % against 91.70 % without this PR. The CPU-tier hits now end at partial tails, as designed.

Related: #60533 (core proof), #52832 (producer partial tails), #54165 (a different bug in the same file).

## Claims

- With an EAGLE group and align Mamba, a CPU-tier hit can now end at `prefix_match_unit` granularity, as a GPU prefix-cache hit already does. Before, it ended at a whole scheduler block, minus one more block for the EAGLE pop.
- The EAGLE group's tail is keyed at `boundary + eagle_proof_margin`, the same proof that core uses since #60533. Mamba groups and non-EAGLE groups stay keyed at the boundary.
- The tail is stored on the step that computes the proof.
- With an EAGLE group, only a request that loaded from the CPU tier stores its partial tail.
- No change without an EAGLE group, or where partial tails are not supported (DCP > 1, `blocks_per_chunk > 1`, mixed block sizes, sliding-window groups). No new config option.

## Validation

### Serving A/B

**Setup.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (36 GDN + 12 full-attention layers + 1 MTP layer), TP8 + EP on 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, MTP 3, scheduler block 800 tokens, `prefix_match_unit` 16, `--kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 256`. MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm, same node type.

**SLO** (Artificial Analysis percentile convention): **P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s** and **P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms** (that is, P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" below is the share of requests that meet both limits. The SLO holds when SLO pass ≥ 95 %.

| Arm | SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | Mean | Goodput | CPU → GPU load (whole run) | GPU prefix hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 92.01 / 90.92 / 92.18 % | 91.70 % | 1.866 req/s | — | — |
| Parts 1 + 2 only (tail stored on every turn) | 85.2 / 87.3 / 87.2 % | 86.6 % | 1.67–1.72 req/s | 19.9 TB | 79.0 % |
| **This PR** (parts 1 + 2 + 3) | 93.49 / 91.93 / 91.84 % | **92.42 %** | **1.922 req/s** | **16.0 TB** | **85.2 %** |

The gain of this PR over "without" (+0.7 points, +3 % goodput) is within about two repeat spreads. So I claim no regression, not a speed-up. The "This PR" arm ran a backport on vLLM 81198e97 with the store policy behind an opt-in flag. On this model every partial tail is an EAGLE tail, so that flag gives the same rule as this PR's default.

**Same-day control (15 Oct, one node, 1 × 60 min per arm, same setup).** The "parts 1 + 2 only" arm above ran on another day; on the same day and node as this PR the gap is smaller:

| Store rule | GPU → CPU store per request | Requests done | Output tok/s per GPU | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parts 1 + 2 only (no store gate) | 247 MB | 7,450 | 111.7 | 949 / 2,297 ms | 14.07 / 23.41 ms |
| Store gate `num_locally_computed_tokens >= boundary` (review suggestion) | 247 MB | 7,490 | 111.6 | 935 / 2,203 ms | 14.16 / 23.07 ms |
| **This PR** (store only after a load from the CPU tier) | **126 MB** | **7,721** | **113.6** | 924 / **2,025 ms** | **13.69 / 22.56 ms** |

Part 3 halves the stores and, against no gate, lowers P95 TTFT by 12 % and P95 TPOT by 4 % (one run per arm). The "−5 points" of the 3 × 60 table is not reproduced on a single day; treat it as an upper bound. The review-suggested gate rarely applies here: the stored tail is past the request's GPU prefix hit.

<details>
<summary>Why parts 1 + 2 alone are slower (earlier A/B)</summary>

| Measure | Without this PR | Parts 1 + 2 only |
|---|---|---|
| CPU-tier hit tokens mod 800 | 0 in all snapshots | not 0 (e.g. 224): partial tails are served |
| SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | 90.0 / 89.2 / 89.5 % | 75.1 / 79.3 / 79.9 % |
| Goodput | 1.83–1.89 req/s | 1.31–1.43 req/s |
| P95 / P99 TTFT | 2.22–2.35 / 3.13–3.58 s | 2.94–4.18 / 5.5–13.9 s |
| P50 / P95 TPOT | 14.1–14.3 / 23.9–24.5 ms | 15.7–16.4 / 29.0–34.0 ms |
| MTP mean acceptance length | 2.676 | 2.676 |
| GPU → CPU store bytes / time | 3.00 TB / 3,814 s | 6.93 TB / 8,196 s |
| Scheduler lookup time (sum) | 1.3 s | 8.4 s |

The tails work: they are stored, found and loaded, and the drafter is unchanged. But each turn stores one new tail block (800 tokens, about 6 MB) in every KV group. Most requests hit the GPU prefix cache on the next turn, so most of these stores are never read. Tail stores were 18,650 (about one per request) and 64.5 % of the 6.93 TB stored. Part 3 removes these stores.

How the bug was found: without this PR, `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` was an exact multiple of 800 in all 17 snapshots of two 3-hour runs (example: 402,580,800 = 503,226 × 800). With part 1 only, it was still a multiple of 800. That pointed to the store gate.

</details>

### Unit tests

All in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`:

| What | Tests |
|---|---|
| Proof key: store and lookup | `test_eagle_proof_margin_follows_core_hit_alignment`, `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_keys_attention_at_proof`, `test_eagle_partial_lookup_loads_attention_proof` |
| Store gate (part 2): round trip | `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True]`: fails with part 1 only, passes with part 2 |
| Store only when the proof is in the prompt | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_proof_in_prompt` (5 cases) |
| Popped chunk looked up once | `test_eagle_partial_lookup_probes_popped_chunk_once` (6 lookups instead of 7; 7 instead of 9) |
| Store policy (part 3) | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_offload_load` ([False] and [True] cases) |

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| A100 (CUDA), nightly 5555a2d8 image, whole `offloading_connector/` | 589 passed, 0 failed. With #61375 also applied: 590 passed. |
| macOS (CPU, `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`), whole `offloading_connector/`, 21 Oct, head 321cd8672 | 603 passed, 2 skipped. Split branches: parts 1 + 2 601 passed; with part 3 603 passed. |
| `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0) | clean |

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
```

This PR and #61375 (a different bug in `offloading/scheduler.py`) merge without conflicts.

## Details

**Root cause 1: lookup.** `SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec` set `supports_partial_tail = False` when any group was an EAGLE group. For an EAGLE group, the complete-chunk lookup asks for one extra chunk and then drops it. So the hit ended one scheduler block before the last stored chunk, and no partial tail was tried.

**Root cause 2: store gate.**
1. With EAGLE block drop, core stops the prefill at the Mamba checkpoint T = floor(P/h)·h − h.
2. On the next step (tokens T..P), the state is copied (CoW), and the manager hands `(group, cow_block, T)` to the connector one time.
3. The scheduler builds the connector metadata before `_update_after_schedule`, so `num_computed_tokens == T` at that point.
4. So the gate `boundary + margin > num_computed_tokens` reads `T + h > T`. This is always true, so the store is always skipped, and the hand-off does not come again.

**Changes.**
- Remove the EAGLE exclusion from `supports_partial_tail`.
- Key the EAGLE non-recurrent groups at `boundary + margin` in store, lookup and load.
- Margin rule as in core: one hash unit if `cache_hit_alignment_tokens` < block and the group manager supports fine-grained lookup; else one block.
- Widen the partial search by one block, with bridge keys for the dropped chunk. That chunk is looked up once per lookup; a miss skips that block.
- Check the proof against `min(num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens[req_id], num_prompt_tokens)`. The cap keeps the proof out of speculative tokens.
- With an EAGLE group, store a partial tail only if `update_state_after_alloc` scheduled a CPU-tier load for this request (`RequestOffloadState.loaded_from_offload`). Complete chunks and aligned boundary states are stored as before.

**Why the proof-step store is safe.** Stores are only queued in `wait_for_save` and are sent at the start of the next step. The CPU transfer stream waits on the compute stream at that point, so the copy runs after this step's forward wrote the proof block.

**Difference from #60695.** Mooncake stores one key per hash unit. The native connector stores whole chunks and keeps its chunk-level EAGLE drop for complete chunks. So only the partial-tail key of EAGLE groups changes.

**Limitations.**
- If the hand-off step stops before `T + h`, the tail is not stored. I ran core's chunk-split code on 20,000 prompts (1k–200k tokens) per configuration. No hand-off was lost when block ≤ `max_num_batched_tokens` with EAGLE or single-module MTP. Losses occur only with multi-module MTP (0.2–0.45 %) or with a block larger than the token budget (≤ 1.7 %). A fix would need core to keep the CoW block across steps; not done.
- The store policy is a heuristic. A request served only from the GPU prefix cache stores no EAGLE tail. If the GPU later evicts that prefix, the next turn's CPU-tier hit ends at the last complete chunk. That turn then loads from the CPU tier and stores its tail, so the turn after it can get a partial hit. Measured on one workload only.
- When the dropped chunk is present, the search covers two blocks. This applies only with an EAGLE group.
- Existing CPU caches hold no EAGLE tails, so no migration is needed.

**Size:** `offloading/scheduler.py` +161 / −32 (no core files changed); tests +400 / −1. Part 3 alone is 7 lines (`RequestOffloadState.loaded_from_offload`, set in `update_state_after_alloc`, checked in `_build_partial_tail_store_jobs`) and 57 test lines.

**Why part 3 stays in this PR.** Without it, parts 1 + 2 make serving slower in the A/B above (SLO pass 86.6 % against 91.7 % without this PR; same-day P95 TTFT 2,297 against 2,025 ms). A split would land that regression until the second PR merges. Extra stores cost latency, not only bandwidth: on A100 the copy engine serves GPU → host copies of different streams in order. A 4 KB copy on its own stream takes 0.04 ms; with a 32 MB or 128 MB store queued on another stream (one copy or `swap_blocks_batch`), it waits 1.3 or 5.1 ms (1 × A100-SXM4-40GB, test script on request). MRV2 copies the sampled tokens to the host in this way, so each queued store byte can delay the step output. The split is ready if a reviewer prefers it: branches `offload-eagle-keying-only` (parts 1 + 2) and `offload-eagle-store-gate-split` (part 3) on my fork.

title: [MoE] Shape-based padding for FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 experts (gated and non-gated)
author: jhaotingc
body:
## Overview

The FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE kernel needs `intermediate % 128 == 0` and `hidden % 256 == 0`; otherwise it fails with `No valid config found`. This PR pads MXFP8 experts by shape on that backend, for gated and non-gated experts alike, so MXFP8-MoE checkpoints with misaligned expert sizes can run.

## Claims

- MXFP8 MoE layers with misaligned intermediate or hidden sizes now run on `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`, gated or not.
- Aligned models are unchanged: no copy and no runtime padding.
- A W4A4 checkpoint with an MXFP8 MoE that this enables reaches **1.71×** the output tok/s/GPU of the BF16 model on GB300 at concurrency 64.

## Validation

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k mxfp8` gives 14 passed on B200. That is the new test (gated SiLU and non-gated ReLU², aligned and misaligned shapes such as 1856×2688, against `fused_experts` on the dequantized weights) plus the 4 existing MXFP8 TRT-LLM tests.

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"moe_backend":"flashinfer_trtllm"}' \
  --mamba-cache-mode none --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 --use-replayssm \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":32768}'
```

- Accuracy (GB300): GPQA-diamond through NeMo Gym on 1x GB300, TP1, MTP=2 (198 questions x 8 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), served as above plus
  `--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3`. pass@1 (mean over the 8 repeats ±
  standard error) is 76.45 ± 0.70% without prefix reuse and 76.58 ± 0.45% with prefix reuse
  (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, no ReplaySSM).
- Perf (GB300, TP1, speed-bench 1k prompts / OSL 200, no spec decode, same serve flags otherwise, concurrency 64): the W4A4 + MXFP8-MoE checkpoint reaches **9,640 output tok/s/GPU** (189.6 tok/s/user) vs BF16 5,648 (101.2), i.e. 1.71× throughput and 1.87× per user.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy.

## Details

- New `align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm`, next to `align_moe_weights_for_fi`:
  - It reuses `align_moe_weights_for_fi` for the intermediate size, padding gate and up halves separately.
  - It pads the hidden size with zero weights, and pads the UE8M0 scales the same way with 127 (scale 1.0).
- `prepare_fp8_moe_layer_for_fi` calls it on the MXFP8 TRT-LLM path and sets `intermediate_size_per_partition` and `hidden_dim` at the call site. The MoE runner then pads the activations to the padded hidden size and crops the output.
- The test uses `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`. `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`) never passes `activation_type`, so it always runs the kernel gated.

title: [Perf] per_token_group_quant_8bit: multiply by reciprocal instead of dividing per element
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Speed up FP8 per-token-group quantization by computing the per-group scale reciprocal once and multiplying, instead of dividing per element. This covers both CUDA group-quant kernels: `per_token_group_quant_8bit` (smem and register-resident schedules) and the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`), so that all CUDA fp8 group-quant paths share the same reciprocal-multiply numerics. ~1.2-1.3x kernel speedup on GB300 across M=1..32768; ~1-2% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (TP4).

## Claims

- 1.15-1.29x faster `per_token_group_fp8_quant` CUDA kernel on GB300 across M=1..32768 (details below).
- All CUDA fp8 group-quant paths (unfused kernel, fused RMSNorm+quant kernel, Triton fallback, UE8M0 path) now use the same reciprocal-multiply numerics; previously the fused and unfused kernels could disagree by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements.
- ~0.6-2.0% e2e TPOT improvement on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, at concurrency 1-64.
- Accuracy-neutral: GSM8K / GPQA-Diamond deltas within noise (details below).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_per_token_group_quant.py`: 848 passed, including `test_per_token_group_quant_fp8_register_matches_smem` (bitwise register-vs-smem equality; both schedules are changed identically, so the invariant is preserved).
- Scale outputs are bit-identical to main; quantized values can differ by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (randn data) when a quotient lands within 1 fp32 ulp of an fp8 rounding boundary.

### Microbenchmarks

GB300, K=4096, group=128, bf16 -> fp8e4m3 + fp32 scales. FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graph and cold L2; median of interleaved rounds. Both columns are standalone same-toolchain builds (nvcc 13.1) of the register-resident kernel; repro harness: `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_per_token_group_quant.py`.

| M | main (us) | this PR (us) | speedup | achieved BW (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 2.30 | 1.92 | 1.20x | 6 GB/s |
| 4 | 2.34 | 1.92 | 1.22x | 26 GB/s |
| 16 | 2.56 | 2.14 | 1.20x | 93 GB/s |
| 64 | 2.69 | 2.27 | 1.19x | 350 GB/s |
| 256 | 3.20 | 2.78 | 1.15x | 1.14 TB/s |
| 1024 | 6.14 | 5.02 | 1.22x | 2.53 TB/s |
| 4096 | 15.23 | 12.19 | 1.25x | 4.17 TB/s |
| 16384 | 52.35 | 41.09 | 1.27x | 4.95 TB/s |
| 32768 | 101.25 | 78.34 | 1.29x | 5.19 TB/s |

The kernel is memory-bound (~2 FLOPs/element; TFLOPS is not the meaningful metric here). This PR lifts achieved bandwidth from 4.0 to 5.2 TB/s at M=32768. A flat-index Triton variant we prototyped reaches 6.7 TB/s at M=32768 but loses at small M; modifying the existing CUDA kernel is the lower-risk change.

### E2E perf

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, 8k input / 1k output, vllm bench serve; median TPOT. main (`c077dc663d`) and the branch (`1aca0a263f`) ran sequentially on the same GB300 node:

| Concurrency | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.27 | 6.23 | -0.6% |
| 4 | 8.30 | 8.14 | -1.9% |
| 16 | 12.06 | 11.82 | -2.0% |
| 64 | 24.98 | 24.67 | -1.2% |

Request throughput +1.2% at concurrency 64. Note: the e2e delta includes a toolchain effect (branch built from source with local nvcc 13.1; baseline is the nvcc 13.0 wheel, whose stock quant kernel is mis-scheduled -- see Details), so it mildly overstates the pure source-change effect. The same-toolchain kernel numbers above are the honest claim.

### Accuracy

Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP4, identical server flags on the same GB300 node:

| Task | main | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K flexible-extract (n=1319) | 0.8211 | 0.8112 | -0.99pp |
| GSM8K strict-match (n=1319) | 0.8158 | 0.7991 | -1.67pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (n=198) | 0.8586 | 0.8687 | +1.01pp |

Mixed and within noise (binomial std error ~1.06pp per arm at n=1319), but GSM8K drifts down directionally; consistent with the ~0.05% of elements whose fp8 rounding flips under reciprocal-multiply.

## Details

- Root cause: `div.rn.f32` is a multi-instruction slow sequence, and the kernel issued it once per *element* when one division per *group* suffices. The kernel's own UE8M0 path already uses reciprocal-multiply (a power-of-two scale makes the reciprocal exact); this PR applies the same transform to the fp32-scale path.
- The per-element division was inherited from the SGLang kernel this file was ported from (#21083); the register-resident path (#55330) kept it so the new schedule stayed bit-exact with the smem one. That invariant is a test convenience, not an accuracy requirement, and is preserved by changing both schedules identically.
- Numerics: this is the same rcp-mul numerics class already shipped by this kernel's UE8M0 path, vLLM's Triton fallback (`_per_token_group_quant_fp8`), and SGLang's production quant kernel.
- Scope: no Python/dispatch changes. The file is also hipified into ROCm builds; the change uses only portable float ops, so ROCm gets the same numerics (not separately benchmarked there).
- Related work: #60903 adds a separate Triton row kernel for prefill-sized inputs (large M only); this PR instead speeds up the existing CUDA kernel at all M and is complementary. No open PR duplicates this change.
- Consistency: the fused RMSNorm+group-quant kernel (`layernorm_utils.cuh`, the target of `RMSNormQuantFusionPass` for block-FP8 models, on both CUDA and ROCm via hipify) is switched to the same reciprocal-multiply. Without this, fused and unfused paths diverge by 1 fp8 ulp on ~0.05% of elements (caught by `test_fused_quant_layernorm` and `test_mamba_prefix_cache`). The fused kernel also drops 4 div.rn per vec4. Per-token fp8 keeps exact per-element division for FBGemm parity; int8 paths are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Toolchain note: nvcc 13.0 x sm_100 mis-schedules the stock kernel</summary>

All official artifacts (release pipeline nvcc 13.0.2, Dockerfile CUDA_VERSION=13.0.3) target `... 10.0 ...` (no sm_103). nvcc 13.0 targeting sm_100 mis-schedules this kernel's div.rn slow paths: 864 instructions / 3095 static stall cycles vs 568 / 1655 under nvcc 13.1; the shipped wheel runs the stock kernel at 167.6us vs 101.2us for a 13.1 rebuild at M=32768 (sm_100 SASS loads natively on sm_103; verified with CUDA_DISABLE_PTX_JIT=1). This PR's variant is insensitive to the compiler (78.3us on nvcc 13.0 vs 78.1us on 13.1) because it removes the per-element div.rn entirely. Worth a separate build-toolchain discussion; out of scope here.
</details>

title: [Perf] Tune Triton GDN decode tiles on SM100-family GPUs
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Tune the existing Triton packed GDN decode launch on SM100-family GPUs. Smaller value tiles improve utilization at small batches and reduce per-CTA work with FP32 recurrent state.

## Claims

- **1.34–1.74× faster kernel** at B=1–64 for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next TP4 layout with FP32 state on GB300; **1.21–1.34×** at B=1/2/4 with BF16 state.
- **1.0–2.2% higher output throughput** in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 serving, with unchanged full GSM8K and C=8 check scores.
- A 12-line dispatch change; existing kernel math and interfaces are preserved. FlashInfer is benchmarked as a comparison candidate only and is **not integrated by this PR**.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

GB300 (152 SMs), BF16 QKV, `(H, HV)=(4, 12)`, `K=V=128`, Q/K normalization enabled. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. CUPTI kernel time with CUDA graphs and cold L2; medians of seven shuffled rounds, 40 samples per call. Main uses BV32; PR uses the tile selected by the heuristic.

**FlashInfer is an ideal-input comparison:** `gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(backend="flashinfer")` with contiguous Q/K/V prepared outside the timed call. These numbers exclude layout-conversion/copy costs and do not represent an integrated vLLM serving path. The E2E results below compare main against tuned Triton only.

**FP32 recurrent state**

| Batch | Main (µs) | PR (µs) | Speedup | FlashInfer, not integrated (µs) |

| 2 | 5.60 | 3.30 | 1.70× | 4.43 |

| 64 | 24.21 | 18.06 | 1.34× | 19.54 |

**BF16 recurrent state**

| 32 | 8.19 | 8.19 | 1.00× | 9.09 |
| 64 | 14.14 | 14.14 | 1.00× | 12.72 |

For BF16 state at B≥8, the PR selects unchanged BV32; the main and PR columns therefore use the same measured launch.

Triton output and recurrent state matched the baseline bit-for-bit in these checks. FlashInfer is not bit-identical: output checks used `atol=rtol=1e-3`; FP32-state checks used `atol=rtol=1e-5`, while BF16-state checks required `atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-2` after ten recurrent updates. No FlashInfer model-accuracy claim is made.

<details>

GB300, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next local head layouts `(H, HV)`, BF16 activations and FP32 state. Speedup is main / PR kernel time; median of five shuffled rounds with 40 CUPTI samples each. Eager execution and ten recurrent CUDA-graph updates matched bit-for-bit.

| Batch | TP1 (16, 48) | TP2 (8, 24) | TP4 (4, 12) | TP8 (2, 6) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.56× | 1.69× | 1.80× | 1.87× |
| 2 | 1.40× | 1.57× | 1.74× | 1.77× |
| 4 | 1.38× | 1.36× | 1.62× | 1.75× |
| 8 | 1.41× | 1.41× | 1.37× | 1.63× |
| 16 | 1.33× | 1.40× | 1.39× | 1.47× |
| 32 | 1.19× | 1.30× | 1.40× | 1.36× |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark reproduction</summary>

Run from the feature checkout in an installed CUDA development venv with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and `cupti-python`. The script loads the baseline kernel from upstream commit `28d679e762`, uses the checkout's PR dispatch, and prepares the FlashInfer inputs before timing. Save as `bench_gdn.py` and run `.venv/bin/python bench_gdn.py`.

```python

    fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode as tuned,

    generator = torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(1234)
    order_rng = random.Random(1234)
    for state_dtype in [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16]:

            ids = torch.arange(1, batch + 1, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
            initial = torch.randn(batch + 1, 12, 128, 128, device='cuda',

            # FlashInfer ideal case: Q/K/V layout conversion is outside timing.

            k = mixed[:, 512:1024].view(batch, 1, 4, 128).contiguous()
            v = mixed[:, 1024:].view(batch, 1, 12, 128).contiguous()
            states = {name: initial.clone() for name in ['main', 'PR', 'FI']}
            outputs = {name: torch.empty(batch, 1, 12, 128, device='cuda',
```
