title: [Kernel][Perf] Add H100 tuned configs for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B to the batch-invariant matmul table
author: Monishver11
body:
## Overview

In short: in batch-invariant (BI) mode (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`), every bf16 linear layer and the lm_head run the Triton kernel `matmul_kernel_persistent` instead of cuBLAS. Its tile comes from a per-GPU table, and the Hopper table only has the five Qwen3-1.7B shapes (measured on an H20), so Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B run the default 128x128x64 tile on H100. This PR adds H100-measured entries for their 8 TP=1 shapes to the `"hopper"` family.

With BI on, on an H100 SXM:
- `vllm bench latency` is 1.85-2.79x faster than main.
- The BI tax (latency with BI on / latency with BI off) drops from 2.13-2.99x on main to 1.03-1.20x with this PR.
- GSM8K stays within 0.5 standard error (SE) of main.

Related: tracker [#27433](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/27433), same kind of table as [#53247](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53247), [#57456](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57456), [#58495](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58495).

## Key results

- 8 new `(N, K)` entries in `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS["hopper"]`: gate_up/down/lm_head of Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B plus their shared qkv/o. Existing entries and other families are not touched.
- One `BLOCK_K` per shape, so a row's K-reduction order does not depend on M. Checked bit for bit through the real `matmul_persistent` dispatch: 2028/2028 cases identical.
- Kernel (H100 SXM, cold L2): geomean 2.03x vs main over 80 (shape, M) cases, 2.89x at M <= 64; the slowest case is 1.00x (Qwen3 gate_up at M=2048, 827 vs 828 us). At M <= 64 the kernel is now 0.90-1.12x of cuBLAS time (main: 1.48-4.09x).
- E2E latency with the flag on (fresh process per run, 2 interleaved rounds):

| model, workload | BI=0 (s) | BI=1 main (s) | BI=1 this PR (s) | PR vs main | BI tax main -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B, 32 in / 128 out, bs 8 | 0.854 | 2.452 | 0.881 | 2.78x | 2.87x -> 1.03x |
| Llama-3.1-8B, 1024 in / 32 out, bs 8 | 0.403 | 0.859 | 0.444 | 1.94x | 2.13x -> 1.10x |
| Qwen3-8B, 32 in / 128 out, bs 8 | 0.893 | 2.668 | 0.956 | 2.79x | 2.99x -> 1.07x |
| Qwen3-8B, 1024 in / 32 out, bs 8 | 0.414 | 0.917 | 0.495 | 1.85x | 2.22x -> 1.20x |

- `vllm bench serve` (1024 in / 128 out, 1000 prompts, rate inf, 3 interleaved rounds, req/s; rounds 1 / 2 / 3, then the mean). Llama-3.1-8B gains 13.6%. Qwen3-8B does not change; Details explains why (the execution mode these shapes switch on, not the tiles).

| model | BI=0 | BI=1 main | BI=1 this PR | PR vs main | throughput tax main -> PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 28.29 / 28.35 / 28.32, 28.32 | 21.62 / 21.69 / 21.61, 21.64 | 24.71 / 24.57 / 24.48, 24.59 | +13.6% | 1.31x -> 1.15x |
| Qwen3-8B | 27.43 / 27.47 / 27.54, 27.48 | 21.45 / 21.48 / 21.51, 21.48 | 21.50 / 21.48 / 21.47, 21.48 | 0.0% | 1.28x -> 1.28x |

- GSM8K (5-shot, BI=1): every difference to main is within 0.5 SE.

| model | main strict / flexible | this PR strict / flexible |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B | 0.7180 ± 0.0124 / 0.7832 ± 0.0114 | 0.7119 ± 0.0125 / 0.7839 ± 0.0113 |
| Qwen3-8B | 0.8764 ± 0.0091 / 0.8779 ± 0.0090 | 0.8741 ± 0.0091 / 0.8757 ± 0.0091 |

The raw output for every row of these tables is under Validation.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GPU: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 SXM, 132 SMs, power limit 700 W of 700 W.
- Software: driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, triton 3.8.0.
- main = 307c5844ad. PR = main + this commit, applied on the box with `git am` (same diff).
- main and PR are the same checkout, switched with `git checkout`. Every run is a fresh process.
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct checkpoint: `unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`, an ungated copy. It has the same architecture and layer shapes as `meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`; its config.json adds `pad_token_id`. I did not compare the weights against the gated repo.
- [#61118](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61118) merged after this base. It enables Inductor's `batch_invariant` flag. It can only change the torch.compile arms (main, and PR + torch.compile under Details). It does not change this PR's default breakable-graph mode, because that mode does not run Inductor.

**Bitwise.**
- Path: `matmul_persistent` on the PR tree, all 13 hopper shapes.
- Check: a probe row at rows 0, M/2 and M-1 must equal the same row computed at M=1.
- M values (39): 1-17, every bucket edge ±1, 100, 1000, 3000 and 4096.
- 2 seeds. Weight as `w.t()` (the linear layout) and as a contiguous `(K, N)` tensor.
- Result: 2028/2028 identical, 0 mismatched.

**Tests** (PR tree):

```
pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_matmul_batch_invariant.py                                  # 35 passed, 2 skipped
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3-8B pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py            # 22 passed
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pytest -v tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py  # 22 passed
```

**Kernel**, `matmul_persistent` main -> PR, us per call.
- Each point is a CUDA graph of 4-24 launches. The script aims for about 2 ms of work per replay (4 to 20 launches), rounded up to whole cycles of the weight copies.
- The launches cycle over enough weight copies to read >= 4x L2 per pass.
- main is the mean of two runs, one before and one after the PR run. The two runs agree within 0.98-1.08x.

| layer (N, K) | M=1 | M=8 | M=64 | M=256 | M=2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| o, both (4096, 4096) | 69 -> 18 (3.77x) | 63 -> 16 (4.01x) | 48 -> 16 (3.04x) | 34 -> 19 (1.76x) | 135 -> 125 (1.08x) |

| Qwen3 lm_head (151936, 4096) | 936 -> 407 (2.30x) | 907 -> 411 (2.21x) | 673 -> 425 (1.59x) | 727 -> 624 (1.17x) | 4773 -> 4574 (1.04x) |

All 10 buckets per shape, with both main runs and the PR config, are in `kernel/report_mean_main_vs_pr.md` in the attached logs.

**Latency** (`vllm bench latency`):
- 2 rounds per arm. Every run is a fresh process. Arms are interleaved per round.
- Arms: BI off = `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0` on main; main and this PR = `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on that tree.

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm bench latency --model unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --max-model-len 2048 --input-len 32 --output-len 128 --batch-size 8 --num-iters-warmup 10 --num-iters 30

```

The raw output of all 24 runs is in the four "Raw output: vllm bench latency" dropdowns at the end of this section.

**Serve** (`vllm bench serve`):
- 3 rounds per arm, with a fresh server for every run. Arms are interleaved per round.
- Each server first gets a 64-prompt warmup run, which is not measured.

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 2048 --port 8000
# warmup (not measured)
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model <model> --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 --num-prompts 64 --request-rate inf --seed 1
```

- The raw output of all 18 runs is in the two "Raw output: vllm bench serve" dropdowns at the end of this section.
- Llama-3.1-8B, main -> PR: mean TPOT 116.4 -> 103.2 ms (BI off: 88.4 ms), mean TTFT 20.41 -> 18.12 s.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Align speculator hidden norm in GLM-4.5/4.6 MoE and GLM-OCR MTP with GLM5Next to recycle post-final-hidden.
author: spandantiwari
body:
### Overview

Three GLM-family MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) models — `glm4_moe_mtp.py` (GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.5-Air / GLM-4.6), `glm4_moe_lite_mtp.py` (GLM-4.7-Flash), and `glm_ocr_mtp.py` (GLM-OCR) — return the **pre-final-norm** hidden from the MTP layer, so the speculator recycles a hidden that is one RMSNorm short into the next draft step's `hnorm`. The established GLM/DeepSeek-NextN contract (already merged in vLLM by #47448 and also SGLang's `glm4_moe_nextn`/`deepseek_nextn` `vllm/models/glm5next/common/mtp.py`) recycles the **post-final-norm** hidden. This PR extends that contract to the three models it missed, and registers them in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.model_returns_tuple()` so Model Runner V1 unpacks the new tuple return. Draft-only change; verified output is unaffected.

**Relation to #62986:** #62986 (opened after this PR) fixes the same recycle for `Glm4MoeMTP` only, DeepSeek-style; its description offers to close in favour of this PR once the V1 registration is included, which it now is (`6ecfab6`). #62987 (enabling `torch.compile` for `Glm4MoeMTP`) is independent.

### Claims

- **Correctness/contract alignment:** each MTP layer now applies the final norm once (fused `shared_head.norm(hidden, residual)`) and returns the post-final-norm hidden for both tuple positions, with `compute_logits` consuming it directly — identical to #47448 and `glm5next`.
- **Both model runners:** Model Runner V2 unpacks tuple returns generically; Model Runner V1 (`SpecDecodeBaseProposer`) only unpacks registered architectures, so `Glm4MoeMTPModel`, `Glm4MoeLiteMTPModel` and `GlmOcrMTPModel` are added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Without that, V1 crashes on the first draft step (below).
- **Lossless:** speculative decoding verifies every drafted token, so the target-visible output is unchanged; only the drafter's recycled state changes (affects draft steps ≥1, i.e. `num_speculative_tokens ≥ 2`).
- **No performance regression, and no performance claim.** On a real checkpoint (GLM-4.5-Air) a controlled, paired acceptance measurement shows **no statistically significant change** in draft acceptance (details below).

### Validation

**Drafter contract (unit, real objects):** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden`, parametrized over GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-OCR configs (shrunk). Each drafter is built by `get_model` with `load_format="dummy"` and runs its real forward. The feedback hidden must equal `shared_head.norm` of the MTP block output (captured with a forward hook), which is also what `compute_logits` used to feed the `lm_head`, so logits are unchanged.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py -k feeds_back_final_normed
# model files from the PR base (49f944be3e): 3 failed
E       AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
E       Mismatched elements: 1536 / 1536 (100.0%)
# this PR: 3 passed
```

**Both model runners (e2e through `LLM`, real weights):** `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1|mrv2]` runs `zai-org/GLM-OCR` with `num_speculative_tokens=2` and asserts both draft positions are accepted. Per-position acceptance on MI355X: MRV2 `[0.610, 0.285]`, MRV1 `[0.592, 0.271]`.

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py
# first commit of this PR (c10a4c9: tuple return, no V1 registration), [mrv1]:
TypeError: only integer tensors of a single element can be converted to an index
FAILED ...::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners[mrv1] - EngineDeadError
# this PR: 2 passed
```

The registration itself is also covered by `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (CPU CI), extended with the three architectures. The new e2e directory runs in the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo (+ GLM)" step. `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` and `test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py`: 13 passed; `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean.

**Test durations** (`pytest --durations=0`, single MI355X; checkpoints already cached):

| test | cases | time per case |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_feeds_back_final_normed_hidden` (new) | 3 | 1.1–4.9 s (GLM-4.5-Air 4.9 s, GLM-OCR 1.4 s, GLM-4.7-Flash 1.1 s) |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/glm/test_mtp.py::test_glm_mtp_drafts_on_both_model_runners` (new) | 2 | 52 s (MRV1), 94 s (MRV2, incl. `torch.compile` + CUDA-graph capture) |
| `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer_sampling.py::test_mtp_model_returns_tuple` (3 cases added, CPU) | 3 | < 0.5 s |

The e2e test adds about 2.5 min to the "Spec Decode MTP DeepSeek + MiMo + GLM" step (first run also downloads `zai-org/GLM-OCR`, 2.7 GB).

**Acceptance measurement (end-to-end, fixed-prefix)** — GLM-4.5-Air (bf16), MI355X, `method=mtp`, k=3, 600 gsm8k prompts, each generating one spec-decode round from a **fixed starting prefix**, paired per prompt. Position 0 does not consume the recycled hidden, so it is a near-control (not bit-exact — see below):

| position | before (pre-norm) | after (post-norm) | diff | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| p0 (near-control) | 0.7330 | 0.7298 | −0.0032 | 0.88 |
| p1 | 0.5438 | 0.5479 | +0.0042 | 0.86 |
| p2 | 0.2232 | 0.2277 | +0.0045 | 0.82 |

Paired per-prompt accepted tokens: +0.018 ± 0.016 (Wilcoxon p=0.25). The position-0 result is **statistically consistent with no change** (p=0.88); its tiny drift is floating-point from the eager→fused add+norm (mathematically identical). No affected position shows a significant change either. This is an end-to-end comparison from fixed prefixes; it does not isolate each later position's conditional acceptance, since draft histories can still diverge within a round. Net: acceptance (and thus speed) is effectively unaffected.

**Reference** — SGLang `glm4_moe_nextn.py` / `deepseek_nextn.py` apply the final norm and recycle the post-norm hidden; GLM-4-MoE NextN is a faithful DeepSeek-V3 NextN clone.

### Details

Root cause: the MTP layer forward ended with `hidden_states = residual + hidden_states; return hidden_states` (pre-final-norm), and `compute_logits` applied `shared_head` to it. The speculators store the model's returned hidden as the next step's `previous_hidden_states` (fed into `hnorm`), so the recycled state was missing the final `shared_head` RMSNorm that DeepSeek/`glm5next` apply; the logits path was always correctly single-normed. Fix (per file):

```python
hidden_states, _ = self.shared_head.norm(hidden_states, residual=residual)
return hidden_states, hidden_states
```

plus `compute_logits`: `shared_head.head, hidden_states` (drop the second norm), and the three architectures added to `model_returns_tuple()`. Affects the single-module AR path (`num_nextn_predict_layers=1`, k≥2 — the common GLM-4.5/4.6 case) and the multi-module path; k=1 is unaffected.

The two tuple elements are intentionally the same post-norm tensor, as in #47448 and `glm5next`, which go through the same recycle sites: the MRV2 AR step-0 setup stores `last_hidden_states[idx]`, MRV2 steps ≥1 and the multi-module path recycle the second element, and V1 unpacks the tuple once the architecture is registered.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, the sparse-indexer prefill path still upcasts DeepGEMM's BF16 MQA logits to FP32 and ranks them with `top_k_per_row_prefill`. This PR ranks the BF16 logits with DeepSelect directly, as decode already does since #56464.

## Claims

- On SM100 with `deep_select`, each indexer prefill chunk drops the FP32 upcast (`as_fp32_logits`) and its top-k gets 3.7x faster.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DEP2 on GB200, 8 requests per rank of 4,096 new tokens on a 128K prefix hit: 429.8 -> 401.5 ms per step (-6.6%), indexer 64.5 -> 30.9 ms.
- The selected top-k values are unchanged: BF16 widens to FP32 exactly. Which index wins among exactly equal logits was already unspecified (see #56749).
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K strict-match 0.924 / 0.923 over two runs and passkey retrieval 20/20 at ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (DEP4 on GB200).
- Default behavior is unchanged: only `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'` takes the new path. DCP, XPU, other top-k backends and logits whose row stride DeepSelect cannot read keep the FP32 path.

## Validation

Top-k alone, one GB200, CUPTI, cold L2, median of 3 rounds. Rows of one query chunk over 65,536 compressed keys (a 128K V4.1 request) with causal row ends, top-k 512, random BF16 logits. Base is `as_fp32_logits` + `top_k_per_row_prefill`, new is `deep_select_topk(..., end=row_ends)`:

| rows | base (us) | new (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 66.5 | 13.6 | 4.9x |
| 2048 | 414.4 | 110.1 | 3.8x |
| 4096 | 777.2 | 210.0 | 3.7x |
| 8192 | 1503.9 | 410.7 | 3.7x |

On every row both select exactly the values `torch.topk` selects; index sets differ only among ties at the 512th value, and all indices lie inside the row.

Prefill step, `vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with dummy weights, DEP2 on one GB200 node, `--case 'ds8x4k=8*4096@131072' --kv-len-jitter 0 --max-num-batched-tokens 34816`, no speculative decoding, FlashMLA MegaAttn with the MXFP4 indexer, `deep_select` top-k, rank 0 under nsys, ms per step:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| step (bench median) | 429.8 | 401.5 |
| indexer logits + top-k | 64.5 | 30.9 |
| of which upcast + top-k | 39.4 | 5.7 |

The step numbers come from our DSv4.1 branch (nightly 49cb2bbf plus DSv4.1 changes outside the indexer); `sparse_attn_indexer` there is identical to main before this change.

Tests on GB200, same branch with this change:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "deep_select or sparse_indexer" \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py
43 passed, 4 skipped
```

No new test: `test_deep_select_topk` and `test_deep_select_topk_preallocated_output` already cover what this path relies on (BF16 input, per-row `end`, -1 fill for rows shorter than top-k, output into a slice of a wider buffer).

Accuracy with this change (`vllm serve`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 on one GB200 node, `sparse_indexer_topk_backend="deep_select"`, DSpark K=5 with standard rejection sampling, greedy):

| eval | result |
|---|---|
| passkey retrieval, ~8K / 31K / 62K-token prompts (20 each; 4K-31K compressed keys per row, well above top-k) | 20/20, 20/20, 20/20 |
| GSM8K, lm_eval 5-shot, max 1024 tokens, concurrency 32, strict-match (two runs) | 0.9242 / 0.9227 (±0.0073) |
| DSpark acceptance length over the second GSM8K run | 3.44 (48.9% per draft token) |

The GSM8K and acceptance numbers match what we saw before this change on the same model (0.9318 strict-match and 3.36 in a P/D setup).

## Details

- Multi-request chunks: since #61149, DeepGEMM returns compressed logits in which every row starts at column zero (`row_starts is None` on CUDA), so `end = cu_seqlen_ke - cu_seqlen_ks` is each row's full causal interval for any number of requests in a chunk. #57206 tried this before that change, limited itself to single-request chunks, and was closed.
- Duplicate check: #57206 (closed, see above); #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits on the decode path; #60618 (WIP) fuses scoring and top-k for prefill in a new kernel; #56749 changes tie-breaking of the existing prefill kernel. None changes the `deep_select` prefill path.
- The logits chunk budget (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`) still assumes FP32 logits; counting BF16 would allow chunks twice as tall and is left for a follow-up.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, write and validate this change and to draft this description.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] Enable the fp8 indexer cache on gfx942
author: akii96
body:
## Overview

Unlocks `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'` for MiniMax-M3 on ROCm gfx942 (MI300-series, CDNA3). gfx950 (MI350-series) keeps its fp8 routing through the AITER indexer, and CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- fp8 indexer cache now selects on gfx942: Triton scorers get an e4m3**fnuz** cache instead of bf16, with correct saturation in both index-cache writers.
- +32% KV cache capacity for the same GPU memory.
- Serving throughput is neutral at short context and better at long context; GSM8K is unchanged.
- gfx950 keeps the pre-patch routing (fp8 via the AITER indexer, e4m3fn/OCP convert); NVIDIA keeps e4m3fn, `constexpr` 448.

## Validation

8x MI325X (gfx942), nightly `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e`, `EmbeddedLLM/MiniMax-M3-FP8-dynamic`, TP4, `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 262144`.

Indexer selection from serve logs:

| run | log line |
|---|---|
| before | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=bf16, sm100=False]` |
| after | `MiniMax M3 indexer: selected Triton (no fmha_sm100) [topk_blocks=16, indexer_kv_dtype=fp8, sm100=False]` |

KV cache (same `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`):

| | KV tokens | max concurrency @ 262k |
|---|---|---|
| before | 4,554,368 | 17.37x |
| after | 6,020,992 | 22.97x |

`vllm bench serve` (openai-chat, random dataset, exact ISL/OSL, `--ignore-eos --temperature 0`, N=32/48/16/8, median):

| ISL/OSL/conc | Out tok/s | Δ | TTFT p50 (ms) | Δ | TPOT p50 (ms) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8k/1k/8 | 468.6 → 470.4 | +0.4% | 3540 → 3519 | −0.6% | 13.95 → 13.93 | −0.1% |
| 8k/1k/16 | 697.4 → 700.4 | +0.4% | 4359 → 4365 | +0.1% | 18.85 → 18.66 | −1.0% |
| 32k/1k/8 | 284.2 → 290.0 | +2.0% | 9945 → 9830 | −1.2% | 18.43 → 17.98 | −2.4% |
| 128k/1k/4 | 92.6 → 96.3 | +4.0% | 21587 → 21104 | −2.2% | 22.12 → 20.94 | −5.3% |

GSM8K (lm-eval 0.4.13, `local-chat-completions`, 8-shot, chat template, temp 0, 1319 samples):

| | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| before | 94.69% ± 0.62 | 94.62% |
| after | 95.00% ± 0.60 | 94.92% |

Kernel tests on gfx942 (`tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py`): **61 passed, 32 skipped (nvfp4-only), 0 failed**, including the new insert-saturation, foreign-flavour-rejection, and fp8-vs-bf16 top-k equivalence tests. 

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# after (before: omit the last flag)
export HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0
vllm serve EmbeddedLLM/MiniMax-M3-FP8-dynamic \
  --served-model-name minimax-m3 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --async-scheduling --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --language-model-only \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --model minimax-m3 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
  --save-result --result-dir . --result-filename result.json

pip install "lm-eval[api]"
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,model=minimax-m3,num_concurrent=16,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 8 --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024 --output_path gsm8k_out

python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_fp8_triton_indexer.py -v
```
</details>

## Details

Root cause, three pieces:

- `select_indexer_impl_cls` refused `indexer_kv_dtype="fp8"` on every ROCm platform, although the Triton scorers are flavour-agnostic (fp8 x fp8 accumulated in fp32).
- The index cache was pinned to e4m3**fn** (`torch.float8_e4m3fn`), which gfx942 cannot convert.
- The fused qknorm/rope/kv-insert writer picked its convert with `#if defined(HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP)` — the macro is always defined (to 0 or 1), so gfx942 took the OCP branch and emitted OCP-labelled bytes that read back as wrong fnuz values (e.g. 1.1 -> 1.0, 0.77 -> 0).

The fix: the cache takes `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` (fnuz on gfx942, fn on gfx950/CUDA as before), the selector admits fp8 on ROCm gfx942 via the platform's `on_gfx942()` predicate, and the writer picks the flavour per target (`__gfx942__` -> fnuz) with saturation at `quant_type_max_v` (224 for fnuz, 448 for e4m3fn). Host checks expect the device's own flavour via the existing `is_fp8_ocp()`, and the Triton index-cache insert (AITER sparse-PA path) saturates at the same bound instead of producing NaN for out-of-range keys. gfx950's fp8 path keeps going through the AITER indexer (`SUPPORTED_ARCHS=("gfx950",)`), selected before this fallback is consulted.

Not a duplicate: the closest open PRs touching this area (#60930 CuTe prefill scorer, #59979/#59980 FMHA/MSA) are NVIDIA-side work; none enable the fp8 index cache on gfx942

AI assistance (GLM5.3-Flash) was used during the creation of this PR

title: [Model][Perf] Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and MoE finalize
author: WoosukKwon
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse Beam's TP all-reduce with its sandwich norms and, for TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 MoE layers, the top-k finalize. TP only; replicated-token EP deferral is in #62073, which builds on this PR. Follow-up to #62074 (merged). The kernel is built ahead of time in `csrc/beam/`, with no runtime JIT and no CUDA source in the model folder.

## Claims

- `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu`: MNNVL one-shot/two-shot all-reduce with Beam's FP32 norm-residual-norm epilogue and an optional MoE finalize before the reduction (keeping the local BF16 rounding). Exposed as `torch.ops._C.beam_allreduce_norm`, plus `beam_allreduce` (two-shot all-reduce only) for the large-batch path, which then runs the Triton boundary kernel.
- `csrc/mnnvl_lamport.cuh`: the subset of FlashInfer's MNNVL Lamport device helpers (`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh`, v0.7.2, the version vLLM pins) that the kernel uses, vendored with its license header.
- Beam defers the TRTLLM-Gen NvFP4 top-k finalize into the fused all-reduce under TP, using the existing `FusedMoEConfig.defer_moe_finalize()`. No shared MoE code changes.
- Same speed as the previous JIT build of this kernel, and 6–16% faster at hidden 8192 from 64 tokens up (microbenchmarks below).

## Validation

**Unit tests** on GB200 (4 GPUs):

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_beam_construction.py tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_trtllm_nvfp4_moe.py
```

178 passed, 3 skipped (8-GPU case; two upstream FlashInfer tile-config skips). This covers the 2- and 4-rank all-reduce and MoE finalize numerics.

**TP8 across two GB200 nodes** (one MNNVL clique): the all-reduce numerics worker from `test_beam_numerics.py` (batch changes, one-shot/two-shot, large-batch path, CUDA-graph replay) passes at hidden 5120 and 8192 when launched with `torchrun --nnodes=2`. The 8-rank MoE-finalize case was not run (its test is single-node).

**FlashInfer version:** these runs used an environment with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 installed. `trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh` is byte-identical in v0.7.2, and the `flashinfer.comm.mnnvl` allocator APIs used here are unchanged (v0.7.2 only adds NVML init/shutdown around a capability probe).

**Build:** `_C_stable_libtorch` built for SM100 with CUDA 13.2; `csrc/beam/allreduce_norm.cu` also compiles for `sm_90a`. Not run on Hopper.

**Kernel microbenchmark**, GB200, BF16, each op captured 20× in a CUDA graph; µs per call, slowest rank. "JIT" is the previous FlashInfer-JIT build of the same kernel, "AOT" is this one. Fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm:

| config | 1 tok | 8 tok | 64 tok | 256 tok | 1024 tok | 4096 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, hidden 5120 (JIT → AOT) | 5.39 → 5.75* | 5.48 → 5.43 | 8.70 → 8.78 | 11.71 → 11.67 | 34.06 → 33.71 | 138.0 → 139.2 |
| TP4, hidden 8192 | 6.34 → 6.31 | 6.34 → 6.21 | 9.97 → 9.34 | 19.00 → 16.05 | 64.52 → 54.28 | 251.2 → 226.8 |
| TP8, hidden 5120 | 6.53 → 6.48 | 6.42 → 6.39 | 9.00 → 8.97 | 12.89 → 12.88 | 35.52 → 35.53 | 140.3 → 140.4 |
| TP8, hidden 8192 | 7.86 → 7.78 | 7.98 → 7.91 | 10.59 → 9.88 | 19.82 → 16.67 | 68.27 → 57.19 | 265.1 → 225.8 |

TP4 is the median of 3 runs; TP8 is the mean of two runs with the measurement order swapped. \*Whichever kernel is measured first in a process reads about 0.4 µs slow at 1 token; with the order reversed, TP4/5120 at 1 token is 5.79 (JIT) → 5.36 (AOT). The kernel code is unchanged: register usage matches, and at hidden 5120 the AOT kernel on the JIT path's workspace matches the JIT kernel within 0.07 µs. The hidden-8192 gap appears only with the JIT path's own workspace sized for 8192 tokens (it vanishes at 4096); its cause was not isolated.

**Performance:** TODO — end-to-end before/after against #62074 (standard TP all-reduce), TP8 batch-1 decode and 8 × 2K prefill on GB200.

## Details

- **Why vendor FlashInfer's helpers instead of reusing vLLM's MNNVL Lamport kernels:** on GB200, vLLM's Lamport all-gather (`csrc/custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.cuh`) is about 10% slower at TP4 and 25–40% slower at TP8 than FlashInfer's one-shot all-reduce, which does the same communication plus a reduction (TP8, 64 tokens × 5120: 16.7 vs 11.9 µs). Its reduce-scatter + all-gather pair is 1.3–1.8× slower than FlashInfer's single-launch two-shot. A likely cause is that vLLM waits on peer ranks one at a time, while FlashInfer polls them all at once; not verified with a patched kernel. Building on vLLM's primitives would have regressed Beam, so the device code is kept as-is.
- **Workspace:** FlashInfer's `McastGPUBuffer` still maps the multicast memory. The Lamport protocol, its initialization and its generation flags are vLLM's, so the build no longer depends on FlashInfer's headers or installed version. Torch symmetric memory works too, but measured 0.2–0.3 µs slower per call at 1–4 tokens (even from 8 tokens up). Rounding it to the 512 MB multicast granularity didn't help. Beam's GB200 path already requires FlashInfer for its MoE.
- **Build:** compiled only for SM90/SM100 (`VLLM_ENABLE_BEAM_ALLREDUCE`), with `--fmad=false` on that file only, so the FP32 boundary math is not contracted into FMAs. `BeamAllReduceWorkspace.create` returns `None` (standard TP all-reduce) when the op is not built, multicast is unavailable on any rank, or the shape/TP size is unsupported.
- **CI coverage:** `tests/models/test_beam_numerics.py` runs on a CPU agent in Buildkite, so the GPU and multi-GPU cases skip in CI. They were run on GB200 as above.
- **Scope:** an earlier revision also added `defer_moe_finalize(allow_ep=True)` to `FusedMoEConfig` for TP=1, EP>1. It moved to #62073, which extends it to MegaMoE under DP/EP, so this PR leaves the shared MoE config untouched.
- **Not a duplicate:** no other open PR touches Beam's all-reduce.

title: [PCP] Allow decode-only full CUDA graphs for DSv3.2/GLM-5.2/5.3 sparse MLA with DCP=1
author: LucasWilkinson
body:
## Overview

Allows decode-only full CUDA graphs (`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` / `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) under MRV2 PCP with DCP=1 for sparse-MLA models on the DeepSeek-V3.2 attention path (DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2/5.3: `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa`). In that mode, decode requests are round-robin sharded across PCP ranks. These models previously had to run with `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, but the pure-decode full-graph path from #53867 already handles them. Other `index_topk` models (DSv4/V4.1, MiniMax-M3, ...) still require `NONE`, because they need model-specific work (see #61555 for DSv4.1).

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 with TP1 × PCP4 + EP captures and replays decode-only full CUDA graphs.
- On GSM8K, that is 2.6× faster than eager, with matching accuracy (0.9083 vs 0.9075).

## Validation

Tested with GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on 4×B300: `-tp 1 -pcp 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64`:

| cudagraph_mode | GSM8K accuracy | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| NONE | 0.9075 | 379.5 s | 330 |
| FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 0.9083 | 145.9 s | 859 |

Every rank captured 11 FULL and 19 PIECEWISE graphs.

`pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: passes.

## Details

- Pure FULL mode is still rejected, so prefills under PCP keep running piecewise.
- DeepSeek-V3.2 shares GLM-5.3's attention/indexer code but was not run end-to-end.
- Not validated yet with MTP.

title: [Perf][AuxOutput] Do not rescan referenced keys in the routed-experts store
author: aoshen02
body:
## Purpose

Split from #62044 (by @faresobeid): only the store eviction fix.

`BlockObjectStore` kept referenced and unreferenced objects in one LRU, and eviction scanned it from the oldest key, skipping referenced ones. Keys referenced by running requests pile up at the front, so every `put()` that had to evict rescanned all of them on the writer thread. #62044 measured about 9 ms per `put` with 300k keys, and reports that removing this rescan cut the writer thread from 281 s to 2.3 s over 20 RL steps on GLM-4.5-Air, for +15.6% throughput.

The store now follows `BlockPool`'s free block queue: the LRU holds only unreferenced objects.

- `_slots` maps every stored key to its slot.
- A key leaves the LRU when its reference count goes from 0 to 1, and goes back to its tail when the count drops to 0. Within one `put()`, released keys end up after the batch's objects, in release order, as before.
- Eviction takes keys from the front of the LRU. As before, it skips keys stored by the same `put()` unless that call also releases them; they are at the tail by then.

With balanced retains and releases, eviction order, victims and errors are the same as before. Releasing a key that is not referenced raises `KeyError`, as before; keys released earlier in that call go to the tail of the LRU instead of keeping their old position, so later victims can differ. The writer thread stops after that error.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py
```

`test_store_eviction_does_not_rescan_referenced_keys` fills a store with 900 referenced and 100 unreferenced objects, then makes 100 `put()` calls. The referenced keys are a `str` subclass that counts its own hashes, so any dict or set lookup of a referenced key is counted, whatever container the store uses. The test also checks that the 100 unreferenced objects are the ones evicted and that every referenced object stays readable. It does not touch store internals.

## Test Result

- `test_store.py`: 65 passed.
- The new test counts 0 hashes of referenced keys with this change and 180,000 on `main` (limit 900). It also fails on `main` with `_references` or `_lru` renamed.
- Differential fuzz against `main` (not part of the PR), 5,000 random sequences of `put` (duplicate keys, varying payloads, retains, releases) and `get` on stores of 1 to 10 slots:
  - balanced references: stored keys, allocated keys, reference counts and eviction order are identical after every operation;
  - with unreferenced releases: the store invariant holds after every operation; 404 sequences pick different victims after the `KeyError`.
  - Evicting from the wrong end of the LRU differs on the first sequence.

## Benchmark

GLM-4.5-Air, one GB200 node (TP4), `gpu_memory_utilization=0.9` (2,434,064 KV tokens, 167,341 store objects), `max_model_len=20480`, routed experts enabled. Each step is an RL-style rollout: 64 prompts x 8 samples (512 sequences), 1k-16k output tokens with `ignore_eos`, seeded per step so every run generates exactly the same 13,448,609 tokens over 3 steps. Both arms use the same 2026-10-16 nightly image and differ only in `store.py`; runs are ordered main, PR, PR, main. The store is set to 1.1x the KV-sized default so that `main` does not hit the full-KV crash fixed by #62044. Writer-thread time is the sum of `BlockObjectStore.put` wall time.

| Run | Step 0 | Step 1 | Step 2 | Throughput | Writer `put` time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 510.5 s | 487.8 s | 425.5 s | 9,446 tok/s | 526.0 s |
| PR | 417.2 s | 415.0 s | 414.4 s | 10,788 tok/s | 4.4 s |
| PR | 417.5 s | 415.1 s | 413.9 s | 10,789 tok/s | 7.3 s |
| main | 420.0 s | 545.5 s | 549.4 s | 8,878 tok/s | 617.7 s |

Throughput is +17.7% (9,162 to 10,788 tok/s on average). On `main`, the step time follows the writer-thread time: about 420 s at 140 s of `put`, about 545 s at 240 s. With `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` (753,552 KV tokens, about 52k objects) the writer was busy for 17% of each step on `main` and throughput was unchanged (5,868 vs 5,897 tok/s), so the gain needs a store large enough for the rescan to delay the engine.

### Reproduce

Run the script below once with `main` and once with this PR, on one node with 4 GPUs (`max_bytes` is 1.1x the default store size for this model and KV size):

```python
import random
import sys
import time

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

WORDS = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "prime", "integer", "triangle", "sum",
         "product", "remainder", "circle", "radius", "matrix", "vector", "angle"]


def main():
    model, steps = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
    llm = LLM(
        model=model,
        tensor_parallel_size=4,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        max_model_len=20480,
        enable_return_routed_experts=True,
        aux_output_config={"max_bytes": 985_303_808},
        seed=0,
    )
    for step in range(steps):
        rng = random.Random(1000 + step)
        prompts, params = [], []
        for g in range(64):
            body = " ".join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(150, 900)))
            text = f"Problem {step}-{g}: {body}. Solve it step by step."
            for _ in range(8):
                prompts.append(text)
                params.append(SamplingParams(temperature=1.0, ignore_eos=True,
                                             max_tokens=rng.randint(1024, 16384)))
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        outs = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
        dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
        gen = sum(len(c.token_ids) for o in outs for c in o.outputs)
        print(f"step {step}: {dt:.1f} s, {gen} tokens, {gen / dt:.0f} tok/s", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```bash
python repro.py zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air 3
```

A single step with this script gave 459.3 s on `main` and 417.7 s with this PR for the same 4,543,356 tokens.

title: [ROCm][Build] Compile paged attention kernels in parallel (7.6x faster attention build)
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Overview

`csrc/rocm/attention.cu` is a single 3.9k-line translation unit whose kernel instantiation is the tail of the ROCm build: ~9 min of a ~10.5 min build, on one core. This inflation was probably especially caused by recent: #42755  (adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` as a template parameter to all 12 kernels = interleaved + non-interleaved instantiation (+50%))

This PR splits the instantiations into one translation unit per (dtype, kv-cache dtype, head size) combination so ninja builds them in parallel.

*Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this (searched issues and PRs for `attention.cu` split / translation unit / ROCm compile time / `MAX_JOBS`). The closest open items are #17419 (general "builds are too slow" RFC) and #60906 (reuse the CMake build dir for editable installs); both are orthogonal to removing the single-TU bottleneck.*

## Claims

- Attention kernel compile drops from **547 s on 1 core to 72 s on 12 cores** (7.6×); the full editable install from ~10 min 40 s to ~1 min 35 s.
- `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link drops from ~2 s to 0.26 s (it no longer waits behind one 9-minute object).
- No behavior change: identical template instantiations, identical dispatch order, unchanged `paged_attention` signature and op registration.
- Cost: `_rocm_C.abi3.so` grows 196.3 MB → 219.2 MB (+11.6%) and aggregate CPU work grows ~30%, both traded for the 7.6× wall-clock win.

**How the file got this big.** The instantiation matrix was grown one axis at a time:

| PR | landed | what it added | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8310 | 2024-09-13 | initial ROCm custom paged attention | 1,038 lines, 4 kernels; already `{fp16,bf16}` × head `{64,128}` × block `{16,32}` × alibi `{on,off}` |
| #8577 | 2024-09-19 | fp8 KV cache | adds the `KV_DTYPE`/`cache_t` axis (fp8, `kFp8E4M3`) |
| #12348 | 2025-03-04 | "Faster Custom Paged Attention" rewrite | 4 → 6 kernels (`mfma16`, `mfma4`, partition `reduce`), +1,084/−422 |
| #17139 | 2025-05-07 | FP8 output fusion | `if (fp8_out_scale) → OUTT=uint8_t` = ×2 |
| #17004 | 2025-05-21 | RDNA/NAVI support on v1 | duplicates the kernel set for gfx11/gfx12, 6 → 12 `__global__`, ≈×2, +1,880/−171 |
| #22222 | 2025-09-15 | fp8 paged attention update | adds `MFMAType` (`Fp8` vs `F16`) = ×2 on the fp8 path |
| #42755 | 2026-10-15 | Qwen3-30B QK-norm/RoPE/KV-cache fusion | adds `USE_INTERLEAVED_V_CACHE` to all 12 kernels = +50% |

Cumulative, per architecture: 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × head (2) × block (2) × fp8-out (2) × alibi (2) × {NAVI, non-NAVI, interleaved} ≈ 288 launcher instantiations → ~860 device kernels in one file. `--offload-arch` values are additionally compiled serially inside that file, so release builds covering `gfx90a;gfx942;gfx950` pay ~3× the per-architecture cost.


## Validation

Compile times on MI350 in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-39983a5e7a5a575a7829f5d5ada50a33d9337ec1` with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx950`; no compiler flags were set by hand, `-O2 -g` comes from the default `RelWithDebInfo` build type:

| Step | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| attention kernel compile (wall) | 547 s on 1 core | 72 s on 12 cores (58–72 s per TU) |
| `attention_dispatch.cu` (now the dispatch TU only) | — | 15 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` link | ~2 s | 0.26 s |
| full `MAX_JOBS=64 pip install -vvv -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation` | 10 min 40 s | 1 min 35 s |
| `_rocm_C.abi3.so` size | 196.3 MB | 219.2 MB |

Per-edge timings come from `.ninja_log` of a cold build (`CCACHE_DISABLE=1 ninja -j64 _rocm_C`); all 12 attention TUs start within 2 ms of each other and finish 58–72 s later, so the split parallelizes as intended.

Kernel correctness — the positive matrix covers head 64/128 × block 16/32 × fp16/bf16 × kv auto/fp8 × alibi on/off × interleaved-V on/off × GQA 1/4/8, i.e. every one of the 12 instantiation TUs:

```bash
# f16 MFMA path (default)
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k num_heads0 -q
# 128 passed, 256 deselected, 414 s

# fp8 MFMA path (*_fp8_fp8 TUs)
VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1 python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention -k "num_heads0 and fp8" -q
# 64 passed, 320 deselected, 206 s

# head-size `default:` branch of the dispatch
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_attention.py::test_paged_attention_unsupported_head_sizes -q
# 7 passed, 1 s
```

No model eval is included: the split does not change kernels, dispatch, or numerics, only how many objects they are compiled into.

**Left for other PRs** (no automated coverage today, unchanged by this PR):
- [ ] Block-size `default:` of `ATTN_LAUNCH` (`Unsupported block size: `): `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes()` returns `MultipleOf(16)`, so `block_size=64` does reach the op — needs a `test_paged_attention_unsupported_block_sizes` analogue of the head-size test.
- [ ] `*_fp8_fp8` TUs in CI: only run here via `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_MFMA_PAGE_ATTN=1`, and no `.buildkite/` or `.github/` job sets it; parametrizing a subset over `mfma_type in {"f16", "fp8"}` would cover them.
- [ ] `fp8_out_scale` (`OUTT=uint8_t`, doubles the instantiations in every TU): no test references it.
- [ ] `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3"` alias handled in `attention_dispatch.cu`: untested.
- [ ] Compile-test the NAVI regions with `PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH="gfx1100;gfx1201"`: the `__HIP__GFX9__`/NAVI `#if` blocks are now evaluated once per file and were only exercised on MI350.

## Details

**Root cause.** A HIP translation unit is compiled by one clang process on one core; there is no clang equivalent of `nvcc --threads`, and additional `--offload-arch` values are also processed serially inside that process. `attention.cu` instantiates 12 kernels across 6 dtype/kv-cache combinations × 2 head sizes × 2 block sizes × alibi on/off × fp16/fp8 output × 2 v-cache layouts × CDNA/NAVI, so the whole tail is one serial 9-minute compile that `MAX_JOBS=64` cannot help with. (The popular "`Linking _moe_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` is slow" symptom is a ninja progress artifact: the link is 159 ms and the following line is simply not printed until `attention.hip.o` finishes.)

**Why splitting helps, measured.** Compile time is linear in the number of instantiations: restricting head size to 64 (half the instantiations) gives 270 s vs 547 s for the full set. So distributing the instantiations over N TUs gives ~N× wall-clock, minus a fixed cost.

**Why not just drop debug info.** Building the same TU with `-g0` gives 451 s vs 547 s, i.e. `-g` is only ~18% of the cost, and it would change the shipped build type. Splitting removes 475 s while keeping `RelWithDebInfo`.

**Design.** `csrc/rocm/attention_kernels.cuh` (renamed from `attention.cu`) holds the device helpers, all kernel and launcher templates, and the parameter-list macro. Each `csrc/rocm/attention_paged_attn_<head>_<dtype>_<kv>.cu` is ~4 lines: it includes the header and instantiates one combination via `ATTN_LAUNCH(...)`, exposing a fixed-head-size entry point. `csrc/rocm/attention_dispatch.cu` keeps `is_navi_gpu()` and the dtype/kv-cache dispatch (unchanged order) and forwards to those entry points. The instantiation sets are disjoint, so nothing is compiled twice on purpose. hipify follows quoted includes, so the new header is hipified like any other (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) and no build-system special-casing is needed beyond listing the new `.cu` files in `VLLM_ROCM_EXT_SRC`. Renaming `attention.cu` to `attention_kernels.cuh` keeps the 3.9k moved lines recorded as a rename, so `git blame`/`--follow` survive.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- `.so` grows 196.3 → 219.2 MB (+11.6%), and the extra is debug info, not code: `.hip_fatbin` carries the device DWARF, and each TU emits its own copy of it for the headers/types it includes (the split's objects total 207.6 MB vs 169.4 MB, of which `.hip_fatbin` is 188.8 MB with `-g` but 42.2 MB with `-g0`, i.e. the ISA does not duplicate). Building these TUs with `-g1` gives a 96.1 MB `.so` and `-g0` a 74.9 MB one, both well below `main`'s 196.3 MB; that is left out here because it changes shipped debug info for the ROCm kernels, so it belongs in its own PR (there is exactly one out-of-line device helper, `warpReduceMax`, so marking helpers `__forceinline__` recovers nothing).
- Adding a head size, dtype, or kv-cache combination now means adding a TU and a `CMakeLists.txt` entry; the comments in `attention_kernels.cuh` and `CMakeLists.txt` point at this.
- The split is unbalanced: head size 128 TUs take ~70 s vs ~59 s for head size 64. Splitting within head size 128 (e.g. by block size) would lower the 72 s further, but the floor is ~20 s of frontend parsing per TU (measured with `-fsyntax-only`), so gains beyond 12–24 TUs are small unless a precompiled header is added.
- `attention_kernels.cuh` is hipified (`attention_kernels_hip.cuh`) like the ~15 other headers already in the tree (`quant_utils.cuh` → `quant_utils_hip.cuh`, `layernorm_utils.cuh`, …). `hipify_all` is an `add_custom_target` with no output file, so ninja treats it as always dirty and re-runs hipify on every build (~1 s), which regenerates those headers; editing the source header is therefore re-hipified normally and picked up by the next compile.

title: [Core][MRV2] Warm up the sampler after CUDA graph capture to stop memory growth under load
author: GodRishUniverse
body:
## Overview

On Model Runner V2, GPU memory keeps growing after startup while load ramps up. The sampler makes an fp32 copy of the `[num_reqs, vocab]` logits on every step. `capture_model()` ends with `empty_cache()`, so serving starts with no cached block of that size, and each new largest batch reserves a slightly bigger block while the smaller ones stay cached.

V1 already avoids this: `compile_or_warm_up_model` runs the sampler once at the largest batch *after* `capture_model()` ("on purpose to prevent memory buffers from being cleared by `torch.accelerator.empty_cache`"). This PR adds the same step for MRV2.

**Depends on #57926.** That PR makes `_dummy_sampler_run` take the fp32 path and counts it in `profile_run`. Without it, the dummy run skips the copy and this warm-up keeps nothing.

## Claims

- Memory no longer grows step by step under load (Qwen3-4B: +1.77 GB in 18 steps to +0.11 GB in 1 step; Gemma-4-31B TP4: +0.24 to +0.003 GB per GPU).
- No KV cache cost on top of #57926.
- No throughput change.

## Validation

**Qwen3-4B, TP1, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`**

| | main | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 106,912 | 105,680 | 105,680 |
| Memory growth under load | +1.78 GB (18 steps) | +1.77 GB (18 steps) | +0.11 GB (1 step) |
| Peak GPU memory under load | 25.72 GB | 25.54 GB | 24.11 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=16 / 64 / 160 / 256 | 608 / 1279 / 1562 / 1519 | 607 / 1277 / 1563 / 1503 | 608 / 1276 / 1561 / 1499 |

**Gemma-4-31B-it, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-memory 3GB`**

| | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 18,806 | 18,806 |
| Memory growth under load (each GPU) | +0.24 GB (3 steps) | +0.003 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=8 / 32 / 64 / 128 | 133 / 496 / 520 / 536 | 133 / 496 / 521 / 537 |

Setup:
- Hardware and software: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB), ROCm 10.1, torch 2.13, vLLM `8a6c0449b3` with #57926 and this PR.


Run on `main`, #57926 and #57926 + this PR. Requests carry no sampling params, so each model's default top-k/top-p applies.

**Qwen3-4B, 1 GPU**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 1280 --max-concurrency 256 --request-rate inf --seed 1256
```

**Gemma-4-31B, 4 GPUs** (fixed KV size so all builds get the same KV cache)

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --kv-cache-memory 3221225472 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model google/gemma-4-31B-it --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 640 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --seed 1128
```


## Details

- Not tested on NVIDIA; the code path is the same. I can test on it.

title: [Feature][HiSparse] Add a platform backend for device operations
author: zhenwenqi2024
body:
## Overview

Add a platform-selected backend so hardware plugins can reuse HiSparse's runtime and connector. CUDA uses the same cache operations and kernels.

Related: #60072. Ascend integration: vllm-project/vllm-ascend#19109.

## Claims

- Add `HiSparseBackend` for cache operations, host registration, IPC handles, resident-row payload handling, capture queries, DMA and statistics dtype.
- Let each platform select its HiSparse backend through a `@classmethod` hook. The base platform returns `None`; CUDA overrides the method in `platforms/cuda.py`.
- Validate cache formats before allocation and prepare device views inside the existing initialization rollback scope.
- Use `torch.Stream`, `torch.Event` and `torch.accelerator` directly for common device operations. Only IPC events need backend-specific creation/import/export. FP8 prefill keeps its existing custom-op call.

Speculative group prefetch is excluded. Follower staging keeps the original `decode_batch` condition. No CUDA performance improvement is claimed.

## Validation

- CPU fixture follow-up for [Buildkite #97663](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97663#01a17e0c-4bb9-473c-a68f-35f5ad9fe991): planning and configuration tests now select the real CUDA HiSparse backend through the platform hook instead of overriding the old CUDA predicates. Unsupported-platform checks use the hook's `None` result. On Linux/aarch64 with PyTorch 2.10 and an explicit CPU target, the command below gave `22 failed, 5 passed` at `5b8e00878206`, then `27 passed` with `bb13de1884ba`. Existing capacity, layout and configuration assertions were retained. This is CPU validation, not CUDA/NPU execution.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py -k hisparse
```

The default Qwen3-0.6B configuration was cached for both runs; no model weights were loaded.

- The platform selector and CUDA override use `@classmethod`, matching other platform backend hooks. Class/instance calls and descriptor inheritance were checked on the actual base class and exact CUDA method source. An independent audit of the exact Ascend override confirmed existing instance calls remain compatible; its matching classmethod override is still needed for class calls. This CPU descriptor check does not qualify device execution or the full Ascend pair.

- Whole-PR follow-up checked the eight changed vLLM modules and all 28 test files mentioning HiSparse, including 43 literal module patch targets. Existing connector tests now patch the accelerator/backend entry points, the row-DMA fixture initializes its backend, and resident-prefill gathering uses a bound runtime. Existing payload and ordering assertions are retained.
- The existing zero-token TP ordering regression reproduced four `AttributeError` failures on the removed patch target before the fix and passed all four parameters afterward. It used exact production/test definitions in an out-of-tree CPU runner. The draft-mirror runner reaches pinned allocation but cannot execute on CPU-only torch; device regressions remain unrun locally.

- Applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, markdownlint-cli2, SPDX, import checks and test tethering. Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two checked-in resident-gather cases passed with real CPU tensors and the actual `HiSparseBackend`, checking page stride, reordered/repeated rows and packed-byte payloads. An out-of-tree runner selected the unchanged test function to avoid full worker-module imports; no backend or torch methods were substituted. This is not a full vLLM pytest or device result.
- A real CUDA stream/IPC-event ordering regression was added to the existing attention suite; it is not run locally.
- Standard worker pytest collection was attempted on Windows with faulthandler and terminated with an access violation (exit `-1073741819`). CUDA/NPU model, graph replay, accuracy and performance validation remain pending.
- Hooks for untouched CUDA, workflow, shell, dependency and Rust files were skipped to avoid unrelated tool installation. No unfiltered full-hook run is claimed.

Focused commands for a prepared vLLM environment:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -k hisparse
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  -k 'hisparse_generic_stream or index_group_converts_decode_indices_once or hisparse_fp8_prefill_gather'
```

The existing Buildkite worker and attention suites select these files. Retained additions check real payload values and initialization rollback; mock-only backend routing tests have been removed.

## Details

A plugin overrides `Platform.get_hisparse_backend_cls()` with its backend's qualified class name. Lookup is lazy and cached by class name. HiSparse uses generic torch streams, events, current-stream queries and synchronization. The constructor validates backend availability once. Generic resident gathering has a base implementation; plugins may override packed-payload handling.

The linked Ascend draft must align its resolver workspace ownership and tests with this interface before the pair can merge. Its currently published head still accesses the removed `backend_state` field. Speculative group prefetch is separate work in #63801. Installed PTA 2.10.0.post7 headers provide generic stream/event/device-guard operations, but this source inspection does not establish NPU graph replay or final-pair correctness. Final-head Ascend integration and device validation remain required.

The scheduler, HMA allocation, residency policy, KV formats and attention math keep their existing ownership. The device-view hook runs once after allocation and before binding; per-step metadata and transfers stay outside it. Existing PP/CP/graph restrictions remain. DMA submission retains upstream error handling; this PR adds no exception-drain/quarantine branch or unused backend state.

The open HiSparse PRs checked for overlap, including #57602 and #60358, address ROCm execution/registration and other fixes. This PR provides the platform interface without their kernels or unrelated lifecycle changes.

AI assistance was used for implementation and preparation. Final human review and hardware/model validation remain required before merge.

title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Copy-based Q zero-pad for large eager mega-attention steps
author: roborluo
body:
## Overview

  Makes the per-layer Q pad + KV insert of DeepSeek-V4.1 mega-attention layers **1.9-2.15x faster** on eager steps of 2048 tokens or more at TP2, with bit-identical outputs. On layers with 32 live heads padded to 64 (TP2 of a 64-head model), those steps
  now run the fused insert op in its existing KV-only mode and build the zero-padded, chunk-interleaved Q with a contiguous Triton copy, instead of padding Q inside the fused op.
  Part of #57448, on top of FlashMLA mega attention (#56935) and the interleaved V4.1 KV records (#61371); related: #58872, #55654, #60076 (see *Not a duplicate*).

  ## Claims

  - **1.9-2.15x faster Q pad + KV insert per layer** on eager steps of 2048-16384 tokens (2.10x at 8192 tokens; table below). With 32 live heads padded to 64, the Q half of the fused op reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for
  its KV half, and it writes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, in 16-element pieces `64 * 16` elements apart. The copy writes each token's 32 rows of 1024 elements contiguously.
  - **Bit-identical results:** the padded Q and the sliding-window KV cache bytes equal those of the fused launch (for NaN-free Q), so model outputs do not change.
  - **Narrow, automatic dispatch:** only eager steps with at least 2048 query tokens on mega-attention layers with 32 of 64 padded heads take the new path. Captured CUDA graphs, smaller steps, other shards (TP1/TP4/TP8 of a 64-head model), other attention
  backends and other platforms run exactly as before. There is no new flag, env var or config option.
  - **No new sync or memory:** the per-step decision reads only host metadata, and the padded Q tensor has the shape the op would have allocated itself. A full GSM8K run against a server started with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` detects no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Kernel time** of the Q pad + KV insert per layer, fused op vs KV-only launch + copy (bf16, 32 live / 64 padded heads, `python bench_q_pad_copy.py` below: each arm replayed as a CUDA graph and timed with CUDA events, median; correctness asserted before
  timing; two runs agree to within 0.1%):

  | Tokens | **Speedup** |
  | ---: | ---: |
  | 512 | 1.61x (below the 2048-token threshold: keeps the fused op) |
  | 1024 | 1.87x (also below the threshold: the copy's extra eager launch eats this; see the 64-16384 sweep in the comments) |
  | 2048 | **1.93x** |
  | 4096 | **2.06x** |
  | 8192 | **2.10x** |
  | 16384 | **2.15x** |

  The shipped copy launch config (`BLOCK_ROWS=4`, 4 warps) is the fastest of the 12 configurations swept at 2048 tokens and tied fastest at 8192.

  <details>
  <summary>bench_q_pad_copy.py</summary>

  ```python
  """Fused Q pad + KV insert vs KV-only insert + _pad_interleaved_q (32 of 64 heads)."""

  import statistics

  import torch
  from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

  from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.attention import (
      _pad_interleaved_q,
      _pad_interleaved_q_kernel,
  )
  from vllm.triton_utils import triton

  LIVE, PADDED, D, ROPE, BLOCK, REC = 32, 64, 512, 64, 64, 528
  op = torch.ops._C.fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert
  # After q_head_padded: eps, block_size, then the mega-attention layer's flags
  # apply_q_norm, kv_mxfp8, apply_q_rope and is_q_interleaved.
  TAIL = (1e-6, BLOCK, False, True, False, True)


  def bench_us(fn):
      times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(fn, use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True)
      return statistics.median(times) * 1e3


  def compare(n):
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      kv = torch.randn(n, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      pos, slots = torch.arange(n), torch.arange(n)
      cos_sin = torch.randn(n, ROPE)  # values do not affect timing
      cache_a = torch.zeros(n // BLOCK + 1, BLOCK * REC, dtype=torch.uint8)
      cache_b = torch.zeros_like(cache_a)
      out = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

      def fused():
          return op(q, kv, cache_a, slots, pos, cos_sin, PADDED, *TAIL)

      def kv_only():
          op(q, kv, cache_b, slots, pos, cos_sin, 0, *TAIL)

      def copy():
          _pad_interleaved_q(q, out)

      # Correctness before timing: same cache bytes and Q bits as the fused launch.
      want = fused()
      kv_only()
      copy()
      assert torch.equal(cache_a, cache_b)
      assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))

      t_fused, t_kv, t_copy = bench_us(fused), bench_us(kv_only), bench_us(copy)
      t_new = bench_us(lambda: (kv_only(), copy()))
      # Every byte read or written once: Q in, padded Q out, KV row, position,
      # slot and cos/sin row in, KV record out.
      nbytes = n * ((LIVE + PADDED) * D * 2 + D * 2 + 16 + ROPE * 4 + REC)
      print(
          f"{n:6d} {t_fused:9.1f} {t_kv:11.1f} {t_copy:8.1f} {t_new:11.1f} "
          f"{t_fused / t_new:7.2f}x {nbytes / t_fused / 1e3:11.0f} "
          f"{nbytes / t_new / 1e3:9.0f}"
      )


  def sweep(n):
      """Time the copy alone per launch config; the PR ships BLOCK_ROWS=4, 4 warps."""
      q = torch.randn(n, LIVE, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      want = torch.empty(n, PADDED, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      _pad_interleaved_q(q, want)
      rows = n * (D // 16)
      for block_rows in (1, 2, 4, 8):
          for num_warps in (2, 4, 8):
              out = torch.empty_like(want)
              run = _pad_interleaved_q_kernel[(triton.cdiv(rows, block_rows),)]
              args = (q, out, rows)
              kwargs = dict(
                  LIVE=LIVE * 16,
                  PAD=(PADDED - LIVE) * 16,
                  BLOCK_ROWS=block_rows,
                  num_warps=num_warps,
              )
              run(*args, **kwargs)
              assert torch.equal(out.view(torch.int16), want.view(torch.int16))
              t = bench_us(lambda run=run, args=args, kwargs=kwargs: run(*args, **kwargs))
              print(f"{n:6d} {block_rows:10d} {num_warps:9d} {t:8.1f}")


  torch.set_default_device("cuda")
  torch.manual_seed(0)
  print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "torch", torch.__version__)
  print("tokens  fused_us  kv_only_us  copy_us  kv+copy_us  speedup  GB/s(fused, new)")
  for n in (512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384):
      compare(n)
  print("tokens  BLOCK_ROWS  num_warps  copy_us")
  for n in (2048, 8192):
      sweep(n)
  ```

  </details>

  **In serving** (TP2, mega attention selected explicitly, Engram offload and indexer settings as in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe). 8192-token steps are above the default CUDA-graph capture sizes, so they run eagerly and take the new path: the torch
  profiler of an 8192-token prefill shows `_pad_interleaved_q_kernel` (server flag `--profiler-config '{"profiler": "torch", "torch_profiler_dir": "./prof"}'`, then the bench command below with `--profile --num-prompts 2`).

  ```bash
  vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
    --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
    --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --no-enable-prefix-caching

  vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1 \
    --num-prompts 128 --max-concurrency 16
  ```

  **Correctness: unit tests** (CUDA GPU with the `_C` extension built):

  ```bash
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py::test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert"
  pytest -v tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py
  pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer"
  ```

  | Test | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | `test_q_interleaved_pad_copy_matches_fused_insert` (new) | 6 passed |
  | `test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, whole file | 221 passed |
  | `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` | 2 passed |

  The new test runs the KV-only launch plus `_pad_interleaved_q` and the fused launch on the same input at 17, 1024 and 2049 tokens (both sides of the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`), with and without 5 trailing DP-padding rows that have no slot. It requires
  identical cache bytes and identical padded-Q bits, with the copy writing into a NaN-filled buffer.
  **Lint:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0), `typos`, `py_compile` and the local pre-commit hooks (`check_spdx_header`, `check_forbidden_imports`, `check_torch_cuda`, `check_boolean_context_manager`, `check_init_lazy_imports`,
  `validate_config`, `check_test_tethering`) pass on the four changed files, and so does the pre-commit mypy hook (`tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, Python 3.11).

  **CI coverage:** the new test is in `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, which `:nvidia: (H100) DeepSeek V4 Kernels`, `:nvidia: (B200) DeepSeek V4 Kernels` and the `:amd: (MI355 DPX) DeepSeek V4 Fused Kernels` mirror run. This
  PR's test change triggers them, but their `source_file_dependencies` do not list `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`, so a later change to the copy alone would not re-run the test; I can add it if wanted. `test_compressor_kv_cache.py` runs in
  `:nvidia: (B200) Miscellaneous Kernels`. No CI job serves mega attention at TP2 (the DeepSeek-V4.1 GSM8K config in CI is TP4, where the copy is off), so the serving check above is a manual run.

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention applies Q RoPE itself and reads Q chunk-interleaved: per token, 32 chunks of `[heads, 16]` with the padding heads at the tail of every chunk. The V4.1 layer norms `qr` before `wq_b`, so the Q half of
  `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_rope_quant_insert` is a pure zero-pad in that layout. With 32 live heads padded to 64 it reads 32 KiB and writes 64 KiB per token, against about 1.8 KiB for the KV half sharing the launch, so on large steps the op's time
  is mostly the Q pad. The op processes Q one (token, head) slot per warp, and in this layout a head's 16-element lane chunks sit `padded_heads * 16` elements apart; the copy instead writes each (token, chunk) row of 1024 elements contiguously.

  **Design.**
  - `_pads_q_by_copy` is set once per layer: the layer reads Q interleaved (`accepts_unnormed_unroped_query`), has 32 live heads padded to 64, and `max_num_batched_tokens >= 2048`. Such layers register `_pad_interleaved_q` for JIT warmup, so the first
  long prefill does not compile it.
  - Per step, `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` takes the copy when the layer qualifies, the step has at least 2048 tokens and the current stream is not capturing. The op then runs with `q_head_padded=0`, the KV-only mode TP1 mega attention already uses on
  main: it schedules no Q slots and runs the same per-token RoPE, MXFP8 quantization and paged insert, skipping DP-padding rows as before (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` launches the same KV kernel; passing 0 keeps the existing call).
  `_pad_interleaved_q` then writes the padded Q into a fresh `[num_tokens, 64, 512]` tensor.
  - `_pad_interleaved_q` is a Triton kernel over `num_tokens * 32` rows, one per (token, 16-dim chunk): 512 live elements copied, then 512 zeros. It goes through `triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup` like other warmed Triton launchers.
  - 1024 equals the op's `NUM_TOKEN_CUTOFF`, where it switches to its reduced-grid kernel; smaller steps keep one launch. The copy would also win at 512 tokens (1.61x above), but steps that small normally run inside captured CUDA graphs, which keep the
  fused pad.
  - The branch lives in the shared `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert`, next to the existing interleaved-Q handling; a mega-attention override would have to duplicate that method's KV-insert setup.

  **Exactness.** With norm and RoPE off, the op's live-Q path converts bf16 to fp32 and back with no arithmetic in between, which reproduces every non-NaN value bit for bit, and it stores +0.0 in the padding slots. The copy moves the bits unchanged and
  stores the same +0.0. The KV half runs the same code in both modes, and the test compares the cache bytes with `rtol=0, atol=0`.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - Eligible steps issue two launches instead of one; the extra Triton launch is host-side overhead that large prefill steps hide.
  - Only the 32-of-64 shard qualifies: with 16 or 8 live heads a chunk's padding is 768 or 896 columns, not the power of two `tl.arange` needs, so TP4/TP8 keep the fused pad.
  - Work captured into a CUDA graph keeps the fused pad, so the copy applies only where this method runs outside stream capture: by default, steps above the largest captured size; under Model Runner V1, whose wide eager region spans this method, also
  captured sizes of 1024 tokens or more.
  - Deployments that select another attention backend (for example FlashInfer sparse MLA) are unaffected.
  - The CUDA op is unchanged; reworking its interleaved Q stores would keep a single launch, but in a kernel shared by every DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 backend.

  **Compatibility.**
  - Backends and platforms: the FlashMLA sparse, FlashInfer and ROCm layers do not read Q interleaved, so `_pads_q_by_copy` is false for them; mega attention itself is SM10x-only. DeepSeek-V4 (non-4.1) code is untouched.
  - TP sizes (64-head model): TP1 (64 live heads) already skips the pad; TP2 takes the copy; TP4 and TP8 are unchanged.
  - Prefill context parallelism (#59857) selects the FlashMLA layer, so it never reaches the copy; the stand-in layer of `test_v41_pcp_swa_cache_matches_non_pcp_writer` now declares `_pads_q_by_copy=False`, since that test calls
  `_fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert` on it. The SM90-only token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` (#58872) never meets mega attention, and `forward_kv` (decoder replay) builds no Q.
  - CUDA graphs: capture keeps the fused pad, so captured graphs are unchanged. Batch invariance: both paths produce the same bits, so taking the copy (which depends on the step's token count) changes no result.
  - CPU/GPU sync: none added; the decision reads `q.shape[0]`, a flag set at init and the stream's capture state.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched open PRs and PRs since 2026-08-15 for "pad interleaved q", "qnorm rope kv insert", "Q pad mega" and "heads padded 64 decode"; none moves the mega-attention Q pad out of the fused insert. Related work: #56935
  added mega attention and the fused interleaved pad this PR bypasses on large eager steps; #61371 changed the V4.1 KV record, which both launch modes share; #58872 added the token-sharded `fused_wqa_wkv` whose `_SHARD_FUSED_WQA_WKV_MIN_TOKENS` sits next
  to the new constant; #60076 (open) switches the ROCm DSpark context-KV insert to the existing KV-only `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` and touches neither mega attention nor its Q pad (it and this PR edit different tests in
  `tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py`). #55654 (open) adds KV-only insert ops (`fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_quant_insert`, and `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_norm_rope_quant_insert` with kv_norm folded in) so DeepSeek-V4's DSpark `_insert_context_kv` no
  longer builds a dummy query. This PR adds no KV op and touches neither DSpark nor DeepSeek-V4: it calls the existing `q_head_padded=0` mode of the fused op from the V4.1 attention layer. That path also sees DP-padding rows (more KV rows than slots),
  which the fused op's KV-only mode skips and #55654's ops reject. The only file both PRs touch is `tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`, where each adds tests.

  **AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to develop this change, port it onto current main, run vLLM's `pr-checklist` skill and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation reported above.

  ---

  <details>
  <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>
  <summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

  - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
  - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

  - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
