  - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
  - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [Perf][Kernel][DSv4.1] Swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention for small TP2/TP4 steps
author: roborluo
body:
## Overview

  Makes DeepSeek-V4.1's per-layer decode attention step **1.4-2.15x faster** for decode steps of up to 16 tokens at TP2 / TP4, by adding a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention kernel to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer (#56935) on SM10x. Steps of up to 16
  tokens with 16 or 32 live heads per rank (TP4 / TP2 of the 64-head model) now take it instead of the mega kernel, which pads the heads to 64.
  Part of #57448; it reads the interleaved V4.1 KV records from #61371. Related work that this PR does not duplicate (see Details): #59418, #61615, #57711, #61868.

  ## Claims

  - **1.4-2.15x faster decode attention for 1-16 tokens:** 1.8-2.15x with 16 live heads (TP4) and 1.4-1.8x with 32 (TP2), for both NVFP4 and fp8 compressed records (per-layer Q pad + KV insert + attention, table below; the lower ends are B300). End to end at TP2 this is 4.5-7.6% lower median TPOT at concurrency 1-16 (see the A/B comment). The mega kernel's FP8 decode maps
  query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads; swap-AB puts the KV slots on M and only the live heads on N.
  - **Accuracy:** the output's error against an fp64 reference is at most 1.1x the mega kernel's, and the output is within 2% of the mega kernel's, over 64 test cases.
  - **Automatic and contained.** There is no new flag, environment variable or config option. Every other decode step, layer and TP size keeps the mega kernel; prefill and other platforms are unchanged. The new kernel is CUDA-graph safe and deterministic,
  and adds no host sync.

  ## Validation

  **Performance.** This PR adds a swap-AB arm to the existing `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py`. Each arm's per-step ops (Q pad + KV insert + attention) are timed as a CUDA graph replay, the same harness that produced the mega vs split-KV
  table in `flash_mla_mega_attn.py`.

  ```bash
  for heads in 16 32; do
    for rec in 288 528; do
      .venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_dsv41_mega_attn.py \
          --local-heads $heads --extra-bytes $rec --decode-s-q 1 2 4 8 16 32 64
    done
  done
  ```

  Speedup = mega step time / swap-AB step time (median of two runs, which differ by at most 9% per cell):

  | Live heads | Compressed record | 1 token | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 | 64 |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 16 (TP4) | NVFP4 (288 B) | **2.15x** | **2.00x** | **2.06x** | **1.94x** | **2.04x** | 1.25x | 0.94x |
  | 16 (TP4) | fp8 (528 B) | **2.13x** | **1.96x** | **2.02x** | **1.90x** | **1.99x** | 1.22x | 0.91x |
  | 32 (TP2) | fp8 (528 B) | **1.76x** | **1.66x** | **1.71x** | **1.62x** | **1.71x** | 0.98x | 0.73x |

  At 32 tokens swap-AB still wins with 16 heads (1.22-1.25x) but only breaks even with 32 (0.98-1.02x), and at 64 it loses with both, so `_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS = 16` is the largest step size where it wins for both head counts. On B300 (nightly 76c6f3f2) the same harness gives 1.83-2.0x with 16 heads and 1.41-1.64x with 32 heads at 1-16 tokens, for both record formats. As in the existing harness,
  every replay reuses the same buffers, so the KV reads hit a warm L2 for both kernels; timed alone with the L2 flushed before every call, the attention kernel is 1.6-2.3x faster than the mega kernel over 48 shapes with 1-16 tokens (geomean 1.94x).

  **Correctness: unit tests.** The kernel tests skip unless the GPU is SM10x and the CuTe DSL is built with CUDA 13.2+.

  ```bash
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/test_swapab_decode.py
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v "tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py::test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode"
  ```

  | Test (cases) | Checks | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `test_matches_reference` (64) | 16/32 heads x 1/2/5/16 tokens x NVFP4/fp8 compressed records x 64/128-slot pages x partial/full lengths. Output is finite; Frobenius and max-abs error vs an fp64 reference are <= 1.1x the mega kernel's; within 2% of the
  mega output | 64 passed |
  | `test_untouched_padding` (2) | Padding heads' output groups keep their bytes | 2 passed |
  | `test_cuda_graph_and_determinism` (12) | Repeated eager calls and a CUDA graph replay agree bit for bit, also after the inputs change in place | 12 passed |
  | `test_dispatch_rule` (9, CPU) | Which kernel each dispatch condition selects | 9 passed |
  | `test_warmup_key_matches_launch` (4, CPU) | The key the layer registers at construction is the key a decode step launches, on a compressed cache shaped as the model runner binds it | 4 passed |
  | `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (3, existing) | The V4.1 cache writers and FlashMLA agree on the interleaved records the kernel reads | 3 passed |

  ## Details

  **Motivation.** Mega attention is the default DeepSeek V4.1 decode path on SM10x. Its FP8 decode kernel takes 64 or 128 query heads, so at TP2 and TP4 half or three quarters of its MMA work goes to padding heads. The mega vs split-KV note in
  `flash_mla_mega_attn.py` already records that this padded-head cost dominates small decode steps. Small steps are what low-concurrency decode and spec-decode verify and draft steps run.

  **Why a separate kernel, not a FlashMLA change.** FlashMLA's decode maps query heads to the MMA's M dimension, which is at least 64. Serving 16 or 32 heads without padding needs the opposite mapping, with KV slots on M and heads on N. That is a
  different kernel, not a smaller tile. In FlashMLA it would be CUDA C++ shipped through a vllm-project/FlashMLA release and a vLLM bump, as #61371 was. The CuTe DSL kernel instead compiles from Python at JIT warmup, needs no build change, and lives next
  to its only caller in the DSv4.1 model package. It is adapted from SGLang's swap-AB DSv4 decode attention (Apache-2.0, attribution in the file header).

  <details>
  <summary>Kernel design</summary>

  - **MMA shape.** `SwapABDecodeKernel` (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/swapab_decode_attn.py`) puts the KV slots on the tcgen05 MMA's M side (128 rows) and the live heads on N (16 or 32).
  - **One CTA per (token, KV tile).** Tiles are 64 slots of the SWA list or 128 slots of the compressed list. Each CTA:
    - gathers its slots' V4.1 records in place (fp8 528 B, NVFP4 288 B, each token's scales after its data);
    - dequantizes them exactly to bf16 in SMEM;
    - RoPEs Q in fp32 from the mega kernel's chunk-interleaved, head-padded layout;
    - computes S = KV Q^T and O = KV^T P, with P split into bf16 hi and lo parts.
  - **One cluster per token.** A token's tiles form one thread-block cluster: 6 CTAs for V4.1-Flash's 128-slot window plus 512 compressed slots. The cluster merges the partials and the attention sink over DSMEM in a fixed peer order. It then applies the
  inverse RoPE and writes MXFP8 with the mega kernel's rounding rule into the o-fused buffers `wo_a` reads, for the live heads' groups only.
  - **One launch.** The kernel uses PDL and has no workspace, second kernel, allocation or host sync.
  - **JIT warmup.** The compile key is (live heads, slot-list widths, compressed record size, SWA and compressed page sizes); the token count is the grid's y dimension. Every field is fixed when the layer is built: the backend has one kernel block size (128), so a compressed page always holds
  `128 // compress_ratio` slots, whatever the KV cache manager's block size. The layer registers the key in `__init__`, next to its other JIT warmups, and `kernel_warmup` compiles it before CUDA graph capture. V4.1-Flash needs two keys, one per compressed page size.

  </details>

  **Dispatch.** `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention._forward_decode_mega` takes the swap-AB kernel only when all of these hold:
  - the GPU is SM10x;
  - the layer has a compressed cache;
  - the layer has 16 or 32 live heads;
  - a token's tiles fit one portable cluster: `ceil(window / 64) + ceil(index_topk / 128) <= 8`;
  - the CuTe DSL imports and was built with CUDA 13.2+, which the direct fp8 / fp4 to bf16x2 conversions need (PTX ISA 9.2);
  - `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off;
  - the step has at most 16 decode tokens (`_SWAPAB_MAX_TOKENS`). Under CUDA graphs this is the padded count, so each captured graph holds exactly one of the two kernels;
  - the step's SWA list is exactly the window. DSpark's non-causal draft steps widen it, so they keep the mega kernel.

  The first six conditions are fixed when the layer is built. The last two are host-side shape checks on each step. If any condition fails, the step runs the mega kernel exactly as before.
  **Complexity.** The change adds about 1,260 lines of kernel code (about 400 of them are 23 small inline-PTX wrappers) and about 100 lines in the layer. Nothing changes in the model runner, the scheduler, FlashMLA or shared attention code. At runtime the
  kernel module is imported only by SM10x layers with a compressed cache, 16 or 32 heads and an importable CuTe DSL. Most of the maintenance cost is the inline PTX and the SMEM / TMEM layout math. Both are documented next to the code, and the tests pin
  them to an fp64 reference and to the mega kernel.

  **Tradeoffs and limitations.**
  - **Cost grows with tokens.** The kernel runs one cluster of up to 8 CTAs per token, and its 150+ KiB of SMEM means one CTA per SM. Hence the 16-token cutoff, which is the same for TP2 / TP4 and both record formats: in the table above swap-AB is at
  least 1.6x faster at every step size up to 16 tokens (at least 1.4x on B300).
  - **Not bit-identical.** The fp32 sums are ordered differently from the mega kernel's, so the output depends on which kernel the step size selects. Batch-invariant runs therefore keep the mega kernel at every size.
  - **Unused Q padding.** The fused KV insert still zero-pads Q to 64 heads, which swap-AB does not read. This keeps one Q contract for both kernels.
  - **Toolchain.** The kernel needs a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+. With an older build the layer keeps the mega kernel and the kernel tests skip.
  - **Startup.** V4.1-Flash adds two JIT compiles per worker, at warmup.

  **Compatibility.**
  - **Scope.** Only `DeepseekV4MegaAttnAttention` changes. The FlashMLA sparse layer, FlashInfer sparse MLA, and the SM90, SM120 and ROCm paths are untouched. TP1 (64 heads) and TP8 (8 heads) keep the mega kernel.
  - **Model runners.** Both V1 and V2 build the model under the JIT warmup registry, so both register the key.
  - **CUDA graphs, batch invariance, spec decode.** See Dispatch above.
  - **Unchanged.** Prefill, the KV cache layout and checkpoints.

  **CI.** The new tests run in the optional (nightly) 4xB200 step, renamed "(4xB200) DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA Kernels" (`models_basic.yaml`, key `dsv41-nvidia-kernels-4xb200`), next to the specialized-decode tests. The kernel tests need SM10x, the FlashMLA mega ops and a CuTe DSL built with CUDA 13.2+, and skip otherwise; with vLLM's pinned `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0` they run. The optional "(B200)
  LM Eval Spec Decode" step runs the V4.1-Flash NVFP4 DSpark TP4 GSM8K config. It runs at full concurrency, where few steps are small enough for swap-AB.

  **Not a duplicate.** On 2026-10-18 I searched GitHub (open PRs plus PRs since 2026-08-15) for "swap-AB", "swapab", "small-head decode", "heads padded 64 decode", "mega attention DSv4.1" and "V4.1 decode attention". No PR adds an SM10x small-head decode

title: [Perf][MRV2] Parallelize staged writes across 1024-element chunks
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

`_apply_write_kernel` (MRV2 `StagedWriteTensor` / `FusedStagedWriter`) runs one program per staged write and loops over 1024-element chunks, so writing an admitted long prompt into its `all_token_ids` row runs on a single SM. This PR launches one program per chunk instead. It also removes per-block checks from `BlockPool.get_new_blocks` when neither prefix caching nor a metrics collector is enabled.

## Claims

- Long staged writes are 31x faster at 128K tokens (76 -> 2.5 us) and 120x faster at 855K tokens (443 -> 3.7 us) on GB200. Small writes (decode steps, block tables) do not regress.
- In DEP decode, every admission ran this copy on the admitting rank right before its forward, which made that rank the straggler for the step. With this PR, admitting a request adds ~10 us of rank skew instead of ~200 us.
- `get_new_blocks` + `free_blocks` for 4000 blocks without prefix caching: 616 -> 528 us.

## Validation

**Kernel microbenchmark**, GB200, FlashInfer CUPTI, int32, old kernel copied into the script, outputs checked equal before timing:

| writes | old (us) | new (us) | speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 x 1 token (decode step) | 2.82 | 2.30 | 1.2x |
| 256 x 8 (block table) | 2.78 | 2.32 | 1.2x |
| 1 x 8K | 7.04 | 2.24 | 3.1x |
| 1 x 32K | 20.94 | 2.18 | 9.6x |
| 1 x 128K | 76.32 | 2.46 | 31.0x |
| 1 x 855K | 443.42 | 3.71 | 119.5x |
| 1 x 128K + 63 x 1 token | 75.20 | 5.94 | 12.7x |

**Serving context** (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, P/D decode instance, DEP, 128K-token prompts, GB200; measured on our internal branch, which runs the same kernel): at DEP32 BS64, the admitting rank was the last to reach the first MoE in 90 of 98 steps, 252 us behind the median rank (46 us in steps with no admission). With this change at DEP8 BS64, the last rank trails the median by 73 us when a rank admits vs 63 us when none does.

**BlockPool**: in-process CPU microbenchmark, 4000 blocks, `enable_caching=False`, no metrics collector, NUMA-pinned on GB200 Grace, best of 5 x 200: 616 us (current code path) -> 528 us.

**Tests** (GB200):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
# 266 passed, 4 skipped
```

The existing `test_staged_write_inflight` already covers multi-chunk and mixed-length writes on the `StagedWriteTensor` path. The new `test_block_tables_fused_write_spans_multiple_chunks` covers a fused write longer than one chunk.

## Details

- Grid dim 1 is `cdiv(max_write_len, 1024)`. Programs past the end of a shorter write are fully masked. Each `StagedWriteTensor` records its longest staged write as it stages, so launching adds O(1) host work. Computing the max from `cu_lens` at apply time would cost ~40 us per 1024 writes on Grace. The bytes written are unchanged, and no new sync is added.
- Tradeoff: in a batch with one long write and many short ones, the short writes launch programs that exit immediately (1 x 128K + 63 x 1: 5.9 us vs 2.5 us for 1 x 128K alone). This is still far below the old 75 us.
- `get_new_blocks`: blocks popped from the free queue always have `ref_cnt == 0`, so the no-caching, no-metrics path sets `ref_cnt = 1` directly. The caching and metrics paths are unchanged.
- Duplicate check: #62018 fuses separate staged-write calls into fewer launches, and #51334 / #59908 reduce the host-side staging cost. None of them changes how the kernel parallelizes a single long write, so they are complementary to this PR.

title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3] MonoKernel decode for M3 MXFP4 on MI355X
author: micah-wil
body:
### Summary
Adds an opt-in specialized decode path (`--monokernel`) for MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 on gfx950. During decode, layers 3–59 run their FFN half as one persistent FlyDSL launch:
- TP all-reduce, residual add and post-attention RMSNorm;
- the FP32 router with top-4 selection;
- the shared and routed BF16×MXFP4 experts;
- the final TP all-reduce.
Attention, the dense layers 0–2, prefill and mixed batches stay on the stock path.
- Follows the RFC #60904 / Kimi-K3 layout: `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/specialized_decode/`. There is one `plan()` per step, and layers are selected with `step.layer(i)`.
- Supports eager and FULL CUDA graphs, at 1–16 decode rows. Larger batches, PIECEWISE steps and prefill use the stock path.
- Startup refuses unsupported configs (default-deny), with every reason reported. Kernel faults fail-stop on every rank, and no token is returned from a failed step.
- Requirements: TP4 on gfx950, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}'`, `--moe-backend aiter`, `VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1`, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.
- Temporary dependency: imports the DeepSeek-V4.1 `mono.common` FlyDSL helpers (peer memory, sync), to move once a common AMD runtime lands.
### Results (MI355X, TP4, FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs)
Baseline is the recommended serve command. `--monokernel` adds the flags it requires.
**Random 1024 in / 1024 out**
| Concurrency | Baseline TPOT (ms) | `--monokernel` TPOT (ms) | TPOT | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.12 | 4.27 | **−16.6%** | 192 → 230 (**+19.6%**) |
| 2 | 5.54 | 4.85 | **−12.5%** | 355 → 403 (+13.4%) |
| 4 | 6.23 | 5.69 | **−8.7%** | 628 → 687 (+9.3%) |
| 8 | 7.46 | 6.88 | **−7.8%** | 1054 → 1136 (+7.8%) |
| 16 | 8.89 | 8.87 | parity | 1755 → 1751 |
| 32 (stock fallback) | 11.51 | 11.54 | parity | 2684 → 2708 |

**Long context, 8192 in / 1024 out:** TPOT −14.9% at concurrency 1 (5.25 → 4.47 ms), −9.0% at 4 (6.42 → 5.84 ms), and −3.4% at 16 (10.12 → 9.78 ms).
**MT-Bench (chat, greedy, ≤1024 output tokens):** TPOT −17.0% at concurrency 1 (5.00 → 4.15 ms; 196 → 235 tok/s), −8.6% at 4 (6.30 → 5.76 ms), and parity at 16.
Kernel-only effect, against the same server with identical flags and no `--monokernel`: TPOT −19.1% at concurrency 1, −14.3% at 2, −11.1% at 4, −8.8% at 8, and parity at 16.

### Accuracy (GSM8K 5-shot, full 1319, flexible-extract)
| Config | Score |
|---|---|
| Same flags, no `--monokernel` | 0.8969 |
| `--monokernel` | 0.9052 (paired +0.83 pp, 95% CI [−0.83, +2.50], McNemar p=0.37) |

### Commands
Baseline:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 \
vllm serve amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --block-size 128 --trust-remote-code \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --mm-encoder-tp-mode data --mm-encoder-attn-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --max-model-len 10240
```
`--monokernel`, which is the baseline plus:
```bash
VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 ... \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
  --moe-backend aiter --monokernel
```
Benchmarks. Each point is preceded by a discarded warmup with a different seed. `--num-prompts` is max(32, 4×concurrency) for random and max(16, 4×concurrency) for MT-Bench.
```bash
# random
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code --backend vllm \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# MT-Bench
vllm bench serve --model amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path philschmid/mt-bench --skip-chat-template \
  --hf-output-len 1024 --temperature 0 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --seed 1234
# accuracy
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,model=amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4,num_concurrent=4,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 1234
```
### Limitations / follow-ups
- Spec decoding is refused in this PR. The stock path is about 1.6× faster than `--monokernel` 
- TP4 only. TP2 and TP8 are follow-ups.
- At 16 rows the kernel is at parity

title: [Perf][MoE] Add H200 FP8 fused MoE config for Beam-1.0 TP8
author: ischencheng
body:
## Overview

Reflection Beam-1.0 FP8 on H200 runs TP8 with `--moe-backend triton`, as in its recipe. There is no tuned config for its fused MoE shape (`E=256, N=320`, fp8_w8a8), so every layer uses the default config. This PR adds a tuned H200 config for that shape. It also lets `benchmark_moe.py` time the per-token activation / per-channel weight FP8 path that Beam's compressed-tensors checkpoint runs, and parse `BeamForCausalLM`. Follow-up to #62074.

## Claims

- Fused MoE on 1xH200, Beam-1.0 TP8 shape, per-token FP8 path: 3-19% faster at 96-512 tokens when replaying top-k ids recorded from Beam's real weights, and 9-45% faster at 96-1536 tokens with uniform random routing. At 1024 tokens the kernel goes from 31% to 57% of the HBM bound.
- One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 on 1xH200 (all 52 layers, dummy weights, uniform simulated routing): a decode step at 128 and 256 requests takes 9.4% and 16.7% less time.
- Up to 64 tokens and from 2048 tokens the file holds the default config, so small-batch decode and prefill do not change. With DFlash2 (recipe: 7 draft tokens), a verify step has 8 rows per request, so 12-192 requests land in the range that gets faster.
- `benchmark_moe.py` now times the kernel variant the model runs: for compressed-tensors checkpoints with `strategy: token` input activations it uses per-token activation and per-channel weight scales. Before, it always timed per-tensor FP8.

## Validation

### Kernel with recorded routing (1xH200)

Top-k ids recorded from Beam-1.0 FP8 with real weights (first 6 layers, so MoE layers 3-5, TP1), decode batches of M requests over two corpora: Python and Markdown files from site-packages, and wikitext-103. They are replayed on the TP8 shape (`E=256, N=320, K=5120`, top-8, per-token FP8) with this file and with the default config. 24 recorded steps per M in one CUDA graph, median of 7 replays, µs per step.

| M | code corpus: default → this PR | wikitext: default → this PR | uniform random: default → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 213.9 → 214.0 (+0.0%) | 180.4 → 180.0 (-0.2%) | 313.5 → 313.7 (+0.1%) |
| 96 | 244.5 → 229.8 (-6.0%) | 211.2 → 204.7 (-3.1%) | 357.9 → 326.1 (-8.9%) |
| 128 | 280.5 → 253.2 (-9.7%) | 239.1 → 223.3 (-6.6%) | 387.7 → 337.9 (-12.8%) |
| 256 | 384.7 → 311.4 (-19.1%) | 339.2 → 277.4 (-18.2%) | 468.4 → 357.8 (-23.6%) |
| 512 | 445.4 → 390.2 (-12.4%) | 414.0 → 357.3 (-13.7%) | 488.3 → 397.3 (-18.6%) |

Real routing is not uniform: a decode batch of 128 touches 156 (code) or 133 (wikitext) of 256 experts per layer, against 252 for uniform routing, and the busiest expert gets 76-85 rows. So these steps load fewer experts and are shorter than the uniform ones.

### Kernel with uniform routing (1xH200)

`benchmark_moe.benchmark_config` on the per-token path (`per_act_token_quant=True`), random gating, CUDA graph of 10 calls, 100 iterations, median of 3 runs. "Bound" is the expert weights that uniform routing touches, `256 * (1 - (1 - 8/256)^M) * 4.92 MB`, over 4.8 TB/s; FP8 compute is below that at every M here.

| M | bound µs | default µs (of bound) | this PR µs (of bound) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96 | 250.1 | 366.2 (68%) | 334.4 (75%) | -8.7% |
| 128 | 258.2 | 398.5 (65%) | 346.6 (74%) | -13.0% |
| 256 | 263.2 | 475.2 (55%) | 365.1 (72%) | -23.2% |
| 512 | 264.3 | 497.8 (53%) | 407.0 (65%) | -18.2% |
| 1024 | 266.5 | 856.7 (31%) | 470.1 (57%) | -45.1% |
| 1536 | 268.7 | 902.0 (30%) | 519.7 (52%) | -42.4% |

At 1-64 tokens the tuned configs were within -4% to +0.3% of the default here, and +1.9% at 64 on the recorded code corpus, so the file keeps the default config there.

### One TP8 rank of Beam-1.0 FP8 (1xH200)

All 52 layers and 256 experts; attention heads and widths are one TP8 rank's share (6 Q heads, 1 KV head, expert width 320). Dummy weights with `VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY=uniform_random`, `--moe-backend triton`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Arms ran in one container in the order default, tuned, tuned, default. ms per decode step, median of 4 runs; spread within an arm is under 0.3%.

| | default | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode, 16 requests | 12.13 | 12.12 | -0.1% |
| decode, 128 requests | 25.95 | 23.51 | -9.4% |
| decode, 256 requests | 31.67 | 26.38 | -16.7% |
| 8K prefill chunk | 180.6 | 180.6 | 0.0% |

This run used the tuned configs at 1-64 tokens as well; the file now holds the default there, which only matters for the 16-request row.

### Correctness

Only Triton tile parameters change. At the Beam shape and M = 96, 128, 256, 1024 and 1536, the output with this file and with the default config both have a mean relative error of 1.41-1.44% against the per-column reference in `tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py` (its threshold is 5%). Both configs use `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128`, and the outputs were the same.

`benchmark_moe.py --model reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8 --tp-size 8 --dtype fp8_w8a8 --batch-size 1 128 1024` runs on this branch and prints `Benchmarking per-token activation and per-channel weight FP8.` before the timings (checked on an L4, which has no config file and uses the default config). The tuning run above used the same `benchmark_config` path.

## Details

- Dummy weights route almost every token of a step to the same 8 experts, so each expert sees many rows and larger M tiles win. Without uniform simulated routing, the proxy above shows this file 9.8% and 13.0% slower at 128 and 256 requests. The recorded real routing sits much closer to uniform than to that.
- Per-tensor and per-token FP8 read the same config file name. For this shape, configs tuned on the per-tensor path time within 1% of these on the per-token path.
- The search space was pruned to keep tuning near half an hour: `BLOCK_SIZE_M` 16 up to 128 tokens, 16-32 up to 512, 16-64 above; `GROUP_SIZE_M` in {1, 16, 64}. The pruning was in my tuning script, not in `benchmark_moe.py`.
- Not covered: H100, TP4 (`N=640`), DFlash2 verify, and the full model. 503 GB FP8 needs 8xH200, which I did not run. The recorded routing comes from 3 early MoE layers; later layers may route differently.

Not a duplicate: no open PR adds a fused MoE config for `E=256,N=320`, and none adds per-token FP8 to `benchmark_moe.py`. The open `benchmark_moe.py` PRs change model parsing or error handling (#62526, #49088, #50711, #51353), or add zipf-skewed expert loads (#57100), which is a separate axis from the quantization path here. #61688 (runtime Triton autotune, draft) would make static configs less important if it lands.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the change, run the tuning and the measurements above, and draft this description.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Synchronize adaptive DSpark decisions across TP ranks
author: okorzh-amd
body:
This carries #56831 by @CedricHwong forward to current main. That PR has been idle since 09-14 and no longer passes CI after the rebase. Cedric's commit is kept unchanged, with his authorship. The two commits on top address the review comments on that PR.

Adaptive verification (DSpark) picks the per-step draft budget on the host from rank-local stale confidences, then picks which slots to keep on the device from rank-local live confidences. If TP ranks disagree on either one, they run different batch layouts: different token counts, or equal totals with different request boundaries. That breaks the collectives that follow and can hang them (#54011). This PR makes TP rank 0 authoritative:

1. `get_num_tokens`: `draft_budget` is broadcast with `broadcast_object` (shm MessageQueue, host only).
2. `reallocate_drafts`: on steps that trim, the per-request `capacities` are broadcast from rank 0 before `cu_num_logits` / `query_start_loc` are built.

Both conditions around (2), `draft_budget == 0` and `draft_budget < scheduled drafts`, depend only on the broadcast budget and scheduler-provided counts. Every TP rank therefore takes the same branch, and the collective cannot be entered unevenly.

### Changes vs #56831

- **Test updates for current main.** #56888 renamed `async_copy_to_gpu` to `async_tensor_h2d`; the old monkeypatch no longer resolved, giving 12 failures, and `cpu.yaml` runs `-x`. #58466 made `reallocate_drafts` also return the admitted draft counts. #63421 replaced the compiled budget assignment with a Triton kernel; the CPU test stands in for it with its global top-k reference. #55939 made `tests/v1/spec_decode` type-checked, so the test now narrows `_batch_budget` before indexing it.
- **Real multi-rank test.** `test_tp_ranks_agree_on_verification_layout[2, 4]` spawns gloo ranks with a real TP `GroupCoordinator` and drives the real `get_num_tokens` / `reallocate_drafts`. The ranks' confidences differ by one fp32 ULP, across three cases: a draft-budget tie, an equal-total boundary split, and 64 randomized steps. Every rank must end up with the leader's budget, capacities, `cu_num_logits` and `query_start_loc`. It replaces the single-process budget emulation.
- **Transport.** The capacities sync uses plain `get_tp_group().broadcast`, i.e. c10d on the TP device group, as in #56831.
  - Routing `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` through the device communicator (PyNCCL) would be about 2x cheaper per call. On CUDA it would also avoid creating the device group's NCCL communicator on the first trimmed step. But it changes every `GroupCoordinator.broadcast` caller (PCP `sync_drafts` too) and needs XPU validation, so it will be a separate PR.

Scope: this covers TP. It also covers DCP when PCP = 1; DCP groups span PCP before TP. With PCP > 1, each PCP slice's TP group has its own leader. Since #61994, DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA rejects AV + PCP (it requires fixed-length DSpark). The generic `PCPManager` path still admits it, which predates this PR and is a follow-up.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py`, plus `mypy` / `ruff` via the pre-commit pins.
- Multi-rank CPU harness: real gloo groups, the real `GroupCoordinator` and the real `AdaptiveVerificationManager`. TP 2/4/8, with injected per-rank confidence drift from 1 ULP to large.
- MI355X microbenchmark of both collectives, using vLLM's real TP group (`init_distributed_environment` + `initialize_model_parallel`) at TP2/TP4.
- MI355X end to end:
  - Model: Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7` with `enable_adaptive_verification: true`, V2 model runner, ROCM_ATTN.
  - Workload: 600 GSM8K CoT prompts, output 512, greedy.
  - A/B: main vs this PR, conc 1/16/64, 4 interleaved rounds per arm.
  - Divergence check: an instrumented main that all-gathers every rank's locally computed budget, capacities and confidences on every step.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests** (on main `7e3e3f6ab6`): `test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 31 passed and 7 skipped (the CUDA-only kernel tests). mypy and ruff are clean, and the real-rank test passed 10 of 10 runs.
  - **Without the budget broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the budget tie; 36/64 random steps diverge at TP2, 53/64 at TP4.
  - **Without the capacities broadcast:** the real-rank test fails on the boundary case (4/64 random steps at TP2, 10/64 at TP4: equal totals, different request boundaries). The emulated reallocation tests at TP 2/4/8 fail too.
- **Multi-rank harness:** 0 mismatches on this branch at every world size and drift level.
  - Without the fix, a single fp32 ULP is enough to change the layout. Mismatching steps per 1000 at TP 2/4/8 (capacities or boundaries):
    - 1-16 ULP: 0-2
    - 1e-4 relative: 2-9
    - 1e-2 relative: 65-382
  - Most mismatches have equal totals across ranks but different request boundaries.
- **Per-step cost, MI355X, p50 (p90), slowest rank:**

| | TP2 | TP4 |
|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_object(budget)`: every step that has drafts, host only | 6.7 us (7.5) | 7.9 us (8.2) |
| `capacities` broadcast (c10d, as in this PR): trimmed steps only. Host enqueue + in-stream GPU time; does not depend on num_reqs from 1 to 256 | ~32 + ~25 us | ~33 + ~26 us |
| Worst-case total for a trimmed step, with no overlap | ~64 us | ~68 us (p90 ~76) |

  That is 0.4-1.4% of a 5-15 ms decode step, at most. The host part overlaps GPU work under async scheduling. With PyNCCL (the planned follow-up), a trimmed step costs about 25-29 us.
- **End to end at TP2, measured with the capacities sync on PyNCCL (an earlier revision of this PR); the c10d path still needs an e2e run (GPUs were busy): no measurable regression.** Each delta is within about 1.2 standard deviations; run-to-run CV is 0.2-0.6%.

| conc | output tok/s, main | output tok/s, this PR | delta | TPOT p50, main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 721.0 ± 4.1 | 727.7 ± 10 | +0.9% | 1.311 → 1.314 ms |
| 16 | 5489 ± 12 | 5493 ± 15 | +0.1% | 2.755 → 2.763 ms |
| 64 | 10590 ± 50 | 10585 ± 19 | -0.1% | 5.615 → 5.629 ms |

  Acceptance length is unchanged (±0.7%). There were 0 failed requests in 24 runs. The `capacities` broadcast fired on about 97% of c16/c64 steps and about 7% of c1 steps.
- **Natural divergence was not observed on this setup.**
  - Instrumented main ran 8434 steps at TP2 and 7886 steps at TP4: 0 budget, capacities or confidence mismatches.
  - A separate DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MI355X serving trace ran about 478k AV steps, also with 0 mismatches.
  - Here the confidence inputs are bitwise identical across ranks, because the custom all-reduce sums in a fixed rank order. Divergence needs rank-asymmetric numerics, such as rank-order-dependent reductions, non-deterministic kernels, or the TP8 H20 DeepSeek-V4 setup in #54011.
  - The fix is cheap insurance against that: per the numbers above, about 7 us host per step plus about 19 us per trimmed step.

Co-authored with @CedricHwong (original fix, #56831). Supersedes #56831.

title: [Spec Decode][MRV2] Skip drafting in steps where no request can use the drafts
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Overview

Continues #48244 by @njhill (co-author). In steps where no scheduled request can use the
drafts proposed after the step, the speculator now proposes with K=0 instead of
drafting. Such requests are non-final prefill chunks and requests sure to reach
`max_tokens`. This covers every request on a P/D prefill instance, which runs with
`max_tokens=1`.

Related: #39266 (draft) skips EAGLE drafting on MRV2 for P/D prefill instances and
non-final chunks; this PR decides in the scheduler and also covers requests about to
finish, DFlash and DP. #53426 makes the K=0 draft sync forward optional; this PR keeps
that forward.

## Claims

- On Model Runner V2, when no scheduled request on any DP rank can use the drafts, the
  speculator runs with `num_speculative_tokens=0`:
  - EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP still run the draft prefill pass, which keeps the drafter's KV cache
    in sync, but skip draft sampling and the draft decode steps.
  - DFlash stores the context K/V and skips the query pass. DSpark, DFlash2 and
    LiLiCorr share this code.
- The drafter's prefill pass still runs, so the gain is modest. Prefill-only throughput
  (Qwen3-8B, 64 x 16,384-token prompts, 1 output token, one GB300 GPU) improves by
  **+1.9% with EAGLE3** and **+7.3% with DFlash** at `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, and by
  +1.4% and +2.7% at 2048. On a 1P1D prefill instance every step proposes with K=0,
  and prefill throughput improves by +2.1% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512, and by
  +0.6% and +1.9% at 2048.
- Outputs and acceptance do not change. With batch-invariant kernels, outputs and every
  spec-decode counter are identical to `main`.

## Validation

Qwen3-8B with `AngelSlim/Qwen3-8B_eagle3` (K=3) and `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (K=16),
`--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN`, GB300. Baseline is `main` at `532a7d19d2`, the base of
this PR; every run below used the rebased commit.

An earlier version of this description reported +9.0% (EAGLE3) and +3.4% (DFlash) at 512.
Those runs were CPU-starved (the benchmark processes were confined to one CPU core),
which inflated host-side costs. The numbers below replace them.

**Prefill-only throughput** (total tokens/s; mean of 3 reps on one engine after a warm-up
pass). The workload matches `vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random
--random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 64 --max-model-len 20480`.
main and this PR ran at the same time on two GPUs of one node, then swapped GPUs. The
table shows the GPU whose reps stayed within 1%; on the other GPU, reps of both builds
varied by up to 30%. With the PR, every proposal in these runs used K=0.

| Method | `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | Step time saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 72,100 | 73,144 | +1.4% | 0.4 ms |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 33,834 | 34,473 | **+1.9%** | 0.3 ms |
| DFlash | 2048 | 72,569 | 74,508 | +2.7% | 0.7 ms |
| DFlash | 512 | 32,367 | 34,730 | **+7.3%** | 1.1 ms |

The skipped work is draft sampling and the draft decode steps (EAGLE3), or the query pass
(DFlash). Host time spent in `propose()` at 512 drops from 1.41 to 0.98 ms per step for
EAGLE3 and from 1.05 to 0.92 ms for DFlash; the rest of the saving is GPU time. The
drafter's prefill pass still runs: it writes the draft KV cache that later steps, and on
a P/D decode instance the transferred KV, depend on.

**1P1D prefill throughput.** P and D each on one GPU with `NixlConnector`, the same
drafter on both, P at the given `max_num_batched_tokens`. Through the toy proxy, 3
phases of 128 random 8,192-token prompts at concurrency 32 (`max_tokens=8`). P's waiting
queue was non-empty in at least 89% of samples. main and this PR ran side by side on the
node's two GPU pairs, then swapped; tokens/s and deltas are means over both placements.

| Method | P `max_num_batched_tokens` | main | this PR | Delta | P proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | 2048 | 56,809 | 57,213 | +0.6% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| EAGLE3 | 512 | 28,447 | 29,043 | **+2.1%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |
| DFlash | 2048 | 56,950 | 57,883 | +1.9% | 3,072 / 3,072 |
| DFlash | 512 | 28,527 | 29,524 | **+3.4%** | 12,288 / 12,288 |

**Equivalence** (offline, greedy). There are 80 requests: 24 long prompts chunked at 512
tokens with `max_tokens` 1, 2 or 64, run alone and then mixed with 32 short decode
requests.

| Method | Mode | Outputs equal | Spec-decode counters | Proposals with K=0 (PR) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EAGLE3 | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (3,349 drafts, 1,775 accepted) | 19 |
| DFlash | `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` | 80/80 | identical (2,244 drafts, 2,953 accepted) | 18 |

Without batch invariance, two runs of `main` already differ on 23/80 EAGLE3 outputs, and
main vs this PR differ on 31/80. DFlash is deterministic across runs of `main`, but main
vs this PR differ on 31/80: in a K=0 step DFlash stores all context K/V in one eager
pass instead of partly inside the FULL graph, so rounding can differ, and acceptance then
changes batch shapes.

**Existing e2e tests** give the same results on both:

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/eagle/test_eagle_correctness.py -k "medium and qwen3_eagle3 and not transformers"` | GSM8K 0.886, pass | GSM8K 0.886, pass |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py` (MRV2 reference acceptance) | MT-Bench 4.07, HumanEval 6.42, GSM8K 6.42 | same |
| `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py::test_dflash_correctness[qwen3-mrv2]` | GSM8K 0.884, AL 4.12 | same |

**Serving equivalence.** 1P1D with `NixlConnector` used EAGLE3 K=3 on both sides and CUDA
graphs on. DP=2 used EAGLE3 K=3. Requests were sent one at a time.

| Setup | Outputs equal | Decode-side acceptance length |
|---|---|---|
| 1P1D | 40/40 | identical (1.521, 1.598) |
| DP=2 | 40/40 | identical (1.539, 1.597) |

There were no hangs with DP ranks voting to skip.

**Unit tests.** `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`,
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py` and
`tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py` pass (281 tests), except two
pre-existing PP scheduler tests that fail the same way on `main`.

## Details

- **Scheduler.** It sets `SchedulerOutput.skip_drafts` when no scheduled request can use
  the step's drafts, on the V2 runner and for drafters that reserve lookahead slots.
  `_drafts_unused` counts only the output tokens a request is sure to have, assuming
  every draft is rejected, so it never skips drafts a later step could verify.
- **DP.** The flag is ANDed across ranks in the batch-descriptor all-reduce that already
  runs, giving `DPSyncState.skip_drafts`. The runner then proposes with K=0. A rank
  running a dummy batch votes no, so an idle DP rank disables the skip for that step.
- **Changes from #48244:**
  - The per-request lookahead-slot skip is dropped. For a non-final chunk, the lookahead
    slots are the next chunk's first positions, which are allocated one step later
    anyway. For a finishing request it saves at most about one block for one step.
    Keeping it safely means masking every draft KV write, including inside captured
    FULL draft-decode graphs; the fused decode path is the default on FlashAttention,
    FlashInfer and Triton, and its captured graphs compute their own slot mappings.
  - Skipping reuses the existing `num_speculative_tokens == 0` path, which already skips
    the AR draft decode steps, instead of a separate flag in each speculator.
    `skip_sample` and the DFlash early return also apply to K=0 from dynamic speculative
    decoding.
  - The scheduler reports one flag instead of a set of request ids.
- **Not covered.** Multi-module MTP and the draft-model speculator ignore K, so they
  still draft in these steps and the drafts go unused, as before. N-gram reserves no
  lookahead slots, so the flag is never set for it. MTP, DSpark, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr
  share the changed code but were not run; all validation used Qwen3-8B. MRV1 is
  unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Throughput script (one engine, warm-up then timed reps)</summary>

```python
llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B", speculative_config=spec, max_model_len=20480,
          max_num_batched_tokens=mbt, enable_prefix_caching=False, seed=42,
          attention_backend="FLASH_ATTN")
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
prompts = lambda n: [TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=r.tolist())
                     for r in rng.integers(1000, 100000, size=(n, 16384))]
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True)
llm.generate(prompts(8), params)
for _ in range(3):
    batch = prompts(64)
    t = time.perf_counter(); llm.generate(batch, params)
    print(64 * 16385 / (time.perf_counter() - t))
```
</details>

---

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3] Enable GLM low-latency BF16 GEMM on SM107
author: csahithi
body:
## Overview


The GLM-5.2/5.3 low-latency BF16 GEMM selection (CuTe DSL skinny GEMM + `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` at decode batch sizes) is gated to SM103, so on VRNVL72 (SM107) every unquantized decode projection runs cuBLAS. This PR enables the selection on SM107 with a table swept on VRNVL72, the same way #54606 enabled the Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM plan on SM107.

## Claims


- **VRNVL72 coverage:** on SM107, GLM-5.2/5.3 BF16 decode projections use tuned CuTe DSL skinny GEMM / `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` configs where they beat cuBLAS. That covers fused qkv_a, q_b / indexer wq_b, o_proj (M ≤ 3), indexer wk + weights_proj, shared-expert gate_up / down and MTP eh_proj, at TP4. TP8 q_b keeps the existing SM103 row, re-measured on sm107.
- **Kernel times:** each shape is 1.2× to 1.9× faster than cuBLAS at its target M on VRNVL72 (table below).
- **End-to-end (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, VRNVL72, 8k in / 1k out, vs `main` behavior):** output throughput rises by +8.1% at c1 (ITL 6.35 → 5.86 ms), +5.9% at c2 and +2.2% at c4–c8 without speculative decoding. With MTP K=3 it rises +8.5% at c1, in a single run.
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K is unchanged within run-to-run noise: 0.9735 stock vs 0.9773 with this PR.
- **No change on other devices:** SM103 keeps its existing table and routing (same shapes, M ranges, backends and CuTe warmup set). Every other device stays on the default GEMM. Checked on B300: tests, routing, GSM8K and throughput are unchanged (see Validation).

## Validation


**Kernel microbenchmark** (one VRNVL72 GPU, BF16, CuTe DSL skinny GEMM vs cuBLAS; a (shape, M) entry is in the table only where CuTe wins by more than the 0.15 µs noise band):

| Projection (local N×K, TP4) | M | CuTe (µs) | cuBLAS (µs) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fused qkv_a, replicated (2624×6144) | 4 | 5.84 | 6.91 | 1.18× |
| q_b / indexer wq_b (4096×2048) | 4 | 4.31 | 5.71 | 1.32× |
| o_proj (6144×4096) | 1 | 5.90 | 7.77 | 1.32× |
| indexer wk + weights_proj (160×6144) | 4 | 2.83 | 5.43 | 1.92× |
| shared expert gate_up (1024×6144) | 4 | 3.96 | 5.40 | 1.36× |
| shared expert down (6144×512) | 4 | 3.19 | 4.28 | 1.34× |
| MTP eh_proj (6144×12288) | 1 | 12.90 | 16.96 | 1.31× |

M=4 is the target-model batch for one request with MTP K=3. The TP8 q_b entry (2048×2048) is the existing SM103 row; re-measured on VRNVL72, it beats cuBLAS at every measured M:
- CuTe at M=1–2: 3.2–3.3 vs 5.0 µs.
- `dsv3_fused_a_gemm` at M=3–16: 4.0–4.2 vs 4.9–5.1 µs.

**Decode step profile** (nsys, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 on one VRNVL72 tray, MTP K=3, c=1; the SM107 table vs the SM103 table reused on SM107):
- Step time: 6.97 → 6.87 ms.
- Kernels per step: 2,004 → 1,801.
- Dense-GEMM kernel time: 4,355 → 3,859 µs per step.

Less of the GEMM saving reaches step time because at c=1 the routed-MoE chain on the auxiliary stream is the critical path.

**Accuracy:** GSM8K 5-shot 0.9765 with this change combined with other decode-path changes, vs 0.976 stock (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, VRNVL72, real MTP verification).

**Tests:**
- `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm`.
- GPU (SM103 / SM107): the shape tests now cover the union of both tables' CuTe configs and the SM107 `dsv3_fused_a` range.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `typos` pass at the versions pinned in pre-commit.

**End-to-end A/B** 
- **Model and hardware:** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4 on one VRNVL72 node.
- **Server:** the 8k1k recipe (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 9216 --quantization modelopt_fp4`, Rust front end).
- **Client:** aiperf, synthetic 8000 in / 1000 out, ignore_eos, at least 20 requests per point (5×C at c8).
- **Run order:** stock and this PR alternated (stock, PR, stock, PR), then the MTP arms.
- **Engagement:** every PR arm logged the SM107 table as installed, with both backends available.

| Spec decoding | c | Stock out tok/s (run 1 / run 2) | This PR out tok/s (run 1 / run 2) | Δ | Stock ITL (ms) | This PR ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 1 | 153.0 (152.6 / 153.4) | 165.3 (165.2 / 165.4) | **+8.1%** | 6.35 | 5.86 |
| none | 2 | 286.6 (287.5 / 285.6) | 303.5 (303.0 / 304.0) | **+5.9%** | 6.69 | 6.30 |
| none | 4 | 506.2 (505.7 / 506.6) | 517.5 (517.6 / 517.4) | **+2.2%** | 7.42 | 7.26 |
| none | 8 | 860.2 (858.0 / 862.3) | 879.4 (877.3 / 881.6) | **+2.2%** | 8.58 | 8.39 |
| MTP K=3 | 1 | 201.1 | 218.2 | +8.5% | 4.78 | 4.39 |
| MTP K=3 | 2 | 350.4 | 357.6 | +2.0% | 5.27 | 5.27 |
| MTP K=3 | 4 | 555.1 | 562.2 | +1.3% | 6.74 | 6.53 |

- **Variability:** the two runs per arm without MTP differ by at most 0.7%, well below the deltas.
- **MTP rows:** one run per arm. Sampling is at temperature 1, so acceptance varies: the mean acceptance length over the sweep was 1.58 (stock) vs 1.61 (PR), so part of the MTP difference may come from acceptance.

---

title: [Perf][glm5next] Add SM121 TP=2 skinny-GEMM plans for GLM-5.3-Flash
author: TimRen01
body:
## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash decode TPOT **-15% at concurrency 1 on 2x DGX Spark (SM121, TP=2)** by running the BF16 decode GEMMs on the CuTe DSL skinny GEMM instead of cuBLAS. On `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` the attention projections (KDA and MLA), shared experts and LM head stay BF16 and take roughly 46 of a 68 ms decode step on cuBLAS gemv. `glm5next` has no low-latency GEMM module yet, so this adds one modelled on `qwen4_exp/nvidia/low_latency_gemm.py` (#59753, #59632, #61437) with measured SM121 skinny-GEMM plans for the TP=2 local shapes, installed from `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextMTP`. Supersedes #62949.

## Claims

- 7 local `(N, K)` shapes at M = 1/2/4 (20 entries), routed only on capability `(12, 1)`; other GPUs, dtypes, token counts and shapes keep the standard linear path (cuBLAS).
- Kernel: skinny GEMM is 1.35x to 1.73x faster than cuBLAS gemv at M=1 (238-283 GB/s vs 162-176 GB/s), 1.04x to 1.36x at M=2/4.
- End to end, no speculation, concurrency 1: TPOT 64.0 -> 54.1 ms (-15%), 15.3 -> 18.0 tok/s. With MTP k=3 the decode step is one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1: ITL -3.6%, TPOT -2.7%, 26.7 -> 27.8 tok/s.
- GSM8K (n=100): 93 with cuBLAS, 94 with skinny GEMM.

## Validation

Kernel, cuBLAS (`F.linear`) vs skinny GEMM through the module path on GB10 (CUDA graph replay, weight rotated out of L2, nightly 8e2beaa3bf), cosine 1.000000 between the two outputs for every entry:

| shape (N, K) | layer | M | cuBLAS (us) | skinny GEMM (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (12576, 4096) | KDA in_proj | 1 | 608 | 429 | 1.42x |
|  |  | 2 | 453 | 425 | 1.07x |
|  |  | 4 | 450 | 429 | 1.05x |
| (4096, 4096) | KDA o_proj | 1 | 203 | 137 | 1.48x |
|  |  | 2 | 147 | 136 | 1.08x |
|  |  | 4 | 148 | 140 | 1.06x |
| (2048, 4096) | shared gate_up, MLA qkv_a | 1 | 103 | 64 | 1.61x |
|  |  | 2 | 78 | 64 | 1.22x |
|  |  | 4 | 79 | 63 | 1.24x |
| (4096, 1024) | shared down | 1 | 51 | 30 | 1.73x |
|  |  | 2 | 39 | 29 | 1.34x |
|  |  | 4 | 39 | 29 | 1.36x |
| (8192, 1536) | MLA q_b | 1 | 147 | 102 | 1.44x |
|  |  | 2 | 115 | 102 | 1.13x |
|  |  | 4 | 122 | 101 | 1.20x |
| (4096, 8192) | MLA o_proj | 1 | 291 | - | not included |
|  |  | 2 | 289 | 278 | 1.04x |
|  |  | 4 | 300 | 280 | 1.07x |
| (77440, 4096) | lm_head | 1 | 3606 | 2663 | 1.35x |
|  |  | 2 | 2789 | 2655 | 1.05x |
|  |  | 4 | 2741 | 2581 | 1.06x |

These are cold-L2 numbers, which is the serving case: decode reads each weight once per step and 45 layers do not fit the 24 MB L2. Weighted by how often each shape runs in a decode step, the entries save about 13 ms per step at M=1 and 3 ms at M=2 or M=4 in the probe; the server gains 10 ms at M=1 because the GEMMs interleave with MoE and attention. MLA o_proj at M=1 is not included: cuBLAS already streams this shape at 231 GB/s (162-176 GB/s on the other shapes), so the best skinny config from the sweep gained only 3% in the module path, under the 5% bar. M=8/16 are within 2% of cuBLAS and are not listed.

End to end, cuBLAS (current main) vs skinny GEMM (this PR): `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` TP=2 on two Sparks, FP8 KV, SPEED-Bench 2K in / 1K out, 8 requests at concurrency 1, greedy (`--temperature 0`), two interleaved runs per arm (each cell lists run 1 / run 2), nightly 8e2beaa3bf:

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | GSM8K (n=100) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 64.17 / 63.83 | 63.94 / 63.68 | 15.27 / 15.33 | 93 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 54.14 / 54.10 | 54.03 / 53.96 | 18.02 / 18.03 | 94 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | **-15.4%** | -15.4% | +17.8% | +1 |

With MTP k=3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8`, same nightly and sampling):

| | TPOT p50 (ms) | ITL p50 (ms) | Output tok/s | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cuBLAS (main) | 36.05 / 36.11 | 102.72 / 103.27 | 26.79 / 26.66 | 2.87 / 2.87 |
| skinny GEMM (this PR) | 35.08 / 35.16 | 99.18 / 99.41 | 27.51 / 28.02 | 2.85 / 2.90 |
| change (mean of the two runs) | -2.7% | **-3.6%** | +3.9% | +0.2% |

With MTP the ITL is the decode step (one verify pass at M=4 plus three draft passes at M=1); TPOT and tok/s divide it by the tokens accepted per step. Under greedy decoding the acceptance length stays within 2.85-2.90 across the four runs, so the step gain carries over: TPOT -2.7%, tok/s +3.9%. An earlier 4-request run at model-default sampling gave -12% without speculation (the number in the commit message); with MTP its acceptance length swung 3% between repeats, which hid the step gain.

An nsys census of the skinny GEMM arm shows every listed shape on `CuteSkinnyGemm` in the server (45% of GPU time without speculation, 39.5% with MTP); what is left on cuBLAS is KDA `f_b`/`g_b` (4096, 128) (#57617), the fp32-output router gate (288, 4096) and MLA o_proj at M=1.

Tests: `pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next`, 26 passed on GB10 (table validity, capability routing, hook installation, 20 selected shapes with cosine > 0.999 against `F.linear`). The selected-shape test skips off capability (12, 1), which CI does not have.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction</summary>

```bash
# on each DGX Spark, --node-rank 0 / 1
vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
  --master-addr 192.168.100.1 --master-port 29500 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.84 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --reasoning-parser glm45 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
# MTP k=3 arm: add --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
#   and use --gpu-memory-utilization 0.875 --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 8
# SPEED_BENCH_DIR holds throughput_2k.jsonl, built from nvidia/SPEED-Bench with NeMo-Skills prepare.py
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name speed_bench --dataset-path $SPEED_BENCH_DIR --speed-bench-dataset-subset throughput_2k \
  --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos --num-warmups 2 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 1 \
  --temperature 0 --seed 0
pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py -k glm5next
```

</details>

## Details

- Plans come from a CUDA-graph sweep over block_size, outputs_per_block, k_unroll, vector_width and static_k with the weight rotated out of L2, keeping entries that beat cuBLAS by more than 5%. `(2048, 4096)` serves both the shared-expert gate/up and the MLA fused q_a/kv_a projection.
- The replacement method follows the quant method the layer carries: a quant config that excludes `lm_head` gives `ParallelLMHead` an `UnquantizedLinearMethod` rather than an `UnquantizedEmbeddingMethod`, and the head stayed on cuBLAS until this was handled.
- Not covered: TP=1 (the model does not fit one Spark), KDA `f_b`/`g_b` `(4096, 128)` (#57617), MTP `eh_proj` (a plain `nn.Linear`), and M=3, which uses cuBLAS.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the sweep scripts, the module and the tests; all code and measurements were reviewed and run by the author.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1/K2 for the TP2 compress-ratio-2 layers on MI355X
author: chao-xu-spec
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Faster K1/K2 for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono decode layer on gfx950 (MI355X), applied only to the compress-ratio-2 target layers at TP2. A static build flag, `MonoBuild.tuned`, selects the new paths; their outputs are bit-identical to main's, and every other build (ratio 0/1, TP4, DSpark draft, gfx942, FFN launch) compiles to the same MLIR as on main.

1. **Tuned builds of the ratio-2 layers**: the `MonoBuild.tuned` gate with its own scratch; unsigned index math in the MoE stages; polled ready flags replicated on separate lines; independent loads issued ahead of waits.
2. **Down stage**: two-task down CTAs pipeline their rounds through LDS; their shared-expert down rows are offloaded to the next one-task CTAs.
3. **FFN seam and attention hand-offs**: a shorter seam -> norm -> router chain, whole-sector attention partials, per-tile `wo_a` ready flags.

Each commit builds and is bit-exact on its own. Related: #61482 (moves these kernels to `vllm/models/common/amd/mono/`).

**Rebased** onto main 8977b13a1c, which includes #63576 (K2's combine awaits `krdy` before reading `klen` in index-source launches) and #63689 (vLLM's scale code for zero and subnormal MXFP8 groups). Both fixes apply to the tuned builds as well: the tuned paths share `stage_combine` and its `krdy` wait, and quantize with the same `vllm_mx_code` / `mx_code`. No conflicts; the diff is unchanged.

**Result vs main:** ratio-2 layer K1+K2 8.6-18.1% faster (M = 1..48), index-source launches included; E2E TPOT p50 −3.3% (c32) and −3.7% (c4).

## Validation

8x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39` (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0; no kernel or build changes between it and the base commit); only the Python tree differs between arms.

**Repo tests**

```bash
pytest -v tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py \
  tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py
```

| GPUs | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) | 80 passed, 2 skipped (gfx942 only) |
| 2 | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) | 78 passed, 4 skipped (2 need 4 GPUs) |

The numerics test also checks the tuned layer bit for bit against a `generic=True` runner at 12/36/48 rows.

**Correctness vs main**: 115/115 cases bit-identical at TP2 (92 on tuned builds; all K1+K2 outputs and the SWA cache, hashed per rank, index-source and no-fold launches included). The MLIR of every non-tuned build is byte-identical to main's (168/168 gfx950, 76/76 gfx942).

**Layer microbench** (TP2, ratio 2, K1+K2 µs per layer, cold L2, max over ranks, median of 11 fresh runs on 3 GPU pairs):

| M | 1 | 6 | 12 | 18 | 24 | 36 | 48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 89.1 | 134.4 | 194.1 | 238.2 | 292.8 | 402.1 | 472.2 |
| this PR | 73.0 | 118.6 | 173.0 | 208.3 | 259.1 | 360.2 | 431.8 |
| change | −18.1% | −11.7% | −10.9% | −12.6% | −11.5% | −10.4% | −8.6% |

Weighted by the widths served at c32 / c4: −10.7% / −11.6%. Index-source launches (the ratio-2 layers that feed the indexer, which now wait on `krdy`): −8.9% to −17.3%, weighted −10.9% / −11.4% (7 runs); the `krdy` wait itself costs < 0.6% on main and on this PR.

**E2E** (TP2 + MTP, agentic-coding trace, 1 h per run, CI server arguments; main and this PR on two lanes at once, swapped in a second wave; mean of the two waves vs main; measured before the rebase, same kernel code):

| vs main | c32 | c4 |
|---|---|---|
| TPOT p50 | **−3.31%** | **−3.74%** |
| TPOT p90 | −1.22% | −6.84% |
| interactivity p50 | +3.49% | +3.78% |
| interactivity p90 | +1.16% | +7.59% |
| output tok/s/GPU | +0.53% | −0.66% |
| per-request ITL ratio | 0.973 / 0.976 | 0.970 / 0.960 |

MTP acceptance length 3.51 in every run; TTFT within run-to-run noise.

## Details

**Where it applies**: gfx950, TP 2, compress ratio 2, the target's routing (384 experts, top-6) and SWA window. The gate is static per build; no new flag or env var.

**Tradeoff**: tuned builds lay out their scratch differently, so the runner keys scratch by (width, tuned): up to ~20 MB per tuned width per rank. Peer memory is unchanged.

**Not covered**: gfx942 and DSpark draft builds were not run on GPU (MLIR identical to main's); TP4 is not tuned.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Triton sigmoid+bias top-k when MoE grouping eliminates nothing
author: chennyiiis
body:
## Overview

AITER `biased_grouped_topk` runs an LDS group scan even when the grouping cannot eliminate any expert — that is, when `topk_group >= num_expert_group`, so every group is selected. This adds a register-resident Triton sigmoid+bias top-k and substitutes it at `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk`, the single call site both ROCm routers reach.

Previously this PR specialised `rocm_aiter_grouped_topk` only. Moving it to the wrapper came out of review (thanks @simondanielsson) and covers both paths without touching routing metadata:

| caller | group arguments it passes |
|---|---|
| `GroupedTopKRouter` | the model's own `1/1` for a degenerate router |
| `FusedTopKBiasRouter` | a count synthesised to fit an AITER kernel — measured `2/2` for a 64-expert router — with `topk_group == num_expert_group` |

`vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py` is no longer modified; the diff is three files, additions only.

## Claims

- 1.67×–2.15× on the routing op on gfx942, and 1.16×–1.57× per shape on gfx950, under CUDA graph replay, across the configurations listed below.
- The gate stops at 512 experts and top-8. On gfx950 the kernel loses at top-16 (896-expert top-16 down to 0.62×), so those routers keep AITER — see *Scope and bounds*.
- Equivalent to the call it replaces whenever no group is eliminated, including `num_expert_group == topk_group > 1`, which is the shape `FusedTopKBiasRouter` produces.
- Eager execution is **not** faster, so it is excluded by the substitution rather than claimed as a win.
- Selected expert ids match AITER on 3323 of 3328 routing calls in a live Moonlight-16B-A3B forward and on 1248 of 1248 in Kimi-VL-A3B.
- **Scope: single-token batches only (`_MAX_TOKENS = 1`), as suggested in review**, i.e. one request decoding without speculation, which is where the end-to-end gain is. Larger batches keep AITER.
- End to end on MI355X with current `main`, five models with 64 to 384 experts, 1k to 32k context: **single-request decode is 0.4% to 4.2% faster on every model**, and higher concurrency is within noise; nothing regresses beyond the same-arm drift. GSM8K is unchanged on GLM-5.3-Flash and Kimi-K2.6. Earlier gfx942 runs were within noise.
- No new env var, and no change to router selection or to the advertised routing method.

## Dispatch scope: why this is restricted to CUDA graph steps

The kernel's advantage is device time. Timed from a plain Python loop it is *slower* — it is a Triton launch from Python against a single C++ dispatch, and that overhead is not amortised.

Because the gate is a token-count bound rather than an execution-phase check, eager steps can reach it, so this was measured end to end with `--enforce-eager`, interleaved B-A-B-A on Moonlight:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | ungated PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 488.7 | 471.8 | **−3.5%** | 0.6% / 1.2% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1910.4 | 1876.9 | **−1.8%** | 0.8% / 0.1% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 780.8 | 758.1 | **−2.9%** | 0.8% / 0.2% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3008.8 | 2915.3 | **−3.1%** | 0.0% / 0.9% |

Consistent sign and a magnitude several times the drift, so this is a real regression, not noise. The dispatch therefore substitutes only while a CUDA graph is being captured, tested with `torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()` as `custom_all_reduce.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` already do, and eager steps keep AITER. An earlier revision tested `get_forward_context().cudagraph_runtime_mode` instead; that misses every FULL graph under the V2 model runner, which captures them with the forward context set to `NONE` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`), so on current main it substituted only inside PIECEWISE graphs. Re-running the same eager A/B with the check in place:

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 64 / 256 | 8 | 490.2 | 492.5 | +0.5% | 0.7% / 0.1% |
| 64 / 256 | 32 | 1934.9 | 1933.3 | −0.1% | 1.2% / 0.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 8 | 787.1 | 786.8 | −0.0% | 0.1% / 1.0% |
| 1024 / 1024 | 32 | 3018.7 | 3009.5 | −0.3% | 1.9% / 0.8% |

Instrumentation observed no Triton dispatches with `enforce_eager=True`. With graphs enabled, on current main and MI355X, a server records these substitution decisions while it captures its graphs:

| model | cudagraph mode | substituted with the forward-context check | substituted with the stream-capture check |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (forced by the model) | 0 of 2912 | 494 of 2912 |
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 988 of 8190 | 1482 of 8190 |

494 is 19 captured decode sizes up to 128 tokens times 26 MoE layers; the remaining decisions are larger captured sizes, the profiling run and warm-up runs, all of which keep AITER. Those counts are with the earlier `_MAX_TOKENS = 128`; with the current `_MAX_TOKENS = 1` a Moonlight server substitutes 78 of 8190 decisions, all of them in the 1-token graphs, and keeps AITER everywhere else.

## Validation

All runs on one MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs), torch 2.10.0, triton 3.6.0.

Three checkpoints are used, all with `num_expert_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, a sigmoid router and a `noaux_tc` correction bias. Which one carries which measurement, since they differ:

| model | experts / top-k | context | used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 64 / 6 | 8192 | routing comparison, e2e ≤6k, NIAH 4096, GPQA |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 64 / 6 | 131072 | routing comparison, e2e 1k |
| Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | **256 / 8** | 1M | e2e 1k, GPQA, and the 8k/64k attempt |

NIAH ran at 4096 and GPQA at roughly 1k prompts, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine fault described below appears, so those results and that fault are not in conflict.

Which model carries which measurement, since they differ:

| measurement | model | context used |
|---|---|---|
| unit, micro | — (kernel in isolation) | n/a |
| routing comparison | Moonlight-16B-A3B **and** Kimi-VL-A3B | short decode rows |
| e2e 1k/1k, 6k/1k | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ≤ 7k |
| e2e 1k/1k | Kimi-VL-A3B | ≤ 2k |
| e2e 8k/1k, 64k/1k | **not obtained** — see below | — |
| NIAH | Moonlight-16B-A3B | 4096 |
| GPQA | Moonlight-16B-A3B | ~1k prompts |

NIAH and GPQA ran on Moonlight at 4096 and ~1k respectively, both well under the 8192 input length at which the engine crash below appears, so there is no contradiction between those results and that crash.

### Unit

Against upstream `db3b0f0fa`:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py -k "flat_topk or substitutes"
# 61 passed on MI355X (gfx950), this PR at 7c6559d9 cherry-picked onto main 3966924d
```

Each correctness test compares against `rocm_aiter_ops.biased_grouped_topk(..., 1, 1, ...)` — the exact call being replaced — through the same wrapper production uses.

| test | coverage |
|---|---|
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter` | 40 cases: {bf16, fp32} × {renorm on, off} × 10 shapes, including primes/odd sizes that exercise the masked tail of `BLOCK_E = next_power_of_2(num_experts)`: `(3,257,8)`, `(7,131,5)`, `(13,509,7)`, `(1,2,1)`, `(5,65,3)` |
| `test_flat_topk_casts_bias_like_aiter` | bf16 gating with an fp32 bias — see *Bias dtype* |
| `test_flat_topk_matches_aiter_with_uneliminating_groups` | `num_expert_group == topk_group` ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} × renorm on/off — the `FusedTopKBiasRouter` shape |
| `test_flat_topk_honours_routed_scaling` | `routed_scaling_factor` 1.0 / 2.446 / 2.827 |
| `test_biased_grouped_topk_substitutes_only_when_expected` | captures a real CUDA graph around the wrapper: it substitutes for `1/1` and `2/2` during capture, and not for `8/4` or in eager |

The rest of that file reports 34 failures in my container which reproduce identically on unmodified `db3b0f0fa` (34 failed / 5 passed before this change, 34 failed / 77 passed after it, measured before the review trim); this PR does not touch them.

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/rocm_aiter_moe.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/rocm_sigmoid_bias_flat_topk.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py
```

### Micro

Per-call **device** time under CUDA graph replay, 50 calls captured per graph so the replay overhead is amortised ~50× instead of landing on both arms.

| gating | experts | tokens | AITER (µs) | PR (µs) | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 5.47 / 5.67 / 5.72 / 5.76 | 3.00 / 3.18 / 3.20 / 3.27 | 1.82× / 1.78× / 1.79× / 1.76× |
| bf16 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.80 / 7.03 / 7.07 / 7.14 | 4.01 / 4.14 / 4.16 / 4.26 | 1.69× / 1.70× / 1.70× / 1.67× |
| fp32 | 256 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 6.05 / 6.12 / 6.24 / 6.26 | 2.82 / 2.99 / 3.00 / 3.16 | 2.15× / 2.05× / 2.08× / 1.98× |
| fp32 | 384 | 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.33 / 7.54 / 7.61 / 7.62 | 3.56 / 3.70 / 3.73 / 3.79 | 2.06× / 2.04× / 2.04× / 2.01× |

That is gfx942 (MI300X) at 256 and 384 experts.

On gfx950 (MI355X), the same method over a wider range of shapes: bf16 gating, fp32 bias, `routed_scaling_factor` 2.446, renormalised, six random seeds per point, plus one input where a single row has an exactly tied top score. Expert ids matched a stable-sort reference on every input, and AITER's id set on all 192 random inputs.

| experts | top-k | AITER µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | PR µs, 1 / 8 / 32 / 128 tokens | mean speedup | worst random launch | one tied row |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 6 | 5.40 / 5.79 / 5.85 / 5.77 | 3.45 / 3.65 / 3.72 / 3.74 | 1.57× | 1.51× | 1.33× |
| 256 | 8 | 5.21 / 5.35 / 5.46 / 5.51 | 3.99 / 4.27 / 4.26 / 4.45 | 1.27× | 1.06× | 1.06× |
| 384 | 8 | 5.36 / 5.88 / 5.93 / 5.97 | 4.62 / 5.12 / 5.12 / 5.13 | 1.16× | 1.13× | 0.92× |
| 512 | 8 | 5.50 / 6.11 / 6.17 / 6.23 | 4.56 / 5.20 / 5.20 / 5.45 | 1.18× | 0.98× | 0.95× |
| 512 | 16 | 6.59 / 7.11 / 7.17 / 7.24 | 5.36 / 5.85 / 5.92 / 6.97 | 1.18× | 0.80× | 0.78× |
| 768 | 16 | 11.36 / 12.37 / 12.42 / 12.45 | 6.75 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.06 | 1.67× | 1.04× | 0.98× |
| 896 | 16 | 6.97 / 7.66 / 7.72 / 7.75 | 6.79 / 7.26 / 7.29 / 8.07 | 1.03× | 0.65× | 0.62× |
| 1024 | 16 | 7.12 / 7.80 / 7.85 / 7.91 | 6.76 / 7.24 / 7.28 / 7.28 | 1.07× | 1.04× | 0.64× |

The advantage shrinks as the router widens on gfx950; it does not grow. The slow launches are the tie fallback: when a row has two experts with exactly equal biased scores among its top-k, the fast path picks more than k and that row redoes the selection, and the launch waits for its slowest row. bf16 logits make exact ties common enough at top-16 to matter (0.8% of rows at 896 experts, so about one 32-row launch in five), which is where the 0.6× launches come from. Rows above 512 experts or top-8 therefore stay on AITER.

### Routing comparison on live models

Comparing generated text between arms is not a usable instrument on this setup: it is not deterministic run to run — two baseline-only runs of the same four greedy prompts already diverge. Instead both kernels were run on identical inputs inside a live forward, AITER into the real buffers and the new kernel into scratch, with generation continuing on the AITER result so the measurement cannot perturb the run.

| model | calls compared | calls where **all** selected ids match | max abs weight delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Moonlight-16B-A3B | 3328 | 3323 | 4.77e-07 |
| Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct | 1248 | 1248 | 4.77e-07 |

Both have `n_group=1`, `topk_group=1`, `scoring_func="sigmoid"`, `noaux_tc`, `norm_topk_prob=true`, 64 experts, top-6. The five differing Moonlight calls each carry a weight delta of 1.19e-07 or 4.77e-07; that is consistent with a near-tie in the biased score resolving to a different expert, but the weight delta alone does not prove the scores were exactly equal.

### End to end on MI300X (gfx942)

`vllm serve` + `vllm bench serve`, interleaved, one fresh server per block.

An initial sequential A/B (all of arm 0, then all of arm 1) showed +16–24% throughput. That did not reproduce under interleaved testing and has been withdrawn — the same AITER baseline measured 1789 tok/s sequentially and 2250 tok/s interleaved on a shared host.

| model | in / out | concurrency | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.7% | −0.8% | 0.4% / 1.4% |
| Moonlight | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.8% | −0.9% | 1.1% / 0.6% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +0.4% | −0.6% | 1.0% / 0.9% |
| Kimi-VL | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.7% | −0.9% | 3.6% / 0.7% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 8 | +1.1% | −1.1% | 0.4% / 0.4% |
| Kimi-Linear | 1024 / 1024 | 32 | +0.1% | −0.1% | 1.1% / 0.7% |

Comparable to the same-arm variation, so no gfx942 end-to-end speedup is claimed. The Kimi-Linear rows discard the first repetition of each block: the very first benchmark run of the campaign returned 1066 tok/s against 1510-1543 for the other seven runs of that point, a warm-up artefact rather than a property of either arm.

**The 8k/1k and 64k/1k points are now measured.** The earlier report that they could not be served was wrong, and the reason is worth stating because it is a bug in the benchmark harness rather than in serving.

`vllm bench serve --dataset-name random` samples token ids from `tokenizer.vocab_size`. For this checkpoint that is **163842**, while the model's embedding has `config.vocab_size` = **163840** rows, so ids 163840 and 163841 index past the table and the embedding gather faults. The dataset emits a *contiguous run* of ids, so a 65536-token prompt covers 40% of the vocabulary and nearly always includes one of the two; an 8192-token prompt covers 5%, which is why 8k completed under some seeds and not others. On stock vLLM, with no part of this PR installed, the identical 8192 configuration completes 3/3 with `--seed 7` and faults 3/3 with `--seed 1234`:

| seed | completed | `Memory access fault` |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | 8, 8, 8 | 0 |
| 1234 | 0, 0, 0 | 1 |

That also explains the fault seen earlier on a different machine with Kimi-VL, where the kernel named in the HSA exception was `at::native::vectorized_gather_kernel` — the embedding gather.

Replacing the synthesised prompts with real text (a custom dataset whose maximum token id is 138177, verified below the embedding size) removes the fault entirely: 8 of 8 runs complete at 64k with zero faults.

| in / out | concurrency | AITER tok/s | this PR tok/s | Δ throughput | Δ TPOT | same-arm drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 4305.4 | 4466.3 | +3.7% | −4.0% | 4.1% / 1.7% |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 6154.7 | 6162.5 | +0.1% | −1.2% | 1.4% / 1.8% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 1 | 13528.3 | 14305.7 | +5.7% | −7.0% | 8.6% / 8.4% |
| 65536 / 1024 | 2 | 18045.6 | 17927.5 | −0.7% | −1.6% | 1.7% / 0.9% |
