title: [Perf][HiSparse] Prefetch speculative groups with bounded copy workers
author: zhenwenqi2024
body:
## Overview

Extend HiSparse's existing shared-index group prefetch to multi-token speculative verification, including MTP, and bound the CUDA compact-gather launch as verification expands the batch.

Related: #60072. This is separate from the platform-interface PR #62592. It composes with #60103; slot-invalidation fusion, padding-mask fusion and the all-resident resolver optimization remain in that PR and are not duplicated here.

## Claims

- Eligible pure-decode verification batches can stage follower layers' historical KV on the existing group copy stream, with a separate completion event for each layer.
- Prefetch eligibility is separate from the single-token resident-write and host-mirror policy. Mixed/prefill batches keep per-layer staging.
- Compact gather launches at most 64 thread blocks. Additional rows are processed by the existing workers; batches of at most 64 rows retain their column parallelism.
- Add native payload/graph regression cases and a reusable gather benchmark. Scoped H200 serving and profiling results are reported below; no model accuracy or acceptance improvement is claimed.

## Performance results

Measured on 8 x NVIDIA H200 with GLM-5.2-FP8, TP=8, MTP=3 and the V2 model runner. Both arms were rebuilt from frozen main `a1cfd2c1b584c4ac197db9cc9ac84a6d973d39df`; the candidate adds this PR's changes at `bb84fb5e976f941e9e2b8586f79930be64408a74`. Source/native-library pairs were checked. The table uses the original PR implementation.

Runtime: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, driver 595.58.03; EvalScope 1.14.1 for unprofiled serving measurements.

- Workload: 65,536 input tokens, forced 4,096 or 8,192 output tokens, concurrency 32, 32 requests per case; temperature 0, ignore EOS. Frozen GSM8K-derived long prompts are a synthetic performance workload, not a natural long-reasoning accuracy evaluation. Request bodies match between arms and actual input/output lengths were audited.
- Both arms: `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_ds_mla`, 32 GiB GPU KV cache per rank, 128 GiB shared host pool, `max_model_len=73728`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=32`, prefix caching disabled, seed 42; FLASHMLA_SPARSE / DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER.
- Each initial process ran a separate C32 64K/128 warmup (excluded), then 4K output, 8K output and an 8K repeat. A separate PR process restart repeated warmup -> 4K -> 8K. The restart rows reuse the original main process's corresponding first measurements; they are not additional independent main restarts.
- TPOT is the mean of per-request `(latency - TTFT) / (output_tokens - 1)`, not inter-chunk latency. TTFT includes queueing.

All arrows below are **main -> PR**. Throughput is aggregate output tokens/s; TPOT and TTFT are client means.

| Output / run | Output tok/s | Change | TPOT (ms/token) | Change | TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4K, first | 487.7481 -> 494.6458 | +1.41% | 38.14 -> 37.08 | -2.78% | 107.739 -> 107.676 |
| 8K, first | 780.2473 -> 802.4179 | +2.84% | 26.80 -> 25.35 | -5.41% | 107.713 -> 107.733 |
| 8K, same-process repeat | 782.5196 -> 800.9244 | +2.35% | 26.59 -> 25.50 | -4.10% | 107.541 -> 107.610 |
| 4K, PR restart | 487.7481 -> 495.4115 | +1.57% | 38.14 -> 36.87 | -3.33% | 107.739 -> 107.992 |
| 8K, PR restart | 780.2473 -> 803.6892 | +3.00% | 26.80 -> 25.43 | -5.11% | 107.713 -> 107.901 |

The 32 GiB series completed main 96/96, first PR process 96/96 and restarted PR process 64/64 measured requests, with **zero preemptions in both arms**. Earlier 24 GiB runs had capacity-driven preemptions; increasing capacity is a separate tuning change and its gain is not attributed to this PR.

These observations support a modest benefit for this workload: 8K-output throughput +2.35% to +3.00%, mean TPOT -4.10% to -5.41%, with essentially unchanged mean TTFT. They are not confidence intervals or a general performance guarantee. Host NUMA placement was not pinned; generated continuations and MTP acceptance can differ across processes. No accuracy or acceptance-rate improvement is claimed.

### Profiling

A separate Torch-profiler diagnostic run at 24 GiB GPU KV capacity selected pure-decode steps with 26 requests / 104 verification rows: 24 main steps versus 23 PR steps, excluding one mixed-prefill PR step. Values are medians across rank-level medians, not end-to-end serving results.

| Diagnostic metric | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU pure-decode envelope per step | 63.0585 ms | 54.8721 ms |
| Total gather duration per step | 14.9948 ms | 16.3471 ms |
| Exposed / non-overlapped gather duration | 14.9948 ms | 5.3232 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 67.44% |

The trace supports the intended copy/compute overlap: exposed gather time falls about 64.5%, despite total gather duration increasing. The selected GPU interval is about 13.0% shorter; **this is not a 13% end-to-end speedup**. Tokens and cache hit/miss state may differ. HiSparse traffic counters publish every 2,000 worker calls, so their per-case deltas are not used to attribute transfer-volume changes.

#### Trace timeline: before and after

![HiSparse main versus PR: actual GPU trace timelines and 20–24 ms zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhenwenqi2024/vllm/974d68aa2b97c604003a42163f3257d926f7c606/pr63801/overlap-before-after.png)

The figure is rendered from original GPU event timestamps and durations, grouping events into per-category interval unions. **Left: main. Right: main + this PR.** Orange shows HiSparse gather kernels reading mapped host KV; blue shows other GPU activity; purple is the measured time intersection of the two tracks. In the magnified main panel, gather occupies gaps between other GPU work. In the PR panel, gather runs concurrently with other kernels; the original events include sparse MLA attention, fused MoE and GEMM kernels in these overlapping intervals.

Both panels show **rank 0, 26 requests / 104 verification rows, 24 GiB GPU KV**. To select a representative example, each arm uses the pure-decode step nearest its own rank's median GPU envelope: main step 22 and PR step 21 (zero-based profiler indices). Each panel starts at its own first GPU event; the lower panels show the same relative 20–24 ms window in the separate executions.

| Metric in the displayed step | Main | PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GPU envelope | 63.0919 ms | 54.8733 ms |
| Gather duration (interval union) | 15.0741 ms | 16.6993 ms |
| Gather overlapped with other GPU activity | 0 ms | 10.9321 ms |
| Gather without other GPU activity | 15.0741 ms | 5.7672 ms |
| Gather overlap fraction | 0% | 65.46% |

The gather duration itself increases in this example, while much of it executes alongside other GPU work. **65.46% is this single rank/step's overlap; 67.44% in the table above is the summary across rank-level medians.** Generated tokens and cache states can differ between executions. A time intersection is not a direct measurement of critical-path savings, and this 24 GiB diagnostic is separate from the unprofiled 32 GiB serving results.

## GSM8K accuracy and MTP acceptance

Full real-weight regression on the same 8 x H200, GLM-5.2-FP8, TP8/MTP3, V2 runner and 32 GiB KV configuration above, comparing frozen main `a1cfd2c1` with main + original PR `bb84fb5e`.

Protocol: EvalScope 1.14.1 / GSM8K adapter v1.1, standard `main/test` **all 1,319 questions**, first four training examples in fixed order, thinking enabled with `reasoning_effort=max`, temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 42, concurrency 32, `max_tokens=16384`, normal EOS, non-streaming, no retries. This is a custom greedy regression, not a reproduction of the official GLM model-card score. Dataset: `openai/grade-school-math@3101c7d5072418e28b9008a6636bde82a006892c`; test SHA256 `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. The complete request bodies and model metadata hashes matched across arms.

| Metric | Main | Main + PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unique questions / scored | 1,319 / 1,319 | 1,319 / 1,319 |
| Correct | 1,285 | 1,282 |
| Accuracy, all questions | 97.4223% | 97.1948% |
| Output-budget failures, scored zero | 14 | 8 |
| HTTP errors / missing / duplicate questions | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Accepted / proposed draft tokens | 781,084 / 910,050 | 705,864 / 831,003 |
| Speculative steps | 303,350 | 277,001 |
| True draft-token acceptance | 85.8287% | 84.9412% |
| Mean acceptance length, including bonus token | 3.5749 | 3.5482 |
| Position 1 / 2 / 3 unconditional acceptance | 94.6313% / 86.1961% / 76.6586% | 94.3011% / 85.3723% / 75.1503% |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |

Accuracy changed by **-0.2274 percentage points (three fewer correct answers)**: 11 main-correct answers became wrong, and eight main-wrong answers became correct. All eight gains came from baseline output-budget failures; four of the 11 losses were PR output-budget failures. Every budget failure reached 16,384 tokens with reasoning but no final answer and remained a zero in the full denominator. This single pass does not establish accuracy equivalence or isolate the cause of the differences; no accuracy improvement is claimed.

Acceptance is `sum(accepted) / sum(proposed)`; mean acceptance length is `1 + sum(accepted) / sum(steps)`. All per-request counters, histograms and three position counts reconciled exactly with isolated Prometheus deltas. The table includes the budget failures and excludes the preceding 20-question smoke runs. It does not use EvalScope's streaming-chunk acceptance estimate.

As a secondary diagnostic, excluding the union of either arm's truncated questions leaves the **same 1,300 questions** in both arms: acceptance is 83.8127% -> 83.9579%. This illustrates sensitivity of the token-weighted aggregate to generated continuation lengths; it is not the primary metric or evidence of an acceptance improvement.

Raw responses, per-question reviews/reports, request hashes, metrics snapshots, source-patch hash and native-library identities were archived and audited. The baseline was re-audited without regenerating answers or changing scores after correcting the harness's classification of scored budget failures; the initial failed audit remains preserved. The model/PR implementation and frozen generation protocol were unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Full EvalScope command</summary>

`DATASET_DIR` contains the frozen official train/test JSONL files and the local `main` split mapping; `OUT` is a fresh directory for each variant. Port 18593 is the local raw-response audit proxy forwarding to the model on 18592.

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --model GLM-5.2-FP8 --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://127.0.0.1:18593/v1 --api-key EMPTY \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-args "{\"gsm8k\":{\"dataset_id\":\"$DATASET_DIR\",\"few_shot_num\":4,\"few_shot_random\":false,\"subset_list\":[\"main\"]}}" \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0,"top_p":1,"max_tokens":16384,"seed":42,"timeout":7200,"stream":false,"n":1,"retries":0,"extra_body":{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":true,"reasoning_effort":"max"}}}' \
  --eval-batch-size 32 --seed 42 --work-dir "$OUT" --no-timestamp
```

</details>

These are standard short GSM8K prompts, not inputs padded to 64K. They do not alone validate long-history offload misses or establish performance gains; the separate 64K performance and byte-level device tests above address different aspects.

## Validation

### Rebase validation (2026-10-29)

Rebased the original PR commit `bb84fb5e976` onto main `914d61fc538a84e8487cb16fe8241a70f6f4bf9e`; the updated head is `fc1fd11a1d306ab5f7b2d00e12107d3076e188af`. The only textual conflict was two tests added at the same location in `tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`. Both main's resident-gather stride/payload test and this PR's bounded-decode prefetch test were preserved unchanged, including their parametrization. A per-file comparison verified that all added/removed lines in the seven-file PR patch are identical to the original patch; only surrounding context changed.

- On the isolated rebased Python source, `python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k 'hisparse_resident_gather_preserves_stride_and_payload or hisparse_group_prefetch_requires_bounded_decode_only'`: **10 passed, 55 deselected**. These are CPU tests run with the existing CUDA environment's import dependencies, not a rebuild or device validation of the new base.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, mypy, typos, Markdown formatting, Buildkite keys/test tethering, SPDX/import/config checks, boolean-context/remote-code checks, filenames and Docker ignore rules. The test-tethering check used UTF-8 on Windows. The Windows clang-format launcher failed, so the exact rebased CUDA source was checked on Linux with **clang-format 21.1.2 `--style=file --dry-run --Werror csrc/hisparse_kernels.cu`**, which passed. Python syntax and `git diff --check` also passed.

The performance, profiling, device-test and GSM8K measurements reported above/below remain results for frozen main `a1cfd2c1` plus the original PR `bb84fb5e`; they have **not** been rerun on the new main base.

Linux/CUDA native builds and H200 device checks have now run:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py -k hisparse`: main **45 passed**, PR **53 passed** (12 deselected each).
- Attention HiSparse selection: **53 main / 67 PR passed using out-of-tree compatibility copies** that repaired stale fixtures while preserving assertions. The unmodified baseline selection had 6 fixture failures / 47 passes; this is not a claim that the unmodified checked-in attention suite passed.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_device_stress.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph replay, exact independent CPU byte-level golden comparisons; 656-byte rows, top-k 2048, four layers, up to 32 requests x 4 verification rows with changing active counts. PR Compute Sanitizer memcheck: **2 passed, 0 errors**.
- Supplemental `validation/test_pr63801_stream_consumption.py`: **2 main / 2 PR passed**, eager and CUDA Graph, immediate compute-stream consumption of each layer while follower prefetch proceeds, 64K history and an explicit logical-index readiness event. PR memcheck independently on GPU 0 and GPU 1: **2 passed, 0 errors on each**. These supplemental local tests are not checked-in full-model accuracy tests.

The standard reduced-model E2E suite (`tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`), real-weight accuracy under long-history offload misses, repeated accuracy runs and a broader concurrency / MTP-on-off sweep remain outstanding. The completed standard GSM8K regression above and byte-level device checks do not replace these.

Previously recorded local checks: the isolated CPU harness passed 10 contract cases (stand-in runtime owner); Ruff, syntax, whitespace, markdownlint, typos, SPDX/import checks, Buildkite test tethering and isolated Python 3.11 mypy passed. LLVM 21.1.2 WASM formatting produced identical CUDA source bytes; the native Windows formatter hook was skipped because its launcher failed. These are local results, not a claim of upstream CI success.

## Details

Group prefetch already exists for single-token decode. This extends its eligibility without adding a backend support flag, stream, buffer or CPU readback. Current verification KV remains resident and is written by each layer before its attention; only historical host misses are staged early.

The compact gather previously targeted 64 blocks but launched one block per row once the row count exceeded 64. For example, 32 requests with four verification rows produced a 128-block copy grid. Workers now loop over those rows within a 64-block launch. Miss-count clamping, invalid entries, out-of-range source zeroing and padded hot-page strides keep their existing behavior. Tests cover row counts around the boundary, empty plans, payload bytes and replay with updated inputs.

The launch bound may trade dense-copy bandwidth for compute overlap, as illustrated by the diagnostic trace above. A block-count bound does not reserve particular SMs.

An open-PR search found no equivalent speculative-group-prefetch or bounded-gather change. #60103 handles separate existing launch/resolver overhead; #61263 changes residency hash probing.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, performance/accuracy analysis and preparation of this update. Human review and the remaining validation items above are still outstanding.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Defer async KV loads on HiSparse decoders until in-flight steps finish
author: vMaroon
body:
> **Edited by @MatthewBonanni:** per @LucasWilkinson's suggestion (vMaroon/vllm#2), every async load on a HiSparse decoder is now deferred until the in-flight step is processed; the reuse detection is gone. Overview, Claims, unit tests and Details are updated. The GLM-5.3 results were measured on the earlier revision, which deferred only loads into reused pages.

## Overview

Fixes KV corruption on HiSparse P/D decoders: a NIXL load can overwrite a GPU page while the previous step is still reading it. The request that was reading it emits garbage for the rest of its output. The fix makes the scheduler start every async load on a HiSparse decoder one step later, once the in-flight step is done.

Fixes #63811.

## When it happens

All four hold at once:

1. **HiSparse is on.** It returns a running request's clean resident pages to the GPU pool early; the request keeps reading them until the pool hands them out again.
2. **Async scheduling** (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`): step N is still on the GPU while step N+1 starts.
3. **KV arrives by an async load**: a P/D decoder with `NixlConnector` as consumer. NIXL posts its reads from the CPU, so nothing orders them after step N.
4. **In step N+1, the pool hands one of those returned pages to a new request whose KV comes through that load.**

NIXL then writes the new request's KV into the page while step N still reads it as the owner's KV. The owner's tokens from step N get wrong KV, later steps attend to them, and the output never recovers.

Unaffected: pages filled by a forward or a host restore (ordered on the CUDA stream), and engines without HiSparse or without an async KV load.

## Claims

- Fixes the symptom: output cuts mid-sentence into one repeated token (`locklocklock...` on GLM-5.3) until `max_tokens`, with MTP acceptance at 0.
- With HiSparse enabled, every async load is registered with the connector once the step in flight at its allocation is processed, normally on the next step. Other requests and steps run as before.
- Cost: each async-loaded request on a HiSparse decoder starts its load about one step later. No device sync, and no check for which pages were reused.
- Active only with HiSparse and `defer_block_free` (overlapping steps and a KV consumer); otherwise nothing is deferred.

## Validation

GLM-5.3 on H100, P/D. Decoder TP8 x DP2, MTP 3, MRV2, async scheduling, `MultiConnector` (`NixlConnector` + `HiSparseConnector`), 20,000-block GPU pool. Traffic from `benchmarks/multi_turn`: 46-77K token prompts, 2-4K token answers. Counts are answers with at least 1,024 tokens. The rig runs the production image, a vLLM fork at `110cf9dc12`; "this PR" is this change applied to that fork's scheduler, block pool and KV cache manager (it applies cleanly).

| Free-queue order | Engine | Answers | Page handed to a NIXL load while read | Collapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default | base | 133 | 0 | 0 |
| released pages first | base | 162 | 90 | 81 |
| released pages first | this PR | 173 | 106 (load held) | 0 |

- "Released pages first" is the one-line test change in step 1 below. It makes condition 4 frequent. Any free-block order is valid for the allocator, so a correct engine keeps its output quality under it.
- Collapsed: under 1.3 tokens per step (MTP drafts stop matching) from some point to the end of the answer, for at least 512 tokens. On base, collapse starts a median 35 tokens after the overwrite.
- Holds with this PR: 151 loads, each registered in the pass where step N had been processed, none earlier.
- TTFT of later turns (prompt mostly cached on the decoder) in the stress run: p50 1.98 s base, 2.07 s this PR. First-turn TTFT is not comparable across these runs because the prefill pods' prefix cache state differed.
- Default order with long answers (12-16K tokens, KV pool up to 88% full, base engine): 0 of 5,215 reuses of returned pages went to a NIXL-filled group, so the hold would not have triggered.
- Unit tests in `tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`: a deferred load is registered after the in-flight step, it records its prefix cache stats (with `hits_by_source`) when it starts, a load without deferral registers at once, and an abort while deferred frees the blocks after the in-flight step.

**How to reproduce**

1. In `BlockPool.unpin_blocks`, replace `self.free_block_queue.append_n(released)` with `self.free_block_queue.prepend_n(released)`.
2. Serve GLM-5.3 P/D with a decoder as above. Run `benchmarks/multi_turn/benchmark_serving_multi_turn.py --num-clients 4 --max-active-conversations 8` on a generated config: 20 conversations, 10-12 turns, 15K common plus 30-50K prefix tokens, 1-2.5K token user turns, 2-4K token answers. The tool rejects reasoning-only streams, so accept `reasoning` deltas.
3. On base, within minutes, answers end in a repeated token and the `SpecDecoding metrics` per-position acceptance falls toward 0. With this PR, no degenerate answers.

## Details

- `defer_async_loads` is set at init when `defer_block_free` is on and the KV cache config has a HiSparse host pool.
- With a step in flight, the scheduler puts an async load in `deferred_loads` with the fence `sched_step_seq` at allocation instead of calling `update_state_after_alloc`. `_drain_deferred_loads` starts it in `update_from_output`, next to `_drain_deferred_frees`, once `processed_step_seq` reaches the fence. The request stays in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` meanwhile.
- Connector prefix-cache stats for a deferred load are recorded in `_drain_deferred_loads` after `update_state_after_alloc`, so it keeps `hits_by_source` (the connector attributes tiers only after the load plan exists). The allocation-site stats code is unchanged from main apart from skipping deferred loads.
- Abort while deferred: no load was posted, so the scheduler frees the blocks itself, deferred to the same fence through `last_sched_seq`, which is set when the load is deferred. `NixlConnector.request_finished` already releases the remote blocks of a request it never registered.
- The scheduler already fences block reuse against async connector writes (`defer_block_free`), but only for freed requests' blocks; these pages still belong to a running request. Deferring the registration needs no device sync; the only HiSparse-specific line in the scheduler is the init flag.
- CI does not cover the GPU path (needs NIXL P/D on GPUs).

title: [Perf][Frontend] Compute prompt block hashes in the Rust frontend
author: njhill
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the Rust frontend compute a request's prompt block hashes, so the engine's input thread no longer hashes long prompts while holding the GIL the engine loop needs. Revives the idea of #15652 for the Rust frontend; complementary to #63454 (cheaper engine-side hashing) and related to #43483 (frontend hashes for DP routing). Part of the long-context P/D CPU-overhead work in #63439.

## Claims

- The engine accepts frontend-computed prompt block hashes; prefix-cache hashes are unchanged (byte-identical), so cache hits, KV connectors and KV events are unaffected.
- The Rust frontend covers `sha256` and `sha256_cbor` for plain, LoRA, cache-salt and lookahead (EAGLE) requests; other requests are hashed by the engine as before.
- Removes the GIL-held prompt hashing from the engine's input thread (~50 ms per 227K-token prompt with `sha256`, ~150 ms with `sha256_cbor`), which otherwise stalls the engine loop: +9.6% decode throughput with `sha256` and +39% with `sha256_cbor` on a workload that admits long cached prompts during decode (below).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 114 passed. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm`: all passed, including known-answer vectors generated from the engine's own `Request` / `get_request_block_hasher`.
- E2E on GB300 with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, using a test-only engine patch that recomputes the hashes of every request that arrives with frontend hashes and compares them:

| Config | Requests | Hash check | Cached tokens on repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256`, LoRA | 12 (plain, salts incl. non-ASCII / 300-byte, short, LoRA, LoRA + salt) | 12/12 match | 5424/5427; a new salt or LoRA starts at 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256_cbor`, LoRA | 12 | 12/12 match | same |
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 (lookahead 1) | 8 | 8/8 match | same |

Benchmark (GB300, `Qwen3-0.6B`, Rust frontend, CUDA graphs): 64 streaming decode requests while fully prefix-cached 30K-token prompts (token ids, `max_tokens=1`) arrive at 20/s for 40 s. This resembles a P/D decode instance admitting long prompts. Same binaries in both arms; the "engine" arm stops the engine from advertising `prefix_hash_config`. Mean of 2 interleaved rounds (each within 2%):

| Hash | Prompt hashing in | Decode tok/s | ITL mean / p90 / p99 (ms) | Long-request TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | engine (main) | 16,870 | 3.77 / 8.36 / 10.10 | 27.6 / 46.1 |
| `sha256` | frontend (this PR) | 18,494 (+9.6%) | 3.44 / 6.51 / 9.83 | 25.6 / 37.8 |
| `sha256_cbor` | engine (main) | 13,244 | 4.80 / 10.41 / 15.64 | 34.9 / 61.1 |
| `sha256_cbor` | frontend (this PR) | 18,366 (+39%) | 3.46 / 6.45 / 10.04 | 25.6 / 35.5 |

The gain depends on how much of the engine loop the hashing displaces: a small model and a high arrival rate of long prompts make it large; larger models see a smaller relative gain.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server (both arms): `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-num-seqs 256 --prefix-caching-hash-algo {sha256,sha256_cbor} --enable-prompt-tokens-details`. For the engine arm, set `self.prefix_hash_config = None` in `EngineCore.__init__`. Client: 64 concurrent streaming `/v1/completions` (32-token prompt, `max_tokens=2000`, `ignore_eos`), measuring inter-chunk gaps; after warming 8 distinct 30K-token-id prompts into the prefix cache, send them round-robin at 20 req/s with `max_tokens=1` for 40 s.
</details>

## Details

- `EngineCoreReadyResponse.prefix_hash_config` (algorithm, `hash_block_size`, `NONE_HASH`, lookahead) is set when the engine hashes blocks. Sending `NONE_HASH` means frontends needn't reproduce the seed logic.
- `EngineCoreRequest.block_hashes` seeds `Request.block_hashes`; the existing hasher continues from there. The engine only checks the count (`(prompt_len - lookahead) // hash_block_size`) and otherwise hashes the prompt itself.
- The Rust encoder writes pickle protocol 5 / canonical CBOR exactly. It leaves to the engine: multimodal and prompt-embeds requests, `xxhash*`, keys over one 64 KiB pickle frame, and the rare requests whose strings pickle could memoize by identity.
- The Python frontend doesn't send hashes yet.

title: [ROCm][Kernel] Support persistent_topk on ROCm
author: AndreasKaratzas
body:
- Build `persistent_topk`, its FilteredTopK and sampled_topk tiers, and the shared exact overflow recovery from #62936 with hipcc (wave64-safe `TOPK_*` ballot/shuffle macros, HIP acquire load, clang-compatible `exact_topk_rescan` defaults).
- On gfx950 (at least 144 KiB of LDS), run every batch through `sampled_topk_kernel`, one workgroup per row, and cut clustered rows at the exact sampled rank. gfx942 keeps the persistent kernel. Return early on an empty batch.
- Place the decode logits of `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` after the top-k workspace, so `persistent_topk`'s row states no longer overwrite them.
- Allow the explicit `persistent` sparse-indexer backend on ROCm; `auto` still resolves to `per_row`.
- Route `cooperative` / `persistent` through `SparseIndexerTopk._row_ends`, so `(B,)` `seq_lens` with `next_n > 1` no longer raise "lengths size mismatch".
- Run the `persistent_topk` tests on ROCm, including #62936's candidate-overflow cases, add a test for the logits overlap, and add `persistent` to `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py`.
- Document `persistent` on ROCm in the `KernelConfig` docstring, and run the persistent top-k tests in the MI355 DeepSeek V4 kernels step (MI300 already runs the file).

On ROCm the sparse indexer could only use the in-tree `per_row` top-k or AITER, and asking for `persistent` failed because the op was compiled out. This PR builds it on top of #62936, which is now merged and makes the persistent and filtered paths exact on candidate overflow, so the ROCm-only rescan forks from earlier revisions are gone and ROCm shares that code. Wiring it into GLM-5.3-Flash showed that its decode logits and the top-k workspace both start at offset 0 of the shared workspace, which corrupts row 0 whenever the multi-CTA path runs (gfx942). CUDA is not affected, because its paged MQA logits are not workspace views, and ROCm on main is not either, because it rejects this backend. The backend stays opt-in, so default ROCm top-k selection does not change, but on gfx942, gfx950 and RDNA the decode logits now sit 1 MiB further into the workspace for every backend. On MI355X with k=2048 it is 2.2-2.6x faster than `per_row` and on par with AITER, and in GLM-5.3-Flash serving on this revision it selects exactly what `per_row` selects, with unchanged GSM8K 25-shot accuracy and throughput. This branch is stacked on #62298 (head b47c6178f1), so until that merges the diff against main includes #62298; this PR's own changes are `a2f04ca777..11871cef49` and `2fe6f7e5df`, plus merges of main and #62298.

<details>
<summary>Tests, end-to-end, benchmarks, open items and duplicate check</summary>

**gfx950 dispatch (MI355X, sampled path).**

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k "persistent or sparse_indexer"   # 10x in a loop
206 passed, 50 skipped, 409 deselected                                         # all 10 runs
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py
1 failed, 403 passed, 261 skipped    # test_aiter_decode_topk_matches_per_row_under_mtp compares AITER
                                     # with per_row; neither path changes in this PR
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py \
  test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py test_rocm_paged_mqa_context_lens.py \
  test_rocm_aiter_triton_sparse_mla.py test_sparse_mla_backends.py
171 passed, 269 skipped
```

After merging main (b4a0830f66) and #62298's head (85e0eae614), the persistent group gave the same 206 passed, 50 skipped in all 10 runs, the AITER group the same 1 failed, 403 passed, and the sparse-attention group 177 passed, 271 skipped (main added tests), with one failure in `test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness[...-large_q_pure_prefill-ROCMAiterMLA]`. That test feeds synthetic top-k indices to the attention backend, never reaches this PR's code, and failed 1 of 10 times when looped alone.

The skips in the persistent group are CUDA-only, cooperative, FlashInfer and DeepSelect cases. A randomized `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")` stress run compared values against `torch.topk`: 2,000 cases, 0 failures (k ∈ {512, 1024, 2048}, 0-64 requests, `next_n` 1-4, 1-D and 2-D `seq_lens`, empty batches, NaN/inf, ties, clustered rows). The ROCm-only clustered-rows test from the previous revision (16K, 32K and 128K rows of `randn * 0.01 + 3`, every case failed before) passes on #62936's shared paths, so it was dropped in favour of #62936's overflow test. Because gfx950 always dispatches to `sampled_topk`, some re-enabled tests (for example `test_persistent_topk_reused_group_after_short_row` and `test_persistent_topk_sampled_graph`) pass there without reaching the persistent kernel; the multi-CTA paths get real coverage on MI300 CI and in the gfx942-dispatch runs below. Validation covers gfx950 (MI355X) and gfx942 (MI300X); RDNA (wave32) compiles and admits the backend but was not tested.

**gfx942 dispatch (persistent kernel).** On MI300X (`sharedMemPerBlockOptin` is 64 KiB, so the persistent kernel runs instead of `sampled_topk`), the persistent group gave 176 passed, 80 skipped in 10 of 10 runs; the skips are the sampled-top-k tests that need 144 KiB of LDS and the CUDA-only backends. Before MI300X was available, a local build that capped `max_smem_per_block` and occupancy at 64 KiB on MI355X gave the same counts, and the stress run on it gave 2,000 cases with 0 failures. The cap was never committed.

**Logits overlap.** `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` returned its logits at workspace offset 0, the same place `SparseIndexerTopk` takes the `persistent_topk` workspace from. On the multi-CTA path the op clears its per-group row states there (`cudaMemsetAsync` in `topk.cu`) and then keeps barrier counters and histograms in them. In GLM-5.3-Flash serving with gfx942 dispatch this made 17,346 of 18,964 calls return wrong rows, all in row 0. The logits now come from the same `get_simultaneous` call as a top-k slot in front of them, and the profiling reservation uses the same layout. `test_persistent_topk_on_rocm_paged_mqa_logits` changed 3,088 logits (four groups' row states) with gfx942 dispatch before the fix and none after. On MI300X the test fails the same way with the logits moved back to offset 0 and passes with the fix:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k test_persistent_topk_on_rocm_paged_mqa_logits   # MI300X
1 failed: Tensor-likes are not equal! Mismatched elements: 3088 / 327680 (0.9%)   # logits at offset 0
1 passed                                                                          # this PR
```

Native gfx950 never runs that path, so there it passes either way; ROCm CI runs `test_top_k_per_row.py` on MI300, and the persistent group on MI355.

**End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash (amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP2, MI355X, AITER on, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs, k=512 under kpool 4), on this revision (11871cef49) against its base (1966abc5b2).** For this model, prompts of at most 2,048 tokens never reach the top-k: both decode (`_fill_short_decode_causal_indices`) and prefill (`short_prefill`) fill every causal index and skip it. GSM8K 5-shot (at most 1,521 tokens) and a 1K/1K bench therefore cannot tell the backends apart, so accuracy is compared on GSM8K 25-shot (3,289-5,091 tokens; every request runs the top-k).
- Exactness: an in-model hook re-ran `per_row` on a pre-call copy of the logits for every `persistent` call and compared the selected values per row. It found 0 mismatching rows in 6.94M decode rows per TP rank (2.51M without MTP, 4.43M with MTP 3-token speculation; GSM8K 25-shot plus 1K/8K/32K serving). Fewer than 0.01% of rows pick a different index among tied values.
- The same check with gfx942 dispatch (the 64 KiB LDS cap described above) found 0 mismatching rows in another 4.48M decode rows per rank, including 140K-token prompts with MTP that take the radix path. A capped server with graphs completed 1K/8K/32K serving and 8 of 8 140K-token requests with no fault.
- GSM8K 25-shot (flexible-extract), default vs `persistent`: 0.9295/0.9287 vs 0.9295/0.9265 over two runs each.
- Default backend, this PR vs base, serving throughput (tok/s) and mean TPOT (ms): 1K/1K at c=32 1837.0 vs 1843.6 and 16.53 vs 16.52; 8K/1K at c=16 844.3 vs 844.5 and 16.12 vs 16.01; 32K/1K at c=8 385.8 vs 387.0 and 15.34 vs 15.20. The new logits offset did not trip the locked workspace.
- `persistent` vs default on this PR: 8K/1K 851.3 vs 844.3 tok/s (TPOT 15.80 vs 16.12 ms) and 32K/1K 386.9 vs 385.8 tok/s (15.13 vs 15.34 ms). With MTP (both servers measured side by side on other GPUs): 865.3 vs 863.2 and 405.8 vs 414.0 tok/s.
- MI300X (gfx942, native persistent kernel), same model at TP2 on e707c976bd: the same check found 0 mismatching rows in 2.51M decode rows per rank and in 2.76M with MTP, including 140K-token prompts on the radix path. GSM8K 25-shot, `per_row` vs `persistent`: 0.9196/0.9257 vs 0.9196/0.9166. With graphs, `persistent` completed 8K/32K serving and 8 of 8 140K-token requests with no fault, at 73.5 vs 72.3 tok/s (8K/1K) and 36.6 vs 36.1 tok/s (32K/1K) against `per_row`. Decode takes about 210 ms per token for both backends on this node, so these throughput numbers say little about the top-k itself.
- On the previous revision, the radix path with gfx942 dispatch and 135K-190K-token prompts showed 0 wrong rows in 5.28M checked radix rows with #63475, and 37 of 37 benchmark runs completed. Without #63475 there were 107-137 wrong rows per 2.6M, and every server died with a GPU memory access fault within minutes. Those runs gave `persistent_topk` a private copy of the logits to keep the overlap above out of the measurement.

**Intermittent corruption seen on 2026-10-24.** In an earlier round, 8 of 144 test runs failed with buffers corrupted that the op never writes. It did not reproduce in more than 400 later runs, including every run above. The dumps showed corruption in buffers written before the op ran while the op was exact on what it read, so it is attributed to the environment during a busy window on the shared node, and it is being retested on ROCm 10.

**Benchmark.** CUDA-graph timing on the shapes `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py` uses, us per call, k=2048, width 163840, all outputs checked exact, AITER 0.1.26. `benchmark_top_k_per_row_decode.py --backends native aiter persistent --graph` times the same kernels.

| logits | rows | width | per_row | aiter | persistent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| randn | 1 | 4K | 18.5 | 8.2 | 5.5 |
| randn | 64 | 16K | 26.3 | 13.0 | 16.1 |
| randn | 256 | 32K | 40.1 | 19.0 | 27.3 |
| randn | 64 | 128K | 93.4 | 43.7 | 35.5 |
| randn | 256 | 128K | 102.0 | 50.3 | 41.1 |
| clustered | 1 | 4K | 26.4 | 10.5 | 12.4 |
| clustered | 64 | 16K | 56.5 | 21.5 | 27.1 |
| clustered | 1 | 32K | 90.0 | 40.9 | 44.3 |
| clustered | 64 | 128K | 311.5 | 133.9 | 60.1 |
| clustered | 256 | 128K | 329.9 | 143.8 | 65.7 |

Over all 36 shapes per distribution (1/4/16/64/128/256 rows x 4K-128K), persistent is 2.23x faster than `per_row` and 1.08x faster than AITER on randn logits (ahead on 22/36), and 2.63x faster than `per_row` and 0.98x against AITER on clustered logits (`randn * 0.01 + 3`, ahead on 9/36). Against the previous revision with the ROCm-only forks, #62936's shared paths are 5.7% slower on randn (mostly 32K rows) and 10% faster on clustered logits.

**Duplicate check.** Searched open PRs for `persistent_topk ROCm`, `persistent topk hip`, `ROCm sparse indexer topk`, `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits workspace`, `topk workspace alias`, `_row_ends`, `lengths size mismatch` and `sampled_topk`:
- #50470 routes sparse-indexer decode top-k through AITER, a different backend that complements this one.
- #55122 changes how `persistent_topk` selects ties on CUDA and does not build it for ROCm.
- #38704 moves ROCm sparse-indexer allocations into the workspace manager and does not touch the top-k workspace.
- #41748 replaces the `cudaMemsetAsync` of the row states in `topk.cu` with in-kernel cleanup. It does not build for ROCm or move the logits, but it touches the same code and will need a rebase against whichever lands second.

No open PR builds `persistent_topk` for ROCm, fixes the logits overlap or fixes the `_row_ends` routing.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

speedup_evidence.claim: faster than AITER on randn logits (ahead on 22/36), and 2.63x
5.7% slower on randn (mostly 32K rows) and 10% faster
5.7% slower on randn (mostly 32K rows) and 10% faster

title: [Perf] Tune the Triton packed GDN decode tile on SM90
author: Rockyeast
body:
## Overview

Use `BV = 4` for the Triton packed GDN decode kernel on SM90 (H100/H200) when the recurrent state is FP32,
the SM90 counterpart of #61355 (SM100). The kernel is unchanged; this adds one dispatch branch.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes this kernel's SM90 tile (searched open PRs for "packed decode" and
"GDN decode"; #62961 only touches this kernel's tests). Sibling tunings: #61355 (SM100, merged), #61823
(SM89, open), #54181 (SM120, closed).

## Claims

- **1.02–2.16x faster kernel, 1.34x geometric mean** over 99 `(H, HV, batch)` points on H200 with an FP32
  state (cold L2, CUPTI). `BV = 4` is the fastest tile at all 99 points.
- **1.0–1.8% lower decode latency** serving Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (FP32 state is its checkpoint default),
  matching what the kernel saving predicts; throughput within noise.
- Output and updated recurrent state are **bitwise identical** to `BV = 32` at every measured point.
  BF16 state is unchanged.

## Validation

### Kernel (cold L2)

H200 NVL (132 SMs, 60 MiB L2), `K = V = 128`, BF16 qkv, QK L2-norm on. Each CUDA graph cycles through
enough disjoint state slots that the state touched between two uses of a slot is >= 4x L2 (240 MiB), so
the state is never L2-resident, as in a decode step. Kernel time from CUPTI (`torch.profiler`) over graph
replays; 7 rounds with the tile order shuffled each round, median reported (round-to-round spread <= 1.8%).
Speedup of `BV = 4` over `BV = 32`, FP32 state:

| (H, HV) | B=1 | B=2 | B=4 | B=8 | B=16 | B=32 | B=64 | B=128 | B=256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (16, 48) Qwen3.8-27B TP1 | 1.69 | 1.52 | 1.19 | 1.29 | 1.15 | 1.08 | 1.04 | 1.03 | 1.02 |
| (8, 24) TP2 | 1.86 | 1.70 | 1.52 | 1.21 | 1.29 | 1.17 | 1.09 | 1.04 | 1.03 |
| (4, 12) TP4 | 2.03 | 1.87 | 1.70 | 1.52 | 1.20 | 1.29 | 1.17 | 1.08 | 1.04 |
| (2, 6) TP8 | 2.11 | 2.04 | 1.86 | 1.71 | 1.52 | 1.24 | 1.26 | 1.15 | 1.08 |
| (16, 32) | 1.79 | 1.62 | 1.45 | 1.19 | 1.26 | 1.11 | 1.06 | 1.04 | 1.02 |
| (8, 16) | 1.95 | 1.79 | 1.63 | 1.45 | 1.19 | 1.24 | 1.11 | 1.06 | 1.04 |
| (4, 8) | 2.08 | 1.97 | 1.79 | 1.64 | 1.44 | 1.15 | 1.23 | 1.11 | 1.06 |
| (2, 4) | 2.16 | 2.11 | 1.97 | 1.80 | 1.60 | 1.46 | 1.23 | 1.24 | 1.12 |
| (16, 64) | 1.61 | 1.45 | 1.19 | 1.24 | 1.11 | 1.06 | 1.04 | 1.02 | 1.02 |
| (8, 32) | 1.78 | 1.63 | 1.45 | 1.19 | 1.26 | 1.12 | 1.06 | 1.04 | 1.02 |
| (4, 16) | 1.95 | 1.79 | 1.64 | 1.46 | 1.17 | 1.25 | 1.11 | 1.05 | 1.03 |

Absolute time for (16, 48), `BV = 32` → `4`: 6.65 → 3.94 us at B=1, 19.5 → 15.2 at B=8,
58.0 → 53.9 at B=32, 412.5 → 404.1 at B=256 (bandwidth-bound on the state, so the gain shrinks).
`BV` in {4, 8, 16, 32} gave bitwise-identical output and updated state at all 198 points (FP32 and BF16
state).

### End to end

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (48 GDN layers), vLLM 0.32.0 with this rule applied, H200 NVL, `vllm bench serve`,
random 1024 in / 128 out, prefix caching off, `max_num_seqs 64`; unpatched and patched interleaved,
2 runs each (mean):

| concurrency | metric | unpatched | patched | change | predicted from kernel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | median TPOT | 10.78 ms | 10.65 ms | −1.2% | −1.2% |
| 8 | median ITL | 11.72 ms | 11.51 ms | −1.8% | −1.8% |
| 32 | median ITL | 14.60 ms | 14.45 ms | −1.0% | −1.4% |
| 1 / 8 / 32 | output tok/s | 86.1 / 503.7 / 1085.6 | 86.6 / 508.4 / 1088.0 | +0.5 / +0.9 / +0.2% | |

"Predicted" is the per-call kernel saving at that batch x 48 layers over the step time. The kernel is 3%
of a step at batch 1 and 19% at batch 32.

### Tests

```
pytest -q tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_recurrent_packed_decode.py   # 14 passed on H200 NVL
```

The FP32-state cases (`K = V = 128`) take the new branch on SM90.

<details>
<summary>Microbenchmark script</summary>

```python
"""Packed GDN decode kernel (vLLM's Triton fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode), cold L2:
time per call for each value-tile size BV, batch size and (H, HV) head layout, FP32 and BF16 state.

The wrapper is vLLM's own, with its fixed `BV = min(next_power_of_2(V), 32)` line replaced by a module
variable. Each CUDA graph cycles through enough disjoint state-slot sets that the state touched between
two uses of the same slot is at least 4x the L2 (a decode step touches each sequence's state once).
State slot 0 is the kernel's null slot (skipped), so real slots start at 1. Output and updated state
are compared bitwise with BV=32 at every point. Kernel time comes from CUPTI (torch.profiler) over graph
replays; CUDA-event time per call (which includes the gaps between graph nodes) is recorded too.
BV order is shuffled in each of ROUNDS rounds; reported values are medians over rounds.
usage: gdn_decode_bv_cold.py <out.json>
"""
import inspect, json, math, random, statistics, sys
import torch
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity
from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import fused_recurrent as fr

src = inspect.getsource(fr.fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode)
needle = 'BV = min(triton.next_power_of_2(V), 32)'
assert src.count(needle) == 1
ns = dict(fr.__dict__)
exec(compile(src.replace(needle, 'BV = _BV'), '<packed-decode-bv>', 'exec'), ns)
wrapper = ns['fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode']

LAYOUTS = [(16, 48), (8, 24), (4, 12), (2, 6),      # HV/H = 3 (Qwen3.8-27B at TP1/2/4/8)
           (16, 32), (8, 16), (4, 8), (2, 4),       # HV/H = 2
           (16, 64), (8, 32), (4, 16)]              # HV/H = 4
BATCHES = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256]
BVS = [4, 8, 16, 32]
if __import__('os').environ.get('GDN_QUICK'):
    LAYOUTS, BATCHES = [(16, 48), (2, 6)], [1, 64]
K = V = 128
ROUNDS = 7
EVENT_REPS = 10
CUPTI_REPS = 3
dev = 'cuda'
props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
L2 = props.L2_cache_size
FOOTPRINT = 4 * L2
torch.manual_seed(0)
random.seed(0)
print('DEVICE', torch.cuda.get_device_name(), 'SMs', props.multi_processor_count, 'L2', L2, flush=True)


def kernel_us(g, sets):
    """Mean CUPTI duration of one packed-decode kernel over CUPTI_REPS graph replays."""
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
        for _ in range(CUPTI_REPS):
            g.replay()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
    durs = [e.device_time for e in prof.events()
            if 'packed_decode' in e.name and e.device_type == torch.autograd.DeviceType.CUDA]
    if not durs:
        durs = [e.cuda_time for e in prof.events() if 'packed_decode' in e.name and e.cuda_time > 0]
    return (sum(durs) / len(durs), len(durs)) if durs else (None, 0)


def event_us(g, sets):
    us = []
    for _ in range(EVENT_REPS):
        e0, e1 = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        e0.record(); g.replay(); e1.record(); e1.synchronize()
        us.append(e0.elapsed_time(e1) * 1000 / sets)
    return statistics.median(us)


rows = []
for state_dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
    for H, HV in LAYOUTS:
        A_log = torch.randn(HV, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
        dt_bias = torch.randn(HV, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
        for B in BATCHES:
            elsize = torch.empty((), dtype=state_dtype).element_size()
            set_bytes = B * HV * V * K * elsize
            sets = max(2, math.ceil(FOOTPRINT / set_bytes))
            pool = torch.randn(1 + B * sets, HV, V, K, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32).mul_(0.02).to(state_dtype)
            pristine = pool[:1 + B].clone()   # slot 0 (null) + set 0; timing updates `pool` in place
            qkv = torch.randn(B, 2 * H * K + HV * V, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            a = torch.randn(B, HV, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            b = torch.randn(B, HV, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            idx = [torch.arange(1 + s * B, 1 + (s + 1) * B, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32) for s in range(sets)]
            out = torch.empty(B, 1, HV, V, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            real = torch.arange(1, 1 + B, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
            res, graphs = {}, {}
            for bv in BVS:
                ns['_BV'] = bv
                st = pristine.clone()
                wrapper(qkv, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, K ** -0.5, st, out, real, True)
                res[bv] = dict(out=out.clone(), state=st[1:].clone(), ev=[], cu=[])
                def step(bv=bv):
                    ns['_BV'] = bv
                    for s in range(sets):
                        wrapper(qkv, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, K ** -0.5, pool, out, idx[s], True)
                stream = torch.cuda.Stream(); stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
                with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
                    step()
                torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
                g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
                with torch.cuda.graph(g):
                    step()
                g.replay()
                graphs[bv] = g
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            ncupti = {}
            for _ in range(ROUNDS):
                order = BVS[:]
                random.shuffle(order)
                for bv in order:
                    res[bv]['ev'].append(event_us(graphs[bv], sets))
                    cu, n = kernel_us(graphs[bv], sets)
                    ncupti[bv] = n
                    if cu is not None:
                        res[bv]['cu'].append(cu)
            ref = res[32]
            us_ev = {v: round(statistics.median(res[v]['ev']), 3) for v in BVS}
            us_cu = {v: (round(statistics.median(res[v]['cu']), 3) if res[v]['cu'] else None) for v in BVS}
            have_cu = all(us_cu[v] is not None for v in BVS)
            basis = us_cu if have_cu else us_ev
            row = dict(state=str(state_dtype).split('.')[-1], H=H, HV=HV, B=B,
                       sets=sets, footprint_MB=round(sets * set_bytes / 2**20, 1), L2_MB=round(L2 / 2**20, 1),
                       us_cupti=us_cu, us_event=us_ev, cupti_kernels_per_bv=ncupti,
                       speedup_bv4_cupti=(round(us_cu[32] / us_cu[4], 3) if have_cu else None),
                       speedup_bv4_event=round(us_ev[32] / us_ev[4], 3),
                       best_bv=min(BVS, key=lambda v: basis[v]),
                       round_spread_bv4_cupti=(round((max(res[4]['cu']) - min(res[4]['cu'])) / us_cu[4], 3) if have_cu else None),
                       out_abs_max=float(ref['out'].float().abs().max()),
                       out_nonzero_rows=int((ref['out'].float().abs().amax(dim=(1, 2, 3)) > 0).sum()),
                       bitwise_out={v: bool(torch.equal(res[v]['out'], ref['out'])) for v in BVS},
                       bitwise_state={v: bool(torch.equal(res[v]['state'], ref['state'])) for v in BVS})
            rows.append(row)
            print('ROW', json.dumps(row), flush=True)
            del graphs, pool, res
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
json.dump(dict(device=torch.cuda.get_device_name(), sms=props.multi_processor_count, l2_bytes=L2,
               footprint_bytes=FOOTPRINT, rounds=ROUNDS, rows=rows), open(sys.argv[1], 'w'), indent=1)
print('DONE', flush=True)
```
</details>

## Details

- The rule is batch-independent, so on SM90 with an FP32 state only one tile variant is reachable and
  graph capture compiles it; there is no batch-size boundary to warm up.
- BF16 state keeps `BV = 32`: no single rule wins everywhere on SM90 (the best, `4` for `B*HV <= 96`
  else `16`, is 1.18x geometric mean but up to 6% slower, and >2% slower at 7/99 points).
- Measured on H200 NVL only. The branch also covers H100 and H20 (fewer SMs, lower bandwidth), where I
  have not measured it.
- CI: `kernels/fla` runs on B200 and MI355 only, so CI does not reach this SM90 branch. The test above was
  run on H200 against this change.
- No new host synchronization: the branch reads only the state dtype and the device capability, like the
  SM100 branch above it.

title: [Bugfix][Bench] Handle packed hybrid KV and speculative recurrent state
author: WoosukKwon
body:
## Overview

Fix `vllm bench forward` on hybrid attention/recurrent models: initialize packed KV caches using manager-block views and reserve/restore all speculative recurrent state slots.

## Claims

- Packed hybrid KV layouts no longer fail with `No block dim of size ...` during benchmark initialization.
- Verify requests get disjoint recurrent scratch blocks for every configured speculative token, and replay restores all those blocks.
- Changes are confined to benchmark setup and replay state; serving execution and the timed model-forward interval are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 validation of the retained tests: 3 cases passed (native CLI, cache isolation, recurrent state). All targeted pre-commit checks pass.

Base: `b82393b77315692f390880d2e931fdc1fbd13928`. Validation used four GB200 GPUs, native MRV2, and dummy weights (this checks benchmark execution/state, not model accuracy).

| Reproducer | Base | Fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Native GLM-5.3-Flash TP4, FP8 KV, FlashInfer sparse MLA, ngram 5 target-only | All ranks fail: `ValueError: No block dim of size 3979 in (6619401, 64, 132)` | Decode, Verify, Mixed finish; all ranks finite, deterministic, graph/eager relative RMS 0 |
| Tiny Qwen3Next public CLI | `assert 5 == (1 + (7 * 2))` fails: only one state per request | Passes: all speculative slots counted, Verify/Mixed finite and deterministic |
| CPU speculative-state regression | Too few recurrent scratch slots per request | Passes capacity, non-overlap, and complete state-restoration checks |
| CPU packed-view regression | Native GLM reproducer above covers the original layout failure | Passes; adjacent interleaved layers remain unchanged |

Native cases: `decode=1*1@512`, `verify=2*6@512:5`, `mixed=128@512,2*6@512:5`; two samples of two replays. Measured medians were 4.723 / 8.443 / 20.134 ms respectively, with sample spreads 0.04% / 0.03% / 0.05%. These are execution checks, not a speedup claim.

Commands (run from this checkout with the installed vLLM environment):

```bash
/home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -k 'test_bench_packed_kv_blocks or test_bench_speculative_mamba_blocks or test_bench_forward_hybrid_verify' -v
```

Final CPU selection: 7 passed; public CLI: 1 passed (53.47 s), base: 1 failed (52.53 s).

The public CLI regression creates a local tiny Qwen3Next model and checks finite, deterministic Verify/Mixed replay. The benchmark instantiates the real LLM engine. No checkpoint loading behavior changes; dummy weights are appropriate to this forward-state regression.

## Details

Hybrid cache groups can pack multiple attention kernel blocks inside one manager block and interleave layers. The existing `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache_to_manager_blocks` reconstructs the correct manager view without copying. Recurrent state requires one base slot plus `MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks`; unlike attention tails, every recurrent slot may be read or overwritten during verification.

These three fixes form one benchmark-state correctness change: without the packed-view fix the affected hybrid model cannot initialize; without either recurrent-state fix verification allocates or restores the wrong state. The CPU tests check allocation capacity and memory isolation without pinning block IDs or a complete storage layout. The snapshots use additional GPU memory proportional to the actual speculative state slots. Their copies remain outside the measured interval.

Duplicate-work checks searched open PRs for `"bench forward" "KV"`, `"bench forward" "Mamba"`, `"bench forward" "KDA"`, and `"packed" "benchmark"`. No open PR addressed these benchmark-state failures. The issue inventory came from local model experiments and has no linked GitHub issue number. Existing packed-cache connector and kernel PRs affect different paths.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to implement, test, and prepare this change. The human submitter confirmed review of every changed line and execution of the relevant tests before submission.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Build the SWA decode metadata in one launch
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview With `--monokernel` on gfx950 (MI355X), DeepSeek-V4.1 decode batches of up to 32 rows now build their SWA metadata with `swa_decode_meta`'s single Triton launch (#60731). Before, they took vLLM's 8 launches per SWA group. #60731 enabled the kernel only on gfx942, but the kernel has no arch-specific code. This PR converges with #63994: it takes #63994's gate, `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` (`on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`), and adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step and the GPU validation below. ## Claims - **49 fewer launches per decode step at c1: 114 to 65.** That is 7 SWA groups (4 target, 3 DSpark draft), each going from 8 launches to 1. Counted in a torch-profiler trace of each arm. - **Decode step (ITL p50): c1 -100 us (-1.75%), c2 -80 us (-1.16%).** - Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X TP4, `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6 (synthetic AL 3.87, AV off), 32k in / 1k out, on `main` nightly 5d35ce3934. - Runs: 2 rounds with the arms' GPU halves swapped. The per-round deltas are -1.85% and -1.66% at c1, and -1.70% and -0.61% at c2. - **Same metadata, same accuracy.** - On MI355X, the kernel test matches vLLM's ops. - With AV off, GSM8K matches base at 4 parallel requests, where every decode-only step takes the new path (6 runs per arm), and at 8 parallel (10 runs per arm). - Acceptance length (AL) on first passes and on passes with a per-request `cache_salt` is 3.577 in both arms. - With AV on (1 server per arm), GSM8K and AL match as well. - **Unchanged:** gfx942, runs without `--monokernel`, other arches, and prefill, mixed or >32-row batches. The gate test covers arch x flag; the row and prefill guards are #60731's and untouched. There is no new flag. ## Validation **Tests (MI355X, gfx950)** | Test | This PR | Before (PR base) | |---|---|---| | `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py`: kernel vs vLLM's ops, 300 random batches per case | `-k swa_decode_meta`: 2 passed; whole file: 3 passed | (kernel unchanged) | | `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`, with the new gate test (arch x `--monokernel`) | 82 passed | 81 passed, 1 failed: `[gfx950-True]` `assert [] == [False]` | | Extra, not in the PR: the kernel test with the target's 7 rows per request (k=6), the k=6 draft block, and 4 seeds x 500 batches | 8 passed: 4,000 batches; target rows 1-4 and 7/14/21/28, draft rows 6/12/18/24 at width 192 | | - **CI:** - The kernel test (`-k swa_decode_meta`) is added to `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics`. Until now CI ran it only in the MI300 (gfx942) kernels step. - The gate test runs in the existing `(MI355) Basic Models (Other)` mirror. It stubs `launch` and the platform, so no CI job runs `build()` with the real kernel on gfx950. The trace and the GSM8K runs below cover that path outside CI. - **Other checks:** - On MI355X, the gate test kills 6 of 6 gate mutants: `on_mi3xx()` in place of the arch check, gfx942 only, any ROCm arch, no `--monokernel` check, no `cache_clear()`, and `build()` back on `enabled()`. - pre-commit passes on the 5 files at the first commit, and ruff passes on the second. - The PR applies cleanly to current `main`. **Performance.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, one TP4 server per half of the node. The servers run `--monokernel` with DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87 and AV off. The workload is random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, 32 prompts per run, 3 runs per point on the same server. The decode step is ITL p50. | ITL p50 (ms), each cell base / PR | Round 1 (base on GPUs 0-3) | Round 2 (base on GPUs 4-7) | Mean base | Mean PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | c1 | 5.687 / 5.581 | 5.681 / 5.587 | 5.684 | 5.584 | **-100 us (-1.75%)** | | c2 | 6.917 / 6.800 | 6.865 / 6.824 | 6.891 | 6.812 | **-80 us (-1.16%)** | - **Noise:** - The 3 runs on one server span up to 0.3% at c1 and up to 1.0% at c2 (max-min). - The same arm moves 0.1% between GPU halves at c1 and up to 0.75% at c2. - **Image:** `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9`. That is the PR base, which already has #63576, plus 23 commits. - The PR arm is the same image with the PR's 3 vllm files copied in. The end-to-end runs used the first commit. The second only swaps `on_mi3xx()` for `on_gfx942() or on_gfx950()`, which give the same value on gfx942 and gfx950 (`_ON_MI3XX` is exactly those two arches). The tests above ran on the second commit. - Those files are byte-identical between the PR base and 5d35ce3934. - AV-on perf was not measured. **Launch counts.** These come from a torch-profiler trace of each arm: rank 0, c1, 133 decode steps each. The SWA-build kernel counts are the same on every step. The total, fill and copy counts below are the per-step mode; a few steps add the same extra launches in both arms. The PR is 49 launches lower on every step. | Per decode step | base | PR | |---|---:|---:| | All launches (eager kernels plus graph launches): 115 of 133 steps; the others are 117/133 for base, 68/84 for PR | 114 | 65 | | `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (target) and the draft's non-causal index kernel | 4 + 3 | 0 | | `torch.ge` (`compare_scalar_kernel`) / `FillFunctor` | 7 / 9 | 0 / 2 | | `_count_valid_row_entries_kernel` / rocprim scan / `_compact_dense_row_to_ragged_kernel` | 7 / 7 / 7 | 0 / 0 / 0 | | `__amd_rocclr_copyBuffer` | 24 | 10 | | `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` | 0 | 7 | | **SWA metadata launches.** The fill and copy rows also hold 2 fills and 10 copies per step outside the SWA build, in both arms. | **56** | **7** | | `_token_request_mapping_kernel` (control) | 2 | 2 | | GPU time per step (median, profiler on). Base: the target index, compare, count, scan and compact kernels; the draft index kernels, fills and copies are not counted. PR: `_decode_swa_meta_kernel`. | 136.5 us | 36.8 us | **Accuracy and AL** (AV off unless noted). GSM8K-1319 is 8-shot at temperature 0, over `/v1/completions`. AL is real block-rejection acceptance, read from `/metrics`. | GSM8K-1319 | base | PR | Delta | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 4 parallel: every decode-only step takes the new path. 6 runs per arm on 4 servers. | 0.9143 | 0.9151 | +0.0008 | | 8 parallel: steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build. 10 runs per arm on 4 servers. | 0.9146 | 0.9123 | -0.0023 (SE 0.0022). Per-server means: -0.006, below the 0.0077 binomial SE of a single run. | | Mono forced off, so the aiter attention reads the kernel's ragged views. 4 parallel, 2 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9132 | 0.9143 | +0.0011 | | Mono forced off, 8 parallel (mostly vLLM's views). 4 runs per arm, 1 server each. | 0.9166 | 0.9177 | +0.0011 | | AV on, 8 parallel: 2 runs per arm, 1 server each | 0.9143 | 0.9166 | +0.0023 | | AV on, 4 parallel: 1 run per arm | 0.9227 | 0.9158 | -0.0068 (per-run sd is about 0.005) | | AL with AV off, on a first pass (only the shared 8-shot prefix cached) or with a per-request `cache_salt` (nothing cached). 8 runs per arm: 6 at 8 parallel, 2 at 4 parallel. | 3.577 | 3.577 | 0 | | AL with AV on, first pass | 3.373 | 3.383 | +0.010 | - **Run-to-run variation:** - Any two AV-off runs with mono on, at the same parallelism, on the same server or not, differ on 53-88 of the 1319 questions (53-92 including the mono-off runs). - Greedy decode on this stack is not run-to-run deterministic on either arm. The first token can differ even with a fresh `cache_salt`, so a text-identity check was not possible. - **The mono-off rows:** - With `--monokernel`, mono consumes only the dense indices and lengths. - The 4-parallel mono-off row is therefore the end-to-end check of the ragged indices, `indptr` and `is_valid_token`. **Sync check.** One TP4 server per arm ran with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, which polices the worker's `execute_model` and `sample_tokens` after warmup. Each served c1 and c2 (8 requests each, 512 out), 300 GSM8K questions at 4 parallel requests, and 4 greedy probes. Neither arm reported a sync, logged an error or failed a request.
Reproduction commands ```bash IMG=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce3934a7804b298559d2d99eec33792e1eb9 # PR arm: the same image with this PR's 3 files copied over # /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/{ops/__init__.py,ops/swa_decode_meta.py,rocm.py} # Mono-off arms: in .../vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/mono_decode.py, in _decode_step, change # `if not 1 <= rows <= _max_rows():` to `if True:`, so mono declines every step. # Server, 4x MI355X, inside the image VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \ VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \ VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \ vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \ --max-model-len 1048576 --block-size 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' # Accuracy servers: "rejection_sample_method":"block", without synthetic_acceptance_length. # AV-on round: "enable_adaptive_verification":true. # Perf: warm up (c2, 4 prompts, 256 out, seed 7), then run each point 3 times: vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \ --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 # c2: --max-concurrency 2 --seed 102 # GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 8 shots, 1319 questions, temperature 0, max 512 tokens, # 8 or 4 parallel requests. # AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total) # Uncached passes: a unique "cache_salt" per request. # Tests on MI355X pytest tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py -k swa_decode_meta pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # Fail-before: keep the new test, restore the pre-PR vllm files, re-run. git checkout $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/__init__.py \ vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/ops/swa_decode_meta.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py # 81 passed, 1 failed ([gfx950-True]) ```
## Details **Change.** `ops.swa_decode_meta_enabled()`, the gate from #63994, returns true with `--monokernel` on ROCm when `on_gfx942()` or `on_gfx950()` holds. Only `swa_decode_meta.build` uses it. The other gfx942 helpers keep `ops.enabled()`. On gfx942 the two gates agree. **Limits.** - The kernel takes at most 32 rows; gfx950 mono takes up to 48. - With AV off at k=6, steps with 5 or more requests keep vLLM's build: the target at 35 or more rows, and the draft, which is padded to the 36-row graph. gfx942 behaves the same. - With AV on, the cutoff is 32 rows, not a request count. - AV-on `--monokernel` deployments now take this path. The AV-on round served without errors and matched base on accuracy and AL. **Related PRs.** - **#63994** (cpersson-amd) made the same change, and the two are converged here. This PR takes #63994's `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` gate, with Carl Persson as co-author of that commit. It adds the gate test, the MI355 CI step (#63994 used the optional `test-amd.yaml` step) and the GPU validation. #63994 can be closed. - **#58352:** it does not conflict textually, but the gains overlap. If it lands first, about 20 of the 49 launches remain (inferred, not measured). - **#61311** touches 4 of this PR's 5 files: `models_basic.yaml`, `ops/__init__.py`, `rocm.py` and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. - It renames `KernelConfig.monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `specialized_decode`, and replaces `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py` with `test_dsv41_specialized_decode.py`. - Whichever lands second rebases: rename `_monokernel` in `swa_decode_meta_enabled()` and move the gate test. - **#63486 (draft)** moves the DSv4.1 mono CI and `test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`. If it lands first, I drop the `models_basic.yaml` hunk and move the gate test. - **#63891 (draft)** runs fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with `--monokernel`. It adds its own `mi3xx_enabled()` on `on_mi3xx()`, and the same review applies to it. Both PRs touch the same `models_basic.yaml` step and the `ops/__init__.py` docstring; the second to land merges those hunks.
Why the metadata is the same, and who reads it - **What the kernel writes.** `_decode_swa_meta_kernel` is integer Triton with no arch intrinsics. - For rows `[0, n)` it writes `is_valid_token` and the dense window indices and lengths. It sets the lengths from row `n` to the end of the buffer to 0. It writes `indptr[:n+1]` and the ragged indices up to `indptr[n]`. - These are the same values that `torch.ge`, the length fill, `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` (or `ComputeDSparkNoncausalSWAIndicesKernel` for the draft block), `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` and `_copy_ragged_to_graph_buffers` produce. - `build()` returns views of the same persistent buffers, with the same lengths: ragged `[:max(n*width, 1)]` and `indptr[:n+1]`. - **Who reads it.** - **Mono:** with `--monokernel`, every target and DSpark-draft layer runs mono on decode-only steps of 48 rows or fewer that replay a FULL graph or run eagerly. Mono reads only the dense indices and lengths, `slot_mapping` and `token_to_req`. - **aiter sparse MLA:** on steps that mono declines, such as PIECEWISE steps, it (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`) reads the ragged indices between `indptr[t]` and `indptr[t+1]`. It sizes its splits from the ragged view's `numel()`, which is `n*width` on both paths. - **Top-k build:** it reads `is_valid_token` on compressed layers. - Draft and target builders do not share buffers. - **The only bytes that differ** are the ragged entries past `indptr[n]`. vLLM's build copies them from a `torch.empty` tensor; the kernel leaves the previous contents. No reader reads past `indptr`. - **#60154** is on `main` but not in the measured image. It fuses inverse RoPE and the MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse-MLA output, and does not change the index views that call reads. So this argument holds on current `main`.
An AL caveat for anyone reproducing (affects main, not this PR) On 4 of the 10 AV-off servers, AL fell from about 3.58 to 3.42-3.45 on GSM8K passes that repeated the same prompts. Those passes had about 96% prefix-cache hits, against about 89% on a first pass. The 4 servers were 2 base and 2 PR; one of the PR servers had mono forced off. - The two dropped servers that ran later passes stayed low. - On the one dropped server that also ran passes with a per-request `cache_salt`, those passes stayed at 3.58. - Accuracy did not move. - With AV on, the PR server's repeat pass also fell (3.383 to 3.279); base's did not (3.373 to 3.364). Compare AL on first or salted passes only. I will look into the drop separately.
