(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER's all-gather for small TP all-gathers
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

On ROCm gfx950 and gfx942, TP all-gathers now use AITER's IPC all-gather instead of RCCL when the TP group already runs AITER custom all-reduce. "Small" means fp32/fp16/bf16 at TP 2, 4 or 8, up to AITER's own per-rank limit (`should_custom_ag`: vLLM's 128 MiB AITER buffer / (2 x TP) = 32 / 16 / 8 MiB). vLLM adds no cap of its own: in two AITER vs RCCL sweeps, no timed size (TP2: up to 20 of its 32 MiB) was faster on RCCL in both runs. gfx1250 stays on RCCL until it is measured; gfx942 was verified by @frida-andersson on MI325X ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082), Claims). This extends #48247 (DP only) to TP. #48446's RCCL path stays as the fallback. Below, `base` is a main-equivalent image, `pr` adds the previous head's files (b8fd6897a0, with a 2 MiB cap) and `r1` adds 1eb0aa0805's: the round-1 code with a gfx950-only gate, called "this head" below. The current head, 8ca2504b97, is that code rebased onto main with the gate widened to gfx942; it routes gfx950 the same way. See the image table under GPU. cN means N requests in flight.

## Claims

- **Decode step 1.2-1.9% faster at TP4 c1-c4 (4 swapped rounds), 1.4% at TP4 c8 (one swapped pair) and 0.8-1.2% at TP8 c1-c4** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X; `base` matches main on the touched files).
  - TP4 `--monokernel`, previous head, 4 position-swapped rounds (P1-P4): -106 / -120 / -102 us at c1 / c2 / c4 (-1.94 / -1.79 / -1.19%). pr was faster in all 12 round and concurrency pairs, and each drop exceeds the largest same-arm, same-half spread (15 / 27 / 77 us). This head routes c1-c4 decode the same way (every decode gather there is at most 1.81 MB per rank, under the old cap). A c1 re-run on the rebased head gives -113 us against base (previous head: -106 us) and -12 us against pr.
  - TP4 c8 / c16 / c32, this head, where the logits gathers (3.1-14.5 MB per rank) now move to AITER. Against base (one swapped pair, R1/R2): -185 / -350 / -133 us (-1.41 / -2.11 / -0.65%). Against pr (R3/R4, the cap removal alone): -83 / -52 / -307 us. Together they imply pr - base of -102 us at c8, in line with P1-P4 (-106 us at c1), but -298 / +174 us at c16 / c32, where pr differs from base only by Engram gathers. So about 200 us of between-round drift sits in c16 and c32, and neither is established. c8 holds in all four orientations but is marginal: against base, R1's -121 us is just above r1's 116 us same-half spread and inside the cell's largest rep range (145 us); against pr, both orientations (-77 / -89 us) are inside the spread.
  - TP8 without `--monokernel`, previous head (T1-T4: base, pr, pr, base): -0.81 / -1.11 / -1.24% at c1 / c2 / c4, each above the same-arm spread across server starts (21 / 6 / 54 us). The routing there is unchanged; not re-run.
  - Always copying in, instead of AITER's registered capture path (scratch mutant `mut_reg`, M1/M2), costs about 25 us per step at c1, about a quarter of the c1 gain.
  - Under the torch profiler, pr's TP4 step was slower at c1 and c2; without it, pr and r1 were faster than base in every run (see Tradeoffs).
- **gfx942 (MI325X), verified by @frida-andersson** ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63890#issuecomment-6590588082)), with the gate widened to gfx942. The cell is TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32768 -> 1024, 32 prompts, c1. ITL p50 went 7.15 -> 7.01 ms (-140 us) on the same 4 GPUs and 7.04 -> 6.99 ms (-50 us) on different GPU halves: two passes, not position-swapped. TTFT and TPOT were flat, and `niah_single_2` at 16384 scored 1.0. Not measured on gfx942: c2 and up (including the c8+ gathers above the old 2 MiB cap) and the AITER vs RCCL sweep.
- **AITER never lost to RCCL in both of two sweeps** (TP 2/4/8, 768 timed points each; table below). The sweeps cover 1 KiB up to AITER's limit (TP2: up to 20 MiB of its 32), dims 0 / middle / last, bf16 and fp32, eager and graph replay, all bit-exact against RCCL. The better run is at least 1.07x at every point. Run 1 alone lost at 13 points (down to 0.32x, TP2 graph, 2.004 MiB), each at least 1.21x in run 2. Dim 0 (a copy-in plus AITER's kernel against one RCCL kernel) has graph-replay medians of 1.18 / 1.41 / 1.43x at TP 2/4/8 and lost only in run 1 (5 graph points of 128 KiB or less), so it stays on AITER.
- **Bit-exact gathers; GSM8K accuracy unchanged; acceptance length (AL) has no consistent direction.** The PR's GPU test checks TP2 with `torch.equal`, eager and under graph replay; scratch matrices extend this to TP4 and TP8 and up to AITER's limit. On GSM8K-1319 (6 base-vs-PR pairs of the same pass), mean accuracy is 0.916 on both arms, and the per-question flips between arms (68-82) are about the same as within one arm (63-81). AL changed by +0.005, -0.010, -0.021 and -0.055 with pr on half B, and by -0.005, +0.013, +0.027 and -0.014 with r1 on half A. Only the -0.055 (GSM8K-300 with expandable segments, E1, one unswapped run) exceeds every same-arm AL span (at most 0.030). The +0.027 (r1, 16 in flight, no same-condition repeat) exceeds every same-condition span (at most 0.024), but not base's 0.030 across 4/16/32 in flight. The perf tables use synthetic AL 3.87.
- **No change elsewhere.** CUDA, ROCm archs other than gfx950 and gfx942, ROCm without `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, non-TP groups, TP6 and gate rejects keep their current path. No new flag. GPU-checked on gfx950: gate rejects, the DP group and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0`. The arch gate rests on a CPU probe.
- **Not claimed:** gfx1250 (gated off, not tested); gfx942 beyond the reviewer's two c1 passes (no sweep, no c2+, no swapped rounds); other models; timing at TP2 between 20 and 32 MiB per rank (bit-exact in the matrix, not timed). The earlier stack-image result (-2.2% to -2.6% at c1, with 5 other PRs) is context only (see Runs and noise).

## Validation

**CPU** (this head unless noted)
- [x] `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py::test_rocm_tp_all_gather_uses_aiter` (default L4 and MI300 "Distributed Comm Ops" steps): 7/7 pass (whole file: 39 passed, 10 skipped for GPUs). Dropping the `should_custom_ag` check fails exactly the rejection case. A gate widened to gfx1250 (`get_cdna_version() >= 3`) still passes, because the mock sets `use_aiter_tp_all_gather` directly. On the previous head, main's communicator failed the dim-0, middle-dim and last-dim cases, and dropping any one of the TP-size, 16-byte-row, non-empty or 2-D-view checks failed exactly one case (output below).
- [x] Arch-gate probe (scratch; vLLM's own gate inputs, arch faked). AITER all-reduce is enabled only on gfx942, gfx950 and gfx1250, at CDNA versions 3 / 4 / 5. So `in (3, 4)` is true on gfx942 and gfx950 only, and false on gfx90a, gfx908, gfx1250, gfx1100, gfx1201 and non-ROCm. The probe ran for the previous gate (`== 4`); the new result follows from the same logged inputs.
- [x] Emulation against AITER v0.1.26's index math, previous head: 35/35 (c1 call sites at TP2/4/8; int64, uint8, non-contiguous, unaligned rows, empty, 6 GPUs, non-TP group, AITER off).
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on the 4 changed files.

**GPU** (MI355X gfx950, AITER 0.1.26). Every gain credited to the PR compares `pr` or `r1` with `base`, except the cap-removal numbers (`r1` against `pr`) and the sweep (AITER against RCCL inside one image); `revcomm` and `mut_reg` check only the tests and the design.

| Image | Contents | Produced | Credited to the PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5, unchanged; touched files equal main 41f5146b5b | the reference arm of P1-P4, T1-T4, R1/R2 and every accuracy run | reference |
| `pr` | base + the previous head's two files (2 MiB cap, no arch gate) | P1-P4, T1-T4, Q1/S1/E1, profile, sync check, R3/R4; the sweep (cap lifted in the benchmark, so it times this head's path) | TP4/TP8 c1-c4, accuracy at 4 in flight, sweep |
| `r1` | base + this head's two files (gfx950 gate, no cap) | R1-R4, RQ, this head's GPU tests and matrix | TP4 c8 (c16/c32 not established), the c1 re-run, GSM8K at 4/16/32 in flight |
| `revcomm` (scratch) | base + only the previous head's `aiter_custom_all_reduce.py` (this head's but for a docstring); main's `cuda_communicator.py` | the new GPU test fails | no: shows that the test detects the change |
| `mut_reg` (scratch) | pr with `all_gather_unreg` replaced by AITER's registered capture path | M1/M2 copy-in cost; the expandable-segments failure | no: tests the copy-in design |

- [x] `test_rocm_aiter_tp_all_gather` (2 GPUs) passes on r1 and pr, also with expandable segments. With the current gate, it asserts that AITER ran dims `[0, 0, -1, -1, -1, -1]` on gfx942 and gfx950, and that AITER never ran on gfx1250, where AITER all-reduce also starts. It has run only on gfx950.
- [x] **Fails without the change:** on `revcomm` it fails at `assert aiter_dims == expected_dims` (line 196), after every `torch.equal` check passed.
- [x] `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py`: 4 passed on r1, pr and base. In a probe on pr, AITER-on engines took the new path and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_CUSTOM_AR=0` engines stayed on RCCL, with equal greedy output.
- [x] **Gate matrix on r1** (scratch): 79 cases at TP2/4/8, plus TP2/4 with expandable segments; 0 failures. Contiguous cases are bit-exact, eager and under replay. The old cap plus one row and AITER's exact limit go to AITER; the limit plus 16 B or one row, 24-byte rows, non-16-byte totals and int32 go to RCCL. Non-contiguous inputs and the DP group stay on RCCL.
- [x] **The registered capture path fails where copy-in passes:** `mut_reg` raises "a collective buffer cannot be IPC-exported" on the TP2 matrix with expandable segments.
- [x] TP2xPP2 (`test_multi_process_tensor_parallel_pipeline_parallel[test_target3-2-2]`): passes on pr (gathers on AITER) and base.
- [x] AITER vs RCCL sweep at TP2/4/8, run twice.
- [x] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: P1-P4, T1-T4, M1/M2 and 4 GSM8K/AL runs on pr; R1-R4 and GSM8K-1319 at 4/16/32 in flight (RQ) on r1.
- [x] On pr: profile (all 6 RCCL gathers per TP4 decode step moved to AITER at c1/c2/c4), `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` (0 sync errors), and E1 with expandable segments (started, captured, served, ran GSM8K-300).
- [x] 0 Traceback, RuntimeError, EngineDeadError, MEMORY_FAULT or HSA_STATUS_ERROR lines in 34 server logs (24 from the previous-head rounds, 10 from this round), and 0 failed requests out of the 2048 in R1-R4.
- [ ] *Partial:* #48446's TP8 c4 TPOT benchmark, with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash standing in for DeepSeek-V4: one server start per arm, -0.63% mean TPOT, not established.

**Not covered**
- [x] gfx942 (MI325X): DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 c1, run by @frida-andersson with the gate widened (Claims).
- [ ] gfx942: the AITER vs RCCL sweep, c2 and up, and the GPU test. The test runs in the `optional` MI300 "Distributed Features" step.
- [ ] gfx1250: gated off, not tested. Enabling it is a one-line change once the sweep and the test have run on it.
- [ ] No test that runs on gfx950 or gfx942 catches a gate widened to gfx1250.
- [ ] Timing at TP2 between 20 and 32 MiB per rank.
- [ ] r1 re-runs of TP4 c2/c4, TP8, the profile, the sync check and E1 (decode routing there is unchanged from pr).
- [ ] Llama-3.1-70B and DeepSeek-R1 at TP8: their weights are not on the node.
- [ ] GPU runs with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` unset, with `--disable-custom-all-reduce`, and at TP6. TP6 is covered by the CPU mock and AITER off by the previous head's emulation; this head's `__init__` gate only by code reading and the arch probe.
- [ ] The `optional` "(MI300|MI355) Distributed Features" CI steps, which run the GPU test, still need to be unblocked on this PR.

**AITER vs RCCL sweep** (speedup = RCCL time / AITER time). RCCL is base's path, including the `movedim` copy for dim > 0; AITER is this head's path, including the copy-in.

| TP (AITER limit per rank) | Mode | dim 0: median / min | dim > 0: median / min |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 (32 MiB; swept to 16 MiB) | graph | 1.18 / 1.09 (1.01) | 1.33 / 1.17 (0.83) |
| 2 | eager | 2.67 / 1.15 (1.15) | 2.75 / 1.21 (1.03) |

**Performance** (ITL p50 = decode step, ms). MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark k=6, synthetic AL 3.87, adaptive verification off; `vllm bench serve`, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, 32 prompts per concurrency and rep, 2 reps per run, after a warm-up. TP4 `--monokernel` runs two servers at once, one per 4-GPU half (A and B).

<details>
<summary>GPU validation details</summary>

- **Images.** base is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03c5`, unchanged. Its two communicator files have the same sha256 as main 41f5146b5b. This PR's base, 4b47db922b, adds only #63053's DP-only `tcp_store_group is None` check to `cuda_communicator.py`, which r1 carries. pr copies in `cuda_communicator.py` and `aiter_custom_all_reduce.py` from b8fd6897a0, r1 from 1eb0aa0805. `revcomm` copies only b8fd6897a0's `aiter_custom_all_reduce.py`. `mut_reg` is pr with `all_gather_unreg` calling AITER's `custom_all_gather`, which under capture binds IPC-exportable inputs directly. pr, r1, revcomm and mut_reg run this PR's `tests/` (r1 and revcomm this head's); base runs main's. GPU runs (UTC-5): previous head 2026-10-29, this head 2026-10-30.
- **GPU test.** On r1: 6 passed with the `-k` filter below (the new test plus 5 of main's), and 1 passed with `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`; the same on pr. On base, the same 5 of main's tests pass.

Of the 70 contiguous cases, 48 go to AITER and 22 to RCCL; all are bit-exact, eager and under replay. The 9 non-contiguous cases stay on RCCL and raise on both paths (c10d's "Tensors must be contiguous"). With expandable segments none of the 70 inputs was IPC-exportable, and copy-in handled all of them. pr's 61-case matrix ran at TP2, TP4 and TP8, each with and without expandable segments: 0 failures in 6 runs.
- **`mut_reg`** fails the TP2 matrix under expandable segments; in pr's run of the same matrix, 43 of the 52 inputs were not exportable. `mut_reg` registered more graph addresses at capture than pr (12128 vs 11800, 6130 vs 5962 and 521 vs 517 per call), so it bound gather inputs directly. pr registered exactly base's counts.

Exportability was not probed, and `mut_reg` was not run under E1. On both arms AITER logged at startup that expandable segments were enabled, and at capture that they were off ("using the registered custom-allreduce capture path"); both registered the same graph-address counts as without expandable segments. A grep that also matches "cannot be IPC" finds only AITER's informational startup notice.

The half offset (B - A) inside the estimate is +2, -1 and -21 us. The per-round changes have a standard deviation of 4, 10 and 37 us.
- **c4 is the weakest previous-head result.** The rounds range from -138 to -50 us. Individual reps overlap across rounds (pr up to 8.579 ms, base from 8.561 ms), though the round means do not (pr 8.493-8.539, base 8.575-8.651).
- **TP4 per round, this head** (r1 / other arm, ms):

  | Concurrency | R1 (base A, r1 B) | R2 (r1 A, base B) | R3 (pr A, r1 B) | R4 (r1 A, pr B) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 5.327 / 5.444 | 5.331 / 5.440 | 5.318 / 5.342 | 5.334 / 5.334 |
  | 8 | 12.989 / 13.111 | 12.802 / 13.051 | 12.911 / 12.987 | 12.918 / 13.007 |
  | 16 | 16.258 / 16.534 | 16.237 / 16.662 | 16.231 / 16.410 | 16.338 / 16.264 |
  | 32 | 20.454 / 20.509 | 20.248 / 20.459 | 20.288 / 20.600 | 20.239 / 20.541 |

- **Noise on this head.** r1 ran in all four rounds, twice per half. Its same-half spreads (A, B) are 3 / 9 us at c1, 116 / 79 us at c8, 101 / 27 us at c16 and 10 / 166 us at c32. base and pr ran once per half, so they have no same-half spread. The median rep ranges are 17, 122, 161 and 200 us in R1/R2, and 7, 27, 154 and 111 us in R3/R4. At c1, where r1 and pr route identically, R3 still gave r1 - pr = -24 us.
- **Cross-check of the two pairings.** (r1 - base) - (r1 - pr) implies pr - base of -100 / -102 / -298 / +174 us at c1 / c8 / c16 / c32. P1-P4 measured -106 us at c1. At c8-c32 pr differs from base only by Engram gathers (all four at c8 and c16, the two rows gathers at c32), so c1 and c8 are consistent, and c16 and c32 carry about 200 us of between-round drift.
- **Routing at c8-c32.** The target logits gather is 3.6 / 7.2 / 14.5 MB per rank at c8 / c16 / c32, and the draft logits gather 3.1 / 6.2 / 12.4 MB; at c32 the Engram `wkv` gather (2.87 MB) moves too. All are above the old 2 MiB cap and under AITER's 16 MiB limit, so they run on AITER on r1 and on RCCL on pr and base.
- **Rebase.** r1's `cuda_communicator.py` is the rebased head's. At c1 r1 and pr route identically: r1 - base is -113 us against pr - base -106 us (P1-P4 per-round standard deviation 4 us), and r1 - pr is -12 us.
- **Mean TPOT, this head,** moves with the step: against base -2.15%, -1.08%, -1.46% and -0.57% at c1, c8, c16 and c32; against pr -0.20%, -0.60%, -0.12% and -1.24%.
- **TTFT, this head.** Mean TTFT on r1 was lower than base in all 8 orientation pairs: -1.0 / -1.6 ms at c1, -0.4 / -3.2 ms at c8, -5.6 / -14.1 ms at c16 (estimates under 1%) and -272 / -29 ms at c32 (32 prompts, one wave). Against pr it was higher at c1 and c8 in both orientations (+0.06 to +1.4 ms), mixed at c16 (-16 / +5 ms) and lower at c32 (-6 / -232 ms). At c1, where r1 and pr route identically, r1 - base was -1.3 ms (-0.56%) here and pr - base +0.3 ms in P1-P4, so shifts of this size are session noise. Full 16k-token prefill chunks carry Engram gathers of about 50 MB (rows) and 210 MB (`wkv`) per rank, above AITER's limit on every arm; shorter prefill steps can move.
- **TP8.** The same-arm spread spans 2 sequential server starts per arm and is below every change. In all three TP8 cells, the slowest pr rep was faster than the fastest base rep. The T servers also carried `--profiler-config`; their profiler window ran only after the perf benchmarks.
- **Mean TPOT, previous head,** moves the same way. At TP4 it drops 1.92%, 1.67% and 0.87% at c1, c2 and c4. At TP8 it drops 0.81%, 1.06% and 1.99%; the c4 drop is within its 66 us same-arm spread.
- **TTFT, previous head,** is unchanged at TP4: the median TTFT averaged over the 8 runs per arm is 230.2 vs 230.4 ms at c1, 243.4 vs 243.4 ms at c2 and 349.2 vs 349.3 ms at c4 (rep 1 prefills cold, rep 2 hits the prefix cache).
- **Copy-in cost** (TP4, previous head, same recipe). `mut_reg`'s captured gathers bind their (exportable) inputs directly through AITER's registered path, so they skip the copy-in node. M1 has pr on half A and `mut_reg` on half B; M2 swaps them.

  | Concurrency | pr | `mut_reg` | `mut_reg` - pr | Per round, M1 / M2 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 5.345 | 5.320 | -25 us | -25 / -26 us |
  | 2 | 6.580 | 6.558 | -22 us | -18 / -26 us |
  | 4 | 8.515 | 8.518 | +4 us | +29 / -22 us |

  c1 holds in both orientations and exceeds every c1 rep range (at most 16 us) and the 15 us P1-P4 same-arm spread. c2 is inside its rep range (up to 36 us); c4 is noise (`mut_reg`'s reps spread 99 and 134 us). No arm repeated on the same half. The half offset is +0, +4 and +25 us, and mean TPOT differs by -6, -4 and +4 us.
- **E1 timing.** With real block rejection on random prompts, 8 requests per concurrency and one unswapped run, pr's ITL p50 was lower by 123, 107 and 151 us at c1, c2 and c4. This is a smoke test, not a perf result.
- **Earlier stack image** (secondary). That image was nightly 83c078d955 plus #63182, #63027, #63367, #63181 and #63355, with one unswapped run per arm; #63367 there replaces each Engram layer's `wkv` gather with a gate-partials gather. It gave -2.6% at c1 (5.284 to 5.146 ms; -2.2% against the fastest base run, 5.261 ms) and -2.2% at c2; the c2 gain was not established, because that half's base drifted 6.412-6.517 ms. It is not comparable with the swapped runs on the main-equivalent image.
- **#48446-style TPOT.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stood in for DeepSeek-V4: TP8, no spec decode, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, random 8k in / 1k out, c4, 2 reps of 32 prompts, one server start per arm.
  - Mean TPOT went from 7.060 to 7.016 ms (-0.63%), and ITL p50 from 6.950 to 6.887 ms (-0.91%).
  - Rep ranges were 7.043-7.077 and 7.012-7.020 ms. With no same-arm repeat, this is not established.
  - A single-run no-spec sweep on the same servers (random 1k in / 512 out, c1-c64) had pr lower at every concurrency, with ITL p50 down 0.48% to 1.31%. This is not established either.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Sweep details</summary>

- **Method** (scratch benchmark, not in the PR). It ran in `pr` with `AITER_TP_ALL_GATHER_MAX_SIZE` lifted, so the AITER arm is this head's path on gfx950. One process per GPU goes through vLLM's own TP group (`init_distributed_environment`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`), so the AITER instance, its 128 MiB buffer and the RCCL communicator are the ones a server builds.
  - RCCL arm: `DeviceCommunicatorBase.all_gather`, which is what base runs on ROCm (`all_gather_into_tensor`, plus the `movedim` copy for dim > 0).
  - AITER arm: `CudaCommunicator._aiter_all_gather` (gate, 2-D view, copy-in, kernel).
  - Eager: GPU time of 32 back-to-back calls with the CPU ahead. Graph: one CUDA graph of 32 gathers, captured in vLLM's `graph_capture()`, replay timed with events. Per point: the p50 over 60 reps on each rank, then the max over ranks. RCCL 2.30.4.
- **Points.** 768 per run with an AITER time: 600 sweep points (the table) and 168 call-site shapes (DeepSeek-V4.1 logits and Engram gathers, Llama-3 logits, sequence-parallel hidden states). The table's 1.07x minimum also holds for the call sites; the lowest is a 20 MiB dim-0 gather at TP2 (1.07x graph, 1.10x eager).
- **Correctness.** All 1596 rows of the two runs passed the bit-exact checks on every rank: RCCL equals `cat(dist.all_gather)`, and wherever AITER ran, AITER equals RCCL, eager and after graph replay with a changed input.
- **Dips.** Run 1 had 13 points below 1.0x: 11 at 128 KiB or less (10 of them TP8 graph replay), plus 0.32x (graph, 2.004 MiB) and 0.65x (eager, 4 MiB) at TP2, last dim, bf16. Each was at least 1.21x in run 2. Run 2 had one point below 1.0x (0.99x, TP2 graph, fp32, last dim, 4 KiB), which run 1 measured at 1.21x. On run 1 alone, the summary script suggested caps of 2 MiB at TP2 and 64 KiB at TP8; on run 2 alone, AITER's limit at every TP size. No point lost in both runs.
- **Top of the range.** At the largest timed sizes, dim 0 is 1.07-1.15x (TP2 at 16 and 20 MiB, TP4 at 16 MiB) and dim > 0 is 1.15-1.29x. TP8 at 8 MiB is 1.31-2.45x.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1 call sites at TP4** (both runs). The c8 target logits gather (56 rows x 64,640 B = 3.6 MB per rank), which only r1 moves to AITER, is 1.36x faster under graph replay and 1.53x eager. The c4 one (1.8 MB, already on AITER in pr) is 1.49-1.50x and 1.77-1.80x.
- **Sequence-parallel-sized gathers** (TP4, 5120-wide bf16 rows, dim 0): 256 rows (2.6 MB, on RCCL under the old cap) are 1.18-1.19x under graph replay and 1.40-1.41x eager; 1024 rows (10.5 MB) are 1.07-1.08x and 1.14x.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Accuracy details</summary>

- **Setup.** `--parallel N` sets the requests in flight. At 4, both logits gathers are under the old cap, so decode routes the same on pr and r1. r1's 4-in-flight passes differ from pr only in prefill Engram gathers between the old cap and AITER's limit, which now move to AITER: `wkv` at about 164-1,310 tokens and rows at about 683-5,461 tokens per step. At 16 and 32, the target (7.2 / 14.5 MB per rank) and draft (6.2 / 12.4 MB) logits gathers move to AITER on r1 only. AL is 1 + accepted / drafts, from the deltas of the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters.
- **Per-question flips.** GSM8K-1319, base against the PR image on the same pass: 78 and 71 (pr), then 82, 68, 69 and 68 (r1). Any two passes of one image: base 63-81 (15 pairs), r1 70-76 (6 pairs), pr 66 (1 pair). The 82 (r1, cold) splits into 51 r1-only and 31 base-only correct answers. GSM8K-300: base against pr differs on 10-18 questions (mean 13.0, 4 pairs); base differs from itself on 16 between the sync-check and E1 servers, pr on 11.
- **Accuracy.** GSM8K-1319 over the 6 paired passes: 0.9156 on both arms (7246 of 7914 correct each).
- **Same-arm AL differences.** Base: its four 4-in-flight GSM8K-1319 passes span 3.573-3.588 (0.015), all six including 16 and 32 in flight 3.568-3.598 (0.030), and GSM8K-300 differs by 0.009 between the sync-check and E1 servers. pr: 0.000 (GSM8K-1319, cold vs salted) and 0.024 (GSM8K-300). r1's four passes span 3.578-3.595 (0.017; 0.014 at 4 in flight).
- **Why AL can move at all.** The gathers are byte copies, so the PR can change AL only indirectly, for example through timing-dependent batch composition under real rejection.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Profile (pr, c1-c4): gathers moved, and why the profiled step was slower</summary>

**Gathers moved** (TP4, torch-profiler window

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Run DSpark's fused Markov sampling on gfx950 with --monokernel
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

This PR runs #60731's `fused_markov` DSpark sampler (one launch per draft position) on gfx950 (MI355X) with `--monokernel`, for steps of up to 5 requests. Today it runs only on gfx942, so gfx950 runs vLLM's loop of about 51 kernels per decode step at k=6. On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 c1 decode steps get 2.4% faster at equal GSM8K and AL. It interacts with #63181, #63486 and #61311 (see Details).

## Claims

- With `--monokernel` on gfx950, a DSpark decode step's Markov sampling takes k+1 = 7 launches instead of about 51. Measured with the torch profiler, TP4, 2 rounds:
  - GPU kernels per decode step go from 365-366 to 321 (net -44 to -46);
  - the PR runs 7.00-7.01 `_markov_*` kernels per step.
- On gfx950 the fused launches take steps of at most 5 requests (`MAX_ROWS_GFX950`). From 6 on, vLLM's loop is faster there. Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps.
- On MI355X, `main` 335dd77b09 vs this PR (c128b8ba44):
  - Workload: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off, synthetic AL 3.87, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`. Step = ITL p50.
  - Runs: 4 fresh servers per arm in ABBA order, each with 3 runs of 32 prompts. TP2 runs Engram on the host.

  | Config | `main` | PR | Delta | Spread across servers (`main` / PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | TP4 c1 | 5.372 ms | 5.245 ms | **-127 us (-2.36%)** | 0.39% / 0.44% |
  | TP4 c2 | 6.637 ms | 6.498 ms | **-139 us (-2.10%)** | 1.02% / 0.41% |
  | TP4 c4 | 8.614 ms | 8.530 ms | **-84 us (-0.98%)** | 0.91% / 0.49% |
  | TP4 c8 | 13.053 ms | 13.056 ms | +3 us (+0.02%): 8-row steps take vLLM's loop | 0.64% / 1.06% |
  | TP2 c1 | 6.434 ms | 6.288 ms | **-146 us (-2.27%)** | 0.52% / 1.01% |
- GSM8K-1319 and AL are unchanged (6 passes per arm):

  | Parallel requests | `main` GSM8K / AL | PR GSM8K / AL |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8 | 0.9189 / 3.576 | 0.9156 / 3.576 |
  | 4 | 0.9151 / 3.584 | 0.9151 / 3.581 |

  - At 8 parallel requests most steps have 8 rows, so both arms run the loop. At 4, every step takes the fused launches.
  - Numerics change only in the draft, as on gfx942: a 1-bf16-ULP bias difference can change a draft token, and rejection sampling keeps the target distribution.
- Unchanged: runs without `--monokernel`, other archs and every existing fallback (greedy drafts, AV, more than 8 requests, ...). No new flag or env var. No CI config change.
- gfx942 is unchanged by construction: there `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()` is true exactly when `enabled()` is, and the step kernel keeps 4 warps and `MAX_ROWS` = 8. Nothing was rerun on gfx942.

## Validation

All runs are at c128b8ba44 on MI355X. The current head, 9751254a4e, is rebased onto newer `main`. Its only code change since then is the gate refactor below: one check replaces the two wrappers, and it tests the same condition. The `main` arm is `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1`, built from this PR's base. The PR arm is that image plus this PR's `ops/__init__.py` and `ops/fused_markov.py`. The tests run in the image with `--noconftest`, because the image lacks `tblib`.

- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_fused_markov.py` on gfx950 at 4 warps: 6 passed. With `main`'s code: 6 failed (`assert fused_markov.sample_sequential(...)` is False, because the gate is gfx942-only).
- [x] `tests/kernels/models/amd/test_dsv41_gfx942_decode_meta.py` on gfx950 (#63885's kernel test, whose gate now shares the check): 3 passed.
- [x] `tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py`: 82 passed.
  - With `main`'s code, 80 passed and 2 failed:
    ```
    E       assert False is True
    FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py::test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov[gfx950-True-5-True]
    FAILED tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_decode.py::test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov[gfx942-True-8-True]
    ```
    The gfx942 case fails only because `main`'s gate reads `on_gfx942()`, while the test sets the arch through `get_cdna_version()`.
  - Each of these mutants fails the test (CPU runner, gfx950 shim):

    | Mutant | Failed cases |
    |---|---|
    | Gate left gfx942-only | `[gfx950-True-5-True]`, `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | No gfx950 cap | `[gfx950-True-6-False]` |
    | gfx950's cap on gfx942 too | `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | Cap keyed on CDNA3 instead of CDNA4 | `[gfx950-True-6-False]`, `[gfx942-True-8-True]` |
    | `record_monokernel` leaves the shared check cached | `[gfx950-False-1-False]` and 2 SWA gate cases |
    | Shared check ignores `--monokernel` | `[gfx950-False-1-False]` and 2 SWA gate cases |
- [x] `pre-commit run --files` on the 5 changed files passes.
- [x] TP4 c1/c2/c4/c8: 4 rounds, with `main` and PR running at once on the two GPU halves. One half ran (main, PR, PR, main) and the other (PR, main, main, PR).
  - Per round, c1 is 2.04-2.75% faster with the PR, c2 1.34-2.70% faster, and c4 0.60-1.43% faster.
  - c8 ranges from -0.86% to +0.84%.
- [x] TP2 c1: 2 rounds of 4 servers each, 4 servers per arm. The two rounds are 2.51% and 2.02% faster with the PR.
- [x] Launch count from the torch-profiler window on both GSM8K rounds (above).
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL at 8 parallel requests: 2 rounds with the GPU halves swapped, 3 passes per server.
- [x] GSM8K-1319 and AL at 4 parallel requests: same design. Every step has at most 4 rows, so the PR arm takes the fused launches throughout.

**Microbench (the basis for the 5-row cap and for 4 warps).**
- It times one decode step's Markov sampling at k=6: all 6 draft positions, which is 7 launches fused and the whole loop on `main`.
- Shapes: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's head (vocab 129280, rank 256), random bf16 weights.
- Hardware: one MI355X GPU, graph-replayed with the MALL flushed.
- Values: median of 9 rounds of 200 replays, in us per decode step.

| Rows | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM's loop (`main`) | 225 | 286 | 339 | 355 | 1127 | 275 | 283 | 289 |
| fused, 4 warps (this PR; gfx950 takes 1-5) | 120 | 178 | 228 | 281 | 337 | 394 | 447 | 500 |
| fused, 8 warps (an earlier revision) | 120 | 177 | 240 | 290 | 347 | 403 | 457 | 514 |

- `rocm_unquantized_gemm` runs the loop's Markov GEMV on wvSplitK only for `0 < n <= 5`. From 6 rows it takes the generic GEMM, and the loop is cheaper there than the fused launches, whose cost grows by about 54 us per row.
- The loop's 5-row point (1127 us, seen in one run, not profiled) is `main`'s loop, not the fused path. Even without it, the fused 5-row cost (337 us) is below the loop's 4-row cost (355 us).
- 4 warps is 2-5% faster than 8 at 3-8 rows and within 2% at 1-2 rows.
- The microbench only times the two paths. It does not compare their outputs.

- [ ] Optional: `main`+#63181 with and without this PR. Not run: #63181's head d5ed219630 predates #64356 (`DraftLogitsCache`) and passes the cache object where its kernel expects a tensor.

<details>
<summary>Design, commands and per-round results</summary>

**Server** (TP4). For accuracy, use `"rejection_sample_method":"block"` and drop the synthetic AL. TP2 runs the same command with `--tensor-parallel-size 2` and `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}'`, because GPU Engram does not fit at TP2.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter --block-size 128 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --language-model-only \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

**Bench.**
- Each server starts fresh and warms up with 4 prompts at 32k/256 and c2.
- Then 3 runs of each c in {1, 2, 4, 8} (TP2: c1 only), each with 32 prompts and seed 100+c.
- Step = ITL p50, averaged over the 3 runs.

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
```

**Design.**
- TP4: one server per GPU half (GPUs 0-3 and 4-7). Over 4 rounds, the halves ran (main, PR, PR, main) and (PR, main, main, PR).
- TP2: 4 servers at a time: (main, PR, PR, main), then (PR, main, main, PR).
- Every server's log was checked. Each PR server logs `DSpark fused Markov sampling: 6 steps, vocabulary 129280, rank 256, 505 blocks`, and no `main` server does.
- No server failed a request or hit an engine error.

| TP4 round | c1 `main` / PR | c2 `main` / PR | c4 `main` / PR | c8 `main` / PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5.381 / 5.234 (-2.75%) | 6.667 / 6.487 (-2.70%) | 8.616 / 8.557 (-0.68%) | 13.002 / 13.110 (+0.84%) |
| 2 | 5.360 / 5.251 (-2.04%) | 6.635 / 6.509 (-1.89%) | 8.573 / 8.521 (-0.60%) | 13.085 / 12.973 (-0.86%) |
| 3 | 5.377 / 5.257 (-2.24%) | 6.600 / 6.511 (-1.34%) | 8.651 / 8.527 (-1.43%) | 13.053 / 13.058 (+0.03%) |
| 4 | 5.368 / 5.239 (-2.40%) | 6.649 / 6.485 (-2.46%) | 8.618 / 8.515 (-1.20%) | 13.070 / 13.082 (+0.09%) |

**GSM8K** runs on separate block-rejection servers, because the perf servers force a synthetic AL.
- The client is an out-of-tree script over `/v1/completions`, using sglang `few_shot_gsm8k`'s prompt and scoring: 8-shot, temperature 0, at most 512 tokens.
- Each server runs one cold pass and two passes with a per-request `cache_salt`.
- Per pass at 8 parallel:
  - `main`: 0.9151 0.9158 0.9212 0.9196 0.9249 0.9166
  - PR: 0.9189 0.9090 0.9166 0.9151 0.9121 0.9219
- Per pass at 4 parallel:
  - `main`: 0.9105 0.9143 0.9166 0.9128 0.9196 0.9166
  - PR: 0.9090 0.9265 0.9067 0.9105 0.9143 0.9234
- AL = 1 + Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total` / Δ`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total` over each pass.

**Launch count.**
- It comes from the torch-profiler window on the GSM8K servers: c1 x 2 and c2 x 4 prompts at 32k/256, with the prefills prefix-cached.
- For each TP rank, it divides the rank's GPU kernels in the window by its decode steps. All 4 ranks give the same rate.

Per decode step, the PR removes:
- 6 each of argmax, gather, `_gumbel_sample_kernel` and the Markov GEMV (`wvSplitK`, two variants);
- 7 embedding and index lookups;
- about 8.5 copies and about 12 adds.

It adds 6 `_markov_step_kernel` and 1 `_markov_last_kernel`.

**Compile-only, gfx950** (step kernel at 4 warps, BLOCK 256, STEP 0 and 1, 1, 2, 4 and 8 rows; the kernel is unchanged since): 266-342 VGPRs+AGPRs, with no VGPR spills or scratch.
</details>

## Details

**Why:** #60731 was the gfx942 port, so it gated all of its helpers on `ops.enabled()`, which is gfx942-only. `fused_markov` is plain Triton on vLLM's own Gumbel helpers, with nothing gfx942-specific.

**Change:**
- `fused_markov` runs under `ops.monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`: `--monokernel` + ROCm + `get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`, the same CDNA versions as the mono layer.
  - `swa_decode_meta` (#63885) uses the same check, in place of its `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`.
  - The other helpers keep `ops.enabled()`.
- `_why_not` caps CDNA4 (gfx950) at `MAX_ROWS_GFX950` = 5 rows. A larger step takes vLLM's loop, as a step of more than `MAX_ROWS` = 8 already does on gfx942. Under FULL CUDA graphs, the choice is made at capture for each padded batch size.
- Both archs launch the step kernel at 4 warps. `BLOCK` is unchanged.
- No speculator, model-runner or CPU-GPU sync changes.
- Tests:
  - `test_dspark_draft_model_samples_with_fused_markov` now drives the real gate with stub kernels in 4 cases. With `--monokernel`, the fused launches take a 5-row step on gfx950 and an 8-row step on gfx942. vLLM's loop takes a 6-row step on gfx950, and any step without the flag.
  - The gfx942 kernel test clears the new check's cache.
  - No new test or test file.

**CI coverage:** there is no `.buildkite` change.
- The gate test runs in the existing MI355 "Basic Models (Other)" job.
- The kernel test runs only in the MI300 gfx942 kernels job.
- No CI job runs the fused launch on gfx950. It was run by hand at this head: 6 passed.

**Limitations:**
- The kernel test compares the fused launches with vLLM's loop at 1 and 2 requests and k=5 only.
- 3-5-row steps on gfx950 were timed by the microbench and ran end to end at c4 and in GSM8K. Outputs at those row counts are compared only through GSM8K and AL.
- AV on: no effect, because a step with the acceptance estimator or the confidence head falls back to the loop.
- `use_fp64_gumbel` is untested on either arch, as before this PR.

**Related PRs:**
- **#63181:** a separate fusion of the same loop: a Markov GEMV and a sample epilogue, 2 launches per draft position.
  - With both merged, this hook runs first. So #63181's path runs without `--monokernel`, on steps that `fused_markov` declines, and on gfx950 steps of 6-8 requests.
  - Its head predates `main`'s `DraftLogitsCache` and conflicts with `main`. The head-to-head waits for its rebase.
- **#63885** (merged: SWA decode metadata in one launch on gfx950) added `swa_decode_meta_enabled()`. This PR replaces it with `monokernel_cdna3_or_4()`, which both helpers use.
- **#63486** and **#61311** move or delete the test files and the MI300 CI job that runs them, and make the kernel test gfx942-only.
  - #61311 also renames `ops._monokernel` and `record_monokernel` to `_specialized_decode` and `record_specialized_decode`. The shared check and both tests use those names.
  - Whichever lands first, this PR follows: it widens that skip to gfx950 and, after #61311, renames the flag.
- **#61869:** a CUDA-only fused Markov sampler. It does not reach ROCm.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono: tuned K1 at TP4
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Overview

**This draft is stacked on #63027. Only the last commit (`3d923a6848`) is new; the first three (`96fa04ad7a`, `043dd8da90`, `37372f010c`) are #63027's, rebased onto main `4b47db922b`.**

#63027 tunes K1 and K2 for the target's compress-ratio-2 layers at TP2 only. This PR turns its tuned K1 (the attention seam and front) on for every TP4 layer on gfx950 (MI355X), the DSpark draft's included. K2 stays generic at TP4, and TP8 keeps the generic K1. We run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at low concurrency on MI355X as TP4 with `--monokernel`.

## Claims

- **Decode step (ABBA against #63027 rebased, 4 rounds):** c1 -284 us (-5.2%), c2 -326 us (-4.8%), c4 -194 us (-2.2%); every round faster, beyond t x SE and the base A/A spread.
- **Outputs unchanged, by design:** the paths are #63027's, which it shows bit-exact against the generic code at TP2. The numerics test now also compares them bit for bit at TP4: it passes on MI355X, and a mutant one bf16 ulp off in TP4 K1 fails it. GSM8K and AL match base within noise. The draft K1 has no GPU bit check (see test coverage).
- **Scope:** fixed per build, no env var: `MonoBuild.tuned_front = tuned or (not GFX942 and not generic and tp == 4)`. Mono builds only for gfx942 and gfx950, so this means gfx950. TP2, TP8, `generic=True` and gfx942 builds compile as on #63027. TP8 keeps the generic K1; #64152 extends this PR to TP8. TP4 K2 code is unchanged; only its scratch offsets move.
- **Compile level (measured):** TP4 K1 uses 148-174 VGPRs at 1-48 rows (#63027 rebased: 142-240), with no spills and unchanged LDS. TP8 builds are binary-identical to main's.

## Validation

**CPU (done, on the rebased code; the pushed head only trims comments and docstrings, and its AST is identical)**

- [x] Rebased onto main `4b47db922b`, which has #63576, #63689, #63816, #64008 and #64101 (TP8 mono). One conflict, in #63027's first commit (`stages/moe.py`, `stage_route`): the resolution keeps #63816's NaN guard and cursor mask, plus #63027's preloaded tuned bias.
- [x] `pre-commit` passes on the stack's 12 changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint).
- [x] Compile-only (FlyDSL 0.4.0, `COMPILE_ONLY=1`): 252 gfx950 configs per tree (TP2 / TP4 / TP8, including TP4 K1 and K2 at ratio 2 at every width 1-48) and 50 gfx942 configs. The table is in the details below.
- [x] Gate and layout check over 1,728 `MonoBuild` keys per arch (TP2 / TP4 / TP8): only the 288 TP4 non-generic gfx950 layouts change, by 4,608-8,960 B per width. TP2, TP8, `generic=True` and gfx942 are identical.
- [x] Launcher check after #64008's launcher reuse: 1,248 launchers on gfx950, each build gets its own, and no two different builds share a JIT key.
- Test change: at TP4 every `_check_layers` case now also runs a `generic=True` runner (the code this PR replaces) and compares the outputs bit for bit. New case: ratio 0 at 7 rows, the c1 DSpark width. #63027 has no TP4 tuned build, so this comparison is new.
- CI: `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics` (mi355_4, TP2 / TP4) and `:amd: (MI355) DeepSeek-V4.1 Mono Decode Numerics TP8` (mi355_8) run both test files on this PR's paths.
  - CI cost: the mi355_4 job's four test ids took 126 s / 133 s (numerics [2] / [4]) and 250 s / 243 s (layers [2-8] / [4-8]) on MI355X, each in a fresh container with no JIT cache mounted; the job's timeout is 40 min.

**GPU (done, 8x MI355X; base = #63027 rebased, `37372f010c`; PR = base + `3d923a6848`)**

- [x] Unit tests at TP2 / TP4 / TP8: `pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py`. This covers the new TP4 bit compare, the ratio-0 7-row case and the 300-replay stress. Controls:
  - the same tests on #63027 rebased (adapted to its runner API; the TP4 compare runs generic against generic);
  - a mutant that flips one bf16 ulp in TP4 K1's residual store. It must fail the TP4 bit compare.
  - PR: numerics TP2 / TP4 / TP8 PASS; layers [2-8] [4-8] [8-8] [8-28] PASS ([4-42] gfx942-only, skipped). Control #63027 rebased: PASS. Mutant: fails the TP4 compare at `ratio 1, 1 x 6`, as expected.
- [x] ABBA at c1 / c2 / c4 (7 / 14 / 28 target rows): 4 rounds, both arms at once on GPUs 0-3 and 4-7, halves swapped (2 rounds each way), 3 runs of 32 prompts per point and server. The PR stays a draft until then, and is dropped if the gain at c1 or c2 is within drift. A gain counts only when every round has the same sign, |mean| > t x SE (t = 3.18 at 4 rounds), and it is larger than the base A/A spread. c4 is reported, not gating.
  - Resolved at c1, c2 and c4: PR faster in 4/4 rounds, |mean| > t x SE and larger than the base A/A spread (table and noise below). The rule above is met.
- [x] GSM8K-1319 with AL (block rejection): 3 passes per server (one cold, two with a per-request `cache_salt`) at `--parallel 6`, so every decode-only step fits mono's 48 rows. 2 servers per arm, halves swapped.
  - base 0.9185 (AL 3.580), PR 0.9158 (AL 3.583), 6 passes each; PR - base -0.0027 (binomial SE of a difference of two independent passes 0.0107); per-question flips between two passes (mean [min-max]): base vs PR 70.4 [57-81] over 36 pairs, within-arm 68.2 [59-79] (base) / 72.0 [63-82] (PR) over 15 pairs each
- [x] Greedy identity probe against #63027 rebased: the first 256 GSM8K questions at `--parallel 1`, compared by token ids, 2 passes per server. A/A pairs (same server, other server) give the noise floor. Each pass also records the accepted and drafted counts, meant as the only exact check of the draft K1 (GSM8K AL sees it only within noise).
  - Two passes of one arm are token-identical on only 65-79 of 256 answers (means 26.1-29.5%, same or another server; why is not investigated), so the probe cannot show identical outputs. Base vs PR: 64-79 of 256 over 16 pairs (mean 28.2%), at the A/A level; 0 PR-consistent differences (answers that differ in every base-vs-PR pair and in no A/A pair).
  - Acceptance counts: confounded. No base-vs-PR pair is token-identical on every answer, so the counts (max |d| 947, A/A floor 716) cannot isolate the draft K1.
- [x] Profiler K1 / K2 attribution: torch-profiler GPU time per decode step of the target's and the draft's K1 and K2 at 7 and 14 rows, on the GSM8K servers (PR once on each half).
  - 7 rows: K1 -277.2 us per step (target -259.9, draft -17.3), K2 +7.5 us; K1 is 98% of the ABBA step delta. 14 rows: K1 -301.2 us (target -281.7, draft -19.5), K2 +28.7 us; K1 is 93% of it.

**Perf (ABBA, 4 rounds)**

| 4x MI355X TP4 `--monokernel`, DSpark k=6, AV off | base (#63027 rebased) | this PR | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| c1 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 5.449 | 5.164 | -284 us (-5.2%) |
| c2 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 6.720 | 6.395 | -326 us (-4.8%) |
| c4 decode step (ITL p50, ms) | 8.676 | 8.482 | -194 us (-2.2%) |

- **Image and workload:** nightly `3966924d56` with main `4b47db922b`'s mono files; base = #63027 rebased onto main (`37372f010c`, with #63576), PR = base + `3d923a6848` (the pushed PR head); random 32k in / 1024 out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87; 3 x 32 prompts per point and server (seed 100 + 10 x (rep - 1) + c, every rep cold) after a 4-prompt warm-up; 4 rounds, both arms at once on GPUs 0-3 and 4-7, halves swapped between rounds. The images predate #63885 (SWA decode metadata in one launch, now on main), which does not touch the mono files: the absolute us should carry over, the percentages may not.
- **Noise:** c1: SE of the mean delta 1 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 3 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.23% base / 0.29% PR; c2: SE of the mean delta 10 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 33 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.31% base / 0.58% PR; c4: SE of the mean delta 12 us (x t 3.18, df 3 = 38 us), A/A (server-mean) spread 0.73% base / 0.50% PR. Delta = mean over rounds of (PR - base) in the same round.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K per pass, compile-level table, test coverage, reproduction commands</summary>

GSM8K-1319 per pass (8-shot, greedy, `--parallel 6`, real acceptance; one cold pass, then cache-salted ones; at `--parallel 6` every decode-only step fits mono's 48 rows):
- PR: 0.920 / 0.917 / 0.914 / 0.911 / 0.917 / 0.916, AL 3.579 / 3.587 / 3.582 / 3.587 / 3.585 / 3.580
- base: 0.913 / 0.928 / 0.917 / 0.919 / 0.917 / 0.917, AL 3.588 / 3.569 / 3.570 / 3.572 / 3.590 / 3.589 (standard error about 0.0076 per pass)

Compile-only, FlyDSL 0.4.0, gfx950 unless noted:

| | #63027 rebased | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 K1, ratio 2, 1-48 rows | 142-240 VGPR | 148-174 VGPR, no spill, LDS equal at 48/48 widths; fewer instructions at every width but 2 rows (+6) |
| TP4 K1, 7 / 14 / 48 rows | 152 / 152 / 240 VGPR | 170 / 172 / 174 VGPR |
| TP4 K1, other builds at 7-48 rows (ratio 0/1, index source, fold off, draft) | 152-240 VGPR | 170-174 VGPR, no spill, LDS unchanged |
| TP4 K2, 66 builds (1-48 rows, every ratio, index source, fold off, draft) | | same instruction stream once constants are masked; only 26-27 scratch-offset constants move, by 4,608-8,960 B; VGPR and LDS equal |
| TP8, 47 builds | | binary-identical (and 161/161 TP8 builds binary-identical to main) |
| `generic=True` (50), gfx942 (47), TP4 FFN launch (4) | | binary-identical |
| TP2, 19 builds | | 18 binary-identical. K1 at 48 rows differs by 3 instructions with identical IR; the same flip appears between two builds of one tree (compiler nondeterminism) |

gfx942 K2 at 48 rows fails to build on both trees: gfx942 takes at most 42 rows.

**Test coverage**
- Bit-compared at TP4 on gfx950 (the test is CDNA4-only): the target K1, fold on, at ratio 1 (6 rows), ratio 0 (7) and ratio 2 (12, 36, 48).
- Index-source and fold-off K1 are checked only against the model with a tolerance, in `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (TP4 at 8 rows on gfx950; its 42-row case runs on gfx942 only).
- The draft K1 has no unit test, and the acceptance-count check was confounded, so no GPU test checks it exactly; GSM8K AL sees it only within noise (3.580 vs 3.583). Its bit-exactness rests on sharing the target K1's tuned code paths.
- The decode step is timed at 7, 14 and 28 rows (c1 / c2 / c4) only. Steps of 29-48 rows (c5 / c6 at k=6: 35 / 42 rows) are not timed; they have the compile stats above and, at ratio 2, the 36- and 48-row bit compares.
- gfx942 builds are compile-checked only. `timeline=True` (profiling) builds were not compile-checked.

```bash
# Server on 4x MI355X, one per GPU half. For accuracy, use "rejection_sample_method":"block" and drop synthetic_acceptance_length.
# Attribution servers also take --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<dir>","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}'.
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --monokernel --moe-backend aiter \
  --block-size 128 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":6,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.87,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'

# Perf: fresh server, warm-up (c2, 4 prompts, 32k in / 256 out, seed 7), then 3 runs per point.
# Run r at concurrency c uses --seed 100 + 10 x (r - 1) + c, so every run's prompts are new. Step = ITL p50.
vllm bench serve --backend openai --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 32768 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 32 --seed 101 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99
# c2 / c4: --max-concurrency 2 / 4.

# GSM8K: sglang few_shot_gsm8k prompt and scoring, 1319 questions, 8-shot, temperature 0, max 512 new tokens,
# over /v1/completions, 6 in parallel. One cold pass, then two with a unique "cache_salt" per request.
# Identity probe: the first 256 questions, 1 in parallel, one fixed salt per pass, "return_token_ids".
# AL = 1 + delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total) / delta(vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total), read from /metrics.

# Unit tests on 8x MI355X (the TP8 cases need all 8)
pytest -v -s tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py
```
</details>

## Details

**Design**
- #63027's tuned K1 paths (flag copies, norms and gates off the wqkv CTAs, fused fold and slice, wide normed stores, batched norm polls) read no routing dims. At TP4 they apply to every ratio, to fold off, to index sources and to the draft.
- K2 keeps `tuned` (TP2 ratio 2 only). A TP4 tuned K2 hung during FULL capture in an earlier experiment, and that code is gone from #63027's head.

**Scratch**
- K1 and K2 of a width share `_layout(key)`; its K1 regions now follow `tuned_front`.
- The runner keys a scratch by (width, tuned, front), so a front-tuned layout never aliases the FFN launch's generic one.
- The cost is at most 8,960 B per width (48 rows: 11,153,024 -> 11,161,984 B; 14 rows: +5,632 B).
- `build_key()` replaces `tuned()` and the duplicate `MonoBuild` construction in `kernels()`.

**Earlier estimate:** -273 us at c1 and -298 us at c2 (an earlier #63027 K1 revision, one unswapped run per arm); the ABBA above measured -284 us and -326 us.

**Related PRs**
- **#63027** (open, head `d104a70f8d`, conflicts with main): the first three commits here are its commits rebased onto main. When it is rebased, this PR follows. This PR makes two statements in its description stale: "TP4 is not tuned" (TP4 K1 now is), and "every other build ... compiles to the same MLIR as on main" (TP4 K1 is new code; TP4 K2 keeps its instruction stream, but its scratch offsets move). I am happy for this commit to be folded into #63027.
- **#64152** (draft) is stacked on this PR. It changes the gate to `tp in (4, 8)`, so TP8 takes the tuned K1 too.
- **#63892** (sibling, K2 side: batch TP4 K2's X8 copies, load its push's peer bases late) applies cleanly to main, but still conflicts with this stack: 6 hunks in 3 files (the numerics test 1, `layer.py` 1, `stages/moe.py` 4). It gives the same 6 hunks on #63027 rebased alone, so the conflict comes from #63027's commits, not this one. Whichever lands second resolves them.
- **#63486** (draft): it moves this test and reads scratch through `runner.scratch(M)`, which #63027's TP2 ratio-2 steps already break. After this PR the same reads need `build_key(M, ratio)`'s `(tuned, tuned_front)` at TP4 too. Whichever lands second adapts.
- **#61934:** it hoisted K2's FFN-seam loads and was closed with "No e2e gain observed". That is why the ABBA gates this PR.
- No other open PR turns on the tuned K1 at TP4: #63027 is TP2-only, #64152 builds on this PR, and #63892 and #64153 change K2 (TP4 and TP8).

title: [ROCm][Perf] Fuse MXFP8 activation quant into the 1x32 dot_scaled linear for M <= 16
author: RuibinCheung
body:
## Overview

On gfx950, `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` (1x32-scale MXFP8 dense layers: MiniMax-M3/M3.1, ModelOpt/INC MXFP8) runs a separate `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` launch before every `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. For bf16 activations with 1-16 rows, this PR quantizes the activation inside the GEMM instead, so each such linear is one launch and the output is bit-identical. Fused: K <= 1024 for M <= 16, and K = 2048 for M <= 4.

The fused GEMM quantizes only `min(16, next_pow2(M))` activation rows per K step and repeats them to fill the 16-row MFMA tile; that keeps the per-N-tile quant cost proportional to the real rows and is what makes K = 2048 profitable.

## Claims

- Per-call speedup on MI355X: 1.14x-1.64x for K <= 1024 at M = 1-16, and 1.03x-1.27x for K = 2048 at M = 1-4 (1.15x-1.27x for MiniMax-M3.1 o_proj at TP4, 6144 x 2048). Every other shape and M keeps the existing path (1.00x).
- Output is bitwise equal to the existing path (separate quant + `_select_cfg` tile), including where the fused tile has a different `BLOCK_K`/`BLOCK_N`.
- MiniMax-M3.1-Flash TP4 (on #63232), AgentX concurrency 1: o_proj and shared-expert down_proj run fused with no separate quant launch. Over baseline, in two runs with the arm order swapped: P90 TPOT 1.011x in both, P90 interactivity 1.011-1.012x.
- No change under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, for fp16 activations, for M > 16, for K = 2048 at M > 4, or for K > 2048.

## Validation

**Microbenchmark**: "separate" is `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` + GEMM (current behaviour); "fused" is this PR. Speedup over separate, MI355X:

| shape (N x K) | M=1 | M=2 | M=3 | M=4 | M=5 | M=8 | M=16 | M=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6144 x 384 (M3.1 shared down, TP8) | 1.64x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 1.47x | 1.45x | 1.01x* |
| 8192 x 512 | 1.48x | 1.49x | 1.49x | 1.51x | 1.44x | 1.46x | 1.45x | 0.99x* |
| 6144 x 768 (M3.1 shared down, TP4) | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.29x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.26x | 1.00x* |
| 6144 x 1024 (M3.1 o_proj, TP8) | 1.52x | 1.48x | 1.39x | 1.41x | 1.34x | 1.36x | 1.30x | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 1024 | 1.47x | 1.37x | 1.29x | 1.30x | 1.22x | 1.25x | 1.14x | 1.01x* |
| 6144 x 2048 (M3.1 o_proj, TP4) | 1.27x | 1.20x | 1.16x | 1.15x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 4096 x 2048 | 1.17x | 1.11x | 1.05x | 1.03x | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 2560 x 6144 (M3.1 qkv, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |
| 1536 x 6144 (M3.1 shared gate_up, TP4) | 0.99x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* | 1.00x* |

\* not fused at this shape; the column times the fallback, i.e. the noise floor.

**End to end**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X, mono decode off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY CUDA graphs, on #63232 (`8d0f05a0c`, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash`) with this PR applied on top; baseline is the same image unchanged. AgentX trace replay (InferenceX), concurrency 1, 600 s per run, `max-num-seqs` 2; run 1 in the order baseline, this PR, run 2 reversed. This PR / baseline (> 1 is better; TPOT as baseline / this PR; P90 interactivity is InferenceX's `intvty.p90` = 1 / P90 TPOT):

| Run | P90 TPOT | P90 interactivity | Total throughput / GPU |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1.011x | 1.012x | 1.004x |
| 2 | 1.011x | 1.011x | 1.020x |

GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, full test set, greedy), measured with K <= 1024 fused: baseline 96.51 / this PR 96.21 strict-match (stderr 0.51 / 0.53), within one stderr; vLLM is not batch invariant when requests are batched together, so greedy outputs vary between runs even with bit-identical kernels. The fused output is bitwise equal to the existing path for every tested shape, including K = 2048.

## Details

- **Row trimming.** `BLOCK_M` = 16 is the smallest MFMA tile, but at M < 16 only the first M rows are stored. The kernel takes a constexpr `QUANT_ROWS = min(16, next_pow2(M))`, loads and quantizes that many rows, and repeats them with `broadcast_to` + `reshape`. At `BLOCK_K` = 128 the repeat costs more than the saved quant, so those tiles (K = 384, 640, ...) keep quantizing 16 rows. The unfused path passes `QUANT_ROWS = BLOCK_M` and generates the same code as before.
- **Why only M <= 16, and K = 2048 only up to M = 4.** The fused GEMM requantizes the activation once per N-tile. At small M the separate launch (plus the round trip of the fp8 activation and its scales) dominates; with more rows or larger K the redundant quant work wins (table above). The gate does not look at N; cutting K = 2048 at M = 4 keeps every measured N at or above 1.03x.
- **`K` becomes a `tl.constexpr`.** Without it the fused loop is not unrolled/pipelined and the fused GEMM is ~0.8x even at K = 512. #63232 makes the same change.
- **Compiles.** Triton already specializes M on `== 1` and `% 16 == 0`; `QUANT_ROWS` adds up to three more variants per fused shape (6 instead of 3 for M = 1-16 at `BLOCK_K` >= 256; 5 at K = 2048, where M = 5-16 stays unfused). For MiniMax-M3.1 at TP4 that is 17 instead of 12 `_mxfp8_linear_kernel` compiles over M = 1-16 (15 instead of 12 at TP8). They are compiled in the eager warm-up before CUDA graph capture; vLLM's capture sizes include every M from 1 to 16, so decode never compiles at runtime, and graph capture time was unchanged in the end-to-end runs.
- **bf16 only.** The in-kernel fp8 cast makes the compiler enable the FP16 overflow clamp in the MODE register for the whole kernel, so an fp16 output that overflows saturates at +-65504 where the unfused GEMM produces inf. bf16 output is unaffected and bit-identical; fp16 activations keep the separate quant.
- **Batch invariance.** Fused and unfused use different tiles (and therefore K-reduction orders), so under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` (#52231) every M stays on the unfused path.
- **Limitations.** Only gfx950 (`dot_scaled` path). Shapes are tuned on MI355X.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Extend the latency_specialized decode on NVIDIA
author: yaoyaoding
body:
## Overview This PR makes the `latency_specialized` decode from #61868 faster for DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA GPUs. Most of the work is in the decode step's kernels: larger batches now stay on the low-latency paths, more of each step overlaps, and the indexers split their work across the TP ranks. "What changed" below goes through each part. On one GB300 tray with DSpark, the decode step takes 5.9–17.0% less time than on `main` at batch 1 to 32, and AgentX P90 interactivity is 4–26% higher at concurrency 1 to 32, with slightly higher throughput. ![Decode step and AgentX, main against this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/93d0aafb7e0d32b440d597fa680476b5de27d5f9/pr3_perf.png) Left: three ABBA sets at `0cdfc566`, 12 measurements per arm and batch. Right: AgentX at `0cdfc566`, both arms of each concurrency on one tray. ## Validation This branch includes #63914 (merged into this branch), which keeps the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on `main`'s FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1; this PR's two further paths on FlashInfer internals follow the same rule. The runs below are from before this branch merged `main`: `main` at `76518259` on that commit's wheel with FlashInfer 0.7.2, against this PR at `0cdfc566`, except compute-sanitizer, which ran at `5ab5ef9e`, the commit before it (`0cdfc566` adds only a start-up requirement, no runtime weight updates, a test option, a comment and documentation). After the merge, on `main`'s wheel at `ed1a7307` with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, four GB300: these GPU tests pass at `b7bb822b` (`test_kernels.py`, `test_all_gather.py`, `test_decode_topk.py`, `test_sparse_mla_cute.py`, `test_numerics.py`, `test_layers.py`, `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`; all but `test_kernels.py` ran at `d7fcb755`, which differs only in that file), and a TP4 server with `decode_backend: latency_specialized` starts with the specialized decode on and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat request correctly. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1's MoE finalize adds the top-k products in a different order at small batches, so `b7bb822b` lets one test's finalize comparison allow FP32's reordering error. ### Correctness | Task | `main` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K, strict match (1,319, c8, real verification) | 0.9742 | 0.9735 | | GPQA-Diamond (198 × 16, c32) | 0.789 | 0.791 | | AIME25 (30 × 16, c32) | 0.983 | 0.985 | | RULER NIAH (`single_2`, `multikey_2`, `multikey_3`; 32K, 128K, 256K; 40 samples each), concurrency 8 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | RULER NIAH, same, concurrency 32 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | GSM8K with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | | 0.9719, no GPU↔CPU sync reported | | GSM8K with `decode_backend` unset (stock decode) | | 0.9704 | | All-gather stress: CUDA graphs of three back-to-back gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed 2,000,000 times in a seeded random order on four GPUs; every word encodes its rank, gather and replay, checked on the GPU (`test_all_gather.py` as a module; `--custom-all-gather` replays the same graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather) | custom all-gather: 392 stale words | 0 bad words (6,000,000 gathers) |
Tests ```bash # One SM100-family GPU: the new kernels against FlashInfer, cuBLAS or torch references .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_decode_topk.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_sparse_mla_cute.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v # Four GPUs: the all-gather, AllReduceMHC's LL and two-shot protocols, TP4 numerics .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_all_gather.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v # The all-gather stress run (four GPUs), then the same replays on vLLM's custom all-gather .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 --custom-all-gather # Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v ``` | Check | What it covers | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Kernel tests | Routed experts against FlashInfer up to 192 rows, eagerly, in graphs and over 500 replays with alternating inputs (bitwise); the front against the stock chain; pinned and wide low-latency MXFP8 GEMMs; the replicated embedding lookup; the metadata graph against eager builds, with slow clamping builders | 299 passed (with `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`), 1 skipped | | Decode top-k (CuTe DSL) | An exact top-k of the BF16 logits against `torch.topk`, k 512 and 2048, 1–64 rows: sampled and direct paths, crowded, constant and rising values, NaN and infinities, a sample that misses the top values, the wide 16-CTA rows, CUDA graphs; block mode against the stock `select_candidate_blocks` | 77 passed | | Sparse MLA (CuTe DSL) | Against an FP32 reference: widths of 1–5 chunks (128 to 640 columns), masked columns, a token with no active column, as many tokens as the GPU holds clusters for, with and without sinks, CUDA graph replay | 33 passed | | All-gather | Against NCCL, bitwise: int32, BF16 and FP32 inputs of 1 pack to the full 4 MiB, growing and shrinking from call to call, one rank late each call; the sentinel word; CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed in a random order with new contents each replay, 4 GPUs | Passed; the stress run: 0 bad words in 6,000,000 gathers | | `AllReduceMHC` | Shrinking and growing batches in one mailbox with LL only, two-shot only (to 200 rows) and both in turn; the two protocols give the same bits, 4 GPUs | 61 passed (the whole file) | | Numerics, layers (4 GB300) | TP4 collectives through the new paths, including the logits and the row-sharded indexer at 1, 2, 5, 8 and 32 requests through the new all-gather; with the switch on the executor runs, embeds from the replicated table and replays its graphs | Both passed | | compute-sanitizer | memcheck and synccheck over the new kernels' single-GPU tests | memcheck and synccheck: 0 errors each (199 tests: 110 in the two new test files, 89 selected from `test_kernels.py`; at `5ab5ef9e`) | | pre-commit | All hooks | Passes | **CI.** The new test files (the all-gather's among them), the `AllReduceMHC` tests (`test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc`) and `test_engram.py` join the nightly 4×B200 DeepSeek-V4.1 step. Three tests need hardware that step does not have, and skip there: `test_pinned_mxfp8_mm` and `test_wide_low_latency_mxfp8_mm` (the tactics are pinned for GB300, SM103) and the layers test (four GB300).
### Performance All runs: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4), DSpark (5 draft tokens), Model Runner V2, FULL CUDA graphs for decode. The decode step and AgentX use DSpark's synthetic acceptance (length 3.51, as InferenceX runs AgentX); the accuracy runs above verify for real.
Server command and clients Both arms ran the same command, on `main`'s wheel with either `main`'s or this PR's source: ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}' \ --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092]}' \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 4092 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` - Decode step and AgentX: the speculative config adds `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51`. - GSM8K: InferenceX's lm-eval GSM8K (5-shot, temperature 0, all 1,319 questions), 8 requests in flight, one run per cell. - GPQA-Diamond and AIME25: zero-shot through lm-eval, reasoning effort high, temperature 0.6, 16 samples of every question, 32 requests in flight, as for #61868. GPQA-Diamond is InferenceX's task (the last standalone A–D letter, 16,384 output tokens); AIME25 is lm-eval's with DeepSeek-R1's math prompt (65,536 output tokens). - RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER generator and scorer for `niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K tokens, 40 seeded samples per task and length (upstream lm-eval draws 500), 128 output tokens, thinking off, one run per cell. - AgentX: InferenceX's AgentX scenario (AIPerf, the 393-trace corpus), closed loop at a fixed concurrency for 3,600 s. - Decode step: one server per block. A block runs batch 1 (a 524K-token context), batch 8 and batch 32 (84K–648K tokens a request) twice each. The requests are prefilled one at a time, then sent together for 3,000 tokens each, so they decode from the prefix cache. The step is the client-side window in which every request decodes, divided by its chunk count.
**AgentX.** The InferenceX AgentX trace corpus (393 traces), 3,600 s per concurrency, closed loop, DSpark at the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 as InferenceX runs it, at `0cdfc566`. Both arms of a concurrency ran on the same tray, one after the other (the first arm alternates with the concurrency). Each cell reads `main` → this PR. | Concurrency | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Change | Total tok/s/GPU | Change | TPOT p50 (ms) | TTFT p50 (s) | E2E p50 (s) | Requests | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 817.7 → 852.0 | +4.2% | 7,856 → 8,016 | +2.0% | 1.110 → 1.050 | 0.984 → 0.783 | 2.10 → 1.52 | 341 → 395 | | 4 | 666.3 → 808.7 | +21.4% | 10,336 → 10,477 | +1.4% | 1.110 → 1.040 | 0.434 → 0.431 | 1.13 → 1.09 | 764 → 769 | | 8 | 539.6 → 678.7 | +25.8% | 16,813 → 17,198 | +2.3% | 1.280 → 1.110 | 0.414 → 0.434 | 1.26 → 1.16 | 1,443 → 1,456 | | 16 | 431.1 → 536.2 | +24.4% | 29,316 → 29,922 | +2.1% | 1.520 → 1.230 | 0.496 → 0.448 | 1.30 → 1.11 | 2,715 → 2,748 | | 32 | 225.0 → 258.2 | +14.8% | 61,858 → 63,312 | +2.3% | 2.210 → 1.640 | 0.829 → 0.671 | 2.30 → 1.80 | 4,869 → 4,966 | Some trace turns ask for one output token. When that token ends the reasoning, the response has no content, and the client records the request as an error: 0–1 such requests a run for `main` and 0–1 for this PR.
TTFT: API server and engine AgentX TTFT is mostly the API server's single-threaded work before the engine sees the request: chat-template rendering and tokenization of the whole conversation. aiperf's per-request `request_ack_ns` separates that work from the engine's (acknowledgement to first token). This PR changes only worker-side code, and the engine part stays within 18 ms of `main` at every concurrency; the TTFT differences in the table are in the API server: | Concurrency | API server p50 (s) | Engine p50 (s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 0.693 → 0.479 | 0.267 → 0.249 | | 4 | 0.215 → 0.219 | 0.177 → 0.167 | | 8 | 0.237 → 0.244 | 0.150 → 0.153 | | 16 | 0.284 → 0.239 | 0.158 → 0.162 | | 32 | 0.503 → 0.354 | 0.214 → 0.213 |
**Decode top-k.** `decode_topk` against vLLM's opt-in DeepSelect and the stock path (FP32 upcast + `cooperative_topk`), k = 512, µs per call: Random BF16 logits; "valid" is the share of each row's columns before its end. One GB300, a CUDA graph of 20 back-to-back calls, median of 20 replays. Each cell: `decode_topk` / DeepSelect / stock. With row sharding, a rank selects 12 rows at batch 8 and 48 rows at batch 32 (6 rows a request, over 4 ranks). - Up to 12 rows, `decode_topk` is faster than DeepSelect at every shape but two: 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–7.7 against 4.2–4.3 µs), and 1,048,576 columns with 1/8 valid at 12 rows (17.1 against 16.5). - From 24 rows, DeepSelect is faster when 1/8 of the columns are valid (65,536 columns at 48 rows: 17.1 against 4.3 µs) and at 65,536 columns from 48 rows and 524,288 all-valid columns from 48 rows (44.2–44.1 against 46.1–44.7 µs). `decode_topk` stays faster with all 262,144 columns valid (11.8–22.5 against 26.1–26.2 µs). - Above 12 rows, `decode_topk` does not take 1,048,576-column rows, so they use the stock path (81.7–289.3 µs against DeepSelect's 16.6–76.6). - In block mode `decode_topk` is faster at every size (5.9–12.7 against 9.3–80.0 µs). - Against the stock path `decode_topk` is faster at every shape it takes, except 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–17.4 against 6.7–12.9 µs; equal at 24 rows).
