**Memory and start-up.** The replicated embedding table takes 1.32 GB per GPU and the all-gather's mailbox 48 MiB, which the KV cache gives up (106,281,697 → 105,286,588 KV-cache tokens on the tray, −0.9%). Engine start: the engine's init (profile, KV cache, warm-up) took 98.8–103.0 s (`main`) and 98.8–108.9 s (this PR) with warm compile caches, three starts each; a tray's first start, with cold caches, took 680–748 s in either arm. ## Details **Duplicate-work check.** No open PR extends the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode. Related open PRs: - #62633 adds a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer. This PR's sparse-MLA kernel replaces the TRTLLM-gen decode of the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend, which the specialized decode requires. - #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits, and #57109 adds FlashInfer's sampled `gvr_2` as an opt-in indexer top-k. `decode_topk` serves only this model's decode indexers. It also selects the candidate source's blocks, and it covers the 1M-wide rows on 16 CTAs. The comparison with DeepSelect is above. - #62635 fuses the finalize with the shared-expert add where the fused all-reduce + mHC does not take it. This PR's MoE finalize stays deferred into that fused kernel.
What changed, and what each part saved when it was added Each row was measured against the tree before it, mostly as decode-step ABBA blocks on one tray (batch B = B requests × 6 rows). They were measured one at a time, on a moving base that also held DSpark-draft changes not in this PR, so they do not add up exactly. | Change | Why | Measured when added | | --- | --- | --- | | Pinned CuTe DSL MXFP8 tactics for the attention projections above 8 rows | The autotuner sometimes picked an unclustered `wo_b` tactic (15.3 against 5.9 µs at 48 rows), about 310 µs a step at batch 8, depending on the server start | Batch 8 −7.3% | | The next layer's mHC coefficients on the side stream at every executor step (was up to 48 rows) | They ran inline above 48 rows | Batch 32 −3.9% | | Low-batch routed experts up to 64, then 192 rows: a fused front, a routing-record prefix, the router's padding mask | Above 8 rows the stock FlashInfer chain ran (routing, sort, GEMMs, finalize) | Batch 2 −8.6%, batch 4 −7.0%; 12 cold layers at 80–128 rows 10–13% under FlashInfer | | Low-latency MXFP8 projections up to 48 rows | FlashInfer's block-scaled GEMMs, 13.5 µs for the three projections at 12 rows against 4.3 µs of HBM time | Attention sublayer at batch 2 50.4 → 48.5 µs | | Dense indexers row-sharded from two requests; Engram WKV run ahead; candidate expansion overlapped | Every rank scored every row of the indexers | Batch 2–21 −0.6% to −4.7% (all separated) | | Two-shot all-reduce + mHC from 64 rows, adapted from FlashInfer's MNNVL two-shot all-reduce | Each rank read four contributions per value; the owner now sums them once | Batch 21 −1.0%, batch 28 −0.9%; 192 rows 15.7 → 12.1 µs per call | | The dense indexer planned before the index-key wait | 6.6–7.2 µs of reset, schedule and cast waited for the keys without reading them | About −25 µs a step at batch 2, −50 at batch 8 (profile) | | Embedding from a replicated table into the hyper-connection streams | Sharded lookup + all-reduce + copy | Not measured on its own: it was added in a set of four changes, which together gave batch 4 −1.6% and batch 21 −1.4%. From the work it removes, about −13 µs a step is expected at batch 2 and −23 at batch 32 | | Indexer metadata builds on branches of their own | 13 nodes ran in series on one block-table branch | Draft end → next target −7 to −10 µs | | Decode top-k from BF16 logits (CuTe DSL) | `cooperative_topk` plus the FP32 upcast took 182 µs a step on the slowest rank at batch 8 | Batch 2 −1.5%, batch 8 −1.5% (two trays) | | Sparse MLA up to 8 requests (CuTe DSL): a cluster per token, one CTA per 128 columns, merged over distributed shared memory | TRTLLM-gen's kernel at these shapes | Batch 2 −5.3%, batch 4 −2.7%, batch 8 −4.9% | | GEMM2 starts per token tile | GEMM2 waited for GEMM1's whole grid | MoE pair at batch 2 39.2 → 35.4 µs a layer; batch 2 −1.6%, batch 8 −1.3% | | The front's top-k over eight CTAs; its stores after the cluster release | The top-k was issue-bound on one SM (0.18 µs a row) | Batch 2 −1.1%, batch 4 −1.6% (five sets, three trays) | | Layer 20's top-k on 16 CTAs a row | Its 1M-wide rows fell back to the upcast and the stock top-k | Layer 20 at batch 2 38.5 → 24.7 µs a step; batch 2 −1.1% | | The executor's own all-gather for the indexer rows and the logits (CuTe DSL) | `main` gathers them with the custom all-gather, whose Lamport kernel never waits for the rank's own multicast copy, so a late copy can corrupt a later gather of another size (`test_all_gather.py --custom-all-gather` reproduces it) | Not measured on its own | | The decode Q/KV norm and the fused `wo_a` trigger their dependents early (≤ 48 rows) | `wq_b` and `wo_b` load their weights before their own wait, but were launched late | Attention per layer at batch 2 34.9 → 33.4 µs, about −60 µs a step |

title: [Perf][DSA] Token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill under TP; remove indexer row sharding
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Shard DSA sparse-MLA prefill across TP ranks by token instead of by head ("ShardQ", Ulysses style) and remove the indexer TP row sharding from #54951, which it supersedes, including in GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer. Enabled by default for steps with >= 1024 tokens after the decodes (`sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens`), including mixed prefill + decode steps (whose decode tokens stay head-sharded); at 4K the gain is small and within end-to-end noise. Validated on GLM-5.3; GLM-5.3-Flash is covered by a forward-time microbenchmark and a greedy retrieval A/B.

## Claims

- GLM-5.3 (NVFP4, TP4, GB200, default FlashInfer sparse MLA backend) TTFT at concurrency 1: **1.24x at 32K, 1.29x at 64K, 1.40x at 128K** prompts.
- Per-step prefill forward is **1.11x-1.70x faster** than main, growing with context length (16K-token chunk at 128K context: 926 ms -> 544 ms), and **1.18x-1.25x faster than the removed row sharding** even with row sharding forced on. With default settings row sharding never engages: it needs >= 65536 prefill rows in one step, above the default `max_num_batched_tokens`.
- At 64K-token chunks, where main's row sharding engages by default, per-step forward is **1.14x-1.26x faster than row sharding** (B300; 64K chunk at 1M context: 11.17 s -> 9.83 s).
- GLM-5.3-Flash (k-pool indexer, now ShardQ-enabled): per-step forward at 64K-token chunks is **1.08x-1.13x faster than row sharding**, which this PR replaces there too.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps (one prefill chunk plus 32 decodes, GLM-5.3, B300): per-step forward is **1.16x-2.90x faster than main** on FlashInfer and **2.04x-2.97x** on FlashMLA sparse with `fp8_ds_mla`. Before mixed-step support, this PR was up to 2.4x slower than main's row sharding on such steps at a 64K budget.
- B300 serving A/B with the #54951 protocol (GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4, concurrency 1, 256 output tokens, four fresh-process pairs): server TTFT **1.19x at 8K, 1.29x at 32K, 1.46x at 128K, 1.99x at 512K and 2.62x at 1M** (162.5 s -> 62.0 s); 1K-4K prompts (below the threshold) unchanged; generated tokens identical to main in 132/132 matched retrieval probes.
- No accuracy change on gsm8k (5-shot and ~10K-token 45-shot prompts) or long-context passkey retrieval.

- Server: `vllm serve` defaults (FlashInfer sparse MLA backend, FP8 KV cache, default CUDA graphs) plus `--max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-per-request-metrics`.
- Protocol, the same as #54951:
  - Runs: eight fresh server processes in ABBA/BAAB order (main, PR, PR, main, PR, main, main, PR), forming four adjacent restart pairs. Each process runs 3 excluded warmups and 8 measured requests per length.
  - Prompts: exact-token prompts from #54951's generator, the same in both arms. 1M means 1,000,000 input tokens.
  - Sampling: temperature 0, 256 output tokens with `ignore_eos`.
  - Server timings: TTFT runs from scheduling to the first token, and TPOT is the server's mean inter-token latency.
  - Aggregation: the per-process median, then the geometric mean over the four processes of each arm. 95% intervals resample the four restart pairs (20,000 bootstrap draws).
  - Measured requests: 352 main and 352 PR, every one with exactly 256 output tokens.
  - Only difference from #54951's client: the GLM-5.3 non-thinking boundary `<|assistant|><think></think>` in place of GLM-5.3-Flash's.
- **Batch budget:** #54951 used `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536`. On B300 with the default FlashInfer sparse MLA backend, main fails on 65,536-token prefill steps:
  - Every request of 64K or more logs `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` at `flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:478`, about 312 times per request.
  - Those requests return garbage, with 0/15 retrieval correct from 64K to 1M.

  This run therefore uses GLM-5.3's default budget of 16,384. At that budget, main's indexer row sharding, which this PR removes, never engages, so the baseline is main's default path. Both arms logged zero CUDA errors while serving.

    - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: 92 passed, 3 failed (the same 3 fail on the merge base)
    - `tests/distributed/test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py` (4 GPUs): 24 passed, 3 failed (the same 3 fail on the merge base)
    - `test_indexer_dcp_localize.py`: 114 passed
    - `test_mla_context_chunks.py`: 14 passed
    - `test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py`: 42 passed
    - `test_mla_backends.py -k 'dcp or pcp'`: 15 passed
  - `pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py`: 29 passed, 11 skipped
  - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py`: 121 passed
  - `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py`: 21 passed
  - `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: 511 passed, 1384 skipped

## Details

**How it works.** Under TP every rank holds `H / tp` heads, so each rank runs the indexer over all prefill tokens, and the sparse attention kernel processes all tokens for its few heads. ShardQ instead gives each rank a slice of the step's tokens:

1. Tokens split zigzag: each request cuts into `2 * tp` chunks, and rank `r` owns chunks `r` and `2 * tp - 1 - r`, which balances the causal indexer cost.
2. The indexer scores only this rank's tokens and writes their top-k compactly, after the decode tokens' top-k, to the shared top-k buffer.
3. An all-to-all moves the MQA query from `[T, H / tp, D]` to `[T / tp, H, D]`; the sparse attention kernel attends all heads over the replicated KV cache.
4. A second all-to-all restores `[T, H / tp, 512]` for the `W_UV` projection.

The exchanges sit around the regular `forward_mqa` call, next to DCP's `query_gather` and combine; there is no ShardQ-specific attention entry point. They push tokens directly into peers' symmetric-memory buffers with one Triton kernel, falling back to NCCL `all_to_all_single` when the TP group has no symmetric memory. The fp8 query of the FlashInfer backend is exchanged as is.

**Where it applies.**
- Steps with at least `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` tokens after the decodes, one of whose requests is longer than the top-k; shorter prefills already take dense MHA.
- Mixed prefill + decode steps:
  - Only the tokens after the decodes are split. Decodes here are requests of at most `1 + num_speculative_tokens` tokens, and stay head-sharded.
  - The indexer scores every decode token in place, then this rank's tokens compactly after them, so tokens that the indexer treats as prefill but MLA treats as decode stay consistent.
  - The attention layer calls `forward_mqa` twice: once for the decode tokens with the step's metadata, once for this rank's tokens with ShardQ's narrowed metadata (`ShardQMetadata.attn_metadata`, which reads the top-k from `topk_start`). FlashMLA's token-sharded call uses its own lazily initialized scheduler metadata.
  - The decode output is written in place before the restored tokens rather than concatenated.
- The indexer metadata builder chunks only the decode tokens and this rank's tokens (`shardq_gather_indices`), each at its own position, so it makes fewer, fuller launches.
- TP > 1, no DCP/PCP/HiSparse, and no FULL CUDA graphs for mixed batches.
- Backends opt in with `SparseMLACommonImpl.supports_shardq`: FlashInfer sparse MLA and FlashMLA sparse (fp8 mixed-batch path).
- Models mark eligible layers with `MLAAttention(shardq_eligible=...)`: DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash (NVIDIA k-pool indexer) do. Other sparse MLA models keep the head-sharded path.
- The sparse MLA and indexer metadata builders both call `build_shardq_split` and, like every TP rank, derive the same split from the same batch.
- MTP layers are not eligible, including GLM-5.3-Flash's: draft steps reuse each token slot's top-k.

**Config.** New `AttentionConfig` fields `sparse_mla_shard_q` (default `True`) and `sparse_mla_shard_q_min_tokens` (default 1024). `indexer_tp_shard_min_rows` is deprecated, has no effect, and is removed in v0.34.0.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- Memory: the exchange buffers (above) come out of the KV cache budget.
- GLM-5.3-Flash's k-pool indexer, which #54951 row-sharded, now follows the ShardQ split instead. Its MTP layers no longer shard the indexer.

**Not duplicating existing work.** No open PR implements token-sharded sparse-MLA prefill. #54394 and #56944 shard only the indexer rows (like the removed `PrefillRowShard`) and keep attention head-sharded.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this change.

title: [ROCm][Model] Enable ROCm AITER unified attention for MiMo-V2.6
author: vllmellm
body:
## Overview

MiMo-V2.6 has asymmetric K/V head dims (192 / 128), which today pins it to the DiffKV attention backends: any other `--attention-backend` is silently replaced by the DiffKV auto-pick, and the native KV-cache write would copy V with K's head width. This PR makes `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` usable for the model (opt-in, defaults unchanged) and fixes the write kernel.

## Claims

- `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` now selects unified attention for every MiMo-V2.6 layer instead of being dropped; verified on Flash (TP2, TP4, TP8) and on Pro (TP8, gsm8k n=100 parity).
- `reshape_and_cache_flash` writes V with its own head size and head stride. Symmetric callers run the same code as before: the new checks live in the asymmetric branch, and the existing kernel is byte-identical to `main`.
- Accuracy and speculative-decoding parity with the default backend (gsm8k at n=1319, MTP x3 acceptance).
- At long context prefill is 1.43x faster at 128k and 1.21x at 32k, with decode 1.17x faster per token (TPOT p50 2.94 vs 3.45 ms) and output throughput up 21-45%. At 8k with concurrency 8 the two are at parity. Measured with `--block-size 16` on both arms, which tested better than the backend's default for this shape. On Pro at TP8 the same benchmark gives 1.13x prefill and 1.66x lower inter-token latency.

## Validation

### Commands

```bash
# serve (TP4 shown; TP2/TP8 differ only in --tensor-parallel-size; the control arm drops
# --attention-backend and gets the DiffKV auto-pick)
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 270336 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.82 \
  --block-size 16 --trust-remote-code --generation-config vllm \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --disable-prefix-caching \
  --tool-call-parser mimo --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mimo

# serve bench, one cell (input/output lengths and prompt counts per the tables)
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --model XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 131072 --random-output-len 32 \
  --num-prompts 2 --max-concurrency 1 --num-warmups 1 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 0

# gsm8k 25-shot against the running server
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template

# tests
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py
```

### Bench serve

Mimo-V2.6 Flash at TP4:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 7633.8 ms | 5317.7 ms | -30% (1.44x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 4.10 tok/s | 5.96 tok/s | +45% |
| 32k in / 128 out, 4 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 890.9 ms | 738.2 ms | -17% (1.21x) |
| 32k in / 128 out: TPOT p50 | 3.45 ms | 2.94 ms | -15% |
| 32k in / 128 out: output throughput | 96.1 tok/s | 116.0 tok/s | +21% |
| 8k in / 256 out, 8 prompts, c8: ITL p50 | 8.42 ms | 8.48 ms | parity |
| 8k in / 256 out: output throughput | 929 tok/s | 947 tok/s | +2% |

On MiMo-V2.6-Pro at TP8:

| workload | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128k in / 32 out, 2 prompts, c1: TTFT p50 | 9665.0 ms | 8576.9 ms | -11% (1.13x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: ITL p50 | 19.52 ms | 11.77 ms | -40% (1.66x) |
| 128k in / 32 out: output throughput | 3.23 tok/s | 3.68 tok/s | +14% |

Acceptance rate:
| | DiffKV (default) | AITER unified |
|---|---|---|
| MTP acceptance, 128k (acc % / length) | 53.33 / 2.07 | 56.67 / 2.13 |
| MTP acceptance, 32k | 61.40 / 2.23 | 55.60 / 2.11 |
| MTP acceptance, 8k c8 | 57.4-60.5 | 58.2-60.3 |


### lm_eval

| checkpoint | unified | DiffKV | note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash, gsm8k n=1319 | 0.9750 / 0.9742 | 0.9719 / 0.9712 | strict / flexible |

### Needle-In-A-Haystack

Unified attention only; `--max-model-len 270336`, thinking off, greedy.

| probe | config | result |
|---|---|---|
| niah | 265,673 tokens, depths 0 / 50 / 100 % | 3/3 |

### Tests

```
# kernel fix: main's cache_kernels.cu vs this one
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k asymmetric        # 33 failed -> 33 passed
# model change: main's backend selection vs this one (either kernel)
pytest tests/models/test_mimo_v2_attention_backend.py             # 2 failed, 5 passed -> 7 passed
```

The asymmetric kernel test runs MiMo's geometry (K 192 / V 128, 4 KV heads) at both block sizes the model uses (16 and 64) over a parametrized token count, in both layouts unified attention hands the kernel, for bf16 and fp8 caches and per-tensor and per-head scales. The whole file stays green (694 passed, 602 skipped).

The model test gained two checks: the selected backend's *impl* has to be unified attention's, not just its enum; and the cache the layer writes has to match a cache built in torch, per slot, with K in the first `head_dim` columns of a row and V in the remaining `v_head_dim`. Both fail on `main`. The kernel test's buffers carry slack past the cache, so a regressed kernel fails that comparison instead of writing out of bounds.

## Details

`reshape_and_cache_flash_kernel` derived one head size, one page stride, one head stride and one element count from key/key_cache and reused all of them for the value side:

```cpp
cache_t* v_dst_h = value_dst + head * head_stride;             // K's stride
vectorize_with_alignment(value_src, value_dst, n_elems, ...);  // K's width
```

Every caller until now was symmetric, so this was invisible. Unified attention is the first caller that passes `v_head_size != head_size` (MiMo is 192 / 128, packed as one `(head_size + head_size_v)` content dim per KV head), and for it V was read at K's per-head offset, copied at K's width - 64 elements past the end of each head - and written past the end of the cache on the last slot. The asymmetric case now gets its own kernel that addresses V with the value side's own head stride and length; the existing kernel and its NHD fast path are untouched, so symmetric callers run the same code as before.

Model side: the attention backend is chosen per layer, and the gate now consults a backend capability (`supports_head_size_v`) rather than listing backend names. DiffKV declares that it can serve any K/V width relation; unified attention declares `v <= k`, because it splits the page with `split(head_size)`. A backend that cannot serve the shape still gets the previous behaviour: a warning and the DiffKV auto-pick.

Known limitations:

- Requires aiter >= 0.1.25 for the V-dim-masked unified-attention kernels; `main` pins 0.1.26.
- Unified attention serves V narrower than K, not wider (`v_head_dim > head_dim` cannot be expressed by its page split); such a request falls back to the DiffKV auto-pick with a warning.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf]  Enable prefix-cache SWA replay on gfx950
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Overview

Re-enable DeepSeek-V4.1 prefix-cache sliding-window bounded replay on gfx950. Decoder replay is a separate path and is already enabled by #59039 when `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` is on. This PR only restores the prefix-cache path from #57906.

The AITER sparse MLA path consumes slot IDs that `_compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel` has already clamped to `replay_start`. The ROCm force-off in `attention.py` stays in place for every ROCm GPU other than gfx950, including gfx942. On gfx950 the sliding-window cache follows `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay`.

## Claims

- On gfx950, prefix-cache SWA replay is no longer forced off. The flag still defaults on, and `--no-swa-bounded-replay` still disables it. Other ROCm GPUs stay on the existing force-off path.
- On our best MI355X config, end-to-end throughput is 13.5% higher at concurrency 128 and 12% higher at concurrency 256.
- GSM8K and RULER NIAH are unchanged between stock and replay.

## Validation

GSM8K, 1,319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, all questions in flight:

| Arm | Accuracy |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 0.904
| Replay on | 0.902

RULER `niah_single_1` (single needle, word key, number value, repeated haystack), 131,072 tokens, 5 samples, temperature 0:

| Arm | Score |
|---|---:|
| Stock, replay off | 1.0 |
| Replay on | 1.0 |

Prefix-cache sweep across the prefill-chunk boundary. Each point primes eight DP replicas with a shared prefix plus 128 new tokens, then repeats the query. `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` is the hit signal. Every second-wave request completed on both arms, with no GPU fault.

| Prefix tokens | Stock hit tokens | Replay hit tokens |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,920 | 15,360 | 15,360 |
| 2,048 | 16,256 | 16,384 |
| 2,176 | 17,280 | 17,408 |
| 4,096 | 32,640 | 32,768 |

A separate single-request check on an otherwise stock nightly (`00b6c4c`, chunk 2048, DEP8, one request, token-id prompts) shows the config-flag A/B. Warmed requests:

| Shape | Stock | Replay |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8k TTFT | 492 ms | 316 ms |
| 32k TTFT | 1.84 s | 1.23 s |
| 128k TTFT, 1k output | 7.42 s | 4.83 s |
| 128k prefill | 17,667 tok/s | 27,136 tok/s |
| 128k decode | 52 tok/s | 49–62 tok/s |

Decode does not change. A decode step is already one new token inside the window.

CI does not have this MI355X checkpoint, so Buildkite does not cover this path.

## Details

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 40 layers. KV is written at layers 2, 8, 14, and 20. The sliding window is 128 tokens. After layer 20 has written KV for a token, layers 21–39 only need the last 128 tokens. That trim is decoder replay (#59039). It is built from `cache_config.swa_bounded_replay` and is already active on ROCm when the flag is left on.

This change is the prefix-cache half. On a prefix-cache hit, the SWA cache replays from `replay_start` instead of storing the full sliding window. gfx950 can take that path because AITER sparse MLA uses the already-clamped slot list. The old force-off assumed an extra clamp inside the FlashInfer and FlashMLA prefill kernels, which this path does not use. gfx942 cannot take AITER sparse MLA, so it stays forced off.

To enable it on a gfx950 recipe that sets `VLLM_NO_SWA_BOUNDED_REPLAY=1`, remove that setting. Keep model runner V2 and breakable CUDA graphs. A 4096-token prefill chunk is above the 768-token replay trim threshold, so it uses the trimmed graph.


## ROCm consumers

CDNA4 keeps prefix-cache SWA replay. Both ROCm consumers clamp to replay_start:

- Opt-in AITER sparse MLA reads slot ids from _compute_swa_indices_and_lens_kernel, which clamps start_pos.
- The default Triton gather path clamps the prefill gather length in ComputePrefillMetadataKernel and clamps swa_start again in combine_topk_swa_indices.

Every other ROCm GPU, including CDNA3, stays forced off. get_cdna_version() != 4 is the gate.
Limitations:

- Measured on gfx950 with the AITER Triton sparse MLA path.
- The flag defaults on, so gfx950 behavior changes for every DeepSeek-V4.1 server that does not pass `--no-swa-bounded-replay`.

title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4.1] Mono decode at TP8 on MI355X
author: okorzh-amd
body:
## Purpose

Mono decode (`--monokernel`) for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs only at TP2 and TP4. `MonoDecodeLayer._create` refuses any other tensor-parallel size. At conc 1 a TP8 server can still use mono decode: each rank streams half the weights, while the persistent K1/K2 chain stays the same length. This PR makes the existing FlyDSL kernels correct at TP8 on gfx950. That means 8 attention heads per rank, and a 288-wide routed/shared expert intermediate (routed is padded to 384 by the loader).

At TP8 the only kernel changes are the head-tile rounding and one GEMV tail. The cross-rank reduction, MoE, router, K1 front, combine and draft runner already loop over `tp` and need no changes.

## Changes

- `mono/attention/plan.py`, `Dims`: `head_tiles` now rounds up (`cdiv(heads, 16)`), and a new `heads_pad` gives whole tiles. Before this, `head_tiles` was `8 // 16 = 0` at TP8, so the split-attention loops (`back.py`) emitted no MFMAs and would silently produce wrong output once the gate opens.
  - At M=7, ratio 2, the CPU compile for gfx950 shows 0 bf16 MFMAs before the fix and 32 after, the same count as TP4.
  - A rank must have at least one tile; this is asserted.
- `mono/attention/back.py`: the split stage's q/p/st LDS and the stat offset are sized by `heads_pad`. The padded head columns are computed but never stored. That is correct by column independence:
  - each head has its own score max and its own PV column;
  - the stat stores and the combine read only `h < heads`.
- `mono/stages/gemv.py`: the row-major FP8 step load accepts `K % 64 == 32`, which is the shared expert's down projection at K = 288. The last step's upper lanes are clamped into the row, and `_fp8_step_mfma` already zeroes them on both sides.
- `mono_decode.py`: the gate admits TP8. gfx942 stays TP4 only (`:410`).
- Tests: TP8 cases are added to `test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py` (`tp in [2, 4, 8]`) and `test_dsv41_mono_layers.py` (`(8, 8)` and `(8, 28)` on cdna4).

## Test Plan

1. CPU-only FlyDSL compile for gfx950 (AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0), on this branch and on unmodified main:
   - TP8 builds: K1, K2 and FFN at M = 7 and 28; ratios 0, 1 and 2; the index-source and fold variants; and the DSpark draft K1/K2.
   - TP2 and TP4 builds: compared byte for byte against main.
2. GPU, 8x MI355X: a TP8 server with `--monokernel` running the MLPerf conc-1 recipe:
   - DSpark k=6;
   - adaptive verification off;
   - decoder SWA bounded replay;
   - MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer.

   Measurements:
   - `vllm bench serve`, random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic acceptance length 3.87, so the step time is isolated from acceptance;
   - GSM8K-1319, 8-shot greedy, block rejection with real acceptance, on the same server.
3. To run on this branch with 8 GPUs:
   ```
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_numerics.py -k "8"
   pytest tests/models/test_dsv41_mono_layers.py -k "8-8 or 8-28"
   ```

## Test Result

**CPU compile:** every TP8 build compiles with 0 VGPR spills, scratch 0, and LDS ≤ 137,248 B. TP2 and TP4 kernel binaries are byte-identical to main.

| Build | VGPR | LDS (B) |
|---|---|---|
| TP8 K1, M=7 | 142 | 38,944 |
| TP8 K2, M=7 (ratio 1/2, index) | 250 | 96,640 |
| TP8 K2, M=28 | 232 | 137,248 |
| TP8 FFN, M=7 | 243 | 79,408 |
| TP8 draft K2, M=6 | 199 | 96,640 |

**GPU, this PR alone:**
- Image: nightly `5d35ce3934` + this PR, with none of the other open DSv4.1 PRs. `mono/` and `mono_decode.py` are identical to this PR's base.
- Setup: one TP8 server with the MLPerf conc-1 recipe, `--monokernel` on or off and nothing else changed.

Decode step: random 32k in / 1k out, `--ignore-eos`, synthetic AL 3.87; ITL p50 is one DSpark step.

| TP8 | c1 step | c1 tok/s | c4 step | c4 TPOT | c4 tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` (this PR) | **5.36 ms** | 580 | **8.10 ms** | 2.57 ms | 1163 |
| without | 8.59 ms | 392 | 10.10 ms | 3.38 ms | 1014 |
| change | **-37.5%** | +48% | **-19.8%** | -24% | +15% |

Quality, same servers, real (block) acceptance:

| TP8 | GSM8K-1319 (2 runs) | AL | RULER NIAH 32k (8 tasks x 50) | RULER NIAH 128k (8 tasks x 25) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--monokernel` | 0.910 / 0.910 | 3.562 / 3.587 | 0.997 | 0.993 |
| without | 0.923 / 0.923 | 3.563 / 3.593 | 0.998 | 0.990 |

- NIAH: lm-eval 0.4.13, all 8 `niah_*` tasks, greedy, mean over tasks.
- GSM8K: mono on vs off is a paired McNemar of 26/44 flips (p 0.041) and 28/45 (p 0.060). The same arm run twice gives 35/35 and 33/32.
- Status of the GSM8K gap: investigated, but not explained yet. The layer tests below pass, and an earlier TP4 on/off pair went the other way (mono 0.929 vs 0.919).

Layer tests, all passing on 8x MI355X:
- `test_mono_decode_layer_matches_vllm[8]` and `[4]`;
- `test_mono_decode_matches_the_model[8-8]` and `[8-28]`.

CI: an optional `mi355_8` step runs the TP8 cases (the 4-GPU step skips them).

An earlier measurement on nightly `83c078d955` + #63182, #63027, #63367, #63181 and #63355 gave 4.97 ms at c1 for TP8 + mono, vs 5.27 ms for TP4 + mono. There, GSM8K was 0.917 and AL 3.568.

**Follow-ups (not in this PR):**
- With the launch-count reductions in #63885, #63888, #63890 and #63891 and the tuned K1 of #63893 (on #63027) and X8R of #63892 widened from TP4 to TP8, conc 1 reaches **4.53 ms** (GSM8K 0.919, AL 3.570). That is -14% vs TP4 + mono on the same image. The TP8 widening of #63892/#63893 is a follow-up. It also needs #63027's tuned seam (`attn_words`) to poll its 16 per-rank ATTN units in one batch: `POLL_MAX` is 12, so a split batch costs two serial round trips.
- **Not for conc ≥ 4.** At conc 4, one TP8 server is 26% lower in throughput than 2 x TP4 replicas: 1262 vs ~1706 tok/s, TPOT 2.35 vs ~1.71 ms. TP8 mono is a conc-1 configuration.
- The mono kernels' cross-rank spin-waits are unbounded, at TP4 as well. A hang on one rank stalls every rank of the server, which matters more at 8 ranks. A bounded wait with a host fail-stop, as the Kimi-K3 mono has, is planned as a separate PR.

title: [New Model] Add MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Model and Kernels
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

The first PR of the split of #63232. It adds the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash model code (everything under `vllm/models/minimax_m3`, NVIDIA and ROCm, including the DSpark draft) and all kernel changes. The model-runner, sampling and KV cache manager changes from #63232 are left out and will follow as separate PRs (plan under Details).

## Claims

- **Serve MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on Blackwell (SM100/SM103/SM107):** the NVFP4 routed experts of the MXFP8 checkpoint load through the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE with per-token FC1 input scales. The KV cache and the index-K cache run in NVFP4 on the MSA CUTLASS Q8KV4 kernels.
- **DSpark speculative decoding:** a draft model that defaults to the checkpoint's `dspark/` subfolder, with fused draft kernels and a `FLASHINFER_TS` backend for non-causal draft blocks.
- **Decode kernels:**
  - fused QKV+indexer MXFP8 GEMM epilogue;
  - SM100 fused dense GEMM1;
  - persistent QK-norm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel;
  - small-batch MoE finalize fused into all-reduce + Gemma norm + MXFP8 quant;
  - DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (opt-in, with expert parallelism);
  - opt-in NVFP4 indexer decode context parallelism at TP4.
- **ROCm:**
  - NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer on gfx950;
  - one-launch-per-layer FlyDSL mono decode;
  - small-M MXFP8 linear tuning;
  - gfx942 fallbacks.

## Validation

Unit tests ran on GB300 (SM103) against this branch, with MSA `25c1447` (the pinned version) vendored and CUDA 13.4 for the Q8KV4 JIT:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/kernels/attention -k minimax_m3` | 219 passed, 64 skipped (ROCm/other-SM) |
| fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV insert, DSpark draft kernels, MegaMoE, `tests/models/minimax_m3`, Qwen3-DFlash MXFP8 context KV, reasoning parser, speculative config, `FLASHINFER_TS`, DFlash/DSpark spec-decode unit tests, aux hidden states over PP, M3 multimodal processing, `tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py` | 689 passed, 5 skipped, 3 failed (below) |
| `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py` (2 GPUs) | 57 passed, 5 skipped |

The 3 failures (`test_modelopt_fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`, `test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint`, `test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint`) fail identically on `main` in the same environment. They are not caused by this PR.

**End-to-end on this branch.** `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` served with the command below (TP4 on GB300, NVFP4 KV + NVFP4 indexer, DSpark k=7). Higher is better. MAL is the mean number of tokens accepted per verify step, out of 8.

| Eval | Config | Score | DSpark MAL |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k (1319) | chat path, 5-shot, `thinking_mode: disabled`, T=0, max_tokens 2048 | 0.9287 flexible / 0.9196 strict | 4.77 |
| aime26 mean@16 (30 × 16) | chat path, `thinking_mode: enabled`, T=1.0, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 98304 | 0.9271 (pass@16 0.9667) | 3.48 |

Neither run had request errors. gsm8k had no truncated or unanswered rows. On aime26, 11 of 480 samples (2.3%) hit the max_tokens limit, and they are the only unanswered rows.

**On #63232 (the full branch)**, same setup with thinking on (aime26 mean@16, MMMU-Pro strict-match over 3460 questions):

| Arm | aime26 | MMMU-Pro strict | DSpark MAL (aime26 / MMMU-Pro) |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 0.9458 | 0.7936 | – |
| DSpark k=7 | 0.9208 | 0.7861 | 3.33 / 3.21 |

The two arms ran on different revisions of #63232. The paired comparison on one revision was within noise: aime26 +0.00 pp (95% CI ±3.0 pp), MMMU-Pro McNemar p=0.876.

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash -tp 4 --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, "attention_backend": "FLASHINFER_TS", "kv_cache_dtype": "fp8", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic"}' \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
```

Not covered:
- ROCm was not run (no AMD hardware here); the ROCm code is from the AMD contributors' branch and tests.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was not run.

## Details

**Shared code this PR touches.** All of it is opt-in or a no-op for other models:
- `FusedMoEConfig.qat_activation_key` (default `None`): a model declares the activation scheme its experts were QAT'd against. `make_nvfp4_moe_kernel` now raises instead of silently dropping `per_token_activation` for a backend that cannot honor it.
- `ModelOptMxFp8Config.moe_quant_algo` (default `None`): routes `moe_quant_algo: NVFP4` experts to the compressed-tensors NVFP4 MoE.
- `Attention(query_pre_quantized=False)`: lets the DSpark draft skip a second query quantization.
- `DraftModelSpeculator.attn_vllm_config`: the draft's metadata builders now see the draft overrides (attention backend, KV cache dtype). The copies are shallow, so engine-resolved state such as `cache_config.kv_cache_layout` survives. Covered by `test_draft_attention_backend_override.py`.
- New `FLASHINFER_TS` attention backend, `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp`, a MiniMax-M3 TP check for NVFP4 KV, and the MSA pin bump (`968061a` → `25c1447`).
- The CuTe DSL primitives of the DeepSeek-V4.1 all-reduce and the Kimi-K3 latent MoE tail move to `vllm/models/common/ops/moe_tail_fusion`, shared with the M3 finalize fusion. Their callers only change import paths.

**For reviewers:**
- The ROCm mono decode here (`VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_M3_MONO`) predates and overlaps the upstream M3 MonoKernel (#62712, `kernel_config.monokernel`). The two need reconciling; it can also move to its own PR.
- `attention_config.indexer_decode_cp` (NVFP4 indexer, TP4) sits next to the existing `minimax_m3_indexer_cp` (ROCm bf16 Triton CP).
- The Q8KV4 prefill keeps a per-device split workspace that is only allocated on SM107. It was a stopgap on the source branch.

**Split of #63232.** Later PRs:

| PR | Contents | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| this | MiniMax-M3.1 model + DSpark draft + kernels | – |
| 2 | ROCm NVFP4 → MXFP8/MXFP4 online re-quantization and fused shared experts through the online quantization API (needed to serve the NVFP4-expert checkpoint on ROCm) | – |
| 3 | NIXL P/D for per-head-contiguous NVFP4 pages (`AttentionSpec.kv_head_major_slots`) | this |
| 4 | FA4: no descale tensors for a unit per-tensor scale | – |
| 5 (deferred) | DSpark/DFlash sampling performance: Markov bias in the Gumbel kernel, batch-sharded draft sampling, wide DFlash padding, top-k/top-p | this |
| 6 (deferred) | KV cache manager: keep KV zeroing for mixed-precision groups | – |
| 7 (deferred) | SimpleCPUOffload HugeTLB host buffer (not MiniMax-specific) | – |

<details>
<summary>Where the excluded files of #63232 go</summary>

- **PR 2:** `quantization/online/*` (incl. `shared_expert.py`, `requantization.py`), `quantization/utils/config_utils.py`, `fused_moe/{utils,routed_experts}.py`, `quark/*`, `nvfp4_emulation_utils.py`, `base_config.py`, `model_loader/utils.py`, the NVFP4 oracle's re-quantization hook, the dequantize-iterator change in the ModelOpt/CT NVFP4 MoE, and the ROCm NVFP4-expert guard and FSE resolver in `minimax_m3/amd/model.py`.
- **PR 3:** `kv_cache_interface.py` (`kv_head_major_slots`), `nixl/base_worker.py`, the model's `kv_head_major_slots=True`, and its insert test.
- **PR 4:** `v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`.
- **PR 5:** `v1/worker/gpu/{sample/gumbel,sample/batch_shard,input_batch,model_runner}.py`, the rest of the DFlash/DSpark speculators, `v1/sample/ops/topk_topp_*`, the scheduler's DFlash/DSpark draft slots, and `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM.compute_draft_logits_local`.
- **PR 6:** `v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` and `KVCacheConfig.mixed_precision_kv_cache`.
- **PR 7:** `v1/simple_kv_offload/*` and its connector.

title: [Perf][DSA] Read BF16 logits directly in persistent top-k
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Merged by WoosukKwon on 2026-10-30 as [`e31cf3dec7cf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0), following approval of final PR head `5ff957619959`. The validation revisions and their scope are recorded below.

Let the existing persistent top-k backend read BF16 indexer logits and widen loaded scores to FP32 inside its kernels. On SM100 decode without DCP, this removes the full FP32 logits allocation whenever `auto` resolves to persistent, as well as for explicit persistent.

Query chunking is separate work. This PR complements [#62172](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62172), which implements BF16 input for cooperative top-k. This change implements persistent, filtered and sampled paths instead. Open-PR searches found no separate persistent-BF16 implementation. The caller uses the same `takes_bf16_logits()` capability-interface design as #62172; cooperative support remains with that PR.

## Claims

- Keep the existing backend selection and top-k algorithms. Scores loaded from BF16 widen to FP32 before binning/refinement; register score arrays remain FP32.
- Remove the dense FP32 logits copy for supported persistent decode calls, including default auto. Cooperative, DCP and prefill retain their existing behavior. No DeepSelect switch or query-row chunking is introduced.
- Preserve exact selected scores and valid top-k indices in the tested cases. Equal-score index identity/order and generated-token equivalence are not claimed.

## Validation

### Performance breakdown and memory traffic

**DeepGEMM's logits computation is unchanged.** This PR saves work **after** BF16 logits have been produced: it removes the separate BF16-to-FP32 materialization and lets persistent top-k read BF16 directly. It does not reduce Q/K projection work, the score computation, or the number of logits. The measurements below exclude DeepGEMM and are not end-to-end model speedups.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    P["DeepGEMM: unchanged score computation"] --> B["BF16 logits in GPU memory: unchanged"]
    B -->|Before PR| C["Separate conversion kernel: read BF16, write FP32"]
    C --> F["Full FP32 logits buffer"]
    F --> O["Load FP32 scores; existing FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    B -->|With PR: supported persistent calls| N["Load BF16 scores; widen in registers; same FP32 top-k algorithm"]
    O --> I["Top-k indices"]
    N --> I
```

| Where the saving occurs | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| External conversion | Allocate a full FP32 logits buffer; read 2 bytes and write 4 bytes per valid score | Remove this allocation and GPU conversion kernel |
| Top-k input loads | 4 bytes per FP32 score; an aligned four-score load reads 16 bytes | 2 bytes per BF16 score; an aligned four-score load reads 8 bytes and expands to four FP32 registers |
| Score arithmetic inside top-k | FP32 comparison/binning/refinement | The same FP32 algorithm, with on-load widening; register score arrays are still FP32 |

Code: [producer and conversion bypass](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L939-L954), [old allocation and conversion kernel](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L297-L329), and [FP32/BF16 load helpers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6bcc085a55223db05705cf5b9b6e605eb11e9946/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L100).

**Measured breakdown: pre-PR `98fc6da9d735` versus PR `293880733f87`, GB200.** The PR source is unchanged by the subsequent main merges. The BF16 top-k timing includes its loads, register widening, and selection; it is not the cast alone.

| Q / valid K / top-k | External conversion: before → after (µs) | Native top-k: FP32 → BF16 (µs) | Native top-k latency change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 2.848 → removed | 4.832 → 5.632 | +16.56% |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 19.296 → removed | 31.232 → 30.240 | -3.18% |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 35.264 → removed | 44.800 → 42.352 | -5.46% |

The **33–44% full selection-stage improvement** in the long-row cases mainly comes from eliminating the external conversion; native top-k alone improves by only about 3–5%. The short-row native kernel is slower with BF16, while the measured complete caller still improves after removing the conversion. Smaller input loads can help, but widening adds register instructions. Halving score-input bytes does not establish that total HBM traffic or latency halves; cache behavior and multiple passes matter. No hardware-counter measurement proves a bandwidth-only explanation.

**Allocation size and accessed bytes are different quantities.** At Q=128 and valid K=100000, the removed conversion logically reads 25.6 MB of BF16 data and writes 51.2 MB of FP32 data (decimal MB). A single full scan by top-k reads 51.2 MB of FP32 score payload versus 25.6 MB of BF16 payload; this is byte accounting, not measured DRAM traffic. The full FP32 allocation is larger because it retains capacity W=262144 and padded stride=262656: about **128.248 MiB**. That temporary disappears; the original BF16 logits and existing workspace remain. CUDA graph replay does not remove conversion kernels automatically; this PR removes that node and its FP32 storage from supported captured paths.

These component timings are separate cold-cache ablations, **not additive**. The complete caller measurements below remain the primary before/after result.

<details>
<summary>Breakdown measurement method and why the columns are not additive</summary>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`, using the same frozen runtimes and matching fixed BF16 inputs as the full-stage table below. GB200 job 41138: A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph samples per stage/run (60 per arm). Conversion uses the actual `as_fp32_logits`; top-k uses the native persistent entrypoint. Input capacity W=262144, padded stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576.

These are separately captured cold-cache ablations, not timestamps of nodes in one production graph. Conversion warms its FP32 output for the following kernel, while standalone top-k starts cold. The full caller also clears the output-index buffer; this native-only ablation omits that common operation. Summing the component columns therefore does not reconstruct the full-stage table. Jointly captured conversion+FP32 top-k medians are retained separately in the raw results (6.816, 46.5755 and 78.0805 µs); the full caller table remains the primary before/after comparison.

For intuition only, one full score scan would give 2-byte BF16 read + 4-byte FP32 write + 4-byte FP32 read before this PR, versus a 2-byte BF16 read after it. This 10→2 byte accounting excludes unchanged producer writes, metadata/workspace accesses, multiple selection passes and cache effects; it is not a measured traffic reduction or a 5x speedup prediction.

Every ablation passes exact selected-score, valid/unique-index and input-preservation checks. Raw samples, identities and commands are retained in `main_vs_packed_breakdown_v1` (`bench.py`, `run.sbatch`, `SUMMARY.json`, `results/41138_*`). These component measurements do not establish full-model accuracy or end-to-end performance.

</details>

### Full selection-stage results

Recorded performance baseline: **unmodified pre-PR base `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus measured PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`**. The baseline has no persistent BF16 support and widens the BF16 producer output to a full FP32 logits tensor. The PR keeps BF16 for supported persistent calls. Neither arm includes cooperative BF16 support from #62172 or the FP32-producer configuration from #64580. This table measures the whole PR against its pre-PR baseline, not an intermediate PR commit.

Job 41130 on an exclusive GB200: A/B/B/A fresh processes, CUPTI cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, 30 samples/run (60 per arm/shape). The actual indexer caller receives identical fixed injected BF16 logits. **Timing includes the required full-tensor conversion and top-k**, but excludes the real DeepGEMM producer, CPU Python dispatch and the model. Caller/provider source files match the stated revisions. Both target CUDA translation units were rebuilt; unrelated native objects/runtime are held fixed. This is a matched component comparison, not a fresh whole-main build or an end-to-end model benchmark.

| Q / valid K / top-k | Backend | Without PR / with PR median µs | Latency change | Without PR / with PR extra live MiB |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | cooperative (unchanged control) | 7.504 / 7.488 | -0.21% | 64.123 / 64.123 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | persistent | 7.616 / 6.784 | -10.92% | 66.000 / 0.000 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | persistent | 15.648 / 15.456 | -1.23% | 256.498 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | persistent | 47.072 / 31.392 | -33.31% | 128.248 / 0.000 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | persistent | 78.240 / 43.488 | -44.42% | 128.248 / 0.000 |

W=262144, row stride=262656, host scheduling bound=1048576; valid K length is separate. Small-Q cooperative is an unaffected control: both arms still widen and consume FP32, and its 0.21% timing difference is not claimed as an optimization gain. Persistent cases skip the widening in the PR. The longer-context results include removing that conversion; they must not be described as a 33–44% speedup of the top-k kernel alone. No universal speedup or no-regression claim is made for unmeasured shapes/backends/hardware.

<details>
<summary>Per-process medians and memory interpretation</summary>

| Q / valid K / top-k | Baseline run medians µs | PR run medians µs |
|---|---|---|
| 64 / 4096 / 512 | 7.4880, 7.5200 | 7.4880, 7.4880 |
| 65 / 4096 / 512 | 7.6320, 7.6160 | 6.7840, 6.7680 |
| 256 / 8192 / 1024 | 15.6480, 15.6480 | 15.4080, 15.4880 |
| 128 / 100000 / 512 | 46.9120, 47.2000 | 31.4555, 31.2960 |
| 128 / 200000 / 1024 | 78.1755, 78.2400 | 43.5200, 43.3920 |

Extra live peak excludes the already allocated BF16 inputs, outputs and workspace. Zero extra allocation does not mean zero total device/model memory. Graph-private reservations agree across repeats: Q64 66→66 MiB; Q65 66→0 MiB; Q256 258→0 MiB; both Q128 cases 130→0 MiB. Allocator reservation can exceed live tensor bytes. Profiling reservation is unchanged, so increased model KV capacity is not claimed.

All four arms at each shape have identical input hashes and selected-score bit bags, pass valid/unique-index checks, preserve input bits, and witness the expected conversion/dtype/backend behavior. Baseline FP32 widening is bit-exact against the fixed BF16 scores. Prior experiments are archived under their original baselines; their numbers are not mixed into this table.

</details>

**Expanded DeepSeek configuration coverage (GB200, job 41191).** Eighteen additional persistent-path cases use checkpoint-derived top-k and capacity, covering 16K/32K/64K raw contexts, Q=128/512/1024, uniform and mixed valid lengths, empty rows, and rows shorter than top-k. All 18 measured full-stage medians improve by **5.85%–39.66%** versus the same pre-PR baseline; no cooperative performance points were rerun. This is configuration-derived selection-stage coverage, not measured production-frequency coverage or an end-to-end model speedup.

<details>
<summary>All 18 additional cases, model provenance, correctness and measurement limits</summary>

Baseline `98fc6da9d7355d2cc85141980439fded9a5fb61c` versus current PR `293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc`; same pinned matched top-k builds as the primary table, on an exclusive GB200 node (`gb200-rack1-04`). A/B/B/A fresh processes, 30 cold-L2 CUPTI graph replays per process (60 samples/arm). The measured boundary retains actual caller output clearing, conditional conversion and automatic persistent dispatch. It injects deterministic synthetic BF16 logits instead of running DeepGEMM; the kernels and auto policy are not retuned.

| Configuration | Checkpoint revision | top-k | Compression | Logits capacity W / tested stride |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v4_c4 (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark) | `62af8fffb2f7030cac4de2f0169f5b8d1101b646` | 512 | 4 | 262144 / 262656 |
| v41_c2 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) | `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027` | 512 | 2 | 524288 / 525312 |
| v41_c1_dense (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) | `2cba9e42aa026125f3ed06c6d98c1db82f7ca027` | 512 | 1 | 1048576 / 1049088 |
| v32exp_selection (DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp) | `194c67e12b1b0d6df0ef373ddcf215bc84027409` | 2048 | 1 | 163840 / 164352 |

V4/V4.1 checkpoint maximum context is 1048576; dense indexer width is configured context divided by compression. V3.2-Exp's configured maximum is 163840. The 128K deployment-capacity control uses W=32768 and stride=33792. Tested strides round W up to multiples of 1536 and are explicit padded selection-input layouts; they do not assert that every producer version uses this padding. Host scheduling bound equals W. V4.1 c1 measurements apply to its **dense** indexer path, not candidate-consuming sparse-logits layers. V3.2-Exp cases validate its dimensions at the BF16 selection boundary, not its actual producer/model execution.

| Configuration | Q | Valid K max | top-k | Rows | Baseline → PR µs | Change | Extra peak MiB before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| v4_c4 | 128 | 4096 | 512 | uniform | 8.192 → 7.344 | -10.35% | 128.248 → 0.000 |
| v4_c4 | 128 | 8192 | 512 | uniform | 9.888 → 9.104 | -7.92% | 128.248 → 0.000 |
| v4_c4 | 128 | 16384 | 512 | uniform | 13.056 → 11.968 | -8.33% | 128.248 → 0.000 |
| v4_c4 | 512 | 16384 | 512 | mixed | 24.961 → 21.440 | -14.10% | 512.998 → 0.000 |
| v41_c2 | 128 | 8192 | 512 | uniform | 9.536 → 8.736 | -8.39% | 256.496 → 0.000 |
| v41_c2 | 128 | 16384 | 512 | uniform | 12.928 → 11.696 | -9.53% | 256.496 → 0.000 |
| v41_c2 | 128 | 32768 | 512 | uniform | 20.032 → 17.184 | -14.22% | 256.496 → 0.000 |
| v41_c2 | 512 | 32768 | 512 | mixed | 38.752 → 31.280 | -19.28% | 1026.000 → 0.000 |
| v41_c1_dense | 128 | 16384 | 512 | uniform | 12.864 → 11.744 | -8.71% | 512.248 → 0.000 |
| v41_c1_dense | 128 | 32768 | 512 | uniform | 20.128 → 17.104 | -15.02% | 512.248 → 0.000 |
| v41_c1_dense | 128 | 65536 | 512 | uniform | 39.168 → 25.856 | -33.99% | 512.248 → 0.000 |
| v41_c1_dense | 512 | 65536 | 512 | mixed | 80.209 → 48.400 | -39.66% | 2048.998 → 0.000 |
| v32exp_selection | 128 | 16384 | 2048 | uniform | 16.912 → 15.280 | -9.65% | 80.248 → 0.000 |
| v32exp_selection | 128 | 32768 | 2048 | uniform | 25.297 → 21.696 | -14.23% | 80.248 → 0.000 |
| v32exp_selection | 128 | 65536 | 2048 | uniform | 35.520 → 25.472 | -28.29% | 80.248 → 0.000 |
| v32exp_selection | 512 | 65536 | 2048 | mixed | 83.552 → 53.695 | -35.73% | 320.998 → 0.000 |
| v4_c4_128k_capacity | 128 | 8192 | 512 | uniform | 9.568 → 9.008 | -5.85% | 16.496 → 0.000 |
| v4_c4_large_q | 1024 | 16384 | 512 | mixed | 41.952 → 35.200 | -16.09% | 1026.000 → 0.000 |

Q is the total number of query rows. Uniform cases use raw contexts 16K/32K/64K, divided by the listed compression ratio. Mixed cases cycle valid K lengths through 0, top-k/2, top-k, L/4, L/2, L−1 and L, where L is the table's maximum. This deliberately stresses variable-length and empty/padded rows; it is not a measured serving distribution. Q=1024 can represent a large verification batch dimension but does not validate the speculative-decoding pipeline.

All **18 × 4 process/case combinations** pass eager and CUDA-graph replay checks: matching fixed input hashes, exact selected-score FP32 bit multisets against an integer-order reference, in-range unique indices, correct -1 padding, and unchanged input bits. Baseline conversions match the BF16 values widened to FP32 bit-for-bit. All arms agree on selected-score hashes; tie-index identity/order is not required. Observed auto dispatch is persistent in every case; baseline materializes FP32 and current PR consumes BF16.

Extra peak is measured beyond preallocated input/output/workspace; zero does not mean zero model/device memory. The removed FP32 temporary ranges from 16.496 to 2048.998 MiB in these cases. Graph-pool reservations and all per-process medians/raw samples are retained alongside the report. Scope remains one GPU architecture and synthetic score distributions: no new final-commit PD/collocated model performance or generated-token equivalence is established.

Reproducibility bundle: `deepseek_config_coverage_v1/{benchmark.py,CASES.json,MODEL_CONFIGS.json,run.sbatch,summarize.py,SUMMARY.json,MANIFEST.json,results/41191_*}`. Config files, caller/provider sources and loaded native libraries are fingerprinted. Run `sbatch -p normal .../deepseek_config_coverage_v1/run.sbatch` with the recorded runtime paths to repeat the full comparison. An initial attempt (41190) stopped in an untimed benchmark observer due to a CPU/GPU mask mismatch; it produced no timing data and was fixed before every arm of 41191.

</details>

### Correctness and CI


Raw samples, commands, source/native fingerprints and archived prior results are retained in the author review bundle (`main_vs_packed_pr_v1`, job 41130 for the performance table; prior standalone/helper/integration jobs 41117, 41103 and 41107 for the respective correctness scopes). Pre-commit checks passed for the final helper delta. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation and this description.

## Details

The aligned BF16 vector-load helpers use the same packed integer load and bit-expansion implementation as #62172; scalar and guarded tail loads remain available. FP32 overloads are unchanged.

### BF16 and FP32 load behavior

The helpers separate the input storage type from the existing FP32 selection arithmetic:

| Helper | BF16 input | FP32 input |
|---|---|---|
| `to_float(x)` | Widen one BF16 value with `__bfloat162float(x)` | Identity: `return x;` |
| `load_score2(ptr)` | Read 4 bytes containing two BF16 values and expand them to two FP32 values (8 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float2` load (8 input bytes) |
| `load_score4(ptr)` | Read 8 bytes containing four BF16 values and expand them to four FP32 values (16 bytes of value storage) | The existing `float4` load (16 input bytes) |
| Guarded tail load | Read only valid BF16 elements, widen individually, and fill invalid elements with negative infinity | Retain the existing FP32 predicated-load implementation |

For the aligned four-score BF16 helper, [`topk_histogram_4096.cuh:78–82`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L78-L82) contains:

```cpp
const uint2 raw = *reinterpret_cast<const uint2*>(ptr);
return make_float4(
    __uint_as_float(raw.x << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.x & 0xFFFF0000u),
    __uint_as_float(raw.y << 16), __uint_as_float(raw.y & 0xFFFF0000u));
```

`uint2` contains two 32-bit words, so the input payload is 8 bytes. Each word holds two BF16 values. The shifts and masks place each BF16 bit pattern in the upper 16 bits of its own FP32 word; `__uint_as_float` reinterprets that word as a float. `make_float4` returns four 32-bit values: **8 input bytes become 16 bytes of FP32 values, not 32 bytes**. These values feed the kernel's existing FP32 register computation; the helper does not allocate or write a full FP32 logits tensor in global memory.

The [FP32 scalar overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L70-L73) returns its input unchanged, and the [FP32 four-score overload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e31cf3dec7cf14369b0c7a8447cdfb8b387af6e0/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L75-L77) retains `*reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(ptr)`. FP32 inputs are never downcast to BF16.


Code references: [BF16-to-FP32 register conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/csrc/topk_histogram_4096.cuh#L71-L92), [backend capability query](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/indexer_topk.py#L236-L255), and [conditional full-tensor conversion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/293880733f87a095acac787a996e68b097eac7cc/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py#L951-L954).

BF16 input is widened losslessly on load; this avoids materializing FP32 logits in global memory. All existing raw-score rereads, including exact overflow recovery, accept the input type and immediately widen it. The FP32 comparison keys, candidate/refinement logic and backend thresholds are preserved. Candidate-block selection retains FP32 compact scores for auto/persistent so this change does not alter that selection stage's arithmetic.

The capability query reports input support; it does not change `resolve_backend()` or choose a backend by measured speed. It inspects host shape/type metadata without reading GPU tensor values. Cooperative continues to receive FP32. BF16 native persistent requires at least 128 KiB opt-in shared memory and contiguous columns. Existing addressing limits remain unchanged; large-row measurements do not cross the pre-existing filtered uint32 row-offset limit.

### Integration with #62172

The two features can coexist and share `takes_bf16_logits()` plus the same BF16 load helpers. The local reconciled version was validated as described above. **Current online heads still require rebase/conflict resolution**; helper alignment alone does not make them a clean merge.

Whichever PR merges second should:

- Combine cooperative and persistent capability predicates and their test expectations, retaining the existing explicit DeepSelect support.
- Preserve main's exact-overflow correction from #62936 when rebasing the older cooperative branch.
- Retain guarded BF16 predicated loads needed by persistent, instead of importing the cooperative-only assertion that rejects that instantiation.
- Preserve small-Q auto's FP32/cooperative fallback where only the widened stride satisfies TMA alignment, and preserve FP32 compact candidate-block scores for explicit cooperative as well. These integration-policy guards were included in the local validated reconciliation.

No cooperative implementation is copied into this standalone persistent PR. Cooperative-first followed by this PR rebasing onto the shared interface is one straightforward merge order; either order requires the same reconciliation.

title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: reset MoE expert padding at begin
author: hao-aaron
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

At the start of a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336), zero MoE expert padding, so that post-load processing reruns over the same bytes as a cold start. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

MoE expert parameters are often larger than the checkpoint tensors loaded into them: DeepEP rounds the hidden size up, MXFP4 / TRT-LLM / AITER backends round the intermediate size, and block-aligned FP8 TP pads shards. Loaders copy only the checkpoint part. On a direct reload the padding then holds the previous post-processed bytes, which post-load processing processes again. After a `load_format=dummy` cold start (the usual RL setup) it holds random values.

## Claims

- **gpt-oss-20b (TP2, MXFP4), direct reload through IPC weight transfer:** every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh start, both after 3 same-weight syncs and after a dummy start plus one sync. On main, 168 expert tensors differ after every sync and drift from one sync to the next. After a dummy start, 288 differ and GSM8K drops about 2 points.
- Cold start and layerwise reload are unchanged.
- No loader changes: whether to fill is decided from `moe_config` when the checkpoint layout is recorded at cold start, so it also covers dummy and other cold starts that skip loaders, and the load plan (#64418) that bypasses them.

## Validation

**This PR's head (`1e25cc87e2`) with #66010 (`84ab98b6d8`) applied, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 1319 questions, 3 updates; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid). Differing expert parameters are 0 on every rank after every update. Jobs 45934, 45935.

| Sleep | Start | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 2 | Real | 0.9090 → 0.8984 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.8999 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| None | Real | 0.9007 → 0.8969 → 0.9022 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 |

**Layerwise reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise`, the default).** `materialize_meta_tensor` now zeroes the tensor it allocates, because loaders write only checkpoint regions and padding otherwise keeps uninitialized memory. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, no sleep, 1319 questions, on main `5c97556318` with and without that one line. Jobs 46042, 46043.

| Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 160 / 160 / 160 | 0.9037 → 0.0 → 0.0 |
| With the zero fill | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8954 → 0.9007 → 0.9030 |

`test_padded_moe_reload_releases_each_layer` fails 8 of 16 cases without the line.

**main vs this PR, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, reload from disk, no sleep mode; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with each arm's Python files overlaid, PR at e6403484fc; later commits change a comment and a CI trigger and merge main). "Differing" counts expert parameters per rank, out of 160, against a real cold start on the same arm. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. Jobs 45840, 45841.

| Start | Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real | main | 120 / 120 / 120 | 0.9052 → 0.9105 → 0.8984 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9014 → 0.9067 → 0.9075 |
| Dummy | main | 160 / 160 / 160 | — → 0.8787 → 0.8400 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | — → 0.8976 → 0.8999 |

On main after a dummy start the padding is random and GSM8K keeps falling across updates. Run-to-run noise on the real cold start is up to 1.5 points, so the real-start GSM8K rows don't separate the arms; the tensor counts do.

**Earlier revision.** The tables below ran before the fill became zero-only (it then kept block scales at 1).

**End to end** (GB200, nightly wheel 81a2879403 with each arm's Python files overlaid, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, real IPC weight transfer). "Differing" means device tensors (registered and reachable from module attributes) whose digest differs from a fresh real start; GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. The PR ran at 5b3856b564; later commits change only tests.

| Model (TP, MoE backend) | Arm | Real start + 3 syncs: differing | GSM8K | Dummy start + 1 sync: differing | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b (TP2, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16`) | main | 168 / 168 / 168 | 0.9030 | 288 | 0.8825 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9022 | 0 | 0.8969 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, intermediate 576 → 640; NCCL, trainer on a second node) | main | 120 / 120 / 120 per rank | 0.9022 | 160 per rank (MoE)† | — |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9045 | 0 (MoE)† | — |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4, FlashInfer TRT-LLM, intermediate 192 → 256) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8961 | 0 | 0.8878 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8939 | 0 | 0.8961 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP4, Triton, block-aligned TP) | main | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9075 | 1152* | 0.8992 |
| | this PR | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.9037 | 1152* | 0.9007 |

- On main, the gpt-oss tensors that differ are expert biases and scales after real-start syncs, and all six expert parameters after a dummy start.
- The two Qwen3 configs are already correct on main: `_zero_intermediate_padding` and the block-aligned TP loader fill rewrite their padding on every load. They show the change does no harm.
- \* Attention KV-cache scales the checkpoint doesn't contain keep their random dummy values. This happens on both arms and isn't MoE padding; it's fixed separately (KV-scale `dummy_weight_value`).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: on main the 120 tensors per rank are `w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` of all 40 MoE layers, and their bytes change on every sync; after a dummy start `w2_weight` differs too. PR 3 ran at b5130fff61, main at e5d9bad98e. † The Engram embedding tables (about 203 GB, tensors of ~98 GB) can't be sent through the transfer path, so after a dummy start they keep dummy values in both arms and GSM8K isn't meaningful there; they are the only tensors that differ on this PR.
- Jobs: 44520, 44529 (gpt-oss); 44521 (BF16); 44522, 44530 (FP8); 45005, 45002 (DeepSeek-V4.1).

**Cold-start A/B** (A = main 81a2879403, B = this PR a096f3f138, same nightly wheel, same node, arms back to back). GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions; throughput from `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64.

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K A → B | Output tok/s A → B | KV cache A → B |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4, chat GSM8K (TP2) | 0.8886 → 0.8976 | 14390 → 14727 | 7.259M → 7.259M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4; intermediate 192 → 256) | 0.8946 → 0.8893 | 9230 → 9444 | 6.791M → 6.791M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (TP4) | 0.9045 → 0.9083 | 7269 → 7098 | 7.274M → 7.274M |

All within noise: GSM8K within 1 point, throughput within 2.4% in both directions, KV cache identical. At cold start this PR only records the fill list (jobs 44551–44553).

**Unit tests** (GB200, job 44519):
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py::test_direct_reload_after_dummy_start_resets_padding[block|static]` builds a real fp8 `RoutedExperts` with intermediate 256 → 384, fills every parameter with 7 instead of loading, records, then begins and loads. It checks that the result equals a zero-initialized load, that per-expert scalars and `e_score_correction_bias` are left alone, and that the record made at cold start decides the fill.
- `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` and `test_direct_reload.py` and `test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py` on the final code: 153 passed (GB200 job 23710). Earlier, `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` and `test_reload.py -k padded` (layerwise) also passed.

## Details

**Design.**
- `RoutedExperts.padding_fill_params()` applies when `moe_config` shows the hidden size or the per-partition intermediate size rounded up past its unpadded value, or block-aligned TP sharding.
- It returns the layer's parameters minus per-expert scalars: a parameter is filled if it has more than two values per expert. So per-tensor and static input scales, which may be absent from the checkpoint, are kept.
- `record_checkpoint_layout` stores `(module, name)` at cold start, before post-load processing. Some post-load processing pads only the runtime copy and writes the padded size back into `moe_config`, so the decision must not be made later.
- `begin_direct_reload` looks up each name after the view-back, skips parameters post-load processing has dropped, and zero-fills the rest whole. Loaders then overwrite every checkpoint region.

**Requirement.** The fill erases the checkpoint region too, so every checkpoint tensor loaded into these parameters must be resent on every update. The direct delivery contract in `direct.py` says so; the completeness check (F2 in #54477) will enforce it.

**Padding value.** Everything is filled with 0. A padding-only scale block only multiplies weights the same fill zeroes, so its value doesn't change the output. MXFP4 (DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss) and NVFP4 scales are created as zeros or empty, so 0 also matches a cold start. Block-aligned TP padding is rewritten by its loader after the fill, with scales at 1. Weights created with `torch.empty` had uninitialised padding at cold start; they get 0 here.

**`moe_config` is the source today, not the only possible one.** A layer padded some other way implements `padding_fill_params()` and reuses the same fill.

**Not changed.** Layerwise reload, the block-aligned TP loader fill, and `_zero_intermediate_padding` (cold start still needs it, since those weights are `torch.empty`).

**History.** This replaces this PR's earlier design, where loaders recorded the padding regions on every load and `fill_padding` wrote them before post-load processing. That design worked with layerwise reload and partial updates. Under the decision to require full updates and to drop layerwise reload (#54477), the fill at begin is much smaller and needs no loader changes. The streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 TP split moved to #65353, and Inkling AMD's padding (#64690) is covered by this fill.
