title: [Model Loader] Run the model-level post-load hook once at the end of every load and reload
author: hao-aaron
body:
Thanks to Tony Wang (@new-TonyWang) for design and review contributions.

PR 1 of the direct weight reload stack (RFC #54477). It replaces #57733. The code is the same, plus the Llama4 DP-vision fix that #57733 dropped when it was narrowed.

## Problem

RL weight updates do not load a model in one `load_weights` call. The weight-transfer engines (NCCL, IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) and `reload_weights` call it once per bucket, or once per tensor, between `initialize_layerwise_reload` and `finalize_layerwise_reload`. On main, three things go wrong with that:

1. **The model-level hook never runs after a reload.** `finalize_layerwise_reload` only finishes the layers. The model's `process_weights_after_loading()` runs only from the cold-load path. So any state a model derives from its weights in that hook, such as fused buffers or broadcast copies, keeps the old weights' values after an update.
2. **Some models do that work inside `load_weights` instead.** It then runs once per bucket, on partial weights. Under layerwise reload it runs while the layers are still on meta, which fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. This affects DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, the DFlash/DSpark drafters and Muse Spark.
3. **Checks on "what this call loaded" fire on every bucket.** A bucket that happens not to contain a layer or head raises "MTP layer N weights missing", or silently sets the DSpark `confidence_head` to `None`.

## Fix

- **One finish step.** New `finalize_model_weights(model)` calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. It is called once at the end of a cold load (as before, after per-layer quant processing) and once at the end of every `finalize_layerwise_reload`. That covers `reload_weights` and the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.
  - The sparse NCCL engine patches weights in place without layerwise reload; its `finish_weight_update` now calls `finalize_model_weights` once.
  - An M2N update whose plan is all direct does not call `finalize_layerwise_reload`, so it still skips the hook, as on main.
  - The torchao reload decorator and the expert-substitution error path finish the layers in the middle of a load. They now call `finalize_layerwise_processing`, so they do not run the model hook early.
- **Post-load work moves from `load_weights` into the hook.** Each `load_weights` below now only loads, and the hook runs at the end:
  - DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA, V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD: the mHC broadcast (V4.1 AMD's `finalize_mega_moe_weights` is a no-op).
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA: the Engram checkpoint page-cache drop and THP collapse. They now also run after every reload and after dummy loads; both are harmless to repeat.
  - DeepSeek-V4 XPU target, MTP and DSpark: `finalize_mega_moe_weights`. The lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` is removed, since dummy loads run the hook too.
  - Qwen3 DFlash / Qwen3 DSpark / Gemma4 DSpark / Muse Spark DSpark: `_build_fused_kv_buffers`.
    - The hook now runs after quant processing.
    - In Qwen3 DFlash/DSpark and Gemma4 DSpark, the fused path that reads `.weight` directly is used only when the projections are unquantized and not CPU-repacked (`_reads_raw_weights`). Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method.
    - Muse Spark DSpark still slices `qkv_proj.weight` directly, now after quant processing, so a quantized or CPU-repacked Muse Spark drafter would read kernel-layout weights.
    - Qwen3 DFlash's MXFP8 context K/V projection copied the K/V rows of each layer's QKV weight and scales, which is only valid before quant processing. It is now created at construction and loaded from the checkpoint's K/V tensors as they stream through `load_weights`, so its own post-load step runs and a reload refills it in place.
  - Muse Spark AMD and Muse Spark DSpark: `materialize_residual_path_constants`.
- **The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop their workaround.** They had reordered the weight stream so that the language model's in-`load_weights` finalization saw all its weights (`stream_language_model_first`, `finalizes_weights_during_load`, `_weights_finalized`). That is no longer needed and is removed.
- **"Complete load" checks are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`**, which the weight-transfer engines turn off during an update:
  - The MTP layer checks in DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next and Kimi-K3 (AMD/NVIDIA).
  - The DSpark `confidence_head` drop in Qwen3, Gemma4 and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (NVIDIA/AMD).
  - The Qwen3 DSpark vocab checks.
  - `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- **dots3 vision: the block compile runs once.** The vision hook now reruns after every reload, and main's `compile_block_modules` would wrap the blocks in another `torch.compile` each time. It now compiles in place with `Module.compile` (parameter names keep no `_orig_mod`) and only once. The vision MoE is unchanged from main: its hook fuses the experts into FP8 once, deletes the checkpoint experts and returns early afterwards, so a reload leaves the vision experts as they are.
- **Llama4 DP vision (`mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`).**
  - Before: the vision attention used `ReplicatedLinear`, and `load_weights` gathered `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and called `torch.cat` once all three had arrived. An update that sends them in separate calls failed on `torch.cat` of `None`.
  - Now: it uses `QKVParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` with `disable_tp=True` in DP mode, so q/k/v go through the normal stacked mapping and each part is written into its rows as it arrives. `_consolidate_qkv_weights` is removed.
- **Raw Tensorizer loads use the shared loader path.** Loading a non-vLLM-tensorized checkpoint used its own `_load_model_serialized_cpu`, which ran the model hook but skipped per-layer `process_weights_after_loading`. It now goes through `BaseModelLoader.load_model`.

## Not in this PR

- **Weights combined from several checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights`.** A weight plus its scale, or a fused FP8 qkv, still need every part in the same call, as on main:
  - the FP8 indexer `wk` dequant;
  - GLM5-next MLA projections;
  - MiMo-V2 fused qkv;
  - Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding.

  These are later PRs in the stack (PR 6).
- **Drafters that still finish inside `load_weights`, unchanged from main:**
  - LiLiCorr: the coverage check and `materialize_inference_buffers`.
  - Laguna DFlash: the fused KV build.
  - Qwen3 XPress: the `mix.L` check, `fold_from_raw_` and the fused buffers. It also inherits the new DFlash hook, so at cold start its fused KV buffers are built twice, the second time after quant processing.

  A bucketed update of these drafters behaves as on main. LiLiCorr and Laguna are in the F9 follow-up.
- **Hooks that are not safe to rerun.** Every model-level hook reachable from a top-level model was checked for a second run on reloaded weights. These are not fixed here:
  - **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (model, MTP, DSpark): a reload now fails instead of leaving wrong weights.**
    - On main this hook ran only at cold start, so a reload left the mega-MoE experts and the preshuffled attention and gate/up weights unshuffled or stale.
    - With this PR it reruns at the end of a reload. With `fuse_shared_expert`, the first run sets `shared_experts = None` (`finalize_mega_moe_weights`), so the second run raises `AttributeError` in `load_shared_expert`.
    - Without it, the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early (stale experts), and `prepare_attn_preshuffle` / `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` shuffle in place again, so layers that the update did not resend are shuffled twice.
  - **dots3 vision MoE: stale, as on main.** Making it reloadable without keeping the BF16 experts resident (about 11 GiB per GPU on dots3-note-prev-fp8 TP4) needs a loader that quantizes each expert into the fused FP8 buffers as it arrives; that is a follow-up.
  - **Muse Spark NVIDIA: stale, as on main.** The router multiplier is folded once and then dropped, and the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early after dropping `w13_weight`.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 XPU mega-MoE: guarded, as on main.** `finalize_weights` returns early once the weights are transformed. The XPU runtime currently rejects mega-MoE, so the hook is a no-op.
  - **Rebuilt as new tensors.** Kimi-K3 AMD's MLA `_w_fold` and Muse Spark's residual `alpha`/`beta` are re-created by the hook, so a captured CUDA graph keeps reading the old ones.
    - On main Kimi-K3's hook did not run on reload, and Muse Spark rebuilt them the same way from `load_weights`, so neither is worse than main.
    - The DFlash/DSpark (Qwen3, Gemma4, Muse Spark) and Beam DFlash2 context K/V buffers, and Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark's `_context_kv_norm_weights`, are also re-created. The V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads the context K/V buffers, so after a reload it reads freed memory and draft acceptance drops (Beam DFlash2 TP4, split reload: 7.03 → 4.89; MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP8 DSpark TP4: 5.70 → 4.07). Outputs stay correct because the target verifies the drafts. Writing these buffers back in place is PR 5 (`refill_derived`); with it, acceptance after the reload matches the cold start.

## Tests

- Unit tests:
  - `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::TestModelHookOnSplitLoad`: the model hook runs once, after all weights, for a layerwise reload split into two buckets, a partial layerwise update, and a sparse NCCL update in two chunks.
  - `tests/models/test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py`: the MXFP8 context projection matches the QKV projection, following the real load order (post-load steps, then the context buffers).
  - `test_expert_substitution.py`: updated for the Tensorizer path.
  - `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_vl.py`: replaces `test_deepseek_v4_vl_stream_weights.py` and `test_deepseek_v4_vl_rocm.py`. It checks that the VL wrappers leave finalization to the hook.
  - `test_tensorizer.py::test_deserialized_hf_weights_are_ready_for_forward`.
- Run on GB200 (slurm 41251), nightly `dc45a5f552` (this PR's merge base) with this branch at `4df1d673d` overlaid:
  - Passed: `test_reload.py::TestModelHookOnSplitLoad` 2, `test_qwen3_dflash_mxfp8_context_kv.py` 6, `test_deepseek_v4_vl.py` 3, `test_expert_substitution.py` 13.
  - `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_lilicorr.py`: 33 passed after `7e0898bdc` (its coverage test builds the model without `__init__` and needed `_context_kv_proj`).
  - `test_tensorizer.py::test_deserialized_hf_weights_are_ready_for_forward` was not run here: the venv has no `tensorizer` package.
- End to end, Llama-4-Scout BF16 (RedHatAI mirror) on GB200, slurm 41251 (same build):
  - Setup: TP=4, `mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`, prefix caching off.
  - The vision q/k/v are reloaded in separate `load_weights` calls in v, k, q order, through `initialize_layerwise_reload` / `finalize_layerwise_reload`.
  - main fails with `expected Tensor as element 0 ... got NoneType` (the `torch.cat` in `_consolidate_qkv_weights`).
  - This PR: 1047/1047 tensors byte-identical to cold start, and the greedy image+text sample is identical before and after the reload.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark on GB200, head `0403d305a`, nightly `dbcf568821` with this branch overlaid:
  - **Cold start with the DSpark drafter** (slurm 40659): TP=4, 7 speculative tokens, GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy.

    | | GSM8K | draft acceptance |
    |---|---|---|
    | main | 0.9477 | 0.4938 |
    | this PR | 0.9484 | 0.4938 |

  - **Weight update through NCCL** (slurm 40658), with the [sharded-trainer benchmark](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier/tree/sharded-trainer-bench/scripts/vllm_weight_update_client/bench):
    - Setup: server TP=2, trainer `fsdp=2`, layerwise reload, 2 syncs of a checkpoint in which every tensor changes.
    - The audit compares every device tensor with a fresh server on that checkpoint.
    - main: the update fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` (the post-load step inside `load_weights`).
    - This PR: 3440 tensors compared, 0 mismatched, no memory growth.
    - 86 derived tensors are reallocated: MoE kernel scale configs and permute caches, `gemm1_clamp_limit`, `tid2eid`, the RoPE cache and `topk_indices_buffer`. These are rebuilt by layerwise reload's per-layer processing, not by this PR's hook; keeping their addresses is the job of direct reload (#58382).
- Cold-start A/B against the same nightly, on GB300, H200 and MI355X ([comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64357#issuecomment-6512153023)): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Qwen3-8B + DFlash, Llama-4-Scout FP8 with DP vision, dots3-note-prev-fp8 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI355X. GSM8K, image accuracy, DFlash acceptance length, throughput and KV cache size match within run-to-run noise. The dots3 KV cache loss it found came from the earlier dots3 vision MoE change, which is reverted here.
- Not covered: DeepSeek-V4.1 reload (needs two nodes), the drafter weights during an update (the benchmark updates only the target), Muse Spark, dots3 reload, XPU and ROCm reload.

title: [Spec Decode][ROCm] draft_lm_head_quantization for DSpark drafters
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This lets the DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 DSpark drafters use `draft_lm_head_quantization` (#59973), which so far was limited to EAGLE and MTP. A drafter that shares the target `lm_head` then computes its base logits through a private FP8 or NVFP4 copy of that head, while the target keeps verifying with its own BF16 head. It is the vLLM counterpart of sgl-project/sglang#39622.

```bash
vllm serve <model> --speculative-config \
  '{"method": "dspark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}'
```

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X, AgentX, `"fp8"`: ITL P50 is 4.0% lower at TP2 c1 and 2.4% lower at TP4 c1. A trace shows the draft-head GEMM going from 348 µs to 60 µs per step. From c8 up the result is neutral within noise.
- Acceptance length and GSM8K are unchanged within run-to-run noise, because the target still verifies with its own head.
- No new mechanism: the sharing logic EAGLE and DSpark had in common is now one helper, `share_target_lm_head`, and DSpark opts in through `DSparkSpeculatorConfig.supported_options`. Off by default.

## Validation

All runs: MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-edad8b03` (the same vLLM commit as this PR's base) with the changed files mounted, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, InferenceX recipe `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml` (DSpark k=5, probabilistic drafting, `--monokernel`). The only difference between arms is `"draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"`.

**AgentX** (InferenceX `infx.bench agentic`, golden synthetic AL 3.51, 900 s, fresh server per point, one run per point). ITL P50 in ms, BF16 head -> FP8 head:

| | c1 | c2 | c4 | c8 | c16 | c32 | c64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 | 1.89 -> 1.81 (**-4.0%**) | 1.90 -> 1.81 (-4.9%) | 1.95 -> 1.86 (-4.5%) | 2.26 -> 2.24 (-0.7%) | 3.13 -> 3.11 (-0.5%) | 4.67 -> 4.69 (+0.4%) | 9.42 -> 9.35 (-0.8%) |
| TP4 | 1.56 -> 1.52 (**-2.4%**) | 1.57 -> 1.52 (-2.9%) | | | | | |

The c1 numbers match the trace below. At c2 and c4 the trace accounts for only about 0.5% (44 µs per step at c4), so most of the improvement measured at those points is run-to-run variance.

**Draft-head kernel per decode step** (torch profiler, TP2, rank 0, 60 steps). The draft-head GEMM is swapped one for one, and the target verify head (`Cijk_..._BBS`, about 104 µs) is untouched:

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| c1 (M=5) | `wvSplitK_hf_sml` 347.8 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 54.6 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |
| c4 (M=20) | `Cijk_..._BBS` 104.5 µs | `Cijk_..._F8BS` 55.8 µs + per-token quant 5.0 µs |

**Acceptance and accuracy** (TP2, `rejection_sample_method: block`):

| | BF16 head | FP8 head |
|---|---|---|
| AL, AgentX traces at c8 (from `vllm:spec_decode_*` counter deltas, about 112k drafts each) | 3.416 | 3.400 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319, greedy, 2 runs | 0.909 / 0.913 | 0.904 / 0.914 |

**Tests** (MI355X, rebased branch): `pytest tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py`: 54 passed, 4 skipped (the NVFP4 cases, which are CUDA-only). `pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py::test_mtp_draft_lm_head_quantization`, which exercises the refactored EAGLE/MTP path with `"fp8"`: passed. `pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main`, including mypy: passed.

<details>
<summary>Full AgentX table, draft-head microbenchmark, run notes</summary>

| TP | conc | ITL mean/P50/P90 (ms) | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT mean (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 1.99/1.89/2.27 -> 1.92/1.81/2.26 | 78.6 -> 80.4 | 247 -> 242 |
| 2 | 2 | 2.02/1.90/2.30 -> 1.93/1.81/2.27 | 109.7 -> 109.2 | 249 -> 252 |
| 2 | 4 | 2.28/1.95/2.97 -> 2.11/1.86/2.41 | 137.6 -> 143.8 | 152 -> 140 |
| 2 | 8 | 2.50/2.26/3.64 -> 2.49/2.24/3.47 | 215.6 -> 212.9 | 140 -> 148 |
| 2 | 16 | 3.12/3.13/3.78 -> 3.17/3.11/3.78 | 336.3 -> 336.6 | 2030 -> 1999 |
| 2 | 32 | 5.03/4.67/6.02 -> 5.25/4.69/5.89 | 659.8 -> 661.8 | 6485 -> 6527 |
| 2 | 64 | 10.25/9.42/14.29 -> 10.05/9.35/14.19 | 1120.4 -> 1134.2 | 315 -> 321 |
| 4 | 1 | 1.61/1.56/1.80 -> 1.58/1.52/1.80 | 44.7 -> 44.9 | 189 -> 193 |
| 4 | 2 | 1.62/1.57/1.80 -> 1.60/1.52/1.81 | 56.6 -> 59.3 | 191 -> 207 |

At each TP2 point both arms ran at the same time on GPU pairs {2,3} and {4,5}, swapping pairs every point. The TP4 points ran one arm at a time on the same four GPUs. AgentX replays paced traces, so at low concurrency the arms serve different request mixes and token throughput follows that mix. ITL is the speed metric.

Draft-head GEMM alone (`ParallelLMHead` against `quantized_lm_head_copy`, CUDA-graph replay), in µs:

```
TP2 64640 x 5120   M=5    M=10   M=20   M=40   M=80   M=160  M=320
BF16               352.4  96.7   99.4   101.4  107.0  124.2  185.0
FP8                57.0   56.7   57.2   59.0   63.3   71.4   171.6
TP4 32320 x 5120
BF16               183.9  60.5   55.5   59.9   71.7   73.8   136.9
FP8                33.7   33.7   32.3   38.3   38.2   49.2   63.2
```

</details>

## Details

- **Changes**:
  - `share_target_lm_head` in `eagle/utils.py`, next to `_should_share`, installs the target head or its quantized copy, raises if quantization was requested but the drafter keeps its own head, and returns the installed head. `load_eagle_model` uses the returned head for the MTP `shared_head` fixup. `load_dspark_model` passes its vocab-size check as `can_share`. `load_dflash_model` can adopt it with `quantization=None` in a follow-up.
  - `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` accepts `draft_lm_head_quantization` only for `DSparkDraftModel` and `DSparkV41DraftModel`. Other DSpark drafters may read `lm_head.weight` directly: Muse Spark casts its activations to the head's dtype, which would be FP8 for a quantized copy. They are rejected during config validation, before the target loads. EAGLE's `head_dtype` check is shared through `check_draft_lm_head_quantization`.
  - Weight reload and weight transfer already refresh the copy, because `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` and `share_source_lm_heads` run on any `DraftModelSpeculator`.
- **Not a duplicate of #47584**: that PR adds a separate env var (`VLLM_DSPARK_FP8_DRAFT_HEAD`) and a new rowwise FP8 module, for the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4 DSpark path only. This PR reuses the existing `draft_lm_head_quantization` config and kernel selection, so it works on any platform with an FP8 linear kernel.
- **Kernel on ROCm**: `"fp8"` resolves to `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` (hipBLASLt FP8 `_scaled_mm`).
- **Why c1 benefits most**: at M=5 (one request, five drafts) the BF16 dispatch picks `wvSplitK`, which is about 3.5x slower than at M=10. `deepseek_v41/amd/ops/draft_lm_head.py` already pads around that, but only on gfx942. A lossless fix to that dispatch is a separate follow-up.
- **Memory**: one extra FP8 copy of the per-rank head shard, about 0.33 GB at TP2 and 0.17 GB at TP4 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. It is created during model loading, so KV sizing accounts for it.
- **CI coverage**: the quantized copy and its refresh are covered by the existing `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_draft_lm_head.py`. The shared EAGLE/MTP path is covered by the MTP e2e test above. The DSpark path is validated end to end above. CI has no DSpark checkpoint test for it. `"nvfp4"` takes the same path but was not measured here.

title: [ROCm][Quantization] NVFP4 MoE re-quantization and fused shared experts through online quantization
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Second PR of the split of #63232, stacked on #64111. Its base is `minimax-m31-flash-model`, so only this PR's commit shows up; it will be retargeted to `main` after #64111 merges. The change lets ROCm serve NVFP4-expert checkpoints such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: the routed experts are re-quantized to MXFP4/MXFP8 at load. It also makes fused shared experts (FSE) work with online quantization.

## Claims

- **NVFP4 MoE re-quantization without an NVFP4 backend:** main can already re-quantize serialized NVFP4 MoE (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark) to an online MoE method. This PR makes that work where no NVFP4 MoE backend exists (ROCm):
  - The NVFP4 oracle skips backend selection for layers whose checkpoint method only serves as the dequantization source (`requantization_source_scope`).
  - `dequantize_weight` for MoE now yields `(experts, w13, w2)` per group of experts, which bounds the staging memory.
- **FSE with online quantization:** `OnlineSharedExpertLoader` stages the shared expert at load and quantizes it into its routed slot after loading. It replaces `RoutedExperts._fused_shared_expert_quantizer`, which only handled full-precision shared experts. Supported combinations:
  - NVFP4 routed experts re-quantized to MXFP4, with the shared expert re-quantized to the same scheme;
  - Quark MXFP4 routed experts (kept as stored) with an MXFP8 shared expert quantized to MXFP4 online.

  FSE is refused with a warning when the shared and routed experts would not run with the same `(weight, activation)` keys. Two cases raise `NotImplementedError`: BF16 routed experts quantized online combined with a quantized shared expert, and reloading weights with FSE.
- **MiniMax-M3 on ROCm:** a clear error for the NVFP4-expert checkpoint unless the routed experts are re-quantized (`--quantization-config.moe mxfp4` or `mxfp8`).
- **Two small ROCm fixes from the same branch:**
  - gfx942: the online FP8 PTPC MoE quantizes W13 in torch, because `dynamic_per_token_scaled_fp8_quant` can crash there during load.
  - The MXFP8 Triton activation quant uses a tuned block size for M == 1.

## Validation

Pre-commit passes, including mypy (Python 3.11) on all changed files.

Unit tests were run on GB300 (CUDA) for this branch and for #64111 (its base) in the same environment. The changed and new tests pass; the failures were identical on both branches (table below).

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_fused_shared_expert.py tests/quantization/test_online.py \
  tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py tests/quantization/test_fp8_per_channel.py \
  tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_nvfp4_emulation.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py
```

| | this PR | #64111 |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 656 | 646 |
| skipped | 86 | 54 |
| failed | 27 | 27 (the same tests) |

- The 10 extra passes are this PR's new tests.
- The 32 extra skips are the ROCm-only tests in `test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py`.
- The 27 shared failures are environmental: engine start-up on GPUs shared with other jobs (about 10 GB free), a Triton "PTX compiled with an unsupported toolchain" error in this environment, and one out-of-memory error. Three `test_modelopt` failures also fail on `main` here.

Not covered:
- `tests/quantization/test_online_shared_expert_fusion.py` holds most of the coverage of this PR (NVFP4 routed × online targets × FSE for compressed-tensors and Quark, Quark MXFP4 routed + MXFP8 shared, NVFP4 oracle skip). It is ROCm-only, and its CI jobs are disabled (`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`: pending locked torchao dependencies). I did not run it: there is no AMD hardware here.
- No ROCm end-to-end run on this branch. The code comes from the AMD contributors' branch (#63232).

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** #63547 (draft) also serves the NVFP4 M3.1 checkpoint on AMD, but converts NVFP4 → MXFP4 inside the model (`minimax_m3/common/nvfp4_mxfp4.py`). This PR goes through the generic online quantization API instead, so it applies to any ModelOpt, compressed-tensors or Quark NVFP4 MoE and supports FSE.
- **Shared code touched (all at load time, no forward-path change):**
  - `resolve_quant_method` builds the checkpoint method of re-quantized experts under `requantization_source_scope`.
  - `select_nvfp4_moe_backend` returns the emulation backend inside that scope.
  - `QuantizeMethodBase.dequantize_weight` returns an iterator for MoE. All three MoE implementations (ModelOpt, compressed-tensors, Quark NVFP4) and the one caller are migrated.
  - `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` and `load_weights` route shared-expert slots through the loader.
  - `process_weights_after_loading` finalizes the staged shared experts. It is a no-op unless FSE and online quantization are both used.
  - `is_shared_expert_quant_fse_compatible` now compares the effective `(weight, activation)` keys of the routed and shared experts.
  - `QuarkLinearMethod.dequantize_weight` supports MXFP8.
- **Conflicts with main:** main's #61457 (per-layer FSE selection) landed after the source branch. I kept main's `resolve_layer_fused_shared_expert`. The source branch's extra warning, for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` set without AITER MoE, was dropped: it also fires on CUDA, where AITER is unavailable.
- **Docs:** `docs/features/quantization/online.md` already documents NVFP4 MoE re-quantization; FSE with online quantization is not documented yet.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to port these changes from #63232 and resolve the conflicts with main. The original code is by fxmarty-amd (re-quantization + FSE), andyluo7 (gfx942 FP8) and hongxiayang (MXFP8 M=1), credited in the commit. The submitter reviewed the port and ran the tests above.

title: [Perf] Skip custom-op dispatch for FlashInfer dense GEMMs in eager
author: YangXu1990uiuc
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cut the per-call host overhead vLLM adds in front of FlashInfer dense GEMMs (BF16, FP8 per-tensor and block-scale, MXFP8, NVFP4, W4A16) and their activation-quantize ops in eager mode, e.g. prefill without CUDA graphs. Companion to flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7788 (merged), which removed 25–50 µs from FlashInfer's own dispatch.

## Claims

- Eager host time per linear call drops by 31–53 µs (MXFP8 q_b 142 → 91 µs, NVFP4 q_b 130 → 97 µs; table below).
- The same bypass applies to the other FlashInfer GEMM ops: FP8 `bmm_fp8` and W4A16 `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4` save ~10–16 µs per call in an isolated op microbenchmark, and the quantize ops save 2–5 µs.
- Under `torch.compile`, the ops that were `torch.library.custom_op` now go through `direct_register_custom_op`, about 17–23 µs cheaper per call for the MXFP8 GEMM.
- No behavior change: op names, schemas and fake impls are unchanged, eager outputs are bit-identical, and compiled graphs still record the custom ops.

## Validation

Host µs per call (enqueue rate, warm, no per-call sync), FlashInfer cute-dsl backend (the SM100 default), Kimi K3 projection shapes (public config) at M=4096, FlashInfer with #7788. 15 interleaved rounds × 150 calls, medians; IQR ≤ 2 µs.

| path | shape (N×K) | bare FlashInfer call | vLLM `layer(x)` main | this PR | saved |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| MXFP8 | q_b 18432×1536 | 75.8 | 141.7 | **91.0** | 50.7 |
| MXFP8 | o_proj 7168×12288 | 69.7 | 136.8 | **85.4** | 51.4 |
| NVFP4 | q_b 18432×1536 | 63.3 | 130.3 | **97.3** | 33.0 |
| NVFP4 | o_proj 7168×12288 | 66.1 | 134.5 | **101.8** | 32.6 |

The cutlass backend shows the same savings (31–51 µs), and M=8 is within a few µs of M=4096.

- `torch.library.opcheck` (`test_schema`, `test_autograd_registration`, `test_faketensor`, `test_aot_dispatch_dynamic`) passes for `vllm::mm_mxfp8` and `vllm::flashinfer_mm_fp4` as re-registered, with `NvmlCudaPlatform` / dispatch key `CUDA`.
- Outputs of the eager path, the op path, and the direct FlashInfer call are bit-identical (`torch.equal`) for MXFP8 (cutlass, cute-dsl) and NVFP4 (cutlass, cute-dsl).
- `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` over the MXFP8 linear still records `vllm.mxfp8_quantize` and `vllm.mm_mxfp8` without graph breaks.

The second commit extends this to every FlashInfer dense-GEMM-path op. Isolated op microbenchmark, host µs per call (64×256×512), vLLM main → this PR. `opcheck`, eager == op (`torch.equal`), and `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` still emitting the op were checked for each:

| op | main (`custom_op`) | this PR (eager) |
|---|--:|--:|
| `mm_mxfp8` (cutlass) | 56.5 | 41.7 |
| `flashinfer_mm_fp4` (cutlass) | 58.0 | 43.7 |
| `bmm_fp8` (auto) | 58.2 | 42.6 |
| `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4` | n/a | 68.3 via op → 57.9 |
| `flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize_8x4` | 15.9 | 11.6 |
| `flashinfer_nvfp4_quantize` (8x4) | 22.4 | 17.2 |
| `flashinfer_mxfp4_quantize` | 18.2 | 13.4 |

Already directly registered, now also bypassed in eager (same checks; FP8 block-scale on H100 because the kernel is SM90; the `dynamic_` op was checked for eager == op and compile, not opcheck):

| op | via op | this PR (eager) |
|---|--:|--:|
| `cuda_flashinfer_bf16_gemm` (flashinfer_cutedsl) | 108.3 | 93.1 |
| `flashinfer_fp8_blockscale_gemm` (M=16, H100) | 20.1 | 17.3 |
| `dynamic_flashinfer_deepgemm_blockscale_gemm` (M=16, H100) | 23.7 | 20.0 |

**Limitations:** these numbers come from a harness that replicates the vLLM call path line by line (`ColumnParallelLinear.forward` / `RowParallelLinear.forward` → `ModelOptLinearMethod.apply` → the FlashInfer linear kernels in `kernels/linear/`), on an SM100 part. It is not an end-to-end serving benchmark. vLLM's compiled extension was not available in that environment, so for NVFP4 the C++ `scaled_fp4_quant` was substituted with an equivalent-schema op that launches FlashInfer's FP4 quantize kernel. Absolute NVFP4 numbers may therefore be high by up to ~13 µs, while the before/after delta is unaffected. Relying on CI for the existing tests, including `tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_mxfp8_trtllm.py`, which opchecks `vllm::mm_mxfp8`.

## Details

Root cause: `vllm::mm_mxfp8` and `vllm::flashinfer_mm_fp4` were registered with `@torch.library.custom_op`, the slow registration path that `direct_register_custom_op` exists to avoid. Every eager linear call went through them, plus `vllm::mxfp8_quantize`. A no-op with the same signature costs 8.3 µs as a `custom_op`, 3.2 µs via `direct_register_custom_op`, and 0.15 µs as a plain call. The real GEMM costs 32–35 µs more through the op than called directly, because FlashInfer's Python dispatch also runs slower under the dispatcher.

Changes:
- Add `eager_bypass_custom_op()` next to `direct_register_custom_op` in `vllm/utils/torch_utils.py`. It wraps a registered op so that only Dynamo tracing goes through the dispatcher, where the op is needed as a graph boundary; eager calls go straight to the implementation. `vllm/ir/op.py` uses the same idea for `enable_torch_wrap`.
- Move the FlashInfer `torch.library.custom_op` ops (`mm_mxfp8`, `flashinfer_mm_fp4`, `bmm_fp8`, `flashinfer_mm_bf16_fp4`, `flashinfer_mxfp4_quantize`, `flashinfer_nvfp4_quantize`, `flashinfer_mxfp8_quantize_8x4`) to `direct_register_custom_op`, keeping the same names, schemas and fake impls, and call them through the bypass. Do the same for the already directly-registered BF16 (`cuda_flashinfer_bf16_gemm`) and FP8 block-scale ops, and for `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`.
- Cache the "use FlashInfer's MXFP8 quantize or fall back" decision (2 imports, a capability query and `has_flashinfer()` per call).

Not included, because these change semantics or are out of scope:
- `skip_check=True` on the FlashInfer GEMM, which would save a further 8–15 µs but drops FlashInfer's per-call validation.
- Folding quantize + GEMM into one op. That only helps compiled mode (~2–4 µs), and for NVFP4 it would hide `_C.scaled_fp4_quant` from the attention/quant fusion passes.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep KV cache zeroing for mixed-precision UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs groups
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Preserve KV cache zeroing when mixed-precision `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` groups are reduced for the scheduler. Resolve the zeroing decision across workers so pipeline stages agree even when only one stage has mixed precision. Split out of #63232 (MiniMax-M3.1-Flash); this change remains independent of the other split PRs.

## Claims

- Scheduler projection preserves the decision to zero newly allocated attention blocks.
- All PP workers initialize zeroing when any worker requires it. This prevents MRV2 from receiving zeroing work on a stage without a zeroer.
- Uniform-precision attention-only configurations continue to skip zeroing.

## Validation

The same regression tests were run on original PR head `998f165a2ab0ce47f63ff280b96a600901c7d914` and this revision.

| Check | Original PR head | This revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config matrix: uniform, mixed first stage, mixed second stage | 1 passed, 2 failed (`False is True` on a uniform worker) | 3 passed |
| Related scheduler, Mamba, and PP config tests | Not rerun | 7 passed |
| Qwen3-0.6B, MRV2, PP=2, FP8 KV, BF16 layer 0 | Worker_PP1 asserted that `kv_block_zeroer` is not None; first completion returned HTTP 500 | 1 passed; PP=2 and PP=1 first-token top-5 logprobs match at the helper's precision |
| Pre-commit on the seven changed files | Not rerun | Passed |

CPU commands (with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''`):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config_keeps_zeroing -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  -k 'test_generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config or test_wrapped_mamba_group_requires_block_zeroing or test_get_kv_cache_configs_pp_sharding' -q
```

GPU command, run through Slurm with two visible GB200 GPUs and cached real weights (before: job 40854, 1 failed; after: job 40859, 1 passed in 171.17 s):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=$PWD CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pipeline_parallel.py \
  -k test_pp_mixed_precision_kv_cache -v -s --tb=short
```

The regression compares PP=2 against PP=1 using the existing `generate_close` helper: greedy first-token top-5 logprobs rounded to two decimal places. Both revisions use the same existing native build. This validates the Python configuration/zeroing path with Qwen, not MiniMax native operators or model accuracy on a benchmark. No performance claim is made.

The E2E test is included in the existing pipeline/context parallelism CI steps, with dependencies added for the changed core files. NVIDIA coverage is in the existing optional nightly step; AMD coverage uses its existing PR step. AMD was not run locally.

## Details

`generate_scheduler_kv_cache_config` reduces each `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` to one layer spec. Recomputing mixed precision after that reduction loses information. Saving only worker 0's mixed-precision result also leaves PP workers inconsistent: a uniform stage skips zeroer initialization although it receives the scheduler's `new_block_ids_to_zero`.

`has_mixed_precision_kv_cache` remains a local fact. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` becomes a stored execution decision, initialized from each worker's full configuration. The planner ORs that decision across workers after final replanning, and scheduler projection preserves it through deepcopy. The tradeoff is that uniform stages also zero new attention blocks when another stage requires zeroing.

This extends the metadata-preservation fix in #49623 to intra-group precision and PP worker agreement. It is not a duplicate of the open fixes for transfer destinations/tails (#62313, #55085), backend-specific block reuse (#58716), or initial allocation zero fill (#59432).

AI assistance was used: Claude for the original split, and OpenAI Codex for this follow-up implementation, regression tests, and validation.

title: [XPU][Perf] Reuse GDN metadata across KV cache groups on XPU
author: gc-fu
body:
## Overview

Let XPU use the existing Model Runner V2 path that reuses GDN attention metadata across KV cache groups (#58762). Both the reuse path and the aligned state index precompute it depends on in mamba `align` mode were limited to CUDA; this PR allows XPU in both checks.

## Claims

- On XPU, hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 family) build GDN metadata once per KV cache spec per step and re-gather state indices for the other groups via `update_block_table()`, as on CUDA. With 3 GDN KV cache groups, 2 of 3 metadata builds per step are replaced.
- Outputs are unchanged.

## Validation

Intel Arc Pro B70, MTP with `num_speculative_tokens=3`, eager mode, prefix caching on (mamba `align` mode), greedy decoding with `logprobs=1`. GDN metadata calls were counted inside the workers; baseline is unmodified main.

| Model | Config | GDN `build()` calls (baseline → this PR) | `update_block_table()` calls | Outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | TP=1, bf16, B1+B8 | 819 → 273 | 0 → 546 | tokens and logprobs identical across 5 processes |
| Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 | TP=2, B1+B8, per worker | 2133 → 711 | 0 → 1422 | tokens identical across 4 processes; B8 logprobs identical; B1 max logprob difference 0.093, baseline-vs-baseline 0.075 |

Throughput on Qwen3.5-0.8B (128 input / 64 output tokens, median of 5 runs per process, A-B-B-A process order):

| Batch | Baseline (A1 / A2) | This PR (B1 / B2) | Paired change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 183.5 / 181.1 tok/s | 189.4 / 192.1 tok/s | +3.2% / +6.1% |
| 8 | 1329.9 / 1342.0 tok/s | 1404.9 / 1399.1 tok/s | +5.7% / +4.3% |

Run-to-run variation within a process was up to 5%. On Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 the throughput difference was within run-to-run noise.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py
# 70 passed, 36 skipped (existing CUDA-only cases)
```

Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passed.

## Details

`GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.supports_update_block_table` required `device.type == "cuda"`. In mamba `align` mode, `update_block_table()` reads the indices produced by `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.compute_aligned_state_indices()`, which asserted `seq_lens.is_cuda`. Qwen3.5 uses `align` mode by default when prefix caching is enabled, so allowing XPU only in the first check fails at that assert. The precompute is a Triton kernel and runs unchanged on XPU; identical outputs above confirm the indices match the per-group build.

No new test is added: the existing builder tests that cover `update_block_table()` are device-independent and pass, and there is no existing unit test for the precompute numerics; the change only widens two device checks, and the end-to-end comparison above exercises both on XPU.

#58851 moves this sharing into the builder and drops the CUDA check for sharing itself, but keeps the aligned-index precompute CUDA-only. This PR is independent of it; the `compute_aligned_state_indices()` change is still needed for XPU in `align` mode either way.

Limitations: XPU only (no CUDA behavior change), eager mode only; graph mode was not exercised.

title: [Perf][Qwen3.5] (NVIDIA-only) Fused norm+quant and gate+quant
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fuse quantization into RMSNorm and attention output.

| producer | consumer (quant key) | kernel |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma add-RMSNorm | attn `qkv_proj`, GDN `in_proj_qkvz` (static FP8 or NVFP4) | new Triton `gemma_add_rms_norm_quant`; for GDN it also writes the bf16 normed input that `in_proj_ba` reads |
| post-attention Gemma add-RMSNorm | MLP `gate_up_proj` (NVFP4 or static FP8). Only used by dense layers | same kernel |
| GDN gated RMSNorm | `out_proj` (static FP8) | FP8-output option on `fused_gdn_gated_rms_norm` |
| attention sigmoid output gate | `o_proj` (static FP8) | FP8-output option on `fused_sigmoid_gate_mul` |

Related:
- #56530 (AR+norm+quant at TP>1, complementary)
- #61073 (same contract for generic `RMSNorm`)
- #45364 / #45855 / #42469 / #61783 / #59553 (other norm+quant fusion efforts).

No open PR covers the Qwen3.5 NVIDIA no-compile path.

**Which checkpoints engage (first-party census)**

| checkpoint | quant layout | fusions engaged |
|---|---|---|
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | attn q/k/v/o + GDN in_qkv/z/out static FP8; MLP NVFP4 g16 | all four (192 quant kernels/step, runtime-verified) |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4` | attn/GDN static FP8; MoE experts NVFP4 | the three FP8 fusions (post-attn norm feeds the bf16 router) |
| `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` | dynamic per-token FP8; MLP NVFP4 | NVFP4 norm fusion only |
| `nvidia/Qwen3.5-122B/397B NVFP4` | experts-only NVFP4 | none
| official `Qwen/Qwen3.5-*-FP8`, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-*-FP8` | block-FP8 128x128, dynamic | none |

## Claims

- **1.7–2.0× faster than the unfused norm+quant chain** at decode batch sizes and **1.1–1.6×** at large M, for every fused kernel at every M from 1 to 8192.
- **2.2–6.7% lower TPOT** serving `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` on B300 at TP1 (up to 6.5% at TP2 c64)
- **Unchanged accuracy**: full GSM8K within noise of main.
- Everything that does not match the contract (block/per-token/dynamic FP8, padded NVFP4, BF16, W4A16, LoRA, MoE router input) keeps the existing path, verified by the audit matrix in Details.

## Validation

### Microbenchmarks

- GB300, FlashInfer CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2 (rotating buffers > 3× L2); real checkpoint norm weights and scales; median of 5 shuffled processes (range < 2%).
- Unfused is the serving chain: in-place `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` (or the existing gated-norm/gate kernel) + `scaled_fp8_quant` / `scaled_fp4_quant`.

**attn in-norm + FP8 (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.64 | 2.69 | 1.73× |
| 32 | 5.12 | 2.66 | 1.92× |
| 512 | 8.29 | 5.44 | 1.52× |
| 8192 | 71.23 | 44.03 | 1.62× |

**GDN in-norm + FP8 + bf16 y (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.67 | 2.75 | 1.70× |
| 32 | 5.15 | 2.75 | 1.87× |
| 512 | 8.32 | 5.95 | 1.40× |
| 8192 | 71.23 | 56.51 | 1.26× |

**post-norm + NVFP4 (5120)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.42 | 3.26 | 1.36× |
| 32 | 4.99 | 3.30 | 1.51× |
| 512 | 7.87 | 6.85 | 1.15× |
| 8192 | 69.60 | 50.02 | 1.39× |

**gated norm + FP8 (6144)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.81 | 1.89 | 2.02× |
| 32 | 4.19 | 2.27 | 1.85× |
| 512 | 10.66 | 7.71 | 1.38× |
| 8192 | 78.37 | 52.35 | 1.50× |

**gate + FP8 (6144)**

| M | Unfused (µs) | Fused (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.71 | 1.92 | 1.93× |
| 32 | 4.00 | 2.05 | 1.95× |
| 512 | 7.55 | 4.58 | 1.65× |
| 8192 | 69.12 | 42.24 | 1.64× |

Fused outputs match the chain: residual bitwise, bf16 y within 1 ulp (different sum-of-squares reduction order), FP8/FP4 codes within 1 step (≤1e-4 of elements; bitwise on B300 — not guaranteed across archs).

### E2E perf

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, B300, random 8k/1k, 10 warmups, c1 × 32 / c16 × 160 /
c64 × 640 prompts; median TPOT. Base is current main (includes #64425). TP1: two runs
with reversed arm order (A B B A). TP2: one run (A B).

TP1, TPOT (ms), both runs:

| Concurrency | Main | Branch | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.263 / 5.263 | 4.882 / 4.934 | −6.7% |
| 16 | 8.756 / 8.752 | 8.065 / 8.264 | −6.7% |
| 64 | 23.246 / 23.268 | 22.825 / 22.663 | −2.2% |

Base-vs-base (noise floor): ≤0.1% at all concurrencies; branch-vs-branch ≤2.4%.
Change is the average of the two runs.

TP2, TPOT (ms), one run:

| Concurrency | Main | Branch | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.135 | 4.070 | −1.6% |
| 16 | 6.209 | 6.063 | −2.4% |
| 64 | 15.637 | 14.614 | −6.5% |

### E2E accuracy

GSM8K, 5-shot, greedy, 1319 questions, CUDA graph, same checkpoint and node:

| Task | Main | Branch |
|---|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 0.9492 | 0.9545 |

Reproduce:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 16384 [--tensor-parallel-size 2]
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-warmups 10 --max-concurrency {1,16,64} --num-prompts {32,160,640}
```

## Details

Dispatch logic
- Entrypoint: `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer.forward`, per norm, one of three paths:
  - TP>1 with the FlashInfer fused all-reduce+norm: AR+norm wins, quant runs separately. AR+norm+quant in one kernel is #56530's scope.
  - Consumer takes `kFp8StaticTensorSym`, or `kNvfp4Dynamic` with zero K padding and `K % 64 == 0` (the norm writes whole 4-column scale tiles): norm+quant.
  - Otherwise the existing plain norm. Eligibility is checked per call through `get_input_quant_key`, since keys appear after weight loading and LoRA hides them.
- The fused kernels assert on layout violations. One exception: `fused_sigmoid_gate_mul` takes a quantized eager fallback for a strided gate view (num_heads == 1 per TP rank).
- The gate fusion lives in `Qwen3NextAttention`, so a Qwen3-Next checkpoint with a static-FP8 `o_proj` also engages it; the norm fusions are Qwen3.5-only. Only the gated-norm, gate and layer-0 fusions engage at TP>1 (65 of 192 quant kernels/step).

Limitations:
- Per-token and 128x128 block FP8 are not included
- The warp-dispatch rule was swept on GB300 (SM103) only; a B200 re-sweep may move the last few percent.

<details>
<summary>Audit matrix, PDL, warmup, follow-ups</summary>

| case | result |
|---|---|
| TP1 `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (the target) | all four fusions, 192 quant kernels/step removed (instrumented) |
| TP2/4/8 with FlashInfer AR | AR+norm on norms after layer 0; gated norm, gate, layer-0 norm fused; per-norm choice, no conflict |
| TP>1 without FlashInfer AR | same as TP1 |
| all-NVFP4 W4A4 | norms → NVFP4 (GDN with bf16 side output); dummy-weight run engages in eager and graph |
| block / per-token / dynamic FP8 | fallback; dummy MoE block-FP8 run: no fusion, no crash |
| NVFP4 K padding or `K % 64 != 0` | fallback (dispatch gate) |
| BF16 / W4A16 | fallback (no key) |
| eager vs CUDA graph | both; QA produced and consumed inside a graph segment |
| MTP / spec decode | target layers fused; bf16 MTP layer falls back (the official 27B checkpoint ships no MTP head, so exercised by unit tests, not e2e) |
| layer 0 (residual None) | plain norm + quant; residual = input |
| MoE (`qwen3_5_moe_text`) | input norms fused; post-attn norm keeps bf16 (router); dummy MoE static-FP8 run engages |
| weight reload | scales read from the layer per call, as in the unfused path |
| LoRA | wrapper sets `requires_unquantized_input` → fallback |
| non-contiguous inputs | fused norm and gated norm assert; sigmoid gate takes the quantized eager fallback |

**PDL.** The fused norm launches with `launch_pdl=True` unconditionally (one fat CTA per
row, `gdc_wait` before the first load, `gdc_launch_dependents` after the stores). A/B on
B300, M = 1..32768, FP8 and NVFP4: neutral-to-faster in self-chain (−0.2% to −15%) and
production-like chains (−0.4% to −3.6%); an adversarial early-trigger predecessor costs
at most +4% at M=128, nothing at M ≥ 1024. Outputs bitwise identical with PDL on/off.
At M ≤ 128 the kernel also launches its dependents immediately after `gdc_wait`,
overlapping the consumer GEMM's weight load (~2% chain win); above that the prelaunched
consumer grid steals SMs (fp8 +4-7% at M ≥ 192), so it is gated by M.

**Warmup.** Not in the dedicated JIT-warmup registry (as before this PR); all reachable
variants compile during the standard dummy-run and capture-size sweeps. The jit-monitor
E2E lane is currently skipped (#49349).

**Follow-ups (not in this PR).** AR+norm+quant at TP>1 (#56530); block-FP8 consumer
contract for the official `Qwen/*-FP8` checkpoints; B200 warp re-sweep; earlier
`gdc_launch_dependents` beyond M=128 if the consumer grid is small; split rows across
CTAs at small M for NVFP4. Also related: #41021 (per-shard FP8 scaling — would turn the
static-per-tensor gate here into a fallback), #41457 (fusing `in_proj_ba` into `in_proj`
would remove the bf16 side output).
</details>

## Test plan

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_gemma_add_rms_norm_quant.py
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_sigmoid_gate_mul.py
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_output_projection.py tests/models/test_qwen3_5.py
  tests/fusion/test_quant_activation_contract.py`: **98 passed on B300**. The new test
  is wired into a new `:nvidia: (B200) Qwen3.5` step in
  `.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` (the tests/kernels/core lane is H200 MIG,
  where this SM100 test would only skip).
- Dummy-weight dispatch runs (eager and CUDA graph): all-NVFP4 W4A4, MoE static FP8,
  MoE block FP8.
- `pre-commit run` on all changed files passes.

AI assistance: written with Claude Code; reviewed and hardened with Kimi Code and a
Codex second-opinion review. A human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and
benchmarks above.

title: [Kernel][DSA] Restore FP32 indexer MQA logits for non-DeepSeek models and add `indexer_logits_dtype`
author: zyongye
body:
## Overview

Bump DeepGEMM to `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` tip `ae4fd25`. It restores FP32 output for `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits` behind a `logits_dtype` argument (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46) and fixes the mega_mhc CUDA-graph replay barrier (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#48). The tip also includes MegaMoE NVFP4 epilogue and BF16 weight-layout changes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#51), which touch no MQA-logits kernel.

This PR also adds `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` (`auto` default, `float32` or `bfloat16`) for the DSA sparse indexer. #61149 had forced BF16 indexer logits on SM100, because that DeepGEMM release dropped `logits_dtype`. `auto` restores FP32 for GLM-5, GLM-5.3 and HY-V4, and keeps DeepSeek-V3.2/V4/V4.1 on main's behaviour (BF16 on SM100).

## Claims

- New option `-ac.indexer_logits_dtype={auto,float32,bfloat16}`. It applies to every CUDA user of DeepGEMM's dense MQA-logits kernels:
  - the DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4);
  - the GLM-5.3 kpool indexer;
  - the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode indexer.
- **Per-model default (`auto`).** On SM100, GLM-5, GLM-5.3 and HY-V4 go back to FP32 logits, and DeepSeek-V3.2/V4/V4.1 keep main's BF16. Against an FP64 reference on GB300, FP32 logits select the exact top-2048. BF16 logits change 0.4–0.75% of the selected tokens.
  - The DeepSeek default is set in the `DeepseekV32ForCausalLM` and `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMConfig` config hooks. GLM-5 runs the DeepSeek-V3.2 model class, so the default is keyed on the architecture name rather than on the layer.
  - Indexer models without a hook resolve `auto` to FP32. An explicit `float32` or `bfloat16` overrides the model default.
- **SM90/SM120 behaviour is unchanged by default**, for every model including DeepSeek. These architectures always produced FP32; `bfloat16` is now also available there.
- With the default top-k backend (`auto`), FP32 decode logits skip the `as_fp32_logits` upcast that main launches on SM100.
- `bfloat16` keeps main's current SM100 behaviour: BF16 head weights, BF16 reduction, and DeepSelect ranking BF16 logits directly.
- The sparse MQA-logits path (`indexer_sparse_logits`) is unchanged and always BF16.

## Validation

The unit tests and the logits table are from 1x GB300 (SM100 family) at the earlier pin `9918052`; `ae4fd25` changes only MegaMoE on top of it. The tests marked "at ae4fd25" and the GLM-5.3 eval ran on GB200 at the current pin.

**Unit tests.** `test_deepgemm_fp8_mqa_logits` and `test_deepgemm_fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` are now parametrized over both logits dtypes and assert the output dtype.

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                                  # 13 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -k sparse_mqa_logits  # 22 passed
# at ae4fd25, GB200:
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                                  # 13 passed
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k decode_chunk                                 # 13 passed
```

**Logits accuracy.** The script below runs both dtypes through vLLM's wrappers on random inputs (64 heads, head dim 128). It compares each against an FP64 reference computed on the same FP8-quantized inputs. Overlap is the fraction of each row's top-2048 tokens that match the FP64 top-2048. Time is the median `do_bench` µs in eager mode. The BF16 column includes the FP32 upcast that every non-DeepSelect top-k needs.

| Case | Rel. error FP32 / BF16 | Top-2048 overlap FP32 / BF16 | µs FP32 / BF16 + upcast |
|---|---|---|---|
| prefill 2048 q × 16K kv | 6.4e-8 / 4.8e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9959 | 217 / 210 |
| prefill 4096 q × 64K kv | 6.3e-8 / 4.8e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9929 | 1770 / 1645 |
| decode b=64, ctx 16K | 6.5e-8 / 4.9e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9958 | 54 / 93 |
| decode b=8, ctx 64K | 6.7e-8 / 5.0e-3 | 1.0000 / 0.9925 | 49 / 92 |

- In prefill, BF16 is 3–7% faster even after the upcast.
- In decode, the gap is mostly the extra upcast launch; these timings are not CUDA-graphed. DeepSelect with BF16, which skips the upcast, was not timed.

**Per-model default.** `tests/models/test_indexer_logits_dtype_config.py` (CPU) resolves `auto` through each indexer architecture's config hook, on and off SM100, and checks that explicit values win: 30 passed.

**CLI.** `--attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype` defaults to `auto` and accepts `float32` or `bfloat16`; other values (e.g. `float16`) are rejected.

**E2E: GLM-5.3 GSM8K.** `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (FP8), TP4 on 4x GB200, no MTP, at `afb1192fd7` with DeepGEMM `ae4fd25`. Run with `lm_eval` local-completions, 5-shot, on all 1319 questions.

```
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --attention-config.indexer_logits_dtype {auto,bfloat16}
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
    --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=128,tokenized_requests=False
```

| `indexer_logits_dtype` | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` (FP32 for GLM) | 93.10 ± 0.70 | 93.03 ± 0.70 |
| `bfloat16` (main's SM100 behaviour) | 93.18 ± 0.69 | 93.03 ± 0.70 |

- The two settings are equal within noise.
- This was expected: GLM-5.3's indexer selects 2048 pools of 4 tokens (8K tokens), more than any GSM8K prompt, so top-k never drops a token. The eval confirms that both logits paths serve correctly, not that FP32 selects better tokens.
- Long-context MRCR, which exercises top-k selection, is still pending.

<details>
<summary>compare.py (logits accuracy / timing script)</summary>

```python
"""FP32 vs BF16 indexer logits through vLLM's DeepGEMM wrappers: error against
an fp64 reference on the same quantized inputs, top-k agreement, and rough
kernel timings (incl. the FP32 upcast the default top-k needs for BF16)."""

import torch
from triton.testing import do_bench

from vllm.model_executor.layers.sparse_attn_indexer import as_fp32_logits
from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import (
    _ceil_to_ue8m0,
    fp8_fp4_mqa_logits,
    fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits,
    get_num_sms,
    get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata,
    mqa_logits_mx_inputs,
    mqa_logits_use_mx_scales,
)

torch.manual_seed(0)
H, D, TOPK = 64, 128, 2048
DTYPES = (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16)


def quant_k(k):
    sf = _ceil_to_ue8m0(k.abs().float().amax(-1, keepdim=True).clamp(1e-4) / 448.0)
    kq = (k / sf).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    return kq, sf.squeeze(-1)


def encode(sf):
    if not mqa_logits_use_mx_scales():
        return sf
    b = (sf.view(torch.int32) >> 23).to(torch.uint8)
    return b[..., None].repeat_interleave(4, -1).view(torch.int32)[..., 0]


def topk_overlap(a, b, valid):
    a = a.masked_fill(~valid, float("-inf")).topk(TOPK, -1).indices.sort(-1).values
    b = b.masked_fill(~valid, float("-inf")).topk(TOPK, -1).indices.sort(-1).values
    hits = [
        torch.isin(x, y).float().mean().item() for x, y in zip(a, b, strict=True)
    ]
    return sum(hits) / len(hits)


def prefill(seq_len, seq_len_kv):
    q = torch.randn(seq_len, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    k = torch.randn(seq_len_kv, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    w = torch.randn(seq_len, H, device="cuda") / H
    q8 = q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    k8, ksf = quant_k(k)
    rows = torch.arange(seq_len, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    ks = torch.zeros_like(rows)
    ke = rows + (seq_len_kv - seq_len) + 1
    width = int((ke - ks).max())
    # fp64 reference on the dequantized inputs, compressed like the kernel
    # (ks == 0); row chunks bound the [rows, H, N] fp64 intermediate.
    kd = (k8.double() * ksf.double()[:, None])[:width]
    ref = torch.cat(
        [
            (
                torch.einsum("mhd,nd->mhn", q8[i : i + 256].double(), kd).relu()
                * w[i : i + 256].double()[..., None]
            ).sum(1)
            for i in range(0, seq_len, 256)
        ]
    )
    valid = torch.arange(width, device="cuda")[None] < (ke - ks)[:, None]
    out = {}
    for dt in DTYPES:
        qs, wk = mqa_logits_mx_inputs(q8, None, w, dt)

        def run(dt=dt, qs=qs, wk=wk):
            lg = fp8_fp4_mqa_logits(
                (q8, qs), (k8, encode(ksf)), wk, ks, ke, width, logits_dtype=dt
            )
            return as_fp32_logits(lg, ke - ks)

        lg = run()
        err = (lg.double() - ref).abs().masked_fill(~valid, 0)
        rel = (err.sum() / ref.abs().masked_fill(~valid, 0).sum()).item()
        out[dt] = (lg, rel, do_bench(run, warmup=25, rep=200))
    return out, ref, valid


def decode(batch, ctx, block=64):
    q = torch.randn(batch, 1, H, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    nblk = batch * ctx // block
    k = torch.randn(nblk, block, D, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    w = torch.randn(batch, H, device="cuda") / H
    q8 = q.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
    k8, ksf = quant_k(k)
    cache = torch.empty(nblk, block * (D + 4), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
    cache[:, : block * D] = k8.view(nblk, -1).view(torch.uint8)
    cache[:, block * D :] = encode(ksf).view(torch.uint8).view(nblk, -1)
    cache = cache.view(nblk, block, 1, D + 4)
    tables = torch.randperm(nblk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view(batch, -1)
    lens = torch.full((batch, 1), ctx, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    idx = torch.arange(batch, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
    sched = get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata(lens, block, get_num_sms(), indices=idx)
    kd = (k8.double() * ksf.double()[..., None])[tables.long()].view(batch, -1, D)
    ref = torch.einsum("bhd,bnd->bhn", q8[:, 0].double(), kd).relu()
    ref = (ref * w.double()[..., None]).sum(1)
    valid = torch.ones_like(ref, dtype=torch.bool)
    out = {}
    for dt in DTYPES:
        qs, wk = mqa_logits_mx_inputs(q8, None, w, dt)

        def run(dt=dt, qs=qs, wk=wk):
            lg = fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits(
                (q8, qs), cache, wk, lens, tables, sched, ctx,
                logits_dtype=dt, indices=idx,
            )
            return as_fp32_logits(lg, lens.view(-1))

        lg = run()[:, :ctx]
        rel = ((lg.double() - ref).abs().sum() / ref.abs().sum()).item()
        out[dt] = (lg, rel, do_bench(run, warmup=25, rep=200))
    return out, ref, valid


def report(name, res):
    out, ref, valid = res
    f32, b16 = out[torch.float32], out[torch.bfloat16]
    print(
        f"{name}: rel_err fp32={f32[1]:.2e} bf16={b16[1]:.2e} | "
        f"top{TOPK} overlap vs fp64 ref: fp32={topk_overlap(f32[0], ref, valid):.4f} "
        f"bf16={topk_overlap(b16[0], ref, valid):.4f} | "
        f"us fp32={f32[2] * 1e3:.1f} bf16(+upcast)={b16[2] * 1e3:.1f}"
    )


print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), "mx_scales:", mqa_logits_use_mx_scales())
report("prefill 2048x16384", prefill(2048, 16384))
report("prefill 4096x65536", prefill(4096, 65536))
report("decode  b=64 ctx=16384", decode(64, 16384))
report("decode  b=8 ctx=65536", decode(8, 65536))
```
</details>

## Details

**Semantics per architecture**, following vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46:
- On SM100, the head-weights dtype selects the reduction. `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` now takes `logits_dtype` and casts the weights to it:
  - FP32 weights reduce in FP32;
  - BF16 weights reduce in BF16 and emit BF16 logits.
- SM90/SM120 keep FP32 weights for either output dtype.

**Memory profiling.** The indexer's dummy logits allocation is now sized from `logits_dtype` instead of from the architecture. The GLM-5.3 kpool profile also counts the BF16 output alongside its FP32 copy.

**Interaction with open PRs.** #62170 (emit BF16 indexer weights on SM100) and #62172 / #64138 (BF16 input for cooperative / persistent top-k) optimize the BF16 path. They still apply wherever the logits are BF16, including DeepSeek's SM100 default. With FP32 logits:
- #62170's BF16 weights would be upcast back to FP32;
- the top-k changes don't engage, since the logits are already FP32.

**Upstream DeepGEMM note.** vllm-project/DeepGEMM#46 relaxed the shared weights-dtype check. As a result, the sparse MQA-logits kernels, which read BF16 weights, now also accept FP32 weights on SM100. vLLM always passes BF16 there (`sparse_mqa_indexer.py`), so it is unaffected; this should be fixed in DeepGEMM.

**Not a duplicate.** Open-PR searches for `logits_dtype`, `indexer fp32 logits`, `mqa logits bf16`, `DeepGEMM bump` and `deepgemm.cmake` found no PR that restores FP32 indexer logits or bumps to this pin. The related PRs listed above build on the BF16 path rather than adding a dtype switch.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] Sequence parallelism and GEMM-RS for TP + MegaMoE
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds sequence parallelism (SP) to MiniMax-M3 on NVIDIA when running TP + EP with the MegaMoE backend, plus the GEMM-RS kernel for `o_proj` and the dense MLP `down_proj`. The design follows the existing Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1 SP.

Without SP, MegaMoE already shards tokens across TP ranks internally, but then writes its shard into a zero-filled full-size buffer, and the next RMSNorm all-reduces it. So every layer pays 2 full all-reduces: one after attention, and one on a mostly-zero MoE output. With SP, the residual stream stays sharded by token, and each MoE layer does 1 all-gather before attention and 1 reduce-scatter after `o_proj`. MegaMoE consumes the shard directly. The 3 dense layers do one more all-gather/reduce-scatter pair around their MLP.

## Claims

- SP is enabled automatically for TP > 1 + EP + MegaMoE + PP1, same rule as DeepSeek-V4.1 and Kimi-K3. GEMM-RS is opt-in with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`.
- On 4×GB300 with `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (8k in / 1k out, DSpark spec decode), compared to TP4 + EP without SP:
  - P50 TTFT is 14-20% lower at all concurrencies.
  - Output throughput is +6.5% at concurrency 16 and +13.6% at concurrency 64, a tie at concurrency 4, and -4% at concurrency 1 (see below).
- gsm8k is unchanged.

## Validation

All benchmarks were done on a single 4×GB300 node, with `f81a414fae` as the base and `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` (`9e7ebac`). The serve command is the "Single node (TP4, NVIDIA GB200)" command from the [vLLM recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash), plus `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. 3 setups are compared:

- **TP4**: the recipe command as-is, on main
- **TP4 + EP**: `-ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, on main
- **TP4 + EP + SP**: same flags with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1`, on this PR

<details>
<summary>Serve command (TP4 + EP + SP)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1 \
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  -tp 4 -ep --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "nvfp4", "use_prefill_query_quantization": true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER_TS","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
```

</details>

### E2E: SpeedBench throughput_8k

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat \
  --dataset-name speed-bench --speed-bench-config throughput_8k \
  --speed-bench-max-input-len 8192 --speed-bench-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-warmups 5 --sweep-max-concurrency 1,4,16,64 --sweep-num-prompts-factor 10
```

The full sweep was run twice for each setup, restarting the server in between. Each cell is the range over the 2 runs; best (by mean) in **bold**.

**Output throughput**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **410–411 tok/s** | 370 tok/s | 355 tok/s |
| 4 | **1,022–1,058 tok/s** | 928–950 tok/s | 945–972 tok/s |
| 16 | 2,212–2,245 tok/s | 2,254–2,260 tok/s | **2,397–2,410 tok/s** |
| 64 | 3,937–3,938 tok/s | 4,299–4,338 tok/s | **4,896–4,914 tok/s** |

**P50 TTFT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 164–166 ms | 140 ms | **111–114 ms** |
| 4 | 190–193 ms | 163–167 ms | **134–137 ms** |
| 16 | 200–202 ms | 179–184 ms | **151–152 ms** |
| 64 | 289–329 ms | 266–280 ms | **233–236 ms** |

**P50 TPOT**

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | **2.53 ms** | 2.68 ms | 2.76 ms |
| 4 | **3.65–3.79 ms** | 4.30–4.53 ms | 3.98–4.28 ms |
| 16 | 6.55–6.64 ms | 6.52–6.81 ms | **6.12–6.68 ms** |
| 64 | 15.38–15.71 ms | 14.05–14.08 ms | **12.16–12.39 ms** |

As expected, pure TP4 is the fastest at low concurrency, and EP pulls ahead at high concurrency. SP lowers TTFT at every concurrency, with no overlap between the ranges, and widens EP's lead in throughput at concurrency 16 and 64. At concurrency 4 and for TPOT at concurrency 16, the SP and EP ranges overlap, so those are a tie.

At concurrency 1, TPOT is 3% higher with SP. This comes from spec decode acceptance (3.10 vs 3.20), not from slower steps: TPOT × acceptance length is the same (8.56 ms vs 8.58 ms). Concurrency 1 only has 10 prompts, so a small numerical difference in the outputs is enough to change the acceptance length. It was identical in both runs.

<details>
<summary>Acceptance length (mean of 2 runs)</summary>

| Concurrency | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.02 | 3.20 | 3.10 |
| 4 | 3.08 | 3.11 | 3.09 |
| 16 | 3.14 | 3.15 | 3.17 |
| 64 | 3.15 | 3.14 | 3.16 |

</details>

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, chat completions, temperature 0. One eval per server start (run 1 / run 2).

| Metric | TP4 | TP4 + EP | TP4 + EP + SP (this PR) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| flexible-extract | 95.53 / 95.75 | 95.45 / 95.98 | 96.13 / 95.45 |
| strict-match | 95.00 / 95.45 | 95.22 / 95.68 | 95.91 / 95.22 |

### GEMM-RS microbenchmark

```bash
torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -- benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gemm_rs_ar.py \
  --model minimax_m3 --backend flashinfer_cutedsl \
  --m 128 512 768 1024 1152 1280 1536 2048 4096 8192 16384 32768
```

TP4, N=6144. Baseline is the existing unfused path in vLLM (MXFP8 GEMM + `sp_reduce_scatter`).

| M | o_proj (K=2048) baseline | o_proj GEMM-RS | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 36.6 us | 39.8 us (0.92x) | 55.9 us | 60.5 us (0.92x) |
| 512 | 61.8 us | 63.3 us (0.98x) | 64.6 us | 64.9 us (1.00x) |
| 768 | 68.2 us | 67.4 us (1.01x) | 68.7 us | 66.7 us (1.03x) |
| 1024 | 79.0 us | 76.9 us (1.03x) | 79.0 us | 72.9 us (1.08x) |
| 1536 | 101.5 us | 84.0 us (1.21x) | 105.3 us | 82.2 us (1.28x) |
| 2048 | 114.1 us | 90.9 us (1.26x) | 119.4 us | 89.2 us (1.34x) |
| 4096 | 179.3 us | 133.7 us (1.34x) | 191.6 us | 129.9 us (1.47x) |
| 8192 | 271.3 us | 211.6 us (1.28x) | 299.7 us | 210.0 us (1.43x) |
| 16384 | 475.0 us | 363.6 us (1.31x) | 558.9 us | 374.4 us (1.49x) |
| 32768 | 952.6 us | 680.1 us (1.40x) | 1146.9 us | 704.8 us (1.63x) |

M=512-1536 was repeated two more times. GEMM-RS was faster at M ≥ 1024 every time, while M=768 was mixed, so GEMM-RS is only used for M ≥ 1024.

Above 1024 tokens, the fused dense GEMM1 hands `down_proj` an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation`, so the BF16-input numbers above include an activation quantization that production skips. Re-measured with the same pre-quantized input for both paths (range over 2 runs):

| M | down_proj (K=3072) baseline | down_proj GEMM-RS |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1152 | 66.4–74.4 us | 61.4–66.2 us (1.08–1.12x) |
| 1280 | 72.8–74.9 us | 63.6–65.7 us (1.14x) |
| 1536 | 88.9–91.4 us | 65.1–66.7 us (1.37x) |
| 2048 | 109.7–110.3 us | 76.9–78.2 us (1.41–1.43x) |
| 4096 | 173.8–175.8 us | 111.3–114.0 us (1.54–1.56x) |
| 8192 | 279.4–279.7 us | 190.6–192.1 us (1.45–1.47x) |
| 16384 | 534.0–534.7 us | 343.3–345.2 us (1.55–1.56x) |
| 32768 | 1083.8–1087.4 us | 650.4–652.4 us (1.66–1.67x) |

GEMM-RS stays faster at every M above the threshold.

### Tests

- `tests/kernels/test_gemm_rs_ar.py`: extended with a pre-quantized MXFP8 input for both MXFP8 backends. Passes on 2×GB300. CI runs it in the 2×B200 distributed step.
- E2E SP needs 4 SM100 GPUs in one NVLink domain plus the M3.1 checkpoint, which CI does not have. It is covered by the benchmark and gsm8k runs above.

## Details

Changes in `vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py`:
- **Model forward**: shard the hidden states after the embedding, and shard the MegaMoE padding mask once. At the end, all-gather the output together with the EAGLE3/DSpark aux hidden states in 1 collective.
- **Attention**: all-gather the input, reduce-scatter the output (`o_proj` + `sp_reduce_scatter`, or GEMM-RS).
- **MegaMoE**: takes the shard as-is (`input_is_sequence_sharded`), so no shard/gather/zero-fill. The existing `use_sequence_parallel` flag in `MiniMaxM3MoE` is renamed to `shard_replicated_input`, since it means the opposite of model-level SP.
- **Dense MLP** (3 of 60 layers): all-gather, `gate_up` (keeps the fused dense GEMM1) and `down_proj`, then reduce-scatter.
- **Fusions**: the AR + Gemma RMSNorm fusions are skipped under SP, since there is nothing left to all-reduce.

**GEMM-RS with a quantized input** Above its token threshold, the fused dense GEMM1 outputs an MXFP8 `QuantizedActivation` instead of BF16. So `GemmRsAr.apply()` now accepts it and skips its own quantization. The scales are already in the F8_128x4 swizzled layout that the kernel expects.

**Limitations and follow-ups**
- MTP blocks and PP > 1 don't use SP.
- The dense MLP stays TP-sharded instead of adding Kimi-K3's replicated option, since it is only 3 layers.
- The all-gathers move BF16. Gathering the MXFP8 `qkv_proj` input instead would halve the bytes; this is left for a follow-up.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and to run the validation above.

title: [Model Loader] Refill weight-derived tensors in place on every post-load rerun
author: hao-aaron
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep tensors derived from weights (kernel constants, inverse scales, decode copies) at their startup addresses when post-load processing reruns on a weight reload, so captured CUDA graphs read the new values instead of freed memory. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477, rule 3). Builds on #64357 (merged); replaces aoshen02/vllm#180.

> **Direct reload.** #64336 (direct reload core) is now in main, and this branch has main merged. The direct reload tests that waited on it are back in this PR (see Validation). Results marked "direct" were measured with #64336 on both arms, before it merged.

## Claims

- After a weight reload with CUDA graphs on, MoE models whose post-load step derives kernel tensors serve the same output as before the reload. Without this PR they collapse:
  - gpt-oss-20b (TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct reload): GSM8K 0.39 → 0.01;
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL): 0.90 → 0.01 with direct reload, 0.93 → 0.00 with layerwise reload.
- With direct reload (#64336), every tensor the MoE kernel reads keeps its cold-start address across a reload on these backends: TRT-LLM MXFP4/NVFP4, CuteDSL NVFP4 (including per-locality-domain shards), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/FP8, and per-tensor FP8 (including TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor's shuffled weights).
- After a draft-model weight update, the tensors the V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads (DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norms, including Beam's DFlash2 and Kimi-K3's DSpark drafters) keep their addresses. Without this PR, Beam DFlash2 acceptance fell from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update.
- The same holds for linear kernels that derive tensors in their post-load step (CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8, Marlin W4A8-INT8/FP8, b12x NVFP4 W4A16, ModelOpt block-quant), for the ROCm gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER shuffles, Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and the bf16x3 router split, and for MXFP4 MoE on Marlin (gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.43 → 0.00 after a reload without this PR, 0.45 → 0.43 with it).
- Humming MoE: its post-load step runs once per quant method; direct reload refuses it (in main with #64336).
- Across 17 served models with direct reload (3 full-checkpoint updates each, measured by aoshen02), GSM8K holds after every update with this PR; on main it collapses on 8 of them (e.g. gpt-oss-120b 0.80 → 0.006, Kimi-K3 0.95 → 0.25).
- No cold-start change: GSM8K, throughput and KV cache match the base on 12 model/backend configurations, all within noise.

## Validation

All runs are on GB200 with nightly `4b47db922` plus this branch's Python files. "Base" = main `255431b5e` + #64357 + #64336.

**Reload with CUDA graphs on.** Start a server on a checkpoint, then record greedy tokens and top-1 logprobs on 8 fixed prompts (one request at a time) and a 300-question GSM8K slice. Push 2 weight updates through the NCCL weight-transfer engine and record the same again. "Greedy = fresh" compares with a fresh server on the last checkpoint sent; for a same-weight update the fresh server is the one before the update.

| Model, MoE backend, reload mode | Update | Base: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh | This PR: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.390 → **0.013**, 0/8 | 0.393 → 0.413, **8/8** |
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | 2 perturbed variants | → 0.007 (fresh 0.007), **0/8** | → 0.003 (fresh 0.003), **8/8** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.903 → **0.007** | 0.927 → 0.900 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, layerwise | same weights ×2 | 0.927 → **0.000** | 0.923 → 0.910 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8, direct and layerwise | same weights / perturbed | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- The "this PR" MXFP4/NVFP4 rows ran on `a4a859064`; the FP8 rows ran on this PR's first commit (`deaba72c6`). Since then the FP8 and MXFP4/NVFP4 paths changed only in comments and type annotations, and the direct-reload-only branch of `replace_parameter` moved to #64336.
- The perturbed variants flip the low bits of every FP4/FP8 payload and scale the scales by 2^k. These models score ≈0 themselves, so those rows are judged by token equality with the fresh server.
- One perturbed gpt-oss run (job 41424) gave 0/8 against the fresh server. This was not reproducible: three reruns gave 8/8.
- **NVFP4 CuteDSL** is not bit-reproducible across servers: two cold starts agree on 0–2 of 8 greedy sequences. GSM8K is its signal.
- **FP8 block quant** has no per-tensor derived constants, so it is a no-regression row.

**Served reload across models (aoshen02, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6543567448)).** Direct reload, GSM8K before → after 3 full-checkpoint updates, main vs this PR plus the review commits (aoshen02/vllm#227, now on this branch). Model runs used the tree before the final simplification commit, and before the ModelOpt gather-copy fix.

**Follow-up fixes and runs (aoshen02, [fixes](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6561171660), [Kimi-K3 specialized decode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6556376943), [replicates](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6553386769)).** Direct reload, 3 full-checkpoint updates, GSM8K before → after:

| Kimi-K3 specialized decode, TP8×2 GB300 (main vs this PR) | 0.947 → **0.282** | 0.950 → 0.950 |
| Kimi-K3 specialized decode + DSpark (acceptance) | 0.952 → **0.048** (0.524 → **0.0001**) | 0.950 → 0.948 (0.521 → 0.523) |

- Kimi-K3 specialized decode needs `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` and `mla_prefill_backend: TRTLLM_RAGGED` to cold start (also on main).
- The linear-kernel fixes (`41d68f5e8`) add 8 cases to `test_direct_reload_keeps_kernel_tensor_addresses`; the 7 runnable on GB300 fail on the base and pass with the fix (CUTLASS W4A8 is SM90-only, b12x SM12x-only: code-reviewed). Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` (`ddd596922`): `test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` fails before, passes after on MI355X.
- Unit tests on the integrated head (GB300, `test_keep_param_objects.py`, `test_utils.py`, `test_direct_reload.py`, `test_reload_moe_kernels.py`, `test_muse_spark_logits_local.py`): 105 passed, 1 skipped (SM90-only W4A8).
- The two largest drops with this PR in aoshen02's coverage runs (Mixtral-8x7B FP8 per-tensor TRT-LLM -1.6 pt, gpt-oss-20b TRT-LLM -1.6 pt) are noise: over three runs each, the mean change is -0.2 and -0.9 pt (one GSM8K standard error ≈1.3 pt); main collapses on both.

**Regression tests: fail without this PR, pass with it.** Base = #64357's final head `e9e1d3331` (now in main) with this PR's test files copied in, slurm 41676. This PR = `dc4d86041`, slurm 41675; the later main merge does not change this PR's code.
