It uses Qwen3-4B + `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16`, the pair the other tests in that directory use. `test_reload_moe_kernels.py` uses real weights and one engine start; Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 is already used on B200 CI by the GSM8K MoE eval (`moe-refactor-dp-ep/config-b200.txt`), so it is likely cached.

**Draft-model weight update with CUDA graphs on** (MRV2, which captures the speculator's context K/V step in a FULL graph). Two same-weight draft updates go over NCCL through `/start_draft_weight_update` (the verifier trainer with its start call pointed at the draft route). Measured: acceptance length on a 300-question GSM8K slice before and after the update, plus greedy tokens on 8 prompts.

| Target + drafter | Base: acceptance pre → post | This PR: acceptance pre → post | Greedy post = pre |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B + `z-lab/Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` (TP1, 16 tokens) | 4.1456 → 4.1461 | 4.1465 → 4.1461 | 8/8 both |
| Qwen3.8-27B + `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (TP1, 7 tokens) | 6.0167 → 6.0167 | 6.0167 → 6.0167 | 8/8 both |
- **Why acceptance holds on the base for the Qwen3 drafters:** a same-weight update writes identical bytes, and the freed buffers the graph still reads keep them until something reuses that memory. The address test above catches the move deterministically.
- **Beam DFlash2:** like the Qwen3 drafters on the base, it rebuilds its context K/V stacks with `torch.cat` in the post-load step. aoshen02 measured acceptance falling from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update without this fix (`1d14daff1`, since moved here), i.e. there the freed memory was reused before the next forward. Why it was reused there and not in the Qwen3 runs above was not isolated; the address test is the deterministic check.
- **Gemma-4-E2B + MTP (TP2)** cannot be measured: the draft update fails on both base and this PR while loading weights (`size of tensor a (1536) must match ... (256)`). The assistant's draft-dim `embed_tokens` is loaded into the target embedding the drafter shares. This happens before this PR's code and is a separate issue.

**Cold-start A/B (no reload).** Base vs this PR on the same wheel and node, back to back:
- GSM8K: 5-shot greedy, all 1319 questions;
- throughput: `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64;
- KV cache tokens.

A swapped pass (this PR first) runs when GSM8K differs by more than 1 point or throughput by more than 3%. On every MoE row, both arms logged the targeted MoE backend.

<details>
<summary>12 model/backend configurations: all within noise</summary>

Ran on `56836f49f`. Later commits changed the compressed-tensors NVFP4 input scales (now plain refilled attributes) and the Quark FP8 / lazy-fallback paths; the reload E2E rows and tests above cover them on the final code.

| Model (hardware, TP) | GSM8K base → PR | Other | Output tok/s base → PR | KV cache base → PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4 (GB200, TP1) | chat: 0.8976 → 0.9067 | | 10679 → 10706 | 3.286M → 3.286M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8 (GB200, TP1) | 0.8999 → 0.8992 | | 6682 → 6687 | 1.484M → 1.484M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B + online FP8, Triton (GB200, TP1) | 0.8886 → 0.8999; swapped: 0.8992 → 0.8984 | | 5580 → 5617; swapped: 5650 → 5616 | 1.479M → 1.479M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (compressed-tensors), CuteDSL (GB200, TP1) | 0.8923 → 0.8946 | | 7779 → 7718 | 1.616M → 1.616M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (ModelOpt), TRT-LLM NVFP4 (GB200, TP1) | 0.8863 → 0.8954 | | 9078 → 9020 | 3.234M → 3.234M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (ModelOpt), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4 (GB200, TP1) | 0.8832 → 0.8772 | | 7222 → 7188 | 3.237M → 3.237M |
| Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 (per-tensor), TRT-LLM FP8 (GB200, TP2) | 0.9325 → 0.9363; swapped: 0.9333 → 0.9272 | | 4150 → 4015; swapped: 3915 → 4123 | 1.668M → 1.668M |
| Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8, FlashInfer CUTLASS FP8 (GB200, TP2) | 0.9371 → 0.9295; swapped: 0.9265 → 0.9272 | | 3771 → 3503; swapped: 3683 → 3716 | 1.674M → 1.674M |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8 block), TRT-LLM FP8 (GB200, TP4) | 0.9075 → 0.9189; swapped: 0.9189 → 0.9151 | | 3315 → 3257; swapped: 3176 → 3229 | 1.824M → 1.825M |
| Qwen3-8B + DFlash (GB200, TP1) | 0.8878 → 0.8878; swapped: 0.8878 → 0.8878 | acceptance length 4.130 → 4.128; swapped: 4.130 → 4.130 | 3813 → 4082; swapped: 4064 → 3979 | 946k → 946k |
| Gemma-4-E2B-it + MTP assistant (GB200, TP2) | chat: 0.5861 → 0.5868; swapped: 0.5861 → 0.5868 | acceptance length 3.679 → 3.680; swapped: 3.679 → 3.680 | 11407 → 10575; swapped: 11500 → 11558 | 8.934M → 8.934M |
| Muse Spark open 816B NVFP4 + DSpark, TRT-LLM NVFP4 (GB200, TP4) | 0.9507 → 0.9530; swapped: 0.9522 → 0.9530 | acceptance length 3.951 → 3.945; swapped: 3.945 → 3.952 | 1641 → 1549; swapped: 1603 → 1622 | 84k → 84k |

- **Noise floor:** ±2% throughput, ±0.1 GSM8K points (base = PR on Qwen3-8B, job 41260). Every difference beyond it reverses or disappears in the swapped pass.
- **KV cache:** within 300 tokens on every row (GLM +273, Gemma-4 MTP +112), identical elsewhere.
- **Chat GSM8K:** gpt-oss and Gemma-4 report GSM8K through chat completions. Through plain completions they score 0.32 and 0.06, with the same base/PR match.
- **Not selectable:** gpt-oss with `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass` fails at startup on both arms.
- **Not run:** Kimi-K3 (no weights cached; TP8/16), W4A8 (no checkpoint), Laguna / Gemma4 DSpark / LiLiCorr (no checkpoints), Quark / INC (AMD only).

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `process_weights_after_loading` reruns on every reload (#64357), in both layerwise and direct mode. Many quant methods and models build tensors from the weights there as new allocations: kernel constants (SwiGLU alpha/beta/clamp folded by `g1_alphas`, `g1_scale_c`, inverse activation scales), experts objects rebuilt with fresh constants, decode-path copies. Captured CUDA graphs keep the startup pointers, so after a reload they read freed memory. Every weight is reloaded correctly, so comparing weight values cannot see it.

**Fix.**
- `replace_parameter` already refills parameters in place (unchanged here).
- `refill_derived(obj, name, tensor)` (new) refills a plain attribute in place when shape, dtype and device match, else replaces it. It never creates a parameter, and the held tensor must own its storage.
- MoE experts objects list the tensors their kernels read in `kept_constants`. `keep_constants(layer)` keeps them on the layer and points the new object at them. `FallbackExperts` forwards it to both wrapped experts.

<details>
<summary>Sites</summary>

- **MoE:**
  - TRT-LLM MXFP4/FP8/NVFP4 constants, including the MXFP4 LoRA experts (which declare the MXFP4 names themselves, since the MRO resolves the base experts' empty tuple first) and their FC1 bias index, now built at construction instead of lazily (Quark NVFP4 skips the experts' post-load step and keeps the constructor's).
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS SwiGLU constants, and `fake_input_scale` on its MXFP4-weight / MXFP8-activation path.
  - CuteDSL `per_token_global_scale` and per-locality-domain shards.
  - CUTLASS FP8/W4A8 strides.
  - TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor: the weight shuffle writes into the weights instead of rebinding `.data` (without alignment padding `w2` is the layer parameter itself).
  - FP8 per-tensor `g1/g2_alphas` and `a1/a2_gscale` (now also Quark W8A8 FP8).
  - NVFP4 `a1/a2_gscale`; compressed-tensors NVFP4 input scales.
- **Linear kernels:** CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8 `weight_chan_scale` and Marlin W4A8-INT8 `input_global_scale` (linear and compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE) go through `replace_parameter`; Marlin W4A8-FP8 scales its weight scales in place; b12x NVFP4 W4A16 and ModelOpt block-quant reuse the packed weight's storage, as b12x MXFP8 and tensor FP8 already do.
- **MXFP4 MoE on Marlin:** `begin_direct_reload` zeroes the storage it views back to checkpoint layout, since the loaders write only the unpadded region and the repack moved bytes into the padding. A stopgap: #64352 records and fills the padding right before the post-load step, which also covers layerwise reload and is what the load plan (#64418) needs.
- **ROCm:** the gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER CK shuffles (`AITER_MXFP4_BF16`, `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`) return the shuffled tensors for `replace_parameter` instead of rebinding `.data`; Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` use `refill_derived`.
- **Fused MoE gate:** with fused shared experts (e.g. ROCm AITER), Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5 and AliceAI pass `shared_expert_gate` to `MoERunner`, which concatenated it with the router weight on the first forward and never rebuilt it, so routing kept the cold-start gates. `finalize_model_weights` now refills `_combined_gate_weight` in place after every load (`test_fused_gate_weight_refilled_after_reload`: fails on the previous head, passes with the fix; slurm 43121 / 43118).
- **Kimi-K3:** the specialized decode's packed MoE front, padded TP16 down projection, and KDA conv weight and norm, refreshed from a model-level post-load hook. The MLA inverse q/k scales. `PreparedMla` keeps the softmax and KV-cache scales as host floats; that is safe because no quant config gives K3's attention a KV-cache method, so its post-load step resets the q/k scales to 1.0 every run (a code comment says so).
- **GLM-5-next:** the indexer's fp32 head gate.
- **ModelOpt W4A16 NVFP4:** the gather copies (Qwen3-DSpark `markov_w2`), now refilled attributes instead of non-persistent buffers re-registered on every rerun.
- **Muse Spark:**
  - The residual alpha/beta coefficients and the NVIDIA NVFP4 MoE constants.
  - The router output multiplier, two patterns:
    - NVIDIA folds it in the router weight's loader (once per load).
    - AMD already keeps its post-load fold on main, guarded by a flag the loader clears, with its bf16x3 router planes refilled in place; unchanged here.
- **Drafters:** DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norm stacks (Qwen3, Laguna, Gemma4, Muse, Beam DFlash2, Kimi-K3 DSpark), Gemma4 MTP's gathered lm_head (built in the post-load step, outside inference mode), LiLiCorr buffers. Drafter weights are updated through the weight-transfer engines' draft target (`start_draft_weight_update`), whose finish reruns the drafter's post-load step.

</details>

**Limitations / known gaps.** Direct reload (#64336) is the target path; layerwise reload is planned for removal (F10 in the #54477 tracker), so its gaps are listed but not planned for fixing.

*Affect direct reload:*
- **Muse Spark MegaMoE:** `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed and drops checkpoint parameters, so a reload leaves the experts stale (or fails to load them), along with the hybrid TRT-LLM scales built there. Same on main. Tracked as F15.
- **DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE (MiniMax-M3 NVFP4, Step-5 NVIDIA): the L2 activation scale is a host float.** The max of `w2_input_scale` is passed by value to the Triton prepare kernel and to DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe`, so CUDA graphs keep the cold-start value when an update changes `w2_input_scale` (QAT-style updates such as verl's NVFP4 W4A4 send it on every sync). Fix: vllm-project/DeepGEMM#49 takes the scale as a device tensor, then vLLM bumps the pin and passes a buffer refilled in place. Tracked as F16; moving the max into PWAL is #64418 L2.
- **Qwen3 XPress:** `XPressHead.build_fused_buffers` builds its fused copies anew.
- **FlashInfer b12x NVFP4 MoE** (SM12x only, opt-in): it rebinds the weight scales to new storage and rebuilds their MMA views and `_fc2_input_scale`.
- **FlashInfer MoE-EP megakernel** rebinds the layer parameters to new adapter buffers on every rerun.
- **DeepSeek-V4 AMD:** e8m0 upcasts, compressor `cat` and the MegaMoE early return; handled separately in aoshen02/vllm#226. None of them runs for V4.1.
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 CuteDSL output is not reproducible within one server, reload or not,** so `test_reload_keeps_moe_output` checks only its tensor addresses (gpt-oss TRT-LLM keeps the output comparison too). The token comparison failed about 1 in 10 CI runs. On GB200 (slurm 41919), generating the same 4 prompts 20 times on one server without any reload, every repeat differed in tokens from the first and 6 of 20 failed `check_logprobs_close` (1 of 20 eager); after each of 10 reloads, 3 of 10 failed (1 of 10 eager), at the same rate. Top logprobs moved by ~0.2 between repeats. None of the 3225 GPU tensors reachable from the model (parameters, buffers and plain attributes, including quant methods, MoE kernels and experts) moved across any of the 10 reloads.
- **Untested in CI:** the Gemma4 MTP, DSpark (Muse, Gemma4, Kimi-K3), Beam DFlash2 and LiLiCorr drafter refills (the CI test covers Qwen3 DFlash), the Muse Spark NVIDIA router fold and NVFP4 MoE constants, the Kimi-K3 specialized decode `refresh_weights` (`decode.py`, `dense.py`, `kda/prepared.py`; validated end to end above) and the ROCm fixes (validated on MI355X above). Muse Spark is the only served row not rerun on the final code (the gated checkpoint is no longer accessible); it passed on the tree before the final simplification commit.

*Found in review, also on main ([aoshen02](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6550731296)):*
- **Compressed-tensors static per-tensor FP8 MoE** fails the first update with `input_scales of w1 and w3 of a layer must be equal`: the loader compares against the post-processed cold-start value. Dropping the check is #64418 L4.
- **`pack_tensors` does not align entries,** so `unpack_tensor` fails with `storage_offset() must be divisible by 8 to view Byte as Long` when a tensor follows one whose byte size is not a multiple of its element size (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Mistral-Large-3, Inkling-NVFP4, Laguna).
- **Gemma-4 MTP draft update** fails with a size mismatch: after cold start the assistant's `embed_tokens` is the target's (see Validation).
- **LiLiCorr `load_weights`** checks full checkpoint coverage on every call; the packed engine calls it once per buffer, so drafts over one buffer fail with `checkpoint coverage mismatch`.
- **CUTLASS INT8 fails at engine startup on SM103** (`cutlass_gemm_caller ... Error Internal`), with or without this PR.

*Layerwise reload only (not planned):*
- **Laguna DFlash and LiLiCorr** build their buffers in `load_weights`, which meets meta tensors under per-tensor layerwise reload.
- **MoE quant configs are rebuilt around layerwise's temporary parameters.** Values stay correct, but the temporaries stay alive (F12).
- **Humming MoE** keeps its once-per-method guard; direct reload refuses it at cold start (in main, #64336).
- **Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 CuteDSL, layerwise reload: output after reloading the same weights is flaky.** It differed from the output before the reload in 2 of 4 GB200 runs (first token changed, coherent text). The direct reload case passed every run. The flakiness is not from the main merge: the layerwise case alone passed on both the pre-merge and post-merge heads. Without this PR, layerwise output collapses on every run (GS

title: [ROCm][UMBP] Support UMBP standalone mode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
author: shen-shanshan
body:
## Overview

Run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on ROCm with the standalone `UMBPStoreConnector`, backed by a node-local MORI UMBP server. The aiter sparse MLA fast paths stay on, and the pool keeps a single copy of the TP-replicated MLA KV.

RFC: #57187

## Claims

- On MI355X, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash runs the InferenceX agentic recipe with standalone UMBP (DSpark MTP, monokernel, mxfp4 indexer). Prefixes evicted from the GPU prefix cache are restored from the pool.
- With UMBP, the ROCm attention keeps `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA` and the NaN-free extra-cache path. Before this PR, any KV connector turned them off.
- At TP > 1, each MLA-style group (compressed KV, SWA, indexer K) is stored once instead of `tp_size` times.
- GSM8K accuracy is unchanged, even with 93% of prompt tokens restored from the pool.
- On AgentX, the gain grows with how far the working set exceeds GPU KV: +46% throughput when it does not fit (TP2 c192), +3.8% when it barely fits (DP2 c256). UMBP adds no overhead when everything fits (TP2 c128).
- No behavior change for other connectors, embedded UMBP, or non-ROCm platforms.

## Validation

Setup: single node, 2x MI355X, MORI v1.2.3.post1 built with UMBP, 128 GiB standalone DRAM pool with default connector options. The engine uses the InferenceX recipe `dsv41flash/vllm/mi355x-fp4-mtp/agentic.yaml`, `override_tp2_c64`:

```bash
UMBP_DRAM_CAPACITY=$((128 * 1024**3)) UMBP_SSD_ENABLED=0 \
  umbp_standalone_server unix:///tmp/umbp/standalone.grpc.sock

VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 2 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --moe-backend aiter --block-size 128 --monokernel \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"UMBPStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mode":"standalone","endpoint":"unix:///tmp/umbp/standalone.grpc.sock"}}'
```

**Accuracy: GSM8K.**
- `lm_eval` with 5-shot, all 1319 questions, `local-completions`, `num_concurrent=64`, `max_gen_toks=2048`.
- The baseline has no connector and runs once. The UMBP deployment runs twice: pass 1 stores, then `/reset_prefix_cache`, then pass 2 restores the same prompts from the pool.

| Run | strict-match | flexible-extract | Mean acceptance length | Prompt tokens from UMBP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0.9212 ± 0.0074 | 0.9204 ± 0.0075 | 3.43 | 0 |
| UMBP pass 1 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9325 ± 0.0069 | 3.42 | 0 |
| UMBP pass 2 | 0.9295 ± 0.0071 | 0.9287 ± 0.0071 | 3.44 | **92.7%** |

- Every gap is within about 1.2 combined standard errors.
- Draft acceptance stays flat. Corrupted restored KV would lower it, because probabilistic rejection sampling keeps outputs exact even with bad drafts.

**Performance: InferenceX AgentX.**
- Client: `python3 -m infx.bench agentic` replaying the `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` trace, `DURATION=3600`.
- The UMBP arm adds only `--kv-transfer-config`. Each arm is a fresh deployment, run once.
- The recipe's own TP2 points stop at c64, where GPU KV holds every session. So the tests push concurrency past that point, in three setups:

| Setup | Code base | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| TP2 c128 / c192 | `main` @ `51c6dfd8c8` | Recipe flags as above. GPU KV is 29.4M tokens. |
| DP2 c256 | `main` @ `77d2790e78` | `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2`, without expert parallelism, so attention runs DP2 and MoE runs TP2. `--monokernel` is dropped because mono decode rejects DP. A `vllm-router` `consistent_hash` front end keeps each session on one rank. GPU KV is 26.8M tokens per rank. |

Each cell is baseline → UMBP (Δ).

| Metric | TP2 c128 | TP2 c192 | DP2 c256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total throughput / GPU (tok/s) | 245.3K → 246.8K (+0.6%) | 179.3K → 262.5K (**+46%**) | 270.3K → 280.6K (**+3.8%**) |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 4,097 → 4,120 (+0.6%) | 2,778 → 3,954 (+42%) | 4,053 → 4,194 (+3.5%) |
| TTFT mean / p90 (s) | 0.50 / 0.96 → 0.47 / 0.87 | 7.12 / 19.46 → 1.59 / 4.18 (−78% / −79%) | 1.69 / 2.66 → 1.40 / 2.47 (−17% / −7%) |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 19.5 → 19.2 | 58.0 → 37.0 (−36%) | 54.8 → 52.4 (−4%) |
| E2E latency mean (s) | 19.9 → 19.6 | 59.9 → 36.3 (−39%) | 50.2 → 48.0 (−4%) |
| Prompt tokens from GPU prefix cache | 94.7% → 94.8% | 87.8% → 88.1% | 92.9% → 93.1% |
| Prompt tokens from UMBP | 0.14% | 4.8% | 0.2% |
| Prompt tokens computed | 5.3% → 5.1% | 12.2% → 7.1% (−42%) | 7.1% → 6.7% (−6%) |

- **TP2 c128:** The sessions fit in GPU KV, so UMBP has almost nothing to restore. Throughput and TPOT stay within single-run noise, so UMBP adds no overhead.
- **TP2 c192:** The sessions overflow GPU KV and the prefill-bound baseline is overloaded. UMBP restores prefixes that were evicted while their sessions sat between turns. That cuts computed prefill by 42% and drains the queue. AgentX replays in a closed loop, so a faster turn issues the next one sooner and the latency gain also shows up as throughput.
- **DP2 c256:** Each rank serves about 128 sessions against 26.8M tokens of KV, so the overflow is small and so is the gain. Both ranks hit the pool, with load split about 50/50.

## Details

**Other backends are unaffected.** The hook's only caller is the ROCm-only `deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`. Embedded UMBP keeps per-rank keys. Every other connector still turns the ROCm fast paths off.

**Limitations.**
- Single node only.
- Without SWA replay on ROCm, the SWA group is stored too.
- Extensible KV cache:
  - It allocates through VMM, which the standalone server cannot map over HIP IPC.
  - Current main turns the extensible KV cache off automatically for UMBP on ROCm.
  - The perf runs still pass `--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache` on both arms. Otherwise the connector-free baseline would get a larger KV cache than the UMBP arm.

---

title: [ROCm][HY4] Use breakable graphs without torch.compile
author: zixi-qi
body:
## Overview

Remove `torch.compile` support from the HY4 AMD backbone and use breakable HIP graphs by default, matching the NVIDIA execution approach. This follows #57526 while retaining graph capture for prefill and decode.

## Claims

- Retain HIP graph replay without compiling the AMD backbone.
- Improve output throughput by 18.7% and median TPOT by 15.6% in the measured C8 decode workload.

## Validation

Benchmarked public `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` on upstream `b91df5a9`, 8× MI355X, TP8/MRV2, BF16 activations/KV, identical prompts and serving settings, and no speculation or prefix caching. Ran compiled → no compile → compiled, three repeats per arm; the table compares medians of six compiled controls and three no-compile runs.
The client streams `/v1/completions` with seeded synthetic token prompts, temperature 0 and `ignore_eos=true`.

| Workload (concurrency; input/output tokens) | Compiled tok/s | No compile tok/s | Change | Compiled TPOT | No compile TPOT |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1; 1024/256 | 36.77 | 42.62 | +15.9% | 26.26 ms | 21.88 ms |
| C8; 4096/600 | 245.71 | 291.59 | **+18.7%** | 30.65 ms | **25.86 ms (−15.6%)** |
| C8; 4096/16 | 42.91 | 44.89 | +4.6% | 132.25 ms | 127.13 ms |
| C8; mixed 128–6144/32–256 | 181.30 | 206.61 | +14.0% | 36.76 ms | 31.68 ms |

The main C8 throughput ranges were 241.71–249.22 versus 286.54–293.28 tok/s. Mixed-workload TTFT increased 5.5% (555→586 ms).

Compilation freezes prefill-sized MXFP8 GEMM tiles into small-batch decode. Without it, graph capture selects decode-specific tiles: `_mxfp8_linear_kernel.kd` summed duration falls **7.534→2.437 ms per rank/step**, with the same 411 calls. Forcing prefill tiles back reproduces 69% of this kernel-time penalty. Both paths retain HIP graph replay; attention and communication barely change. These kernel sums are not wall-clock latency.

### GPQA-Diamond

Parent `f2ba523d67` versus patch `c4f150d739`, same checkpoint: all 198 questions, zero-shot chat, temperature 0.9/top-p 1.0, matched prompts and seeds, 65,536 output-token limit and concurrency 15. Scores use explicit final-answer exact match; blank/unextractable answers count as wrong.

| Dataset | Compiled | No compile | Difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GPQA-Diamond | 91.92% (182/198) | 92.42% (183/198) | +0.51 pp |

Truncations decreased from 5 to 3. Other accuracy discrepancies remain under investigation; this GPQA result alone does not establish overall accuracy parity.

`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_hyv4_rocm.py -v -s`: **6 passed** on AMD. The new default-graph regression fails on the unmodified parent and passes with this patch.

title: [CPU][Perf] Speed up GDN speculative-decode recurrent update
author: ekintel
body:
**Purpose:** Speed up `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`, which runs in every GDN layer during speculative-decode verify on CPU (e.g. Qwen3.5/3.6 with DFlash/MTP).
- Work is split over (sequence, value head, 64-column block) instead of (sequence, value head). At batch 1, Qwen3.6 now has 64 work items instead of 32.
- Each item loads its fp32 state block once and keeps it in cache across all draft tokens. The old kernel re-read the previous slot twice per token.
- The per-token intermediate states, which are only read again on a later step, are written with streaming stores (AVX-512, aligned addresses). This avoids the read-for-ownership on every store.

**Test plan:**
- New `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_spec_cpu`: fp32/bf16/fp16 state; uneven, empty and 0-accepted rows; value dim not a multiple of the vector width. All existing GDN CPU tests pass.
- New `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_gdn_spec.py`: cold-state, 30 layers.

**Results (GCP c4-standard-48, 23 threads):**
- Kernel, 30 layers, 8 tokens: fp32 state 9.01 → 4.91 ms (−45%); bf16 state 4.90 → 2.61 ms (−47%).
- End-to-end, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash2 (7 speculative tokens), HumanEval, concurrency 1: median ITL 127.85 → 120.08 ms (−6.1%), mean TPOT 23.23 → 22.07 ms (−5.0%), output throughput 38.17 → 39.92 tok/s (+4.6%). Acceptance length 5.58 vs 5.53.

**Kernel, batch scaling (fp32 state, 8 tokens per request, 30 layers):**

 | batch | before | after |
 |---|---|---|
 | 1 | 8.97 ms | 5.45 ms (−39%) |
 | 4 | 28.60 ms | 20.77 ms (−27%) |
 | 16 | 110.86 ms | 82.89 ms (−25%) |

 **Accuracy:** gsm8k (5-shot, limit 200) through the full DFlash2 + Qwen3.6-35B-A3B server: 0.290 after vs 0.295 before (±0.032 standard error). Outputs are not bit-identical: the summation order changed, and with bf16/fp16 state the running state stays fp32 between draft tokens within a step.

 **Tests:**
 - `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py`: 224 passed, including the new spec-kernel test with an unaligned state cache.
 - `pytest tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py -k mtp`: Qwen3.5-0.8B (GDN) with MTP, 1 passed.

Assisted by GHCP.

title: [Perf][MiniMax-M3] (NVIDIA-only) Fused norm+quant MXFP8
author: gau-nernst
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Overview

Add a new Triton kernel for fused norm+quant MXFP8. To simplify integration, this kernel also covers additional no-quantize callsites:
- norm+quant before QKV proj
- No quantize: Input norm, final norm, MTP enorm/hnorm

dspark drafter's per-head norms remain on FlashInfer kernels.

## Claims

- MXFP8 norm + quantization: 1.39–1.60× faster than the norm → quantize chain across M=1–16K tokens (launch-bound at small M); 6.46 TB/s at M=16K tokens (~96% of the 6.76 TB/s streaming ceiling).
- BF16 norm: faster than FlashInfer at all but one measured M (plain M=1024 tokens: 0.99×, noise level).
- Bitwise residuals/UE8M0 scales; E4M3 code distance ≤1; BF16-out within 1 BF16 ulp.
- GSM8K accuracy: 0.9360 vs 0.9380 base (1-question delta, within noise). E2E prefill TTFT p50 is 0.4–0.9% lower at c=1/16 and neutral at c=4; decode TPOT p50 is neutral at c=32 and 5.4–9.6% lower at c=128/512 (2 rounds per arm).

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_norm_mxfp8.py -v` → **13 passed** on GB300.
- `pre-commit`: all hooks passed.

### Microbenchmark

- CUPTI cold-L2 CUDA-graph medians, 3 rotated rounds, GB300 SM103, H=6144 BF16 elements. BW counts 7.03 bytes/element: BF16 x in, residual in + out, FP8 out, UE8M0 scales; measured streaming ceiling: 6.76 TB/s.

**Fused MXFP8 norm vs FlashInfer norm + separate MXFP8 quantize chain**

| Tokens (M) | Norm → quantize | Fused | Speedup | Fused BW |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.64 µs | 3.33 µs | 1.39× | 13.0 GB/s |
| 4 | 5.15 µs | 3.26 µs | 1.58× | 53.0 GB/s |
| 16 | 5.28 µs | 3.30 µs | 1.60× | 209 GB/s |
| 64 | 5.41 µs | 3.68 µs | 1.47× | 751 GB/s |

| 4096 | 46.27 µs | 31.78 µs | 1.46× | 5.57 TB/s |
| 16384 | 169.26 µs | 109.54 µs | 1.55× | 6.46 TB/s |

**BF16-out norm parity vs FlashInfer norm**

- This PR also backs the plain BF16 norm paths. Speedup = FlashInfer ÷ Triton latency, range across 2 bench runs; latencies are from the latest run.

| Form | Tokens (M) | FlashInfer | Triton | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fused-add | 1 | 2.91 µs | 2.72 µs | 1.058–1.071× |
| Fused-add | 4 | 3.33 µs | 2.75 µs | 1.209× |
| Fused-add | 16 | 3.46 µs | 2.82 µs | 1.228–1.253× |
| Fused-add | 64 | 3.68 µs | 3.01 µs | 1.223× |
| Fused-add | 256 | 4.80 µs | 4.42 µs | 1.087× |
| Fused-add | 1024 | 11.04 µs | 10.40 µs | 1.062× |
| Fused-add | 4096 | 32.38 µs | 31.87 µs | 1.014–1.016× |
| Fused-add | 16384 | 116.80 µs | 116.16 µs | 1.006× |
| Plain | 1 | 2.91 µs | 2.59 µs | 1.123–1.136× |
| Plain | 4 | 3.46 µs | 2.59 µs | 1.317–1.333× |
| Plain | 16 | 3.39 µs | 2.59 µs | 1.309× |
| Plain | 64 | 3.49 µs | 2.59 µs | 1.346× |
| Plain | 256 | 4.06 µs | 3.39 µs | 1.198× |
| Plain | 1024 | 7.42 µs | 7.52 µs | 0.987–0.991× |
| Plain | 4096 | 20.22 µs | 18.62 µs | 1.086× |
| Plain | 16384 | 61.95 µs | 61.66 µs | 1.005× |

Faster everywhere except plain M=1024 tokens (0.99×, noise level; a standalone re-measure had the ordering flipped). In the MXFP8 checkpoint, the BF16 path serves the post-attention norm (TP1 branch of the fused all-reduce helper), the final norm, and the MTP norms.

### E2E serving

- `vllm bench serve`; MiniMax-M3.1-Flash on GB300; base = `upstream/main`, PR = this branch.
- 2 full runs per arm; ranges shown.
- Decode used the mega MoE backend (`--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`); both configs use dspark speculative decoding.

**Prefill:** PP2 TP1, 100k-token random prefix + 8k-token input, 1 output token.

| Concurrency | Base TTFT p50 | PR TTFT p50 | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 288.0 ms | 286.5–286.9 ms | 0.4–0.5% |
| 4 | 638.2–642.4 ms | 638.2–640.7 ms | -0.4–+0.7% |
| 16 | 1835.9–1836.0 ms | 1820.4–1820.6 ms | 0.8–0.9% |

**Decode:** DEP4, 60k-token cached prefix, 1024 output tokens.

| Concurrency | Base TPOT p50 | PR TPOT p50 | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32 | 7.18–7.61 ms | 7.61–7.70 ms | -7.2–0.0% |
| 128 | 11.75–12.03 ms | 10.72–10.88 ms | 8.8–9.6% |
| 512 | 22.06–22.95 ms | 20.87–21.23 ms | 5.4–7.5% |
| 1024 | 34.82–35.54 ms | 33.68–34.71 ms | 0.3–5.2% |

Speedup is per-round paired (base vs PR within the same run), range across 2 rounds; decode is neutral at c=32 and faster at c≥128, so the fusion does not regress decode.

### GSM8K

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, PP2 TP1 on 2× GB300; first 500 examples, 5-shot, temperature 0, `max_tokens=8192`:

| Config | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: |
| upstream/main | 0.9380 |
| This PR | 0.9360 |

0.002 delta = 1 question, within run-to-run noise; the BF16 norm path differs from FlashInfer by at most 1 ulp, MXFP8 path is bitwise-identical.

## Details

- `MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm.forward` calls the Triton kernel (`ops/norm_mxfp8.py`) via `gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp8(x, weight, eps, residual=None, mxfp8=True)`.
- Non-2-D inputs (the dspark drafter per-head norms, e.g. (16384, 4, 128)) keep the FlashInfer kernels.
- `forward_input_norm` passes `mxfp8=True` when `get_input_quant_key(qkv_proj) == kMxfp8Dynamic` with a supported FlashInfer MXFP8 linear kernel.
- TP>1 keeps the fused all-reduce + norm path; that helper's TP1 branch calls the norm module, so it uses Triton too.
- Kernel: hidden size is `tl.constexpr`; token count is `do_not_specialize` (2 compiled variants total: MXFP8 on/off). Specializes on `None` residual/`sf` pointers instead of constexpr flags; asserts 2-D row-contiguous inputs, with arbitrary row stride supported.
- PDL: every CTA calls `gdc_wait` before any global access, then `gdc_launch_dependents`.
- Model-local to MiniMax-M3 NVIDIA; no new flags or dependencies.

**Duplicate-work check (2026-10-31):** no open NVIDIA MiniMax-M3 TP1 norm+MXFP8 PR found.

| Related PR | Why this is distinct |

| [#62509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62509) | ROCm M3.1; this targets NVIDIA |
| [#61073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61073) | General QuantizedActivation fusion contract, still iterating; this PR uses model-local dispatch and can migrate later |
| [#64723](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64723) | TP>1 Qwen3.5 fusion; complementary scope |
| [#61783](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61783) | Compile-pass NVFP4 fusion; different format/mechanism |

title: [Perf][DCP] Up-project the MLA decode output before the A2A merge
author: whx-sjtu
body:
## Overview

With `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, MLA decode all-to-alls each rank's partial latent output and applies `W_UV` after the LSE merge. This PR applies it to all DCP-gathered heads first, so the all-to-all carries 130 instead of 514 bf16 values per head (Kimi-K3, 512/128). The merge is linear per head, so only rounding changes.

## Claims

- `MLADCPManager.v_up_proj_combine` is set only for the NCCL all-to-all without PCP; symmetric-memory and `ag_rs` paths are unchanged.
- `MLAAttention` and Kimi-K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention` (also the DSpark draft's) use it when `W_UV` is unquantized. On by default.
- Cost per MLA layer: the gathered `W_UV` (+12 MiB for Kimi-K3 at TP8/DCP8, 0.32 GiB per GPU; the local `W_UV` is a view of `kv_b_proj` and adds nothing) and a BMM over N times the heads. Below 8 decode tokens that BMM costs more than the all-to-all saves, so it merges first there.
- Kimi-K3 1P1D on MI355X, TP8/DCP8, decode-bound C16 / C32: throughput +0.6% / +1.1%, 90th-percentile interactivity +1.4% / +2.8%. Decode step -1.1% / -1.7% at 24 / 32 running requests. Prefill-bound C72: interactivity +4%, throughput flat.

## Validation

- Measured here: a new 2-rank test against merge-then-project passes on MI355X, fails with a wrong head order, and runs in the Distributed Features CI steps.
- Measured here: per-layer microbenchmark, 8x MI355X, 96 or 64 heads, cold weights: project-then-merge is +1.1 µs (+4-5%) at 1-4 tokens, even at 8, and -12% to -48% from 16 to 360 tokens.
- Measured here: selection asserts pass; an 8-rank simulation at Kimi-K3 shapes gives both orders the same fp64 relative error, 2.30e-3. pre-commit clean.
- Not from this branch: end-to-end numbers (runtime patch, same math, nightly `3966924d`); GSM8K 0.958 at C32 (both orders), 0.963 at C72.

<details><summary>Tests, numeric check, end-to-end setup and numbers</summary>

Tests, on MI355X with the `3966924d` image and this branch's files overlaid:

```
$ pytest -v -s tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k v_up_proj
4 passed, 31 deselected
```

The `v_up_proj_combine` asserts sit in the three `MLADCPManager` selection tests of `test_dcp_direct_a2a_lse_reduce.py`. Each of the two files has 7 failures that are identical on the unmodified image (an fp32 LSE compared with a bf16 reference in `return_lse` cases, CUDA-only direct ops); `test_dcp_a2a.py` is not in CI today, hence `-k v_up_proj`.

Numeric check. One process simulates 8 DCP ranks with the real pack and unpack-combine Triton kernels: 96 gathered heads, 12 per rank, L=512, V=128, bf16, 5 query tokens per request; the first request has KV on rank 0 only and NaN partial output elsewhere. Error of the merged output against an fp64 merge-then-project reference, as Frobenius relative error / largest element error (output RMS 0.66 to 0.70):

| Requests | Merge then project | Project then merge | Largest difference between the two |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 2.19e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.19e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 1.56e-2 |
| 24 | 2.29e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.29e-3 / 1.90e-2 | 1.56e-2 |
| 32 | 2.30e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.30e-3 / 2.02e-2 | 3.13e-2 |
| 48 | 2.32e-3 / 1.43e-2 | 2.32e-3 / 2.65e-2 | 3.13e-2 |

All-to-all payload per rank per layer at 160 tokens: 15.8 MB before, 4.0 MB after (computed).

End-to-end setup (not run from this branch). Kimi-K3 1P1D prefill/decode disaggregation on 2 nodes of 8x MI355X, TP8 + DCP8 per role, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a` with `VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0`, FP8 KV cache, DSpark speculative decoding with 4 draft tokens, Mooncake RDMA, agentic multi-turn trace. vLLM ROCm nightly `3966924d` with `MLAAttention` and Kimi-K3 `MultiHeadLatentAttention` patched at runtime to project before the merge.

| Concurrency | Projection | Total tok/s/GPU | P90 interactivity | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C16 | before merge | 5,257.4 | 108.0 | - |
| C16 | after merge (control) | 5,227.0 | 106.5 | - |
| C32 | before merge | 10,492.2 | 75.8 | 0.958 |
| C32 | after merge (control) | 10,379.9 | 73.7 | 0.958 |
| C72 | after merge | flat, see below | 38.2 | - |
| C72 | before merge | flat, see below | 39.8 | 0.963 |

Token-weighted inter-token latency: 8.3 to 8.2 ms at C16, 11.1 to 10.9 ms at C32. The control runs used different node pairs from the before-merge runs. C72 is prefill-bound; total throughput was 15,909 and 15,831 tok/s/GPU across the two runs.

Decode-only A/B on one MI355X node at a C48-like batch: decode step 46.5 to 46.0 ms at 24 running requests, 53.9 to 53.0 ms at 32.

</details>

## Details

On by default: a2a is opt-in or model-selected, and CUDA with DCP symmetric memory keeps its direct combine. Both orders round twice to the activation dtype.

Limitations: not run on CUDA, or end to end from this branch; the 8-token threshold is measured on MI355X only. DeepSeek-V3.2 attention and direct symmetric-memory A2A keep merge-then-project.

Related: #48196 (draft, conflicting) puts the same projection, for every DCP backend, in a larger sparse-MLA change predating `MLADCPManager`. AI-assisted (Claude in Cursor).

title: [Perf][Rust Frontend] Serialize SSE chunks before building the event
author: davidteather
body:
## Overview

Build streamed SSE frames with `Event::data(serde_json::to_string(..))` instead of `Event::json_data(..)` in the chat completions, completions, generate and Responses routes. Same wire bytes, 1.9–2.7× less time per frame.

The serialization lives in one `EventExt::json` helper next to `sse_response`, whose doc records why it avoids `json_data`. The three identical chat completions, completions and generate SSE stream functions are merged into one generic `openai_sse_stream`.

## Claims

- Per-frame SSE serialization is 46–62% faster (criterion bench table below).
- Wire output is byte-identical
- Heap operations per frame are not increased (5–7 on both paths)
- Reach: every streaming request on the Rust frontend

## Validation

Criterion, axum 0.8.8, Apple M-series, mimalloc, `critcmp` over one run (both variants in one binary and every case first asserts identical wire bytes through axum's `Sse` response):

| case | `json_data` (old) | `data(to_string)` (new) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| content_token | 504.8 ns | 224.4 ns | 2.25× |
| reasoning_token | 503.7 ns | 223.2 ns | 2.26× |
| first_role | 554.3 ns | 246.6 ns | 2.25× |
| content_escapes | 557.8 ns | 239.3 ns | 2.33× |
| content_120B | 568.0 ns | 305.4 ns | 1.86× |
| finish | 616.0 ns | 254.6 ns | 2.42× |
| tool_args | 693.4 ns | 275.5 ns | 2.52× |
| logprobs_top5_token_ids | 2.13 µs | 799.7 ns | 2.66× |

Intervals were within ±1%, and a repeat run reproduced each variant within ~1%.

End to end, `vllm-rs` + `vllm-mock-engine` + `vllm-bench` (streaming chat, 2048 requests, 3 alternated rounds) showed about −8% server CPU and +6% req/s. That run was on a shared laptop under load, so treat it as directional only. I have no GPU end-to-end number.

Tests:

```
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server                        # 655 passed, 0 skipped
cargo clippy -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings  # clean
cargo fmt --check                                       # clean
```

No new tests. This is a behavior preserving change, and the existing route tests already parse the streamed `data:` lines. Byte identity was checked separately against the real chunk types (above). Evals: not applicable. Output bytes are unchanged.

Not a duplicate: searched open and closed PRs for `json_data`, `Event::data`, "Rust Frontend SSE" and "SSE serialization". The open PRs that touch these route files (#63926, #63739, #61275, #64573, #63481, #58783) do not edit these lines.

## Details

serde_json writes a chunk as dozens of small fragments; a typical 230-byte chat chunk takes 77 `write` calls, 59 of them 1–2 bytes. `json_data` passes each fragment straight to axum's `EventDataWriter::write_buf`, which repeats a newline/CR scan, a flag check and a `BytesMut` reserve per fragment, and regrows the buffer from capacity 0 as fragments arrive. Serializing into a `Vec` first makes those writes an inlined memcpy, and `data()` does one scan and one copy.

The cost is one extra temporary `String` per frame. The event buffer then grows in fewer steps, so total heap operations stay the same or drop by one. Output is identical because compact serde_json never emits a raw `\n` or `\r`.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to find this target while profiling the Rust frontend against the mock engine, draft the patch, and build the benchmark and identity check. I reviewed every line, traced where the win comes from in axum's and serde_json's source, and re-ran the tests and benchmarks above myself. I can answer for the change.

title: [Perf][Model] DeepSeek V4/V4.1 Vision: encode a call's images in packed passes
author: subhashpolisetti
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 Vision run the ViT and aligner once per image, even when a call carries several images. This PR encodes a call's images in one packed pass through `forward_packed`, the path V4.1's encoder CUDA graphs already use. No new flag.

## Claims

- Across 54 multi-image encoder calls, encoding is 2.0–2.6× faster on V4 and 1.6–2.1× faster on V4.1, on two H100 machines. No call got more than 2% slower.
- With the real V4 checkpoint on 2× B200, median TTFT drops from 367–378 ms to 271 ms for 4-image requests at concurrency 1, and from 914–959 ms to 548 ms on VisionArena at concurrency 16.
- MMMU-Pro scores match main within run-to-run noise (862 correct vs 861 / 860 on main; multi-image 75 vs 74 / 75) on a direct-answer setup described below. Startup KV-cache capacity is effectively unchanged in the tested configuration.
- Cost: peak encoder memory per call grows with the number of images, up to about 1.7 GB more on V4 and 2.0 GB on V4.1 for a 32-image call. Output is not bit-identical to the per-image path, and the PR disagrees with main on more answers than main does with itself (200 vs 96 of 1730), in both directions.

## Validation

**Encoder.** H100, FlashAttention, real tower weights, random patches at VisionArena sizes. 54 multi-image calls, 3 rounds, shuffled call order, alternating arm order. [Benchmark script](https://gist.github.com/subhashpolisetti/0f74ea61d8c3dbd32d7e5ef49a235f85). ms is the median across calls, and peak is the largest across calls, measured above the allocation just before the call. Per-image → this PR:

| images per call | V4 ms | V4 peak MiB | V4.1 ms | V4.1 peak MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 59.6 → 29.9 | 141 → 142 | 59.6 → 30.1 | 120 → 189 |
| 4 | 119.2 → 47.0 | 79 → 281 | 118.8 → 57.9 | 132 → 371 |
| 8 | 237.6 → 88.8 | 87 → 450 | 236.3 → 101.8 | 110 → 530 |
| 16 | 483.0 → 172.2 | 105 → 883 | 481.6 → 219.2 | 148 → 1133 |
| 32 | 962.9 → 328.4 | 144 → 1832 | 961.2 → 418.6 | 190 → 2191 |
| **all 54 calls, total** | **2.61×** | | **2.10×** | |

The first version of this PR capped a pass at 8 images. In the same container, the capped version gave similar speedups of 2.55× and 2.08×, with lower peak memory on 16+ image calls.

**Accuracy.** MMMU-Pro standard (10 options), 1730 questions, 138 with more than one image. Real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp`, 2× B200, TP2 + EP, FP8 KV cache, block size 256, greedy, thinking off, no speculative decoding, `max_tokens=32`, concurrency 32. Runs in the order main → this PR → main, with a fresh server each time and 0 failed requests.

| | main | this PR | main again |
|---|---|---|---|
| correct, all 1730 | 861 | 862 | 860 |
| correct, 138 multi-image | 74 | 75 | 75 |

| answers that changed | total | multi-image | right → wrong | wrong → right |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main vs main again | 96 | 7 | 21 | 20 |
| this PR vs main | 200 | 13 | 47 | 48 |
| this PR vs main again | 196 | 11 | 50 | 52 |

Scoring takes the option letter only from the start of the reply or after "answer is"; anything else counts as no answer. That leaves 131 / 136 / 135 replies with no answer (main / PR / main again), mostly step-by-step explanations at the 32-token limit, and the same 2 multi-image replies in every run. Finish reasons were not saved, so I can't confirm each one hit the limit. This is a direct-answer setup, not a full MMMU-Pro evaluation, so the scores aren't comparable with published results.

Most changed answers are single-image questions. Under concurrency, images from different requests share an encoder call, so they also take the packed path.

Encoder-level error against an FP32 per-image reference, on 3 multi-image calls built from 2 real photos, is unchanged from the capped version:

| model | per-image | packed | packed vs per-image |
|---|---|---|---|
| V4 | 3.29 / 3.84 / 5.47% | 3.28 / 3.85 / 5.47% | 0.39 / 1.33 / 0.16% |
| V4.1 | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.02% | 2.19 / 2.03 / 2.01% | 0.04 / 0.16 / 0.24% |

**KV cache.** Startup KV-cache size on the same servers: 202,321 and 202,340 tokens on main, 202,335 with this PR.

**Serving.** Same servers, run after MMMU-Pro, 0 failed requests. Values are main / main again → this PR, one run each.

| workload | requests | median TTFT ms | p99 TTFT ms | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 images, concurrency 1 | 100 | 378 / 367 → 271 | 413 / 431 → 311 | 2.51 / 2.56 → 3.44 |
| VisionArena, concurrency 16 | 500 | 959 / 914 → 548 | 9608 / 1012 → 652 | 10.0 / 16.0 → 24.6 |

The first main VisionArena run had a slow tail and lower throughput than the second, so I'd compare throughput and p99 against the second. The median is similar in both.

**Tests.** The unit test is removed, as requested. It compared packed and per-image output on H100 and passed there. Accuracy is covered by the MMMU-Pro run above.

**Revision.** All runs used the `190df0b900` main wheel with this PR's files on top. The PR is rebased on `bca1bc6516`, and the commits in between don't touch these files. The speedup depends on the machine: my first H100 run gave 2.01× and 1.63× (per-image 44.9 ms for 2 images, capped version, which runs within 2% of the uncapped one in the same container), this one 2.61× and 2.10× (59.6 ms). The per-image path is bound by kernel launches, so it is sensitive to the host. On one H100, the per-image path of the two main wheels (`2abde627d9`, `190df0b900`) differs by about 4%, close to the 2.6% between two runs of the same wheel, so the gap is mostly the machine.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 8}'

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name hf --dataset-path lmarena-ai/VisionArena-Chat --hf-split train \
  --hf-output-len 8 --num-prompts 500 --max-concurrency 16

vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp --port 8000 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 8 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 4 --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 4, "video": 0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config "{(768, 1024, 1): 0.4, (434, 600, 1): 0.3, (512, 512, 1): 0.3}" \
  --num-prompts 100 --max-concurrency 1
```

MMMU-Pro prompt: the question, then the options as `A. ...`, then "Answer with the option's letter from the given choices directly.", with the question's images before the text. The answer is the option letter at the start of the reply or after "answer is"; any other reply counts as no answer.

</details>

## Details

`_process_image_input` loops over images, so each one pays for its own kernel launches through 32 blocks. `forward_packed` runs them together, with per-image attention through `cu_seqlens`.

- **Scope.** Packing applies only to FlashAttention with two or more images. One image gains nothing from it, and I didn't measure other backends, so both keep the per-image path. `run_dp_sharded_vision_tower` and the graph manager's eager fallback are unchanged.
- **Memory.** Peak encoder memory grows with the images in a call. The startup profile run encodes the maximum items per batch, and the KV-cache size above did not change.
- **Rounding.** Each matmul sees more rows, so packed output rounds differently. Together with batching, that can change generated answers; the evaluation above shows more disagreements with no net change in scores, but does not separate the two causes.
- **Not tested.** V4.1 serving and MMMU-Pro (encoder results only), AMD (it shares the helper), thinking mode, DSpark speculative decoding, and MMMU-Pro with a larger output budget.
- **Overlaps.** #62802 has since merged and this branch still merges cleanly with main. #57985 touches some of these files and merges cleanly too. It removes the patch dtype cast, which is why `merge_mask` takes its dtype from the aligner weights. #58782 conflicts in `amd/vl_model.py`. #64435 and #57872 also target V4.1 but don't touch these files.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Keep P/D prompt tails on FULL graphs with adaptive verification
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview On a P/D decode instance with adaptive verification (AV), a step that admits a KV-transferred request runs eager instead of replaying the FULL decode graph, and under DP every rank runs eager with it. This PR fixes the condition that rejects the graph, in the runner and in the EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP drafter: two lines. ## Claims - **Before.** On D, a transferred request recomputes its last prompt token, so it is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts, the shape of a decode row. It still counts as prefilling (`has_prefill=True`). The AV path (#57263) drops the query-length bound for any batch with `has_prefill`, so the AV decode graph rejects the step. The step runs eager under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (PIECEWISE under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`), and the requests already decoding in the batch run eager with it. DP ranks agree on the bound, so one rank's arrival makes every rank run eager. - **After.** The bound is dropped only when the batch is not `decode_graph_eligible` (#58400). That existing classifier admits a one-token extension over existing KV and rejects real prefills, and the non-AV decode path already uses it. The drafter uses the same condition, so it keeps the target's padded layout (#62796). - **Effect.** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark, vLLM P/D recipe settings at 1P1D DEP4. On main, eager steps (about 6x slower than FULL) take 60–77% of D's time, and most of them are ranks pulled eager by another rank's arrival. With this PR all of them replay FULL: output throughput is **2.0x** (OSL 256) and **1.76x** (OSL 1024), and D TPOT goes from 19.2 to 6.95 ms and from 10.6 to 5.69 ms. - **No degradation expected.** The changed value only feeds CUDA graph dispatch, and matching is monotonic: a bound where there was `None` can only add a match, since graphs without a bound match either way. Only AV captures bounded graphs, so dispatch without AV is unchanged. Real prefills (multi-token prompts, one-token prompts without prior KV, PCP batches) still run eager or PIECEWISE. GSM8K and draft acceptance stay within the baseline's run-to-run spread (DSpark and MTP, TP4 and DEP4). - **No extra resources.** No new graphs are captured, so graph count, CUDA graph memory and KV cache size are unchanged. The condition is a host-side bool already computed each step, so there is no new GPU sync or DP collective. - **Trade-offs.** An arrival step now pads its requests to the graph's capture size, the same padding every decode step pays; it is still about 6x faster than eager in the runs below. With D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, arrival steps move from PIECEWISE to FULL; D TPOT is unchanged within noise (TP4 cross-check below).
Code path on main: why an arrival step runs eager 1. **The arriving request counts as prefilling.** `prefill_len` is the number of tokens handed to the runner ([`states.py#L106`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/states.py#L106)), usually the prompt length. `num_computed_prefill_tokens = min(num_computed_tokens, prefill_len)` ([`model_runner.py#L1332-L1336`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1332-L1336)). On D, the transferred KV covers all but the last prompt token, so the request arrives with `num_computed = prefill_len - 1` and is prefilling ([`#L1385-L1386`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1385-L1386)). After that step `num_computed >= prefill_len`, and the request decodes. 2. **`has_prefill` clears the bound.** The runner passes `max_query_len = None` for any batch with `has_prefill` ([`model_runner.py#L1848-L1851`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1848-L1851)), and so does the drafter ([`speculator.py#L273`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/target_dependent_ar/speculator.py#L273)). 3. **DP spreads `None`.** Ranks exchange the bound and keep it only if no rank sent `None` ([`dp_utils.py#L117-L119`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/dp_utils.py#L117-L119)). 4. **AV decode graphs need a bound.** With AV, decode graphs are captured as varlen graphs with `max_query_len=decode_query_len` ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L305-L319)). A bounded graph matches only a batch that carries a bound within it ([`cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py#L130-L133)), so a `None` batch matches no decode graph. Under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` there is no PIECEWISE graph to fall back to, so the step runs eager. 5. **Without AV this does not happen.** Uniform decode graphs carry no bound and are matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible` ([`model_runner.py#L1404`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py#L1404), [`utils.py#L1011`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/be09292f0904ae594c5eeca401a926baefb90be5/vllm/v1/worker/utils.py#L1011)). An arrival row (1 real token + K placeholder drafts) is uniform with the decode rows, so the step replays FULL. This PR uses `decode_graph_eligible` in step 2, the same classifier step 5 already uses.
## Validation All runs use upstream main `b8c04dd3b4` with that commit's precompiled wheel, 1P1D on two GB200 nodes over NIXL, with a fresh P/D pair per run. "Baseline" is that main commit without this PR. ### Performance The deployment follows the vLLM recipe preset for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (`gb300_agentx_pd`, from InferenceX #3941), scaled to one GB200 node per role: - P: DEP4, 64 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, no AV. - D: DEP4, 40 seqs/rank, `max_num_batched_tokens=400`, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with capture sizes 6..240, AV on, no prefix caching. - Both: DSpark K=5, MegaAttention, MegaMoE, DeepSelect top-k, Engram CPU offload. The client keeps 320 requests in flight (2x D capacity). Each request goes to P with `max_tokens=1`, then streams from D. Prompts are unique, outputs use `ignore_eos`, and 640 warmup requests run first. Baseline and this PR run in ABAB order; the table shows both rounds. TPOT and TTFT are measured on the D stream; TTFT includes queueing, since the client oversubscribes D. | Workload | Version | Output tok/s | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ISL ~290, OSL 256, 4096 req | baseline | 4,100 / 4,385 | 19.0 / 19.4 ms | 33.4 / 32.8 ms | 7.4 / 6.8 s | | | this PR | **8,559 / 8,519** | **6.93 / 6.97 ms** | 10.5 / 10.5 ms | 3.6 / 3.7 s | | ISL ~2.2K, OSL 1024, 2048 req | baseline | 8,533 / 8,666 | 10.7 / 10.6 ms | 19.3 / 19.4 ms | 13.0 / 12.8 s | | | this PR | **15,099 / 15,231** | **5.71 / 5.66 ms** | 9.9 / 10.1 ms | 7.3 / 7.2 s | **Why it is large under data parallelism.** DP ranks agree on one graph shape per step, and the agreed query-length bound is `None` if any rank sends `None`. So a single rank admitting a transferred request forces every rank's step to run eager, including ranks that only have decodes. A second traced run of the same setup splits D's steps per rank (4 ranks, warmup excluded). Step time is the gap to the next step on the same rank: | Workload | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | FULL decode steps | Time in eager steps | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | OSL 256 | baseline | 11.7%, eager, 102 ms | **20.5%, 102 ms** | 67.8%, 15.0 ms | 77% | | | this PR | 10.0%, FULL, 15.2 ms | 0 | 90.0%, 15.4 ms | 0 | | OSL 1024 | baseline | 5.4%, eager, 101 ms | **13.0%, 101 ms** | 81.6%, 17.1 ms | 60% | | | this PR | 5.5%, FULL, 16.1 ms | 0 | 94.5%, 17.7 ms | 0 | Steps forced eager by another rank outnumber a rank's own arrival steps 1.75–2.4x. The chance that some rank admits a request in a given step rises with the DP size, so we expect the effect to be larger on the recipe's DEP16 decode (not measured here). The gain depends on how often a decode step admits a transferred request, so it is smaller for longer outputs. In the TP4 cross-check below, D under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with this PR reaches the same TPOT (6.7 ms) as the same D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where arrival steps ran PIECEWISE instead of eager.
TP4 cross-check: P PIECEWISE, D TP4 FULL_DECODE_ONLY + AV, 128 seqs, 128 in flight, ISL ~290, OSL 256, 3 ABAB rounds | Model | Version | TPOT mean (3 rounds) | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 20.0 / 20.0 ms | 29.9-31.0 ms | 1.08-1.12 s | | | this PR | 6.72 / 6.70 / 6.75 ms | 9.4 ms | 0.40-0.42 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 17.8 / 24.7 / 25.8 ms | 35.0-37.6 ms | 1.41-1.54 s | | | this PR | 5.42 / 5.41 / 5.38 ms | 7.1-7.2 ms | 0.37-0.39 s | Same workload with D under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, where main runs arrival steps PIECEWISE and this PR runs them FULL: | Model | Version | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | D TTFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark K=3 | baseline | 6.72 ms | 9.38 ms | 0.44 s | | | this PR | 6.75 ms | 9.27 ms | 0.41 s | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP K=3 | baseline | 5.44 / 5.68 ms | 7.41 / 7.48 ms | 0.47 / 0.39 s | | | this PR | 5.33 ms | 7.19 ms | 0.39 s |
### Correctness Setup: - P and D TP4 + EP. - D: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` + AV, 128 seqs. - The decode-side graph mode is traced per step on all ranks; the ranks agree. - "Arrival step" means a decode-eligible batch with `has_prefill`, i.e. it contains a transferred request computing its last prompt token. Workload per run: - 8 serial prompts (19..8195 tokens), 16 staggered and 32 burst requests. - Two direct-to-D negative controls: a multi-token prompt without transferred KV, and a fresh one-token prompt. - Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 8, temperature 0. **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=3)** | Version | Arrival steps | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 1128 eager | 6 eager | 1190 / 1319 | 1.962 | | this PR | **1316 FULL** | 6 eager | 1194 / 1319 | 1.961 | | baseline, repeat | | | 1187 / 1319 | 1.976 | **DeepSeek-V4-Flash + MTP (K=3)**, which uses `TargetDependentARSpeculator` | Version | Arrival steps: target / drafter | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | eager / eager (1010) | 1248 / 1319 | 1.879 | | runner condition only | FULL / **eager** (1168) | 1249 / 1319 | 1.877 | | this PR | **FULL / FULL** (1163) | 1253 / 1319 | 1.873 | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5), DEP4 recipe config from the performance section** | Version | Own arrival steps | Decode steps forced eager by another rank | Real prefills | GSM8K | Accepted tokens / draft | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | baseline | 5.0%, eager | 11.7%, eager | 2 eager | 1193 / 1319 | 2.067 | | this PR | 5.1%, **FULL** | **0** | 2 eager | 1184 / 1319 | 2.049 | | baseline, repeat | | | | 1196 / 1319 | 2.048 | | this PR, repeat | | | | 1200 / 1319 | 2.090 | Serving with expert parallelism is not bitwise deterministic run to run. Baseline spans 1193–1196 and 2.048–2.067; this PR spans 1184–1200 and 2.049–2.090. Between the first baseline and first PR runs, 45 questions flip correct → wrong and 36 wrong → correct. With only the runner condition, an arrival step replays the target graph padded to, for example, 32 requests, while the drafter runs eager over the 7 real ones on the same attention metadata. That is the mismatch #62796 removed. On this sparse-MLA model it costs no measurable acceptance; #62793 shows that it does on FA3. In every run, all measured requests succeeded, with no preemptions and no KV transfer failures. Pure decode steps are FULL in every run, except the startup warmup steps, which run eager. The GSM8K and acceptance differences fall within the baseline repeat spread.
Unit tests ```bash pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \ tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_dp_utils.py \ tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py # 116 passed, on the branch rebased onto current main ``` - Reverting only the runner condition fails `test_prompt_tail_keeps_decode_graph_bound[True-8]`. - Reverting only the drafter condition fails `test_draft_prefill_matches_shared_target_metadata_shape[decode-eligible-prefill-tail]`. - Both files already run in CI under `tests/v1/worker` and `tests/v1/cudagraph`.
## Details **Request path.** 1. The proxy sends the prompt to P with `max_tokens=1` and `do_remote_decode`; P prefills and returns KV transfer metadata. 2. The proxy sends the same prompt with that metadata to D. D's scheduler pulls the KV over NIXL and marks the whole prompt as computed. 3. On load completion, the scheduler sets `num_computed_tokens = N - 1`, so D recomputes the last prompt position to get logits for its first sampled token. With K speculative tokens, the request is scheduled as 1 real token + K placeholder drafts (`q = K + 1`): the shape of a decode row. 4. The runner classifies the batch and dispatches a CUDA graph. This step is the one that changes. **Root cause.** In step 4, the request is still prefilling (`num_computed_prefill < prefill_len`), so `has_prefill` is True. - #57263 cleared the runner's `max_query_len` for any batch with `has_prefill`, because a varlen decode graph matched on that bound alone would admit a short real prefill. - Two days later, #58400 added `decode_graph_eligible`, which treats a one-token extension over existing context as a decode. Input preparation already handles this case through `prefill_runs_as_decode`. #58400 wired the classification into the uniform decode path only. - The varlen path that AV uses kept the `has_prefill` check. So with AV off, D replays FULL on arrival steps; with AV on, it does not. - `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose` has the same check for its draft-prefill dispatch. **Dispatch before and after.** The red edge is main's path for a P/D arrival step; the green edge is the path this PR takes. Real prefills take the grey path in both. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["D step: transferred request = 1 real token + K placeholder drafts
(+ requests already decoding)"] --> B["gather_batch_req_state
has_prefill = True
decode_graph_eligible = True"] P["Real prefill: multi-token prompt, or one-token prompt without context"] --> Q["decode_graph_eligible = False"] Q --> N B -->|"main: if has_prefill"| N["max_query_len = None"] B -->|"this PR: if not decode_graph_eligible"| K["max_query_len = K + 1"] N --> S["DP sync: the agreed bound is None if any rank sent None"] S --> X["AV varlen FULL decode graph rejected on every DP rank
FULL_DECODE_ONLY → eager · FULL_AND_PIECEWISE → PIECEWISE"] K --> Y["AV varlen FULL decode graph replayed
(drafter draft-prefill uses the same bound and padded layout)"] linkStyle 3 stroke:#d62728,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 4 stroke:#2ca02c,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 2 stroke:#999999 ``` Without AV, the decode graph is matched by `uniform_token_count`, which already uses `decode_graph_eligible`, so arrival steps were not affected. **Change.** - Two conditions change from `has_prefill` to `not decode_graph_eligible`: one in `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`, one in `TargetDependentARSpeculator.propose`. The other edits update comments that described the old rule. - The classifier, scheduler, input preparation, capture sizes and kernels are unchanged. - Keeping the bound only removes one rejection reason. The existing graph checks (query-length bound, request/token coverage, explicit eager, DP agreement on the bound) still apply. - DFlash/DSpark drafters dispatch with a fixed uniform shape and are not affected. - Model Runner V1 does not support AV, so it needs no change. **Relation to #64915.** #64915 contains the same runner condition as part of a larger feature: varlen decode graphs for fixed-width speculation, with new backend and capacity checks. This PR is only the AV bug fix. It adds the drafter condition, which #64915 lacks, plus a regression test and P/D validation with real KV transfer, which #64915 lists as outstanding. If this PR merges first, #64915 drops the overlapping line. No other open PR changes these conditions. **Limitations.** - GPU validation covers DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DSpark) and DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MTP) on GB200 with the MLA backends those models use. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Only set PDL launch attr for MoE top-k gating on SM90+
author: srkim-business
body:
## Overview

Fixes #65055. Since #59737, `topkGating` is launched with the PDL attribute on every CUDA arch. Pre-SM90 GPUs cannot use PDL, but stream capture still records the attribute as a programmatic edge in the CUDA graph, and replaying those graphs is slower. This PR sets the attribute only when the device is SM90+. SM90+ keeps the #59737 behaviour; older GPUs launch without the attribute, which measured the same as the v0.32 `<<<>>>` launch. The standalone effect was measured on sm80, sm86 and sm89; end-to-end numbers are A100 only.

## Claims

- 4× A100, TP4 + EP + MTP (our deployment config, private NVFP4 checkpoint of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; setup below): per-request decode is 6.5–13.6% faster in 17 of 18 prompt × concurrency (1–16) cells, and 2.1% in the 18th. At concurrency 16: prose 74.3 → 80.1 and code 88.7 → 94.8 tok/s, close to the last commit before #59737 (3b05805d4: 81.5 and 95.3, one run).
- Standalone CUDA (no vLLM): the attribute adds one programmatic edge per launch and 0.6–1.1 µs of graph replay per edge on A100 (sm80), RTX A4000 (sm86) and RTX 4090 (sm89), in every round; without the attribute `cudaLaunchKernelEx` matches `<<<>>>`.
- 1× A100, CUDA graph replay of a router GEMM → `topk_softmax` chain: 6.9–9.0% faster for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Qwen3-30B-A3B and OLMoE shapes at 1/16/48 tokens, in every round against a no-change rebuild.
- 1× A100 end to end, `vllm bench latency`: batch 1 is 0.7% faster for OLMoE-1B-7B (every round vs a no-change rebuild, 2 of 3 rounds vs the shipped build) and 1.2% faster for Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 (every round). Batch 16 is within noise for both.
- No accuracy change: GSM8K 5-shot on Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 is 85.90% (base) vs 86.13% (fix). The kernel body is identical.
- SM90+ is unchanged by construction (the same attribute is set as before); not measured.

## Validation

Hardware: A100-PCIE-40GB, driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130, vLLM v0.33.0 (4ba787ec9). `base` = the v0.33.0 `_moe_C` as shipped. `rebuilt` = the same source built with the same toolchain, no change. `fix` = `rebuilt` + this diff. Builds are `_moe_C` only, for sm80, overlaid on the v0.33.0 install. The diff applies unchanged to main (the file is identical).

**Tests**

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py` on A100: base 864 passed, fix 864 passed.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`): Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 85.90% → 86.13%; OLMoE-1B-7B (base model, near the floor with this script) 9.93% → 10.01%. Invalid rate 0–0.8%.
- CI: the L4 (sm89) "MoE Kernels" step runs `tests/kernels/moe` on `csrc/moe/` changes and covers the launch without the attribute; the SM90+ launch is unchanged. No new test: there is no functional change, and a regression check would need graph-edge inspection or timing, which does not belong in `tests/`.

**Op chain, CUDA graph, µs per replay** (median of 6 rounds, A/B/B/A order; Δ = median paired `fix − rebuilt`)

| shape (experts, top-k, hidden, layers) | tokens | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (512, 10, 2560, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 843 / 893 / 917 | 846 / 894 / 916 | 782 / 831 / 850 | −7.6% / −6.9% / −7.2% |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (128, 8, 2048, 48) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 592 / 672 / 688 | 596 / 674 / 691 | 542 / 620 / 636 | −9.0% / −7.9% / −8.0% |
| OLMoE-1B-7B (64, 8, 2048, 16) | 1 / 16 / 48 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 194 / 209 / 221 | 177 / 192 / 204 | −8.7% / −8.4% / −7.8% |

**End to end, `vllm bench latency`** (input 128, output 256, 3 rounds, ms per step)

| model | batch | base | rebuilt | fix | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 1 | 2.952 | 2.950 | 2.932 | −0.7% (3/3 rounds vs rebuilt, 2/3 vs base) |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 | 16 | 7.789 | 7.731 | 7.802 | within noise |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 1 | 5.805 | – | 5.722 | −1.2% (3/3 rounds) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | 16 | 12.188 | – | 12.136 | within noise (2/3 rounds faster) |

<details>
<summary>TP4 setup</summary>

v0.33.0, 4× A100-PCIE-40GB, `--tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel`, NVFP4 weights, MTP with 2 draft tokens, `--compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'`, bf16 KV, a custom logits processor. Client: c concurrent streaming chat requests, 384 output tokens, model-default sampling; per-request decode = (tokens − 1) / (last − first token time), averaged. Prose / code / numbers prompts × c = 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16; two server starts per arm, A/B/B/A. With MTP, c = 1 varies by about ±10% from run to run through the draft acceptance rate.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA reproduction (no vLLM) and commands</summary>

48 × (plain kernel → consumer kernel); only the consumer launch changes. A100, 21 rounds:

| consumer launch | graph replay, GPU µs | eager, GPU µs |
|---|---:|---:|
| `<<<>>>` | 128.7 | 239.8 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute | 128.7 | 239.3 |
| `cudaLaunchKernelEx` + PDL attribute | 181.8 | 239.8 |
| PDL attribute on the first consumer only | 130.3 | 239.4 |

Same harness, graph replay, other pre-Hopper GPUs (21 rounds, PDL attribute slower in every round):

| GPU (arch) | `<<<>>>` µs | + PDL attribute | per edge | `cudaLaunchKernelEx`, no attribute |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A100-PCIE-40GB (sm80) | 128.7 | +53.1 (+41%) | 1.1 µs | +0.03 |
| RTX A4000 (sm86) | 83.6 | +29.9 (+36%) | 0.62 µs | +0.11 |
| RTX 4090 (sm89) | 79.0 | +30.0 (+38%) | 0.63 µs | −0.10 |

`cudaGraphGetEdges` reports one programmatic edge per PDL launch on all three. The standalone harness and the op-chain script are in https://gist.github.com/srkim-business/ec5db57f7b78a9c9f06af65c891216c2.

```bash
# end to end (OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4, batch 1 and 16)
vllm bench latency --model <model> --batch-size <1|16> --input-len 128 --output-len 256 \
  --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 15 --seed 0 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
# GSM8K
vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --seed 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --seed 42 --num-questions 1319 --max-concurrency 64
# kernel tests
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_fused_topk.py
```

</details>

## Details

- Root cause: on pre-SM90 the attribute does nothing for eager launches, but stream capture records it as a programmatic edge (`cudaGraphGetEdges` counts one per launch on sm80). Each edge adds about 1.1 µs of GPU time per graph replay on A100.
- #59737 first had this host check (uncached); review asked to drop it for consistency with `topk_softplus_sqrt` / `per_token_group_quant` and to avoid `cudaGetDevice` + `call_once` per eager launch. The measurements above are the reason to bring it back. It is cached in a function-local static as in `fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert_kernel.cu` (`numAttrs = (sm_version >= 90) ? 1 : 0`), so eager launches pay nothing per call. This also matches the scope in #59737's own description ("Enable PDL for the consumer on SM90+"). Python launch sites already gate PDL on `current_platform.is_arch_support_pdl()`.
- The static is initialized once per template instantiation, on the device the caller's `DeviceGuard` selects. It assumes all GPUs in a process share the major arch, which holds for vLLM workers (one GPU each); a mismatch would only affect speed, not results.
- The 1-GPU gain (about 1%) matches the GPU-side edge cost. The TP4 + EP + MTP gain does not: at concurrency 16 a decode step goes from about 29.5 to 27.3 ms, while 48 edges × 1.1 µs is about 0.05 ms per forward; we have not located the rest. The TP4 A/B swaps only `_moe_C` (shipped → this diff built from the same source); on one GPU a no-change rebuild is within 0.8% (median) of the shipped build, so we attribute the gain to this diff.
- Other C++ launchers still set the attribute on all archs, for example `topk_softplus_sqrt_kernels.cu` and `per_token_group_quant.cu` (the latter can run on sm89 for FP8). They are left out to keep this fix small enough to cherry-pick; a shared helper can follow if maintainers prefer.
- Not a duplicate: no open issue or PR changes this launch attribute (searched `topkGating PDL`, `topk_softmax PDL`, `59737`). #62912 (open) changes top-k selection in the same file and keeps `config.numAttrs = 1` as context next to this change, so whichever lands second needs a small rebase; it does not touch the attribute.
- Not covered: Hopper/Blackwell (unchanged code path, not measured), sm75 and older, end to end on GPUs other than A100, and a full main build (only `_moe_C` was rebuilt and overlaid on v0.33.0).
- This is a performance regression against v0.32.0; we'd like it cherry-picked into a v0.33.x patch release if one is planned.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.
