title: [ROCm][Perf][MiniMax-M3.1] Four-wave decode top-k for the NVFP4 indexer
author: chao-xu-spec
body:
## Overview

On gfx950, the MiniMax-M3.1 NVFP4 indexer picks the 16 best blocks of every decode row with one wave per row. This PR gives each decode row four waves and merges their top-16 lists exactly, so the ordered block ids are unchanged. No other kernel, flag or call site changes.

## Claims

- Decode top-k is 4.1x faster over the decode shapes of a served MiniMax-M3.1 AgentX run (18.9 -> 4.65 us per call, weighted by how often each shape occurs, real index scores); 4.07x in the live server (21.2 -> 5.2 us per call). With random scores the same shapes give 1.26x: the old kernel is much slower on real scores (see Details).
- End to end (TP4, 2 runs per arm): c16 +1.34% and c32 +2.47% tok/s/GPU, TPOT p50 -12.2% / -12.0%, p90 -8.3% / -8.2% (interactivity p50 +13.9% / +13.6%, p90 +9.0% / +8.9%).
- Same output as before: bit-for-bit equal to AITER's `pa_sparse_block_topk` and to the old kernel in 4,500 sweep cases (772,650 rows); eager and CUDA-graph replay agree. In a replay of the real served calls 1 of 2,816 decode rows differs, in a call with duplicate page ids where the old kernel's own output changes from run to run. GSM8K and spec-decode accept length are unchanged.
- **Costs:** With random scores a call is up to 12% slower when every row is under about 213k tokens; with real scores that only shows for calls in which no row triggers the old kernel's slow path. See Limits.

## Validation

**Microbench.** MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m31-flash` with the two top-k files of this PR on top of main (7b77ed581d; the files are unchanged on main at 76c6f3f2a9, where the test file was re-run); stock = main's files. CUDA-graph replay of 16 back-to-back calls on distinct score buffers, 1 GiB memset (cold L2) before every replay, median of 20 replays per process, 6 fresh processes per arm; per-call us, median of the 6 (process-to-process range at most 0.07 us ours, 0.21 us stock). 1 index head, 4 rows per request, output equal in every process. Scores are the real output of the unchanged scorer on captured queries and index-K pages of a served run (grid cells: re-scored captured requests clipped to the cell's lengths; live lengths uniform in [max/2, max]). Rows = requests, columns = max sequence length (graph width). Not a repo benchmark (none exists for this op); the method is in the details block.

Stock / ours, us (speedup), real scores:

| Requests | 64k | 128k | 256k | 512k |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10.5 / 4.00 (2.6x) | 11.4 / 4.00 (2.9x) | 12.2 / 4.44 (2.8x) | 20.8 / 4.71 (4.4x) |
| 2 | 8.7 / 4.05 (2.1x) | 15.0 / 4.05 (3.7x) | 18.5 / 4.51 (4.1x) | 20.6 / 4.64 (4.4x) |
| 4 | 16.5 / 4.10 (4.0x) | 17.4 / 4.10 (4.3x) | 18.3 / 4.54 (4.0x) | 35.3 / 4.68 (7.6x) |
| 8 | 18.3 / 4.11 (4.4x) | 18.3 / 4.12 (4.4x) | 20.4 / 4.64 (4.4x) | 35.9 / 4.74 (7.6x) |
| 16 | 18.3 / 4.15 (4.4x) | 18.4 / 4.23 (4.3x) | 20.1 / 4.69 (4.3x) | 36.5 / 4.86 (7.5x) |
| 32 | 18.4 / 4.23 (4.3x) | 18.5 / 4.34 (4.3x) | 20.6 / 4.84 (4.2x) | 36.8 / 5.18 (7.1x) |
| 64 | 18.5 / 4.35 (4.2x) | 18.6 / 4.45 (4.2x) | 20.7 / 5.16 (4.0x) | 36.8 / 5.83 (6.3x) |
| 100 | 18.6 / 4.77 (3.9x) | 18.8 / 4.95 (3.8x) | 21.0 / 5.81 (3.6x) | 37.4 / 6.90 (5.4x) |

Served shapes (20 decode graph calls of a TP4 AgentX c16 run: real lengths, padded batch, max length 1M, 1-14 requests), weighted by call count: stock 18.91 us (18.91-18.92), ours 4.65 us (4.65-4.66) per call, 4.06x (per process 4.06-4.07x); per call 1.04x to 7.4x. The same shapes with random scores: 5.79 / 4.61 us, 1.255x (table and per-call numbers in the details block).

**E2E.** amd/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 (MXFP4 experts, MXFP8 dense linears), TP4 EP1 on 4x MI355X, nvfp4 KV and indexer cache, DSpark with 3 draft tokens (synthetic acceptance 2.88), DBO, max-model-len 1M, `--max-num-seqs` 32 (c16) / 64 (c32). CI image plus an overlay of the two changed files (the four files of the decode top-k and its scorer are byte-identical to main's); stock = the image as is. InferenceX AgentX replay (agentx-harness 1.0.12, cc-traces-weka-062126), 3600 s per run, the CI client flags; 2 runs per arm in ABBA order (stock, ours, ours, stock), server restarted per run; ranges are min-max of the 2 runs. Throughput, TPOT and interactivity gains (p50 and p90) are above the floor at both concurrencies (both ours runs above both stock runs). **Accuracy.** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, chat completions, max_tokens 12288, concurrency 64; CI conc-64 recipe with real verification (block rejection sampling; the synthetic acceptance of the benchmark recipe degrades text). 2 servers per arm in ABBA order. vLLM's `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (2 passes per server, 4 values per arm) and the CI harness (lm-eval, the CI-pinned version, 1 pass per server).

```python
# bench_topk.py (random scores)
import sys, json, math, statistics, torch
from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.index_topk_decode.host import minimax_m3_index_topk_decode_indices as topk
K, QL = 16, 4
width = lambda msl: (1 << (math.ceil(math.ceil(msl / 128) / 64) - 1).bit_length()) * 64
flush = torch.empty(1 << 30, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"); res = {}
for msl in [65536, 131072, 262144, 524288, 1 << 20]:
    for nr in [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32, 64, 100]:
        gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(nr * 1000003 + msl)
        seq = torch.randint(msl // 2, msl + 1, (nr,), generator=gen).int().cuda()
        scores = []
        for _ in range(K):
            s = torch.randn(1, nr * QL, width(msl), generator=gen)
            s = torch.where(torch.rand(s.shape, generator=gen) < 4.0 / s.shape[-1], s + 6, s)
            s[:, :, 0] = 1e30; scores.append(s.cuda())
        outs = [torch.empty(1, nr * QL, 16, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") for _ in range(K)]
        def fn():
            for i in range(K): topk(scores[i], outs[i], seq, max_seq_len=msl, query_len=QL)
        fn(); torch.accelerator.synchronize()
        g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
        with torch.cuda.graph(g): fn()
        ts = []
        for _ in range(20):
            flush.zero_(); a, b = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
            a.record(); g.replay(); b.record(); torch.accelerator.synchronize(); ts.append(a.elapsed_time(b) * 1000 / K)
        res[f"{nr}x{msl}"] = statistics.median(ts)
json.dump(res, open(sys.argv[1], "w"))
```

## Details

Each decode row is one workgroup that walks the row's block scores in windows, keeps a running top 16 and ranks the candidates. The old kernel did this with a single wave over windows of 1,664 blocks (213k tokens); rows longer than that serialize on the one wave. Now the workgroup has four waves, each walking every fourth window of 1,024 blocks with its own candidates and running top 16, and the lists are merged by an exact rank over (score, block id), which reproduces AITER's order including ties, NaN and infinities. A wave with no live window pads its list with dead entries, and a row of at most one window skips the merge. The lane-bound threshold uses 16 bits instead of 12 and falls back to all 32 bits when too many keys pass. Prefill compiles to the same code as before. The kernel name for decode changes from `..._w26` to `..._w16`.

Why real scores matter: the old kernel keeps the keys above a bound and ranks at most 64 of them per window; when more pass, it rebuilds the candidates, and with many near-ties it runs an exact bit search on one wave. Random scores never reach that. Real index scores sit in a narrow range, so the 12-bit bound lets more than 64 keys through in about a third of the rows (emulated on the captured rows: 33% of rows with the old bound and window size, 6% with the 16-bit bound), and a call takes as long as its slowest row. Calls in which no row overflows run at the random-score time. I did not build a 16-bit-bound-only or four-wave-only variant, so I cannot say how much of the 4x comes from each.

Limits:
- Slower in some calls: when every row is under about 213k tokens and no row overflows the old kernel's candidate buffer, a call is up to 12% slower (about 0.5 us on a 4 us call; random-score table, and the 0.88x-0.92x served calls there) and 8-9% slower at 100 requests under 131k tokens. In my real-score runs no cell (20 served calls, 32 grid cells, 6 cells of 131k-213k rows) is slower than stock (lowest 1.04x), but about 30% of single-request calls with 131k-213k rows have no overflowing row (emulation). The launch only sees the graph's `max_seq_len` (1M in serving), not the row lengths, so the host cannot choose between the two kernels.
- The real-score grid cells are re-scored captured requests, not replays of served calls; the max length 1M column is random-score only.
- E2E was run on the published ROCm image with the two files overlaid, not on a build of current main: the CI recipe (DBO with this multimodal model) does not start on main under Model Runner V2, and I did not change the recipe. The kernel files are identical to main's; other kernels' shares differ on main (for example the MXFP8 fusions), so the gain on main may differ.
- c16 and c32 only (c1-c8 do not use this indexer path; c64 not run); one model, TP4, DSpark, DBO on; 2 runs per arm.
- Validation is gfx950 only, and no Buildkite step runs the test file on gfx950 (I ran it on MI355X). The microbench is not in `benchmarks/kernels/`.
- A 2-way merge for rows up to 2,048 blocks would halve the 131k-213k regression (+8 lines); it is not in this PR.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the top-k files or their test file (checked against main at 76c6f3f2a9). #64198 (MXFP4 K/V and index cache) does not touch them. #64264 (NVFP4 kernel warmup at startup) and #64273 (monokernel decode on M3.1) are closed drafts that only carried the same bytes of these files as main. #64448 (decode CP for DSpark 7) is open and edits the indexer module and the CP push kernel, not the top-k kernel, so it is complementary.

title: [Spec Decode] Support XPress + Acceptance Estimator
author: tomasruizt
body:
## Overview

Adaptive verification does nothing for XPress today. The acceptance estimator is created, but XPress never feeds it, so the AV budget reads an uninitialised confidence buffer and prunes every draft after the first. Turning AV on makes XPress about 3x slower than leaving it off.

This wires XPress to the estimator, using the logits the draft tokens are sampled from.

## Performance

One H100, Qwen3-8B with the XPress b16 draft, 15 draft tokens, greedy, prefix caching off, SPEED-Bench throughput_1K shuffled with seed 42. AIPerf runs a concurrency grid of 1, 8, 32, 64 and 128 with 30 s cells and 3 trials. Throughput is output tokens in the steady window of each cell, median over the trials.

![Throughput-interactivity pareto](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tomasruizt/vllm/assets/xpress-av/xpress-av-pareto.png)

AV off is the same curve on both commits, within 1%, which is also the spread between trials. On main, AV on verifies one token per step and loses 26% to 71% of throughput. Here it costs 8% at c1 and c8, and from c32 up it is faster than AV off: the budget verifies fewer drafts (AL 3.0 to 3.3 against 3.5 to 3.7), which makes each target step cheaper and more than pays for the shorter accept run.

<details>
<summary>Per-cell results</summary>

| c | AV off tok/s | AV on, main | AV on, this PR | AL off | AL on, main | AL on, this PR |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 408 | 118 | 375 | 3.78 | 1.00 | 3.50 |
| 8 | 2,494 | 812 | 2,291 | 3.54 | 1.01 | 3.17 |
| 32 | 4,468 | 2,227 | 5,389 | 3.67 | 1.01 | 3.04 |
| 64 | 4,471 | 2,856 | 6,242 | 3.58 | 1.01 | 3.19 |
| 128 | 4,967 | 3,665 | 6,810 | 3.68 | 1.00 | 3.32 |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Server and client commands</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ADAPTIVE_VERIFICATION_PROFILE_CONTEXT_LEN=2048 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --served-model-name qwen \
  --max-model-len 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-uvicorn-access-log \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8640 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16","num_speculative_tokens":15,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
```

```yaml
# aiperf profile --config sweep.yaml, one invocation per AV mode
sweep: {type: grid, parameters: {phases.profiling.concurrency: [1, 8, 32, 64, 128]}}
multi_run: {num_runs: 3, cooldown_seconds: 5}
benchmark:
  endpoint:
    url: http://127.0.0.1:8640
    type: chat
    streaming: true
    use_server_token_count: true
    extra: {temperature: 0, max_completion_tokens: 1024, chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}}
  datasets:
    - {name: main, type: file, format: speed_bench_throughput_1k, path: throughput_1k.jsonl, sampling: shuffle, random_seed: 42}
  phases:
    - {name: profiling, type: concurrency, duration: 30, grace_period: 30, concurrency: 1}
```

</details>

## Claims

- AV on no longer collapses: acceptance length 1.08 to 7.26 on the e2e case (7.39 with AV off), acceptance rate 0.005 to 0.42.
- Throughput goes from a 26-71% loss on main to an 8% cost at c1 and c8, and a 21-40% gain from c32 up, because the budget spends fewer verified drafts per step.
- Accuracy is unchanged: GSM8K 0.885 with AV on and off, 1,319 questions.
- AV off is untouched. The draft is bit-identical, and both commits measure within 1% in every cell.

## Validation

The existing Qwen3-8B + XPress b16 case gets an `enable_adaptive_verification` variant in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/xpress/test_xpress.py`. It runs in the nightly XPress job, so no buildkite change is needed.

| commit | result |
|---|---|
| main `f9db1756e9` | `1 failed in 647.96s`, `acceptance_rate=0.005`, `acceptance_len=1.078` |
| this PR | `2 passed in 113.91s`, AV off `0.43 / 7.39`, AV on `0.42 / 7.26`, GSM8K `0.885` both |

<details>
<summary>Failure on main</summary>

```
E  AssertionError: method=dflash target=Qwen/Qwen3-8B, draft=UIUC-SSAIL/Qwen3-8B-XPress-b16, eager=False,
   acceptance_rate=0.005, acceptance_len=1.078; expected acceptance_rate >= 0.375
E  assert 0.005191845631765376 >= 0.375
```

</details>

Unit: `pytest -v tests/v1/spec_decode/test_xpress_head.py` gives 4 passed. It covers both `xpress_topc` paths and asserts the draft is unchanged when no logits are requested.

## Details

`draft_token_confidence_probs` is allocated with `torch.empty` and only written by `_maybe_predict_acceptance`. DFlash and DSpark call it, XPress did not, so the AV budget read uninitialised survivals and the estimator never saw a single feature or verdict.

`jacobi_refine_greedy` now returns the logits of its last pass next to the draft ids, and `XPressSpeculator` hands them to the estimator. Both paths return exactly the logits the argmax ran on, the summed bias over the vocabulary or the top-C candidate scores when `xpress_topc` is set. Nothing is computed when AV is off.

The draft is unchanged, so AV now only decides how many draft tokens to verify, which is what it was meant to do.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Index INT8 MoE per-channel weight scales independently of act quant - #58570
author: fxmarty-amd
body:
**PR authors: @gokay-ai @ahsan-ca @fxmarty-amd - resubmitting https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58570 here with some minor fixes.** I lost ability to push to `https://github.com/gokay-ai/vllm.git` so landing here.

## Overview

Fixes #58532

`QuarkW8A8Int8MoEMethod` can load static per-tensor activation scales with per-output-channel weight scales. The legacy Triton `fused_experts` path still used `per_act_token_quant` to pick both layouts, so static activations (`per_act_token_quant=False`) also took the tensor weight-scale branch. Routed experts' channel scales were ignored.

This keeps the legacy static-INT8 path (no oracle migration) and splits the two flags:

- The non-block W8A8 Triton kernels (`fused_moe_kernel` and the batched `moe_mmk` kernels) index A scales with `per_act_token_quant` / `per_channel_quant` and W scales with a new `per_out_ch_quant` constexpr. `TritonExperts` and the batched Triton experts forward `quant_config.per_out_ch_quant`.
- `int8_w8a8_moe_quant_config` / `make_int8_moe_quant_config` now take `per_out_ch_quant`. Quark, compressed-tensors and online INT8 set it from the actual weight scheme.
- Quark INT8 (static and dynamic branches) derives `per_act_token_quant` from the activation `QuantKey` and `per_out_ch_quant` from the weight `QuantKey`, instead of deriving activation granularity from `weight_qscheme`.

No open PR already covers this combo. #57092 is the opposite mixed case (per-token acts + per-tensor weights) and is still open.

### Note on `per_out_ch_quant` defaults

`FusedMoEQuantConfig.make` and the `fp8` / `int8` / `int4` quant-config factories keep `per_out_ch_quant=False` as the default (unchanged from `main`). All in-tree production callers now pass it explicitly. `Fp8MoEMethod` passes `per_out_ch_quant=False`, which matters for per-token activations + per-tensor weights under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.

**Behavior change for callers of the factories:** previously, setting `per_act_token_quant=True` alone made the Triton kernels index weight scales per channel. Now the weight-scale layout follows `per_out_ch_quant`, so callers with per-channel weight scales must pass `per_out_ch_quant=True`. The in-tree tests that relied on the implicit coupling were updated (`test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py`, `test_int8_kernel.py`, `test_cpu_fused_moe.py`, `test_deepep_moe.py`, `test_deepep_v2_moe.py`). The direct Triton launchers (`invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel`, `dispatch_fused_moe_kernel`, `fused_experts_impl`, `invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel`) still default `per_out_ch_quant=None` to `per_channel_quant`.

This is a stopgap: as per #61024, `FusedMoEQuantConfig` should move to `QuantKey` and drop the `per_act_token_quant` / `per_out_ch_quant` flags.

The W8A16 path does not need the flag: the W8A16 kernels always index weight scales per output channel.

## Validation

Run on MI350X (gfx950), ROCm `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly image, at commit
9cd72c182ad74b20f19ebd90cd835c5beaec4d6f (branch head, `main` merged in,
working tree clean). The checkout was installed editable
(`pip install -e . --no-deps --no-build-isolation`); the compiled extensions were
built from this same source tree, and the only later change in the tree was the
`per_out_ch_quant` docstring.

New / modified tests:

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k int8
# 23 passed, 118 deselected, 14 warnings in 79.59s (0:01:19)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k launcher
# 3 passed, 1086 deselected, 17 warnings in 1.05s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_zen_cpu_int8_moe.py
# 474 passed, 509 skipped, 14 warnings in 154.18s (0:02:34)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_triton_moe_ptpc_fp8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_int8_kernel.py
# 76 passed, 16 warnings in 20.35s

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_cpu_fused_moe.py -k int8
# 1 skipped, 14 warnings in 0.25s  (x86 CPU int8 kernel not available on this node)

pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_deepep_v2_moe.py
# 74 skipped, 18 warnings in 1.19s  (DeepEP not available on this node)
```

`test_quark_int8_static_per_channel_weight_scales` (GPU) perturbs per-channel scales of a routed vs an unrouted expert, for both `w13` and `w2`. It fails on `main` and passes here.

Possibly impacted tests (shared Triton MoE kernels / quant configs):

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/kernels/moe/test_block_int8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py
# 858 passed, 382 skipped, 18 warnings in 272.95s (0:04:32)
```

No model eval: this is scale indexing, not a serving/accuracy algorithm change. `test_quark_int8_w8a8_moe` runs the `amd/tiny-qwen3-moe-w8a8-int8` end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Avoid the MNNVL FlashInfer all-reduce with HiSparse
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #64327. Unblocks #63801.

FlashInfer's MNNVL fused all-reduce + residual + RMSNorm has a cluster-barrier race (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782). The vLLM default single-node backend has been MNNVL since #61989. With HiSparse running host-memory gathers on its copy stream, the race fires and the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` (Xid 13 `CTA Not Present`).

With HiSparse enabled and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=auto`, backend selection now:
- single node: uses `trtllm`;
- multi-node: disables FlashInfer all-reduce, since `trtllm` doesn't support multi-node groups.

An explicit `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` setting is still respected. This is temporary: the check should be removed once vLLM picks up a FlashInfer release with #7782.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k "flashinfer_auto_backend or workspace_failure or standalone_workspace"
```

## Test Result

Server check that the new path runs: 4× H100 (driver 580.126.09), `main` + #63801 (Python side; kernels from the `main` precompiled wheel) + this PR, GLM-5.3 config with dummy weights cut to 5 layers, HiSparse with spec decode. Same build, same load; the only difference is the backend env var.

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND={mnnvl,auto} \
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 --enforce-eager --load-format dummy \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 5, "first_k_dense_replace": 5, "indexer_types": ["full", "full", "full", "shared", "shared"]}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G \
  --max-model-len 67584 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":16}}'

# 6 waves, seeds 1..6
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 52000 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.25 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 32 --ignore-eos --seed $seed
```

| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND` | Fused AR workspace | Result | Output tok/s (mean of 6 waves) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mnnvl` (stock behavior) | `backend=mnnvl` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 499 |
| `auto` (this PR) | `backend=trtllm`, logs `Using flashinfer allreduce backend trtllm: ...` | 6/6 waves, 0 failed requests | 552 |

HiSparse was reading heavily from host memory (8.9 TB host-to-device, ~50% hot-buffer miss rate), but this reduced server didn't hit the race on H100 even with `mnnvl`. The crash evidence is the B200 result below and the standalone repro in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#7782, which faults within seconds on this same box.


10 passed. The two new HiSparse cases fail without the change.

Server-level evidence that `trtllm` avoids the crash (from #64327 / flashinfer#7782, set by hand via `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm`): GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP8 on 8× B200 with HiSparse went from a crash on wave 1 in 7/7 runs (MNNVL) to clean for 4/4 waves (TRTLLM), at about 3% lower decode throughput.

title: [HiSparse] Support the extensible KV cache
author: MatthewBonanni
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Lets HiSparse run on the extensible KV cache (#56492), which previously excluded it. HiSparse's device pool is reserved and grown like any other KV cache. Its host pool stays outside it.

## Claims

- HiSparse uses the extensible KV cache by default.
- At default flags, GPU+host KV capacity grows by 16% and throughput matches `main`. GSM8K under heavy host offload also matches `main`.
- HiSparse with NIXL P/D and with the Mooncake store connector works on the extensible cache.
- Fixes two warmup crashes that removing the gate exposed:
  - the FlashInfer HiSparse autotune read hot blocks that had not been committed;
  - context-prefill warmup overflowed the hot group's fixed-size block-table rows.

## Validation

All runs on B200 with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, against base 3b6eeb0606.

**Default flags.** GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4, no `--gpu-memory-utilization`. Two runs each, server restarted for every point.
```
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 17408 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --num-prompts 2c --max-concurrency c --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

| | GPU+host KV tokens | c=16 tok/s | c=16 TPOT | c=64 tok/s | c=64 TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 1,313,935 | 661 / 666 | 20.3 / 20.1 ms | 949 / 944 | 54.3 / 54.7 ms |
| PR | 1,529,536 | 668 / 664 | 20.1 / 20.2 ms | 956 / 962 | 53.9 / 53.5 ms |

- The PR's log shows `Extended KV cache to 367616 blocks (63.11 GiB)`.
- At c=64, HiSparse stats show heavy host traffic in both variants.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, concurrency 32. The same server at `--max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.625` and `host_pool_gib` 32.
- PR: `Extended KV cache to 6208 blocks`, scores 0.904 and 0.912.
- `main` with `--num-gpu-blocks-override 6208`: 0.923 and 0.914.
- Both ran with 12.8k tokens of KV capacity against about 48k demanded, with about 14M hot-buffer misses and 61–65 GB H2D per stats interval.

**P/D.** Tiny DeepSeek-V3.2 with dummy weights, one prefiller and one decoder. The decoder is sized only by `--gpu-memory-utilization`.
- **NIXL:** the decoder runs `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector, NixlConnector]`. Greedy outputs match HiSparse without P/D (5/5 prompts, 48/48 tokens) with a 1.26M-block pool and with a 768-block pool, where imports land in host memory. Without the post-extend cache-dict fix, the handshake fails: `RuntimeError: Engine ... holds KV layer 'model.layers.0.self_attn.attn', which has no counterpart here.`
- **Mooncake store:** `MultiConnector[HiSparseConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector]` starts and serves requests. Without the fix, startup fails: `ValueError: Missing transferable KV caches for layers: [...]`.

**Warmup crashes on `main`.** Run the GSM8K command on `main` with only the gate removed:
- `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in `FlashInferMLASparseImpl.autotune_hisparse_decode`;
- with autotune disabled, `Block table write ... exceeds row capacity (128 > 64)`.

**Tests**, all passing:

| File | Passed |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` | 6/6 |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_extensible_kv_cache.py` | 20/20 |
| `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py` | 66/66 |
| `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py` | 36/36 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py` | 248/248 |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` | 98/98 |

One more NIXL HMA case needs a gated checkpoint that could not be downloaded.

New tests:
- **`test_hisparse_extensible_kv_cache`:** greedy outputs and the post-extend `kv_caches_by_layer` (layers, dtypes, devices, shapes, storage sizes) must equal a fixed-size cache of the same block count. It fails with either warmup fix reverted, and before the resident/hot rebind (resident entries spanned the whole reservation). CI runs it on H200, which does not use the FlashInfer autotune, so only SM100 guards the autotune fix.
- **`test_shrink_kv_cache_configs_leaves_host_resident_tensors`:** fails on `main`, where the measured shrink rescales the host pool's tensor.

The NIXL/Mooncake registration itself has no permanent test: there is no HiSparse P/D CI job.

## Details

- **Host-resident tensors stay out of the extensible paths.** `ExtensibleKVCache`, `committed_views`/`committed_kv_cache_tensors` and `shrink_kv_cache_configs` skip `host_resident` tensors. `host_resident` is an existing generic field.
- **The post-extend cache dict matches the fixed path's.** The runner keeps the dict `init_kv_cache` returned (`kv_caches_by_layer`); `extend_kv_cache` swaps in the committed views and passes it to `runner.kv_caches` and the connectors. Host layers keep their views and HiSparse's hot slabs stay out. `committed_views` gives layers laid out over the raw buffer (`has_layer_views=False`) the committed prefix, and `rebind_hisparse_device_caches` rebinds HiSparse's resident and hot views over it, so they span the committed blocks rather than the reservation. CUDA graphs captured before extend stay valid: the base address does not move.
- **Autotune:** the HiSparse autotune commits `cdiv(topk, hot_block_size)` blocks before tuning.
- **Warmup:** clamps reservations to the spec's block-table row length (`max_num_blocks_per_req`), which bounds HiSparse's fixed-size hot rows. Mamba is exempt: in non-align modes `MambaManager` can hold more blocks than its row length.
- **Considered:** feature-owned `if hisparse:` branches in the model runner and `extend_kv_cache`. That is more code, and it still needs the same planning changes.
- **Not covered:** sleep/wake with HiSparse on the extensible cache.

title: [Perf][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graphs: one replay per batch, finer grid up to one max budget
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview Encoder (ViT) CUDA graphs only help while eager is bound by host launch time. On main, graphs are captured up to `max_num_batched_tokens` (16384 by default), and a batch is greedily split into several padded replays, so large batches often run slower as graphs than eagerly. This PR applies one rule to every model, in the style of the LLM's CUDA graphs: - **One replay per batch.** A batch replays the smallest budget that holds it; anything else runs as one eager forward. - **A finer budget grid up to one global maximum.** The new `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (default 5120) works like the LLM's maximum capture size. The default balances graph memory against replay coverage using the GB200 measurements below; it is not a universal GPU-bound threshold. Larger batches run eagerly, with a known Gemma 4 trade-off documented below. `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` still overrides both. No model has its own setting. Follow-up: #66067 (stacked on this PR) moves the per-model encoder CUDA graph code that is copied across Qwen2/2.5/3-VL, GLM-4.1V and Cohere Compass into shared mixins, with no behavior change. **This PR builds on #65084** (shared capture buffers, by @Isotr0py), which is now merged; it is rebased onto it. All budget graphs share one set of input and output buffers sized for the largest budget, so the finer grid below costs no extra buffer memory. This PR's own changes: - [`fcba393f65`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65227/commits/fcba393f65): one replay per batch, budget grid, global maximum, largest item first, and eager-path fixes. - [`8bf9354b99`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65227/commits/8bf9354b99): GLM-4.1V rounds its capture size up like the other models. **This also fixes a crash on current main.** #65084's finer budgets (80, 96, ...) make GLM-4.1V's round-down capture too few rows, so with encoder CUDA graphs on (the default) a single 252x252 image stops the engine with `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (324)` (GLM-4.1V-9B, GB200, default `limit_mm_per_prompt`; eager runs). With this PR the same requests run, with both video-enabled and image-only limits, and match eager within run-to-run noise (except the known 672x672 video-enabled case fixed by #65453). See Details. - The remaining commits document and validate `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget`. ## How dispatch changes `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute()` receives one encoder batch (all images or videos the scheduler sends to the encoder in one step) and returns one output per item. **Before (main).** A batch is greedily split into groups, and each group replays its own padded graph. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Encoder batch: N items"] --> B["Sort items, smallest first"] B --> C["Greedy packing into groups:
each group has at most max_batch_size items
and at most the largest budget in tokens (16384 by default);
a large item also starts a new group when running it
separately needs less total budget than merging it"] C --> D["Next group"] D --> E{"Smallest captured budget
that holds the group?"} E -- "found" --> F["Replay that graph
(input padded up to the budget)"] E -- "none: one item larger
than the largest budget" --> G["Eager forward of the group"] F --> H["Postprocess the group"] G --> H H -- "more groups" --> D H -- "done" --> I["Outputs in request order"] ``` A batch of K groups costs K replays, each padded to its budget. Graphs go up to 16384 tokens, where most encoders are already GPU-bound, so a large batch split into several padded replays is often slower than one eager forward. **After (this PR).** The whole batch replays at most one graph; anything that does not fit runs as one eager forward. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Encoder batch: N items"] --> B["Sort items, largest first"] B --> C{"N <= max_batch_size, and a captured budget
(at most encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget, 5120)
holds all tokens of the batch?"} C -- "yes" --> D["One replay of the smallest such graph"] C -- "no" --> E["One eager forward of the whole batch"] D --> F["Postprocess once"] E --> F F --> G["Outputs in request order"] ``` Models with several encoder paths (Step3-VL, DeepSeek-OCR) take this decision once per path. **Captured graphs (startup).** | | Before (main) | After (this PR) | | --- | --- | --- | | Budgets | Quarter-octave steps up to 1024, then half-octave steps, up to the model's largest budget, usually `max_num_batched_tokens` (64, 80, 96, ..., 12288, 16384: 25 graphs) | Quarter-octave steps up to 1024, every 128 up to 2560, then 1/8-octave steps, up to `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (64, 80, 96, ..., 4608, 5120: 36 graphs). The same for every model | | Buffers | One set of buffers sized for the largest budget, shared by all graphs (#65084) | Unchanged; the largest budget is now 5120, so the shared buffers are smaller | | Fixed-size items (Step3-VL, DeepSeek-OCR) | Budgets are multiples of the item size, so up to 16 items fit exactly (#65084) | Unchanged | | User override | `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` | Unchanged; it also overrides the maximum | ## Claims - **Faster than current main** (which includes #65084): 1.07x–1.13x geomean encoder latency on 6 models with real weights, 1.10x–1.21x on batches above 2560 tokens. GLM-4.1V cannot be compared because current main crashes on it (see above); this PR fixes that. - **About 3x less graph memory than current main**, for example 4.99 → 1.79 GiB (MiniMax-M3) and 6.29 → 2.25 GiB (DeepSeek-V4.1), because graphs stop at 5120 tokens instead of 16384. - Against main before #65084 (the earlier measurements kept below): 1.03x–1.30x on 24 models. One known slower case: Gemma 4 batches of exactly 32 images run eagerly and are 9% slower than an exactly fitting graph (see "Choosing the maximum"). - **Simpler:** one global maximum instead of per-model tuning, and one replay per batch instead of greedy packing. This PR's own change is −10 lines outside tests and docs. - **Correct:** no batch on any model matches eager worse than on main, and the encoder CUDA graph test suite fails the same tests as on main. ## Validation All runs: GB200, BF16, default settings (no user budgets). ### Encoder latency and memory vs current main, real weights **Baseline** = main at `ebc97ad8d0` (includes #65084). **After PR** = this PR (`eebc7d0dcf`) on the same main. Encoder only, TP1, 48 batches of 1–40 images with random, continuous sizes and counts (token totals 45–16,128); InternVL3 runs 34 because its tiles are fixed. Each cell is the median of 10 timed calls of the full encoder step. Order Baseline, After PR, After PR, Baseline; each batch keeps the faster of its two runs. | Model | After PR speedup (geomean) | Batches > 2560 tokens | Batches >2% slower | Encoder graphs | Graph memory | Capture time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | InternVL3-8B | 1.133x | 1.172x | 0 / 34 | 17 → 28 | 2.89 → 0.98 GiB | 4.2 → 3.9 s | | Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 1.113x | 1.214x | 0 / 48 | 25 → 36 | 3.59 → 1.34 GiB | 12.9 → 13.2 s | | MiniMax-M3 | 1.086x | 1.119x | 2 / 48 (60 tokens +2.2%, 3996 tokens +2.1%) | 25 → 36 | 4.99 → 1.79 GiB | 7.4 → 7.2 s | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 1.072x | 1.137x | 0 / 48 | 25 → 36 | 6.29 → 2.25 GiB | 6.0 → 7.5 s | | Kimi-K2.5 (vision) | 1.071x | 1.099x | 9 / 48 (≤6.6%, single images ≤384 tokens) | 25 → 36 | 3.03 → 1.12 GiB | 6.1 → 6.5 s | | Qwen3.8-27B | 1.067x | 1.121x | 5 / 48 (≤3.3%, single images ≤374 tokens) | 25 → 36 | 3.31 → 1.16 GiB | 7.9 → 7.5 s | | GLM-4.1V-9B | main crashes | – | – | – | – | – | Batches of at most 600 tokens use the same budgets on both sides (the grids agree below 1024). There, main's own two runs differ by a median 1.1–3.7% (Kimi-K2.5 3.7%, up to 9.7%; Qwen3.8 2.5%, up to 24%), and the median After PR vs Baseline difference is −1.0% to +2.0% (Kimi-K2.5 +2.0%, others ≤ +0.8%). ### Encoder latency and memory vs main before #65084, real weights These are the earlier measurements. **Baseline** = main at `ef8870b09f`, before #65084 merged; **After PR** = this PR's pre-rebase head on that main, which carried #65084's commit. After the rebase, encoder outputs are bitwise identical to that head (see Correctness). Encoder only, TP1. Each model runs 48 batches of 1–40 images whose sizes and counts are random and continuous (token totals 45–16,128); InternVL3 runs 34 because its tiles are fixed. Each cell is the median of 10 timed calls of the full encoder step (input staging, replay or eager, output copies). Baseline and After PR ran in the same session in the order Baseline, After PR, After PR, Baseline, and each batch keeps the faster of its two runs. | Model | After PR speedup vs Baseline (geomean) | Batches >2% slower | Encoder graphs | Graph memory | Capture time | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen2.5-VL-7B | 1.300x | 0 / 48 | 9 → 36 | 3.85 → 1.34 GiB | 9.3 → 11.2 s | | InternVL3-8B | 1.202x | 0 / 34 | 7 → 28 | 3.19 → 0.98 GiB | 3.1 → 4.8 s | | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 1.189x | 0 / 48 | 9 → 36 | 6.46 → 2.25 GiB | 4.4 → 7.1 s | | MiniMax-M3 | 1.182x | 0 / 48 | 9 → 36 | 5.12 → 1.79 GiB | 6.9 → 6.8 s | | Kimi-K2.5 (vision) | 1.167x | 3 / 48 (≤2.8%) | 9 → 36 | 3.22 → 1.12 GiB | 5.5 → 7.5 s | | Qwen3.8-27B | 1.144x | 2 / 48 (≤3.1%) | 9 → 36 | 3.63 → 1.16 GiB | 6.2 → 7.0 s | | GLM-4.1V-9B | 1.143x | 1 / 48 (2.1%) | 9 → 36 | 5.00 → 1.48 GiB | 8.8 → 15.8 s | "Graph memory" is the device memory taken by encoder graph capture. The batches more than 2% slower are all single images of at most 600 tokens (2–5 ms), and they are noise: their graphs have the same shape as main's, main's own two runs differ by a median 1.3–2.7% and up to 11% on these batches, and the median After PR vs Baseline difference over all single images of at most 600 tokens is −0.3% to +0.4% for Kimi-K2.5, Qwen3.8 and GLM-5.3-Flash. ### Encoder latency, every other model (vs main before #65084) Same harness, batches and order, with dummy weights (Gemma 4: real weights), for every other model with encoder CUDA graph support that loads on this machine. Gemma 3 and Llama 4 use ungated mirrors of the same configs; Idefics3 is SmolVLM-256M. Rows marked † ran the exact PR head. For the other rows the graphs are the same as the PR head's (identical budgets and capture code up to 5120 tokens), and batches above 5120 tokens use the eager time measured in the same run; see "Choosing the maximum". | Model | After PR speedup (geomean) | Batches >2% slower | | --- | --- | --- | | LFM2-VL | 1.266x | 0 / 48 | | Idefics3 (SmolVLM-256M) | 1.263x | 1 / 46 (4096 tokens, +2.4%) | | Ernie-4.5-VL † | 1.214x | 0 / 48 | | Qwen2-VL-2B | 1.203x | 0 / 48 | | GLM-5.3-Flash † | 1.197x | 3 / 48 (≤4.9%, single images ≤496 tokens) | | DeepSeek-VL2 | 1.195x | 0 / 40 | | Llama 4 | 1.178x | 0 / 45 | | Mistral 3 | 1.178x | 0 / 48 | | Kimi-VL | 1.169x | 0 / 48 | | Cohere Compass | 1.153x | 1 / 48 (80 tokens, +3.8%) | | Qwen3-VL-2B † | 1.151x | 4 / 35 (≤6.6%, single images ≤208 tokens) | | Step3-VL-10B | 1.138x | 0 / 48 | | DeepSeek-OCR | 1.135x | 0 / 48 | | Qwen3.5-0.8B † | 1.120x | 5 / 48 (≤6.0%, single images ≤80 tokens) | | Gemma 3 | 1.079x | 0 / 48 | | Gemma 4 (E2B) | 1.072x | 0 / 48 | | Kimi-K3 (vision) | 1.033x | 0 / 48 | The slower single images on the † rows are noise in the same way: on Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3.5-0.8B, main's own two runs differ by a median 8.0% and 2.4% on these images, and the median After PR vs Baseline difference is −2.1% and −0.5%. Graph memory on the † rows: Ernie-4.5-VL 4.03 → 1.33 GiB, GLM-5.3-Flash 4.03 → 1.38 GiB, Qwen3-VL-2B 3.63 → 1.14 GiB, Qwen3.5-0.8B 2.36 → 0.76 GiB. ### Choosing the maximum (measured vs main before #65084) For every batch, the harness also times eager on the same inputs. This gives, for any maximum X, what each batch would cost with graphs up to X and eager above (the grid below X does not depend on X). Over all 24 models: | Maximum | Models with a batch >2% slower than main because it ran eagerly | Worst such batch | Geomean speedup over all 24 models | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2560 | 7 of 24 (Qwen3-VL-2B, Qwen3.5-0.8B, Gemma 4, Ernie-4.5-VL, LFM2-VL, Mistral 3, GLM-5.3-Flash) | +42% (Qwen3.5-0.8B) | 1.161x | | 3072 | 7 of 24 (same) | +42% (Qwen3.5-0.8B) | 1.163x | | 4096 | 1 of 24 (Gemma 4) | +10% (Gemma 4) | 1.167x | | **5120** | **0 of 24** | — | **1.169x** | | 8192 | 0 of 24 | — | 1.167x | | 16384 (no maximum) | 0 of 24 | — | 1.165x | DeepSeek-V4.1 needs the batched eager forward of this PR for this: with main's one-forward-per-image eager, every maximum below 8192 makes some of its batches 2–3x slower. 5120 is the smallest maximum at which no model has a batch in this set that is slower than main because it ran eagerly. Gemma 4, for example, has 4480-token batches that are 10% slower than main when they run eagerly. Gemma 4 is the model that sets this bound, and its random batches jump from 16 images (4480 tokens) to 24 (6720), so I measured every image count in between and above (280 tokens per image, same harness, main / PR / PR without a maximum, two runs each, best of two): | Images (tokens) | Main | This PR (5120) | This PR, no maximum | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 16 (4480) | graph 4480 | graph 4608: 1.00x | 1.00x | | 17–18 (4760–5040) | graph 8960 | graph 5120: 1.75x | 1.75x | | 19–23 (5320–6440) | graph 8960 | eager: 1.27x–1.52x | 1.32x–1.58x | | 24–28 (6720–7840) | graph 8960 | eager: 1.03x–1.11x | 1.10x–1.32x | | 32 (8960) | graph 8960 | eager: **0.91x** | 1.00x | Speedups are vs main. Gemma 4's encoder stays host-bound up to at least 8960 tokens: a graph at the next budget is 0–19% faster than eager there. So with the 5120 maximum it is faster than main except at exactly 32 images, where main's power-of-2 budget fits exactly and eager is 9% slower. Covering that needs a maximum of 8960, which costs graph memory on every model (Gemma 4: 3.58 → 8.68 GiB) and makes large-encoder models slightly slower, because above ~5000 tokens their eager forward is already faster than a padded graph (DeepSeek-V4.1 geomean 1.187x at 5120, 1.169x at 8192). I kept 5120 and accept this Gemma 4 case. Users who serve many-image Gemma 4 batches can raise `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget`. ### Correctness An encoder CUDA graph must give the same output as eager. Every check below compares this PR and main against eager on the same inputs. | Check | Models | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Encoder output, graph vs eager, 48 random + 34 fixed batches | 7 models with real weights, 17 with dummy weights | No batch is close to eager on main but not close After PR (`torch.allclose(atol=0.01, rtol=0.01)`). No model has more batches that differ from eager than on main (Qwen2.5-VL 46 → 16 of 96 runs, MiniMax-M3 34 → 20, others equal). | | `test_vit_cudagraph_image` / `_video`: graph vs eager tokens, dummy weights | All 22 models in the test file, as configured and with pinned budgets removed (default grid) | After PR and Baseline fail exactly the same tests: Gemma 3, Llama 4, MiniCPM-V 2.6 (gated repositories this machine cannot download) and MiniCPM-V 4.0 (fails to start with encoder graphs on main too). | | Encoder output, graph vs eager, vs current main `ebc97ad8d0` | The 6 real-weight models above | Same or fewer batches not close to eager After PR: Qwen2.5-VL 34 → 16 of 96 runs, MiniMax-M3 28 → 20, others equal (InternVL3 0, DeepSeek-V4.1 0, Kimi-K2.5 6, Qwen3.8 6). | | Rebase onto merged #65084: encoder outputs of this head vs the pre-rebase head `08c8e8ec90` | GLM-4.1V-9B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3.8-27B (real weights, 34–35 fixed batches each) | Bitwise identical: 0 of 3992 item outputs differ. | | `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py` | — | 96 passed. On current main (`ebc97ad8d0`), 16 of them fail: the one-replay dispatch, budget grid and `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` tests. | The batches that still differ from eager are single images, from bf16 rounding when one image runs in a padded replay (relative L2 1–4%, as on main). Gemma 4 cannot be compared at the encoder level: the harness passes its images as one padded tensor, so graph and eager return different row counts on both versions; the test suite covers its serving path. End-to-end generated-token checks with real weights (Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3.8, Qwen2-VL, GLM-4.1V, LFM2-VL; TP1, TP2, Model Runner V2) were run on an earlier revision of this PR that used per-model caps: 0 non-tied divergences. They were not rerun on this revision.
Review follow-up: token-budget configuration validation `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` now rejects `0` and negative values; `None` and positive integers remain valid. The regression tests call the real `LLM` entry point with an empty local model directory, so invalid caps must be rejected before model loading. No weights or GPU compute are needed. Using the existing Python virtual environment, baseline `45d7c06185dc` with the new tests: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k 'max_token_budget_rejected or valid_max_token_budget_preserved' -q --tb=short ``` Result: **2 failed, 3 passed, 91 deselected**. Both invalid caps pass configuration validation and reach `ModelConfig`, which rejects the empty model directory instead of reporting the expected `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget must be positive` error (`Regex pattern did not match`). With the fix, including adjacent initialization and default-budget tests: ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k 'TestInitInvariantValidation or TestDefaultBudgetTable' -q --tb=short ``` Result: **23 passed, 73 deselected**. Valid configurations retain their existing execution paths; this follow-up does not change dispatch or rerun the model benchmarks above.
## Details **Why a graph can lose.** Eager latency is roughly max(host launch time, GPU time). A replay costs the GPU time of its whole captured shape, padding included. Once eager is GPU-bound there is no launch time left to save, so padding and extra replays are pure cost. Main captures up to 16384 tokens and splits a batch into several padded replays. **Why one global maximum and not per-model tuning.** An earlier revision of this PR capped some models at 2560 and left others uncapped, based on per-model measurements. That needed a decision for every model and for every subclass that inherits one, so it is not maintainable. The measurements above support 5120 as a common memory/performance compromise, with the documented Gemma 4 32-image regression. Graph memory is a little higher than with per-model caps (MiniMax-M3 1.79 vs 1.01 GiB), and speed is within about 1–2%. **GLM-4.1V capture size (`8bf9354b99`).** GLM-4.1V sized each dummy capture item as `budget // max_batch_size`, while the other models round up. With the old power-of-2 budgets this was exact. The finer grid has budgets such as 96 with `max_batch_size` 64: one 96-token image needs 384 patch rows, but the graph captured 64 × 1 × 4 = 256, so replay fails in `_copy_padded_buffer` ("size of tensor a (256) must match the size of tensor b (384)"). Found on GLM-4.1V-9B with a single 96-token image. Since #65084 merged on its own, main has the finer budgets without this fix and crashes the same way (re-checked end to end on main `ebc97ad8d0`: a 252x252 image fails with 256 vs 324 rows; eager and main plus this commit run). After the fix, all 82 GLM-4.1V batches and all 34 GLM-5.3-Flash batches (which inherits the code) run and match eager as on main. **Eager paths.** Batches above the maximum now take each model's `encoder_eager_forward`, which main rarely used. Three were fixed: - **DeepSeek-V4.1:** ran one forward per image, which is 2–3x slower than main's graphs on large batches. It now runs all images as one varlen batch through the same forward as the graph. - **Ernie-4.5-VL:** ran the resampler twice and crashed (`shape '[-1, 10240]' is invalid`). - **DeepSeek-VL2:** had no `encoder_eager_forward` and returned `None`. **Trade-offs and limitations.** - **More graphs:** 36 instead of 9. Buffers are shared, so memory still drops. Capture takes 0–3 s longer, except GLM-4.1V (8.8 → 15.8 s). - **Other GPUs:** only GB200 was measured; no AMD hardware was available. If eager becomes GPU-bound later on another GPU, `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` can be raised. - **Video frame capacity (fixed by #60112):** a graph holds `min(max_batch_size * max_frames_per_video, token_budget)` frames. With the default video limit, `max_frames_per_video` is 1, so a single long low-resolution video (e.g. 130 frames at 112x112 on Qwen2.5-VL) overflows `cu_seqlens` and crashes the engine, on main too (reported and reproduced by subhashpolisetti). #60112 runs such batches eagerly; it needs a small rebase after this PR. - **GLM-4.1V-family image replays with video enabled (fixed by #65453):** capture pads `cu_seqlens` to `max_frames_per_batch` but image replays pad to `max_batch_size`, so GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash image outputs are wrong when video is enabled, on main too. The image correctness checks above ran with video disabled. - vorapolsiloai's MI355X serving numbers posted below were for an earlier revision (startup timing probe). **Not a duplicate.** #65084 (merged) shares capture buffers but keeps greedy multi-replay dispatch; this PR builds on it. #65351 is a similar buffer-sharing change. #66067 (stacked on this PR) moves the per-model encoder CUDA graph code into shared mixins. ---

title: [Quantization] Remove QuTLASS and fp_quant, run QuIP NVFP4 on Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Removes QuTLASS and the deprecated `fp_quant` method, and runs compressed-tensors NVFP4 checkpoints with a Hadamard input transform (QuIP) on Humming. Supersedes #61671, and makes #51112 moot.

## Claims

- QuIP NVFP4 checkpoints load and generate again. At `main` they crash at startup on SM100+.
- The checkpoint's declared FP4 activation is honored, with no fallback to A16 on this path.
- Input transforms always receive unquantized activations, which also fixes the generic transform path.
- The `_qutlass_C` build dependency, the `fp_quant` method, and about 1,800 lines of code are gone.

**Breaking:** `fp_quant` checkpoints no longer load. They already failed to load on `main`, and the method has been deprecated since #31688.

## Validation

B300 (SM103), humming-kernels 0.1.18. FP-Quant numbers below are from a scratch prototype, since that path is removed here; the QuIP row was re-run on this branch.

**Tests**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/quantization/test_nvfp4.py -k 'quip or hadamard_fp4_routing'` | 8 passed |
| `pytest tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py -k transforms_perplexity` | 3 passed |
| QuIP generation with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | clean |
| `pre-commit` on changed files | passed |

Reproducer on `main`: `LLM(model="nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-quipv16-nvfp4")` fails during startup with `'QuantizedActivation' object has no attribute 'shape'`.

**GSM8K** (600 questions, 5-shot, greedy, %)

| Checkpoint | QuTLASS* | Humming A4 | Humming A16 + Hadamard |
|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.2-1B QuIP NVFP4 (float: 32.3) | 18.8 | 17.3–20.5 (this branch) | 22.8 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant RTN NVFP4 (float: 66.8) | 23.5 | 21.3 | 45.2 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant QAT NVFP4 | 55.0 | 52.0 | 62.0 |
| Qwen3-1.7B FP-Quant RTN MXFP4 | 16.3 | 15.3 | 26.7 |

\* `main` cannot run these, so the baseline needed small harness patches for the two root causes below. FP-Quant rows ran in eager mode.

A4 vs QuTLASS is a statistical tie (paired p = 0.13–0.93), though lower in every prototype row. Run-to-run noise is large: two passes in one process scored 17.3 and 20.5, with 196/600 identical outputs.

**GEMM GPU time** (µs, graph replay, real `down_proj` weights, N=2048, K=6144, warm L2, not hand-tuned)

| M | QuTLASS + cutlass | QuTLASS + FlashInfer | Humming A4 | Humming A16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 17.9 | 7.7 | 9.7 | 9.8 |
| 1024 | 36.8 | 24.1 | 15.9 | 41.4 |
| 8192 | 164.9 | 146.4 | 75.8 | 240.6 |

NVFP4 shown. Graph replay was used because CUPTI failed in this environment (`cupti-python` 13.3.1).

## Details

**Root causes on `main`**
- `fp_quant`: checkpoints contain `backward_hadamard_matrix`, which `FPQuantLinearMethod` never registers, so loading fails.
- QuIP: since #44260 NVFP4 layers expose `input_quant_key`, so producers pass a `QuantizedActivation`, which the transform methods cannot handle. Per #61671, SM12x also fails because QuTLASS wheels contain only `sm_100` code.
- Neither was caught because the job holding the QuIP perplexity test is commented out. The new tests are in `test_nvfp4.py`, whose Blackwell job does run.

**Routing:** Humming is used for W4A4, SM100+, a `hadamard` input transform with `head_dim` in 16–128, no output transform, and backend `auto` or `humming`. Everything else uses the generic transform path. Humming's block size 16–256 output matched the dense Sylvester matrix to bf16 rounding.

**What is lost**
- QuEST for MXFP4. None of the 36 public `fp_quant` models use it.
- Bit-exact output against QuTLASS, since scale rounding differs.
- Fused handling of non-Sylvester dense transforms. They use the generic path, which is slower and was not tested here.
- About 2 µs at M=1–16 versus the CT FlashInfer path.

**Not validated:** SM120, and TP>1 (`HadamardTransform` still raises `NotImplementedError`). `Humming float4e2m1 activation is slow on SM103` still logs, though A4 was the fastest option at M ≥ 1024. Plain NVFP4 on `--linear-backend humming` still falls back to A16 on SM10x and is unchanged here.

Not a duplicate: open PRs #61671 and #51112 fix QuTLASS rather than remove it.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip the combine staging copy in flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided
author: vadiklyutiy
body:
## Overview

`flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided` copies the whole expert output into FlashInfer's symmetric workspace before every combine (`moeA2APrepareCombineKernel`). This PR hands the experts the workspace combine region through the existing `allocate_fused_expert_output` hook, as `allgather_reducescatter` already does with its combine input, so FlashInfer detects the workspace-backed payload and skips the copy. Follow-up to #54268.

## Claims

- Removes the staging copy of every received row before combine. On B200 EP4 with Qwen3.5-397B shapes the copy costs 163 us per MoE layer at 16K tokens per rank (~0.5 GB read + 0.5 GB write of HBM).
- One-sided dispatch + combine microbenchmark: −6 / −43 / −161 us at 1K / 4K / 16K tokens per rank.
- End-to-end prefill throughput on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 (DP4 + EP, 4× B200): +1.4% to +3.2% across ISL 512–32K, faster at every ISL, ~10M input tokens per point. gsm8k unchanged.
- No change when the hook cannot apply: experts that do not reduce top-k themselves, outputs that are not bf16/fp16, or a shape/device mismatch keep vLLM's own buffer and the existing copy.

## Validation

Hardware: one DGX B200 node (8 GPUs on NVSwitch), FlashInfer 0.7.2, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7. Baseline is `main` at 51c6dfd8c8, the parent of this change.

### Unit tests

```bash
python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_mnnvl_alltoall.py -v
python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py -k flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided -v
```

- `test_mnnvl_alltoall.py`: 5 passed, 13 skipped. The multi-GPU tests are skipped by `requires_ptrace` on this bare-metal host (no `CAP_SYS_PTRACE`), so `test_one_sided_manager_lifecycle`, `test_one_sided_manager_workspace_grow` and the new `test_one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace` were also run directly on 2 GPUs (bypassing only the marker): all 3 passed.
- `test_one_sided_expert_output_in_workspace` dispatches through `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager`, writes the expert output into the buffer returned by `allocate_fused_expert_output`, runs the real `finalize()`, and checks that combine got `payload_in_workspace=True` and the output is exact.
- `test_moe_layer.py -k flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`: 2 passed, 8 skipped (no supported config / EPLB requires EP).

### Microbenchmark (communication only)

EP4 on B200, hidden 4096, top_k 10, 512 experts, NVFP4 dispatch, bf16 combine, random routing. `flashinfer.testing.bench_gpu_time_with_cupti` with cold L2 and CUDA graphs, 100 iterations, median of the slowest rank. The "with copy" case passes a separate expert-output tensor (current vLLM), the "no copy" case passes the buffer from `get_combine_input_buffer()`. No expert GEMM in either case, so the difference is the removed copy.

| tokens/rank | AGRS (us) | one-sided, with copy (us) | one-sided, no copy (us) | delta |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 169.2 | 97.9 | 92.0 | −5.9 |
| 4096 | 357.8 | 324.5 | 281.4 | −43.1 |
| 16384 | 982.3 | 1195.3 | 1034.4 | −160.9 |

p10–p90 of the one-sided medians stays within ±1.5%. nsys shows `moeA2APrepareCombineKernel` at 13.4 us (1K) and 163.3 us (16K) per call, matching the 4K/16K deltas.

### End-to-end

One server at a time on the same GPUs 0–3 of the node: the full sweep on the baseline server, then the server is stopped and this PR is started on the same GPUs and runs the same sweep. Load comes from the Rust benchmark client (`vllm-bench` 0.1.0), which starts in milliseconds, so the measured window is not affected by client startup:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 40960 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --language-model-only --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85

# prefill-bound: ~10M input tokens per point, 1 output token, all requests at once
vllm-bench --backend vllm --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8101 \
  --model nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 --tokenizer <local snapshot> \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len $ISL --random-output-len 1 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((10 * 1048576 / ISL)) \
  --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 10
```

One run per ISL and server, after a 1024-prompt warmup. Both servers got the same prompts (same seed, identical input token counts) and no request failed.

| ISL | prompts | baseline input tok/s | this PR input tok/s | ratio | baseline duration (s) | this PR duration (s) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 20480 | 130205 | 134084 | 1.030x | 80.4 | 78.1 |
| 1024 | 10240 | 133693 | 138033 | 1.032x | 78.3 | 75.9 |
| 2048 | 5120 | 135770 | 138764 | 1.022x | 77.2 | 75.5 |
| 4096 | 2560 | 134813 | 137933 | 1.023x | 77.7 | 76.0 |
| 8192 | 1280 | 132550 | 134780 | 1.017x | 79.1 | 77.8 |
| 16384 | 640 | 128228 | 129970 | 1.014x | 81.8 | 80.7 |
| 32768 | 320 | 117129 | 119326 | 1.019x | 89.5 | 87.9 |

The ~2% at long ISL matches what the removed copy predicts. With 32K batched tokens per rank the copy costs ~0.33 ms per MoE layer, ~20 ms over the model's 60 MoE layers, against a prefill step of ~1.1 s (4 × 32K tokens at ~117K tok/s).

gsm8k (5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions`, 1319 questions):

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 0.8135 ± 0.0107 | 0.7930 ± 0.0112 |
| this PR | 0.8211 ± 0.0106 | 0.7998 ± 0.0110 |

## Details

**Root cause.** Combine in the one-sided backend is pull-based: each rank reads its tokens' partial results directly from the owners' workspace over NVLink, so the expert output must live in the symmetric workspace. `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedPrepareAndFinalize` did not override `allocate_fused_expert_output`, so the modular kernel gave the experts a buffer from vLLM's workspace manager and `finalize()` passed that buffer to `combine()`. FlashInfer then launched `moeA2APrepareCombineKernel` with `ep_size * tokens_per_rank` CTAs to copy every received row into the combine region. `NaiveDPEPPrepareAndFinalize` (AGRS) already overrides the hook, so AGRS never paid an equivalent copy.

**Change.** `allocate_fused_expert_output` returns `communication.get_combine_input_buffer(dtype)`, a `[ep_size * tokens_per_rank, hidden]` view of this rank's combine region. `finalize()` is unchanged: `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll.combine()` compares the payload pointer with that buffer and passes `payload_in_workspace=True`, and FlashInfer reduces the copy kernel to a single CTA that only bumps the round flag. The hook returns `None` (old behavior) unless the experts reduce top-k themselves (`TopKWeightAndReduceNoOP`), the dtype is bf16/fp16 (the combine region is sized for 16-bit rows), and shape and device match.

**Why it is safe.**

- The combine region starts after the last dispatch payload region (cacheline aligned), so experts can read the dispatched activations while writing their output.
- Peers may still be reading a rank's combine region right after its combine returns. The next layer's experts write that region only after the next dispatch, which waits for completion flags that every peer sets after its own combine. This is the same point where the staging copy writes today.
- The view is valid between dispatch and combine. The modular kernel calls the hook from `_fused_experts`, after `_prepare` (dispatch) and before `_finalize` (combine). The address depends only on the workspace base and `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank`, so CUDA graph capture is unaffected.
- No new host-device synchronization: the hook only builds a tensor view.

**Duplicate check.** No open or closed PR touches `allocate_fused_expert_output` or `get_combine_input_buffer` for this backend (`gh pr list --search` on both names, "nvlink one sided combine copy", and `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`). Related but different: #59134 (dispatch sizing for experts that quantize their own inputs).

**AI assistance.** This change, its tests, the benchmarks and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and the results above.

title: [Kernel] Marlin: remove 8-bit (INT8/FP8) activation support, rely on Humming
author: mgoin
body:
## Overview

Part of #65560.

Remove INT8 and FP8 activation support (W4A8) from the dense and MoE Marlin kernels. Marlin becomes a 16-bit-activation kernel, and Humming covers 8-bit activations. Independent of #65540 (Marlin PTX-only build); this PR leaves the fp16/bf16 Marlin arch lists alone.

## Claims

- Removes Marlin's W4A8-INT8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4) and W4A8-FP8 (GPTQ/AWQ INT4, MXFP4) paths: the sm89 FP8-activation kernels and their SM89/SM12x build targets, the INT8-activation instantiations, the 8-bit paths in both templates, the `marlin_int4_fp8_preprocess` op, `a_scales` on `marlin_gemm`/`moe_wna16_marlin_gemm`, and `is_a_8bit` on the repack ops. Net −2039 lines.
- `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed, and setting it raises an error with a migration hint. The replacement is `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'` (or `float8e4m3`), documented in `docs/features/quantization/README.md`.
- Compressed-tensors W4A8-FP8 checkpoints on SM89/SM12x, which previously fell back to Marlin, now select `HummingLinearKernel`.
- No change for FP8-weight Marlin (W8A16, MXFP8) or any 16-bit-activation format.

## Validation

DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), CUDA 13.0, `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.1` source build of this branch (kernel tests rerun after rebasing onto main without #65540, with native sm_120f Marlin cubins).

Kernel tests: `test_marlin_gemm.py` 254 passed, `test_moe.py -k marlin` 189 passed / 6 skipped, `test_marlin_tile_padding.py` 98 passed, `test_reload.py -k marlin` 6 passed, `test_marlin_vs_trtllm_mxint4.py` 1 passed. The counts dropped because the 8-bit-activation cases were removed. pre-commit (incl. mypy) passes.

GSM8K, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4`, 100 questions, 5-shot:

| Config | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| default (Marlin W4A16) | 0.62, 3348 tok/s | 0.60 / 0.62 (2 runs), 3364 tok/s |
| W4A8-INT8 (main: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8`; PR: `--quantization humming` + `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}'`) | 0.68, 3413 tok/s | 0.63, 4008 tok/s |
| W4A8-FP8 (same, `fp8` / `float8e4m3`) | 0.69, 3554 tok/s | 0.62, 3842 tok/s |

The 100-question accuracy gaps are within noise. On the full set (1319 questions, accuracy only):

| Config | main (Marlin) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| W4A16 | 0.622 | 0.622 (Marlin) |
| W4A8-INT8 | 0.625 | 0.644 (Humming) |
| W4A8-FP8 | 0.591 | 0.603 (Humming) |

I checked that the Humming runs actually quantize activations by reading the loaded layer config: `a_dtype=int8, as_dtype=float32`. Note that `--linear-backend humming` with the same env var does **not** quantize activations for GPTQ/AWQ (`a_dtype=float16`), which is why the docs point to `--quantization humming`. Setting `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` now fails at startup with: `ValueError: VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE has been removed. Marlin no longer supports 8-bit activations. Use --quantization humming and set the activation dtype with VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG, e.g. '{"dtype":"int8"}'.`

```bash
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct-GPTQ-Int4 --quantization humming --max-model-len 8192
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 100
```

## Details

- On main, the Marlin 8-bit path was already narrow. For linear layers it only worked with GPTQ symmetric INT4: AWQ + `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE=int8` fails at load with "W8A8 is not supported by marlin kernel". FP8-weight + FP8-activation was plumbed in Python but never instantiated.
- Template changes are constant folding of `is_a_8bit == false`, so the 16-bit kernels compile to the same code. The `mma` helpers lose the k=32 path and the `k_size`/`idx` params, and the repack kernels lose their `is_a_8bit` template param.
- `MarlinLinearKernel.can_implement` rejects 1-byte activation types, so selection falls through to Humming. `ConchLinearKernel` now also rejects non-16-bit activations; it had no activation check and sits between Marlin and Humming in the CUDA list.
- `int_wna16` MoE conversion returns 8 entries instead of 10 (the INT8 input global scales are gone). Every in-tree caller is updated.
- Not validated: Humming W4A8 MoE end to end. Marlin MoE W4A8 was only reachable through the removed env var.
- Deprecation: `VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE` is removed without a deprecation cycle. Setting it is now a hard error, raised from `validate_environ` via a new `envs.removed_environment_variables` map, and the message points to `--quantization humming` with `VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG`. Without the error, a user who set it would silently fall back to W4A16. Covered in `tests/config/test_config_generation.py::test_unrecognized_env`.

Superseded open PRs that extend Marlin W4A8: #58326, #48926, #38066, #50096, #59895, #61405, #49039, #57091. No open PR removes these paths (searched "VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE", "marlin w4a8", "marlin int8/fp8 activation", "remove marlin").

title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graph: cap each graph's frame slots at its token budget
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

When encoder CUDA graphs are on and the model accepts video, every captured graph is sized for `max_batch_size x max_frames_per_video` frames, including the graphs for small token budgets. For GLM-4.1V that is 64 x 600 = 38,400 frames, so even the smallest graph computes at least 38,400 tokens, and every image or video request replays a graph far larger than its input.

This PR caps each graph's frame slots at its token budget.

## Claims

- **GLM-4.1V** (encoder graph on, video allowed, which is the default):
  - Median image request: 470–481 ms → 31–32 ms.
  - Median video request: 475–484 ms → 35–36 ms.
  - Eager takes 57 ms (image) and 61 ms (video). Before this PR the graph path was ~8x slower than eager; after it, it is faster.
- **Qwen2.5-VL-7B at 128k context:**
  - Median image request: 30–33 ms → 27 ms.
  - Median video request: 32–33 ms → 30–31 ms.
- **Video outputs are unchanged:**
  - GLM-4.1V: graph outputs match eager bit for bit.
  - Qwen2.5-VL: graph outputs match main's graph outputs token for token.
  - Both hold for single videos and for 4-video batches replayed as one graph.
- **No effect** when video is disabled, or when `max_frames_per_batch` is at most the budget.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, default ViT attention backend.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Latency.**
- One engine per run with `limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1}`, so image and video requests share the same graphs.
- Each run sends 24 image requests and 24 video requests one at a time, with `max_tokens=1`.
- Images and videos are fresh random inputs, so there are no encoder-cache hits:
  - images cycle through 6 sizes from 224x224 to 896x672;
  - videos have 4–16 frames at 224–448 px.
- Each graph-on request replays exactly one graph, counted via `EncoderCudaGraphManager.execute` calls.
- Runs were in the order baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline. The two values per cell are pass 1 / pass 2, each the median request latency.

| Model (`max_model_len`) | Requests | Baseline, graph on | This PR, graph on | Eager |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | image | 469.8 / 480.6 ms | 31.9 / 31.2 ms | 56.8 ms |
| GLM-4.1V-9B (8192) | video | 475.4 / 484.2 ms | 35.9 / 35.2 ms | 60.7 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | image | 32.6 / 30.3 ms | 27.2 / 27.1 ms | 56.9 ms |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (128000) | video | 32.1 / 31.9 ms | 30.8 / 29.7 ms | 55.7 ms |

**Video correctness.** Greedy decoding with `logprobs=2`; each comparison is graph vs eager on the same tree, and every video is fresh.

| Model | Inputs | Graph replays | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V (`max_model_len=8192`, 38,400 → budget frame slots on every graph) | 4 single videos (48 tokens each) + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | each 4-video batch is one replay | tokens identical, logprob diff 0 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B (`max_model_len=128000`, 896 → budget frame slots on graphs ≤ 512) | 4 single videos + 2 batches of 4 videos (32 tokens each) | 4 single replays, and each 4-video batch is one replay | identical to main's graph: 12/12 token sequences |

On Qwen2.5-VL, both main and this PR match eager on 10 of 12 sequences. The 2 that diverge are the same on both. Each divergence happens at a step where eager's top-2 logprobs are exactly tied, after bf16 differences of up to 0.24 in logprob. That drift between graph and eager already exists on main and is unrelated to this change.

On GLM-4.1V, the encoder outputs for videos were also compared directly:
- Graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of ≤ 0.2%, the same as eager vs eager in a different batch.
- Replaying after other inputs have dirtied the capture buffers gives identical outputs.

**Unit tests.** `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 79 passed. The new test captures with `max_frames_per_batch=1000` and checks two things: each graph keeps `min(1000, budget)` frame slots, and a video batch still replays. `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Image latency (square images only); run with cudagraph_mm_encoder True and False.
import time, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192, max_num_seqs=8,
          enable_prefix_caching=False, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1, "video": 1},
          compilation_config={"cudagraph_mm_encoder": True})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
rng, sp, ts = np.random.default_rng(0), SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), []
for _ in range(6):
    for s in (224, 336, 448, 672):
        im = Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 255, (s, s, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
        t = time.time(); llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}], sp)
        ts.append(time.time() - t)
print(f"median {1e3 * sorted(ts)[len(ts) // 2]:.1f} ms")
```

The video runs use the same setup with synthetic videos (4–16 frames, 224–448 px). For correctness they use `temperature=0` and `logprobs=2`, run once with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` on and once off, and compare tokens and logprobs. For batches, 4 fresh videos are submitted in one `generate` call.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `EncoderCudaGraphManager` passes one `max_frames_per_batch` to every budget's capture. That value is `max_batch_size * max_frames_per_video`, which became the default in #40445.

Qwen2/2.5/3-VL and GLM-4.1V build their capture layout from it: each item gets `frames_per_item = max_frames_per_batch // max_batch_size` frames, and each frame has at least one token. The captured size is therefore at least `max_frames_per_batch` tokens, whatever the budget.

How badly a model is affected depends on where its frame limit comes from:
- **GLM-4.1V:** the limit is a constant 600 frames per video, so every budget captures at least 38,400 tokens.
- **Qwen:** the limit is derived from `max_model_len` and the video limit, so the graphs grow only with long contexts. For example, Qwen2.5-VL at 128k context gets 896 frame slots, which inflates the 64–512 budgets.

**Fix.** Every frame yields at least one output token, so a batch that fits budget `B` has at most `B` frames. Concretely:
- Each graph is captured with `min(max_frames_per_batch, B)` frame slots.
- That value is stored in `BudgetGraphMetadata`.
- Replay pads `cu_seqlens` to the same per-graph value.

The model capture layouts are unchanged; they shrink because they derive from the value passed in.

Every auto or validated configuration keeps `B >= max_batch_size`, so a graph never gets fewer frame slots than `max_batch_size`, and image replays are unaffected.

`EncoderCudaGraphManager` is shared by Model Runner V1 and V2 (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py`), so both get the fix. The change adds no host sync.

**Related: GLM-4.1V image outputs (not changed by this PR).**
- On main, with video enabled, GLM-4.1V image replays are numerically wrong. GLM registers no `cu_seqlens` padding, so the replay buffer's tail is filled with zeros.
- Measured at the encoder output on main, graph vs eager has a relative L2 error of up to 169% for a 576-token image. Eager vs eager in a different batch varies by only 0.2–2.7%.
- This PR does not fix that: 576-token images are still wrong with it. #65453 registers the padding and fixes it; with both applied, the error is back within the eager variation.

**Not a duplicate:**
- #60112 (open) falls back to eager when a replay exceeds a capture buffer.
- #43403 (closed draft) proposed an eager fallback for `T > frames_per_item`.
- #65453 (open) registers `cu_seqlens` padding for GLM-4.1V and Kimi-K2.5.

None of these changes the capture size. #65453 touches the same padding path but no lines in common; with this PR, capture and replay still use the same per-graph frame count.
