title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Fix FlashInfer ViT attention for GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash
author: Pb314314
body:
## Overview

With `--mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER`, the GLM-4.1V/4.5V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash vision encoders fail on main, in eager mode and with encoder CUDA graphs alike.

This PR fixes their attention so FlashInfer runs and matches the other ViT backends. The default backend's output does not change.

## Claims

- **FlashInfer now works on all three models.** On main, every forward asserts `sequence_lengths is not None`. With this PR, FlashInfer's output differs from FlashAttention's by the same amount as `TORCH_SDPA`'s does.
- **Batching is now correct.** With only the assert fixed, every sequence after the first in a batch read the wrong `v`:
  - outputs were off by 166% relative L2, or NaN;
  - capturing a 1024-token encoder graph hit an illegal memory access.
  
  With this PR, an image's output in a batch matches its output alone within 0.2%, in either batch order.
- **Default backend unchanged.** FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main. Encoder latency is 1.5% lower, since `v` is no longer copied.

## Validation

**Setup.**
- GB200, bf16, TP1.
- Baseline is main at 2a777ce26e; this PR is the same commit plus the change.

**Method.**
- Each image is a fresh random image of 224x224 to 896x672.
- Every value is the relative L2 error `‖a − b‖ / ‖b‖` of the vision encoder output.

**Backend agreement (eager).** In the cross-backend columns below, FlashInfer is this PR; FlashAttention and SDPA are main. "Batched" is the largest error of an image's output in a 5-image batch against its output alone, over both batch orders.

| Model | Weights | FlashInfer, main | FlashInfer vs FlashAttention | SDPA vs FlashAttention | FlashInfer, batched vs alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking | real | AssertionError | 2.55–2.82% | 2.42–2.88% | ≤ 0.21% |
| GLM-OCR | real | AssertionError | 4.20–5.72% | 3.93–6.72% | ≤ 0.26% |
| GLM-5.3-Flash (vision tower only) | random, seeded | AssertionError | 2.81–2.94% | 2.81–2.91% | ≤ 0.34% |

GLM-5.3-Flash uses the real `config.json` and processor with seeded random vision weights, because the full checkpoint was not available.

**Encoder CUDA graphs with FlashInfer (GLM-4.1V, `max_model_len=8192`, video enabled).**
- Graph vs eager is ≤ 0.20% for 6 single images (64–576 tokens) and 4 videos (256–768 tokens).
- Replaying after a larger batch has dirtied the capture buffers gives identical output.
- This holds with and without #65453.
- On main, capture fails.

**Default backend.**
- GLM-4.1V, GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash FlashAttention outputs are bitwise identical to main: single images, batches in both orders, and GLM-4.1V graph replays.
- GLM-4.1V encoder latency was measured over 34 batches of 1–200 images (64–13,800 tokens). Each value is the median of 15 runs. Runs went baseline, this PR, this PR, baseline, and each batch keeps the faster pass.

| | This PR / baseline (geomean) | Slowest batch | Batches > 2% slower | Baseline pass-to-pass spread (median) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 0.985 | 0.996 | 0 / 34 | 0.13% |
| Eager | 0.984 | 1.001 | 0 / 34 | 0.35% |

**FlashInfer vs FlashAttention latency (GLM-4.1V, with this PR).**
- This PR is a correctness fix; it does not make FlashInfer faster. FlashAttention (FA4) stays the default backend.
- Measured over the same 34 batches as above, alternating FlashAttention, FlashInfer, FlashInfer, FlashAttention, keeping the faster pass per batch.
- Every FlashInfer batch matched eager within the graph-vs-eager tolerance.

| | FlashInfer / FlashAttention (geomean) | Range | Batches > 2% slower |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph replay | 1.003 | 0.989–1.032 | 2 / 34 |
| Eager | 1.041 | 0.999–1.159 | 10 / 34 |

- **With graphs:** the two backends are within 1.1% for batches above 1,300 tokens. Smaller batches are up to 3.2% slower with FlashInfer.
- **In eager mode:** most batches up to 1,100 tokens are 12–16% slower with FlashInfer, where per-call host overhead dominates. Above 1,300 tokens they are within 2%.

**Tests.**
- This PR adds GLM-4.1V to `test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs`, which runs FlashInfer with encoder CUDA graphs on image and video batches. It fails on main (`assert sequence_lengths is not None`) and passes with this PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`: 78 passed.
- `pre-commit` passes.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```python
# Fails on main with AssertionError; runs with this PR.
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

llm = LLM("zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking", max_model_len=8192,
          mm_encoder_attn_backend="FLASHINFER", limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 2})
P = ("[gMASK]<sop><|user|>\n<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
     "Describe the image.<|assistant|>assistant\n")
im = Image.fromarray(np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 255, (448, 448, 3), dtype=np.uint8))
print(llm.generate([{"prompt": P, "multi_modal_data": {"image": im}}],
                   SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8))[0].outputs[0].text)
```

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py::test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs -k glm4_1v
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** The FlashInfer ViT path, `flashinfer_wrapper` (cuDNN batch prefill), needs two things these models did not provide.

1. **`sequence_lengths`.**
   - GLM-4.1V's `prepare_encoder_metadata` already computes it, but the vision transformer never passes it to its blocks.
   - GLM-OCR and GLM-5.3-Flash do not compute it in eager mode either. They also build plain `cu_seqlens` there, rather than FlashInfer's offset layout from `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens`.
2. **The `v` layout.**
   - `maybe_recompute_cu_seqlens` gives q/k token offsets of `hidden_size` and v offsets of `3 * hidden_size`. It expects `v` to be a view into the fused qkv output, as in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL.
   - The GLM attention made `v` contiguous, so its token stride was `hidden_size`. Every sequence after the first then read `v` at three times its real offset.

**Fix.**
- Thread `sequence_lengths` through the GLM vision attention and blocks.
- Keep `v` as a view: `.contiguous()` now applies only to `q` and `k`, which RoPE copies anyway.
- On the eager paths, build FlashInfer's metadata when FlashInfer is selected:
  - GLM-5.3-Flash reuses its existing `prepare_encoder_metadata`;
  - GLM-OCR calls the same `MMEncoderAttention` helpers inline, because its inherited `prepare_encoder_metadata` needs position embeddings that GLM-OCR removes.
- Other backends keep their existing code paths.

**Not covered.** GLM-5.3-Flash with encoder CUDA graphs was not run end to end: the full checkpoint was not available. Its graph path uses the same metadata keys as GLM-4.1V, which was tested.

**Related.** #65453 aligns FlashInfer's `cu_seqlens` between capture and replay for GLM and Kimi-K2.5. It touches different lines and composes with this PR; the graph results above hold with and without it.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds FlashInfer ViT support for the GLM vision encoders. #65453 assumes FlashInfer already runs on these models.

title: [Perf] Vectorize silu_and_mul_per_block_quant for large inputs
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` launches one 128-thread block per (token, group). Each thread issues one 2-byte load, and the group max is a shared-memory tree reduction. At prefill sizes the kernel runs at ~0.9 TB/s on H200. It is therefore 1.3-2.2x *slower* than the unfused `silu_and_mul` + `per_token_group_quant_fp8` pair it replaces.

This PR adds a vectorized variant (16B loads, warp-shuffle reduction, 8B stores) for large inputs. The existing kernel stays for small inputs, where it has lower latency. Both produce bitwise-identical results.

## Claims

- At >= 16k rows the fused kernel is 2.0-2.45x faster than before, and now 8-53% faster than the unfused pair. At <= 64 rows (decode) it is unchanged. See the table below.
- Paths that use the fused kernel today get faster prefill:
  - the Triton FP8 MoE with `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0`;
  - the `SiluMul+BlockQuant` compile fusion, where it matches.
- Prerequisite for #65794, which enables the fused path by default (superseding #64906 and #43399). With the old kernel, that change costs -3.8% prefill on Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8.

## Validation

**Kernel:** H200, bf16 in, fp8 out, group 128, CUDA-graph timed, p10 µs.

| 2I | rows | unfused (silu_and_mul + group quant) | fused, main | fused, this PR | vs main |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 8 | 3.80 | 1.87 | **1.84** | 1.02x |
| 512 | 64 | 4.02 | 2.17 | **2.00** | 1.08x |
| 512 | 512 | 4.51 | 2.70 | **2.53** | 1.07x |
| 512 | 4096 | 7.49 | 7.54 | **4.63** | 1.63x |
| 512 | 16384 | 18.77 | 23.88 | **12.04** | 1.98x |
| 512 | 65536 | 64.88 | 98.58 | **42.49** | 2.32x |
| 1536 | 8 | 3.88 | 1.88 | **1.91** | 0.98x |
| 1536 | 64 | 4.05 | 2.07 | **2.07** | 1.00x |
| 1536 | 512 | 4.59 | 3.94 | **3.29** | 1.20x |
| 1536 | 4096 | 10.98 | 18.25 | **9.48** | 1.93x |
| 1536 | 16384 | 36.93 | 74.68 | **32.52** | 2.30x |
| 1536 | 65536 | 133.29 | 292.75 | **121.94** | 2.40x |
| 4096 | 8 | 3.97 | 1.98 | **1.97** | 1.01x |
| 4096 | 64 | 4.18 | 2.54 | **2.53** | 1.00x |
| 4096 | 512 | 5.95 | 7.38 | **4.60** | 1.60x |
| 4096 | 4096 | 25.55 | 48.17 | **22.28** | 2.16x |
| 4096 | 16384 | 91.15 | 197.16 | **82.37** | 2.39x |
| 4096 | 65536 | 349.48 | 783.51 | **320.24** | 2.45x |
| 24576 | 8 | 5.73 | 2.32 | **2.31** | 1.00x |
| 24576 | 64 | 6.37 | 5.98 | **3.95** | 1.51x |
| 24576 | 512 | 20.94 | 34.80 | **17.11** | 2.03x |
| 24576 | 4096 | 144.98 | 293.35 | **121.90** | 2.41x |
| 24576 | 16384 | 560.98 | 1166.89 | **478.78** | 2.44x |

**End to end:** `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8`, H200 TP1, `--moe-backend auto` (Triton), `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0` (the configuration where main already uses the fused kernel). Two runs per arm, interleaved.

| | prefill in tok/s | mixed out tok/s | TPOT c1 | TPOT c8 | TPOT c32 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (run 1 / run 2) | 65,752 / 64,061 | 7,630 / 7,781 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.86 / 5.85 | 8.33 / 8.54 |
| this PR (run 1 / run 2) | **67,634 / 69,375** | 7,855 / 7,829 | 3.92 / 3.90 | 5.89 / 5.87 | 8.45 / 8.24 |

Prefill is +5.6% (mean of two), mixed +1.7%, and decode unchanged. Workloads, all `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --ignore-eos`:
- prefill: 4096 in / 1 out, concurrency 64, 256 prompts
- mixed: 1024 / 512, concurrency 128
- decode: 1024 / 256 at concurrency 1/8/32

With the default `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` the Triton MoE path does not use the fused kernel on main, so this PR is a no-op there today.

**Tests:**
- New `test_silu_and_mul_per_block_quant_vec_matches_scalar`: the vectorized path vs the scalar path, forced by a 2-byte-misaligned view of the same input. It asserts bitwise equality over bf16/fp16, fp8/int8, group sizes 64/128, and both scale layouts.
- The existing reference tests already hit the vectorized path through their large shapes (512x5120, 256x14336, and the int32-offset-overflow case).
- `tests/kernels/core/test_fused_silu_mul_block_quant.py`: 347 passed (331 on main, plus the 16 new cases).
- `tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_{,manual_}fusion.py`: 126 passed, the same as main.

## Details

**Mapping:** each group is handled by `group_size / 8` lanes (16 for group 128), each owning 8 contiguous elements of gate and up. The max is reduced with `__shfl_xor_sync` over those lanes, and lane 0 writes the scale.

**Dispatch:** the vectorized kernel is used for 16-bit inputs with 16B-aligned input and 8B-aligned output, when `num_tokens * num_groups >= 3072`. The threshold is measured: at <= 2048 groups the one-block-per-group kernel is ~0.4-0.9 µs faster, and above ~3072 groups the vectorized one wins. Misaligned views fall back to the existing kernel.

**Arithmetic:** identical to the existing kernel (`gate * (1 / (1 + exp(-gate))) * up`, `max(amax / qmax, min_scale)`, `x / scale`). The file is not built with `--use_fast_math`.

**Overlaps:**
- #62386 edits the same file (TMA-aligned scale stride). The changes are orthogonal, but whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- #43399 (UE8M0 option) also touches this kernel; the vectorized variant takes the same template flags if both land.

**Duplicate check:** no open PR changes this kernel's performance.

title: [Perf][Core] Reduce per-block CPU cost of KV block allocation and caching
author: njhill
body:
## Overview

Reduces the per-block Python work on the scheduler's main thread when an async KV load starts, is promoted to running, and finishes. These costs grow linearly with prompt length, and on a DP decode instance a slow `schedule()` on one rank holds up the per-step all-reduce.

Related: #61725 limits load starts per step to contain this cost; this makes each load cheaper. #64379 and #65285 target the repeated reservation sum, which is a separate cost.

## Claims

- For a 140K-token request, start + promote + finish CPU time drops about 50% on a DeepSeek-V4.1-shaped KV layout (2.66 to 1.34 ms) and about 45% with one group at block size 16 (10.55 to 5.79 ms).
- Source changes are net neutral in size (+51/-49 lines), and two properties are removed.
- No behaviour change intended. These paths are shared by all requests, so non-P/D traffic benefits too.

**Not yet shown:** an end-to-end improvement. These are scheduler-only numbers, with no real P/D run, so the effect on `schedule()` time and GPU wait in serving is unmeasured.

## Validation

### Timing

Real `Scheduler` and NIXL scheduler connector, with no GPU or transfer. GB200 host (aarch64), Python 3.12, 32 requests per run. Each value is the median of 3 rounds, each round being the median of 5 runs, interleaved with the baseline on one node. Spread between rounds was about 1-5%. ms per request, 140K tokens:

| Phase | DSv4.1 layout, before | After | Change | One group, block size 16, before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Start, fresh blocks | 0.71 | 0.33 | -54% | 2.60 | 1.03 | -60% |
| Promote to running | 1.01 | 0.65 | -36% | 5.97 | 3.76 | -37% |
| Finish | 0.95 | 0.36 | -62% | 1.98 | 1.00 | -50% |
| **Start + promote + finish** | **2.66** | **1.34** | **-50%** | **10.55** | **5.79** | **-45%** |
| Start, evicting cached blocks | 0.99 | 0.72 | -27% | 5.43 | 4.51 | -17% |

The "DSv4.1 layout" is a hand-built model of the KV groups read from the code: compressed MLA at 128 (SM10x), MLA sliding window at 32, one ring block at 8, hash block size 32. **The 128-token window and single compressed group are assumptions**, not confirmed from a real startup log.

These numbers predate the final `get_new_blocks` loop split, which was only measured in isolation: 8,750 fresh blocks, caching on and metrics off, 2.75 to 1.98 ms (-28%), faster in 6 of 6 paired rounds on a noisy x86 laptop with Python 3.13. Treat that size as approximate. The table above is therefore, if anything, slightly conservative for fresh starts.

### Tests

Run on the GB200 cluster against `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`, `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache`, `test_scheduler.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `test_deferred_block_free.py`, `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`, `test_contiguous_kv_packing.py`, `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload` and `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`.

- 19 tests fail on both this change and the baseline when run serially, with none unique to either. The errors sampled were gated models, engine startup and environment problems. **They give no signal here**, and some exercise the block pool (for example `test_cpu_offloading`, `test_tiering_offloading`), so CI results for them matter.
- There was no single clean full run. The full set ran once with the GPU hidden and an incomplete tree (4,048 passed), and failures were then re-run with a GPU and compared against baseline.
- **These runs predate the final `get_new_blocks` loop split**, which has not been through the tests yet. It reads as behaviour-preserving, and CI on this PR will be its first test run.
- The new `test_estimate_cached_tokens_tracks_hashed_prefix_of_each_group` uses a real `KVCacheManager` and passes on both this change and the baseline, as expected for a change that shouldn't alter results.

`ruff` passes. `mypy` was run on the changed files with imports skipped, which is weaker than the repo's hook.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script and commands</summary>

Run from outside the repo root, with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at the checkout:

```bash
# DSv4.1 layout
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= PROF_BLOCK_SIZE=128 PYTHONPATH=<checkout> python prof.py timing dsv41 32 140000
# One group, block size 16
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= PYTHONPATH=<checkout> python prof.py timing one 32 140000
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Async KV load CPU cost: real Scheduler + NIXL scheduler connector, no GPU/transfer.
usage: prof.py timing <config> <n> <tokens> | prof.py cprofile <config> <n> <tokens>
Prints one JSON line of ms/request per phase in timing mode."""
import cProfile, gc, json, logging, os, pstats, sys, time
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS", "1")
import torch
from tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.utils import (create_model_runner_output, create_request,
    create_scheduler, create_vllm_config)
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (CircularBufferSpec, FullAttentionSpec, KVCacheConfig,
    KVCacheGroupSpec, MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec, SlidingWindowSpec)
logging.disable(logging.WARNING)
BS = int(os.environ.get("PROF_BLOCK_SIZE", "16"))

SWA_BS = 32; RING_BS = 8; WINDOW = 128  # DSv4.1 layout; WINDOW is an assumption

def build_dsv41(n, tokens):
    """DeepSeek-V4.1 KV layout: compressed MLA at BS (backend-chosen), MLA SWA fixed at 32, one ring block."""
    c = create_vllm_config(max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=1280, block_size=BS, max_model_len=tokens+1000)
    common = dict(num_kv_heads=1, head_size=512, dtype=torch.uint8)
    num_blocks = (n+1)*(tokens//BS + 2 + WINDOW//SWA_BS + 4)
    kcc = KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["mla"], MLAAttentionSpec(block_size=BS, **common)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["swa"], SlidingWindowMLASpec(block_size=SWA_BS, sliding_window=WINDOW, **common)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["ring"], CircularBufferSpec(block_size=RING_BS, head_size_v=0, **common)),
    ])
    assert [g.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable for g in kcc.kv_cache_groups][:2] == [True, True]
    return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_config=kcc, hash_block_size=SWA_BS)

def build(config, n, tokens):
    if config == "dsv41":
        return build_dsv41(n, tokens)
    c = create_vllm_config(max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=1280, block_size=BS, max_model_len=tokens+1000)
    per_req = tokens // BS + 2
    if config == "one":
        return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=(n+1)*per_req)
    assert config == "swa"
    # Full attention + a sliding window group: the multi-group shape.
    num_blocks = 2*(n+1)*per_req
    kw = dict(block_size=BS, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=1, dtype=torch.float32)
    kcc = KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_tensors=[], kv_cache_groups=[
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["full"], FullAttentionSpec(**kw)),
        KVCacheGroupSpec(["swa"], SlidingWindowSpec(sliding_window=128*BS, **kw)),
    ])
    return create_scheduler(c, num_blocks=num_blocks, kv_cache_config=kcc)

def reqs(n, tokens, hash_bs=None):
    return [create_request(block_size=hash_bs or BS, num_tokens=tokens, max_tokens=1, do_remote_prefill=True,
                           num_remote_blocks=tokens//BS) for _ in range(n)]

class Phases:
    """Runs start -> promote -> finish -> start-over-evictable, each via `run(name, fn)`."""
    def __init__(self, run, config, n, tokens):
        r = build(config, n, tokens)
        hb = SWA_BS if config == "dsv41" else None
        rs = reqs(n, tokens, hb); rs2 = reqs(n, tokens, hb)
        gc.collect(); gc.freeze()  # as the engine does at startup
        for q in rs: r.add_request(q)
        out = run("start_fresh", r.schedule)
        assert len(r.running) == 0 and sum(q.status.name == "WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS" for q in rs) == n, "not all started"
        r.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output([], finished_recving={q.request_id for q in rs}))
        out = run("promote", r.schedule)
        assert len(r.running) == n
        run("finish", lambda: r.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output(list(r.running))))
        for q in rs2: r.add_request(q)
        run("start_evict", r.schedule)
        started = sum(q.status.name == "WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS" for q in rs2)
        assert started == n, f"started {started}"

def timing(config, n, tokens, reps=5):
    res = {}
    for _ in range(reps):
        def run(name, fn):
            gc.disable()
            t = time.perf_counter(); o = fn(); d = time.perf_counter()-t
            gc.enable()
            res.setdefault(name, []).append(d*1e3/n)
            return o
        Phases(run, config, n, tokens); gc.unfreeze()
    print(json.dumps({"config": config, "n": n, "tokens": tokens, **{k: round(sorted(v)[len(v)//2], 3) for k, v in res.items()}}))

def prof(config, n, tokens):
    def run(name, fn):
        p = cProfile.Profile(); p.enable(); o = fn(); p.disable()
        print(f"\n## cProfile {config} {name} (n={n}, overhead inflates Python calls)")
        st = pstats.Stats(p, stream=sys.stdout); st.sort_stats("tottime").print_stats(14)
        return o
    Phases(run, config, n, tokens)

mode, config, n, tokens = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
(timing if mode == "timing" else prof)(config, n, tokens)
```

</details>

## Details

| Change | Why it's cheaper | Relies on |
|---|---|---|
| `block_hash` and `block_hash_num_tokens` become plain fields | No Python call per read in hot loops | Fields are now publicly writable. In `vllm/`, they are set through `set_block_hash`, `reset_hash` and one constructor call in the UMBP connector |
| Skip eviction for unhashed blocks in `get_new_blocks`; early return in `_remove_cached_block_hashes` | Most allocated blocks were never cached | A block only has secondary hashes alongside a primary one |
| Separate loops per mode in `get_new_blocks` | No per-block metrics check on the default path | |
| `_insert_block_hash` only checks `contain` when the block already has a hash | One dict lookup instead of two in the common case | A block with no hash has no cache entries |
| Pack the group id once per `cache_full_blocks` call | No `to_bytes` and helper call per block | |
| Reverse scan in `estimate_cached_tokens` | Stops at the last hashed block instead of visiting them all | Hash coverage never decreases along a block table, including partial and Mamba entries |
| `len([...])` instead of `sum(<genexpr>)` in the NIXL pull scheduler | No generator resume per block | |

**Tradeoffs:**
- With `kv_cache_metrics` on (off by default), every block still takes the eviction call so `on_block_evicted` can run, so that path gains less. That mode wasn't measured in the full benchmark, and the isolated measurement above was inconclusive for it.
- `get_new_blocks` now has three near-identical loops.

**The block size assumption matters for evaluating this work.** The 8,750-blocks-per-request figure comes from a block size 16, single-group setup, including part 1 of #61725. By my reading of the code, DSv4.1 on NVIDIA uses 128 or 64 for its main group, chosen by the backend, so a real load costs about a quarter of the block-size-16 figure before this change. For the same reason, changing the default in #63231 shouldn't affect DSv4.1 on NVIDIA. At block size 64 with one group, this change still gives about -42% (3.04 to 1.75 ms).

title: [Kernel][Perf] Fused GDN MTP: Support DSpark K=8 and use idle SMs at small batch sizes
author: tomasruizt
body:
## Overview This PR makes two changes to the fused GDN MTP decode kernel: 1. **K=8 support:** DSpark K=8 (9 tokens per request) fell back to the slower Triton path. The kernel now handles 9 tokens. Overlaps with #53070. 2. **Split-V:** at small batch sizes, each value head is split over a cluster of 2 or 4 thread blocks to use idle SMs (SM90+). With Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and DSpark K=8, this PR increases output throughput over main by 18% on B300 and 13% on H100 with a single request. With 8 or more concurrent requests, the gain is 6% to 9% on B300 (measured up to 128 requests) and 2% to 6% on H100 (measured up to 32 requests). ## Claims - DSpark K=8 decode steps now use the fused kernel. On main they silently fall back to the Triton delta-rule + gated RMSNorm path in every GDN layer, because the kernel accepts at most 8 tokens. - The cluster split (SM90+) cuts the fused kernel time at 1 request from 22.3µs to 10.2µs on B300 and from 26.2µs to 14.3µs on H100. From 8 requests on, where it does not split, the kernel is 0.4% to 0.9% faster. It also speeds up K=7 by 8% at c1, which already used the fused kernel. - MTP3 does not regress: output throughput rises 2% to 3% at c1 and c2, and matches main from c4 on. - Outputs unchanged: GSM8K and acceptance length match main. ## E2E Benchmarks Serving benchmark. main is `5225a1f17f` (main on 2026-11-04), and this PR is based on it. B300 uses the bf16 model, H100 uses `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8` (bf16 does not fit): ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --language-model-only \ --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-speculator.dspark","num_speculative_tokens":8}' ``` Client: AIPerf 0.13, config and command below. Output tok/s is measured over the steady window, which opens once the first c requests complete. Every reported point passed the validity checks (no errors, preemptions or queueing, server saturated).
AIPerf config and command One run per (repeat, concurrency) cell against the same server. The second repeat goes through the concurrencies in reverse order. `throughput_1k.jsonl` is the SPEED-Bench throughput 1k split. On H100, `model` is `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`. ```yaml schemaVersion: "2.0" randomSeed: 42 benchmark: model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B endpoint: url: http://127.0.0.1:8000 type: chat streaming: true use_server_token_count: true timeout: 120 extra: temperature: 0 max_completion_tokens: 1024 chat_template_kwargs: enable_thinking: false tokenizer: name: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B datasets: - name: main type: file path: throughput_1k.jsonl format: speed_bench_throughput_1k sampling: shuffle random_seed: 42 phases: - name: profiling type: concurrency concurrency: C duration: D grace_period: 120 server_metrics: enabled: true urls: [http://127.0.0.1:8000/metrics] formats: [json] artifacts: dir: artifacts/rR-cC summary: [json] records: [jsonl] runtime: ui: none ``` ```bash duration() { d=30; l=32; while [ $1 -gt $l ]; do d=$((d + 10)); l=$((l * 2)); done; echo $d; } for R in 1 2 3; do CS="1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128 256"; [ $R = 2 ] && CS="256 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1" for C in $CS; do sed "s/concurrency: C/concurrency: $C/; s/duration: D/duration: $(duration $C)/; s|artifacts/rR-cC|artifacts/r$R-c$C|" aiperf.yaml > cell.yaml aiperf profile --config cell.yaml done done ```

The new 4- and 16-request cases cover the split=2 and split=1 paths. The existing cases have at most 3 requests, so they always split on B300 and H100. In CI, `kernels/fla` runs on B200 and `kernels/mamba` on H200 MIG, so both exercise the split path. ## Details **9 tokens.** DSpark K=8 verifies 8 drafts plus the bonus token, so `state_indices` has width 9 and `_can_use_fused_gdn_mtp_decode` rejected it. Raising `kMaxMtpTokens` alone is not enough: the kernel assigned one warp per token and has 8 warps, so the 9th token was skipped. Warps now stride over tokens. Static shared memory at 9 tokens with fp32 state is ~45.6KB, under the 48KB static limit. **Related work.** - #53070 adds the same 9-token support as a separate width-9 template specialization next to the width-8 one. It has had no activity since Aug 31 and predates the move of the kernel to `csrc/gdn/`. This PR raises the cap in place instead (one kernel, warps stride over tokens). The cluster split does not depend on how the 9-token support lands, so it can be rebased onto #53070 if that one is preferred. - benchislett/vllm#8 (draft) extends fused GDN verification to 12 and 16 tokens (K=11 and K=15) on SM107, with a separate wide kernel that is used when the width exceeds `kMaxMtpTokens`. It complements this PR: with both, 9 tokens would use the kernel changed here and 12 or 16 tokens the wide kernel. - #54612 speeds up the Triton spec-decode recurrence for Qwen3-Next, which is the path that DSpark K=8 falls back to on main. This PR moves K=8 off that path to the fused CUDA kernel. **Cluster split.** At small batch sizes the kernel launches one CTA per (request, value head), e.g. 32 CTAs on 148 SMs at batch size 1. On SM90+, each head's V rows are split over a cluster of 2 or 4 CTAs (`blockIdx.z`) while the grid still fits in one wave at 2 CTAs per SM. Each CTA loads and updates its slice of the state. The gated RMSNorm sums the partial sums of squares of the cluster through distributed shared memory, with a final cluster barrier so no CTA exits while others read its shared memory. Without a split, the kernel keeps its single-pass epilogue, so batch sizes of 8 and more are unchanged. On B300 and H100 (HV=32) the split is 4 up to 2 requests, 2 at 4 requests, 1 from 8 requests. **Tradeoffs and limitations.** - The split choice is a host-side heuristic from the SM count, no tuning table. It queries two device attributes on the host per launch, with no GPU sync. - SM80 to SM89 never split. There, the split kernels compile to a trap stub to keep them out of the binary. - Validated on B300 and H100 only. SM100 and SM120 take the same path but were not tested. - Each kernel instantiation now has three split variants. Compiling this file for all 7 target archs (one nvcc 13.0 call with `--compress-mode=size`) takes 71s instead of 36s, and the object grows from 0.41MB to 0.90MB. - Mixed prefill and decode batches still use the unfused path, as before. They are CUDA graphed on main. CC @Jie-Fang @ZJY0516 @gau-nernst @vadiklyutiy @benchislett @BabyDrangoner 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip DP padding rows in TRT-LLM monolithic MoE with vLLM's top-k
author: Pb314314
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## 1. Why this change

Under data parallelism (DP), every DP rank pads its batch to the largest batch on any rank. The FlashInfer TRT-LLM **monolithic** MoE kernels are the default on Blackwell for block-FP8 and MXFP8 checkpoints. They route from the router logits themselves, so padded rows pick experts like real tokens, and the kernel loads and computes those experts.

`VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` (on by default) cannot help here. It works by having vLLM's routers write expert id -1 for padded rows, and the monolithic kernels never call vLLM's routers.

Padding under DP is large:
- In decode steps with up to 32 rows per rank, 34-65% of rows are padding.
- In mixed (prefill + decode) steps, 37-84% of rows are padding, because every rank pads to the rank running prefill.

## 2. What this PR changes

Under DP, the runner routes with vLLM's top-k, where padded rows get -1, and then calls the kernel's precomputed-routing op (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`), which skips those rows. There is no new option: the existing `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns it off (its doc comment now says so).

- `FusedMoEExpertsMonolithic.apply_precomputed_routing` and `supports_precomputed_routing`, implemented for TRT-LLM block FP8 and MXFP8 (`TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`). The kwargs shared with the logits call move to one helper.
- `prepare_routed` for the NaiveDPEP monolithic prepare/finalize: it all-gathers top-k ids and weights instead of logits.
- `MoERunner` takes the routed path under DP.
  - Routers that do not mask padding themselves (`masks_padding` False, e.g. grouped top-k outside DeepEP v2) get the mask applied after top-k in the runner.
  - Routed-expert capture receives the gathered top-k ids, in the same layout as the monolithic kernel's `routing_replay_out`.
  - `routed_scaling_factor` is applied exactly once, as on the modular path: either by the router on the weights or by the runner on the output. The routed kernel call gets `None`.
- FlashInfer autotune tunes the op that runs. Under DP, the autotune cache key now records that the routed op is used, so a cache saved before this PR (which has only the logits op) does not hit and skip tuning. Only models with a MoE layer that can take the routed path get the new key; every other deployment keeps its key and its saved cache.

## 3. When the new path runs

Every MoE forward of the target model where all of these hold:
- Blackwell (SM100) with block-FP8 or MXFP8 MoE weights;
- DP > 1, either with EP and the default `allgather_reducescatter` all2all backend (DeepEP and other all2all backends use modular kernels and are unaffected), or without EP (the MoE layer is then TP-sharded across the DP ranks and always uses the naive DP all-gather, whatever the all2all backend);
- no EPLB and no sequence parallel;
- a routing method the TRT-LLM monolithic FP8 kernel supports;
- `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default);
- the routing simulator (`VLLM_MOE_ROUTING_SIMULATION_STRATEGY`) off. The simulator works by feeding the kernel synthetic logits, so it keeps the logits op.

The decision depends only on DP size, so every DP rank takes the same path. This matters because the two paths dispatch different tensors in the all-gather.

| router | models | validation |
|---|---|---|
| softmax top-k (`FusedTopKRouter`) | Qwen3 MoE, Qwen3-Next / 3.5 / 3.8 FP8 | unit tests + serving (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8) |
| sigmoid + bias (`FusedTopKBiasRouter`, MiniMax2) | MiniMax-M2 / M3 | unit tests + serving (MiniMax-M3-MXFP8) |
| grouped top-k (`GroupedTopKRouter`, DeepSeekV3 routing) | DeepSeek-V3/R1, Kimi-K2, GLM-4.5+ FP8 | unit test vs the kernel's own grouped routing + serving (GLM-5.3-FP8, DP8 + EP) |

**No size threshold.** The top-k launch is a fixed cost per MoE layer. A threshold on batch size would leave out mixed steps, which are the most padded, and would need tuning per model. The cost of having none is on small-expert models at high concurrency (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, section 4.2): some large decode steps are slower, while throughput stays within noise. A FlashInfer-side padding mask would remove the top-k launch: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9000. The runner could then pass the mask instead.

### 3.1 Why only under DP + EP, not TP

**In short:** TP pads almost nothing, so the top-k launch has nothing to save. Forcing the path on under TP4 gives no throughput gain (table below), so it runs only with DP. All DP measurements in this PR are DP + EP; DP without EP also takes the path but is not measured here.

How much of the MoE input is padding. For each step: padded rows / all rows the MoE layers process, summed over DP ranks (TP has one), i.e. 1 - real tokens / (DP ranks x padded batch per rank). Averaged over the steps of Baseline serving runs. Steps are grouped by kind and by the padded batch per rank:

| step kind | DP4 / DP8 (Qwen, M3, GLM) | TP4 (Qwen, M3) |
|---|---|---|
| decode, <=32 rows | 34-65% | 0-0.4% |
| decode, 33-512 rows | 11-22% | 2-5% |
| mixed (prefill + decode) | 37-84% | 4-16% |

In the kernel table (section 4.3), the top-k path loses at 0% padding and only breaks even around 20%.

To check, I forced the same path on under TP4 (a local patch, not in this PR) with MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, which has the largest experts of the three models and so is the best case for this path. Each side was launched twice. Measured on an earlier base (871147447b); the TP path is unchanged since.

| concurrency | throughput, tok/s: Baseline | top-k path forced on | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 791 / 875 | 836 / 862 | +1.9% (within noise) |
| 16 | 1730 / 1681 | 1634 / 1766 | -0.3% (within noise) |
| 64 | 4177 / 4404 | 4308 / 4481 | +2.4% (within noise) |

## 4. Measured results

Summary:
- **Higher serving throughput for large-expert models under DP + EP:** GLM-5.3-FP8 (DP8) +9% / +26% / +27% at concurrency 8 / 16 / 64; MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 (DP4) +13% / +4% / +5% at concurrency 4 / 16 / 64. Both runs better at every concurrency for both models.
- **Small-expert models break even on throughput, with slower large decode steps:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (4.9M-parameter experts, DP4) throughput is within noise at concurrency 4 to 256 (+2.1% / +1.2% / +5.5% / -0.7%). Small decode steps get faster (-4% to -17%), but large decode steps get slower in both runs: +6.4% for 33-128 rows per rank at concurrency 64, and +13.2% (33-128 rows) and +6.6% (129-512 rows) at concurrency 256. Those buckets are 18% and 16% of step time.
- **Accuracy unchanged** on all three router types (softmax top-k, sigmoid + bias, grouped top-k).
- **No gain without DP:** forcing the path on under TP4 does not change throughput beyond noise (section 3.1), so it runs only under DP.
- **Opt-out:** `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` restores main's behavior on this path. It also turns off padding skip on the modular MoE paths, as it already does on main.

Terms:
- **Baseline** = upstream main at this PR's base commit; **After PR** = this change.
- **Concurrency** = requests in flight in `vllm bench serve` (`--max-concurrency`), summed over all DP ranks.
- **Step time** = wall time of one engine step, from a per-step timestamp log on DP rank 0 (a local patch, not in this PR). **decode** steps replay a full CUDA graph; **mixed** steps also run prefill and use piecewise graphs.
- **Rows per rank** = the padded batch size per DP rank.
- Each side was launched twice. **(both runs better)** / **(both runs worse)**: both After PR launches beat (or lost to) both Baseline launches. **(within noise)**: the two sides' values interleave.

Setup:
- GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.3 (main's pin), `vllm bench serve` on ShareGPT, temperature 0.
- Baseline = main 80e0cd68f8, After PR = f13ec7ed53 (this PR on that main; the last commit only changes the routing-simulator case of the autotune key and tests). All runs in one session, launch order Baseline, After PR, After PR, Baseline on one node (two nodes for GLM).
- All three models run with speculative decoding (MTP 3 for Qwen and GLM, EAGLE3 3 for M3), so verification batches also take the new path.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8: DP4 + EP, FlashInfer autotune on. MiniMax-M3-MXFP8: DP4 + EP, autotune off. GLM-5.3-FP8: DP8 + EP on two nodes, autotune off on both sides (section 5).

<details>
<summary>Serve commands</summary>

```bash

vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, DP4 + EP
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --block-size 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true,"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8","minimax_m3_msa_decode_backend":"cutlass"}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"eagle3","model":"<m3-eagle3>","num_speculative_tokens":3,"attention_backend":"FLASHINFER","use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
# GLM-5.3-FP8, DP8 + EP over two nodes (4 local ranks each)
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-model-len 32768 --tokenizer-mode glm5_next --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# Benchmark (ShareGPT, 4-6 prompts per unit of concurrency, at least 32)
vllm bench serve --dataset-name sharegpt --temperature 0 --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --seed 0
```
</details>

### 4.1 Correctness

Unit tests:

```
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_routing.py tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_naive_dp_ep_dbo.py tests/kernels/moe/test_grouped_topk.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routing_simulator.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_routed_experts_capture_monolithic.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py
```

On this PR head (a7442ffcf4), one GB200: 1345 passed, 2 skipped (a column-major-scale case that only applies to [128, 128] blocks), 0 failed.

New tests:
- `test_trtllm_fp8_monolithic_routed_skips_padding[block / mxfp8 / block-grouped]`: on one GPU, on the same quantized input, the experts' routed op equals the monolithic op (the kernel's own routing) on real rows and gives zero on padded rows. Routers covered:
  - softmax top-k (block FP8);
  - sigmoid + bias with routed scaling 2.0 (MXFP8);
  - DeepSeek-V3 grouped top-k (8 groups, top-4 groups, sigmoid + bias, routed scaling 2.5; block FP8).

  Breaking the scaling on the vLLM side makes the grouped case fail.
- `test_runner_routes_dp_padding_rows_to_no_expert[router masks / runner masks]`: under DP the runner passes int32 top-k to the routed op with padding rows at -1, both when the router masks them (real fused top-k router) and when the runner has to. Removing the runner's mask fails the second case.
- `test_runner_prepares_monolithic_logits[dp 1 / 4]`: the routing simulator still feeds the kernel its synthetic logits under DP.
- NaiveDPEP `prepare_routed` all-gathers top-k ids and weights, not logits.
- Grouped top-k outside DeepEP v2 reports `masks_padding` False.
- The autotune cache key changes under DP only for models with a routed-capable MoE layer, and not under the routing simulator.

`test_flashinfer.py` (the routed-vs-logits kernel test, SM100 only) runs in the B200 Kernels CI step, which this PR's files do not trigger, so it runs there only on full or nightly builds; I ran it on GB200 (result above). The other files run in existing MoE and model-executor steps.

GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot. At low concurrency (4 for DP4, 8 for DP8) each DP rank has about one request, so nearly every decode step is mostly padding and takes the new path; at concurrency 256, prefill and mixed steps do too. The models are not deterministic under DP, so I also compare per-question answers across runs:

| model, GSM8K concurrency | Baseline acc | After PR acc | same answer: Baseline vs Baseline | After PR vs After PR | Baseline vs After PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, c4 | 0.967 / 0.969 | 0.971 / 0.970 | 98.9% | 98.9% | 98.7% (98.4-99.2%) |

| GLM-5.3-FP8, c8 | 0.910 / 0.920 | 0.923 / 0.916 | 91.6% | 92.8% | 92.0% (91.4-92.3%) |

Accuracy differences are at most 0.016 (M3 c4) and inside the spread between same-side runs; Baseline vs After PR agreement sits within the Baseline vs Baseline and After PR vs After PR agreement.

### 4.2 Performance

**Why small experts gain less.** The new path adds vLLM's top-k, a fixed 5-15 us per MoE layer. It saves the padded rows' work:
- at small batches, the experts that only padded rows select;
- at large batches, the padded rows' GEMM rows.

Mixed steps under DP are mostly padding (37-84% of rows across the three models), because every rank pads to the rank running prefill.
- GLM-5.3 (38M-parameter experts) and MiniMax-M3 (57M) save far more than the top-k costs.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (4.9M parameters, 512 experts) saves little per row. Its large decode steps are only 11-22% padding, so there the top-k launch costs more than it saves.

Frontier models deployed with DP + EP have experts of 25-66M parameters (DeepSeek-V3/V4, Kimi-K2/K3, GLM-5, MiniMax-M3, Qwen3.8-2.4T), i.e. the GLM / M3 side.

### 4.3 Kernel view

<details>
<summary>One MoE call, top-k + routed op vs logits op</summary>

Single GB200, EP layout as served (Qwen: 128 of 512 experts, M3: 32 of 128, GLM: 32 of 256), random logits, CUDA graph, median of 5 x 50 replays, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. M is rows across all DP ranks. Change in us per call (negative = faster):

| padded share | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (M 8-4096) | MiniMax-M3 (M 8-4096) | GLM-5.3 (M 16-8192) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0% | +2 to +14 (+4% to +11%) | +3 to +21 (+1% to +6%) | +1 to +15 (+1% to +3%) |
| 20% | -2 to +9 | -1 to -25 | +2 to -140 |
| 50% | +7 to -66 | -18 to -53 | -8 to -359 |
| 75% | +2 to -72 | -27 to -119 | -19 to -553 |
</details>

### 4.4 Autotune cache key

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 DP4 with autotune on: main and this PR write different cache directories (`153f2d40…` vs `a4700ae6…`). This PR's cache holds entries for the routed op (top-k id/weight inputs) as well as the logits op, which the draft model's MoE layer still uses (below); main's holds only the logits op. After upgrading, a DP deployment of a block-FP8 / MXFP8 TRT-LLM MoE model retunes once at its first start; other deployments keep their key.

## 5. Limitations

- Only block-FP8 / MXFP8 TRT-LLM monolithic experts. NVFP4 monolithic is not selected under DP + EP; the NVFP4 modular kernel is, and the modular path already uses vLLM's routing and masks padding. FP8 per-tensor, BF16 and MXFP4 keep the kernel's routing.
- DP without EP takes the same path (same padding, same all-gather, TP-sharded experts) but is not measured in this PR.
- Small-expert models: large decode steps are slower (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next +6% to +13% at concurrency 64 / 256), with throughput within noise. `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=0` turns the path off, together with padding skip on the modular paths.
- Draft-model forward passes do not mark padding (the forward context has `is_padding` only under PCP), so MoE layers in MTP drafters keep the kernel's own routing, as on main.
- GLM-5.3-FP8 runs with FlashInfer autotune off on both sides: with autotune on, main crashed at startup on this config in earlier tests (illegal memory access in the TRT-LLM routing kernel during the autotune dummy runs); this is pre-existing and tracked separately.

## 6. Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for padding / monolithic / routed MoE / precomputed routing.
- #50759 (draft) masks padding in vLLM's routers, i.e. the modular path; it does not reach the monolithic kernels. The only overlap is masking padding after top-k for routers that cannot fuse it; this PR does that inline in the runner's routed path.
- #54109 (DeepEP v2 padded format) and #57946 (b12x padding sentinel) are other paths.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and run the experiments. I reviewed every changed line and the measurements.

title: [Perf][Quantization] Use fast SiLU intrinsics in Humming MoE activations
author: mgoin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Use fast SiLU math (`__fdividef` plus a flush-to-zero `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` exp) in the SiLU-family activation expressions that vLLM passes to Humming's `process_input`, the kernel that fuses the MoE w2 activation with input quantization. Humming compiles this kernel without fast math (`ProcessInputKernel.disable_fast_math = True`, added in vllm-project/humming#80), so SiLU currently compiles to a precise `expf` plus IEEE division. This change only affects the activation expression; Humming's quantization, Hadamard and scale math keep the precise flags.

## Claims

- Humming w2 activation+quant kernel is 16–30% faster at prefill sizes on B300, and up to ~40% for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's clamped SwiGLU (see tables).
- gpt-oss-20b end-to-end prefill throughput: +1.9% (MXFP8 activations) / +1.7% (FP8 per-token), n=3, spread ≤0.3%.
- Covers SILU / SILU_NO_MUL, clamped SiLU (SWIGLUOAI, SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE), SITU and SWIGLUSTEP. GELU (`erff`) and `tanhf` are unchanged.
- No accuracy regression: GSM8K unchanged within noise; quantized outputs are bit-identical for MXFP4/MXFP8 and differ in ~1e-6 of bytes for FP8.

## Validation

**Kernel, first commit only (ncu, `--clock-control none`, B300, SiLU-and-mul input `rows x 2N` bf16, one launch per case):**

| case | precise (main) | fast (this PR) | vLLM reference kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 out, N=2048, 65536 rows | 137.6 µs | 115.4 µs | `silu_and_mul` 132.0 µs |
| fp8 block-128, N=2048, 65536 rows | 156.5 µs | 118.4 µs | `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` 682 µs |
| mxfp4, N=2048, 65536 rows | 153.2 µs | 115.5 µs | `silu_and_mul_mxfp4_experts_quant` 171.3 µs |
| mxfp4, N=768, 65536 rows | 63.7 µs | 48.6 µs | |
| any mode, N=2048, 512 rows (decode) | ~5.5–6.3 µs | ~5.5 µs | launch-latency bound, no change |

On main, at prefill sizes the kernel is instruction-issue bound (IPC ~3.5/4, issue slots 80–87% busy, DRAM 45–55% for quantized outputs); the SiLU math dominates the instruction count.

**FTZ exp2 (second commit):** without fast math, `__expf` keeps a denormal guard (an `FSETP` and two predicated `FMUL`s per element). `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` exists on every target; it is bit-identical here because `e^x` only underflows where SiLU(a) == a. CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2, B300, `__expf` → FTZ: +4–10% at prefill sizes for quantized outputs (MXFP4, N=2048, 131072 rows: 232.6 → 215.0 µs), no change at decode sizes.

**DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash w2 shapes** (clamped SwiGLU, limit 10; block-FP8 activations as on Hopper; grouped-EP layout; CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2, B300; main → this PR):

| N (parallelism) | 128 tok | 1024 tok | 8192 tok | 16384 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2304 (EP) | 6.21 → 4.70 µs | 26.08 → 19.04 | 180.2 → 126.7 | 355.7 → 248.6 |
| 640 (TP4, padded) | 3.74 → 3.26 µs | 9.66 → 7.65 | 54.95 → 41.54 | 105.5 → 78.95 |

MXFP8 activations give the same picture.

**Hopper (H200, SM90)**, same harness (CUPTI + CUDA graphs, cold L2), Humming upstream main, default launch configs, main → this PR:

| shape | 128 tok | 1024 tok | 8192 tok | 16384 tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSv4.1 N=2304 (EP), block FP8 | 5.95 → 4.86 µs | 27.23 → 21.95 | 195.8 → 147.6 | 386.2 → 289.6 |
| DSv4.1 N=1152 (TP2), block FP8 | 4.83 → 3.78 µs | 18.30 → 13.54 | 126.2 → 89.4 | 247.1 → 175.4 |
| DSv4.1 N=640 (TP4), block FP8 | 3.23 → 2.82 µs | 10.05 → 7.94 | 61.8 → 45.5 | 122.5 → 87.8 |
| DSv4.1 N=2304, FP8 per-token | 6.91 → 5.12 µs | 28.35 → 21.40 | 185.3 → 134.0 | 364.5 → 261.8 |
| gpt-oss N=2880 (SWIGLUOAI), FP8 per-token | 5.79 → 4.61 µs | 26.14 → 19.36 | 152.9 → 118.8 | 292.7 → 230.5 |

That is +15–41% across these shapes (up to +53% for N=1152 with FP8 per-token); activation-free input quant (w13) is unchanged, as expected.

**Accuracy (through the real Humming kernel):**

- Exhaustive sweep of all 65,280 finite bf16 gate values (up=1) vs an fp64 reference: fp32 output max relative error 3.3e-6 (precise: 1.8e-7) for a ≥ -80, worst in the a ∈ [-12, -6] tail where |SiLU| < 0.015. bf16 output differs from precise on 3 of 65,280 values.
- 8192x2048 inputs (normal, heavy-tailed with outlier channels, 1e-3 scale), fast vs precise: MXFP4 and MXFP8 values and E8M0 scales bit-identical; FP8 per-token / block-128: ~10 of 16.7M bytes differ, fp32 scales within 3.2e-7 relative, dequantized error vs exact SiLU·up identical to 7 significant digits.

**Tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k humming
# 175 passed
```

`test_humming_activation_matches_framework` (already in CI via `tests/kernels/core`) compares each Humming activation against vLLM's reference in fp16/bf16/fp32 with edge and clamp values, at default tolerances.

**GSM8K** (existing Humming configs, 1319 questions, 5-shot, indexed Humming MoE GEMM, B300, main vs this PR side by side):

```bash
cd tests/evals/gsm8k && pytest -s test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=configs/humming/<list>
```

| config | path | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8-block-humming` | SILU + fp8 g128 act | 0.850 | 0.876 |
| `gpt-oss-20b-humming-act-fp8` | clamped SiLU (SWIGLUOAI) | 0.307 | 0.315 |

Differences are within run-to-run noise.

**gpt-oss-20b** (TP1, Humming MoE, B300), main vs this PR:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GPQA (`tests/evals/gpt_oss`, low reasoning, MXFP8 act) | 0.569 | 0.579 |
| GSM8K (1319 q, 5-shot, MXFP8 act) | 0.299 | 0.292 |
| prefill throughput, MXFP8 act (tok/s, n=3) | 192,964 | 196,656 (+1.9%) |
| prefill throughput, FP8 per-token act (tok/s, n=3) | 201,974 | 205,406 (+1.7%) |

```bash
vllm bench throughput --model openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend humming \
  --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 1 --num-prompts 512 --max-model-len 8192
```

The end-to-end gain is smaller than the kernel gain because this kernel is one part of each MoE layer.

## Details

- Why not enable fast math in Humming: `--use_fast_math` also implies FTZ, approximate division and approximate sqrt for the quantization/scale code, which vllm-project/humming#80 turned off on purpose. Requesting the intrinsics only in the activation string keeps that change local.
- `__fdividef` is a standard CUDA intrinsic; `ex2.approx.ftz.f32` is a single PTX instruction available on every target, not an arch-specific one.
- Edge cases: for very negative inputs `1 + exp(-a)` overflows and `__fdividef` returns 0, the correct SiLU limit; large positive inputs return `a`. The FTZ change was checked bit-exact against the `__expf` version for every changed activation over all finite bf16 gate values, in bf16 and fp32.
- Follow-up (not in this PR): Humming's `process_input` launch-config heuristic under-picks vector width (and uses multi-token blocks) on large grids on both SM90 and SM100. Fixing it upstream adds another ~1.4–1.9% end to end on gpt-oss-20b (B300) and 10–55% at the kernel level on H200 and B300; that change belongs in vllm-project/humming.
- No duplicate: the closest open PR is #59514, which changes vLLM's own `silu_and_mul_quant` CUDA kernel, not the Humming path.

title: [Bugfix] Make fused MoE expert weights contiguous before GPU copy in Llama-4
author: yuvalluria
body:
Fixes #31624.

## Summary

In `load_moe_expert_weights`, a sliced/transposed fused MoE expert weight view is passed to `weight_loader()` and copied to GPU while still non-contiguous. A non-contiguous CPU tensor's DMA transfer to GPU is dramatically slower than a contiguous one. Adds `.contiguous()` right before the `weight_loader()` call, on the already-sliced piece — not upfront on the whole weight, since a prior attempt at this fix (#32081, auto-closed by staleness, not rejected) found that naive blanket `.contiguous()` can regress smaller tensors.

## Scope note

A synthetic benchmark on H100 NVL (the real Llama-4 checkpoints, 109B-400B, don't fit on one GPU) tested three locations that could have the same issue. Only the fused MoE expert weight path (this PR) showed an unambiguous, large improvement — FP8 block-scale and Q/K rotary permute tensors were *slower* with `.contiguous()` added at their (smaller) sizes in isolation. Since MoE expert weights dominate total checkpoint bytes, this is the change with validated, measured benefit; the other two locations are deliberately excluded pending more precise real-world sizing data.

## Validation

```
torch 2.6.0a0+df5bbc09d1.nv24.11 | GPU: NVIDIA H100 NVL
=== fused MoE expert weight, basic-indexed view after transpose(-1,-2), shape [64,4096,1024] ===
non-contiguous transfer: mean=574.401ms min=536.849ms max=585.899ms
contiguous() transfer:   mean=28.911ms min=24.788ms max=103.387ms
speedup: 19.87x
```
(A first run on the same shape measured 22.35x; 19.87x on a clean isolated re-run — consistent within normal GPU/CPU scheduling noise.)

title: [Core][Kimi K3.1] KV cache and attention changes to serve Kimi K3.1 at TP8 (Kimi K3.1 split 3/5)
author: ZJY0516
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Split 3/5 of Kimi K3.1 (#65685): serve K3.1 at TP8.** This PR adds the KV cache and attention changes that the K3.1 model (split 1/5, #66030, merged) needs to serve. Splits 1/5 and 2/5 are merged, so the diff against `main` is only this split.

Not a duplicate: it is one part of #65685, split for review. The remaining splits (#65685 for ROCm, P/D and indexer top-k; #66027 for DCP) are stacked on it and do not repeat its changes.

## Claims

- **Packed hybrid KV cache rows** (BLHNC):
  - A model can size the block row that holds every layer's page itself (`get_packed_hybrid_block_size`), so no page is padded.
  - The DS-MLA blob sizes (`DS_MLA_STATE_CONTENT_BYTES`) anchor the mamba page alignment, and the size of the packed-cache MLA draft page.
  - Hybrid targets keep a layer-compact layout under DCP.
- **Kernel-block slot mapping**:
  - A packed token cache may split into kernel blocks when the runner maps its slot mappings (`AttentionGroup.map_to_kernel_slot_mapping`).
  - Speculators opt in (`maps_slot_mapping`; DFlash and DSpark do). Their draft layers form their own attention groups in the target runner, so a DFlash draft gets one more metadata builder there.
  - Backends that write even an uncompressed cache from the block table say so (`AttentionBackend.writes_kv_cache_from_block_table`).
- **Sparse MLA**:
  - A DSA layer on a dense backend raises instead of silently running full attention.
  - The fp8 query is concatenated in place before quantization (about 1 ms per layer of a 32k-token prefill).
  - A ShardQ caller (Kimi K3.1) may pass the indexer query and weights of only the rank's rows. Before, the indexer indexed them again by the gathered-row ids, which read out of bounds (a device-side assert in the first mixed prefill/decode step at TP8).
- **Kimi K3.1 model config** (`KimiK31ForConditionalGeneration` in `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP`): with DSA, the kv-cache dtype defaults to per-tensor fp8 for FlashInfer sparse MLA (the SM10x default) and `fp8_ds_mla` otherwise, and dense drafts get a dense MLA backend (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_dense_draft.py`).
- **FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE** (moved here from split 1/5, so that split does not touch `vllm/v1/attention`):
  - prims_ts, FlashInfer's task-scheduled sparse MLA decode (`kernel_config.flashinfer_sparse_mla_kernel`), for nvfp4_ds_mla and a per-tensor fp8 cache under DCP. It runs only when FlashInfer's prims_ts takes the plan arguments vLLM passes (newer than 0.7.3); on 0.7.3, `auto` keeps trtllm-gen and the prims_ts tests skip.
  - Trtllm-gen query head padding (no head count between 64 and 128) and shared multi-CTA KV counters.
  - The Kimi K3.1 specialized decode uses these again; its tests that need them come with this PR.
- **Specialized decode fix**: the wide MoE grid is sized by the SM count (from #65685).
- FA4 MLA prefill passes `head_size_v`.

## Validation

Two-node TP8 serving on 2 x 4 B300 at be30a1a648, with FlashInfer 0.7.3 (the `main` pin), using `Kimi-K3.1-8L-dummy` (the K3.1 architecture with 8 layers, DSA on layers 4 and 8, 96 heads, MXFP4) with `--load-format dummy`. This checks that it serves; it does not check accuracy. The real checkpoint does not fit the disk here.

vllm serve Kimi-K3.1-8L-dummy --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy -tp 8 \

title: [Perf][Qwen4Exp] Faster QSA kernel for large fp8 batches on Blackwell
author: gau-nernst
body:
## Overview

Faster Qwen4Exp QSA sparse attention with fp8 KV caches on `sm_100`/`sm_103` (B200/B300), in a new leaf module `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_fp8.py`: **2.63×** at the MTP decode/verify shape and **1.37–1.42×** at prefill shapes (GB200 kernel time), and **−4.4% median TPOT** end to end.

Credit: the original kernel design and prototype are by @abmfy, the author of record on the first commit. The upstream port used AI assistance (Kimi Code, Claude Code).

## Claims

- fp8-e4m3 caches on sm_100/sm_103 with `rows × KV heads per rank > 64` (decode/verify and prefill) take a new single-pass kernel instead of split-K.
- bf16 caches, smaller batches, and other GPUs keep the split-K path, bitwise-unchanged.
- Numerics: QK stays in bf16 and PV in fp16 (e4m3 → bf16/fp16 is exact), so every QK/PV product matches split-K; only the fp32 summation grouping differs.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_reference.py
# 82 passed (GB200, ~40 s)
```

- New `test_qsa_fp8_kernel_correctness`: MTP-verify-shaped fp8 batches at every TP head layout (24/2, 12/1, 6/1, 3/1 query/KV heads per rank) through the public entry vs the dense reference (`rtol=atol=2e-2`), with masked tails and a CUDA-graph padding row; asserts the gate engages.
- CI: the B200 step (`qwen4-exp-kernels-b200`) runs the full test file and depends on `ops/qsa.py`/`ops/qsa_fp8.py`.

**Kernel** (GB200, CUDA graphs, 2048 selected tokens/row, 24 query / 2 KV heads):

| Workload | Rows | Split-K | New | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Decode/verify | 400 | 396 µs | 151 µs | **2.63×** |
| Decode/verify | 1600 | 1153 µs | 525 µs | **2.20×** |
| Prefill | 4096–8192 | | | **1.37–1.42×** |

**End to end** (one 4×GB200 node, TP4, MTP3, fp8 KV + indexer cache; `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 8192-token cached prefix, 100 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, concurrency 512, 3000 prompts; 2 runs per arm):

| Metric | main | this PR | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median TPOT | 54.64 ms | 52.22 ms | **−4.4%** |
| Output throughput | 7695 tok/s | 7975 tok/s | **+3.6%** |
| MTP acceptance length | 2.186 | 2.217 | +1.4% |

**Accuracy** (same serving setup):

| Task | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K (5-shot, temp 0, n=2638) | 96.78% | 96.70% |
| GPQA-Diamond (thinking, temp 0, n=198) | 72.2% | 75.3% |
| AIME25 (thinking, temp 0.7, 4 epochs, n=120) | 90.8% | 85.8% |

The AIME25 gap is within sampling noise for 30 problems at temperature 0.7.

## Details

**Design.**
1. **Slot pass:** translate each row's selected tokens through the page table once, shared across KV heads, so the attention loop's K/V addresses are known early enough to prefetch.
2. **Attention kernel:** gather K/V as `int16` pairs of e4m3 codes and convert them exactly to fp16 halves for the MMAs. This cuts byte-wise shared-memory loads (360 → 40 per tile), removes split-K's 94 register spills, and allows 4 warps with a 5-stage `cp.async` pipeline.

**Why a separate kernel.** At the 400-row shape, the best split-K config reaches 1.18×, and folding both ideas into split-K reaches 2.46×. A separate kernel is faster (2.63×) and keeps the split-K fallback bitwise-identical.

**Gate.** `rows × KV heads per rank > 64`: below it split-K is faster (0.7–0.9×); above it the new kernel wins at every TP layout, except about 0.96× at TP4 just below one full wave (~140 programs).

**Limitations.**
- Not bitwise-identical to split-K on the new path (fp32 summation order).
- Only GB200 was measured; sm_103 is unvalidated.
- The slot pass adds one small launch and a `rows × selection width` int32 workspace per call.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Engram: 128-row lookup tiles; split GPU tables across engines
author: Juntian777
body:
## Overview

Two Engram changes for DeepSeek-V4.1:

1. **128-row lookup tiles.** Large Engram lookups are latency bound on their reads. Once the rows fill the persistent grid with 128-row tiles, the lookup now uses them (with 8 warps) instead of 16-row tiles, so each program keeps 8x the reads in flight. Packed rows are copied 8 bytes per load instead of a byte, with both loads issued before the stores. Smaller lookups keep 16-row tiles. The rows read and written are unchanged.
2. **GPU tables split across engines.** Engines in one NVLink domain, such as the prefill engines of a disaggregated deployment, can now split each Engram GPU table's rows over all of their GPUs:

   ```bash
   --engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false, "peer_group_size": 8,
                     "peer_group_store": "/shared/job-dir/engram-peers"}'
   ```

   Each GPU holds 1/`peer_group_size` of every table, and lookups read the other rows from their owner's HBM through the existing peer-read path (#62091), so no engine's step waits on another's. This frees the host memory of a CPU-offloaded copy per engine (188.8 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's two tables), e.g. for a host KV cache tier, without a whole table on any GPU.

Related: #64609 (closed) used 128-row tiles for sorted host lookups only; this keys the tile size on the row count instead, which also covers unsorted lookups from THP host tables (`use_thp`) and HBM tables. #64082 (draft) shares *host* tables across independent instances through a persistent owner process with leases; this PR instead splits *GPU* tables peer to peer, with no extra process and no coordination after startup.

## Claims

- Tiles: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DEP2 on GB300, Engram `cpu_offload` with `use_thp=true` (the InferenceX GB300 prefill setting): 12-33% faster per step, and the step time no longer swings by 50-70% between samples. With `use_thp=false` (sorted small-page lookups) the step time is unchanged (within 0.07%). Output is bitwise identical.
- Split tables: each GPU holds 188.83 GiB / `peer_group_size` of the tables and the engines keep no host Engram tables. Per GPU of a DEP2 engine:

  | tables | HBM | host |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | GPU, split over the engine's 2 GPUs (`cpu_offload: false` today) | 94.42 GiB | 0 |
  | host, shared by the engine's 2 GPUs (`cpu_offload: true`, the default) | 0 | 94.42 GiB |
  | GPU, split over 8 GPUs of 4 engines (this PR) | 23.60 GiB | 0 |
  | GPU, split over 18 GPUs of 9 engines (this PR) | 10.49 GiB | 0 |

  Measured: going from 4 to 8 GPUs per group gives every GPU 23.57 GiB more KV cache (expected 23.60). Lookups are bit-exact with the reference; GSM8K is unchanged.

## Design (split tables)

- Symmetric memory cannot span engines: they share no process group, and its rendezvous rejects equal device ordinals on one node, which every engine's ranks have. Each GPU therefore allocates its slice with cuMem, exports a FABRIC handle, and maps every other GPU's slice.
- The engines meet once, at startup, through a torch `FileStore` at `peer_group_store`: ranks come from an atomic counter, exchanges are numbered in order (every GPU builds and loads the same tables in the same order), and each GPU publishes its handle. Nothing reads the store after startup. A path on the job's shared filesystem works without knowing any host address at launch.
- `ParallelEngramEmbedding.process_weights_after_loading` synchronizes and waits until every GPU of the group has loaded its rows, since peers read them directly. It now does the same for the existing in-engine peer tables: their test read peers' rows with no wait and passed only on timing.
- Each process unmaps its view of every slice when the table goes away (a finalizer on an object the table and its slice tensor hold), and a slice's HBM is freed once every GPU has done so. While any peer is alive it keeps a dead engine's slice mapped, so restarting one engine means restarting the group.
- Limits: DeepSeek V4.1 (Qwen4Exp is a TODO), TP=1, PP=1 (stages build different tables), tables in HBM, CUDA FABRIC handles (an IMEX channel), and no weight reloads (other engines read the rows at any time; the in-engine peer tables still reload). The store path must not exist before the group starts (its directory is created). The peer slices are allocated outside torch, so "Model loading took" does not include them; the KV cache, sized from free memory, does.

## Validation

### 128-row tiles

`vllm bench forward`, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (dummy weights), DEP2 on one GB300 node, `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `sparse_indexer_topk_backend=deep_select`, DSpark k=5, `--max-num-batched-tokens 34816`, `--kv-len-jitter 0`, base = main, both arms on the same GPUs, back to back. Per-rank cases, median step time (sample spread):

| case | `use_thp` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `4*8192@131072` (33,280 tokens) | true | 395.0 ms (54.6%) | 323.1 ms (0.21%) |
| `8192@65536` | true | 95.4 ms (0.22%) | 83.9 ms (0.13%) |
| `2*4096@98304` | true | 134.8 ms (67.2%) | 90.3 ms (0.09%) |
| `4*8192@131072` | false | 323.7 ms | 323.6 ms |
| `8192@65536` | false | 84.1 ms | 84.1 ms |
| `2*4096@98304` | false | 90.4 ms | 90.4 ms |

The `use_thp=true` gain is all in the lookup: on the slower rank, `_engram_lookup_kernel` per forward goes 74.0 -> 3.0 ms (`4*8192@131072`), 12.4 -> 0.78 ms (`8192@65536`) and 16.9 -> 0.77 ms (`2*4096@98304`); no other kernel moves by more than 0.3 ms. The other rank waits for it in the DP collective.

`ParallelEngramEmbedding.lookup` alone, one GB300, 32M-row FP8 table, 12 heads, CUPTI with CUDA graph and cold L2, us (foreground / background):

| table | tokens | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HBM | 2048 | 8.2 / 14.3 | 9.6 / 13.3 |
| HBM | 16384 | 117.7 / 223.5 | 68.0 / 121.3 |
| HBM | 65536 | 461.2 / 884.1 | 242.5 / 456.9 |
| pinned host, unsorted | 16384 | 343.6 / 428.8 | 356.7 / 362.6 |
| pinned host, unsorted | 65536 | 1177.5 / 1517.1 | 1180.9 / 1197.7 |

Outputs match between the arms in every case. Below 128 rows per program (256 tokens here) the launch is unchanged.

Packed rows (the FP8 layout the DP-sharded tables stage), one GB300, 94.4 GiB table whole in HBM or split over 4 GPUs (all 4 looking up), 32k tokens, us: main 263 / 933, 128-row tiles with byte reads 345 / 1132, with 8-byte reads 120 / 198.

Packed lookups then load values and scales before storing either: a load after a possibly aliasing store waits a full round trip. With that, 8-byte reads also pay off on 16-row tiles. 4.8M-row table, 24 heads, foreground, us (main / before / this PR):

| table | tokens | main | before | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HBM | 1 | 3.07 | 3.42 | 2.85 |
| HBM | 256 | 6.78 | 7.52 | 6.14 |
| HBM | 16384 | 257.1 | 116.6 | 101.8 |
| split over 4 GPUs, all looking up | 1 | - | 9.46 | 5.59 |
| split over 4 GPUs, all looking up | 256 | - | 21.91 | 12.07 |
| split over 4 GPUs, all looking up | 16384 | - | 203.4 | 157.3 |

BF16 lookups are unchanged by this.

Tests on GB300: `pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 116 passed, 5 skipped. `test_engram_lookup_matches_torch` gets a 1024-token case, which takes the 128-row tiles (24,576 rows; the threshold is 19,456 on 152 SMs, 9,728 in the background), from HBM and pinned host memory, packed and BF16, bit-exact with the torch reference.

### Split tables

On a multi-node NVLink system (4 GPUs per node, IMEX channel per job):

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py` (4 GPUs): 148 passed, 4 skipped. The new `_check_peer_group_table` splits a table over 4 GPUs through the file store, checks lookups bit-exactly, then drops the table and checks that its HBM comes back (with unmapping disabled, that check fails on all 4 GPUs). It returns early without an IMEX channel, so CI skips it.
- CPU: `pytest tests/test_config.py -k peer_group` (10 passed) and `pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -k peer_group` (3 passed): option validation (incl. PP>1 and Qwen4Exp rejected), the compile hash ignoring the store path, unique ranks under racing joins, a reused store rejected, a missing peer named on timeout, and a reload rejected.
- Stress, one GB300 node: 4 processes, each its own one-GPU engine at device ordinal 0, form a group 20 times over; 4 tables of 4.8M rows each round, BF16 and packed lookups on both tile sizes bit-exact, a reload rejected, and the HBM back after the tables are dropped.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (real weights), DEP2 engines, `cpu_offload: false`; engines on two nodes meet through a store on NFS:

  | engines | `peer_group_size` | tables per GPU | KV cache per GPU |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | 2 x DEP2, one node | 4 | 47.21 GiB | 50.92 GiB |
  | 4 x DEP2, two nodes | 8 | 23.60 GiB | 74.49 GiB |

- GSM8K (lm-eval, 5-shot, greedy, chat completions, 1319 questions), engines answering at the same time while sharing one split table (flexible-extract / strict-match):

  | engines | `peer_group_size` | engine 1 | engine 2 |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | 2 x DEP2, one node | 4 | 0.9742 / 0.9750 | 0.9735 / 0.9742 |
  | 4 x DEP2, two nodes (engine 1 and 2 on different nodes) | 8 | 0.9719 / 0.9727 | 0.9757 / 0.9765 |

  These two runs used that system's own vLLM build with this PR's file-store rendezvous ported in, since this branch's attention calls do not match the FlashMLA build installed there. With this branch itself, all engines loaded the real checkpoint into their slices and passed the startup wait (the memory table above), then stopped in attention warmup on that mismatch.

  With this branch itself on GB300 (4 x DEP2, two nodes, `peer_group_size` 8, store on CephFS, DSpark verifying, all 4 engines at once; before the packed-load change, which leaves the output bytes unchanged): 0.9735 / 0.9742, 0.9727 / 0.9735, 0.9719 / 0.9719, 0.9727 / 0.9735.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [Bugfix][Muse Spark] Avoid the FlashInfer Cake PDL race in gated_residual_rmsnorm
author: jeejeelee
body:
## Overview

Run Muse Spark's `gated_residual_rmsnorm` on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL backend instead of the default Cake backend. The Cake programs for 128 rows or fewer read `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#9343). This corrupts the hidden states that DSpark reads, so DSpark output is garbage at DP + EP with TP=1. No open PR addresses this.

## Claims

- Fixes DSpark at DEP8: AIME25 0% → 98.9%, GSM8K 23.1% → 94.8%, sdAL back to 3.7–3.9.
- No end-to-end perf change at TEP4.

## Validation

B300, Muse Spark NVFP4 + DSpark (7 draft tokens), FP8 KV.

**DEP8 accuracy**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| AIME25 (3 epochs, temperature 0.6) | 0% (garbage output) | 98.9% (pass@3 100%) |
| sdAL, AIME25 | 8.00 | 3.66 |
| GSM8K 5-shot strict / flexible (greedy) | 23.1% / 27.2% | 94.8% / 94.8% |
| sdAL, GSM8K | 1.01 | 3.91 |
| sdAL, greedy probe (1 request / C48) | 1.01 / 1.01 | 3.44 / 3.73 |

Target-only DEP8 scores 100% on AIME25; TEP4 GSM8K is 95.0% with sdAL 3.90.

**TEP4 TPOT (140k in / 512 out, 95% prefix hit, median of 3 runs)**

| concurrency | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.61 ms | 3.61 ms |
| 8 | 8.27 ms | 8.73 ms |
| 48 | 19.16 ms | 18.84 ms |

The c=8 gap is acceptance noise: sdAL was 2.26 vs 2.33. Time per step (TPOT × sdAL) is 19.66 vs 19.41 ms. TTFT matches within 1% at every concurrency.

The kernel runs 5 times per decode step, once per captured aux layer. Per-call latency, B300, CUDA graph of 64 chained calls:

| rows | Cake + PDL (main) | CuTe + PDL (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1.50 µs | 1.58 µs |
| 48 | 2.06 µs | 2.14 µs |
| 384 | 6.38 µs | 6.20 µs |
| 4096 | 52.9 µs | 55.1 µs |

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/muse_spark/common/ops/fused_rmsnorm.py
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
mqa-run --task aime25 --epoch-num 3 --temperature 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --max-tokens 98304 --think true
```

## Details

- **Root cause:** DSpark reads 5 auxiliary target hidden states through `norm_then_gated_residual`, which calls `flashinfer.norm.gated_residual_rmsnorm` with `backend="auto"` and `enable_pdl=True`. For 1–128 rows, the Cake PDL programs prefetch `branch` before `griddepcontrol.wait`. When the preceding kernel triggers its dependents early, the norm reads a stale `branch` and emits NaN. The NaN flows through the draft's context K/V into its logits:
  - Most drafts are rejected (sdAL ≈ 1 under greedy GSM8K), but the NaN drafts that do get accepted still derail outputs (GSM8K 23%).
  - With sampling, NaN draft probabilities pass the acceptance test, so every draft is accepted and the output is garbage (AIME25 0%, sdAL 8.00).
- **Why only TP=1:** the same kernel runs at TP>1 without failing there. The trigger depends on which kernel runs just before it. The target's own boundary uses `gated_residual_next_rmsnorm`, whose Cake programs have no PDL, so target-only serving is unaffected.
- **Why CuTe instead of `enable_pdl=False`:** both fix DEP8 and tie end to end. CuTe keeps PDL and is about 0.5 µs faster per decode-size call. Disabling PDL keeps Cake's numerics and is 7–13% faster per call on prefill chunks of 2048 rows or more, which is under 0.05% of a 140k prefill.
- **Support check:** `supports_gated_residual_rmsnorm` is now asked about the CuTe backend too, so shapes that CuTe can't run fall back to the existing Triton path instead of raising.
- **Revert plan:** go back to the default backend once FlashInfer re-renders the Cake programs with the fix.
- **No unit test:** the race needs a producer that triggers its dependents early. The issue has a standalone repro; the end-to-end DEP8 eval above covers the fix.
